docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Embodied-AI Development Environments Nexus

A robot-learning framework built on Genesis: write a task as one typed config, train it across thousands of GPU-parallel environments, then run the same policy on a real robot.

Get started View on GitHub

docs.title: A task is one typed config
docs.text: Scene, observations, actions, rewards, terminations, events, curricula and the learning runner live in one Pydantic object. It validates when you construct it, saves to JSON or YAML, and turns its variants into CLI flags.

docs.title: Composable terms
docs.text: Observations, rewards, terminations, commands, events and curricula are small registered terms. A plain function with a decorator becomes a new one, and eden terms --grep <text> finds an existing one with its parameters.

docs.title: Robots and objects
docs.text: Humanoids, quadrupeds, arms and dexterous hands come as ready-made robot options, and composite rigs bolt a hand onto an arm. Robot and object assets download on first use.

docs.title: Physics and sensing
docs.text: The Genesis solvers (rigid, PBD, MPM, SPH, FEM) are set through EnvOptions, plus Mochi, an implicit solver that couples rigid, soft, cloth and rod bodies. Cameras render through a rasterizer, a batch renderer or the Nyx path tracer, next to depth, lidar, tactile, IMU, contact and audio sensors.

docs.title: Motion and demonstration data
docs.text: Load human-motion datasets, retarget them to robots, estimate motion from video, teleoperate with GELLO, Meta Quest, PICO or the Wuji Glove, and record or script demonstrations into HDF5 and LeRobot datasets.

docs.title: Train, export, deploy
docs.text: Train with rsl_rl (the default), rl_games, skrl or Stable-Baselines3, on one GPU or many. Export a policy to ONNX or TorchScript, check it against MuJoCo with eden deploy --mujoco, then run it on hardware with eden deploy.

docs.title: From install to a trained policy
docs.text:
pip install eden-world                  # or, in a clone of the repository: uv sync
eden list                               # every registered task and its variant flags
eden train --task reacher               # train a Yam arm to reach sampled targets
eden inference --task reacher --checkpoint <path/to/model.pt> --vis
eden inference --policy homie --vis     # roll out a published policy, no training needed

Installation covers platforms and optional extras, and the Quick start walks through these commands and where their output goes.

docs.title: A task is one config
docs.text:
The reacher task, abridged from eden/tasks/benchmark/reacher/config.py, the template every built-in task follows:

@TASK_REGISTRY.register(modifiers=(ReacherDifficultyMod,))  # adds `eden train --task reacher --difficulty hard`
class ReacherConfig(EdenRLConfig):
    env_options: EnvOptions = EnvOptions(num_envs=4096, episode_length_s=9.0, sim_dt=0.01, sim_substeps=2, ...)
    scene_options: SceneOptions = en.scenes.Empty(robot=en.robots.Yam())
    observation_options: ObservationManagerOptions = ObservationManagerOptions(
        policy=ObservationGroupOptions(
            dofs_pos=observations.DofsPos.configure(entity_name="robot"),
            dofs_vel=observations.DofsVel.configure(entity_name="robot"),
            ...
        ),
    )
    action_options: ActionManagerOptions = ActionManagerOptions(
        joint_pos_controller=actions.ImplicitPDController.configure(
            entity_name="robot", dofs_name="joint*", scale=0.05, reference_source=ReferenceSource.DELTA,
        ),
    )
    command_options: CommandManagerOptions = CommandManagerOptions(
        reaching_target=UniformT3Command.configure(x_range=(0.3, 0.5), y_range=(-0.1, 0.1), z_range=(0.25, 0.35)),
    )
    reward_options: RewardManagerOptions = RewardManagerOptions(
        reaching_task=RewardTerm.configure(func=reaching_reward, weight=1.0, params={...}),
        action_rate=RewardTerm.configure(func=rewards.action_rate_l2, weight=-0.01),
    )
    termination_options: TerminationManagerOptions = TerminationManagerOptions(
        timeout=DoneTerm.configure(func=terminations.time_out, time_out=True),
    )
    runner_options: RslRlOnPolicyRunnerOptions = RslRlOnPolicyRunnerOptions(...)

Key concepts explains each piece, and Your first task builds one from scratch.

docs.title: Gallery
docs.text:
Sensors: a Go2 with LiDAR in a scanned tunnel.

Multi-modality: playing piano, with sound synthesised from the pressed keys.

Beyond rigid bodies: a G1 fills a glass with water at a kitchen tap.

Batch rendering: batched Gaussian-splat backgrounds behind a heterogeneous simulation.

Embodiments: built-in robots, composite rigs and object sets.

Policy zoo: published controllers run as shipped with eden inference --policy <name>.

Motion datasets: loaders that share one motion format.

Cross-embodiment retargeting with eden retarget.

Human-object retargeting: the object comes along, onto a rig or a hand.

Train at scale: eden train --task <task> --num_envs 4096, across GPUs with DDP.

Sim-to-sim: eden deploy --task <task> --checkpoint model.pt --mujoco.

Sim-to-real: eden deploy --task <task> --checkpoint model.pt.

Motion tracking with the native motion manager.

Human-object interaction: humanoids with dexterous hands move objects.

Multi-agent RL: two agents with their own observations, actions and rewards.

Soft-body manipulation: a trained policy wipes a bar with a foam sponge.

Cloth manipulation: two arms fold a towel in half.

Cable routing: a cable routed around two spools into a port.

Calligraphy with a modeled Chinese brush.

Wet-acrylic painting, with the wet paint blending.

Benchmark suites: LIBERO, robosuite, SIMPLER, PolaRiS and more, reimplemented.

docs.title: Acknowledgments
docs.text:
Eden builds on these open-source projects:

  • genesis-world: the simulation backend, with gs-madrona (batch renderer) and genesis-nyx (path tracer).
  • quadrants: the compiler that generates parallel kernels for GPUs and CPUs.
  • IsaacLab and mjlab: reference manager-based environment implementations.
  • ManiSkill: a reference holistic environment for embodied agents.
  • ProtoMotions and MimicKit: reference environments for human motion priors.
  • Holosoma and InstinctLab: reference end-to-end humanoid frameworks.

docs.title: Configs and Task Registry
docs.text:
A task is an EdenConfig subclass: one validated Pydantic object that holds every option group an environment is built from. This page documents the config hierarchy, its serialization helpers, and the task registry that finds configs by name. For how to write a task config, read the task configuration guide; for variants and their CLI flags, read the TaskMods guide.

from eden.tasks import TASK_REGISTRY, TaskMod
from eden.utils.configs import EdenConfig, EdenMimicConfig, EdenRLConfig

Each config class pairs with exactly one environment class (EdenConfig with EnvBase, EdenRLConfig with RLEnvBase, EdenMimicConfig with MimicRLEnvBase); a mismatch raises TypeError at construction. See Environments.

def __init__(self, **data):
    # Seed type metadata as construction data so BaseModel validates it into
    # __pydantic_extra__ (no-op for extra="forbid" classes, which use
    # the serialization envelope instead).
    data.update(option_metadata(self))
    # NOTE: all of the option modifications/validations should be done in the __init__ method
    try:
        BaseModel.__init__(self, **data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        # A misspelled field on an extra="forbid" class should teach the field set, not just
        # name the typo. Only rewritten when every error is extra_forbidden.
        enriched = _enrich_extra_forbidden(type(self), exc)
        if enriched is None:
            raise
        raise enriched from None

docs.title: check_bindings
docs.text:
check_bindings() -> None

Raise if a field this config leaves for a :class:~eden.tasks.registry.TaskMod to fill is unset.

:meth:eden.envs.base.EnvBase.from_config calls this before it constructs the env. A task whose robot (or data) binding lives in a TaskMod ships the robot-specific fields as empty sentinels, and a config that reaches an env without the mod -- TASK_REGISTRY.get(name)(), a subclass registered with modifiers=(), a subclass of an unregistered base -- otherwise fails deep in env.build() on a pattern error that names neither the field nor the mod, or does not fail at all where an empty link list resolves to no links. The base checks nothing; a config with mod-bound fields overrides this to name them and the mod (VelocityTrackingBaseConfig is the worked example).

docs.title: recording_camera
docs.text:
recording_camera() -> CameraOptions

The camera a recording of this task renders, added as rec by :meth:add_recording_camera.

eden inference --rec adds it; so does any script that records the task and calls :meth:add_recording_camera. A method rather than a cameras_options entry so that only a recording run builds it: a camera in the training config costs every training run its setup (and whatever its overlays allocate) though nothing renders it, and a checkpoint replays the config it was trained with. The default follows the robot entity from 1.5 m out, which suits a locomoting robot; a task whose subject is elsewhere, or whose recording paints state the scene does not render (a camera overlay, :mod:eden.entities.camera_overlays), overrides it.

Source code in eden/utils/configs.py 
def recording_camera(self) -> CameraOptions:
    """The camera a recording of this task renders, added as ``rec`` by :meth:`add_recording_camera`.

    ``eden inference --rec`` adds it; so does any script that records the task and calls
    :meth:`add_recording_camera`. A method rather than a ``cameras_options`` entry so that only a recording run
    builds it: a camera in the training config costs every training run its setup (and whatever its overlays
    allocate) though nothing renders it, and a checkpoint replays the config it was trained with. The default
    follows the ``robot`` entity from 1.5 m out, which suits a locomoting robot; a task whose subject is
    elsewhere, or whose recording paints state the scene does not render (a camera overlay,
    :mod:`eden.entities.camera_overlays`), overrides it.
    """
    return CameraOptions(cam_pos=(1.5, 1.0, 2.0), cam_lookat=(0.0, 0.0, 1.0), follow_entity_name="robot")

docs.title: add_recording_camera
docs.text:
add_recording_camera() -> None

Add :meth:recording_camera to this config as its rec camera, in place, unless it already has one.

A rec camera the config already has (a cameras_options: {rec: {...}} override) is kept: replacing it would silently discard the override. It replaces the task's camera whole, overlays included, so the overlays it lacks are named in a warning.

Source code in eden/utils/configs.py 
def add_recording_camera(self) -> None:
    """Add :meth:`recording_camera` to this config as its ``rec`` camera, in place, unless it already has one.

    A ``rec`` camera the config already has (a ``cameras_options: {rec: {...}}`` override) is kept: replacing it
    would silently discard the override. It replaces the task's camera whole, overlays included, so the overlays
    it lacks are named in a warning.
    """
    if self.cameras_options is None:
        self.cameras_options = CamerasOptions()
    declared = getattr(self.cameras_options, "rec", None)
    if declared is None:
        self.cameras_options.rec = self.recording_camera()
        return
    # By value: an overlay read back from a saved config is equal to the one written (its parameters are given their
    # declared types again, so a tuple is not a list).
    dropped = [overlay for overlay in self.recording_camera().overlays if overlay not in declared.overlays]
    if dropped:
        en.logger.warning(
            f"The config declares its own `rec` camera, which replaces {type(self).__name__}.recording_camera() "
            f"whole, so the recording leaves out that camera's overlays {[overlay.name for overlay in dropped]} "
            "(task state the scene does not render, such as ink). To keep them, add them to "
            "cameras_options.rec.overlays, e.g. the entries of config.recording_camera().overlays."
        )

def save_as_file(self, path: str, lock_config: bool = True):
    """
    Save the config as either JSON or YAML file with metadata envelope.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path: str
        The path to save the config.
    lock_config: bool
        Whether to lock the config after saving to prevent further modifications.
    """
    file_type = path.split(".")[-1].lower()
    if file_type not in ["json", "yaml", "yml"]:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported config file extension: {file_type}. Use .json, .yaml, or .yml")

    result = self._serialize()

    if lock_config:
        self.lock()

    dirpath = os.path.dirname(path)
    if dirpath:
        os.makedirs(dirpath, exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w") as f:
        if file_type == "json":
            json.dump(result, f, indent=4)
        else:
            yaml.safe_dump(result, f, sort_keys=False)

def save_as_json(self, path: str | None = None, lock_config: bool = True):
    """
    Save the config as a JSON file with metadata envelope.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path: str | None
        The path to save the config. If not provided, the config will be saved to the log directory.
    lock_config: bool
        Whether to lock the config after saving to prevent further modifications.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``path`` does not end in ``.json`` (case-insensitive). Nothing is written and the
        config is left unlocked.
    """
    path = path or f"{en.log_dir}/config.json"
    # Not an ``assert``: ``python -O`` strips those, and ``save_as_file`` dispatches on the
    # suffix — so ``save_as_json("cfg.txt")`` would silently write a file whose extension
    # ``load_from_file`` refuses. Matched case-insensitively, as ``save_as_file`` is.
    if not path.lower().endswith(".json"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"save_as_json expects a path ending in '.json', got '{path}'. "
            f"Use save_as_yaml for YAML, or save_as_file to dispatch on the extension."
        )
    self.save_as_file(path, lock_config)

def save_as_yaml(self, path: str | None = None, lock_config: bool = True):
    """
    Save the config as a YAML file with metadata envelope.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path: str | None
        The path to save the config. If not provided, the config will be saved to the log directory.
    lock_config: bool
        Whether to lock the config after saving to prevent further modifications.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``path`` does not end in ``.yaml`` or ``.yml`` (case-insensitive). Nothing is
        written and the config is left unlocked.
    """
    path = path or f"{en.log_dir}/config.yaml"
    # See ``save_as_json`` — same ``-O``-stripped assert, same silent-wrong-extension outcome.
    if not path.lower().endswith((".yaml", ".yml")):

            f"Use save_as_json for JSON, or save_as_file to dispatch on the extension."
        )
    self.save_as_file(path, lock_config)

docs.title: load_from_file classmethod
docs.text:
load_from_file(path: str) -> EdenConfig

Load the config from a JSON or YAML file, reconstructing its saved class.

The class the file was saved from is recorded in its metadata, so EdenConfig.load_from_file("logs/.../config.json") returns the concrete task config (ReacherConfig) rather than a bare EdenConfig — which is what makes a generic loader like eden train --config <a saved config.json> work at all: a base EdenConfig has nowhere to put reward_options and rejects the file outright.

cls still constrains the result: the saved class must be cls or a subclass of it, so EdenMimicConfig.load_from_file(<a non-mimic config>) fails loud instead of quietly handing back something that is not an EdenMimicConfig. Files with no class metadata (legacy saves) load as cls.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION path

The path to load the config from.

TYPE: str

RETURNS DESCRIPTION EdenConfig

An instance of the saved class (a cls instance when the file records no class).

Source code in eden/utils/configs.py 
@classmethod
def load_from_file(cls, path: str) -> "EdenConfig":
    """
    Load the config from a JSON or YAML file, reconstructing its saved class.

    The class the file was saved from is recorded in its metadata, so
    ``EdenConfig.load_from_file("logs/.../config.json")`` returns the concrete task config
    (``ReacherConfig``) rather than a bare ``EdenConfig`` — which is what makes a generic
    loader like ``eden train --config <a saved config.json>`` work at all: a base
    ``EdenConfig`` has nowhere to put ``reward_options`` and rejects the file outright.

    ``cls`` still constrains the result: the saved class must be ``cls`` or a subclass of it,
    so ``EdenMimicConfig.load_from_file(<a non-mimic config>)`` fails loud instead of quietly
    handing back something that is not an ``EdenMimicConfig``. Files with no class metadata
    (legacy saves) load as ``cls``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path: str
        The path to load the config from.

    Returns
    -------
    EdenConfig
        An instance of the saved class (a ``cls`` instance when the file records no class).
    """
    return cls.load_from_data(read_config_file(path), path)

@classmethod
def load_from_data(cls, data: dict, source: str = "<data>") -> "EdenConfig":
    """Reconstruct a saved config from already-read data — see :meth:`load_from_file`.

    Split out so a caller that has to *inspect* the data before deciding what to do with it
    (``eden train --config``, which reads :func:`is_full_config` to tell a full save from a
    partial override) can reconstruct without reading the file a second time.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data: dict
        The file's contents, in either the ``_meta``/``config`` envelope or the legacy flat
        layout. Consumed destructively — pass a copy to keep it.
    source: str
        Where ``data`` came from, for error messages.

    Returns
    -------
    EdenConfig
        An instance of the saved class (a ``cls`` instance when the data records no class).
    """
    meta = data.pop("_meta", None)
    if meta is not None and "config" in data:
        # Envelope format: {"_meta": {...}, "config": {...}}
        data = data["config"]
    else:
        # Legacy flat format: metadata sat alongside the fields. It carries the same
        # class tags, so it resolves the saved class the same way.
        meta = {key: data.pop(key, None) for key in (*OPTION_METADATA_KEYS, "eden_version", "genesis_version")}

    options = to_options(data, cls._saved_config_class(meta, source))

    for key, name, current in (
        ("eden", "Eden", get_eden_provenance()),
        ("genesis", "Genesis", get_package_provenance("genesis-world")),
    ):
        if change := describe_provenance_change(meta.get(key), current):
            en.logger.warning(f"{name} differs from the one that saved {source}: {change}.")

    return options

docs.title: Reading and converting config files
docs.text:
Eden config hierarchy (EdenConfig/EdenRLConfig/EdenMimicConfig) and serialization.

  • :class:EdenConfig — base config for all environments (EnvBase).
  • :class:EdenRLConfig — adds reward, termination, command, curriculum, and runner options.
  • :class:EdenMimicConfig — adds motion options for motion-imitation tasks.

Root config classes use Pydantic extra="forbid" (so misspelled fields raise), while inner ManagerOptions / SceneOptions keep extra="allow" to hold dynamic term/entity children. Saved configs use a _meta/config envelope; nested Options recover their type from _option_module_ / _option_class_ keys.

The root config recovers its type the same way: :meth:EdenConfig.load_from_file reads the saved class out of _meta and reconstructs that class, so a generic EdenConfig.load_from_file(path) returns the concrete task config it was saved from. The requested class still constrains the result — the saved class must be a subclass of it — and files with no class metadata load as the requested class. Round-tripping a config through save/load is therefore type-preserving and idempotent (pinned by tests/utils/test_configs.py::test_every_task_config_round_trips_to_a_fixed_point).

def read_config_file(path: str) -> dict:
    """Read a ``.json`` / ``.yaml`` / ``.yml`` config file into a raw dict.

    The single file-reading primitive behind :meth:`EdenConfig.load_from_file` and
    :meth:`EdenConfig.with_overrides_from_file`, so both dispatch on the extension the
    same way and report an unsupported one identically.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path: str
        The path to read.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        The file's contents, exactly as parsed — envelope and all, if it has one.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If the extension is not ``.json``, ``.yaml``, or ``.yml``, or if the file does not
        hold a mapping (a bare scalar or list is never a config).
    """
    path_lower = path.lower()
    if path_lower.endswith(".json"):
        with open(path, "r") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    elif path_lower.endswith((".yaml", ".yml")):
        with open(path, "r") as f:
            data = yaml.safe_load(f)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported config file extension: {path}. Use .json, .yaml, or .yml")

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise ValueError(f"{path} does not hold a config mapping — parsed as {type(data).__name__}.")
    return data

def is_full_config(data: dict) -> bool:
    """Whether ``data`` is a *saved* config (replaces a base) rather than a partial override.

    A save from :meth:`EdenConfig.save_as_file` carries its class and version tags — under a
    ``_meta`` envelope, or (legacy flat saves) alongside the fields. A hand-written partial
    override never does, which is what makes the two forms distinguishable by content instead
    of by flag: ``eden train --config`` reads this to decide whether the file replaces the
    task's config or layers onto it.
    """
    if "_meta" in data and "config" in data:
        return True
    return any(key in data for key in (*OPTION_METADATA_KEYS, "eden_version", "genesis_version"))

def saved_config_qualname(data: dict) -> str | None:
    """The ``module.Class`` a saved config records, or ``None`` when it records no class.

    Reads the same tags :meth:`EdenConfig.load_from_data` reconstructs from, without importing
    anything — so a caller can compare identities (``eden train --config``, checking that a
    saved config is the one its ``--task`` builds) and report a mismatch by name even when the
    saved class is not importable here.

    Parameters
    ----------
    data: dict
        A saved config's contents, in either the ``_meta``/``config`` envelope or the legacy
        flat layout. Not modified.

    Returns
    -------
    str | None
        The dotted qualname, or ``None`` for a file with no class metadata (legacy saves and
        hand-written full configs, which load as whatever class is asked for).
    """
    meta = data.get("_meta") if isinstance(data.get("_meta"), dict) and "config" in data else data
    module_name, class_name = (meta.get(key) for key in OPTION_METADATA_KEYS)
    return f"{module_name}.{class_name}" if module_name and class_name else None

def overrides_from_str(text: str) -> dict:
    """Parse one ``--override`` argument — an inline YAML (or JSON) mapping — into a dict.

    YAML flow style keeps the shell-facing form short and quote-free
    (``'env_options: {num_envs: 64}'``); JSON is a subset, so the explicit form works too.
    Note that PyYAML implements YAML 1.1 implicit typing, where ``off`` / ``no`` / ``yes``
    parse as booleans — quote any value that should stay a string.

    Parameters
    ----------
    text: str
        The inline mapping.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        The parsed override data, ready for :meth:`EdenConfig.with_overrides_from_dict`.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``text`` is not parseable, or parses to something other than a mapping — the
        common case being a file path, which belongs to ``--config``.
    """
    try:
        data = yaml.safe_load(text)
    except yaml.YAMLError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Could not parse override {text!r} as an inline YAML mapping: {e}") from e

    if not isinstance(data, dict):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Override {text!r} is not a mapping — it parsed as {type(data).__name__}. Write it as "
            f"'env_options: {{num_envs: 64}}'. To load overrides from a .json/.yaml file, use --config."
        )
    return data

serialize_obj_with_metadata(obj)

Recursively serialize an object, capturing Options type metadata.

Captures _option_module_ and _option_class_ metadata from Options instances. This works by using model_dump() for data but accessing actual Option objects to extract their metadata.

NamedTuple values (e.g. Genesis TemperatureProperties) subclass tuple and are serialized as plain lists of fields in field order; to_options reconstructs them using the surrounding Pydantic field annotations on load.

Source code in eden/utils/configs.py 
def serialize_obj_with_metadata(obj):
    """Recursively serialize an object, capturing Options type metadata.

    Captures ``_option_module_`` and ``_option_class_`` metadata from Options
    instances. This works by using ``model_dump()`` for data but accessing actual
    Option objects to extract their metadata.

    NamedTuple values (e.g. Genesis ``TemperatureProperties``) subclass ``tuple`` and are
    serialized as plain lists of fields in field order; ``to_options`` reconstructs them
    using the surrounding Pydantic field annotations on load.
    """
    if isinstance(obj, Options):
        # A field left at a None default is dumped as absent, not as an explicit None: loading would
        # otherwise mark it set, and Genesis reads set-ness — a solver whose options merely list `dt`
        # among `model_fields_set` divides the sim dt by it (`MochiOptions(dt=None)` would crash the build).
        unset_none = {name for name in type(obj).model_fields if name not in obj.model_fields_set}
        unset_none = {name for name in unset_none if getattr(obj, name, None) is None}
        result: dict = obj.model_dump(exclude=unset_none)

        # Stamp type metadata at dump time. The getattr fallback covers extra="forbid" options
        # (which don't carry it in __pydantic_extra__), so entities stored as unannotated scene
        # children still recover their concrete class on load even though they forbid extras.
        result["_option_module_"] = getattr(obj, "_option_module_", obj.__module__)
        result["_option_class_"] = getattr(obj, "_option_class_", obj.__class__.__name__)

        # Now recursively process each field value to capture nested Options metadata
        for field_name in list(result.keys()):
            if field_name not in OPTION_METADATA_KEYS:
                # Try to get the actual object using getattr to handle all cases
                # (including fields not in __dict__ due to defaults, properties, etc)
                try:
                    actual_value = getattr(obj, field_name)
                    # If the actual value is an Options object, recursively serialize it
                    if isinstance(actual_value, Options):
                        result[field_name] = serialize_obj_with_metadata(actual_value)
                    else:
                        # Recurse over the live field value so container fields
                        # (for example list[Union[...Options]]) keep subclass data
                        # that may be erased by model_dump() schema narrowing.
                        result[field_name] = serialize_obj_with_metadata(actual_value)
                except AttributeError:
                    # Field doesn't exist, keep the dumped value and recurse
                    result[field_name] = serialize_obj_with_metadata(result[field_name])

        return result
    elif isinstance(obj, BaseModel):
        # For other BaseModel instances, serialize and recurse
        result = obj.model_dump()
        for key, value in list(result.items()):
            result[key] = serialize_obj_with_metadata(value)
        return result
    elif isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {key: serialize_obj_with_metadata(value) for key, value in obj.items()}
    elif isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
        return [serialize_obj_with_metadata(item) for item in obj]
    elif isinstance(obj, Enum):
        return obj.value
    elif isinstance(obj, np.ndarray):
        return obj.tolist()
    elif isinstance(obj, torch.Tensor):
        return obj.detach().cpu().numpy().tolist()
    # in case of np/torch scalars, cast to plain numeric types
    elif isinstance(obj, bool):
        return bool(obj)
    elif isinstance(obj, int):
        return int(obj)
    elif isinstance(obj, float):
        return float(obj)
    return obj

def get_options_class_from_qualname(qualname: str):
    """
    Dynamically import and retrieve an Options class from its fully qualified name.

    Parameters
    ----------
    qualname : str
        The fully qualified name of the Options class (e.g., "eden.options.managers.actions.ActionTermOptions")

    Returns
    -------
    Type[Options]
        The Options class

    Raises
    ------
    ImportError
        If the module cannot be imported
    AttributeError
        If the class cannot be found in the module
    """
    import importlib

    # Split the qualname into module path and class name
    parts = qualname.rsplit(".", 1)
    if len(parts) != 2:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid qualified name: {qualname}. Expected format: 'module.path.ClassName'")

    module_path, class_name = parts

    # Import the module
    try:
        module = importlib.import_module(module_path)
    except ImportError as e:
        raise ImportError(f"Could not import module '{module_path}': {e}")

    # Get the class from the module
    try:
        return getattr(module, class_name)
    except AttributeError:
        raise AttributeError(f"Class '{class_name}' not found in module '{module_path}'")

def to_options(config: dict, base_options: Options | type[Options]):
    """
    Reconstruct the original Options instance from serialized data.

    Eden options (config root classes included) are rebuilt with validation, so an unknown key on
    an ``extra="forbid"`` class raises, while ``extra="allow"`` classes (ManagerOptions,
    SceneOptions, etc.) keep unknown keys as their dynamic term/entity children. Genesis-native
    options skip validation, and an ``extra="forbid"`` one drops unknown keys with a warning — see
    :func:`_safe_model_construct`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    config: dict
        The serialized field data.
    base_options: Options | type[Options]
        The target type, as either a class or an instance to take the class of. Only the
        *type* is read, so pass the class when there is nothing to instantiate it from —
        a task config's ``__init__`` can be expensive and its result is discarded here.
    """
    options_cls = base_options if isinstance(base_options, type) else type(base_options)

    # Convert all config attributes
    res = {}
    for key, value in config.items():
        field_info = options_cls.model_fields.get(key)
        field_annotation = field_info.annotation if field_info is not None else None
        res[key] = _convert_value(value, field_annotation)

    return _safe_model_construct(options_cls, res)

docs.title: Task registry
docs.text: Tasks register themselves with @TASK_REGISTRY.register() on the config class. The registry scans the source of eden.tasks (and of every package an installed distribution names under the eden.tasks entry-point group) on first lookup without importing it, so there is no central index to update. TASK_REGISTRY.build(name, **kwargs) returns a configured instance with the task's TaskMods applied, which is what eden train does; TASK_REGISTRY.get(name) returns the bare class, and instantiating that yourself skips every mod.

docs.title: TaskRegistry
docs.text:
TaskRegistry()

Task registry with two lookup paths, tried in order.

  1. Eager registry — populated by @TASK_REGISTRY.register() decorators or explicit register(cls, ...) calls.
  2. Auto-discovery — an AST scan of the configured search packages (default ["eden.tasks"]) finds @TASK_REGISTRY.register() decorators in every *.py file without importing them. On first :meth:get miss we import only the one file that matches the requested name; that triggers the decorator and populates the eager registry.

Tasks self-register at the definition site — no central index in eden/tasks/__init__.py to keep in sync. Out-of-tree tasks join the scan through the :data:TASK_ENTRY_POINT_GROUP entry point of the distribution that ships them, so eden list / eden train --task see them without importing anything; a script can also call :meth:add_search_path before its first lookup.

Auto-discovery rules (files that are NOT scanned):

  • __init__.py is skipped — put decorated classes in a sibling module such as config.py.
  • files whose name starts with _ are skipped (e.g. _meta.py) — private modules are treated as implementation details.

Auto-discovery rules (decorator recognition):

  • The scan recognizes @<name>.register where <name> is bound, in the same file, to TASK_REGISTRY via an absolute import from eden.tasks or eden.tasks.registry (from ... import TASK_REGISTRY or ... as X). Both forms work.
  • Using the literal name TASK_REGISTRY without importing it from a recognized location emits a warning — the scan will not silently miss the registration.

Usage::

# Preferred: decorator at definition site; modifiers passed to the
# decorator so they live on the registry (not on the config class,
# which is a Pydantic model and should only hold serializable schema).
@TASK_REGISTRY.register(modifiers=(ReacherDifficultyMod,))
class ReacherConfig(EdenRLConfig):
    ...

cfg = TASK_REGISTRY.build("reacher", difficulty="hard")  # a configured instance, mods applied
cls = TASK_REGISTRY.get("reacher")                       # the bare class; cls() runs no mod

def __init__(self) -> None:
    self._registry: dict[str, Any] = {}
    # Modifiers attached at registration time (override class attr). ``_INHERITED`` stands
    # for "take the nearest registered base's", resolved on read by _resolve_modifiers.
    self._modifiers: dict[str, tuple[TaskMod, ...] | _Inherited] = {}
    # Memo for that walk, dropped whenever a registration changes what it would answer.
    self._resolved_modifiers: dict[str, tuple[TaskMod, ...]] = {}
    # Packages add_search_path added to the scan (eden.tasks always), each mapped to the source
    # task_source() reports for its tasks.
    self._search_packages: dict[str, str] = {"eden.tasks": "eden"}
    # The registrations _do_register set aside because their name clashes, by "module:Class",
    # as (name, class, modifiers entry): the class answers to no name, but a subclass still
    # inherits its modifiers through it, and a rescan that ends the clash registers it.
    self._clashing_registrations: dict[str, tuple[str, Any, tuple[TaskMod, ...] | _Inherited]] = {}

    # What the scan found. _ensure_discovered recomputes all of it, entry points included, so a
    # rescan sees a plugin fixed or installed since; nothing else writes it.
    # name -> "module.path:ClassName". None means "not yet scanned".
    self._discovered: dict[str, str] | None = None
    # name -> modifier display-names, read from the decorators.
    self._discovered_modifiers: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    # Every package scanned, eden.tasks first, mapped to its source label (task_source()).
    self._package_sources: dict[str, str] = {}
    # What the scan could not answer, kept so that only a lookup it could change raises it (one
    # broken plugin must not stop every built-in task): entry points that name no scannable
    # package, as (the package it names, message, cause), and names registered in several
    # scanned files, as name -> [(module:Class, file path)].
    self._broken_entry_points: list[tuple[str, str, BaseException | None]] = []
    self._collisions: dict[str, list[tuple[str, str]]] = {}

Sequence of TaskMod instances (preferred) or bare TaskMod subclasses (auto-instantiated with no args). Applied in order by :meth:build. That inheritance is live: it re-resolves on every read, so re-registering the class the mods come from — or registering it after this one — updates this task too, whichever order the two ran in. The registration override=True replaces counts, so shadowing a built-in with a subclass keeps the built-in's mods; that one is a snapshot, since the registration it came from no longer exists. () opts out; a class with no registered ancestor gets none either way.

def register(
    self,
    obj: Any = None,
    *,
    name: str | None = None,
    override: bool = False,
    modifiers: tuple[ModifierEntry, ...] | None = None,
) -> Any:
    """Register a config class eagerly. Can be used as a decorator or function call.

    Parameters
    ----------
    obj: Any
        The config class to register. When ``None``, returns a decorator.
    name: str | None
        Lookup name. Defaults to ``_default_task_name(cls.__name__)``
        (``to_snake_case`` with any trailing ``_config`` stripped).
    override: bool
        If ``True``, silently replace an existing registration with the
        same name.
    modifiers: tuple[ModifierEntry, ...] | None
        Sequence of TaskMod **instances** (preferred) or bare TaskMod
        subclasses (auto-instantiated with no args). Applied in order by
        :meth:`build`. ``None`` (the default) inherits the modifiers of the
        nearest registered class in ``obj``'s MRO, so a subclass of a task
        keeps the mods that bind it — its robot, its data — instead of
        building against the parent's unset sentinels. That inheritance is
        **live**: it re-resolves on every read, so re-registering the class
        the mods come from — or registering it after this one — updates this
        task too, whichever order the two ran in. The registration
        ``override=True`` replaces counts, so shadowing a built-in with a
        subclass keeps the built-in's mods; that one is a snapshot, since the
        registration it came from no longer exists. ``()`` opts out; a class
        with no registered ancestor gets none either way.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``modifiers`` is ``None`` and the nearest registered ancestor is
        registered under several names with different modifiers, none of them
        the ``name`` being replaced — pass ``modifiers=`` explicitly to pick.
        A later registration that makes an already-registered task ambiguous
        the same way raises from :meth:`get_modifiers` / :meth:`build` instead
        — :meth:`modifier_names`, a display path, falls back to the names the
        decorators declare.
    """

    def deco(cls: Any) -> Any:
        if not isinstance(cls, type):
            # Every lookup reads the class's module and name, so anything else would register
            # here and then fail far from this line.
            raise TypeError(
                f"TASK_REGISTRY.register() takes a config class; got {cls!r} ({type(cls).__name__}). "
                "Register the class itself, and apply what a factory would set through modifiers=(...)."
            )
        self._do_register(name or _default_task_name(cls.__name__), cls, override=override, modifiers=modifiers)
        return cls

    return deco if obj is None else deco(obj)

def add_search_path(self, package: str) -> None:
    """Register an additional package root to AST-scan for decorated tasks.

    Only the process that calls it sees the package, so it suits a script that does its own
    lookups::

        from eden.tasks import TASK_REGISTRY
        TASK_REGISTRY.add_search_path("my_project.tasks")

    For the ``eden`` CLI to see an installed project's tasks, name the package under the
    :data:`TASK_ENTRY_POINT_GROUP` entry-point group in the project's ``pyproject.toml``
    instead. A package that cannot be found is skipped, unlike a broken entry point.
    """
    if package in self._search_packages:
        return
    self._search_packages[package] = package
    # Invalidate the discovery cache so the new package is scanned on the next miss.
    self._discovered = None

def get(self, name: str) -> Any:
    """Get a config CLASS by name.

    Resolution order: eager registry → auto-discovery. The returned object
    is the bare config class, so ``get(name)()`` runs **none** of the task's
    registered TaskMods. For a task whose robot binding lives in a mod,
    that yields a config that constructs and serializes without
    complaint and then fails in ``env.build()`` on an empty link name — an
    error that says nothing about modifiers.
    Use :meth:`build` to obtain a configured instance; reach for ``get``
    only when the class itself is what you want (``issubclass`` checks,
    subclassing, matching a loaded config's type).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``name`` is registered in several scanned files.
    RuntimeError
        If ``name`` is not found and an installed :data:`TASK_ENTRY_POINT_GROUP` entry point
        names no scannable package, which could hold it.
    KeyError
        If ``name`` is not found anywhere.
    """
    qualname = self._lookup(name)
    if qualname is None:
        raise KeyError(self.missing_task_message(name))
    if name not in self._registry:
        # Importing the module triggers @TASK_REGISTRY.register(), which
        # populates self._registry[name].
        importlib.import_module(qualname.rsplit(":", 1)[0])
    if name in self._registry:
        return self._registry[name]
    # Import succeeded but the decorator didn't fire (e.g. the class
    # is gated behind `if __name__ == "__main__":`). Report clearly.
    raise RuntimeError(
        f"Auto-discovered task '{name}' at '{qualname}' but importing its module "
        "did not register it. Check that @TASK_REGISTRY.register() runs at import time."
    )

def get_modifiers(self, name: str) -> tuple[TaskMod, ...]:
    """Resolve and return the TaskMod **instances** associated with ``name``.

    Modifiers live on the registry itself (not on the config class),
    attached via ``register(modifiers=...)``. For decorator-registered
    tasks the decorator's ``modifiers=`` tuple is populated when the
    module is imported, so we call :meth:`get` first to ensure that
    import has happened. A registration that inherits its modifiers
    resolves them here, against the registry as it stands now.
    """
    if name not in self:
        raise KeyError(f"No task named '{name}' found in task registry.")
    # Ensure the module is loaded so the decorator has had a chance to
    # attach modifiers. No-op if already loaded.
    self.get(name)
    return self._resolve_modifiers(name)

def modifier_names(self, name: str) -> list[str]:
    """Modifier display-names for ``name`` **without importing** its module.

    Unlike :meth:`get_modifiers` (which imports the task to return live
    instances), this is purely informational — used by ``eden list`` so a
    read-only listing never triggers a task-module import and the asset
    downloads that can ride along. Prefers modifier instances already
    attached (eager registrations / already-loaded tasks) for exactness,
    an inherited registration included — resolving one reads the other live
    registrations, which needs no import either. Otherwise falls back to the
    identifier names captured from the ``@register(modifiers=...)`` decorator
    during AST auto-discovery — for a decorator without ``modifiers=``, the
    ones its base class's decorator names, since that is what registering it
    inherits. A listing renders rather than raises, so an inherited
    registration left ambiguous by a later one falls back here too; the
    error still belongs to :meth:`get_modifiers` and :meth:`build`, which
    are what a caller acts on.
    """
    try:
        attached = self._resolve_modifiers(name)
    except ValueError:
        attached = ()
    if attached:
        return [type(m).__name__ for m in attached]
    self._ensure_discovered()  # populates self._discovered_modifiers
    return list(self._discovered_modifiers.get(name, []))

Instantiate the config and apply registered TaskMods.

Modifier kwargs are flat and use each mod's prefixed field names (see :meth:TaskMod.flag_for). For an unprefixed mod that exposes difficulty, pass difficulty=...; for an instance registered with prefix="left" that exposes robot, pass left_robot=....

def build(self, name: str, **modifier_kwargs: Any) -> Any:
    """Instantiate the config and apply registered TaskMods.

    Modifier kwargs are flat and use each mod's **prefixed** field names
    (see :meth:`TaskMod.flag_for`). For an unprefixed mod that exposes
    ``difficulty``, pass ``difficulty=...``; for an instance registered
    with ``prefix="left"`` that exposes ``robot``, pass ``left_robot=...``.

    Collisions — two mods that would claim the same flag — raise
    ``ValueError`` at build time with both owners listed. Unknown kwargs
    raise ``ValueError`` with the list of accepted flags.
    """
    cls = self.get(name)
    config = cls()
    mods = self._resolve_modifiers(name)

    # Map each prefixed flag to (mod index, field_name, annotation).
    flag_map: dict[str, tuple[int, str, Any]] = {}
    for i, mod in enumerate(mods):
        for field_name, annotation, _default, _help in cli_fields(type(mod)):
            flag = mod.flag_for(field_name)
            if flag in flag_map:
                j, other_field, _ = flag_map[flag]
                raise ValueError(
                    f"Modifier flag collision on task '{name}': '{flag}' is claimed by "
                    f"both mod[{j}] ({type(mods[j]).__name__}.{other_field}) and "
                    f"mod[{i}] ({type(mod).__name__}.{field_name}). "
                    "Give the TaskMod instances distinct prefix values via .with_prefix(...)."
                )
            flag_map[flag] = (i, field_name, annotation)

    unknown = set(modifier_kwargs) - set(flag_map)
    if unknown:
        # Surface a targeted hint when the unknown kwarg matches a
        # keyword-only init param on a registered mod — that's the most
        # common adoption mistake (declaring a CLI knob after `*` so it
        # never reaches the CLI surface). Match on the prefixed flag form
        # so the hint also fires for prefixed mods.
        kwonly_index: dict[str, tuple[TaskMod, str]] = {}
        for mod in mods:
            for field in _keyword_only_fields(type(mod)):
                kwonly_index[mod.flag_for(field)] = (mod, field)
        kwonly_hits: list[str] = []
        for u in sorted(unknown):
            if u in kwonly_index:
                mod, field = kwonly_index[u]
                kwonly_hits.append(
                    f"'{u}' is keyword-only on {type(mod).__name__} (as '{field}') — "
                    f"keyword-only params are non-CLI ctor state. Set it at registration "
                    f"with modifiers=({type(mod).__name__}({field}=...),); if you own "
                    f"{type(mod).__name__} and want a CLI flag, move '{field}' before "
                    f"`*` in __init__."
                )
        hint = ("\n" + textwrap.indent("Hint:\n" + "\n".join(kwonly_hits), "  ")) if kwonly_hits else ""
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unknown modifier kwargs for task '{name}': {sorted(unknown)}. "
            f"Known: {sorted(flag_map) or 'none'}{hint}"
        )

    # Group kwargs per mod, stripping the prefix and validating each value
    # against its declared annotation (Literal membership + primitive type).
    updates_per_mod: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{} for _ in mods]
    for flag, value in modifier_kwargs.items():
        i, field_name, annotation = flag_map[flag]
        _check_cli_value(field_name, annotation, value)
        updates_per_mod[i][field_name] = value

    for mod, updates in zip(mods, updates_per_mod):
        if updates:
            # Deep copy so per-build overrides don't mutate the registered
            # instance; deep so mutable instance state (lists/dicts a
            # subclass might keep) is not aliased across builds.
            applied = copy.deepcopy(mod)
            for field_name, value in updates.items():
                setattr(applied, field_name, value)
        else:
            applied = mod
        config = applied.apply(config)
    return config

def list_tasks(self) -> list[str]:
    """List all registered task names (eager + discovered).

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If a task name is registered in several scanned files.
    RuntimeError
        If an installed :data:`TASK_ENTRY_POINT_GROUP` entry point names no scannable package
        — the list would be missing that package's tasks.
    """
    discovered = self._ensure_discovered()
    if self._collisions:
        raise ValueError("\n".join(_collision_message(n, where) for n, where in sorted(self._collisions.items())))

def task_for_config_qualname(self, qualname: str) -> str | None:
    """The task whose config class is ``module.Class``, or ``None`` if no task owns it.

    The reverse of :meth:`get`, and deliberately **import-free**: eager entries are already
    in memory, and discovered-only entries are matched against the ``module:Class`` string
    the AST scan recorded. Calling :meth:`get` in a loop instead would import every task
    module in the tree — and could raise out of an unrelated one — which is the wrong trade
    for a lookup whose caller is building an error message.

    Parameters
    ----------
    qualname: str
        Dotted ``module.Class`` name, as :func:`eden.utils.configs.saved_config_qualname`
        reads it out of a saved config.

    Returns
    -------
    str | None
        The task name, or ``None`` when no registered or discoverable task declares it.
    """
    discovered = self._ensure_discovered()
    module, _, cls_name = qualname.rpartition(".")
    key = f"{module}:{cls_name}"  # the "module:Class" form the scan and _class_key use
    for name, cls in self._registry.items():
        if _class_key(cls) == key:
            self._raise_if_clashing(name, cls)
            return name
    for name, found in discovered.items():
        if found == key:
            return name
    for name, where in self._collisions.items():
        if any(found == key for found, _ in where):
            raise ValueError(_collision_message(name, where))
    self._raise_if_scan_incomplete(
        f"No task declares '{qualname}', and its module lies under a task package the scan could not read.",
        module=module,
    )
    return None

def task_source(self, name: str) -> str | None:
    """Where the config ``name`` builds comes from, as ``eden list`` shows it.

    ``"eden"`` for a built-in, the distribution's name for a task found through its
    :data:`TASK_ENTRY_POINT_GROUP` entry point, the package for one under a package passed to
    :meth:`add_search_path`, and the defining module for a class registered from anywhere else
    — so a built-in name shadowed by a ``register(..., override=True)`` reads as the module
    that shadowed it. Import-free, like :meth:`config_qualname_for_task`, which it reads.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name: str
        Registered task name.

    Returns
    -------
    str | None
        The source label, or ``None`` when no registered or discoverable task has that name.
    """
    qualname = self.config_qualname_for_task(name)
    if qualname is None:
        return None
    module = qualname.rpartition(".")[0]
    # The innermost search package holding the module, so a package scanned inside another's tree wins.
    owners = [package for package in self._package_sources if _is_under(module, package)]
    return self._package_sources[max(owners, key=len)] if owners else module

def missing_task_message(self, name: str) -> str:
    """The message for a miss on ``name``: a close match, every task there is, and where to declare one.

    The text of :meth:`get`'s ``KeyError`` (so one line), for a caller that reports a miss its own way,
    as ``eden``'s ``--task`` check does. Unlike :meth:`list_tasks`, it lists what the scan resolved
    even while another name clashes or a plugin is broken, since those are reported where they
    are looked up, and the reader here needs the name they mistyped. It raises only what the scan
    itself does (a search-path package whose parents fail to import), and nothing once a lookup
    has scanned.
    """
    available = sorted(set(self._registry) | set(self._ensure_discovered()))
    close = difflib.get_close_matches(name, available, n=1)
    did_you_mean = f" Did you mean '{close[0]}'?" if close else ""
    return (
        f"No task named '{name}' found in task registry.{did_you_mean} "
        f"Available: {', '.join(available) or 'none'}. Note: {OUT_OF_TREE_TASK_HINT}"
    )

docs.title: TaskMod
docs.text:
Tool that modifies an EdenConfig instance.

TaskMod is a plain Python class (not a Pydantic model) because it is logic with a few parameters, not user-facing data. EdenConfig is the Pydantic data model; TaskMod operates on it.

To define one: subclass, declare CLI-tunable parameters as positional-or-keyword __init__ arguments with type annotations, and implement :meth:apply. Non-CLI constructor state goes in keyword-only parameters (after *) — the CLI introspection skips those.

Quick reference (this is the convention agents miss most often)::

def __init__(
    self,
    difficulty: Literal["easy", "hard"] = "easy",  # ← CLI flag (--difficulty)
    *,
    entity_name: str = "robot",                    # ← non-CLI ctor state
):
    self.difficulty = difficulty
    self.entity_name = entity_name

Calling super().__init__() is optional — TaskMod keeps no instance state of its own; _prefix is a class-attribute default that :meth:with_prefix shadows on assignment. So your subclass __init__ can just store its parameters and return.

For per-field CLI --help text, wrap the annotation in typing.Annotated[T, "help text"]. The string metadata is forwarded to argparse; the inner type is what drives validation::

difficulty: Annotated[Literal["easy", "hard"], "Task difficulty preset."] = "easy"

Implement :meth:apply to return the modified config; in-place mutation is fine because :meth:TaskRegistry.build calls cls() fresh on every build (and Pydantic deep-copies the config's BaseModel defaults per instance), so mutations do not leak across builds.

Modifiers attach to a task by passing instances to @TASK_REGISTRY.register(modifiers=(...)) (a bare subclass is accepted and instantiated with no args). Modifiers are stored on the registry, not on the config class. A config registered without modifiers= inherits them from its nearest registered base class; modifiers=() opts out (see :meth:TaskRegistry.register).

Per-instance scoping: chain :meth:with_prefix on a constructed instance so its CLI flags rename from <field> to <prefix>_<field>. The same subclass can be registered multiple times with distinct prefixes.

Example

::

from typing import Annotated, Literal

class RobotMod(TaskMod):
    def __init__(
        self,
        robot: Annotated[
            Literal["allegro", "shadow", "xhand1"],
            "Hand model to load into the scene.",
        ] = "xhand1",
        *,
        entity_name: str = "robot",  # keyword-only → not CLI-exposed
    ):
        self.robot = robot
        self.entity_name = entity_name

    def apply(self, config):
        setattr(config.scene_options, self.entity_name, ROBOT_REGISTRY.get(self.robot)())
        return config

@TASK_REGISTRY.register(modifiers=(
    RobotMod(robot="shadow", entity_name="robot_left").with_prefix("left"),
    RobotMod(entity_name="robot_right").with_prefix("right"),
))
class TwoArmTask(EdenRLConfig):
    ...

# CLI: --left_robot shadow --right_robot xhand1
TASK_REGISTRY.build("two_arm_task", left_robot="allegro", right_robot="shadow")

CLI helpers for building task configs from argparse.

This module wires :class:~eden.tasks.registry.TaskMod parameters into a standard argparse.ArgumentParser so that user-facing scripts can accept flat flags (--difficulty hard, --robot g1) that are translated into typed mod kwargs and applied via :meth:TaskRegistry.build.

get_task_argparser(description: str, default_task_name: str = '', argv: list[str] | None = None) -> ArgumentParser

Build an ArgumentParser with standard flags plus the selected task's mod flags.

The selected task is determined by pre-parsing --task from argv (defaults to sys.argv[1:]). Modifier flags are added only for the selected task, so --help shows only the relevant options. Pass argv explicitly when invoking this from a wrapper that already has its own arg slice (e.g. the eden train / eden inference subcommands forward extra_args) so the peek and the final parse agree on input.

Source code in eden/tasks/parser.py 
def get_task_argparser(
    description: str,
    default_task_name: str = "",
    argv: list[str] | None = None,
) -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    """Build an ``ArgumentParser`` with standard flags plus the selected task's mod flags.

    The selected task is determined by pre-parsing ``--task`` from ``argv``
    (defaults to ``sys.argv[1:]``). Modifier flags are added only for the
    selected task, so ``--help`` shows only the relevant options. Pass
    ``argv`` explicitly when invoking this from a wrapper that already has
    its own arg slice (e.g. the ``eden train`` / ``eden inference``
    subcommands forward ``extra_args``) so the peek and the final parse
    agree on input.
    """
    task_name = _peek_task_name(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv, default_task_name)

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=description, formatter_class=ColorHelpFormatter)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--run_name",
        type=str,
        default="",
        help="Run name, put in the log directory name (<timestamp>-<run_name>-<id>) and so in the wandb run name.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--task",
        type=str,
        default=default_task_name,
        help="Task name. May expose additional mod flags depending on the task.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--config",
        type=str,
        default=None,
        help="Path to a config file (.json/.yaml/.yml). A saved config (one Eden wrote, carrying "
        "its class metadata) replaces the task's config; anything else layers onto it as a "
        "partial override.",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--override",
        action="append",
        default=None,
        metavar="YAML",
        help="Inline config override as a YAML mapping, e.g. --override 'env_options: {num_envs: 64}'. "
        "Repeatable; later ones win. Applied on top of --config.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("--checkpoint", type=str, default=None, help="Path to a checkpoint file.")
    parser.add_argument("--cpu", action="store_true", help="Use CPU backend.")

    if task_name and task_name in TASK_REGISTRY:
        for mod in TASK_REGISTRY.get_modifiers(task_name):
            for field_name, annotation, _default, help_text in cli_fields(type(mod)):
                _add_mod_field_to_parser(parser, mod, field_name, annotation, help_text)

    return parser

def get_task_config(
    task_name: str,
    *,
    run_name: str = "",
    modifier_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    config_path: str | None = None,
    config_overrides: Sequence[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
) -> Any:
    """Build a task config programmatically.

    :meth:`TaskRegistry.build`, then — in this order, later winning — an optional
    ``config_path`` file and any ``config_overrides`` dicts, then a sanitized ``run_name``
    written to ``runner_options`` if present.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task_name: str
        Registered task to build.
    run_name: str
        Run name to write onto ``runner_options``; ignored when empty.
    modifier_kwargs: dict[str, Any] | None
        TaskMod kwargs forwarded to :meth:`TaskRegistry.build`.
    config_path: str | None
        A ``.json``/``.yaml``/``.yml`` config file. A saved config replaces the task build; a
        partial one layers onto it. See :func:`_apply_config_file`.
    config_overrides: Sequence[dict[str, Any]] | None
        Override dicts applied on top of everything else, in order — the ``--override`` payload.

    Returns
    -------
    Any
        The task's config instance.
    """
    modifier_kwargs = modifier_kwargs or {}
    config = TASK_REGISTRY.build(task_name, **modifier_kwargs)
    if config_path:
        config = _apply_config_file(config, config_path, task_name=task_name, modifier_kwargs=modifier_kwargs)
    for overrides in config_overrides or ():
        config = config.with_overrides_from_dict(overrides)
    _apply_run_name(config, run_name)
    return config

def get_task_config_from_args(args: argparse.Namespace, run_name: str = "") -> Any:
    """Build a task config from an argparse Namespace produced by :func:`get_task_argparser`."""
    config = get_task_config(
        args.task,
        run_name=run_name,
        modifier_kwargs=_collect_modifier_kwargs(args, args.task),
        config_path=args.config,
        config_overrides=overrides_from_args(args),
    )

    runner_options = getattr(config, "runner_options", None)
    if runner_options is not None:
        if eden_dist.is_distributed():
            # Each rank sees one isolated GPU as cuda:0 via CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES;
            # "auto" resolves to that through gs.device, keeping device selection
            # uniform with the non-DDP path.
            runner_options.device = "auto"
        if args.cpu:
            runner_options.device = "cpu"
    return config

def read_config_arg(path: str) -> dict:
    """Read the ``--config`` argument — :func:`read_config_file` plus the CLI's own redirect.

    The two flags each take what the other rejects, so each names the other when handed it:
    ``--override <a path>`` already points at ``--config``, and this is the mirror. The
    redirect fires on a *positive* identification — the value is something ``--override``
    itself would accept — not on a guess about the string, so a genuine path with the wrong
    extension (or unreadable contents) still gets the plain message.

    Parameters
    ----------
    path: str
        The ``--config`` value.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        The file's contents, as :func:`read_config_file` returns them.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        Naming ``--override`` when ``path`` is an inline mapping; otherwise unchanged from
        :func:`read_config_file`.
    """
    try:
        return read_config_file(path)
    except ValueError as e:
        if not _is_inline_mapping(path):
            raise  # a real path, just not one we can read — its own message is the right one
        raise ValueError(
            f"--config takes a .json/.yaml/.yml path, but {path!r} is an inline mapping. Pass it to --override instead."
        ) from e

def explicit_task_mods(task_name: str, modifier_kwargs: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:
    """Return the ``--`` flags for task mods set away from their default.

    The comparison baseline is ``getattr(mod, field_name)`` — the mod *instance's* value,
    which is exactly what :func:`_add_mod_field_to_parser` uses as the argparse default (not
    the ``__init__`` signature default, which can differ when a task registers a mod with an
    overridden instance value). So a flag left unset — or passed at its default — reads as
    *not* explicitly set.

    Used to fail fast wherever mods collide with a config that is authoritative on its own
    (a saved ``--config``, a checkpoint's sibling ``config.json``) and would otherwise be
    silently ignored.

    Parameters
    ----------
    task_name: str
        The registered task whose mods to compare against.
    modifier_kwargs: dict[str, Any]
        Flag-keyed mod values, as produced by :func:`_collect_modifier_kwargs`.

    Returns
    -------
    list[str]
        The dash-prefixed flag names that differ from their default.
    """
    if not task_name or task_name not in TASK_REGISTRY:
        return []
    changed = []
    for mod in TASK_REGISTRY.get_modifiers(task_name):
        for field_name, _annotation, _default, _help in cli_fields(type(mod)):
            flag = mod.flag_for(field_name)
            if flag in modifier_kwargs and modifier_kwargs[flag] != getattr(mod, field_name):
                changed.append(f"--{flag}")
    return changed

docs.title: ReferenceSource
docs.text:
Bases: StrEnum

Source of the reference offset added on top of the joint PD controller setpoint.

The offset is added on top of raw_action * scale + offset by the joint PD controllers in :mod:eden.managers.terms.actions.joint_actions.

Options

ZERO: no reference offset. DEFAULT: the entity's default_dofs_pos for the controlled DOFs. MOTION_REF: per-step joint position read from the motion manager (env.motion_manager.data[entity_name].dofs_pos[:, 0, :]); used for residual policies that learn deltas on top of a retargeted demonstration. DELTA: per-step joint position captured from the entity at the start of each control step (entity.get_dofs_pos(...)); the action is then a delta on top of the previous step's DOF position. Constant across decimation substeps. ACCUMULATE: the action is integrated onto a persistent target, target_t = clamp(target_{t-1} + raw * scale, soft_pos_limits), starting from and reset to default_dofs_pos. Unlike DELTA (which re-reads the measured DOF position each step), the target accumulates across steps. The action manager keeps the raw delta, so obs/reward terms read it directly. Requires offset == 0 and a position controller.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
Motion datasets load human or robot motion (motion capture, retargeted clips, hand-object recordings) into the BatchMotionSequence layout the motion manager plays back. Each loader is a DatasetBase subclass that fetches its files, parses them, caches the result and applies DatasetModifiers. The motion datasets guide covers downloading, licences and the runnable examples.

from eden.datasets import DATASET_REGISTRY, LAFAN1RetargetedG1Dataset
from eden.options.datasets import DatasetOptions

Datasets and modifiers register under a snake-case key derived from the class name.

Re-estimate velocities by finite differences of the (retimed) positions instead of carrying the source velocities through. Defaults to True.

TYPE: bool

Refuse a cache that predates one of _cache_identity_fields (its value is unknown); False accepts it with a warning. A differing value always raises. Defaults to True.

TYPE: bool

Also load the parametric body-model pose and shape (MANO / SMPL family) of the sequences that have one, as body_pose_quat / body_shape / body_model. Off by default: nothing extra is read, stored or cached, and no simulation-side buffer ever holds them. Only datasets that declare support take it (_supports_body_model_params); a cache prepared without it is refused rather than loaded short.

TYPE: bool

body_model_dir

Directory of the body-model files (e.g. MANO_RIGHT.pkl / MANO_LEFT.pkl), for datasets that need the model to read a release (expanding a PCA pose, locating the root joint). The files are licence-gated and never shipped.

TYPE: str | None

Class Attributes

file_extension: str The extension of the motion files. motion_sequence_keys: tuple[str, ...] The distinct names of the actors present in the dataset. motion_dofs_name: dict[str, list[str]] Per actor (motion_sequence_keys entry), the names of the stored dofs_pos columns, in order. motion_links_name: dict[str, list[str]] Per actor, the names of the stored link rows, in order. _hf_allow_patterns: tuple[str, ...] | None Glob patterns limiting what the automatic download fetches from the HF repo. None fetches the whole repo. Set this when the repo holds splits this loader never reads. _hf_data_subdir: str | None Directory inside the downloaded (and, if applicable, unpacked) repo that holds this loader's motion files, as a relative /-separated path. None reads the repo root.

Notes

The automatic download runs three independent stages, each opt-in: _hf_allow_patterns decides what is fetched, _post_download_process unpacks archives in place and returns the root, and _hf_data_subdir narrows that root to the directory this loader reads. Only the download path goes through them — an explicit raw_data_path is used as given, so it must already point at the equivalent of the narrowed directory.

The two layout attributes are private class attributes, not options: a repo's layout belongs to the loader that reads it, so a retarget for another robot or split is a subclass declaring its own. Both are checked when the class is defined.

def select_trajectories(self, trajectories_idx: torch.Tensor | list[int] | slice) -> None:
    """Select a subset of trajectories from the loaded dataset, discarding the rest.

    Parameters
    ----------
    trajectories_idx : torch.Tensor | list[int] | slice
        The trajectory indices to keep.
    """
    for key in self.motion_sequence_keys:
        self.motion_sequences[key] = self.motion_sequences[key].select(trajectories_idx)

    if isinstance(trajectories_idx, torch.Tensor):
        trajectories_idx = trajectories_idx.tolist()
    elif isinstance(trajectories_idx, slice):
        trajectories_idx = list(range(len(self.all_motion_files)))[trajectories_idx]

    self.metadata["all_motion_files"] = [self.metadata["all_motion_files"][i] for i in trajectories_idx]
    self.all_motion_files = [self.all_motion_files[i] for i in trajectories_idx]
    for key in self._PER_CLIP_METADATA_KEYS:
        value = self.metadata.get(key)
        if value is None:
            continue
        self.metadata[key] = (
            value[trajectories_idx] if isinstance(value, np.ndarray) else [value[i] for i in trajectories_idx]
        )

def motion_labels(self, key: str) -> list[str]:
    """The per-clip label list ``self.metadata[key]``, one entry per loaded trajectory.

    Parameters
    ----------
    key : str
        A per-clip metadata key the dataset declares in ``_PER_CLIP_METADATA_KEYS`` (e.g. ``"objects"``).
    """
    if key not in self._PER_CLIP_METADATA_KEYS or key not in self.metadata:
        raise KeyError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} has no per-clip metadata {key!r}; its per-clip keys are "
            f"{list(self._PER_CLIP_METADATA_KEYS)} (metadata present: {sorted(self.metadata)})"
        )
    labels = [str(v) for v in self.metadata[key]]
    if len(labels) != len(self):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(self).__name__}.metadata[{key!r}] has {len(labels)} entries but the dataset holds {len(self)} "
            f"trajectories; per-clip metadata must stay aligned with the trajectories."
        )
    return labels

margin_overrides

Pass {"tx": 0.2, "ty": 0.2, "tz": 0.2, "roll": 0.5, "pitch": 0.5, "yaw": 0.5} to mirror dexmachina exactly.

TYPE: dict[str, float] | None DEFAULT: None

RAISES DESCRIPTION KeyError if ``entity_name`` is not a registered motion sequence key. ValueError if the entity has no ``dofs_pos`` data, zero DOFs, or ``motion_dofs_name`` desynchronized from ``dofs_pos`` (a name list that does not name every column). Source code in eden/datasets/base.py 
def compute_dofs_pos_range(
    self,
    entity_name: str,
    *,
    margin: float = 0.15,
    margin_overrides: dict[str, float] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, tuple[float, float]]:
    """Per-DOF ``(min - m, max + m)`` over every loaded demo frame.

    Mirrors dexmachina's ``demo_data.get_joint_init_limits`` (the ``limits`` half).
    Output keys come from ``self.motion_dofs_name[entity_name]``; values are
    plain Python floats so the dict can be passed to
    ``EntityOptions.soft_dofs_pos_limits`` without binding to a device at
    config time.

    Configuration-time only: forces a GPU→CPU sync via ``.cpu().tolist()``,
    so callers should resolve the dict once during config build (not per
    step).

    Parameters
    ----------
    entity_name:
        Key into ``self.motion_sequences``.
    margin:
        Default pad applied to both ends. Dexmachina's default is 0.15.
    margin_overrides:
        Substring → margin. If a DOF name *contains* a key, its value
        replaces ``margin`` for that DOF. When more than one substring
        matches a single DOF the last one wins, and a config-time warning
        is logged. Pass
        ``{"tx": 0.2, "ty": 0.2, "tz": 0.2, "roll": 0.5, "pitch": 0.5, "yaw": 0.5}``
        to mirror dexmachina exactly.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError if ``entity_name`` is not a registered motion sequence key.
    ValueError if the entity has no ``dofs_pos`` data, zero DOFs, or
    ``motion_dofs_name`` desynchronized from ``dofs_pos`` (a name list
    that does not name every column).
    """
    bms, names = self._validate_dofs_motion(entity_name)
    flat = bms.dofs_pos.concatenated_tensor  # (total_frames, num_dofs)
    lo = flat.amin(dim=0).cpu().tolist()
    hi = flat.amax(dim=0).cpu().tolist()
    margins = self._resolve_dof_margins(names, margin, margin_overrides)
    return {n: (lo_i - m, hi_i + m) for n, lo_i, hi_i, m in zip(names, lo, hi, margins, strict=True)}

Per-DOF qpos at frame of demo sequence sequence_idx.

Companion to :meth:compute_dofs_pos_range for the per-clip default_dofs_pos override (dexmachina set_custom_init_qpos). Defaults to the first frame of the first loaded sequence — the dexmachina convention is one clip per task, so this is the common case. When the dataset holds multiple clips, pass sequence_idx to pick the one this task config targets; TaskMod configs select a clip explicitly.

Configuration-time only: forces a GPU→CPU sync via .cpu().tolist(), so callers should resolve the dict once during config build (not per step).

Returns {dof_name: q} as plain Python floats.

RAISES DESCRIPTION KeyError if ``entity_name`` is not a registered motion sequence key. ValueError on any of: no ``dofs_pos`` data, ``motion_dofs_name`` desynchronized from ``dofs_pos`` (a name list that does not name every column), or ``frame`` / ``sequence_idx`` negative or out of range. Dataset-level desync is checked **before** ``frame`` / ``sequence_idx`` bounds so the deeper config error surfaces first. Source code in eden/datasets/base.py 
def compute_dofs_pos_at(self, entity_name: str, *, frame: int = 0, sequence_idx: int = 0) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Per-DOF qpos at ``frame`` of demo sequence ``sequence_idx``.

    Companion to :meth:`compute_dofs_pos_range` for the per-clip
    ``default_dofs_pos`` override (dexmachina ``set_custom_init_qpos``).
    Defaults to the first frame of the first loaded sequence — the
    dexmachina convention is one clip per task, so this is the common
    case. When the dataset holds multiple clips, pass ``sequence_idx`` to
    pick the one this task config targets; ``TaskMod`` configs select a clip
    explicitly.

    Configuration-time only: forces a GPU→CPU sync via ``.cpu().tolist()``,
    so callers should resolve the dict once during config build (not per
    step).

    Returns ``{dof_name: q}`` as plain Python floats.

    Raises
    ------
    KeyError if ``entity_name`` is not a registered motion sequence key.
    ValueError on any of: no ``dofs_pos`` data, ``motion_dofs_name``
    desynchronized from ``dofs_pos`` (a name list that does not name every column),
    or ``frame`` / ``sequence_idx`` negative or out of range. Dataset-level
    desync is checked **before** ``frame`` / ``sequence_idx`` bounds so the
    deeper config error surfaces first.
    """
    if frame < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"frame must be >= 0, got {frame}")
    if sequence_idx < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"sequence_idx must be >= 0, got {sequence_idx}")
    bms, names = self._validate_dofs_motion(entity_name)
    num_seqs = int(bms.buffer_length.numel())
    if sequence_idx >= num_seqs:
        raise ValueError(
            f"sequence_idx {sequence_idx} out of range; entity '{entity_name}' has {num_seqs} sequence(s)."
        )
    seq_len = int(bms.buffer_length[sequence_idx].item())
    if frame >= seq_len:
        raise ValueError(
            f"frame {frame} is out of range for sequence {sequence_idx} of "
            f"entity '{entity_name}' (buffer_length={seq_len})."
        )
    # (num_dofs,) at the chosen (sequence, frame); mask is scalar True after the bounds check.
    qpos_t, _ = bms.dofs_pos.get_with_mask((sequence_idx, frame))
    qpos = qpos_t.cpu().tolist()
    return dict(zip(names, qpos, strict=True))

Each per-key state_dict is produced by BatchMotionSequence.to_state_dict() and contains only tensors and primitive Python types — no custom objects — so the file is torch.load(mmap=True)-loadable.
