def source_positions(self) -> torch.Tensor:
    """``(B, n_src, 3)`` world position of every emission point, parallel to :attr:`src_hist`.

    An emission point rides its link with the offset rotated into the link's frame; a static one sits at its
    offset. Poses are the solver-frame ones (``relative=False``), matching ``eden.entities.sensor.Sensor``.
    """
    self._assert_active("source_positions")
    pos = self._src_offset.clone()
    if self._attached_cols.numel() > 0:
        solver = self._sim.rigid_solver
        links_pos = solver.get_links_pos(links_idx=self._attached_links)
        links_quat = solver.get_links_quat(links_idx=self._attached_links)
        if solver.n_envs == 0:
            links_pos, links_quat = links_pos[None], links_quat[None]
        pos[:, self._attached_cols] = links_pos + transform_by_quat(pos[:, self._attached_cols], links_quat)
    return pos

def blocks_since(self, last_render: int, who: str) -> int:
    """Blocks synthesized since a consumer last rendered at ``n_updates == last_render``; warn once if over 1.

    A consumer reads the newest block, so one render per :meth:`update` yields a continuous signal. Eden's
    default ``EnvOptions.update_sensors_every_substep=False`` skips sensor updates on intermediate decimation
    sub-steps, so with ``decimation=4`` a sensor renders every fourth block and its ``read()`` is a gapped
    stream — fine as an observation, wrong as a recording. That distinction is invisible in the data, and
    the decimation is Eden's, which a Genesis sensor cannot see at build, so say so on the first gapped render.

    Parameters
    ----------
    last_render : int
        :attr:`n_updates` as it stood at the consumer's previous render.
    who : str
        Name of the consuming sensor's options class, for the warning.
    """
    n_blocks = self._n_updates - last_render
    if n_blocks > 1 and not self._warned_gapped:
        self._warned_gapped = True
        en.logger.warning(
            f"{who} is rendered once per {n_blocks} synthesized audio blocks, so read() is a gapped stream "
            "rather than continuous sound. Propagation delay, attenuation and Doppler stay correct (the delay "
            "line advances every step), and this is harmless when the signal is an observation. Set "
            "EnvOptions.update_sensors_every_substep=True to render every block, e.g. when writing the signal "
            "to an audio file."
        )
    return n_blocks

    """
    if not self._active:
        return
    for source in self._sources:
        source.reset(envs_idx)
    if self._src_hist.numel() > 0:
        self._src_hist[slice(None) if envs_idx is None else envs_idx] = 0.0

docs.title: Microphone
docs.text:
Airborne point microphone: the rendering stage of the audio pipeline.

Provenance

Ported from neuroagents-lab/tactile-genesis @ 3023bcd (Genesis/genesis/engine/sensors/spatial_audio.py), where it is a Genesis in-tree sensor reading a scene-level AudioManager. Here it renders :class:~eden.engine.sensors.audio.AudioContext instead, which needs no Genesis change; see :mod:eden.engine.sensors.audio.

Deviations from upstream: enable_occlusion is dropped (upstream declares it and never reads it); attenuation is a Literal rather than a free str whose typos fell back to inverse; the sample history lives on the context, not the microphone; and the link attachment goes through Genesis' KinematicSensorMixin, so pos_offset is link-local and set_pos_offset works as on any other sensor.

Limitation: free-field propagation only — no occlusion, no reflections, no room response. A microphone behind a wall hears the source as if the wall were not there.

docs.title: SpatialAudio
docs.text:
Bases: KinematicSensorOptionsMixin['SpatialAudioSensor'], SimpleSensorOptions['SpatialAudioSensor']

A mono point microphone that hears every audio source registered with the scene.

read() returns (B, audio_substeps): this step's block of samples, one microphone signal per environment. Sources are summed with ref_distance-referenced distance attenuation and delayed by distance / speed_of_sound through a fractional delay line.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION entity_idx

Global entity index the microphone rides. -1 pins it in the world at pos_offset.

TYPE: int

link_idx_local

Local link index on that entity.

TYPE: int

pos_offset

Microphone position: in the link's frame when attached, world when static.

TYPE: array - like[float, float, float]

euler_offset

Accepted for parity with other link-attached sensors; a mono point microphone has no direction, so it does not change what is heard.

TYPE: array - like[float, float, float]

audio_substeps

Samples rendered per physics step. Must match every source in the scene; the effective sample rate is audio_substeps / sim_dt.

TYPE: int

speed_of_sound

Propagation speed in m/s, setting the delay per meter. Default 343.0 (air, ~20 °C).

TYPE: float

ref_distance

Distance in meters at which a source is heard at unit gain. Attenuation is clamped closer than this, so a source passing through the microphone stays finite. Default 0.1.

TYPE: float

attenuation

Falloff with distance. 'inverse' is ref/r (sound pressure, the physical free-field law and the usual choice); 'inverse_square' is (ref/r)**2, falling off faster.

TYPE: (inverse, inverse_square) DEFAULT: 'inverse'

enable_doppler

Ramp delay and attenuation across each block from last step's value to this step's, which pitch-shifts a source in relative motion. Costs nothing extra; disable for a static rig.

TYPE: bool

max_delay

Longest propagation delay to keep history for, in seconds. Sources farther than max_delay * speed_of_sound are heard at that clamped delay rather than their true one. Sizes the delay line, so raise it only as far as the scene needs. Default 0.03 (~10 m).

TYPE: float

Examples:

A microphone on a robot's head, hearing its own motors:

>>> from eden.options import SensorOptions
>>> from eden.engine.sensors.spatial_audio import SpatialAudio
>>> mic = SensorOptions(
...     sensor=SpatialAudio(audio_substeps=20, ref_distance=0.2),
...     attach_entity_name="robot",
...     attach_link_name="head_link",
... )

Per-class state of every :class:SpatialAudioSensor, batched so one pass renders them all.

The listener parameters are grown one column per sensor at build, alongside the link buckets and offsets of KinematicSensorMetadataMixin. prev_dist also depends on the source count, which is only final once every source has registered, so it is allocated on the first render instead. The sample history itself is not here: it belongs to :class:~eden.engine.sensors.audio.AudioContext, which advances it every simulation step whether or not a microphone renders.

Renders :class:~eden.engine.sensors.audio.AudioContext into one microphone signal per listener.

For each (listener, source) pair the current distance gives an attenuation and a delay in samples; the delay indexes the per-source sample history with linear interpolation between the two straddling samples, and the results are summed over sources. Interpolating the delay across the block from its value one simulation step ago to its current one is what produces Doppler: a shrinking delay reads the history faster than real time, raising the pitch.

Claim the scene's sample rate and append this listener's column.

def build(self):
    """Claim the scene's sample rate and append this listener's column."""
    super().build()

    sm = self._shared_metadata
    context = self._shared_context
    # A microphone alone in the scene is valid (it renders silence), so activate rather than
    # register: activation is what a *consumer* of the registry declares.
    context.activate()
    context.require_audio_substeps(self._options.audio_substeps, type(self._options).__name__)

    sm.speed_of_sound = concat_with_tensor(sm.speed_of_sound, self._options.speed_of_sound)
    sm.ref_distance = concat_with_tensor(sm.ref_distance, self._options.ref_distance)
    sm.inverse_square = concat_with_tensor(sm.inverse_square, self._options.attenuation == "inverse_square")
    sm.doppler = concat_with_tensor(sm.doppler, self._options.enable_doppler)

    K = self._options.audio_substeps
    if sm.ramp.numel() == 0:
        sm.ramp = (torch.arange(1, K + 1, device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float) / K).view(1, 1, 1, K)
        sm.age = torch.arange(K - 1, -1, -1, device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float).view(1, 1, 1, K)

    # The delay line must span this listener's longest delay plus the block it renders.
    dt_sub = self._manager._sim.dt / K
    delay_samples = int(self._options.max_delay / dt_sub) + 2
    context.require_history(K + delay_samples)

docs.title: Live playback
docs.text:
Listen to an audio sensor while the simulation runs.

:class:LiveAudioPlayer streams the blocks an audio sensor's read() returns to the sound card, one block per simulation step, so a scene can be heard as it is watched. It needs no Python audio package: the samples are piped as raw PCM into whichever command-line player the machine already has (aplay or ffplay).

Hearing the simulation in sync means running it in real time, and the player is what enforces that:

  • A simulation faster than real time is slowed down. :meth:LiveAudioPlayer.write sleeps until the sound card is about to need the block, keeping only lead seconds queued. Without that the pipe would swallow seconds of audio ahead of the picture.
  • A simulation slower than real time cannot be helped — the sound card runs dry. Each time it does, the player counts a dropout and rebuilds its cushion of silence, so one slow step costs one short gap instead of leaving the stream on the edge of crackling from then on. :meth:LiveAudioPlayer.close reports the count, so "did it keep up" is a number rather than an impression.

The cushion is the whole of the delay this module adds, because the players are told not to add their own. Left at their defaults they would: a stock aplay holds back 0.5 s of audio before it starts and stays that far behind (measured: 680 ms), ffplay 2 s. So aplay is given a buffer no deeper than lead and ffplay its low-delay flags, which leaves lead plus the sound server's own few tens of milliseconds. :meth:LiveAudioPlayer.close measures that figure — how long the player keeps sounding after the last block — and reports it. SoX's play is not tried: a play on PATH is not reliably SoX, and its latency was never measured here.

Eden's interactive viewer already paces env.step() to sim_dt, so a scene light enough to hold that rate plays cleanly with the viewer open. It also needs one read() per simulation step (decimation=1); see the engine addons guide on gapped reads.

This module is not imported by :mod:eden.engine.sensors and installs no sensor.

docs.title: LiveAudioPlayer
docs.text:
LiveAudioPlayer(sample_rate: int, gain: float = 1.0, lead: float = 0.06, command: tuple[str, ...] | None = None)

Stream mono float blocks to the sound card in real time, through a command-line player.

Use as a context manager around the simulation loop::

with LiveAudioPlayer(sample_rate=16000, gain=0.2) as speaker:
    for _ in range(steps):
        env.step()
        speaker.write(env.sensors["mic"].read()[0])

A recording can be peak-normalized after the fact; a live stream cannot, since the peak is not known yet. The samples are scaled by a fixed gain instead and soft-limited with tanh, so a louder moment than expected saturates smoothly rather than wrapping around.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION sample_rate

Samples per second: audio_substeps / sim_dt of the sensor being played.

TYPE: int

gain

Scale from the sensor's arbitrary units to full scale [-1, 1], applied before the soft limiter.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

lead

Seconds of audio kept queued ahead of the sound card, which is also how far the sound trails the simulation. Larger rides out slower steps without a dropout; smaller keeps the sound closer to the picture.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 0.06

command

Player command reading raw mono S16_LE PCM from stdin, with {rate} standing for the sample rate and {buffer_us} for lead in microseconds. It must not buffer ahead by itself, or the sound will trail by that much more. None picks the first of aplay and ffplay found on PATH.

TYPE: tuple[str, ...] | None DEFAULT: None

ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION dropouts

Times a block arrived after the queue had run dry, i.e. audible gaps so far.

TYPE: int

trailing

Seconds the player kept sounding after the last block was written, measured by :meth:close: how far the sound trailed the simulation. About lead plus the sound server's latency when the player is well behaved.

TYPE: float

Source code in eden/engine/sensors/playback.py 
def __init__(self, sample_rate: int, gain: float = 1.0, lead: float = 0.06, command: tuple[str, ...] | None = None):
    if command is None:
        command = next((player for player in _PLAYERS if shutil.which(player[0])), None)
        if command is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"No command-line audio player found; looked for {[player[0] for player in _PLAYERS]} on PATH. "
                "Install one (ALSA's aplay or ffmpeg's ffplay), or pass `command`."
            )
    self._command = [part.format(rate=sample_rate, buffer_us=round(lead * 1e6)) for part in command]
    self._sample_rate = sample_rate
    self._gain = gain
    self._lead = lead
    self._process = subprocess.Popen(self._command, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE)
    self._started_at: float | None = None
    self._seconds_written = 0.0  # of the caller's audio; the silences this player inserts are not counted
    self.dropouts = 0
    self._last_write_at: float | None = None
    self.trailing = 0.0

docs.text:
write(block: Tensor | ndarray) -> None

Queue one block, first sleeping until the sound card is lead seconds from needing it.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION block

Mono float samples of one environment, any shape; flattened in order.

TYPE: Tensor | ndarray

Source code in eden/engine/sensors/playback.py 
def write(self, block: "torch.Tensor | np.ndarray") -> None:
    """Queue one block, first sleeping until the sound card is ``lead`` seconds from needing it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    block : torch.Tensor | np.ndarray
        Mono float samples of one environment, any shape; flattened in order.
    """
    if isinstance(block, torch.Tensor):
        block = block.detach().cpu().numpy()
    samples = np.tanh(self._gain * np.asarray(block, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1))

    # The queue holds `lead + due_in` seconds: the sound card has consumed `now - started_at` of the
    # `lead + seconds_written` handed over so far.
    block_seconds = samples.size / self._sample_rate
    now = time.perf_counter()
    ran_dry = self._started_at is not None and self._started_at + self._seconds_written - now < -self._lead
    if self._started_at is None or ran_dry:
        # Open with `lead` seconds of silence. That is the cushion: while the simulation keeps up the queue holds
        # `lead` seconds, and a slow step eats into it instead of into the sound. Once it is used up, start over.
        self.dropouts += ran_dry
        self._started_at = now - self._seconds_written
        samples = np.concatenate((np.zeros(round(self._lead * self._sample_rate)), samples))
    due_in = self._started_at + self._seconds_written - now
    if due_in > 0.0:
        time.sleep(due_in)

    try:
        self._process.stdin.write((samples * 32767.0).astype("<i2").tobytes())
        self._process.stdin.flush()
    except BrokenPipeError:
        stderr = self._process.stderr.read().decode(errors="replace").strip()
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Audio player `{' '.join(self._command)}` exited early: {stderr or 'no output'}"
        ) from None
    self._seconds_written += block_seconds
    self._last_write_at = time.perf_counter()

docs.text:
close() -> None

Let the queued audio finish, stop the player, and report how the simulation kept up.

Source code in eden/engine/sensors/playback.py 
def close(self) -> None:
    """Let the queued audio finish, stop the player, and report how the simulation kept up."""
    if self._process.stdin.closed:
        return
    try:
        self._process.stdin.close()
    except BrokenPipeError:
        pass
    self._process.wait()
    self._process.stderr.close()
    # The player exits once the last sample has sounded, so how long it outlives the last write is how far the
    # sound was trailing: the cushion plus whatever the player and the sound server buffer.
    self.trailing = time.perf_counter() - self._last_write_at if self._last_write_at is not None else 0.0

    en.logger.info(
        f"🔈 played {self._seconds_written:.2f} s of audio with {self.dropouts} dropouts, trailing the simulation "
        f"by ~{1e3 * self.trailing:.0f} ms"
    )
    if self.dropouts:
        en.logger.warning(
            f"The simulation fell behind real time {self.dropouts} times, each one a gap in the sound. Lighten "
            "the scene or raise `lead`, or write a WAV and listen afterwards."
        )

docs.title: MochiSolver
docs.text:
A fully implicit multi-physics solver hosted by Eden on stock Genesis: each substep solves one nonlinear system over the rigid and articulated bodies and the vertex positions of deformable ones (tetrahedral solids, thin shells, discrete elastic rods), with a smooth signed-distance penalty contact model. Eden installs it in a scene on the scene's first Mochi entity. Every entity in a Mochi scene, the ground plane included, takes a Mochi*MaterialOptions (material options), and the default contact stiffness needs eden.init(precision="64").

The Eden-side entity wrappers are MochiRigidEntity and MochiSoftEntity on the entities page.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Options configuring the MochiSolver.

Upstream Genesis declares a solver's options as a field of its SceneOptions; the MochiSolver is hosted by Eden, so its options class lives here and :func:eden.engine.solvers.mochi.hosting.install_mochi_solver hands it to the solver.

docs.title: MochiOptions
docs.text:
Bases: GravityMixin, TimeBasedMixin

Options configuring the MochiSolver.

MochiSolver is a fully-implicit solver: at every substep it solves a single nonlinear system in which the inertia of every rigid body and a smooth signed-distance penalty contact model (regularized Coulomb friction, viscous normal damping) are assembled together. There is no separate collision response stage: contact is re-detected at every Newton iterate and enters the same residual and Hessian as the inertia, which is what keeps large time steps stable and is the prerequisite for coupling deformable bodies into the same system without a coupler.

Note

Double precision (gs.init(precision="64")) is recommended. The default contact stiffness of 1e9 Pa/m combined with a 1 mm activation threshold makes the Newton system ill-conditioned in single precision.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION integrator

Time integration scheme: "backward_euler" (first order, strongly damped) or "bdf2" (second order, closer to energy-conserving; needs the previous two steps so the first step of a fresh or reset scene falls back to backward Euler). Defaults to "backward_euler".

TYPE: str

use_newton_euler_inertia

Whether the rotational inertia enters as the Newton-Euler residual I dw/dt + w x I w instead of the variational merit of the rotation. The merit form derives from a potential and is what the line search monitors; the Newton-Euler form is exact for gyroscopic effects but its Hessian is approximate. Defaults to False.

TYPE: bool

n_newton_iterations

Maximum number of Newton iterations per substep. Defaults to 4.

TYPE: int

newton_abs_tol

Absolute tolerance on the mass-weighted residual norm (unit acceleration under gravity gives a norm of order one). Defaults to 1e-3.

TYPE: float

newton_rel_tol

Relative tolerance on the mass-weighted residual norm with respect to its value at the first iteration. Defaults to 1e-6.

TYPE: float

explosion_control

Whether a substep whose residual grows beyond explosion_rel_tol times its initial value or beyond explosion_abs_tol is flagged as diverged: the affected environment is reset to its previous pose with zero velocity and an error is raised at the next error check. A NaN residual is flagged either way. Defaults to True.

TYPE: bool

explosion_abs_tol

Absolute residual norm above which the solve is considered diverged. Defaults to 1e9.

TYPE: float

explosion_rel_tol

Residual growth factor above which the solve is considered diverged. Defaults to 1e4.

TYPE: float

linesearch_type

Step acceptance rule: "residual_norm" accepts the first trial whose residual norm does not exceed the current one, "armijo" requires a sufficient decrease of the incremental potential (costs an extra energy assembly per trial), "none" always takes the full Newton step. Defaults to "residual_norm".

TYPE: str

n_linesearch_iterations

Maximum number of step reductions (by linesearch_alpha) per Newton iteration. The last trial is kept even if it did not improve. Defaults to 4.

TYPE: int

linesearch_alpha

Step size reduction factor between two line search trials. Defaults to 0.5.

TYPE: float

linesearch_wolfe1

Sufficient decrease parameter of the Armijo rule. Defaults to 1e-4.

TYPE: float

linear_solver

Linear solver for the Newton system: "ldlt" (dense Cholesky of every simulation island, exact, cubic in the number of degrees of freedom of the island), "pcg" (block-Jacobi preconditioned conjugate gradient, linear per iteration), or "auto" (dense when the largest island of the environment has at most dense_solver_max_dofs degrees of freedom, PCG otherwise). Bodies coupled by the contact candidates of the step form an island. Defaults to "auto".

TYPE: str

dense_solver_max_dofs

Largest island solved with the dense solver under "auto". Defaults to 50.

TYPE: int

dense_matrix_max_dofs

Largest total number of degrees of freedom for which the dense matrix of the system is allocated (memory quadratic in this number per environment); beyond it every environment is solved with PCG. Defaults to 256.

TYPE: int

n_pcg_iterations

Maximum number of conjugate gradient iterations. If None, the number of degrees of freedom capped at 500. Defaults to None.

TYPE: int

pcg_rel_tol

Relative tolerance of the conjugate gradient solve. Ignored under the "adaptive" tolerance strategy. Defaults to 1e-5.

TYPE: float

pcg_abs_tol

Absolute floor of the conjugate gradient stopping test, on the norm of the preconditioned residual (the residual scaled by the inverse of the Hessian diagonal, i.e. a displacement). A solve stops as soon as that norm drops below the floor, whatever the relative tolerance asks for; mochi's default. Set to 0 to disable. Defaults to 1e-9.

TYPE: float

linear_tolerance_strategy

How tightly each Newton step solves its linear system: "constant" always solves to pcg_rel_tol, so the accuracy of a substep is set by pcg_rel_tol and n_newton_iterations alone; "adaptive" starts each substep at a loose tolerance and tightens it as the nonlinear residual drops, spending far fewer conjugate gradient iterations per Newton step but leaving more truncation error in the step it takes, which can cost an extra Newton iteration on scenes that would otherwise converge in one. Prefer "adaptive" (mochi's default policy) when the conjugate gradient dominates the substep and a relative accuracy of order 1e-5 is enough, "constant" when accuracy per substep matters more than the cost of reaching it. Defaults to "adaptive".

TYPE: str

friction_model

Regularization of the Coulomb friction force around zero sliding velocity: "c1" has compact support (exact Coulomb beyond friction_falloff_vel), "cinf" is smooth everywhere (never exactly Coulomb, better conditioned). Defaults to "c1".

TYPE: str

use_fitted_friction_hessian

Whether the friction Hessian uses a quadratic fit that is the same in every tangential direction. The exact Hessian converges faster close to the solution but can stall the Newton iterations at the stick-slip transition. Defaults to True.

TYPE: bool

friction_with_collider_normal

Whether the friction plane is defined by the collider's distance gradient (True) or by the colliding surface normal (False). Defaults to True.

TYPE: bool

fade_friction

Whether friction fades out as the colliding surface normal and the collider gradient become aligned, i.e. as a sample point passes through the far side of a thin collider. Defaults to True.

TYPE: bool

implicit_normal_force_for_dissipation

Whether friction and damping scale with the normal force evaluated at the current iterate instead of the one recovered at the start of the step. The implicit form is required for an accurate coefficient of restitution through normal damping; the explicit form is cheaper and smoother. Defaults to False.

TYPE: bool

boundary_element_type

Quadrature rule placing contact sample points on the collision triangles: "P1Q1" (centroid), "P1Q3" (3 points per triangle, degree 2), "P1Q6" (6 points, degree 4). More points resolve contact patches better at a proportional cost. Defaults to "P1Q3".

TYPE: str

equality_stiffness

Stiffness of the penalty enforcing the equality constraints of the articulations (connect, weld and joint couplings; loop closures): the constraint violation is penalized by 0.5 * k * |c|^2. Defaults to 1e6.

TYPE: float

equality_damping

Damping of the equality constraint penalty, 0.5 * (d / dt) * |c - c_prev|^2. Defaults to 0.

TYPE: float

max_contact_pairs_per_env

Capacity of the list of (link, collider geom) pairs whose bounding boxes overlap within a substep. If None, the number of possible pairs. Defaults to None.

TYPE: int

broadphase_margin

Absolute padding of the per-step conservative bounding boxes in meters. Defaults to 0.01.

TYPE: float

spatial_hash_bins_per_item

Bins of the spatial hash that locates the collider spheres of shells and rods per inserted sphere, rounded up to a power of two; more bins shorten the chains a query walks at the cost of memory (4 bytes per bin per environment). The tetrahedra of solids use a bounding-box hierarchy instead. Defaults to 2.

TYPE: int

max_soft_hits_per_sample

Capacity of the list of contacts between deformable boundary samples and rigid colliders, per sample. Exceeding it halts the simulation with an error. Defaults to 2.

TYPE: int

max_deformable_collider_hits_per_query

Capacity of the list of contacts between sample points (rigid or deformable) and the tetrahedra of the deformable solid colliders, per sample point. Defaults to 2.

TYPE: int

max_point_cloud_hits_per_query

Capacity of the list of contacts between deformable samples and the collider spheres of shells and rods, per deformable sample (rigid samples get max_soft_hits_per_sample slots each). If None, 4 when a shell or rod has self-contact (a sample then sees the spheres of the opposing layer of its own body) and 2 otherwise; the capacity is a per-sample average over a shared list, and exceeding it halts with an error naming this option. Defaults to None.

TYPE: int

record_contacts

Whether individual contact points can be read back through entity.get_contacts(); their buffers are allocated at the first readback. Defaults to True.

TYPE: bool

use_sleeping

Whether bodies at rest are put to sleep: a sleeping body keeps its pose exactly and costs neither contact nor element work until an awake body comes near it or a setter changes its state, its controls, the gravity or the contact settings. It pays off for scenes with many settled objects. The cost is physical: slow motion stops for good, such as creep on a slope or the slow settling of a soft body, and the trajectory differs from a run without sleeping. Bodies under an active controller and rods never sleep. Defaults to False.

TYPE: bool

sleep_threshold

A step counts as at rest for a body when the solve reduced its residual by less than this factor from the warm start, which an unforced body at equilibrium does not improve on. Higher values sleep sooner. Only steps whose solve meets the Newton tolerances count: in single precision, a soft body at rest can stall just above the default newton_abs_tol and then never sleeps. A looser tolerance such as 5e-3 lets it sleep, at the cost of accuracy. Defaults to 0.5.

TYPE: float

sleep_min_steps

Consecutive steps at rest after which every body of an island at rest goes to sleep. Fewer steps sleep sooner but can freeze a body at the turning point of a slow swing. Defaults to 20.

TYPE: int

sleep_max_speed

Speed in m/s above which a body never counts as at rest, whatever its residual: it keeps a body coasting without forces (whose motion the BDF2 warm start predicts exactly) awake. Defaults to 1e-2.

TYPE: float

step_kernel

How a step is executed: "monolith" runs the whole step of every environment in one kernel (one thread per environment, one launch per step, no host round trips), "pipeline" runs each stage as its own kernel with the host driving the loops, "graph" runs the step as one graph-launched kernel whose Newton, line-search and conjugate-gradient loops run on the device with the stages parallel over items and environments (one launch per step). "auto" picks the monolith on the CPU (the pipeline for deformable scenes of at least 3000 vertices when several CPU threads run) and, on the GPU, for rigid scenes of at most 64 degrees of freedom, the pipeline otherwise. The graph kernel is opt-in: on GPUs without device-side graph conditionals (before compute capability 9.0) the runtime replays its loop bodies from the host with one flag readback per round, which runs at the pipeline's speed, and the single module compiles several times slower than the pipeline's kernels (minutes for a cloth with self-contact and an arm). Defaults to "auto".

TYPE: str

graph_pcg_unroll

Conjugate-gradient iterations per round of the graph step kernel's inner loop (each round costs one flag readback on GPUs without device-side graph conditionals; each unrolled iteration is compiled once more). Defaults to 1.

TYPE: int

joint_limit_stiffness

Stiffness in N/m (N*m/rad) of the penalty holding revolute and prismatic joints inside their range. Joint limits are soft: the violation at rest is the limit torque divided by this stiffness. Higher values reduce the violation but stiffen the Newton system. Defaults to 1e4 (the original engine defaults to 100).

TYPE: float

joint_limit_damping

Damping in Ns/m (Nm*s/rad) of the joint limit penalty, resisting the velocity of the violation. Defaults to 0.

Whether to batch link info. Defaults to False.

TYPE: bool

batch_joints_info

Whether to batch joint info. Defaults to False.

TYPE: bool

batch_dofs_info

Whether to batch DOF info. Defaults to False.

TYPE: bool

IK_max_targets

Maximum number of simultaneous target links of an inverse-kinematics solve (the scratch buffers are quadratic in it and allocated at the first solve). Defaults to 6.

docs.title: Base
docs.text:
Bases: Material[EntityT]

Base class of the materials simulated by the MochiSolver, holding the contact parameters they share.

Contact between two bodies is a smooth penalty on the signed distance of sample points placed on one body's collision surface to the other body's signed distance field (SDF). Every pair parameter is combined from the two bodies' values by geometric mean, except the smoothing distance, the activation threshold and the alignment threshold, which are read from the collider body alone.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION friction

Coulomb friction coefficient. Default is 0.5.

TYPE: float

penalty_coefficient

Contact stiffness in Pa/m: pressure per unit of penetration once the penalty ramp is fully active. Higher values reduce penetration at the cost of a stiffer, more ill-conditioned Newton system. Default is 1e9.

TYPE: float

penalty_smoothing_half_distance

Half-width in meters of the smooth ramp between zero contact pressure and the linear regime. The pressure ramps up over twice this distance below the activation threshold, so a wider ramp gives softer, better conditioned contact and a narrower one sharper contact onset. Default is 0.005.

TYPE: float

penalty_threshold

Signed distance in meters at which contact pressure starts to build up. Positive values start pushing bodies apart before they touch (a contact skin), negative values allow some interpenetration before responding. Default is 0.001.

TYPE: float

friction_falloff_vel

Sliding speed in m/s below which the Coulomb friction force is regularized towards zero. Larger values give smoother, more robust stick-slip transitions with more creep under static load; smaller values approach exact Coulomb friction with a stiffer system. Default is 0.01.

TYPE: float

viscous_friction

Tangential viscous friction coefficient in s/m, multiplying the normal force and the sliding velocity. Default is 0.

TYPE: float

normal_viscous_damping

Normal viscous damping coefficient in s/m, multiplying the normal force and the approach velocity. This is the mechanism controlling the coefficient of restitution: 0 gives fully elastic penalty contact, larger values dissipate more impact energy. Default is 0.

TYPE: float

max_alignment_normals

Cosine in [-1, 1] between the colliding surface normal and the collider gradient above which the contact is disabled, so that a body embedded past the far side of a thin collider can escape rather than being trapped. Default is 0.

TYPE: float

has_gravity

Whether gravity acts on this body. Default is True.

TYPE: bool

contact_layer

Name of the contact layer of this body. Contact between two layers can be disabled at the solver level. Default is "default".

TYPE: str

Note

This class should not be instantiated directly.

Thin shell (cloth-like) material simulated by the MochiSolver.

The surface triangles of the morph are the finite elements: a Saint Venant-Kirchhoff membrane on the metric of the mid-surface and a Koiter-type bending term on its discrete curvature, both thickness-integrated. docs.text:
resolve(radius)

Stiffnesses and inertia per unit length of a circular cross-section of the given radius; overrides win.

Source code in eden/engine/solvers/mochi/materials/rod.py 
def resolve(self, radius):
    """Stiffnesses and inertia per unit length of a circular cross-section of the given radius; overrides win."""
    area = np.pi * radius**2
    second_moment = np.pi * radius**4 / 4.0
    shear_modulus = self.E / (2.0 * (1.0 + self.nu))
    return {
        "axial_stiffness": self.axial_stiffness if self.axial_stiffness is not None else self.E * area,
        "flexural_stiffness": (
            self.flexural_stiffness if self.flexural_stiffness is not None else self.E * second_moment
        ),
        "torsional_stiffness": (
            self.torsional_stiffness
            if self.torsional_stiffness is not None
            else shear_modulus * 2.0 * second_moment
        ),
        "linear_density": self.linear_density if self.linear_density is not None else self.rho * area,
        "linear_rotational_inertia": (
            self.linear_rotational_inertia
            if self.linear_rotational_inertia is not None
            else self.rho * 2.0 * second_moment
        ),
    }

docs.title: Hosting on stock Genesis
docs.text:
Host the MochiSolver in a scene of stock Genesis.

Upstream Genesis has no seam for a solver it does not ship: Simulator.__init__ builds a fixed list of solvers, Scene.add_entity decides a surface's defaults from a closed chain of isinstance checks on the material, and the visualizer names each solver it draws. This module stands in for the edits a Genesis fork would make, one scene at a time and never on a class, so a scene without a Mochi entity runs exactly the upstream code:

  • :func:install_mochi_solver builds the solver and appends it to the simulator's solvers. From then on the scene takes Mochi materials in scene.add_entity, holds the solver as scene.mochi_solver, draws its bodies with the rasterizer, restores them on a reset and frees the solver's arrays with the scene, as a scene of the fork would. It refuses scene.export, which the fork allows: gs.Scene.load rebuilds a scene on stock Genesis, without the solver;
  • :func:create_mochi_scene is gs.Scene(..., mochi_options=...) of the fork: a new scene, installed;
  • :func:add_mochi_entity is what scene.add_entity does for a Mochi material;
  • :func:find_mochi_solver returns the solver of a scene, or None.

What the solver itself needs beyond this (registering its error flags, clearing them when an environment is reset) lives in :class:~eden.engine.solvers.mochi.mochi_solver.MochiSolver.

def find_mochi_solver(scene: Scene) -> MochiSolver | None:
    """The MochiSolver installed in ``scene``, or None if no Mochi entity was ever added to it."""
    for solver in scene.sim.solvers:
        if isinstance(solver, MochiSolver):
            return solver
    return None

Build a MochiSolver for scene and register it with its simulator, its visualizer and its reset.

Call it once per scene, before the scene is built and before any Mochi entity is added.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION scene

The unbuilt scene. Its renderer must be the rasterizer, the only one the solver is bound to.

TYPE: Scene

options

The solver's options. Their unset dt and gravity come from the scene's SimOptions.

TYPE: MochiOptions | None DEFAULT: None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION MochiSolver

The installed solver, also reachable as scene.mochi_solver.

Source code in eden/engine/solvers/mochi/hosting.py 
def install_mochi_solver(scene: Scene, options: MochiOptions | None = None) -> MochiSolver:
    """Build a MochiSolver for ``scene`` and register it with its simulator, its visualizer and its reset.

    Call it once per scene, before the scene is built and before any Mochi entity is added.

    Parameters
    ----------
    scene : Scene
        The unbuilt scene. Its renderer must be the rasterizer, the only one the solver is bound to.
    options : MochiOptions | None
        The solver's options. Their unset ``dt`` and ``gravity`` come from the scene's ``SimOptions``.

    Returns
    -------
    MochiSolver
        The installed solver, also reachable as ``scene.mochi_solver``.
    """
    if scene.is_built:
        gs.raise_exception("The MochiSolver must be installed before the scene is built.")
    if find_mochi_solver(scene) is not None:
        gs.raise_exception("This scene already has a MochiSolver: install it once, then add every Mochi entity to it.")
    renderer = scene.visualizer.raytracer or scene.visualizer.batch_renderer
    if renderer is not None:
        gs.raise_exception(
            f"The MochiSolver cannot be drawn by {type(renderer).__name__}: Eden binds it to the rasterizer only, "
            "which every camera of this scene would then skip. Pass `renderer=gs.renderers.Rasterizer()`, or render a "
            "Mochi scene with a Nyx camera (examples/recipes/mochi/_nyx.py)."
        )

    sim = scene.sim
    # SceneOptions fills the values a solver's options leave unset (dt, gravity) from SimOptions, for the solvers it
    # declares only.
    options = (options or MochiOptions()).model_copy_from(scene.options.sim)
    solver = MochiSolver(scene, sim, options)
    sim._solvers.append(solver)
    # The name a scene of the fork holds the solver under, which the code written for the fork reads.
    scene.mochi_solver = solver
    _bind_add_entity(scene)
    _bind_reset(sim, solver)
    _bind_destroy(sim, solver)
    _bind_rasterizer(scene, solver)
    _bind_export(scene)
    return solver

def create_mochi_scene(mochi_options: MochiOptions | None = None, **scene_kwargs) -> Scene:
    """A new ``gs.Scene(**scene_kwargs)`` with a MochiSolver installed (see :func:`install_mochi_solver`).

add_mochi_entity(scene: Scene, morph: Morph, material: Material, surface: Surface | None = None, visualize_contact: bool = False, vis_mode: str | None = None, name: str | None = None) -> Entity

Scene.add_entity for a Mochi material, on a scene :func:install_mochi_solver was called on.

The upstream Scene.add_entity cannot take one: its surface defaults end in a bare exception for the deformable materials, and Simulator._add_entity hands a Rigid to the RigidSolver, which declares the most derived class of the two that claim it. An installed scene's add_entity routes Mochi materials here.

Source code in eden/engine/solvers/mochi/hosting.py 
def add_mochi_entity(
    scene: Scene,
    morph: Morph,
    material: "Material",
    surface: "Surface | None" = None,
    visualize_contact: bool = False,
    vis_mode: str | None = None,
    name: str | None = None,
) -> "Entity":
    """``Scene.add_entity`` for a Mochi material, on a scene :func:`install_mochi_solver` was called on.

    The upstream ``Scene.add_entity`` cannot take one: its surface defaults end in a bare exception for the deformable
    materials, and ``Simulator._add_entity`` hands a ``Rigid`` to the RigidSolver, which declares the most derived
    class of the two that claim it. An installed scene's ``add_entity`` routes Mochi materials here.
    """
    solver = find_mochi_solver(scene)
    if solver is None:
        gs.raise_exception("No MochiSolver in this scene: call `install_mochi_solver(scene, options)` first.")
    if scene.is_built:
        gs.raise_exception("Entities can be added only before the scene is built.")
    if not isinstance(material, mochi_materials.Base):
        gs.raise_exception(f"`add_mochi_entity` takes a Mochi material, got {type(material).__name__}.")
    if visualize_contact:
        gs.raise_exception(
            "`visualize_contact` draws the RigidSolver's contacts only; a Mochi entity has none to draw."
        )

    if surface is None:
        surface = gs.surfaces.Default()
    if isinstance(morph, collections.abc.Iterable) and not isinstance(morph, Morph):
        morph = tuple(morph)
    if isinstance(morph[0] if isinstance(morph, tuple) else morph, (gs.morphs.Box, gs.morphs.Cylinder)):
        surface.smooth = False
    if surface.double_sided is None:
        surface.double_sided = isinstance(material, mochi_materials.Shell)
    if vis_mode is not None:
        surface.vis_mode = vis_mode
    if surface.vis_mode is None:
        surface.vis_mode = "visual"
    allowed = ("visual",) if isinstance(material, _SOFT_MATERIALS) else ("visual", "collision", "sdf")
    if surface.vis_mode not in allowed:
        gs.raise_exception(
            f"Unsupported `surface.vis_mode` for material {type(material).__name__}: '{surface.vis_mode}'. Expected "
            f"one of: {list(allowed)}."
        )
    # Mochi contact samples the authored collision triangles, so a file mesh is kept as it is unless asked otherwise.
    # The rigid-entity description would otherwise convexify it, since a `Mochi.Rigid` is a `Rigid`.
    for each_morph in morph if isinstance(morph, tuple) else (morph,):
        if isinstance(each_morph, gs.morphs.FileMorph) and each_morph.convexify is None:
            each_morph.convexify = False

    sim = scene.sim
    entity = solver.add_entity(sim.n_entities, material, morph, surface, visualize_contact, name=name, desc=None)
    sim._entities.append(entity)
    if entity.desc is not None:
        scene._desc.entities.append(entity.desc)
    return entity

docs.title: MochiSolver
docs.text:
MochiSolver(scene: Scene, sim: Simulator, options: MochiOptions)

Bases: GravityMixin, TimeBasedMixin, KinematicSolver

Fully-implicit multi-physics solver with smooth penalty contact.

Every substep solves one nonlinear system over the generalized coordinates of all rigid and articulated bodies and the vertex positions of all deformable bodies, whose residual is the gradient of an incremental potential (inertia, gravity, damping, elasticity and the contact penalty with its friction and damping terms) and whose Hessian is assembled from per-link, per-contact-pair and per-tetrahedron blocks. The solve is a damped Newton iteration with a line search; contact is re-detected at every iterate.

Source code in eden/engine/solvers/mochi/mochi_solver.py 
def __init__(self, scene: "Scene", sim: "Simulator", options: MochiOptions) -> None:
    super().__init__(scene, sim, options)
    self._options: MochiOptions = options
    self.sdf_info: array_class.SDFInfo | None = None
    self._is_contacts_recorded = False
    # Environments whose kinematic state was changed from outside the solver; their multistep history is rebuilt
    # at the start of the next step. Allocated at build, once the batch size is known.
    self._external_state_dirty_mask = None
    self._external_state_subscriber = Subscriber(
        frozenset({StateChange.GEOMETRY, StateChange.DYNAMICS}), callback=self._on_external_state_change
    )
    # Island node of every degree of freedom and the index of every node, for the setters to wake what they change.
    # Allocated at build when sleeping is enabled.
    self._dofs_node = None
    self._nodes_idx = None
    # Deformable bodies live outside the kinematic tree.
    self._soft_entities = gs.List()
    self.soft_info = None
    self.soft_state = None
    self._soft_vverts_render = None
    self._soft_vverts_vert_idx = None

def add_entity(self, idx, material, morph, surface, visualize_contact=False, name=None, desc=None):
    morphs = desc.morphs if desc is not None else ((morph,) if isinstance(morph, Morph) else tuple(morph))
    if len(morphs) > 1:
        gs.raise_exception("Heterogeneous morphs are not supported by the MochiSolver.")
    if isinstance(morphs[0], (gs.morphs.Terrain, gs.morphs.USD, gs.morphs.Drone)):
        gs.raise_exception(f"Morph {type(morphs[0]).__name__} is not supported by the MochiSolver.")

    if isinstance(material, (mochi_materials.Elastic, mochi_materials.Shell, mochi_materials.Rod)):
        is_rod = isinstance(material, mochi_materials.Rod)
        if not is_rod and not isinstance(
            morph, (gs.morphs.Box, gs.morphs.Sphere, gs.morphs.Cylinder, gs.morphs.Mesh)
        ):
            gs.raise_exception(
                f"Morph {type(morph).__name__} is not supported for deformable Mochi bodies (Box, Sphere, "
                "Cylinder or Mesh expected)."
            )
        if is_rod and not isinstance(morph, Rod):
            gs.raise_exception(
                "A `Rod` material (eden.engine.solvers.mochi.materials) requires a `Rod` morph "
                "(eden.engine.solvers.mochi.morphs)."
            )
        entity = MochiSoftEntity(
            scene=self._scene,
            solver=self,
            material=material,
            morph=morph,
            surface=surface,
            idx=idx,
            idx_in_solver=self.n_soft_entities,
            v_start=self.n_soft_verts,
            vvert_start=self.n_soft_vverts,
            vface_start=self.n_soft_vfaces,
            name=name,
        )
        self._soft_entities.append(entity)
        return entity

    return super().add_entity(idx, material, morph, surface, visualize_contact, name, desc)

def build(self):
    if self.is_active:
        other_solvers = [
            solver
            for solver in self.sim.solvers
            if solver is not self and solver.is_active and type(solver) is not KinematicSolver
        ]
        if other_solvers:
            gs.raise_exception(
                "MochiSolver cannot run alongside other physics solvers: "
                f"{[type(solver).__name__ for solver in other_solvers]}."
            )
        if self.sim.requires_grad:
            gs.raise_exception("MochiSolver does not support differentiable simulation.")

    self._n_geoms = self.n_geoms
    self._n_verts = self.n_verts
    self._n_free_verts = self.n_free_verts
    self._n_fixed_verts = self.n_fixed_verts
    self._n_faces = self.n_faces
    self._n_edges = self.n_edges
    self._geoms = self.geoms

    self.n_geoms_ = max(1, self.n_geoms)
    self.n_verts_ = max(1, self.n_verts)
    self.n_faces_ = max(1, self.n_faces)
    self.n_edges_ = max(1, self.n_edges)
    self.n_free_verts_ = max(1, self.n_free_verts)
    self.n_fixed_verts_ = max(1, self.n_fixed_verts)

    super().build()
    self._init_default_armature()
    self._external_state_dirty_mask = np.zeros((self._B,), dtype=bool)
    # Which of the two linear arms have environments to solve; refreshed at every substep by _select_linear_arms.
    self._has_dense_envs = False
    self._has_pcg_envs = False

    if not self.is_active:
        return

    self.n_soft_entities_ = max(1, self.n_soft_entities)
    self.n_soft_verts_ = max(1, self.n_soft_verts)
    self.n_soft_elems_ = max(1, self.n_soft_elems)
    self.n_shell_elems_ = max(1, self.n_shell_elems)
    self.n_rod_elems_ = max(1, self.n_rod_elems)
    self.n_rod_stencils_ = max(1, self.n_rod_stencils)
    self.n_attachments_ = max(1, self.n_attachments)
    self.n_dofs_total_ = max(1, self.n_dofs_total)

    if gs.qd_float == qd.f32 and any(
        entity.material.penalty_coefficient >= 1e8 for entity in (*self._entities, *self._soft_entities)
    ):
        gs.logger.warning(
            "MochiSolver runs in single precision with a contact stiffness of 1e8 Pa/m or more: the Newton system "
            "is ill-conditioned and contact accuracy degrades. Consider `gs.init(precision='64')`."
        )

    self._init_vert_fields()
    self._init_geom_fields()
    kernel_update_geoms(
        self._scene._envs_idx, self.dyn_state, self.dyn_info, self.rigid_info, self.rigid_config, True
    )
    self._init_mochi()
    # The base solver latches these flags at the end of each step and raises them at the start of the next, and a
    # setter of the state of some envs clears theirs (see Solver.register_errors)
    self.register_errors(
        self.data_manager.errno,
        {
            MochiErrorCode.OVERFLOW_MOCHI_CONTACT_PAIRS: (
                f"Exceeding max number of contact pairs ({self._max_pairs}). Please increase the value of "
                "MochiSolver's option 'max_contact_pairs_per_env'."
            ),
            MochiErrorCode.OVERFLOW_MOCHI_CONTACTS: (
                "Exceeding the capacity of a contact list: increase MochiSolver's option "
                "'max_soft_hits_per_sample', 'max_deformable_collider_hits_per_query' or "
                "'max_point_cloud_hits_per_query' (see `get_contact_capacity_usage()`). With "
                "record_contacts=True the rigid contact record (2 slots per sample, not configurable) can fill too."
            ),
            MochiErrorCode.MOCHI_DIVERGED: (
                "MochiSolver diverged: the residual of the implicit solve blew up. Reduce the time step or the "
                "contact stiffness, or increase 'n_newton_iterations'."
            ),
        },
    )
    self._init_soft()
    self._step_kernel = self._resolve_step_kernel()
    # loop counters of the graph step kernel (the same physical arrays every launch)
    self._newton_counter = qd.ndarray(qd.i32, shape=())
    self._round_counter = qd.ndarray(qd.i32, shape=())
    self._pcg_counter = qd.ndarray(qd.i32, shape=())
    # The contact points recorded for readback are allocated at the first readback (see `_record_contacts`).
    self.hit_readback = get_mochi_hit_readback(self, 1, 1, 1, 1)
    self._is_hit_readback_allocated = False
    self._links_entity_idx = np.array([link.entity.idx for link in self.links] or [-1], dtype=gs.np_int)
    self._geoms_link_idx = np.array([geom.link.idx for geom in self.geoms] or [-1], dtype=gs.np_int)
    self._soft_entities_idx = np.array([entity.idx for entity in self._soft_entities] or [-1], dtype=gs.np_int)
    links_node, dofs_node = self._island_nodes()
    self.island_state = get_mochi_island_state(self, links_node, dofs_node)
    if self._options.use_sleeping:
        self._dofs_node = torch.as_tensor(dofs_node, device=gs.device)
        n_nodes = len(self._entities) + len(self._soft_entities)
        self._nodes_idx = torch.arange(n_nodes, dtype=gs.tc_int, device=gs.device)
    self._init_sdf()
    self.subscribe(self._external_state_subscriber)
    kernel_reset_history(
        self._scene._envs_idx, self.dyn_state, self.dyn_info, self.mochi_info, self.mochi_state, self.rigid_config
    )
    self._forward_kinematics()

def substep_pre_coupling(self, f):
    if not self.is_active:
        return
    self._sync_external_state()
    if self._step_kernel == "graph":
        options = self._options
        n_linesearch = (
            0 if self.mochi_config.linesearch_type == LINESEARCH.NONE else options.n_linesearch_iterations
        )
        pcg_unroll = options.graph_pcg_unroll
        kernel_step_graph(
            self._newton_counter,
            self._round_counter,
            self._pcg_counter,
            self.dyn_state,
            self.dyn_info,
            self.rigid_info,
            self.sdf_info,
            self.geoms_init_AABB,
            self.mochi_info,
            self.mochi_state,
            self.contact_state,
            self.hit_readback,
            self.island_state,
            self.eq_info,
            self.eq_state,
            self.soft_info,
            self.soft_state,
            self.rigid_config,
            self.mochi_config,
            self.n_shell_elems > 0,
            self.n_rod_elems > 0,
            pcg_unroll,
            max(1, n_linesearch),
            self._dense_max_dofs,
            len(self._entities),
            options.n_newton_iterations,
            self._n_pcg_iterations,
            -(-self._n_pcg_iterations // pcg_unroll),
            self._max_samples_per_soft_entity,
            self._errno,
        )
        self._is_forward_pos_updated = True
        self._is_forward_vel_updated = True
        self._is_contacts_recorded = False
        return
    if self._step_kernel == "monolith":
        options = self._options
        n_linesearch = (
            0 if self.mochi_config.linesearch_type == LINESEARCH.NONE else options.n_linesearch_iterations
        )
        kernel_step_monolith(
            self.dyn_state,
            self.dyn_info,
            self.rigid_info,
            self.sdf_info,
            self.geoms_init_AABB,
            self.mochi_info,
            self.mochi_state,
            self.contact_state,
            self.hit_readback,
            self.island_state,
            self.eq_info,
            self.eq_state,
            self.soft_info,
            self.soft_state,
            self.rigid_config,
            self.mochi_config,
            self.n_shell_elems > 0,
            self.n_rod_elems > 0,
            max(1, n_linesearch),
            self._dense_max_dofs,
            len(self._entities),
            options.n_newton_iterations,
            self._n_pcg_iterations,
            self._max_samples_per_soft_entity,
            self._errno,
        )
        self._is_forward_pos_updated = True
        self._is_forward_vel_updated = True
        self._is_contacts_recorded = False
        return

    kernel_step_start(
        self.dyn_state,
        self.dyn_info,
        self.rigid_info,
        self.mochi_info,
        self.mochi_state,
        self.island_state,
        self.rigid_config,
        self.mochi_config,
    )
    if self.has_soft:
        kernel_soft_step_start(
            self.mochi_state, self.soft_info, self.soft_state, self.rigid_config, self.mochi_config
        )
        if self.n_shell_elems > 0:
            kernel_shell_stage_start(self.mochi_state, self.soft_info, self.soft_state, self.rigid_config)
        if self.n_rod_elems > 0:
            kernel_rod_step_start(
                self.mochi_state, self.soft_info, self.soft_state, self.rigid_config, self.mochi_config
            )
    self._forward_kinematics(with_velocity=False)
    kernel_store_stage_start_poses(self.dyn_state, self.mochi_state, self.rigid_config)
    if self.mochi_config.has_equalities:
        kernel_equalities_stage_start(
            self.dyn_info,
            self.rigid_info,
            self.mochi_info,
            self.mochi_state,
            self.eq_info,
            self.eq_state,
            self.rigid_config,
        )
    if self.mochi_config.has_attachments:
        kernel_attachments_stage_start(self.mochi_state, self.soft_info, self.soft_state, self.rigid_config)
    kernel_reset_newton(self.mochi_state, self.rigid_config)
    kernel_conservative_bounds(
        self.dyn_state, self.dyn_info, self.mochi_info, self.mochi_state, self.contact_state, self.rigid_config
    )
    kernel_broadphase_pairs(
        self.dyn_state,
        self.dyn_info,
        self.mochi_info,
        self.mochi_state,
        self.contact_state,
        self.rigid_config,
        self._errno,
    )
    if self.has_soft:
        kernel_soft_conservative_bounds(
            self.mochi_state, self.mochi_info, self.soft_info, self.soft_state, self.rigid_config
        )
        kernel_soft_broadphase(
            self.dyn_state,
            self.dyn_info,
            self.mochi_info,
            self.mochi_state,
            self.contact_state,
            self.soft_info,
            self.soft_state,
            self.rigid_config,
            self._errno,
        )
    kernel_build_islands(
        self.dyn_info,
        self.mochi_info,
        self.mochi_state,
        self.contact_state,
        self.soft_info,
        self.soft_state,
        self.island_state,
        self.eq_info,
        self._dense_max_dofs,
        len(self._entities),
        self.rigid_config,
        self.has_soft,
        self.mochi_config.has_dense,
        self.mochi_config.has_equalities,
        self.mochi_config.use_sleeping,
    )
    self._select_linear_arms()
    self._newton_solve()
    kernel_post_stage(
        self.dyn_state, self.dyn_info, self.rigid_info, self.mochi_info, self.mochi_state, self.rigid_config
    )
    if self.has_soft:
        kernel_soft_post_stage(self.mochi_state, self.soft_info, self.soft_state, self.rigid_config)
        if self.n_rod_elems > 0:
            kernel_rod_post_stage(self.mochi_state, self.soft_info, self.soft_state, self.rigid_config)
    if self.mochi_config.use_sleeping:
        kernel_update_sleep(
            len(self._entities),
            self.dyn_state,
            self.dyn_info,
            self.mochi_info,
            self.mochi_state,
            self.soft_info,
            self.soft_state,
            self.island_state,
            self.rigid_config,
            self.has_soft,
        )
    self._forward_kinematics()
    self._is_forward_pos_updated = True
    self._is_forward_vel_updated = True
    self._is_contacts_recorded = False

def get_state(self, f=None):
    if not self.is_active:
        return None
    state = MochiSolverState(self, self.sim.cur_step_global)
    kernel_get_kinematic_state(
        state.qpos,
        state.dofs_vel,
        state.links_pos,
        state.links_quat,
        self.dyn_state,
        self.rigid_info,
        self.rigid_config,
    )
    state.qpos_prev = qd_to_torch(self.mochi_state.qpos_prev, copy=True).permute((2, 0, 1)).contiguous()
    state.dofs_vel_prev = qd_to_torch(self.mochi_state.dofs_vel_prev, copy=True).permute((2, 0, 1)).contiguous()
    state.links_vel = qd_to_torch(self.mochi_state.links_vel, copy=True).permute((1, 0, 2)).contiguous()
    state.links_ang = qd_to_torch(self.mochi_state.links_ang, copy=True).permute((1, 0, 2)).contiguous()
    state.links_vsym = qd_to_torch(self.mochi_state.links_vsym, copy=True).permute((1, 0, 2, 3)).contiguous()
    state.links_vel_prev = (
        qd_to_torch(self.mochi_state.links_vel_prev, copy=True).permute((2, 0, 1, 3)).contiguous()
    )
    state.links_ang_prev = (
        qd_to_torch(self.mochi_state.links_ang_prev, copy=True).permute((2, 0, 1, 3)).contiguous()
    )
    state.links_vsym_prev = (
        qd_to_torch(self.mochi_state.links_vsym_prev, copy=True).permute((2, 0, 1, 3, 4)).contiguous()
    )
    state.n_hist = qd_to_torch(self.mochi_state.n_hist, copy=True)
    if self.has_soft:
        kernel_soft_get_state(
            state.soft_pos,
            state.soft_vel,
            state.soft_pos_prev,
            state.soft_vel_prev,
            self.soft_state,
            self.rigid_config,
        )
    return state

def set_state(self, f, state, envs_idx=None, *, partial: bool = False) -> None:
    if not self.is_active:
        return
    # The kinematic state is restored (and subscribers notified) by the base class; the integration history is
    # restored on top, leaving nothing for the external-state sync of the next step to rebuild.
    super().set_state(f, state, envs_idx, partial=False)
    envs_idx = self._scene._sanitize_envs_idx(envs_idx)
    _kernel_set_history(
        envs_idx,
        state.qpos_prev,
        state.dofs_vel_prev,
        state.links_vel,
        state.links_ang,
        state.links_vsym,
        state.links_vel_prev,
        state.links_ang_prev,
        state.links_vsym_prev,
        state.n_hist,
        self.mochi_state,
        self.rigid_config,
    )
    kernel_update_geoms(
        self._scene._envs_idx, self.dyn_state, self.dyn_info, self.rigid_info, self.rigid_config, False
    )
    kernel_update_geom_aabbs(self.geoms_init_AABB, self.dyn_state, self.dyn_info, self.rigid_config)
    if self.has_soft:
        kernel_soft_set_state(
            envs_idx,
            state.soft_pos,
            state.soft_vel,
            state.soft_pos_prev,
            state.soft_vel_prev,
            self.soft_state,
            self.rigid_config,
        )
    self._external_state_dirty_mask[tensor_to_array(envs_idx)] = False
    self._is_contacts_recorded = False
    # A restored environment starts over: whatever error it raised (a diverged solve) is cleared, as the rigid
    # solver clears its own, so that resetting the environments `get_error_envs_mask` names lets the others go on.
    self.clear_errno(envs_idx)

def destroy_arrays(self) -> None:
    """Free the ndarrays of the solver right away, as `Simulator.destroy` frees those of the other solvers.

    `Simulator.destroy` gathers the arrays to free from `data`, which this solver refuses, so the destroy of its
    scene calls this instead, after it (see `eden.engine.solvers.mochi.hosting`). They are those its attributes
    hold, alone or in the structs (dataclasses) and the containers they hold. One already freed — by an earlier
    call, or by `Simulator.destroy` as the array of another solver — is left alone; a field is freed by `qd.reset`.
    """
    for array in _iter_ndarrays(vars(self).values(), set()):
        if array.arr is not None:
            qd_destroy_data(array)

def get_contacts(self, as_tensor: bool = True, to_torch: bool = True, is_padded: bool = False):
    """
    Contact points of the current state, as a dict of arrays laid out (n_envs, n_contacts, ...) (see
    `MochiEntity.get_contacts` and `MochiSoftEntity.get_contacts`). The contact axis holds the largest
    per-environment count; shorter environments carry -1 indices and zeros in their unused slots.
    """
    self._record_contacts()
    n_contacts = torch.zeros((self._B,), dtype=gs.tc_int, device=gs.device)
    kernel_count_contact_records(self.hit_readback, self.soft_state, n_contacts, self.rigid_config, self.has_soft)
    n_max = max(1, int(n_contacts.max()))

    def ints(*shape):
        return torch.full((self._B, n_max, *shape), -1, dtype=gs.tc_int, device=gs.device)

    def floats(*shape):
        return torch.zeros((self._B, n_max, *shape), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)

    contact_data = {
        "entity_a": ints(),
        "entity_b": ints(),
        "link_a": ints(),
        "link_b": ints(),
        "geom_a": ints(),
        "geom_b": ints(),
        "verts_a": ints(4),
        "bary_a": floats(4),
        "verts_b": ints(4),
        "bary_b": floats(4),
        "position": floats(3),
        "normal": floats(3),
        "distance": floats(),
        "force_a": floats(3),
        "weight": floats(),
    }
    kernel_gather_contact_records(
        self._links_entity_idx,
        self._geoms_link_idx,
        self._soft_entities_idx,
        self.mochi_info.samples,
        self.hit_readback,
        self.soft_info,
        self.soft_state,
        self.rigid_config,
        self.has_soft,
        contact_data["entity_a"],
        contact_data["entity_b"],
        contact_data["link_a"],
        contact_data["link_b"],
        contact_data["geom_a"],
        contact_data["geom_b"],
        contact_data["verts_a"],
        contact_data["bary_a"],
        contact_data["verts_b"],
        contact_data["bary_b"],
        contact_data["position"],
        contact_data["normal"],
        contact_data["force_a"],
        contact_data["distance"],
        contact_data["weight"],
    )
    contact_data["force_b"] = -contact_data["force_a"]
    if is_padded:
        contact_data["n_contacts"] = n_contacts if self.n_envs > 0 else n_contacts[0]
    if self.n_envs == 0:
        contact_data = {key: value[0] for key, value in contact_data.items()}
    if not to_torch:
        contact_data = {key: tensor_to_array(value) for key, value in contact_data.items()}
    return contact_data

Signed distance and distance gradient of world points to a collider geom, in the world frame, as seen by the contact model (a grid collider only answers inside its grid; other points are flagged invalid).

RETURNS DESCRIPTION (distances, gradients, is_valid) : tuple of arrays of shape (n_points,), (n_points, 3), (n_points,) Source code in eden/engine/solvers/mochi/mochi_solver.py 
def get_collider_distances(self, geom_idx, points_world, envs_idx=None):
    """
    Signed distance and distance gradient of world points to a collider geom, in the world frame, as seen by the
    contact model (a grid collider only answers inside its grid; other points are flagged invalid).

    Returns
    -------
    (distances, gradients, is_valid) : tuple of arrays of shape (n_points,), (n_points, 3), (n_points,)
    """
    envs_idx = self._scene._sanitize_envs_idx(envs_idx)
    points = torch.as_tensor(points_world, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device).reshape((-1, 3)).contiguous()
    distances = torch.zeros((points.shape[0],), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    gradients = torch.zeros((points.shape[0], 3), dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    is_valid = torch.zeros((points.shape[0],), dtype=torch.bool, device=gs.device)
    _kernel_get_collider_distances(
        int(geom_idx),
        int(envs_idx[0]),
        points,
        distances,
        gradients,
        is_valid,
        self.dyn_state,
        self.dyn_info,
        self.sdf_info,
        self.mochi_info,
        self.mochi_config,
    )
    return distances, gradients, is_valid

def get_convergence_info(self):
    """Per-environment outcome of the last solve: number of Newton iterations, number of conjugate-gradient
    iterations summed over the Newton iterations, status (0 running, 1 converged, 2 stopped at the iteration budget,
    3 diverged), and the plain residual norm before and after the solve.

    }

def get_contact_capacity_usage(self):
    """Per bounded contact list, the largest per-environment count of the last full assembly (the one the last
    linear solve used) and the capacity of the list (what the `max_*` options size), to tune the capacities of a
    scene.
    """
    usage = {"contact_pairs": (int(qd_to_numpy(self.contact_state.n_pairs).max()), self._max_pairs)}
    if self.has_soft:
        usage["soft_hits"] = (int(qd_to_numpy(self.soft_state.n_soft_hits_max)), self._max_soft_hits)
        usage["soft_collider_hits"] = (int(qd_to_numpy(self.soft_state.n_sc_hits_max)), self._max_sc_hits)
        usage["point_cloud_hits"] = (int(qd_to_numpy(self.soft_state.n_pc_hits_max)), self._max_pc_hits)
    return usage

get_links_pos(links_idx=None, envs_idx=None, *, ref: link_ref_frame = link_origin, relative=False)

Link positions in the requested reference frame, as RigidSolver.get_links_pos.

KinematicSolver's own getter knows only the link origin; the inertial frames the other references name are maintained by this solver as well, so the whole ref vocabulary is answered here.

Source code in eden/engine/solvers/mochi/mochi_solver.py 
def get_links_pos(
    self,
    links_idx=None,
    envs_idx=None,
    *,
    ref: link_ref_frame = link_ref_frame.link_origin,
    relative=False,
):
    """Link positions in the requested reference frame, as ``RigidSolver.get_links_pos``.

    ``KinematicSolver``'s own getter knows only the link origin; the inertial frames the other references name
    are maintained by this solver as well, so the whole ``ref`` vocabulary is answered here.
    """
    ref_frame = self._sanitize_ref_frame(ref)
    if ref_frame == link_ref_frame.root_COM:
        tensor = qd_to_torch(self.dyn_state.links.root_COM, envs_idx, links_idx, transpose=True, copy=True)
    elif ref_frame == link_ref_frame.link_COM:
        i_pos = qd_to_torch(self.dyn_state.links.i_pos, envs_idx, links_idx, transpose=True)
        root_COM = qd_to_torch(self.dyn_state.links.root_COM, envs_idx, links_idx, transpose=True)
        tensor = i_pos + root_COM
    else:
        return super().get_links_pos(links_idx, envs_idx, relative=relative)
    return tensor[0] if self.n_envs == 0 else tensor

def get_links_vel(
    self, links_idx=None, envs_idx=None, *, ref: link_ref_frame = link_ref_frame.link_origin, relative=False
):
    """Link velocities in the requested reference frame, as ``RigidSolver.get_links_vel``."""
    ref_frame = self._sanitize_ref_frame(ref, has_root_COM=False)
    if ref_frame == link_ref_frame.link_origin:
        return super().get_links_vel(links_idx, envs_idx, relative=relative)
    cd_vel = qd_to_torch(self.dyn_state.links.cd_vel, envs_idx, links_idx, transpose=True, copy=True)
    cd_ang = qd_to_torch(self.dyn_state.links.cd_ang, envs_idx, links_idx, transpose=True)
    i_pos = qd_to_torch(self.dyn_state.links.i_pos, envs_idx, links_idx, transpose=True)
    tensor = cd_vel + cd_ang.cross(i_pos, dim=-1)
    return tensor[0] if self.n_envs == 0 else tensor

@mutates(StateChange.MODEL)
def set_links_contact_params(self, links_idx, **params):
    links_idx = tensor_to_array(links_idx).reshape((-1,))
    geoms_idx = np.concatenate(
        [np.arange(self.links[i_l].geom_start, self.links[i_l].geom_end) for i_l in links_idx], dtype=gs.np_int
    )
    for name, value in params.items():
        if value is None:
            continue
        field = self.mochi_info.geoms.__getattribute__(name)
        values = qd_to_numpy(field)
        values[geoms_idx] = value
        field.from_numpy(values)
    self._wake_nodes(self._nodes_idx, self._nodes_idx, self._scene._envs_idx)

def set_soft_vertices_target(self, entity, verts_idx, pos, envs_idx=None):
    envs_idx = self._scene._sanitize_envs_idx(envs_idx)
    is_shared = verts_idx.ndim == 1
    verts_idx = self._per_env_vertices(verts_idx, envs_idx)
    n_verts = verts_idx.shape[1]
    # A tensor already on the device goes straight to the kernel: this is called every control step.
    pos = torch.as_tensor(pos, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=gs.device)
    if is_shared and pos.shape == (n_verts, 3):
        pos = pos[None].expand(len(envs_idx), -1, -1)
    if pos.shape != (len(envs_idx), n_verts, 3):
        gs.raise_exception(
            f"Expected an array of shape ({len(envs_idx)}, {n_verts}, 3)"
            + (f" or ({n_verts}, 3)" if is_shared else "")
            + f", got {tuple(pos.shape)}."
        )
    kernel_soft_set_vertices_target(
        envs_idx, verts_idx, entity.v_start, pos.contiguous(), self.soft_state, self.rigid_config
    )
    if self.mochi_config.use_sleeping:
        i_n = len(self._entities) + entity.idx_in_solver
        self._wake_nodes(self._nodes_idx[i_n : i_n + 1], self._nodes_idx, envs_idx)

def set_soft_entity_contact_params(self, entity, **params):
    material = entity.material
    keys = (
        "penalty_coefficient",
        "friction",
        "penalty_smoothing_half_distance",
        "penalty_threshold",
        "friction_falloff_vel",
        "viscous_friction",
        "normal_viscous_damping",
    )
    values = []
    for key in keys:
        value = params.get(key)
        if value is None:
            value = getattr(material, key)
        else:
            setattr(material, key, value)
        values.append(float(value))

    )

    self._is_contacts_recorded = False

Rigid entity simulated by the MochiSolver.

Loading, kinematics, pose/velocity access and joint control are shared with RigidEntity. Contact is the solver's smooth penalty model, so the contact readback exposes the sample-based contact points; the mass-matrix and constraint-solver specific accessors of the rigid solver are unavailable.

docs.title: get_contacts
docs.text:
get_contacts(with_entity=None, exclude_self_contact=False, is_padded=False)

Returns the contact points computed at the end of the most recent scene.step(), filtered to those involving this entity (and with_entity if given).

A contact point is a sample of the collision surface of side A pressed into the distance field of side B (a rigid geom, or a deformable body). The returned dict has the keys 'entity_a', 'entity_b' (scene entity indices), 'link_a', 'link_b', 'geom_a', 'geom_b' (-1 for a deformable side), 'verts_a', 'bary_a', 'verts_b', 'bary_b' (entity-local vertices and weights a deformable side is spread over, -1 padded), 'position', 'normal' (unit, pointing away from B), 'distance' (signed, negative when penetrating), 'force_a' (force on A), 'force_b' (= -force_a), 'weight' (surface measure the sample stands for) and, for a parallelized scene or with is_padded, 'valid_mask'. Shapes are (n_envs, n_contacts, ...) for a parallelized scene and (n_contacts, ...) otherwise; an unparallelized scene without is_padded keeps only the matching contacts.

Source code in eden/engine/solvers/mochi/mochi_entity.py 
def get_contacts(self, with_entity=None, exclude_self_contact=False, is_padded=False):
    """
    Returns the contact points computed at the end of the most recent `scene.step()`, filtered to those involving
    this entity (and `with_entity` if given).

    A contact point is a sample of the collision surface of side A pressed into the distance field of side B
    (a rigid geom, or a deformable body). The returned dict has the keys 'entity_a', 'entity_b' (scene entity
    indices), 'link_a', 'link_b', 'geom_a', 'geom_b' (-1 for a deformable side), 'verts_a', 'bary_a', 'verts_b',
    'bary_b' (entity-local vertices and weights a deformable side is spread over, -1 padded), 'position', 'normal'
    (unit, pointing away from B), 'distance' (signed, negative when penetrating), 'force_a' (force on A),
    'force_b' (= -force_a), 'weight' (surface measure the sample stands for) and, for a parallelized scene or
    with `is_padded`, 'valid_mask'. Shapes are (n_envs, n_contacts, ...) for a parallelized scene and
    (n_contacts, ...) otherwise; an unparallelized scene without `is_padded` keeps only the matching contacts.
    """
    return filter_entity_contacts(self._solver, self, with_entity, exclude_self_contact, is_padded)

docs.text:
MochiSoftEntity(scene, solver, material, morph, surface, idx, idx_in_solver, v_start, vvert_start, vface_start, name=None)

Bases: Entity

Deformable body simulated by the MochiSolver: a tetrahedral mesh (materials.Elastic), a thin shell made of the surface triangles of the morph (materials.Shell) or a discrete elastic rod along the polyline of a Rod morph (materials.Rod), whose vertex positions are unknowns of the implicit solve.

The solid simulation mesh is tetrahedralized from the morph surface (tetgen options on the morph), or read directly from a tetgen '.node' / '.ele' file pair or a legacy ASCII '.vtk' file given as a gs.morphs.Mesh. The boundary triangles (all triangles of a shell) carry the contact samples and the render mesh; a rod carries its samples on the centerline and renders as a tube.

Source code in eden/engine/solvers/mochi/mochi_soft_entity.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    scene,
    solver,
    material,
    morph,
    surface,
    idx,
    idx_in_solver,
    v_start,
    vvert_start,
    vface_start,
    name=None,
):
    self._is_shell = isinstance(material, mochi_materials.Shell)
    self._is_rod = isinstance(material, mochi_materials.Rod)
    if self._is_rod != isinstance(morph, Rod):
        gs.raise_exception(
            "A `Rod` morph (eden.engine.solvers.mochi.morphs) requires a `Rod` material "
            "(eden.engine.solvers.mochi.materials), and conversely."
        )
    super().__init__(idx, scene, morph, solver, material, surface, name=name)
    self._idx_in_solver = idx_in_solver
    self._v_start = v_start
    self._vvert_start = vvert_start
    self._vface_start = vface_start
    self._attachments = []
    self._contact_skin = None

    self.sample()

    # Boundary triangles (outward winding), all triangles of a shell, none for a rod (its contact samples lie on
    # the centerline).
    if self._is_rod:
        self._surface_tri_np = np.zeros((0, 3), dtype=gs.np_int)
    elif self._is_shell:
        self._surface_tri_np = self.elems
    else:
        self._surface_tri_np = self._boundary_triangles(self.elems)
