find_named_dofs(dofs_name: str | Sequence[str] | None = None) -> DofSelection

Resolve names to a :class:DofSelection: the selected DOFs' columns and local indices.

One resolution feeds both, so the two always describe the same DOFs, in the same order. Selection follows the class note: only the controlled joints (those in :attr:dofs_name) can be selected, through the same simulator-side resolver find_named_dofs_idx_local uses, so a query selects the same joints in both. Resolve in build(), not every step.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION dofs_name

Names, globs or regexes of joints in :attr:dofs_name. None selects every controlled DOF, in column order.

TYPE: str | Sequence[str] | None DEFAULT: None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DofSelection

One name, column and local index per selected DOF.

Source code in eden/entities/dofs_default_mixin.py 
@gs.assert_built
def find_named_dofs(self, dofs_name: str | Sequence[str] | None = None) -> DofSelection:
    """Resolve names to a :class:`DofSelection`: the selected DOFs' columns *and* local indices.

    One resolution feeds both, so the two always describe the same DOFs, in the same order.
    Selection follows the class note: only the controlled joints (those in :attr:`dofs_name`) can
    be selected, through the same simulator-side resolver ``find_named_dofs_idx_local`` uses, so a
    query selects the same joints in both. Resolve in ``build()``, not every step.

    Parameters
    ----------
    dofs_name : str | Sequence[str] | None
        Names, globs or regexes of joints in :attr:`dofs_name`. ``None`` selects every
        controlled DOF, in column order.

    Returns
    -------
    DofSelection
        One name, column and local index per selected DOF.
    """
    if dofs_name is None:
        # Every controlled DOF, in column order: what ``dofs_name`` and ``dofs_idx_local`` already hold. An entity
        # that resolved no DOFs has an empty ``dofs_idx_map``, and its ``dofs_name`` is then still the raw config.
        names = list(self.dofs_name) if self.dofs_idx_map else []
        dofs_idx_local = self.dofs_idx_local.tolist() if names else []
    else:
        names, dofs_idx_local = self._resolve_controlled_dofs(dofs_name)
    # ``dofs_idx_map`` takes a controlled DOF's local index to its column.
    columns = [self.dofs_idx_map[int(i)] for i in dofs_idx_local]
    return DofSelection(
        entity_name=self.name,
        names=tuple(names),
        columns=torch.tensor(columns, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device),
        dofs_idx_local=torch.tensor(dofs_idx_local, dtype=gs.tc_int, device=self.device),
    )

def current_support(
    self,
    minimum_clearance: float = 0.1,
    require_roof: bool = False,
    gravity: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    gravity_tolerance: float = 0.1,
    envs_idx: (slice | torch.Tensor) | None = None,
) -> list[ExtendedSupportData]:
    """
    Get the valid current support data at the entity's current pose.

    Parameters
    ----------
    minimum_clearance: float
        minimum clearance to consider for support surface
    require_roof: bool
        if the support has to be covered (e.g., inside shelf, microwave, etc.)
    gravity: torch.Tensor | None
        a normalized gravity vector indicating the gravity direction in world coordinate system
        that the support surface is holding against. ``None`` means ``-z``.
    gravity_tolerance: float
        tolerance for gravity direction alignment
    envs_idx: None | slice | torch.Tensor, optional
        the indices of the environments to query. If None, all environments are considered. Defaults to None.
    """
    if gravity is None:
        gravity = torch.tensor([0.0, 0.0, -1.0], device=gs.device)
    # relative=False: world frame (consistent with get_AABB and the pre-1.1.1 default).
    _pos_cur = self._entity.get_pos(envs_idx=envs_idx, relative=False)
    _quat_cur = self._entity.get_quat(envs_idx=envs_idx, relative=False)
    _T_cur = trans_quat_to_T(_pos_cur, _quat_cur)

    if envs_idx is not None and self._T_reference_inv.shape[0] != 1:
        T_revert = _T_cur @ self._T_reference_inv[envs_idx]
    else:
        T_revert = _T_cur @ self._T_reference_inv

    res: list[ExtendedSupportData] = []
    for d in self._support_data_list:
        if minimum_clearance > 0 or require_roof:
            if require_roof and d.clearance == math.inf:
                continue
            if d.clearance < minimum_clearance:
                continue

        normal = transform_by_R(d.normal, T_revert[..., :3, :3])
        normal = normal / torch.norm(normal, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        # check if the normal is aligned with the opposite gravity direction
        normalized_gravity = gravity / torch.norm(gravity, dim=-1, keepdim=True)
        valid_mask = torch.isclose(
            (normal * -normalized_gravity).sum(dim=-1),
            torch.ones(normal.shape[0], device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float),
            atol=gravity_tolerance,
        )
        res.append(
            ExtendedSupportData(
                polygon=d.polygon,
                transform=(
                    T_revert @ d.transform[envs_idx]
                    if envs_idx is not None and d.transform.shape[0] > 1
                    else T_revert @ d.transform
                ),  # (B, 4, 4)
                normal=normal,  # (B, 3)
                valid_mask=valid_mask,  # (B, )
                sample_points=d.sample_points,
                num_sample_points=d.num_sample_points,
            )
        )
    return res

def pre_build(self) -> None:
    super().pre_build()
    (terrain_geom,) = self._entity.geoms

    assert "height_field" in terrain_geom.metadata
    height_field = terrain_geom.metadata["height_field"]
    self._height_field = torch.as_tensor(height_field, device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)
    assert self._height_field.ndim == 2, f"Height field must be 2D, but got {self._height_field.shape}"
    self._height_field *= self._entity.morph.vertical_scale

    # NOTE: reshape from (width, height) to (height, width) for grid_sample calculation
    # NOTE: we only need one copy since all environments share the same terrain
    self._height_field = self._height_field.T
    # TODO: heterogeneous terrain support
    self._height_field = self._height_field[None, None, :, :].expand(self._env.num_envs, -1, -1, -1)

post_build() -> None
Source code in eden/entities/terrain.py 
def post_build(self) -> None:
    super().post_build()

    # relative=False: world-frame origin (matching the pre-1.1.1 Genesis default).
    self._origin = self._entity.get_pos(relative=False)[0]

    # get_height returns WORLD z: the morph pos z physically raises the surface,
    # so height queries must carry the same offset (the offline exporter's npz
    # already carries origin z the same way). Offset the underlying 2D grid and
    # re-expand so the per-env dimension stays a zero-copy view.
    offset_field = self._height_field[0, 0] + self._origin[2]
    self._height_field = offset_field[None, None, :, :].expand(self._env.num_envs, -1, -1, -1)

    # Calculate total terrain size from subterrain configuration
    subterrain_size = self._entity.morph.subterrain_size
    n_subterrains = self._entity.morph.n_subterrains

    total_x_size = subterrain_size[0] * n_subterrains[0]
    total_y_size = subterrain_size[1] * n_subterrains[1]
    self._size = (total_x_size, total_y_size)

    # Calculate bounds from origin and size
    x_min = self._origin[0]
    y_min = self._origin[1]
    x_max = x_min + total_x_size
    y_max = y_min + total_y_size
    self._bounds = (x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max)

    self._bounds_min_buffer = torch.tensor([x_min, y_min], device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)
    self._bounds_inv_range_buffer = torch.tensor(
        [1.0 / (x_max - x_min), 1.0 / (y_max - y_min)],
        device=gs.device,
        dtype=gs.tc_float,
    )

    self._build_subterrain_buffers()

def export_height_field(self, path: str) -> None:
    """Export this terrain's height field (in meters) to ``path``.

    Writes the versioned ``.npz`` format defined in
    :mod:`eden.utils.terrains.io`, usable by offline tools (e.g. the TCRS
    terrain-adaptive motion retargeter) without rebuilding the scene.
    """
    from eden.utils.terrains.io import export_height_field

    if not hasattr(self, "_origin"):
        raise RuntimeError("Terrain.export_height_field requires a built scene — call env.build() first.")

    (terrain_geom,) = self._entity.geoms
    height_field_m = terrain_geom.metadata["height_field"] * self._entity.morph.vertical_scale
    export_height_field(
        path,
        height_field_m=height_field_m,
        horizontal_scale=self._entity.morph.horizontal_scale,
        origin=tuple(self._origin.tolist()),
    )

Get the height of the terrain at the given xy coordinates.

def get_height(self, grid: torch.Tensor, normalize: bool = True) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Get the height of the terrain at the given xy coordinates.

    Parameters
    ----------
    grid : torch.Tensor, shape (B, h_out, w_out, 2)
        The grid of xy coordinates to sample the height from: world xy (m) if ``normalize`` is True, else
        already normalized to the terrain bounds as [-1, 1].
    normalize : bool, optional
        Whether to normalize world xy to [-1, 1] here (into a new tensor; ``grid`` is not modified).
        Defaults to True.

    Returns
    -------
    height : torch.Tensor, shape (B, h_out, w_out)
        The world-frame z of the terrain surface at the given xy coordinates.
    """
    if normalize:
        # Normalize coordinates to [-1, 1] range expected by grid_sample
        # norm_xy = 2 * (xy - mins) / (maxs - mins) - 1
        grid = 2 * (grid - self._bounds_min_buffer) * self._bounds_inv_range_buffer - 1.0

    # Border padding mode isn't supported on Mac GPU (mps)
    # https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/125098
    interpolated = F.grid_sample(
        self._height_field,  # B, 1, height, width
        grid,  # B, h_out, w_out, 2
        mode="bilinear",
        padding_mode="border" if gs.device.type != "mps" else "zeros",
        align_corners=True,
    )  # B, 1, h_out, w_out

    return interpolated.squeeze(1)  # B, h_out, w_out

def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: EntityOptions):
    self._options = options
    self._env = env
    self._is_attached = False
    self._attachment_parent: Entity | None = None
    self.is_heterogeneous = isinstance(self._options, GroupedEntityOptions)
    # Heterogeneous only: each env's own variant default pose, (num_envs, 3) / (num_envs, 4).
    self._variant_default_root_pos: torch.Tensor | None = None
    self._variant_default_root_quat: torch.Tensor | None = None
    # Heterogeneous only: the variant each env holds, (num_envs,) long, and the first env holding each variant
    # present (all of them, unless there are fewer envs than variants).
    self._env_variant_idx: torch.Tensor | None = None
    self._variant_first_envs: list[int] = []
    # Heterogeneous only: each present variant's value for a per-variant field they differ in; a field
    # they all resolve alike is mirrored as that one value instead. And each variant's material, present or
    # not, so the checks on it do not depend on the env count.
    self._variant_fields: dict[str, list] = {}
    self._variant_materials: list[MaterialLike] | None = None

    # Create morph from options if not already set
    if not self.is_heterogeneous:
        self._create_morph_from_options()
    else:
        self._create_grouped_morphs_from_options()

    # Mirror options onto the instance. Entity does not delegate __init__ to
    # ConfigurableMixin -- see mirror_options_onto's docstring for why, and for the
    # aliasing this protects against. Unlike the mixin, Entity sets no ``_uid``: its
    # ``uid`` is the wrapped Genesis entity's, so there is nothing to seed here.
    # SupportSurfaceMixin's attributes need no skip list -- get_parameter_names() walks
    # only ConfigurableMixin bases, so they never show up here.
    mirror_options_onto(self, self._options)
    if self.is_heterogeneous:
        self._resolve_variant_fields()

    # forward_vec is derived from the options' front direction (single source of truth);
    # entities without a front (e.g. primitives) keep the class default.
    self.forward_vec = getattr(self._options, "front", self.forward_vec)
    self.forward_vec = torch.tensor(self.forward_vec, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=self.device).unsqueeze(0)

docs.title: FEMEntity
docs.text:
FEMEntity(env: EnvBase, options: EntityOptions)

Bases: Entity

Entity subclass for FEM-based deformable materials (Elastic, Cloth, Muscle).

FEM entities use vertex-based state (positions and velocities of mesh vertices) rather than rigid-body state. They have no DOFs, links, or joint-based control.

The Genesis FEMEntity does not expose get_pos/get_vel/get_quat/get_ang, so this class overrides those methods to provide a compatible interface (mean vertex position, mean velocity, identity quaternion, zero angular velocity).

Source code in eden/entities/base.py 
def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: EntityOptions):
    self._options = options
    self._env = env
    self._is_attached = False
    self._attachment_parent: Entity | None = None
    self.is_heterogeneous = isinstance(self._options, GroupedEntityOptions)
    # Heterogeneous only: each env's own variant default pose, (num_envs, 3) / (num_envs, 4).
    self._variant_default_root_pos: torch.Tensor | None = None
    self._variant_default_root_quat: torch.Tensor | None = None
    # Heterogeneous only: the variant each env holds, (num_envs,) long, and the first env holding each variant
    # present (all of them, unless there are fewer envs than variants).
    self._env_variant_idx: torch.Tensor | None = None
    self._variant_first_envs: list[int] = []
    # Heterogeneous only: each present variant's value for a per-variant field they differ in; a field
    # they all resolve alike is mirrored as that one value instead. And each variant's material, present or
    # not, so the checks on it do not depend on the env count.
    self._variant_fields: dict[str, list] = {}
    self._variant_materials: list[MaterialLike] | None = None

    # Create morph from options if not already set
    if not self.is_heterogeneous:
        self._create_morph_from_options()
    else:
        self._create_grouped_morphs_from_options()

    # Mirror options onto the instance. Entity does not delegate __init__ to
    # ConfigurableMixin -- see mirror_options_onto's docstring for why, and for the
    # aliasing this protects against. Unlike the mixin, Entity sets no ``_uid``: its
    # ``uid`` is the wrapped Genesis entity's, so there is nothing to seed here.
    # SupportSurfaceMixin's attributes need no skip list -- get_parameter_names() walks
    # only ConfigurableMixin bases, so they never show up here.
    mirror_options_onto(self, self._options)
    if self.is_heterogeneous:
        self._resolve_variant_fields()

    # forward_vec is derived from the options' front direction (single source of truth);
    # entities without a front (e.g. primitives) keep the class default.
    self.forward_vec = getattr(self._options, "front", self.forward_vec)
    self.forward_vec = torch.tensor(self.forward_vec, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=self.device).unsqueeze(0)
    self.default_root_pos = torch.tensor(self.default_root_pos, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=self.device).unsqueeze(0)
    self.default_root_quat = torch.tensor(
        self.default_root_quat,
        dtype=gs.tc_float,
        device=self.device,
    ).unsqueeze(0)

def get_pos(self, envs_idx=None, *, relative: bool = False):
    """Return mean vertex position (geometric centroid), shape (B, 3).

    Note: this is the unweighted mean of vertex positions, not the
    mass-weighted center of mass. ``relative`` must be False (see
    :meth:`~eden.entities.base.Entity._reject_relative`).
    """
    self._reject_relative(relative, "get_pos")
    state = self._entity.get_state()
    pos = state.pos  # (B, n_vertices, 3)
    centroid = pos.mean(dim=1)  # (B, 3)
    if envs_idx is not None:
        return centroid[envs_idx]
    return centroid

def get_vel(self, envs_idx=None, *, frame: Literal["world", "body"] = "world"):
    """Return mean vertex velocity, shape (B, 3). Only world frame is supported."""
    if frame != "world":
        raise ValueError(f"FEMEntity only supports frame='world', got '{frame}'.")

def get_quat(self, envs_idx=None, *, relative: bool = False):
    """Return identity quaternion (wxyz) for all envs, shape (B, 4).

    FEM entities have no rigid-body orientation. Returns a constant identity
    quaternion for interface compatibility. ``relative`` must be False (see
    :meth:`~eden.entities.base.Entity._reject_relative`).
    """
    self._reject_relative(relative, "get_quat")
    if self._identity_quat is None or self._identity_quat.shape[0] != self._env.num_envs:
        self._identity_quat = (
            torch.tensor([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0], device=self.device).expand(self._env.num_envs, -1).contiguous()
        )
    if envs_idx is not None:
        return self._identity_quat[envs_idx]
    return self._identity_quat

docs.text:
set_com_offset(offset, envs_idx=None)

Place the soft body's undeformed build-time shape, translated by offset.

Every vertex lands at its build-time position plus offset, so the body is reset to its undeformed shape (any current deformation is discarded), and the offset is always measured from the build-time pose: repeated calls do not accumulate, like :meth:~eden.entities.rigid.RigidEntity.set_COM_shift is measured from the nominal COM. For an absolute centroid position use :meth:set_pos.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION offset

(3,) (applied to all envs) or (B, 3) (per-env) — an offset from the build-time pose, not an absolute world position. Moved to the sim device, so a host tensor, array or list is fine.

TYPE: array_like

envs_idx

Per-env addressing is unsupported by Genesis FEM entities; must be None.

TYPE: None DEFAULT: None

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

If offset is not rank-1/2 with a trailing dim of 3, or looks like per-vertex data (a (n_vertices, 3) array — use :meth:set_vertex_positions). The (num_envs, 3) vs (n_vertices, 3) shapes only collide when num_envs == n_vertices; then the per-env offset reading this method is named for is taken. (Genesis set_position, and so :meth:set_pos, reads that shape the other way, as per-vertex positions.)

Source code in eden/entities/fem.py 
def set_com_offset(self, offset, envs_idx=None):
    """Place the soft body's undeformed build-time shape, translated by ``offset``.

    Every vertex lands at its build-time position plus ``offset``, so the
    body is reset to its **undeformed** shape (any current deformation is
    discarded), and the offset is always measured from the build-time pose:
    repeated calls do not accumulate, like
    :meth:`~eden.entities.rigid.RigidEntity.set_COM_shift` is measured from
    the nominal COM. For an absolute centroid position use :meth:`set_pos`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    offset : array_like
        ``(3,)`` (applied to all envs) or ``(B, 3)`` (per-env) — an offset
        **from the build-time pose**, not an absolute world position. Moved
        to the sim device, so a host tensor, array or list is fine.
    envs_idx : None
        Per-env addressing is unsupported by Genesis FEM entities; must be None.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``offset`` is not rank-1/2 with a trailing dim of 3, or looks like
        per-vertex data (a ``(n_vertices, 3)`` array — use
        :meth:`set_vertex_positions`). The ``(num_envs, 3)`` vs
        ``(n_vertices, 3)`` shapes only collide when ``num_envs ==
        n_vertices``; then the per-env offset reading this method is named
        for is taken. (Genesis ``set_position``, and so :meth:`set_pos`,
        reads that shape the other way, as per-vertex positions.)
    """
    init_positions = self._entity.init_positions
    offset = torch.as_tensor(offset, dtype=init_positions.dtype, device=init_positions.device)
    # A (n_vertices, 3) array is per-vertex data, not an offset. The shape
    # only collides with a per-env (num_envs, 3) offset when the two counts
    # are equal, in which case we cannot tell them apart and take the offset
    # reading (Genesis would take the per-vertex one; see the forward below).
    n_vertices_differs_from_envs = self.n_vertices != self._env.num_envs
    looks_like_vertices = offset.ndim == 2 and offset.shape[0] == self.n_vertices and n_vertices_differs_from_envs
    if offset.shape[-1] != 3 or offset.ndim > 2 or looks_like_vertices:
        raise ValueError(
            f"set_com_offset expects (3,) or (num_envs, 3); got {tuple(offset.shape)}. "
            f"For absolute per-vertex positions (vertex dim {self.n_vertices}) use set_vertex_positions()."
        )
    # Genesis' own rank-1/2 branch adds the value to the *COM-subtracted* build-time vertices, i.e. it takes an
    # absolute centroid (that is ``set_pos``). Add the offset to the build-time vertices instead and forward
    # absolute per-vertex positions: (3,) -> (n_vertices, 3) tiled, (B, 3) -> (B, n_vertices, 3). Neither shape is
    # ambiguous to Genesis, so the num_envs == n_vertices collision never reaches its rank dispatch.
    self._set_position(init_positions + offset.unsqueeze(-2), envs_idx)

def set_vertex_positions(self, pos, envs_idx=None):
    """Set absolute per-vertex world positions of the soft body.

    This is the rank-2 / rank-3 case of Genesis ``set_position``. Prefer
    this over :meth:`set_pos` when you have full vertex coordinates, so the
    absolute-vertex (vs. centroid) semantics is explicit at the call site.

    Parameters
    ----------
    pos : torch.Tensor
        ``(n_vertices, 3)`` (tiled to all envs) or ``(B, n_vertices, 3)``
        (full batched) absolute per-vertex positions.
    envs_idx : None
        Per-env addressing is unsupported by Genesis FEM entities; must be None.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If ``pos`` is not rank-2/3 with a trailing dim of 3 and a vertex
        dimension equal to ``n_vertices`` (for a COM offset use
        :meth:`set_com_offset`).
    """
    # For both accepted shapes the vertex count is the second-to-last axis;
    # ndim outside {2, 3} (a bare offset or a too-deep batch) has no vertex axis.
    vertex_dim = pos.shape[-2] if pos.ndim in (2, 3) else None
    if pos.shape[-1] != 3 or vertex_dim != self.n_vertices:
        raise ValueError(
            f"set_vertex_positions expects (n_vertices={self.n_vertices}, 3) or "
            f"(B, n_vertices, 3); got {tuple(pos.shape)}. For a COM offset use set_com_offset()."
        )
    self._set_position(pos, envs_idx)

set_pos(pos, envs_idx=None)

Set FEM state via Genesis set_position (shape-dispatched).

Genesis interprets the tensor rank as either a centroid position or absolute per-vertex positions; this method only forwards. Because that dual meaning is invisible at the call site, prefer the explicit :meth:set_com_offset / :meth:set_vertex_positions instead. Kept for compatibility with the generic :class:Entity interface.

Accepted shapes:

  • (3,) — world position of the vertex centroid, applied to all envs.
  • (n_vertices, 3) — absolute per-vertex positions, tiled to all envs.
  • (B, 3) — per-env world positions of the vertex centroid.
  • (B, n_vertices, 3) — full batched per-vertex absolute positions.

(3,) and (B, 3) are absolute: they place the undeformed build-time shape so that its vertex centroid sits at that world position, which is what :meth:get_pos reads back. For an offset from the build-time pose use :meth:set_com_offset.

When num_envs == n_vertices the (B, 3) and (n_vertices, 3) shapes coincide, and Genesis checks (n_vertices, 3) first: a per-env centroid tensor is then silently read as per-vertex positions, collapsing the body. Use :meth:set_vertex_positions or :meth:set_com_offset, which name their meaning, in that case.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION pos

Position tensor (see shapes above).

TYPE: Tensor

envs_idx

Not supported by Genesis FEM entities. Must be None.

TYPE: None DEFAULT: None

If envs_idx is not None.

docs.text:
MochiRigidEntity(env: EnvBase, options: EntityOptions)

Bases: RigidEntity

A rigid or articulated body simulated by the MochiSolver.

Everything :class:RigidEntity offers works unchanged except what the solver never reads: drive-force ranges, joint friction loss and constraint-solver parameters (rejected at options validation), link mass/inertia edits after build (set_mass raises), support surfaces and AABB queries. Contact behaviour is a material property (friction, penalty_coefficient, ...) and can be re-tuned per link with :meth:set_contact_params.

Source code in eden/entities/base.py 
def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: EntityOptions):
    self._options = options
    self._env = env
    self._is_attached = False
    self._attachment_parent: Entity | None = None
    self.is_heterogeneous = isinstance(self._options, GroupedEntityOptions)
    # Heterogeneous only: each env's own variant default pose, (num_envs, 3) / (num_envs, 4).
    self._variant_default_root_pos: torch.Tensor | None = None
    self._variant_default_root_quat: torch.Tensor | None = None
    # Heterogeneous only: the variant each env holds, (num_envs,) long, and the first env holding each variant
    # present (all of them, unless there are fewer envs than variants).
    self._env_variant_idx: torch.Tensor | None = None
    self._variant_first_envs: list[int] = []
    # Heterogeneous only: each present variant's value for a per-variant field they differ in; a field
    # they all resolve alike is mirrored as that one value instead. And each variant's material, present or
    # not, so the checks on it do not depend on the env count.
    self._variant_fields: dict[str, list] = {}
    self._variant_materials: list[MaterialLike] | None = None

    # Create morph from options if not already set
    if not self.is_heterogeneous:
        self._create_morph_from_options()
    else:
        self._create_grouped_morphs_from_options()

    # Mirror options onto the instance. Entity does not delegate __init__ to
    # ConfigurableMixin -- see mirror_options_onto's docstring for why, and for the
    # aliasing this protects against. Unlike the mixin, Entity sets no ``_uid``: its
    # ``uid`` is the wrapped Genesis entity's, so there is nothing to seed here.
    # SupportSurfaceMixin's attributes need no skip list -- get_parameter_names() walks
    # only ConfigurableMixin bases, so they never show up here.
    mirror_options_onto(self, self._options)
    if self.is_heterogeneous:
        self._resolve_variant_fields()

    # forward_vec is derived from the options' front direction (single source of truth);
    # entities without a front (e.g. primitives) keep the class default.
    self.forward_vec = getattr(self._options, "front", self.forward_vec)
    self.forward_vec = torch.tensor(self.forward_vec, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=self.device).unsqueeze(0)
    self.default_root_pos = torch.tensor(self.default_root_pos, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=self.device).unsqueeze(0)
    self.default_root_quat = torch.tensor(
        self.default_root_quat,
        dtype=gs.tc_float,
        device=self.device,
    ).unsqueeze(0)

def get_contacts(
    self, with_entity: Entity | None = None, exclude_self_contact: bool = False, is_padded: bool = False
):
    """Contact records of this body, optionally filtered to the pair with ``with_entity``.

    Requires ``MochiOptions.record_contacts`` (the default). Each record carries both sides'
    entities/links/geoms (-1 where a side is deformable), the deformable-side vertices and
    barycentric weights, position, unit normal (away from side B), signed distance, force on
    A and quadrature weight. Shapes are ``(n_envs, n_contacts, ...)`` when batched.

    Parameters
    ----------
    with_entity : Entity, optional
        Restrict to contacts with this (Eden) entity. Defaults to None (all partners).
    exclude_self_contact : bool, optional
        Drop contacts between two links of this entity. Defaults to False.
    is_padded : bool, optional
        Return fixed-size padded arrays with a ``valid_mask``, the invalid slots' floating-point fields zeroed;
        taken regardless while the env's graded phase runs under a CUDA graph (see
        :meth:`~eden.entities.base.Entity._query_contacts`). Defaults to False.
    """
    partner = None if with_entity is None else with_entity._entity
    return self._query_contacts(
        lambda padded: self._entity.get_contacts(
            with_entity=partner, exclude_self_contact=exclude_self_contact, is_padded=padded
        ),
        is_padded,
    )

MochiSoftEntity(env: EnvBase, options: EntityOptions)

Bases: Entity

A tetrahedral solid, thin shell or rod simulated by the MochiSolver.

Vertex-based like :class:FEMEntity: no links, DOFs or rigid pose. get_pos is the vertex centroid, get_quat the identity, and set_quat raises — bake the orientation into default_root_quat (the morph) instead. Four calls are pre-build only because they change what the solver assembles: :meth:attach_to_link, :meth:set_visual_mesh, :meth:set_contact_skin and :meth:set_rest_positions. Register them with env.register_pre_build_hook so they run after scene.add_entity (when :attr:init_positions exists) and before scene.build()::

env.register_pre_build_hook(lambda: finger.attach_to_link(gripper, "finger_link", verts_idx))
env.build()

:meth:set_visual_mesh goes through the morph transform, so it must precede :meth:set_rest_positions (it raises otherwise). :meth:set_contact_skin cannot be combined with :meth:set_rest_positions in either order (both raise). :meth:attach_to_link only records indices and can go anywhere in the hook.

docs.title: attach_to
docs.text:
attach_to(entity: Entity, link_name: str, attach_offset=None, attach_quat=None) -> None

Mount this body on a link of a Mochi rigid entity — what SceneOptions.attachments_dict calls.

The mounting transform has the meaning it has for :meth:RigidEntity.attach_to: the body's own frame (its default_root_pos / default_root_quat frame, in which a primitive is centred) sits at (attach_offset, attach_quat) in the link frame, defaulting to default_root_pos / default_root_quat. The vertices of the face nearest the link origin — those within :data:MOUNT_FACE_TOLERANCE of the extreme along the line from the body centre to the link origin — are tied to the link by :meth:attach_to_link; the rest of the body hangs off them and deforms. A sponge mounted under a gripper is {"sponge": ("robot", "hand", (0, 0, 0.13), (1, 0, 0, 0))}. Each tie is :data:MOUNT_TIE_TO_MATERIAL times as stiff as the body's material is at one vertex. Only tetrahedral solids mount this way; a shell or a rod raises.

The solver anchors each tied vertex in the link frame of the build configuration (every joint at zero), so the rest geometry is placed there before the build, and :meth:post_build then carries the whole body to wherever the parent's default joint positions put the link.

def attach_to(
    self,
    entity: Entity,
    link_name: str,
    attach_offset=None,
    attach_quat=None,
) -> None:
    """Mount this body on a link of a Mochi rigid entity — what ``SceneOptions.attachments_dict`` calls.

    The mounting transform has the meaning it has for :meth:`RigidEntity.attach_to`: the body's own
    frame (its ``default_root_pos`` / ``default_root_quat`` frame, in which a primitive is centred) sits
    at ``(attach_offset, attach_quat)`` in the link frame, defaulting to ``default_root_pos`` /
    ``default_root_quat``. The vertices of the face nearest the link origin — those within
    :data:`MOUNT_FACE_TOLERANCE` of the extreme along the line from the body centre to the link
    origin — are tied to the link by :meth:`attach_to_link`; the rest of the body hangs off them and
    deforms. A sponge mounted under a gripper is ``{"sponge": ("robot", "hand", (0, 0, 0.13), (1, 0, 0, 0))}``.
    Each tie is :data:`MOUNT_TIE_TO_MATERIAL` times as stiff as the body's material is at one vertex. Only
    tetrahedral solids mount this way; a shell or a rod raises.

    The solver anchors each tied vertex in the link frame of the *build* configuration (every joint at
    zero), so the rest geometry is placed there before the build, and :meth:`post_build` then carries the
    whole body to wherever the parent's default joint positions put the link.
    """
    if not isinstance(self.material, en.materials.MochiElasticMaterialOptions):
        raise NotImplementedError(
            f"MochiSoftEntity '{self.name}' is a {type(self.material).__name__} body; attachments_dict mounts "
            f"tetrahedral solids (MochiElasticMaterialOptions) only. Tie a shell or rod to a link with "
            f"`attach_to_link(...)` from `env.register_pre_build_hook(...)`, choosing the vertices yourself."
        )
    if not isinstance(entity, MochiRigidEntity):
        raise TypeError(
            f"MochiSoftEntity '{self.name}' can only be mounted on a Mochi rigid entity, but its parent "
            f"'{entity.name}' is a {type(entity).__name__}: a Mochi scene holds Mochi bodies only. Give "
            f"'{entity.name}' `material=MochiRigidMaterialOptions(...)`."
        )
    mount_pos = np.asarray(self._options.default_root_pos if attach_offset is None else attach_offset)
    mount_quat = np.asarray(self._options.default_root_quat if attach_quat is None else attach_quat)
    if np.linalg.norm(mount_pos) < MOUNT_FACE_TOLERANCE:
        raise ValueError(
            f"MochiSoftEntity '{self.name}' is mounted with its centre at the origin of link '{link_name}' "
            f"(offset {tuple(mount_pos.tolist())}), so no face of it is nearest the link and none can be "
            f"tied. Offset the body to sit against the link, e.g. attach_offset=(0, 0, <half its height>)."
        )

    def _do_attach():
        gs_link = _get_link_or_raise(entity, link_name)
        # Rest geometry in the body frame, the mesh as authored (scaled) about its own origin. The morph rotated
        # it about its vertex centroid, not about default_root_pos, so undo exactly that placement.
        rest_world = np.asarray(self.init_positions, dtype=gs.np_float)
        morph_pos = np.asarray(self._entity.morph.pos, dtype=gs.np_float)
        verts_body = (self._entity.world_to_morph_frame(rest_world) - morph_pos).astype(gs.np_float)
        verts_link = gs_utils_geom.transform_by_trans_quat(
            verts_body, mount_pos.astype(gs.np_float), mount_quat.astype(gs.np_float)
        )
        tied = _mount_face(verts_link)
        if len(tied) < 3:
            raise ValueError(
                f"MochiSoftEntity '{self.name}': only {len(tied)} vertex(es) lie on the face nearest link "
                f"'{link_name}', too few to hold the body. Refine the mesh, or rotate the body so a face "
                f"(not an edge or corner) points at the link."
            )
        link_pos, link_quat = _link_build_pose(gs_link)
        self.set_rest_positions(gs_utils_geom.transform_by_trans_quat(verts_link, link_pos, link_quat))
        extent = verts_link.max(axis=0) - verts_link.min(axis=0)
        spacing = float(np.prod(extent) / len(verts_link)) ** (1.0 / 3.0)
        stiffness = MOUNT_TIE_TO_MATERIAL * self.material.E * spacing
        self._entity.attach_to_link(gs_link, tied, stiffness=stiffness, damping=MOUNT_DAMPING)
        self._mount = (entity, link_name, verts_link)

    self._env.register_pre_build_hook(_do_attach)
    self._is_attached = True
    self._attachment_parent = entity

def post_build(self) -> None:
    """Carry a mounted body from the build pose of its link to the link's current pose."""
    if self._mount is None:
        return
    parent, link_name, verts_link = self._mount
    link = parent.get_link(link_name)
    verts = torch.as_tensor(verts_link, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=self.device)
    verts = verts.unsqueeze(0).expand(self._env.num_envs, -1, -1)
    pos = link.get_pos().unsqueeze(1).expand_as(verts)
    quat = link.get_quat().unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, verts.shape[1], -1)
    world = gs_utils_geom.transform_by_trans_quat(verts, pos, quat)
    self.set_vertex_positions(world)
    self.set_vertex_velocities(torch.zeros_like(world))

@gs.assert_unbuilt
def set_rest_positions(self, positions) -> None:
    """Move the body's rest geometry before the scene is built (pre-build only).

    The build reads :attr:`init_positions` to fill the solver, and :meth:`attach_to_link` anchors each
    vertex in the frame of the link it coincides with *at build time* — so a soft body mounted on a link
    whose pose is only known once the model is parsed is placed here, from a pre-build hook, rather than
    through the morph. ``positions`` must have the body's own vertex count and ordering.

    Call :meth:`set_visual_mesh` *before* this, not after: it places the render mesh through the morph
    transform and binds it to the tetrahedra by barycentric coordinates, which then carry it along.

    Parameters
    ----------
    positions : array_like
        World rest positions, shape ``(n_vertices, 3)``.
    """
    self._require_added("set_rest_positions")
    if self._has_contact_skin:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"MochiSoftEntity '{self.name}': set_rest_positions() cannot follow set_contact_skin(). The skin "
            f"is placed through the morph transform but embedded in the tetrahedra only at build, so moved "
            f"rest positions leave it outside the body and its contact samples act from the wrong place. "
            f"Swapping the two calls does not help either: place the body through the morph "
            f"(`default_root_pos` / `default_root_quat`) to keep the skin, or drop the skin."
        )
    positions = np.asarray(positions, dtype=self._entity.init_positions.dtype)
    if positions.shape != self._entity.init_positions.shape:
        raise ValueError(
            f"MochiSoftEntity '{self.name}'.set_rest_positions expects "
            f"{self._entity.init_positions.shape}, got {positions.shape}."
        )
    self._entity.init_positions = positions
    self._rest_positions_moved = True

def set_visual_mesh(self, file: str, pos=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), euler=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), scale: float = 1.0) -> None:
    """Skin a detailed render mesh onto the simulation tetrahedra (solids only, pre-build only).

    ``pos`` / ``euler`` / ``scale`` place the render mesh in the *simulation mesh's file frame*; the
    entity's morph transform is then applied to it, and each of its vertices is bound to the tetrahedron
    it falls in by barycentric coordinates, so it follows the deformation. Because the placement goes
    through the morph, this must run *before* :meth:`set_rest_positions` — which raises here if it
    already ran, rather than leaving a render mesh embedded against geometry that has since moved away
    (the visual mesh then extrapolates far outside the body, and the body renders as nothing).

    Parameters
    ----------
    file : str
        Mesh file (resolved through :func:`eden.utils.assets.get_asset_path`).
    pos : array-like[float, float, float], optional
        Offset of the render mesh in the simulation mesh's file frame. Defaults to zero.
    euler : array-like[float, float, float], optional
        Rotation of the render mesh in degrees. Defaults to zero.
    scale : float, optional
        Uniform scale of the render mesh. Defaults to 1.0.
    """
    self._require_added("set_visual_mesh")
    if self._rest_positions_moved:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"MochiSoftEntity '{self.name}': set_visual_mesh() must be called before "
            f"set_rest_positions(). The render mesh is placed through the morph transform and embedded "
            f"in the tetrahedra as they stand now, so embedding it after the rest geometry has moved "
            f"binds it to the wrong place. Swap the two calls: the barycentric embedding carries the "
            f"render mesh along when the rest positions move."
        )
    self._entity.set_visual_mesh(file=get_asset_path(file), pos=pos, euler=euler, scale=scale)

def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: CameraOptions, key: str = ""):
    self._uid = gs.UID()
    self._options = options
    self._env = env
    #: The camera's key in ``EnvBase.cameras`` ("" when built outside an env). Not ``name``, which a configurable
    #: already has: its class's registry-style name, ``"camera"``.
    self.key = key

    # CameraOptions declares every Camera parameter, so today this only ever takes the
    # options branch -- the class-default fallback is unreachable here. It is still routed
    # through the shared helper so a parameter added to Camera/SplatCamera but not to the
    # options (``overlays`` is a mutable class default) cannot reintroduce the
    # aliasing (see mirror_options_onto).
    mirror_options_onto(self, self._options)

    # Resolve cam_intrinsic → override cam_fov / cam_resolution on self
    if self._options.cam_intrinsic is not None:
        intrinsic = self._options.cam_intrinsic
        assert intrinsic.shape == (3, 3), "`cam_intrinsic` should be a 3x3 matrix"
        en.logger.warning("`cam_intrinsic` is provided, ignoring `cam_fov` and `cam_resolution`")
        self.cam_fov = resolved_cam_fov(self._options)
        self.cam_resolution = (
            int(math.ceil(intrinsic[0, 2] * 2)),
            int(math.ceil(intrinsic[1, 2] * 2)),
        )
        en.logger.info(
            f"Using `cam_intrinsic` to set `cam_fov`: {self.cam_fov} and `cam_resolution`: {self.cam_resolution}"
        )

    # Resolve cam_extrinsic → override cam_pos / cam_lookat / cam_up on self
    if self._options.cam_extrinsic is not None:
        extrinsic = self._options.cam_extrinsic
        assert extrinsic.shape == (4, 4), "`cam_extrinsic` should be a 4x4 matrix"
        en.logger.warning("`cam_extrinsic` is provided, ignoring `cam_pos`, `cam_lookat`, and `cam_up`")
        T = np.linalg.inv(extrinsic)
        pos, lookat, up = T_to_pos_lookat_up(T)
        self.cam_pos = tuple(pos)
        self.cam_lookat = tuple(lookat)
        self.cam_up = tuple(up)

    # Validate follow vs attach
    if self._options.follow_entity_name != "":
        assert self._options.attach_entity_name == "", (
            "`attach_entity_name` should be empty if `follow_entity_name` is provided"
        )
        assert self._options.attach_link_name == "", (
            "`attach_link_name` should be empty if `follow_entity_name` is provided"
        )
        assert self._options.attach_offset is None, (
            "`attach_offset` should be None if `follow_entity_name` is provided"
        )
        assert self._options.attach_quat is None, "`attach_quat` should be None if `follow_entity_name` is provided"
    elif self._options.attach_entity_name != "":
        assert self._options.follow_entity_name == "", (
            "`follow_entity_name` should be empty if `attach_entity_name` is provided"
        )
        assert self._options.attach_link_name != "", (
            "`attach_link_name` should be provided if `attach_entity_name` is provided"
        )
        assert self._options.attach_offset is not None, (
            "`attach_offset` should be provided if `attach_entity_name` is provided"
        )
        assert self._options.attach_quat is not None, (
            "`attach_quat` should be provided if `attach_entity_name` is provided"
        )

    # Compute attach_T from offset/quat (stored on self, not options)
    if self._options.attach_entity_name != "" and self._options.attach_offset is not None:
        self.attach_T = trans_quat_to_T(
            np.array(self._options.attach_offset),
            np.array(self._options.attach_quat),
        )

    # Determine backend: sensor (add_sensor) vs legacy (add_camera)
    self._sensor_options = self._options.sensor_options
    self._cam = None  # Legacy camera object (set in pre_build)
    self._sensor = None  # Sensor object (set in pre_build)
    # Video recording is Eden-owned for both backends: one frame per render call,
    # streamed to file (see start_recording).
    self._recording: _Recording | None = None

    # Constructed now, so an unknown overlay or a misspelled parameter fails at env construction; built in a
    # post-build hook, once the managers they read exist.
    self._overlays: list[CameraOverlay] = [
        build_camera_overlay(self, overlay_options, i) for i, overlay_options in enumerate(self.overlays)
    ]
    composites = [type(overlay).__name__ for overlay in self._overlays if isinstance(overlay, BackgroundComposite)]
    if len(composites) > 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Camera {self.display_name}: CameraOptions.overlays declares {len(composites)} background composites "
            f"({composites}); a camera has one background. Keep one, and list in its entities every entity it "
            "should replace."
        )
    self._overlays_built = False
    self._frame_envs_idx_cache: dict[tuple[int, bool], torch.Tensor] = {}

set_attach_transform(offset_T) -> None

Replace the camera-to-link attach transform declared via attach_offset/attach_quat.

Accepts a single (4, 4) transform or a batched (n_rendered, 4, 4) stack for per-env camera mounts (camera-extrinsics domain randomization): Genesis composes the attached pose as link_T @ offset_T, which broadcasts over a batched offset. A batched offset requires a batched camera (batch renderer or env_separate_rigid) and one transform per rendered env — anything else would only crash later, deep inside the next render, so it is rejected here.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION offset_T

def set_attach_transform(self, offset_T) -> None:
    """Replace the camera-to-link attach transform declared via ``attach_offset``/``attach_quat``.

    Accepts a single ``(4, 4)`` transform or a batched ``(n_rendered, 4, 4)`` stack for
    per-env camera mounts (camera-extrinsics domain randomization): Genesis composes the
    attached pose as ``link_T @ offset_T``, which broadcasts over a batched offset. A
    batched offset requires a batched camera (batch renderer or ``env_separate_rigid``)
    and one transform per rendered env — anything else would only crash later, deep
    inside the next render, so it is rejected here.

    Parameters
    ----------
    offset_T : torch.Tensor | np.ndarray
        The new camera pose(s) relative to the attached link, shape ``(4, 4)`` or
        ``(n_rendered, 4, 4)``.
    """
    if self._uses_sensor_backend:
        raise NotImplementedError(
            "set_attach_transform() is not supported with the sensor backend. "
            "Use the legacy camera backend (remove sensor_options from CameraOptions)."
        )
    if self.attach_entity_name == "":
        raise RuntimeError(
            "set_attach_transform() requires an attached camera — declare "
            "attach_entity_name/attach_link_name (+ attach_offset/attach_quat) in CameraOptions."
        )
    shape = tuple(offset_T.shape)
    if shape[-2:] != (4, 4) or len(shape) not in (2, 3):
        raise ValueError(f"offset_T must be (4, 4) or (n_rendered, 4, 4), got {shape}.")
    if len(shape) == 3:
        # Genesis composes batched poses only for a batched camera, over exactly the
        # rendered envs; a mismatch here surfaces as an opaque matmul/set_pose error
        # inside the next render (and a stray (1, 4, 4) would silently broadcast).
        if not self._cam._is_batched:
            raise ValueError(
                f"offset_T is batched ({shape}) but camera {self.display_name} is not batched — "
                "batched mounts need the batch renderer or env_separate_rigid."
            )
        n_rendered = len(self._env.scene.visualizer._context.rendered_envs_idx)
        if shape[0] != n_rendered:
            raise ValueError(
                f"offset_T has batch size {shape[0]} but the camera renders {n_rendered} envs "
                "(rendered_envs_idx) — provide one transform per rendered env."
            )
    rigid_link = self._env.entities[self.attach_entity_name].get_link(self.attach_link_name)
    self._cam.attach(rigid_link, offset_T)
    self.attach_T = offset_T

def set_quat(self, quat, envs_idx=None):
    """Set the camera orientation from a quaternion (wxyz), keeping current position.

    Parameters
    ----------
    quat : array-like, shape (4,) or (N, 4)
        Quaternion in (w, x, y, z) format.
    envs_idx : array-like, optional
        Environment indices. If None, applies to all environments.
    """
    if self._uses_sensor_backend:
        raise NotImplementedError("set_quat() is not supported with the sensor backend.")
    if self.is_attached:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Cannot set orientation on an attached camera. Detach it first or modify the attachment offset."
        )
    # Genesis keeps the camera pose on the host in float64 numpy
    # (https://github.com/Genesis-Embodied-AI/Genesis/pull/3571), so the quaternion and the env index join it there.
    quat = tensor_to_array(quat, dtype=np.float64)
    if envs_idx is None:
        idx = ()
    else:
        # Raises on a malformed or out-of-range index, naming it; any accepted form becomes an index tensor, a mask
        # stays a mask.
        envs_idx = sanitize_envs_idx(envs_idx, self._env.num_envs, prefer_slice=False)
        # A device index costs one sync whatever is done here, since Genesis' set_pose brings envs_idx to the host
        # too: this copy waits for the queued work, and the one in set_pose finds none left.
        idx = tensor_to_array(envs_idx)
    # Use internal _pos (without envs_offset) to match set_pose's coordinate space
    pos = self._cam._pos[idx]
    T = trans_quat_to_T(pos, quat)
    self._cam.set_pose(transform=T, envs_idx=envs_idx)

Open a video file and record one frame per render() / render_rgb() call.

Frames are encoded and streamed to the file as they are rendered, so the recording length is not bounded by memory. The output path and framerate are fixed for the whole video, hence given here rather than at stop_recording().

A camera that renders several environments at once (batch renderer, or env_separate_rigid) records one video per environment, named {stem}_{i}{ext} after the environment's position in the rendered batch.

TYPE: str DEFAULT: None

fps

Framerate the video is encoded at. Must be positive. Playback speed is fps render calls per second, whatever the simulation timestep.

def start_recording(self, video_path: str | None = None, fps: float = 60.0):
    """Open a video file and record one frame per ``render()`` / ``render_rgb()`` call.

    Frames are encoded and streamed to the file as they are rendered, so the
    recording length is not bounded by memory. The output path and framerate are
    fixed for the whole video, hence given here rather than at ``stop_recording()``.

    One frame per render call is Eden's recording contract: a kinematic replay that
    never steps the scene records exactly as a stepped rollout does. Genesis' own
    ``camera.start_recording`` instead captures inside ``scene.step()``, which would
    record nothing for a replay script.

    A camera that renders several environments at once (batch renderer, or
    ``env_separate_rigid``) records one video per environment, named
    ``{stem}_{i}{ext}`` after the environment's position in the rendered batch.

    Parameters
    ----------
    video_path : str, optional
        Output video file path, ending in '.mp4'. Defaults to
        ``{log_dir}/video_{timestamp}.mp4``.
    fps : float, optional
        Framerate the video is encoded at. Must be positive. Playback speed is
        ``fps`` render calls per second, whatever the simulation timestep.
    """
    if self._recording is not None:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Already recording to '{self._recording.path}'. Call stop_recording() first.")
    # Checked here rather than left to the encoder: a non-positive framerate otherwise
    # surfaces as a PyAV error on the first frame, deep inside the render loop.
    if fps <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"Framerate of a recording must be positive; got fps={fps}.")

    self._recording = _Recording(path=video_path or f"{en.log_dir}/video_{get_now()}.mp4", fps=fps)

Finalize the video file(s) named by :meth:start_recording.

Frames are encoded as they are recorded, so this only flushes the ones the encoders still hold and closes the files.

A recording that captured no frame writes no file at all. That is said out loud rather than passed over: it means nothing rendered while the recording was open, which is a mistake in the calling loop far more often than an intent.

Source code in eden/entities/camera.py 
def stop_recording(self):
    """Finalize the video file(s) named by :meth:`start_recording`.

    Frames are encoded as they are recorded, so this only flushes the ones the
    encoders still hold and closes the files.

    A recording that captured no frame writes no file at all. That is said out loud
    rather than passed over: it means nothing rendered while the recording was open,
    which is a mistake in the calling loop far more often than an intent.
    """
    if self._recording is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Recording not started. Call start_recording(video_path, fps) first — the output path and "
            "framerate belong to start_recording(), not stop_recording()."
        )

    recording, self._recording = self._recording, None

    if not recording.encoders:
        en.logger.warning(
            f"Recording to '{recording.path}' captured no frame, so no video was written. Frames are "
            "captured by render() / render_rgb() — a recording that never renders produces nothing."
        )
        return

    # Every file is finalized before any failure is raised, so one environment failing to
    # encode leaves neither the others open nor the camera unable to record. The first
    # failure is the one raised: a later one is as likely to be its consequence.
    error = None
    for encoder in recording.encoders:
        try:
            encoder.close()
        except gs.GenesisException as e:
            error = error or e
    if error is not None:
        raise error

destroy() -> None

Finalize a recording still running, as part of tearing the camera down.

This is what makes stopping a recording explicitly optional: a camera going away leaves a playable video behind rather than a file the encoder never flushed.

Source code in eden/entities/camera.py 
def destroy(self) -> None:
    """Finalize a recording still running, as part of tearing the camera down.

    This is what makes stopping a recording explicitly optional: a camera going away
    leaves a playable video behind rather than a file the encoder never flushed.
    """
    if self._recording is None:
        return
    try:
        self.stop_recording()
    except gs.GenesisException as e:
        # Teardown carries on regardless, so a video failing to encode takes neither
        # the other cameras nor the scene down with it. The error was already reported
        # by the encoder when it happened.
        en.logger.warning(f"{e}")

def render_unshadowed_rgb(self) -> torch.Tensor | None:
    """This view rendered again with the scene's shadows off, ``(N, H, W, 3)`` on the env's device, which lets
    :func:`~eden.utils.background_shadows.background_shadow_factor` compare every pixel with its own unshadowed
    brightness; ``None`` when the renderer can't (the batch renderer bakes shadows in at build time, and the
    factor then estimates the unshadowed brightness instead).
    """
    if self.renderer_kind != "rasterizer":
        return None
    with _rasterizer_shadows_off(self._env.scene.visualizer):
        rgb = numpy_to_tensor(self._cam.render(rgb=True)[0], device=self._env.device)
    return (rgb if rgb.ndim == 4 else rgb[None])[..., :3]

def render_rgb(self):
    """The camera's RGB frame, with its background composite and overlays painted on, recorded if recording."""
    if self._uses_sensor_backend:
        rgb_out = self._sensor.read().rgb
        # A sensor read is a view into a cache the next step() repopulates, so the
        # recording needs its own copy of it (see _record_frame). The view itself is
        # what is returned, as callers of a sensor read expect.
        return self._finish_frame(rgb_out, may_alias=True)

    # The segmentation comes from the same render as the RGB, so an overlay that reads it costs no extra pass.
    segmentation = self._paints and any(overlay._needs_segmentation for overlay in self._overlays)
    rgb_out, _, segm, _ = self._render(rgb=True, segmentation=segmentation)
    return self._finish_frame(rgb_out, segmentation=segm)

docs.title: Camera overlays
docs.text:
Overlays paint state the scene does not render (ink, marks) or composite a background onto every RGB frame a camera produces. Declare them in CameraOptions.overlays.

Camera overlays: paint what the simulation tracks but does not render onto every RGB frame a camera produces.

Some state a task keeps is visible in the real world but has no geometry in the scene: the ink a marker lays on a whiteboard, the strokes a brush leaves on paper. The task tracks it as a tensor, so a plain camera shows a clean surface. An overlay draws that tensor onto the camera's frames after the renderer has made them.

A camera declares its overlays in :attr:CameraOptions.overlays <eden.options.camera.CameraOptions>, by registry key, so they survive a saved config.json. They are applied in :meth:Camera.render_rgb <eden.entities.camera.Camera.render_rgb> and so reach everything built on it: the returned frame, the camera's recording, :meth:~eden.entities.camera.Camera.snapshot, and an observation that reads the camera. :meth:~eden.entities.camera.Camera.render stays the raw multi-output pass.

A background composite is an overlay too: :class:BackgroundImageComposite replaces a camera's background with an image, :class:SplatComposite with a Gaussian splat (a splat env's cameras). Both replace the pixels where the sim shows one of their entities or nothing at all, and report them through :meth:CameraOverlay.replaced_pixels; the overlays after them leave those pixels as composited, since they no longer show the sim surface an overlay locates its marks on. A camera takes at most one; declare it first, so the overlays after it paint over the composited frame. A splat env's camera shows its splat only when it declares a SplatComposite, as a splat config's :meth:~eden.utils.configs.EdenSplatConfig.recording_camera does.

Writing one: subclass :class:CameraOverlay, declare its parameters as class attributes, register it with @CAMERA_OVERLAY_REGISTRY.register(), and implement :meth:CameraOverlay.paint. Set _needs_segmentation = True to receive the frame's segmentation, which the sim pass renders with the RGB at no extra render. Set _needs_pointcloud = True to receive the frame's world-frame point cloud; the camera renders it once per frame for all its overlays, which costs a second render of the view (its depth). A camera that can render neither (the sensor backend) refuses such an overlay at env construction. Resolve whatever the overlay reads (a metric term, an entity) in :meth:CameraOverlay.build, which runs after the managers are built. Frames rendered before then (the observation manager renders once while it loads, to size its terms) are not painted.

:class:PlanePaintOverlay is the general one: it paints the :class:PaintedPlane a metric term returns (any :class:PaintedPlaneSource), a weight grid on a plane, where the camera sees that plane. It shades the marks as the surface they lie on is shaded, so they keep the shadows and the light the renderer gave that surface.

docs.text:
PlanePaintOverlay(camera: Camera, options: CameraOverlayOptions)

Bases: CameraOverlay

Paints a metric's marks, in color or in their own colours, where the camera sees the plane they lie on.

The metric term metric_name is a :class:PaintedPlaneSource: its painted_plane(envs_idx) is read at every frame for the envs the frame shows only, so a camera over one env never computes the marks of the other thousand. A pixel is on the plane when its world point (from the frame's point cloud, so whatever stands in front hides the marks) lies within max_gap of it. Each pixel is looked up on a supersample x supersample grid of sub-pixels and averaged, since a mark a few millimetres wide can be thinner than a pixel; only the pixels round the grid's image are, so the sub-pixel buffers scale with the marks' footprint in the frame, not with the frame.

A curved surface qualifies when, over the grid, it stays within max_gap of the plane touching it, and its distances along the surface differ from the plane's by well under a cell: the marks are then painted where they lie. A narrow stripe round a tube's crown does (mochi_wipe_the_bar); a mark wrapping round it would not.

The marks are shaded as their surface is. A mark is a change of colour on the surface the metric names (:attr:PaintedPlane.entity_name), so it takes the light that surface's pixel took: the shadow the brush casts over a stroke, the falloff across the sheet, the light's tint. The renderer draws a matte surface as its colour times the light reaching it, so a marked pixel is the rendered pixel times color / surface colour, blended by how much of the pixel is marked: rendered * lerp(1, color / surface colour, weight). The surface colour is read from the built entity, which therefore has to be one plain colour (an image texture is refused at build), and no channel of it may be under :data:MIN_SURFACE_CHANNEL, below which the division amplifies the frame's 8-bit steps into visible banding. A channel the scaling lifts past 255 is clipped.

The multiplication is in each renderer's own colour space, as measured: on the rasterizer the pixel itself is the colour times the light, while the batch renderer multiplies in linear light and encodes its pixels as sRGB, so there the tint applies to the decoded pixel. Other renderers (the ray tracer, whose colour response has not been measured) are refused at build. A surface that cannot be shaded against is refused too, with no flat-colour fallback: an image-textured or multi-coloured surface (paint marks onto a plain-coloured entity laid over it).

The one thing the ratio cannot carry is light a surface reflects on top of its colour: a highlight, or the white sheen the rasterizer's default plastic surface adds in direct light (about 20 of 255 under the default lights, whatever the colour). It is scaled with the mark's colour, so in direct light a dark mark renders without it, up to about that much darker in its dark channels than a surface of the mark's colour would. In shadow, where there is no sheen, the marks match such a surface to within a level or two.

Marks of one colour (an ink's) are painted in color, the camera's to choose, not the metric's: grading never reads it. A task's :meth:~eden.utils.configs.EdenConfig.recording_camera fills it from wherever the task keeps it (the whiteboard marker's ink). Marks of many colours (a painting's) come with their colours (:attr:PaintedPlane.rgb), each shaded as color is, and color is then left out.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION metric_name

The metric term whose painted_plane() is painted.

TYPE: str

color

RGB in [0, 1] of the marks, as the surface's colour is given: a mark at full weight renders as the surface would in this colour. Required for marks of one colour (no colour is right for every mark); left out for marks that come with their own (:attr:PaintedPlane.rgb).

TYPE: tuple[float, float, float] | None

max_gap

How far (m) a pixel's world point may lie off the plane and still be painted. Covers the depth buffer's error at the camera's distance, and a curved surface's sag from its plane.

TYPE: float

supersample

Sub-pixels per side each pixel is looked up on.

def build(self) -> None:
    # Deferred: the managers import the entities, so a module-scope import here would be a cycle.
    from eden.managers.terms.utils import resolve_metric_manager

    manager = resolve_metric_manager(self._env, term="PlanePaintOverlay", metric_name=self.metric_name)
    metric = manager.get_term(self.metric_name)
    if not isinstance(metric, PaintedPlaneSource):
        raise TypeError(
            f"PlanePaintOverlay paints the marks a metric term returns from painted_plane(envs_idx), but metric "
            f"'{self.metric_name}' ({type(metric).__name__}) has no painted_plane(). Set metric_name to a metric "
            f"that keeps marks on a plane (active metrics: {manager.active_terms}); a metric class term becomes "
            "one by defining painted_plane(envs_idx) returning eden.entities.camera_overlays.PaintedPlane."
        )
    self._metric = metric
    # One env's worth, to check the contract here rather than on the first frame.
    plane = metric.painted_plane(torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.long, device=self._env.device))
    subject = f"PlanePaintOverlay: metric '{self.metric_name}' ({type(metric).__name__}) returned a PaintedPlane"
    if plane.rgb is None and self._rgb is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{subject} of marks of one colour (rgb=None), and the overlay has no color to paint them in. "
            "Configure color=(r, g, b) in [0, 1]: a task's recording_camera() passes the colour it keeps (the "
            "whiteboard marker's ink)."
        )
    if plane.rgb is not None and self._rgb is not None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{subject} with the marks' own colours (rgb), so color={self.color!r} would never be painted. Leave "
            "color out for this metric."
        )
    if plane.rgb is not None and tuple(plane.rgb.shape) != (1, *plane.grid.shape, 3):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{subject} with rgb {tuple(plane.rgb.shape)} for one env; expected (1, *grid.shape, 3) = "
            f"{(1, *plane.grid.shape, 3)}, a colour per cell of the grid it returned."
        )
    if plane.rgb is not None and not plane.rgb.is_floating_point():
        raise ValueError(
            f"{subject} with rgb of dtype {plane.rgb.dtype}; the marks' colours must be floating, in [0, 1]. An "
            "8-bit image would tint by its 0-255 values: divide it by 255 first."
        )
    if tuple(plane.weight.shape) != (1, *plane.grid.shape):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{subject} with weight {tuple(plane.weight.shape)} for one env; expected (1, *grid.shape) = "
            f"{(1, *plane.grid.shape)}, one grid per env asked for, on the PlaneGrid it returned."
        )
    if not (plane.weight.dtype == torch.bool or plane.weight.is_floating_point()):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{subject} weight of dtype {plane.weight.dtype}; it must be floating, in [0, 1], or bool (a cell "
            "marked or not). An integer grid has no scale the overlay could read: divide it by its full value "
            "first."
        )
    axes = torch.stack([plane.u_axis, plane.v_axis])
    if not torch.allclose(axes @ axes.T, torch.eye(2, device=axes.device), atol=1e-5):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{subject} with axes u_axis={plane.u_axis.tolist()}, v_axis={plane.v_axis.tolist()}, which are not "
            "orthonormal; the plane test and the cell lookup measure metres along them. Return unit, "
            f"perpendicular axes from {type(metric).__name__}.painted_plane()."
        )
    renderer = self._camera.renderer_kind
    if renderer not in _PIXEL_ENCODING:
        raise ValueError(
            f"PlanePaintOverlay on camera {self._camera.display_name}, whose frames come from the {renderer}. The "
            "overlay shades marks by how the renderer turns a surface's colour into pixels, which is measured for "
            f"the {' and the '.join(k.replace('_', ' ') for k in _PIXEL_ENCODING)} only. Record this camera with "
            "one of those."
        )
    self._srgb = _PIXEL_ENCODING[renderer] == "srgb"
    surface = _plain_surface_rgb(self._env, plane.entity_name, subject=f"{subject} on entity")
    if min(surface) < MIN_SURFACE_CHANNEL:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{subject} on entity '{plane.entity_name}', whose colour {surface} has a channel under "
            f"{MIN_SURFACE_CHANNEL}. The marks are shaded as the surface is, by dividing its rendered pixels by its "
            "colour, and so dark a channel turns the frame's 8-bit steps into visible bands. Lighten the "
            f"surface's colour to at least {MIN_SURFACE_CHANNEL} per channel."
        )
    # A marked pixel is the surface's rendered pixel times the mark's colour over this, at full weight.
    self._surface = torch.tensor(surface, device=self._env.device)
    self._color = None if self._rgb is None else torch.tensor(self._rgb, device=self._env.device)

def paint(self, rgb: torch.Tensor, buffers: OverlayBuffers, envs_idx: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    plane: PaintedPlane = self._metric.painted_plane(envs_idx)
    marks = plane.weight.float()  # a bool or half grid, as build() allows
    rows, cols = plane.grid.shape
    offset = buffers.pointcloud - plane.origin
    u, v = (offset * plane.u_axis).sum(-1), (offset * plane.v_axis).sum(-1)
    gap = (offset * torch.linalg.cross(plane.u_axis, plane.v_axis)).sum(-1)
    on_plane = buffers.pointcloud_valid & (gap.abs() < self.max_gap)

    # The pixels whose centre lies on the grid, grown by one: a sub-pixel interpolates between neighbouring
    # centres, so every sub-pixel on the grid belongs to one of them. The crop is their bounding box over the
    # batch, plus a pixel of margin so its sub-pixels interpolate as they would across the whole frame.
    _, on_grid = self._cells(u, v, plane, rows, cols)
    near = F.max_pool2d((on_plane & on_grid)[:, None].float(), 3, stride=1, padding=1)[:, 0].amax(dim=0) > 0
    hit_rows, hit_cols = (
        torch.nonzero(near.any(dim=1)),
        torch.nonzero(near.any(dim=0)),
    )  # syncs: a render, not a step
    if hit_rows.numel() == 0:
        return rgb
    height, width = near.shape
    r0, r1 = max(int(hit_rows[0]) - 1, 0), min(int(hit_rows[-1]) + 2, height)
    c0, c1 = max(int(hit_cols[0]) - 1, 0), min(int(hit_cols[-1]) + 2, width)

    uv = torch.stack([u, v], dim=1)[:, :, r0:r1, c0:c1]
    if self.supersample > 1:
        uv = F.interpolate(uv, scale_factor=self.supersample, mode="bilinear", align_corners=False)
    cell_idx, on_grid = self._cells(uv[:, 0], uv[:, 1], plane, rows, cols)
    weight = marks.flatten(1).gather(1, cell_idx.flatten(1)).view_as(cell_idx) * on_grid
    if plane.rgb is not None:
        # Each sub-pixel's cell's colour, weighted: averaged with the weights, over each pixel's sub-pixels.
        cells = plane.rgb.float().flatten(1, 2)  # (K, cells, 3)
        index = cell_idx.flatten(1)[..., None].expand(-1, -1, 3)
        color = cells.gather(1, index).view(*cell_idx.shape, 3) * weight[..., None]
        if self.supersample > 1:
            color = F.avg_pool2d(color.permute(0, 3, 1, 2), self.supersample).permute(0, 2, 3, 1)
    if self.supersample > 1:
        weight = F.avg_pool2d(weight[:, None], self.supersample)[:, 0]
    on = on_plane[:, r0:r1, c0:c1]
    weight = torch.where(on, weight, 0.0)[..., None]
    if plane.rgb is None:
        color = self._color * weight  # one colour: the weighted colour is it times the weight
    else:
        color = torch.where(on[..., None], color, 0.0)

    painted = rgb.clone()
    # The surface's rendered pixel already holds the light that reached it (its shadows included); the mark keeps
    # that light and changes the colour it falls on. Each sub-pixel's tint is lerp(1, colour / surface, weight),
    # and averaged over a pixel's sub-pixels that is 1 - weight + (colour * weight) / surface.
    tint = 1.0 - weight + color / self._surface
    crop = rgb[:, r0:r1, c0:c1].float()
    if self._srgb:
        # Through linear light, for the marked pixels only: the crop is the marks' bounding box over every image of
        # the frame, most of it unmarked, and an unmarked pixel's tint is 1.
        marked = weight[..., 0] > 0  # syncs, as the crop does: a render, not a step
        blend = crop.clone()
        blend[marked] = _srgb_encode((_srgb_decode(crop[marked] / 255.0) * tint[marked]).clamp_(max=1.0)) * 255.0
    else:
        blend = (crop * tint).clamp_(max=255.0)
    painted[:, r0:r1, c0:c1] = blend if rgb.is_floating_point() else blend.round().to(rgb.dtype)
    return painted

BackgroundComposite(camera: Camera, options: CameraOverlayOptions)

Bases: CameraOverlay

Replaces the pixels where the sim shows a background with another image: one of entities, or nothing at all (segmentation id 0, the renderer's own background). The overlays after it leave those pixels as composited (:meth:replaced_pixels). Subclasses say where the background comes from (:meth:background).

With shadow_strength the background is darkened where the sim pass shows shadows on entities (:mod:eden.utils.background_shadows). The rasterizer renders the view a second time without shadows to measure them, which needs EnvOptions.rasterizer_shadows on and a GPU-backed OpenGL context. The batch renderer bakes shadows in, so it has them estimated, which is exact for flat, untextured entities under directional lights: an image-textured entity is refused, and at least one BatchRendererOptions.lights entry needs castshadow=True. Shading holds about 20 * N * H * W bytes of temporaries per frame (about 1 GB at 1024 envs of 224x224).

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION entities

Scene entities whose pixels the background replaces, every link of each (segmentation_level may give an entity several ids). The renderer's empty background is always replaced.

TYPE: list[str]

shadow_strength

How strongly the sim's shadows on entities darken the background, in [0, 1]: 0 pastes it as is, so objects cast no shadow on it; 1 turns a background pixel that receives no light black. Needs at least one entry in entities, since the shadows are read from them.

def build(self) -> None:
    # Deferred: the env module imports the entities, so a module-scope import here would be a cycle.
    from eden.utils.misc import resolve_named_entity

    entity_seg_ids = self._env.entity_segmentation_ids
    surface_ids = []
    for entity_name in self.entities:
        entity = resolve_named_entity(
            self._env.entities,
            entity_name,
            hint=f"{type(self).__name__}(entities=...) lists it; list only those.",
        )
        # An entity owns one id per link/geom at segmentation_level="link"/"geom", and every one of them has to
        # be listed or the entity is only partly treated as background.
        seg_ids = entity_seg_ids.get(entity.idx)
        if not seg_ids:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{type(self).__name__}(entities=...) names entity '{entity_name}', but the scene assigns it no "
                "segmentation id, so it could not be masked as background."
            )
        surface_ids.extend(seg_ids)
    #: The segmentation ids replaced: the renderer's empty background (0) and every id of ``entities``.
    self.background_ids = [0, *surface_ids]
    self._background_ids = torch.tensor(self.background_ids, device=self._env.device)
    # The surfaces that receive shadows: every entity id, not the renderer's empty background.
    self._shadow_surface_ids = torch.tensor(surface_ids, dtype=torch.long, device=self._env.device)
    if self.shadow_strength > 0.0:
        self._check_sim_pass_casts_shadows()

def background(self, rgb: torch.Tensor, envs_idx: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    env = self._env
    renderer = env._splat_renderer
    # Per-env mode: refresh the animated Gaussians from sim poses (once per render).
    env._refresh_splat_gaussians()

    # Per-env camera poses: a free camera reports one (4,4), an attached one (N,4,4); in per-env Gaussian mode a
    # single shared pose is broadcast to num_envs so every env's (independently animated) Gaussians are rendered.
    cam_T = torch.as_tensor(self._camera.get_transform(), dtype=torch.float32, device=env.device)
    if cam_T.ndim == 2:
        cam_T = cam_T.unsqueeze(0)
    cam_pos, cam_rot = cam_T[:, :3, 3], cam_T[:, :3, :3]
    if renderer.per_env_gaussians and cam_pos.shape[0] == 1:
        cam_pos = cam_pos.expand(env.num_envs, 3)
        cam_rot = cam_rot.expand(env.num_envs, 3, 3)
    if self._camera.splat_single_view:
        cam_pos, cam_rot = cam_pos[:1], cam_rot[:1]  # one view, used for every image

    width, height = self._camera.cam_resolution
    splat, _ = renderer.render(cam_pos, cam_rot, height, width, self._camera.cam_fov)
    return splat.mul(255).byte()  # the sim pass's uint8 RGB

def build_camera_overlay(camera: Camera, options: CameraOverlayOptions, index: int) -> CameraOverlay:
    """The overlay ``options`` names, constructed for ``camera``: entry ``index`` of its ``CameraOptions.overlays``."""
    where = f"Camera {camera.display_name}: CameraOptions.overlays[{index}]"
    if not options.name:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{where} names no overlay (name={options.name!r}). Build the entry with the overlay class's configure(), "
            "e.g. PlanePaintOverlay.configure(metric_name='drawing', color=(0, 0, 0)), rather than "
            "CameraOverlayOptions(...)."
        )
    try:
        overlay_class = CAMERA_OVERLAY_REGISTRY.get(options.name)
    except KeyError as e:
        raise ValueError(f"{where}: {e.args[0]}") from None
    if (overlay_class._needs_pointcloud or overlay_class._needs_segmentation) and not camera.supports_pointcloud:
        needs = "point cloud" if overlay_class._needs_pointcloud else "segmentation"
        raise ValueError(
            f"{where}: {overlay_class.__name__} paints by the frame's {needs}, which a sensor-backend camera "
            "cannot render. Remove sensor_options from this CameraOptions to use the legacy camera backend."
        )
    return overlay_class(camera, options)

Get the world position of the sensor.

For attached sensors, this computes link_pos + transform_by_quat(offset_pos, link_quat). For static sensors, returns the initial position from sensor options.

def get_pos(self, envs_idx=None) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Get the world position of the sensor.

    For attached sensors, this computes `link_pos + transform_by_quat(offset_pos, link_quat)`.
    For static sensors, returns the initial position from sensor options.

    Returns
    -------
    pos : torch.Tensor
        World position of shape (num_envs, 3).
    """
    if not self.is_attached:
        pos = torch.tensor(self._options.sensor.pos_offset, dtype=torch.float32, device=self._env.device)
        return pos.unsqueeze(0).expand(self._env.num_envs, -1)

    link = self._sensor._link
    # relative=False: world-frame link pose (pre-1.1.1 default) so the sensor pose is
    # composed in world frame. Genesis >=1.1.1 defaults link getters to the user frame.
    link_pos = link.get_pos(envs_idx, relative=False)  # (num_envs, 3)
    link_quat = link.get_quat(envs_idx, relative=False)  # (num_envs, 4) wxyz

    offset_pos = self._sensor._shared_metadata.offsets_pos[:, self._sensor._idx]  # (B, 3)
    if envs_idx is not None:
        offset_pos = offset_pos[envs_idx]

    return link_pos + transform_by_quat(offset_pos, link_quat)
