def get_quat(self, envs_idx=None) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Get the world orientation of the sensor as a quaternion (wxyz).

    For attached sensors, this computes `quat_mul(link_quat, offset_quat)`.
    For static sensors, returns the initial orientation from sensor options.

    Returns
    -------
    quat : torch.Tensor
        World orientation quaternion (wxyz) of shape (num_envs, 4).
    """
    if not self.is_attached:
        quat_np = euler_to_quat([self._options.sensor.euler_offset])  # (1, 4)
        quat = torch.tensor(quat_np, dtype=torch.float32, device=self._env.device).reshape(4)
        return quat.unsqueeze(0).expand(self._env.num_envs, -1)

    link = self._sensor._link
    # relative=False: world-frame link orientation (pre-1.1.1 default).
    link_quat = link.get_quat(envs_idx, relative=False)  # (num_envs, 4) wxyz

    offset_quat = self._sensor._shared_metadata.offsets_quat[:, self._sensor._idx]  # (B, 4)
    if envs_idx is not None:
        offset_quat = offset_quat[envs_idx]

    return quat_mul(link_quat, offset_quat)

def __init__(
    self,
    env_options: EnvOptions | None = None,
    scene_options: SceneOptions | None = None,
    observation_options: ObservationManagerOptions | None = None,
    event_options: EventManagerOptions | None = None,
    action_options: ActionManagerOptions | None = None,
    metric_options: MetricManagerOptions | None = None,
    recorder_options: RecorderManagerOptions | None = None,
    cameras_options: CamerasOptions | None = None,
    sensors_options: SensorsOptions | None = None,
    renderer_options: RendererOptions | None = None,
    *,
    show_viewer: bool = False,
    eval_mode: bool = False,
    **kwargs,
):
    # The config ``from_config`` built this env from, if any. Direct construction
    # leaves it None and :attr:`config` synthesizes a base config instead.
    self._source_config: EdenConfig | None = None

    # Handling of default arguments
    self.env_options = env_options or EnvOptions()
    self.scene_options = scene_options or SceneOptions()
    self.observation_options = observation_options or ObservationManagerOptions()
    self.event_options = event_options or EventManagerOptions()
    self.action_options = action_options or ActionManagerOptions()
    self.metric_options = metric_options or MetricManagerOptions()
    self.recorder_options = recorder_options or RecorderManagerOptions()
    self.cameras_options = cameras_options or CamerasOptions()
    self.sensors_options = sensors_options or SensorsOptions()
    self.renderer_options = renderer_options or Rasterizer()

    if self.env_options.cuda_graph_options is not None and not self._HAS_GRADED_PHASE:
        raise ValueError(
            f"EnvOptions(cuda_graph_options=...) replays the graded phase of RLEnvBase.step (metrics, "
            f"terminations, rewards), but {type(self).__name__} is not an RLEnvBase and has no such phase, "
            "so the option would do nothing. Set cuda_graph_options=None, or build an RL task (an "
            "EdenRLConfig) if graded steps were intended."
        )

    if isinstance(self.renderer_options, BatchRenderer):
        en.logger.info(f"You are using {type(self.renderer_options).__name__} as the renderer options.")
        en.logger.info("Consider adding lights to the scene by `env.scene.add_light()`.")

    self.headless = not show_viewer
    # `eval_mode` only flips training/randomization off; the env count is
    # always `num_envs` so an explicit override can't be silently shadowed.
    self.training = not eval_mode
    self.num_envs = self.env_options.num_envs

    self.sim_dt = self.env_options.sim_dt
    self.dt = self.env_options.decimation * self.env_options.sim_dt
    self._sim_step_counter = 0
    self.episode_length_buf = torch.zeros(self.num_envs, device=self.device, dtype=torch.long)

    self.obs_buf = None
    self.reset_info = None
    # Sanitized index of the envs the last ``_reset_idx`` call actually reset;
    # consumed (and cleared) by ``_dispatch_post_reset`` at the public entry points.
    self._last_reset_envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None = None

    # hooks
    self._pre_build_hooks: list[Callable[[], None]] = []
    self._post_build_hooks: list[Callable[[], None]] = []
    # Called around every scene.step() of step(): before it, then after it (see register_substep_callback).
    self._pre_substep_callbacks: list[Callable[[], None]] = []
    self._substep_callbacks: list[Callable[[], None]] = []
    self._post_build_hooks_drained = False

    # create scene
    # Build default scene kwargs from env_options fields
    scene_kwargs = dict(
        sim_options=gs.options.SimOptions(
            dt=env_options.sim_dt,
            substeps=env_options.sim_substeps,
            requires_grad=env_options.requires_grad,
        ),
        viewer_options=gs.options.ViewerOptions(
            refresh_rate=int(1 / env_options.sim_dt),
            camera_pos=(2.0, 0.0, 2.5),
            camera_lookat=(0.0, 0.0, 0.5),
            camera_fov=40,
            enable_default_keybinds=env_options.enable_default_keybinds,
        ),
        vis_options=gs.options.VisOptions(
            # Genesis renamed ``env_separate_rigid`` to ``split_envs`` and warns on every build that
            # passes the old keyword, so Eden passes the new one.
            split_envs=env_options.env_separate_rigid,
            show_link_frame=env_options.show_link_frame,
            show_world_frame=env_options.show_world_frame,
            show_cameras=env_options.show_camera_frustums,
            segmentation_level=env_options.segmentation_level,
            background_color=env_options.background_color,
            shadow=env_options.rasterizer_shadows,
        ),
        rigid_options=gs.options.RigidOptions(
            # No ``dt=`` here: a solver dt is now an *authored* integration interval, and
            # authoring the step dt while also passing ``SimOptions.substeps > 1`` is a
            # conflict Genesis rejects. The rigid solver derives its rate from
            # ``SimOptions(dt, substeps)`` like every other solver.
            constraint_solver=_CONSTRAINT_SOLVERS[env_options.solver],
            constraint_timeconst=env_options.constraint_timeconst
            if env_options.constraint_timeconst is not None
            else max(0.01, 2 * env_options.sim_dt / env_options.sim_substeps),
            use_gjk_collision=env_options.use_gjk_collision,
            max_collision_pairs=env_options.max_collision_pairs,
            multiplier_collision_broad_phase=env_options.multiplier_collision_broad_phase,
            iterations=env_options.iterations,
            tolerance=env_options.tolerance,
            ls_iterations=env_options.ls_iterations,
            ls_tolerance=env_options.ls_tolerance,
            enable_collision=True,
            enable_self_collision=env_options.enable_self_collision,
            enable_neutral_collision=env_options.enable_neutral_collision,
            enable_joint_limit=True,
            use_hibernation=env_options.use_hibernation,
            batch_links_info=env_options.batch_links_info,
            batch_joints_info=env_options.batch_joints_info,
            batch_dofs_info=env_options.batch_dofs_info,
            enable_multi_contact=env_options.enable_multi_contact,
            enable_torsional_friction=env_options.enable_torsional_friction,
            enable_rolling_friction=env_options.enable_rolling_friction,
            friction_cone=_FRICTION_CONES[env_options.friction_cone],
            integrator=_INTEGRATORS[env_options.integrator],
            impratio=env_options.impratio,
            contact_resolution=_CONTACT_RESOLUTIONS[env_options.contact_resolution],
            noslip_iterations=env_options.noslip_iterations,
        ),
        coupler_options=env_options.coupler_options,
        fem_options=env_options.fem_options,
        mpm_options=env_options.mpm_options,
        sph_options=env_options.sph_options,
        pbd_options=env_options.pbd_options,
        profiling_options=gs.options.ProfilingOptions(
            show_FPS=env_options.show_FPS,
        ),
        renderer=renderer_options,
        show_viewer=show_viewer,
    )

    # Allow extra fields on EnvOptions to override auto-constructed defaults
    extras = env_options.__pydantic_extra__ or {}
    internal_keys = set(OPTION_METADATA_KEYS)
    for key, value in extras.items():
        if key not in internal_keys:
            scene_kwargs[key] = value

    # Explicit kwargs take highest priority
    scene_kwargs.update(kwargs)

    self.scene = gs.Scene(**scene_kwargs)
    # Genesis ships no MochiSolver: Eden hosts one, installed on the scene's first Mochi entity.
    self._mochi_solver: MochiSolver | None = None
    # The misconfiguration flags of the envs a reset or a setter cleared, per solver, which the next control step
    # raises (see `get_solver_error_envs_mask`), and whether any were kept since. Allocated on the first use.
    self._misconfigurations: list[tuple[Any, int, torch.Tensor]] | None = None
    self._has_kept_misconfigurations = False

    # gs-madrona bakes the light count at scene.build(), so BatchRenderer
    # lights must be registered up front. Only the eden BatchRendererOptions
    # subclass carries a ``lights`` field — the raw genesis BatchRenderer has
    # none, and lights declared elsewhere would silently never render.
    if isinstance(self.renderer_options, BatchRendererOptions):
        for light in self.renderer_options.lights:
            self.scene.add_light(**light)

    entity_data: dict[str, EntityOptionsLike] = {}
    composite_attachments: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}
    for key in self.scene_options.keys():
        if key == "attachments_dict":
            continue
        value = getattr(self.scene_options, key)
        if isinstance(value, CompositeEntityOptions):
            # A composite (e.g. a Droid manipulator) is stored in the scene as one
            # unit and unfolds here into its sub-entities + welds. The scene stays the
            # source of truth (it round-trips as the composite); expansion is local to
            # the build. Name collisions / primary-key were checked in SceneOptions.
            sub_entities, sub_attachments = value.expand()
            entity_data.update(sub_entities)
            composite_attachments.update(sub_attachments)
        else:
            entity_data[key] = value

    # Composite welds join the scene's own attachments; both feed the topo sort below
    # and the attach loop that welds children onto parents.
    attachments_dict = {**(self.scene_options.attachments_dict or {}), **composite_attachments}
    if attachments_dict:
        # Order so each attachment parent is immediately followed by its attached
        # subtree. genesis' ``attach`` requires a welded child to be instantiated
        # *consecutively* with its parent (the merged pair is simulated as one
        # kinematic tree whose DOFs must form one contiguous range), so no other
        # DOF-carrying entity may be created between a parent and its child. A plain
        # "parents before children" topological order is not enough: free entities
        # (a table, a cube) declared between the arm and its welded gripper would sit
        # in the middle and genesis rejects the weld. Each entity has at most one
        # parent (``attachments_dict`` is keyed by child), so the graph is a forest —
        # emit each root in declaration order depth-first so a parent and its welded
        # descendants stay adjacent.
        children_of: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
        attached_children: set[str] = set()
        for child_entity_name, spec in attachments_dict.items():
            children_of[spec[0]].append(child_entity_name)
            attached_children.add(child_entity_name)

        ordered_keys: list[str] = []
        seen: set[str] = set()

        def _emit_subtree(name: str) -> None:
            if name in seen:  # defensive: a malformed cycle must not recurse forever
                return
            seen.add(name)
            ordered_keys.append(name)
            for child in children_of.get(name, []):
                _emit_subtree(child)

        for name in entity_data.keys():
            if name not in attached_children:  # roots: entities not welded onto anything
                _emit_subtree(name)

        # A key left unemitted means a child whose parent is missing, or a cycle among
        # attached entities (no root to reach them from).
        if len(ordered_keys) != len(entity_data):
            missing = {spec[0] for spec in attachments_dict.values() if spec[0] not in entity_data}
            if missing:
                raise ValueError(f"attachments_dict references nonexistent entities: {missing}")
            raise ValueError(f"Cycle detected in attachments_dict: {attachments_dict}")
    else:
        ordered_keys = list(entity_data.keys())

    self.entities: dict[str, Entity] = {}
    for entity_name in ordered_keys:
        entity_options: EntityOptionsLike = entity_data[entity_name]
        entity_cls = _entity_class_for_options(entity_options)
        entity = entity_cls(env=self, options=entity_options)
        entity._name = entity_name
        self.entities[entity_name] = entity

    for entity_name, spec in attachments_dict.items():
        attach_to_entity_name, attach_to_link_name = spec[0], spec[1]
        # Optional 4-tuple form carries a (pos, quat) mounting offset; the 2-tuple form
        # falls back to the child's default_root_pos/quat (see RigidEntity.attach_to).
        attach_offset, attach_quat = (spec[2], spec[3]) if len(spec) >= 4 else (None, None)
        self.entities[entity_name].attach_to(
            self.entities[attach_to_entity_name],
            attach_to_link_name,
            attach_offset=attach_offset,
            attach_quat=attach_quat,
        )

    self.cameras: dict[str, Camera] = {}
    self._setup_cameras()

    self.sensors: dict[str, Sensor] = {}
    self._setup_sensors()

docs.title: config property
docs.text:
config: EdenConfig

The config describing this environment — a round trip of the config it was built from.

Built via :meth:from_config, this returns a new instance of the source config's own class (ReacherConfig, not EdenRLConfig), carrying every field the env never receives — runner_options, language_instructions, task-specific fields — verbatim, with every field :attr:_CONFIG_CLASS declares except :attr:_NON_RUNTIME_CONFIG_FIELDS read off the live env, so runtime mutations (and any None the env replaced with a default) are reflected. That is what makes env.config.save_as_json() write a file that reloads into the same task and rebuilds the same env — synthesizing a base config here instead would drop the runner and task fields with no error, since no env parameter carries them.

Constructed directly (EnvBase(env_options=..., ...)), there is no source config to round-trip: this synthesizes a plain :attr:_CONFIG_CLASS from the runtime options only, and the fields the env does not own take their class defaults.

The returned root is a fresh, unlocked object, but its option children are the live ones (not copies) — mutating them mutates the environment. Use env.config.clone() for an independent copy.

@classmethod
def from_config(cls, cfg: TConfig, *, show_viewer: bool = False, eval_mode: bool = False) -> Self:
    """
    Create an environment from a configuration object.

    Inherited by every env class rather than reimplemented per leaf: a hand-copied list of
    option groups drops a forgotten group in silence, the config fully valid and the env
    simply never told. Reading the field list off :meth:`_runtime_option_fields` instead makes
    forwarding a property of the *structure*: that is the same list :attr:`config` reads back
    off the live env, so the two directions are symmetric by construction, and a group added
    to a config leaf later is forwarded without anyone remembering to. Task-specific fields
    are not swept in — the list comes from this env's leaf, not from ``type(cfg)`` — and
    :attr:`config` carries them across via the recorded source instead.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cfg: TConfig
        The configuration object. Must be the leaf this env class reads — see
        :meth:`_check_config_pairing` — with every field a TaskMod binds filled in, see
        :meth:`~eden.utils.configs.EdenConfig.check_bindings`.
    show_viewer: bool
        Whether to show the viewer.
    eval_mode: bool
        Whether to run in eval mode.

    Returns
    -------
    env: Self
        The constructed environment, **unbuilt** — call ``build()`` yourself. The training
        wrappers' ``from_config`` builds and resets; this one does not.
    """
    cls._check_config_pairing(cfg)
    cfg.check_bindings()
    env = cls(
        **{name: getattr(cfg, name) for name in cls._runtime_option_fields()},
        show_viewer=show_viewer,
        eval_mode=eval_mode,
    )
    # Keeps `env.config` faithful to its source: the concrete config class plus the
    # fields no env parameter carries (runner_options, language_instructions, and any
    # task-specific ones). See :attr:`config`.
    env._source_config = cfg

    return env

def register_post_build_hook(self, hook: Callable[[], None]) -> None:
    """Queue ``hook`` to run once at the end of :meth:`post_build_setup`.

    Parameters
    ----------
    hook : Callable[[], None]
        Zero-argument callable, invoked after every entity/camera ``post_build()`` and
        after the managers are loaded.

    Raises
    ------
    RuntimeError
        If :meth:`post_build_setup` already drained the queue, so ``hook`` would be
        registered too late to ever run.
    """
    if self._post_build_hooks_drained:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"register_post_build_hook({getattr(hook, '__qualname__', hook)}) was called after "
            "post_build_setup() drained the post-build hooks, so the hook would never run. "
            "Register it from __init__, from a pre-build hook, or from a manager's "
            "construction (which happens inside post_build_setup, before the drain)."
        )
    self._post_build_hooks.append(hook)

register_substep_callback(callback: Callable[[], None], *, before: bool = False) -> None

Run callback around every scene.step() of :meth:step (decimation times per control step).

For a term that has to act on the simulation state between sim steps — clamp what the solver just did, before the next step integrates it — which neither the action manager (it writes controls before each step) nor a per-control-step hook can do. A before callback runs right before scene.step(), after the action manager has applied its controls; the rest run right after it. Each runs in registration order, with no arguments, on every env; keep them cheap and sync-free, since they sit on the physics hot path.

One scene.step() advances EnvOptions.sim_dt; Genesis' own sim_substeps run inside it, so a callback never sees them.

A setter that overwrites an env's state clears the error flags its solver latched for it (the MochiSolver's and Genesis' particle solvers' do), so a callback calling one would hide the error of that sim step. While a callback is registered, the env keeps the flags of a misconfiguration after every sim step, which the next control step still raises; a corrupt state the setter overwrote is gone with its flag, as Genesis intends.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION callback

Zero-argument callable.

TYPE: Callable[[], None]

before

Run it before each scene.step() instead of after. Defaults to False.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

    """Run ``callback`` around every ``scene.step()`` of :meth:`step` (``decimation`` times per control step).

    For a term that has to act on the simulation state *between* sim steps — clamp what the solver just did,
    before the next step integrates it — which neither the action manager (it writes controls *before* each
    step) nor a per-control-step hook can do. A ``before`` callback runs right before ``scene.step()``, after the
    action manager has applied its controls; the rest run right after it. Each runs in registration order, with
    no arguments, on every env; keep them cheap and sync-free, since they sit on the physics hot path.

    One ``scene.step()`` advances ``EnvOptions.sim_dt``; Genesis' own ``sim_substeps`` run inside it, so a
    callback never sees them.

    A setter that overwrites an env's state clears the error flags its solver latched for it (the MochiSolver's
    and Genesis' particle solvers' do), so a callback calling one would hide the error of that sim step. While a
    callback is registered, the env keeps the flags of a misconfiguration after every sim step, which the next
    control step still raises; a corrupt state the setter overwrote is gone with its flag, as Genesis intends.

    Parameters
    ----------
    callback : Callable[[], None]
        Zero-argument callable.
    before : bool, optional
        Run it before each ``scene.step()`` instead of after. Defaults to False.
    """
    (self._pre_substep_callbacks if before else self._substep_callbacks).append(callback)

@gs.assert_unbuilt
def build(
    self,
    env_spacing: Vec2FType | None = None,
    center_envs_at_origin: bool | None = None,
):
    """Build the underlying Genesis scene and finalize all entities.

    Runs :meth:`pre_build_setup`, builds the vectorized scene, then runs
    :meth:`post_build_setup`. Must be called once before stepping the environment.

    Parameters
    ----------
    env_spacing : tuple[float, float], optional
        Spacing between environments in the xy-plane. Falls back to
        ``env_options.env_spacing`` when None.
    center_envs_at_origin : bool, optional
        Whether to center the grid of environments at the world origin.
        Falls back to ``env_options.center_envs_at_origin`` when None.
    """
    env_spacing = env_spacing if env_spacing is not None else self.env_options.env_spacing
    center_envs_at_origin = (
        center_envs_at_origin if center_envs_at_origin is not None else self.env_options.center_envs_at_origin
    )
    self.pre_build_setup()
    self.scene.build(
        n_envs=self.num_envs,
        env_spacing=env_spacing,
        center_envs_at_origin=center_envs_at_origin,
    )
    self.post_build_setup()
    self._verify_build()

@gs.assert_built
def post_build_setup(self):
    for entity in self.entities.values():
        entity.post_build()

    for camera in self.cameras.values():
        camera.post_build()

    self._load_managers()
    self._validate_manager_order()

    # Managers register post-build hooks from their __init__ (MotionManager's motion-end
    # resync validator), so this must stay below _load_managers(). Iterating the live list lets
    # a hook queue another one; after this point registering is a loud error.
    for hook in self._post_build_hooks:
        hook()
    self._post_build_hooks_drained = True

    # NOTE: save the post setup state for reset
    self.reset_state = self.scene.get_state()

def destroy(self):
    # Cameras first, so a recording still running is finalized while the scene it renders
    # is alive (see Camera.destroy). The scene is destroyed even when one of them fails:
    # a lost video is recoverable, whereas a scene left alive keeps the Quadrants SNode
    # trees every build spends, and the process runs out of them after ~100 builds.
    error = None
    for name, camera in self.cameras.items():
        try:
            camera.destroy()
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - teardown continues; the error is re-raised below
            en.logger.warning(f"Tearing down camera '{name}' failed: {e}")
            if error is None:
                error = e

    self.scene.destroy()

    if error is not None:
        raise error

@gs.assert_built
def summary(self) -> str:
    """Return a human-readable summary of the environment and its managers."""
    msg = "Environment Summary:\n"
    msg += f"Number of environments: {self.num_envs}\n"
    msg += f"Step time step: {self.dt} s\n"
    msg += f"Simulation time step: {self.sim_dt} s\n"
    msg += f"Decimation: {self.env_options.decimation}\n"

    msg += "Managers:\n"
    msg += self.action_manager.summary()
    msg += self.event_manager.summary()
    msg += self.observation_manager.summary()
    if self.metric_manager is not None:
        msg += self.metric_manager.summary()
    msg += self.recorder_manager.summary()
    return msg

def seed(seed: int) -> int:
    """Seed all RNGs used by the environment.

    Applies exactly the seed given: no DDP rank offset, and no write-back to any
    config. Seeding a *run* is :func:`eden.utils.random.apply_run_seed`'s job — the

Envs a physics solver flagged since their last reset, (num_envs,) bool.

The rigid solver's errors (a NaN contact force) and, in a Mochi scene, the Mochi solver's (a diverged implicit solve). The termination manager truncates these envs, and the reward and metric managers drop what their terms read of them, so no value of the corrupt state reaches the learner; the reset clears the flag before the next error check would raise for the whole scene.

A misconfiguration of the scene (a contact capacity overflow, an unsupported collision pair, a NaN gradient under requires_grad; see _RECOVERABLE_SOLVER_ERRORS) is reset and dropped the same way, but the env keeps its flag across the reset, and the next control step raises it with the message that names the option to change (on CUDA, whose check does not wait for the device, the one after).

def get_solver_error_envs_mask(self) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Envs a physics solver flagged since their last reset, ``(num_envs,)`` bool.

    The rigid solver's errors (a NaN contact force) and, in a Mochi scene, the Mochi solver's (a diverged
    implicit solve). The termination manager truncates these envs, and the reward and metric managers drop what
    their terms read of them, so no value of the corrupt state reaches the learner; the reset clears the flag
    before the next error check would raise for the whole scene.

    A misconfiguration of the scene (a contact capacity overflow, an unsupported collision pair, a NaN gradient
    under ``requires_grad``; see ``_RECOVERABLE_SOLVER_ERRORS``) is reset and dropped the same way, but the env
    keeps its flag across the reset, and the next control step raises it with the message that names the option to
    change (on CUDA, whose check does not wait for the device, the one after).
    """
    mask = self.rigid_solver.get_error_envs_mask()
    if self._mochi_solver is not None:
        mask = mask | self._mochi_solver.get_error_envs_mask()
    return mask

def set_global_sol_params(self, sol_params) -> None:
    """
    Set constraint solver parameters.

    Reference: https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/latest/modeling.html#solver-parameters

    Parameters
    ----------
    sol_params: tuple[float] | list[float] | np.ndarray | torch.tensor
        array of length 7 in which each element corresponds to
        (timeconst, dampratio, dmin, dmax, width, mid, power)

producer(), evaluated at most once per pass for each key.

For terms that derive different values from one intermediate — a body-position and a body-rotation error from the same anchor-relative transform, say — so a pass computes it once rather than once per term. A pass (:meth:compute_pass) spans code that only reads the simulation, so the first result holds for the rest of it: each manager's term loop opens one, and RLEnvBase.step opens one across its whole graded phase (metrics, the observation tick, terminations, rewards), which grades one post-physics state. The memo is dropped when the pass ends, and the next pass starts empty. Outside a pass (a term's compute() called on its own) producer simply runs, so a result is never served stale. Every term sharing key receives the same object: treat it as read-only.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION key

Names the intermediate, including every argument it depends on (entity, link names, ...): two calls with one key, from any term of any manager, are assumed to want the same value.

TYPE: Hashable

producer

Computes the intermediate.

def compute_once(self, key: Hashable, producer: Callable[[], _R]) -> _R:
    """``producer()``, evaluated at most once per pass for each ``key``.

    For terms that derive different values from one intermediate — a body-position and a body-rotation
    error from the same anchor-relative transform, say — so a pass computes it once rather than once per
    term. A pass (:meth:`compute_pass`) spans code that only reads the simulation, so the first result holds
    for the rest of it: each manager's term loop opens one, and ``RLEnvBase.step`` opens one across its whole
    graded phase (metrics, the observation tick, terminations, rewards), which grades one post-physics
    state. The memo is dropped when the pass ends, and the next pass starts empty. Outside a pass (a term's
    ``compute()`` called on its own) ``producer`` simply runs, so a result is never served stale. Every term
    sharing ``key`` receives the same object: treat it as read-only.

    Parameters
    ----------
    key : Hashable
        Names the intermediate, including every argument it depends on (entity, link names, ...): two calls
        with one key, from any term of any manager, are assumed to want the same value.
    producer : Callable[[], T]
        Computes the intermediate.

    Returns
    -------
    T
        ``producer()``'s result, from this pass's memo when an earlier term already produced it.
    """
    cache = self._pass_cache
    if cache is None:
        return producer()
    if key not in cache:
        cache[key] = producer()
    return cache[key]

@contextmanager
def compute_pass(self) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Open a :meth:`compute_once` pass for the duration of the block, unless one is already open.

    A pass opened inside another joins it and leaves it open on exit, so a manager's term loop run inside
    the graded phase shares the phase's memo.
    """
    if self._pass_cache is not None:
        yield
        return
    self._pass_cache = {}
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        self._pass_cache = None

@contextmanager
def fixed_shape_query_scope(self) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Make every query in the block take its fixed-shape form (:attr:`fixed_shape_queries`).

    The CUDA graph of the graded phase (``EnvOptions.cuda_graph_options``) runs each graded step in one, the
    warm-up, the eager validation runs and the capture alike: a capture cannot record a host read, and the

    open on exit.
    """
    previous = self._fixed_shape_queries
    self._fixed_shape_queries = True
    try:
        yield
    finally:

Examples:

>>> # Match all entities starting with "robot"
>>> env.get_entities("robot.*")
>>> # Match entities containing "_<number>" (won't match "robot" without a suffix)
>>> env.get_entities(".*_[0-9]+")

def get_entities(self, names: str | list[str]) -> list["Entity"]:
    """
    Get entities by name(s) with regex pattern matching support.

    This method uses `re.match()` which matches patterns from the beginning
    of the entity name. To match entities containing a pattern anywhere,
    prefix with `.*` (e.g., `".*arm"` to match entities containing "arm"; add `$` to anchor the end).

    Parameters
    ----------
    names : str | list[str]
        A single regex pattern string or a list of regex pattern strings
        to match against entity names. Patterns are matched from the
        beginning of entity names.

    Returns
    -------
    list[Entity]
        A list of entities whose names match any of the provided regex patterns.

    Examples
    --------
    >>> # Match all entities starting with "robot"
    >>> env.get_entities("robot.*")
    >>> # Match entities containing "_<number>" (won't match "robot" without a suffix)
    >>> env.get_entities(".*_[0-9]+")
    >>> # Match multiple patterns
    >>> env.get_entities(["robot_[0-9]+", "box.*"])
    >>> # Exact match
    >>> env.get_entities("^robot$")  # or simply "robot$"
    """
    # Normalize input to a list
    patterns = [names] if isinstance(names, str) else names

    matched_entities = []
    for entity_name in self.entities.keys():
        for pattern in patterns:
            if re.match(pattern, entity_name):
                matched_entities.append(self.entities[entity_name])
                break  # Avoid adding the same entity multiple times

    return matched_entities

def reset(
    self,
    envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None = None,
    *,
    seed: int | None = None,
) -> VecEnvReset:
    """Reset the given environments and return their fresh observations.

    Parameters
    ----------
    envs_idx : slice | torch.Tensor, optional
        The environments to reset. If None, all environments are reset.
    seed : int, optional
        If given, seed the RNGs before resetting.

    Returns
    -------
    VecEnvReset
        A ``(observations, extras)`` tuple, where ``extras`` carries reset
        logging info under the ``"log"`` key.
    """
    if envs_idx is None:
        envs_idx = slice(None)
    if seed is not None:
        self.seed(seed)

    self.recorder_manager._on_reset_started(envs_idx)
    with sharing_env_indices(envs_idx):
        self.reset_info = self._reset_idx(envs_idx)
        self._dispatch_post_reset()
    self.recorder_manager._on_reset_finished(envs_idx=envs_idx)
    self.clear_debug_objects()

    self.obs_buf = self.observation_manager.compute(update_history=True)

    return self.obs_buf, {"log": self.reset_info}

def step(self, action: torch.Tensor | dict[str, torch.Tensor] | None = None) -> VecEnvStep:
    """Advance the environment by one control step.

    Applies ``action`` through the action manager, runs ``decimation`` physics
    sub-steps, and computes observations. ``EnvBase`` itself has no reward or
    termination; subclasses (:class:`RLEnvBase`) extend this.

    Parameters
    ----------
    action : torch.Tensor | dict[str, torch.Tensor], optional
        The action to apply. If None, no action is applied (the sim still steps).

    Returns
    -------
    VecEnvStep
        A ``(obs, reward, terminated, timeouts, info)`` tuple. ``EnvBase``
        has no reward or termination, so ``reward``, ``terminated``, and
        ``timeouts`` are always ``None``.
    """
    if action is not None:
        self.action_manager.compute(action)

    self.recorder_manager._on_step_started()

    self._run_sim_steps(apply_actions=action is not None)

    self.episode_length_buf += 1

    # NOTE: cameras are deliberately NOT rendered here — the camera API is
    # pull-based, and `start_recording` captures one frame per `render()`
    # call. See `Camera.start_recording`.

    if self.metric_manager is not None:
        self.metric_manager.compute()

    # Phase 7: the once-per-step tick for stateful observation terms, on the post-physics
    # state and after the metrics so a term may integrate one. See
    # ObservationManager.post_physics_refresh for the contract.
    self.observation_manager.post_physics_refresh()

    # Close the recorded step here — below the phases that grade it, above the ones that
    # prepare the next — which is the position it holds in ``RLEnvBase.step`` (the two bodies
    # agree phase-for-phase, pinned by ``tests/envs/test_base.py``). Closing it after the
    # INTERVAL events would corrupt every recorder term that reads simulation state in
    # ``record_post_step()``: an INTERVAL-mode randomizer (``PushByVelocity`` writes the base
    # DOFs outright) perturbs the robot for the *next* step, so ``SysIDRecorder`` would log
    # "after action A the velocity was V" with a V no physics had produced.
    self.recorder_manager._on_step_finished()

    if _INTERVAL in self.event_manager.available_modes:
        self.event_manager.compute(mode=_INTERVAL, dt=self.dt)

    self.obs_buf = self.observation_manager.compute(update_history=True)

    # NOTE: to match the RLEnvBase.step() return type for consistency
    return (self.obs_buf, None, None, None, {"log": self.reset_info})

def __init__(
    self,
    env_options: EnvOptions | None = None,
    scene_options: SceneOptions | None = None,
    observation_options: ObservationManagerOptions | None = None,
    reward_options: RewardManagerOptions | None = None,
    termination_options: TerminationManagerOptions | None = None,
    event_options: EventManagerOptions | None = None,
    curriculum_options: CurriculumManagerOptions | None = None,
    command_options: CommandManagerOptions | None = None,
    action_options: ActionManagerOptions | None = None,
    metric_options: MetricManagerOptions | None = None,
    recorder_options: RecorderManagerOptions | None = None,
    cameras_options: CamerasOptions | None = None,
    sensors_options: SensorsOptions | None = None,
    renderer_options: RendererOptions | None = None,
    *,
    show_viewer: bool = False,
    eval_mode: bool = False,
    **kwargs,
):
    super().__init__(
        env_options=env_options,
        scene_options=scene_options,
        observation_options=observation_options,
        event_options=event_options,
        action_options=action_options,
        metric_options=metric_options,
        recorder_options=recorder_options,
        cameras_options=cameras_options,
        sensors_options=sensors_options,
        renderer_options=renderer_options,
        show_viewer=show_viewer,
        eval_mode=eval_mode,
        **kwargs,
    )
    # Handling of default arguments
    self.reward_options = reward_options or RewardManagerOptions()
    self.termination_options = termination_options or TerminationManagerOptions()
    self.curriculum_options = curriculum_options or CurriculumManagerOptions()
    self.command_options = command_options or CommandManagerOptions()

    self.max_episode_length_s = self.env_options.episode_length_s
    if not np.isfinite(self.max_episode_length_s) or self.max_episode_length_s <= 0.0:
        # inf/NaN would die two lines below with an opaque OverflowError,
        # and <= 0 would truncate every env on step one;
        # `max_episode_length` feeds integer buffers and the rsl_rl runner.
        raise ValueError(
            f"env_options.episode_length_s must be a positive finite value, got "
            f"{self.max_episode_length_s}. For unbounded episodes, keep a finite horizon "
            "and omit the `time_out` termination term instead — truncation then never fires."
        )
    self.max_episode_length = int(np.ceil(self.max_episode_length_s / self.dt))
    self.common_step_counter = 0

    # Lazily allocated zero-initialized cache for ``extras['final_observations']``.
    # See ``EnvOptions.record_final_observations`` and ``RLEnvBase.step()``.
    self._final_obs_cache: dict[str, torch.Tensor | dict[str, torch.Tensor]] = {}

@contextmanager
def graded_capture_scope(self) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Refuse reads of :attr:`common_step_counter` in the block, which captures the graded phase.

    :class:`~eden.envs.graded_graph.GradedPhaseGraph` captures in one: the graph would replay the count a
    term read there on every later step. Leaving it restores the guard as it found it, so a nested scope
    leaves the outer one open.
    """
    previous = self._graded_capture_active
    self._graded_capture_active = True
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        self._graded_capture_active = previous

def step(
    self,
    action: torch.Tensor | dict[str, torch.Tensor] | None = None,
) -> VecEnvStep:
    """Advance the RL environment by one control step.

    Applies ``action``, runs ``decimation`` physics sub-steps, then computes
    metrics, terminations, and rewards. Done environments are auto-reset
    **after** reward/termination but **before** observation, so the returned
    observations reflect the fresh post-reset state for those environments.

    Parameters
    ----------
    action : torch.Tensor | dict[str, torch.Tensor], optional
        The action to apply. If None, no action is applied (the sim still steps).

    Returns
    -------
    VecEnvStep
        A ``(obs, reward, terminated, timeouts, info)`` tuple.
    """
    if action is not None:
        self.action_manager.compute(action)

    self.recorder_manager._on_step_started()

    # Advance command references BEFORE physics (no-op unless a command term
    # overrides pre_physics_advance, e.g. MotionCommand). Advance-then-grade:
    # advancing the reference before the physics sub-steps makes the post-
    # physics robot get graded against the temporally-aligned reference frame
    # (matching MotionManager) instead of a one-control-step-stale one. Any
    # wrap-teleport therefore precedes physics, keeping forward kinematics fresh.
    if self.command_manager is not None:
        self.command_manager.pre_physics_advance()

    self._run_sim_steps(apply_actions=action is not None)

    # Update env counters.
    self.episode_length_buf += 1
    self.common_step_counter += 1

    # Refresh command terms' cached robot state on the just-computed post-physics
    # state, so metric/termination/reward grade the CURRENT step (S_N) rather than
    # the previous one. Matches IsaacLab/mjlab. See CommandManager.post_physics_refresh
    # for the ordering contract.
    if self.command_manager is not None:
        self.command_manager.post_physics_refresh()

    # NOTE: cameras are deliberately NOT rendered here — the camera API is
    # pull-based, and `start_recording` captures one frame per `render()`
    # call. See `Camera.start_recording`.

    # Phases 6-9: metrics, the observation tick, terminations and rewards, from a CUDA graph when
    # EnvOptions.cuda_graph_options asks for one.
    if self._graded_graph is not None:
        self.reset_buf, self.reward_buf = self._graded_graph()
    else:
        self.reset_buf, self.reward_buf = self._compute_graded()
    self.reset_terminated = self.termination_manager.terminated
    self.reset_timeouts = self.termination_manager.timeouts
    # Gate on is_recording so `.any()` doesn't force a GPU→CPU sync every step during training.
    if self.recorder_manager.is_recording:
        if self.metric_manager is not None and hasattr(self.metric_manager, "success_buf") and self.reset_buf.any():
            self.recorder_manager.set_episode_success(
                self.reset_buf, self.metric_manager.success_buf[self.reset_buf]
            )
    self.recorder_manager._on_step_finished(self.reset_buf)

    # Snapshot pre-reset observations for done envs (opt-in via
    # ``EnvOptions.record_final_observations``). Must run before
    # ``_reset_idx`` since ``scene.reset`` wipes the done envs' state.
    if self.env_options.record_final_observations:
        final_obs = self._record_final_observations()
    else:
        final_obs = None

    # Always call _reset_idx — bool-mask ops are no-ops for all-False. The mask's ids are taken once
    # here, for every consumer that gathers the resetting rows, and its count gates the reset: one
    # GPU->CPU sync for the whole reset rather than one per consumer.
    with sharing_env_indices(self.reset_buf):
        self.reset_info = self._reset_idx(self.reset_buf)
        # Terms rebuild per-step caches from the final post-reset state, before the
        # recorder snapshots new-episode data and observations read them below.
        self._dispatch_post_reset()

    # Record new-episode data after reset, such as initial state snapshots.
    self.recorder_manager._on_reset_finished(envs_idx=self.reset_buf)

    # Curricula are frozen at eval. The gate lives in CurriculumManager, not here, so that it
    # covers reset() as well — see CurriculumManager.compute for why difficulty must not move
    # during an eval rollout, and why the freeze has to be all-or-nothing.
    if self.curriculum_manager is not None:
        self.curriculum_manager.compute()

    if self.command_manager is not None:
        self.command_manager.compute(dt=self.dt)

    if _INTERVAL in self.event_manager.available_modes:
        self.event_manager.compute(mode=_INTERVAL, dt=self.dt)

    self.obs_buf = self.observation_manager.compute(update_history=True)

    if not self.training and self.command_manager is not None:
        self.command_manager.draw_vis()

    extras: dict[str, Any] = {"log": self.reset_info}
    if final_obs is not None:
        extras["final_observations"] = final_obs

    return (
        self.obs_buf,
        self.reward_buf,
        self.reset_terminated,
        self.reset_timeouts,
        extras,
    )

def step(

docs.title: env_class_for_config
docs.text:
env_class_for_config(cfg: EdenConfig) -> type[EnvBase]

Return the env class that builds cfg.

Maps each config leaf to its env class, mirroring the parallel hierarchies:

  • EdenMimicConfig → MimicRLEnvBase
  • EdenSplatRLConfig → SplatRLEnvBase
  • EdenSplatConfig → SplatEnvBase
  • EdenRLConfig → RLEnvBase
  • EdenNyxSplatConfig → NyxSplatEnvBase
  • EdenConfig → EnvBase

The single dispatch point for config→env-class, shared by the from_config wrappers, the CLI play path, and the smoke harness. The configs form an inheritance chain (EdenMimicConfig, EdenSplatRLConfig ⊂ EdenRLConfig ⊂ EdenConfig, and EdenSplatConfig / EdenNyxSplatConfig ⊂ EdenConfig), so the pairs are checked most-specific first — EdenSplatRLConfig before the generic EdenRLConfig branch that would otherwise shadow it, and EdenSplatConfig before the EdenConfig fallback.

The splat env classes are imported lazily: they pull optional renderer dependencies, and a config that is not a splat config must not require them. A splat config that is passed while those dependencies are missing gets the ImportError — that is the actionable failure, and far better than a silent downgrade to RLEnvBase, which would build an env with no splat renderer and no error.

The reverse direction is not stated here: each env declares its own leaf as :attr:EnvBase._CONFIG_CLASS, following the definition-site convention Eden uses for tasks rather than keeping a second central index. Deduplicating the two would mean deriving one by reflection over __subclasses__ — import-order dependent — so they are pinned to each other by tests/envs/test_base.py::test_every_leaf_accepts_its_own_config_and_only_the_two_keywords instead. A new config leaf must therefore update both, and that test says so if it doesn't.

def env_class_for_config(cfg: EdenConfig) -> type[EnvBase]:
    """Return the env class that builds ``cfg``.

    Maps each config leaf to its env class, mirroring the parallel hierarchies:

    * ``EdenMimicConfig`` → ``MimicRLEnvBase``
    * ``EdenSplatRLConfig`` → ``SplatRLEnvBase``
    * ``EdenSplatConfig``   → ``SplatEnvBase``
    * ``EdenRLConfig``      → ``RLEnvBase``
    * ``EdenNyxSplatConfig`` → ``NyxSplatEnvBase``
    * ``EdenConfig``        → ``EnvBase``

    The single *dispatch* point for config→env-class, shared by the ``from_config``
    wrappers, the CLI play path, and the smoke harness. The configs form an inheritance chain
    (``EdenMimicConfig``, ``EdenSplatRLConfig`` ⊂ ``EdenRLConfig`` ⊂ ``EdenConfig``, and
    ``EdenSplatConfig`` / ``EdenNyxSplatConfig`` ⊂ ``EdenConfig``), so the pairs are checked
    most-specific first — ``EdenSplatRLConfig`` before the generic ``EdenRLConfig`` branch that
    would otherwise shadow it, and ``EdenSplatConfig`` before the ``EdenConfig`` fallback.

    The splat env classes are imported lazily: they pull optional renderer dependencies, and a
    config that is not a splat config must not require them. A splat config that *is* passed
    while those dependencies are missing gets the ``ImportError`` — that is the actionable
    failure, and far better than a silent downgrade to ``RLEnvBase``, which would build an env
    with no splat renderer and no error.

    The reverse direction is not stated here: each env declares its own leaf as
    :attr:`EnvBase._CONFIG_CLASS`, following the definition-site convention Eden uses for
    tasks rather than keeping a second central index. Deduplicating the two would mean
    deriving one by reflection over ``__subclasses__`` — import-order dependent — so they are
    pinned to each other by
    ``tests/envs/test_base.py::test_every_leaf_accepts_its_own_config_and_only_the_two_keywords``
    instead. A new config leaf must therefore update both, and that test says so if it doesn't.
    """
    from eden.utils.configs import (
        EdenMimicConfig,
        EdenNyxSplatConfig,
        EdenRLConfig,
        EdenSplatConfig,
        EdenSplatRLConfig,
    )

    if isinstance(cfg, EdenNyxSplatConfig):
        from eden.envs.nyx_splat import NyxSplatEnvBase

        return NyxSplatEnvBase
    # Checked before EdenRLConfig below: EdenSplatRLConfig subclasses it, so the generic RL branch
    # would otherwise shadow it (and drop splat_options silently).
    if isinstance(cfg, EdenSplatRLConfig):
        from eden.envs.splat import SplatRLEnvBase

        return SplatRLEnvBase
    # Checked before the EdenConfig fallback below (it is an EdenConfig, not an EdenRLConfig).
    if isinstance(cfg, EdenSplatConfig):
        from eden.envs.splat import SplatEnvBase

        return SplatEnvBase

    for cfg_cls, env_cls in (
        (EdenMimicConfig, MimicRLEnvBase),
        (EdenRLConfig, RLEnvBase),
        (EdenConfig, EnvBase),
    ):
        if isinstance(cfg, cfg_cls):
            return env_cls
    raise TypeError(f"No env class for config of type {type(cfg).__name__}")

def __init__(
    self,
    env_options: EnvOptions | None = None,
    scene_options: SceneOptions | None = None,
    splat_options: NyxSplatOptions | None = None,
    observation_options: ObservationManagerOptions | None = None,
    event_options: EventManagerOptions | None = None,
    action_options: ActionManagerOptions | None = None,
    metric_options: MetricManagerOptions | None = None,
    recorder_options: RecorderManagerOptions | None = None,
    cameras_options: CamerasOptions | None = None,
    sensors_options: SensorsOptions | None = None,
    renderer_options: RendererOptions | None = None,
    *,
    show_viewer: bool = False,
    eval_mode: bool = False,
    **kwargs,
):
    # Checked here rather than in `from_config` so direct construction is covered too, and
    # so `from_config` stays the one generic body every env inherits. `EdenNyxSplatConfig`
    # validates the *type* when the field is set at construction, but not on later
    # assignment (`cfg.splat_options = SplatOptions()` is accepted).
    if splat_options is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "`NyxSplatEnvBase` requires `splat_options` (it owns a Nyx splat renderer). Set "
            "`splat_options=NyxSplatOptions(...)` on the config, or build a task without "
            "splats through `env_class_for_config(cfg).from_config(cfg)`."
        )
    if not isinstance(splat_options, NyxSplatOptions):
        raise TypeError(
            f"`NyxSplatEnvBase` renders through the Nyx path tracer, so `splat_options` must be "
            f"a `NyxSplatOptions`, not a `{type(splat_options).__name__}`. For "
            f"`SplatOptions`, build the config through `SplatEnvBase`."
        )

    # Held publicly so `env.config` can report it live (a declared EdenNyxSplatConfig
    # field); the private alias stays for the render path and entities/base.py's probe.
    self.splat_options = splat_options
    self._nyx_splat_options = splat_options
    self._nyx_light_fields = self._build_light_fields(splat_options.pcds)
    self._nyx_env_maps = self._build_env_maps(splat_options.env_map_paths)

    super().__init__(
        env_options=env_options,
        scene_options=scene_options,
        observation_options=observation_options,
        event_options=event_options,
        action_options=action_options,
        metric_options=metric_options,

        cameras_options=cameras_options,
        sensors_options=sensors_options,
        renderer_options=renderer_options,
        show_viewer=show_viewer,
        eval_mode=eval_mode,
        **kwargs,
    )

docs.title: CUDA-graph replay of the graded phase
docs.text:
EnvOptions.cuda_graph_options replays the metric, observation-refresh, termination and reward phase of RLEnvBase.step from a CUDA graph. GradedPhaseGraph is the implementation; BakedHostReadError is what it raises when a term reads a value back to the host during capture.

CUDA-graph replay of the graded phase of RLEnvBase.step (EnvOptions.cuda_graph_options).

Between the physics step and the auto-reset, RLEnvBase.step grades the post-physics state: the metric manager, the observation terms' post_physics_refresh tick, the termination manager and the reward manager. That phase reads the simulation (through Genesis' zero-copy views, plain torch indexing) and writes only the managers' own buffers, but it does so in hundreds of small kernels, and on a host-bound step their launches are what it costs: ~3 ms of host time on BeyondMimic at 4096 envs, against ~1 ms of device time. Replayed from a CUDA graph the same kernels launch in ~5 µs, and the checks before each replay (below) take ~70 µs.

A graph replays kernels, not Python, so it is only right for code that keeps its state in tensors it writes in place, and reads no value back to the host — which is the term contract (docs/guides/terms.md). :class:GradedPhaseGraph does not take that on trust (its settings are :class:~eden.options.envs.CudaGraphOptions):

  • It captures after warmup_steps eager steps, once every term has built its lazy caches (building one inside a capture is a host-to-device copy, which a capture rejects).

  • The capture step and the next validation_steps replays are each also run eagerly and compared bit for bit with the graph: every tensor the phase leaves behind (each one bound to an object the walk follows that it writes or rebinds, and each one it writes that no such binding reaches) and the phase's outputs. A mismatch raises, naming the tensors that differ. The two runs go in a different order on each kind of step:

  • On the capture step the eager run goes first (a capture records kernels without running them). It is undone so the capture starts from the same state. Every tensor that existed before it is put back, reached by a binding or not, so the capture's replay does not advance it a second time. One it allocated is not: it may already sit in a cache that outlives the phase (Genesis' contact query), and rolling it back would hand the cache's next reader stale values.

  • On a validated replay the graph goes first and is undone (the same tensors), and the eager run's result is the one kept. Run the other way round, work a capture recorded without being able to replay (a kernel launched outside torch's stream runs once, at capture time) would be redone by the eager run just before the replay read it, and agree. Graph-first, the replay reads the stale value and disagrees.
  • Before every replay it checks what the graph baked in, and re-captures (and re-validates) when it changed: the graded terms' configured fields (a curriculum moving a termination threshold), the env's per-run constants a term may read as Python values (:data:_ENV_CONSTANTS), and every binding on the way to a tensor the capture read (a term or load_state_dict rebinding the tensor, or replacing the dict or helper that holds it, leaves the graph reading the old address). The fields a manager mirrors on the device (:attr:~eden.managers.base.ManagerBase.device_synced_fields, the reward weights) are the exception: the manager's sync_device_fields runs before every replay, so a weight curriculum needs no re-capture.
  • env.common_step_counter changes on every step, so it cannot be watched: reading it during a capture raises :class:BakedHostReadError, naming the term's line. Any other Python value a term reads from outside its own configured fields (another manager's term, a module global) is not watched either, and the graph replays what it read at capture. Keep such a value in a tensor written in place.
  • More than max_recaptures_per_window re-captures within recapture_window steps raise, naming what changed: re-capturing on nearly every step costs more than the eager phase it replaces. A one-off change, such as a curriculum switching stage, re-captures once.

The walk that finds those bindings follows every object reachable from the env through attributes and containers, however deep, except three kinds: the env itself (every term's back-reference to it), the standard library's objects, and the objects of :data:_UNWALKED_PACKAGES (the simulator and torch), which hold the simulation's own state and per-step caches rather than a term's.

GradedPhaseGraph(env: RLEnvBase, compute: Callable[[], tuple[Tensor, Tensor]], options: CudaGraphOptions)

Run the graded phase from a CUDA graph, validated against eager runs of it.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION env

The built env whose graded phase this replays.

TYPE: RLEnvBase

compute

The eager graded phase, returning (reset_buf, reward_buf): RLEnvBase._compute_graded.

TYPE: Callable[[], tuple[Tensor, Tensor]]

options

How to capture, validate and re-capture (EnvOptions.cuda_graph_options).

TYPE: CudaGraphOptions

Source code in eden/envs/graded_graph.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    env: RLEnvBase,
    compute: Callable[[], tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]],
    options: CudaGraphOptions,
) -> None:
    if torch.device(env.device).type != "cuda":
        raise ValueError(
            f"EnvOptions.cuda_graph_options needs a CUDA device, but this env runs on '{env.device}'. Set "
            "cuda_graph_options=None, or run on an NVIDIA GPU with en.init(backend=gs.cuda); gs.gpu is not "
            "enough, as it picks Metal on a Mac."
        )
    self._env = env
    self._compute = compute
    self._options = options
    self._graph: torch.cuda.CUDAGraph | None = None
    self._outputs: tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None = None
    self._fingerprint: tuple[tuple, tuple] | None = None
    self._steps = 0
    self._validations_left = 0
    # The graded steps at which the most recent re-captures ran (not the first capture).
    self._recaptures: list[int] = []
    # The managers the phase runs, and every term whose configured fields a capture bakes in, as
    # ``(label, term, the names of those fields)``: the per-step fingerprint reads them. Resolved once, as
    # the terms are: walking each term class's MRO for its field names on every step cost more host time
    # than the replay saves of it (~150 µs a step on BeyondMimic). A field its manager mirrors on the device
    # is left out.
    self._managers = _graded_managers(env)
    self._terms = self._resolve_terms()
    # The bindings on the way to each tensor the capture read (see :meth:`_watch`): one that now holds
    # another object leaves the graph reading the old address. Set by each capture.
    self._links: list[tuple[str, Any, Any, Any]] = []
    self._leaves: list[tuple[str, Any, Any, tuple]] = []
    # The paths of the tensors the phase leaves behind (each bound tensor it writes, each binding it
    # replaces): what a validated replay compares and undoes. Set by each capture.
    self._state_paths: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
    # The tensors the phase writes that no binding the walk follows reaches (a helper's buffer below the
    # walk, a closure's), held directly: what a validated replay compares and undoes beside the paths. Set by each
    # capture.
    self._unreached: list[torch.Tensor] = []

A host value that changes on every step was read while the graded phase was being captured.

Raised by RLEnvBase.common_step_counter during a capture: the graph would replay the count it read on every later step, so a cadence gated on it (counter % n == 0) would stay on the branch the capture took.

docs.title: Policy export
docs.text:
eden export writes policy.onnx, policy.pt (TorchScript) and policy_spec.json for a runtime outside Eden. See the policy export guide.

Export a trained policy for a runtime outside Eden: an ONNX / TorchScript graph plus policy_spec.json.

eden export (:func:eden.utils.cli.tasks.export_task) builds the checkpoint's own env, loads the runner, and hands both to :func:export_policy, which writes

  • policy.onnx — input obs (the actor's observation groups, concatenated, un-normalized), output actions (the raw policy output, before the action terms scale it), with a dynamic batch axis. A recurrent policy also takes h_in (and c_in for an LSTM), shaped (num_layers, batch, hidden), and returns h_out (c_out): the caller threads the state, starting from zeros;
  • policy.pt — the same composition as TorchScript, batch 1 when recurrent: its hidden state lives in the module, and reset() zeroes it;
  • policy_spec.json — the contract around the graph (:func:build_policy_spec): what fills obs, how actions becomes joint targets, the control rate, and where the graph came from.

The observation normalizer is part of both graphs. The graph comes from the policy model's own as_onnx() / as_jit() (rsl-rl-lib >= 4's export hooks), which is also how a learner overrides the default: RMA's :class:~eden.learning.wrappers.rsl_rl.rma.model.RmaActorModel defines both to export its deployment composition (estimator injected). An inherited hook can export something other than what the model runs, so every export is checked against the runner's inference policy on the env's own observations before anything is written (:func:verify_export). The files are written into a staging directory and moved into place only once checked, so a failed export leaves the output directory as it was.

The spec records the robot's nominal command: the joint-zero offset domain randomization draws per env is left out of the action offset, and an env whose default pose itself was randomized at startup is refused (:func:disable_contract_randomization strips those terms from a config before it is built).

def export_policy(
    runner: Any,
    env: RslRlVecEnvWrapper,
    out_dir: str,
    *,
    formats: tuple[str, ...] = EXPORT_FORMATS,
    task: str,
    checkpoint: str,
    verify: bool = True,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Export ``runner``'s policy to ``out_dir`` and write ``policy_spec.json`` beside it.

    Parameters
    ----------
    runner:
        An rsl_rl runner with ``checkpoint`` loaded.
    env:
        The env the runner was built on: the observations the export is checked on, and what the spec describes.
    out_dir:
        Directory to write into (created if missing). An earlier export there is replaced, and a graph of a format
        not exported this time is removed with it; on a failure the directory is left as it was.
    formats:
        Any of :data:`EXPORT_FORMATS`.
    task:
        The registered task name, recorded in the spec.
    checkpoint:
        The checkpoint path, hashed into the spec.
    verify:
        Check every exported graph against the runner's inference policy (:func:`verify_export`) before writing the
        spec. The ONNX check needs ``onnxruntime``.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, str]
        ``{format: path}`` for every file written, the spec under ``"spec"``.
    """
    unknown = sorted(set(formats) - set(EXPORT_FORMATS))
    if unknown or not formats:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Export formats {unknown or list(formats)} are not supported; choose one or more of {EXPORT_FORMATS}."
        )
    check_export_dependencies(formats, verify=verify)
    get_policy = getattr(getattr(runner, "alg", None), "get_policy", None)
    if get_policy is None:
        raise TypeError(
            f"{type(runner).__qualname__} has no `alg.get_policy()`, so there is no policy model to export. Export "
            f"reads the model through it, as rsl-rl-lib >= 4's algorithms provide it; under rsl-rl-lib 3, upgrade "
            f"(a 3.x checkpoint loads into a 4.x / 5.x runner)."
        )
    policy = get_policy()
    obs_groups = policy_obs_groups(policy)
    refuse_randomized_contract(env.unwrapped)
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    # Staged, then moved in only once checked and described: a graph that failed its check, or a spec cut short, must
    # not land where a deployment could pick it up, nor beside the files of an earlier export.
    staging = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix=".eden-export-", dir=out_dir)
    try:
        staged = {}
        for fmt in EXPORT_FORMATS:
            if fmt in formats:
                staged[fmt] = os.path.join(staging, EXPORT_FILENAMES[fmt])
                (_export_onnx if fmt == "onnx" else _export_jit)(policy, staged[fmt])
        if verify:
            verify_export(staged, runner.get_inference_policy(device=env.device), env, obs_groups)
        spec = build_policy_spec(env.unwrapped, policy, staged, task=task, checkpoint=checkpoint, runner_env=env)
        staged["spec"] = os.path.join(staging, POLICY_SPEC_FILENAME)
        with open(staged["spec"], "w") as f:
            json.dump(spec, f, indent=2)
            f.write("\n")
        files = {key: os.path.join(out_dir, os.path.basename(path)) for key, path in staged.items()}
        for key, path in staged.items():  # the spec last, so it never names a graph not yet in place
            os.replace(path, files[key])
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
    for fmt in EXPORT_FORMATS:
        stale = os.path.join(out_dir, EXPORT_FILENAMES[fmt])
        if fmt not in files and os.path.exists(stale):
            os.remove(stale)  # an earlier export's graph, which the new spec does not describe
    return files

def check_export_dependencies(formats: tuple[str, ...], *, verify: bool) -> None:
    """Raise ``ImportError`` if a package ``formats`` needs is missing: ``onnx`` for the ONNX graph's spec, and
    ``onnxruntime`` to check it.

    ``eden export`` calls this before it builds anything, so a missing extra costs no env build.
    """
    if "onnx" not in formats:
        return
    missing = []
    for package in ("onnx", "onnxruntime") if verify else ("onnx",):
        try:
            importlib.import_module(package)
        except (ImportError, OSError) as exc:  # a broken onnxruntime-gpu wheel fails on its CUDA libraries
            missing.append(f"{package} ({' '.join(str(exc).split())})")
    if missing:
        skip = " onnxruntime only runs the parity check, which --no_verify (verify=False) skips." if verify else ""
        raise ImportError(
            f"Exporting the ONNX graph needs {' and '.join(missing)}. Install the extra with {install_hint('onnx')} "
            f"(for the GPU wheel: {install_hint('onnx-gpu')}). Or export TorchScript only with --format jit.{skip}"

def disable_contract_randomization(config: EdenRLConfig) -> list[str]:
    """Disable ``config``'s event terms that would randomize what the spec records as nominal; return their names.

    Call it before the env is built: ``eden export`` does. :func:`export_policy` refuses an env built with them.
    """
    from eden.managers.event_manager import EVENT_TERM_REGISTRY

    if config.event_options is None:
        return []
    disabled = []
    for name in config.event_options.term_keys():
        term_cls = EVENT_TERM_REGISTRY.get(getattr(config.event_options, name).name)
        if isinstance(term_cls, type) and issubclass(term_cls, _contract_randomization_terms()):
            config.event_options.disable_term(name)
            disabled.append(name)
    return disabled

def refuse_randomized_contract(env: RLEnvBase) -> None:
    """Raise ``ValueError`` if ``env`` was built with an event term that randomizes what the spec records as nominal."""
    event_manager = getattr(env, "event_manager", None)
    if event_manager is None:
        return
    randomizing = {
        name: type(term).__name__
        for _, name, term in event_manager.iter_terms()
        if isinstance(term, _contract_randomization_terms())
    }
    if randomizing:
        listed = ", ".join(f"'{name}' ({cls})" for name, cls in randomizing.items())
        raise ValueError(
            f"The env was built with event term(s) {listed}, which bias each env's default joint pose at startup, so "
            f"policy_spec.json would record env 0's random draw as the robot's default pose and action offset. Build "
            f"the env from a config passed through eden.learning.export.disable_contract_randomization(config) "
            f"first, as eden export does; reading another env's row would only record another draw."
        )

def policy_obs_groups(policy: Any) -> list[str]:
    """The observation groups ``policy`` concatenates into its input, in order — the layout of the graph's ``obs``."""
    groups = getattr(policy, "obs_groups", None)
    if not isinstance(groups, (list, tuple)) or not groups:
        raise TypeError(
            f"{type(policy).__qualname__} has no `obs_groups` list, so the observation layout of an export cannot be "
            f"known. Export reads the groups the model concatenates from that attribute, as rsl-rl-lib >= 4's "
            f"MLPModel sets it; a custom model must set it too."
        )
    return list(groups)

verify_export(files: dict[str, str], inference_policy: Any, env: RslRlVecEnvWrapper, obs_groups: list[str]) -> None

Check every exported graph reproduces inference_policy over :data:VERIFY_STEPS real control steps.

The env is stepped by inference_policy from its current state, under torch.inference_mode as rsl_rl's rollout steps it; each graph then replays the same observations from a zero recurrent state. inference_policy is what eden inference runs, so a learner whose export hook exports anything else — an inherited as_onnx() that skips the model's own forward — fails here, before a spec is written next to it.

RAISES DESCRIPTION RuntimeError

Naming the format, the step and the largest deviation, when a graph disagrees.

Source code in eden/learning/export.py 
def verify_export(files: dict[str, str], inference_policy: Any, env: RslRlVecEnvWrapper, obs_groups: list[str]) -> None:
    """Check every exported graph reproduces ``inference_policy`` over :data:`VERIFY_STEPS` real control steps.

    The env is stepped by ``inference_policy`` from its current state, under ``torch.inference_mode`` as rsl_rl's
    rollout steps it; each graph then replays the same observations from a zero recurrent state.
    ``inference_policy`` is what ``eden inference`` runs, so a learner whose export hook exports anything else — an
    inherited ``as_onnx()`` that skips the model's own forward — fails here, before a spec is written next to it.

    Raises
    ------
    RuntimeError
        Naming the format, the step and the largest deviation, when a graph disagrees.
    """
    reset = getattr(inference_policy, "reset", None)
    if reset is not None:
        reset()
    observations, expected = [], []
    obs = env.get_observations()
    # inference_mode, as rsl_rl's own rollout steps the env: after a `learn()` its buffers are inference tensors,
    # which only an inference-mode step may update in place.
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for _ in range(VERIFY_STEPS):
            actions = inference_policy(obs)
            observations.append(torch.cat([obs[group] for group in obs_groups], dim=-1).cpu())
            expected.append(actions.cpu())
            obs, *_ = env.step(actions)
    for fmt, path in files.items():
        produced = _run_onnx(path, observations) if fmt == "onnx" else _run_jit(path, observations)
        name = os.path.basename(path)
        for step, (got, want) in enumerate(zip(produced, expected, strict=True)):
            if got.shape != want.shape:
                mismatch = f"actions of shape {tuple(got.shape)} where the policy returned {tuple(want.shape)}"
            elif not torch.allclose(got, want, atol=VERIFY_ATOL, rtol=VERIFY_RTOL):
                mismatch = (
                    f"actions up to {(got - want).abs().max().item():.3e} away from the policy's "
                    f"(tolerance atol={VERIFY_ATOL}, rtol={VERIFY_RTOL})"
                )
            else:
                continue
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"The exported {fmt} graph ({name}) does not reproduce the policy: at step {step} it returned {mismatch}. "
                f"The model's export hook exports something other than what it runs; fix the hook rather than the "
                f"tolerance."
            )

Sections: model (the files and their tensors), observations (what fills obs, slice by slice), actions (how actions becomes a command), entities (each commanded entity's DOFs in column order, with default positions and PD gains), rate and provenance. runner_env is the rsl_rl wrapper, for its action clip. env must pass :func:refuse_randomized_contract, as :func:export_policy checks first.

def build_policy_spec(
    env: RLEnvBase,
    policy: Any,
    files: dict[str, str],
    *,
    task: str,
    checkpoint: str,
    runner_env: RslRlVecEnvWrapper | None = None,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The ``policy_spec.json`` contract for ``policy`` as built on ``env``.

    Sections: ``model`` (the files and their tensors), ``observations`` (what fills ``obs``, slice by slice),
    ``actions`` (how ``actions`` becomes a command), ``entities`` (each commanded entity's DOFs in column order,
    with default positions and PD gains), ``rate`` and ``provenance``. ``runner_env`` is the rsl_rl wrapper, for
    its action clip. ``env`` must pass :func:`refuse_randomized_contract`, as :func:`export_policy` checks first.
    """
    obs_groups = policy_obs_groups(policy)
    clip_actions = getattr(runner_env, "clip_actions", None)
    action_terms = _action_spec(env)
    return {
        "schema_version": POLICY_SPEC_SCHEMA_VERSION,
        "model": _model_spec(files),
        "observations": _observation_spec(env, obs_groups),
        "actions": {
            "dim": env.action_manager.total_action_dim,
            "clip": None if clip_actions is None else [-float(clip_actions), float(clip_actions)],
            "terms": action_terms,
        },
        "entities": _entity_spec(env, {term["entity_name"] for term in action_terms if term.get("dofs_name")}),
        "rate": {
            "control_dt": float(env.dt),
            "decimation": int(env.env_options.decimation),
            "sim_dt": float(env.env_options.sim_dt),
        },
        "provenance": _provenance(env, task, checkpoint),
    }

docs.title: rsl-rl-lib algorithms
docs.text:
eden.learning.wrappers.rsl_rl holds one subpackage per algorithm. Each has an options module (what a task configures) next to the implementation.

Models, algorithms and runners for rsl-rl-lib 5, selected through their options' class_name.

  • :mod:.simba — a SimBaV2 actor / critic behind one encoder per observation group.
  • :mod:.muon_ppo — PPO whose optimizer is Muon for the 2-D weights and AdamW for the rest.
  • :mod:.him — HIMLoco (OpenHomie's HIMPPO): a self-supervised history estimator feeding the actor, plus rollout-time symmetry and mirror losses.
  • :mod:.amp_ppo — PPO plus an adversarial-motion-prior style reward (HUSKY).
  • :mod:.rma — the RMA teacher (actor with estimator + scan / privileged / history encoders, PPO with privileged-latent regularization and DAgger) and its depth-student distillation runner (extreme parkour).

Each subpackage ships an options class subclassing the rsl_rl option it replaces (RslRlModelOptions / RslRlPpoAlgorithmOptions / RslRlBaseRunnerOptions) whose class_name defaults to its implementation, so a task selects it with actor=<Options>(...), algorithm=<Options>(...) or runner_options=<Options>(...).

def __init__(
    self,
    obs: TensorDict,
    obs_groups: dict[str, list[str]],
    obs_set: str,
    output_dim: int,
    hidden_dim: int = 512,
    num_blocks: int = 2,
    expansion: int = 4,
    latent_dim: int = 128,
    encoder_hidden_dims: dict[str, list[int]] | None = None,
    default_encoder_hidden_dims: list[int] | tuple[int, ...] = (256,),
    c_shift: float = 3.0,
    compile: bool = False,
    hidden_dims: list[int] | tuple[int, ...] = (),
    activation: str = "swish",
    obs_normalization: bool = True,
    distribution_cfg: dict | None = None,
) -> None:
    if len(hidden_dims) != 0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"SimBaModel got hidden_dims={list(hidden_dims)}, but SimBa has no plain MLP trunk to size. Set the "
            "backbone with hidden_dim / num_blocks / expansion and the per-group encoders with "
            "encoder_hidden_dims, and leave hidden_dims empty."
        )
    encoder_hidden_dims = dict(encoder_hidden_dims or {})
    unknown = sorted(set(encoder_hidden_dims) - set(obs.keys()))
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"SimBaModel encoder_hidden_dims names observation groups {unknown} that the env does not provide; "
            f"available groups: {sorted(obs.keys())}."
        )
    # rsl_rl's MLPModel builds the normaliser, the distribution and a plain MLP trunk; the trunk is replaced
    # below, so build it as small as possible (a 1-wide hidden layer; rsl_rl's MLP needs at least one) rather
    # than at the MLPModel default size.
    super().__init__(
        obs,
        obs_groups,
        obs_set,
        output_dim,
        hidden_dims=[1],
        activation=activation,
        obs_normalization=obs_normalization,
        distribution_cfg=distribution_cfg,
    )
    trunk_output_dim = self.distribution.input_dim if self.distribution is not None else output_dim
    group_dims = [obs[group].shape[-1] for group in self.obs_groups]
    specs = [list(encoder_hidden_dims.get(group, default_encoder_hidden_dims)) for group in self.obs_groups]
    encoder = GroupEncoder(group_dims, specs, latent_dim, resolve_nn_activation(activation))
    self.mlp = nn.Sequential(
        encoder, SimBa(encoder.out_features, trunk_output_dim, hidden_dim, num_blocks, expansion, c_shift)
    )
    if self.distribution is not None:
        self.distribution.init_mlp_weights(self.mlp)
    self._compile_trunk = compile
    self._compiled_trunk = None

docs.text:
forward(obs: TensorDict, masks: Tensor | None = None, hidden_state: Any = None, stochastic_output: bool = False) -> Tensor
Source code in eden/learning/wrappers/rsl_rl/simba/model.py 
def forward(
    self,
    obs: TensorDict,
    masks: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    hidden_state: Any = None,
    stochastic_output: bool = False,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    if not self._compile_trunk:
        return super().forward(obs, masks, hidden_state, stochastic_output)
    if self._compiled_trunk is None:
        self._compiled_trunk = torch.compile(
            self.mlp.forward, backend="inductor", mode="default", fullgraph=True, dynamic=False
        )
    obs = unpad_trajectories(obs, masks) if masks is not None and not self.is_recurrent else obs
    latent = self.get_latent(obs, masks, hidden_state)
    trunk_output = self._compiled_trunk(latent)
    if self.distribution is not None:
        if stochastic_output:
            self.distribution.update(trunk_output)
            return self.distribution.sample()
        return self.distribution.deterministic_output(trunk_output)
    return trunk_output
