docs.text:
motion_finished() -> bool

True once every tracked motion reference has played through to its final frame.

A task drives its reference through the motion manager, through a MotionCommand, or through both, and this reads whichever are present — the same two paths :meth:_advance_motion_reference ticks and :meth:reset_motion_reference rewinds. Reading only the manager would leave on_motion_end silently inert on every command-path deploy (SONIC, beyondmimic_moves), which is most of them.

The signals are the clocks the observation terms see, so hardware and --mujoco agree on when the clip is over. False when no reference is present (a plain RL env, or an entity no motion term tracks — a config question, not a reason to park the robot mid-run) and when any present reference is still running.

Costs one device sync per present reference, per control step, until the end fires — a host-side branch needs the value on the host. Callers latch: on_motion_end stops asking once it has acted (_standing_from / _motion_end_switched), and on_motion_end="continue" never asks at all.

Source code in eden/extensions/deployment/base.py 
def motion_finished(self) -> bool:
    """True once every tracked motion reference has played through to its final frame.

    A task drives its reference through the motion *manager*, through a ``MotionCommand``,
    or through both, and this reads whichever are present — the same two paths
    :meth:`_advance_motion_reference` ticks and :meth:`reset_motion_reference` rewinds.
    Reading only the manager would leave ``on_motion_end`` silently inert on every
    command-path deploy (SONIC, ``beyondmimic_moves``), which is most of them.

    The signals are the clocks the observation terms see, so hardware and ``--mujoco``
    agree on when the clip is over. ``False`` when *no* reference is present (a plain RL
    env, or an entity no motion term tracks — a config question, not a reason to park the
    robot mid-run) and when any present reference is still running.

    Costs one device sync per present reference, per control step, until the end fires —
    a host-side branch needs the value on the host. Callers latch: ``on_motion_end``
    stops asking once it has acted (``_standing_from`` / ``_motion_end_switched``), and
    ``on_motion_end="continue"`` never asks at all.
    """
    signals = [sig for sig in (self._manager_motion_finished(), self._command_motion_finished()) if sig is not None]
    return bool(signals) and all(signals)

step(action: Optional[Tensor | dict[str, Tensor]] = None) -> dict[str, Any]

Send one control step's command, then read and return the resulting observation.

action is the policy's raw output, run through the env's action manager by :meth:action_to_payload. It is None for an extension-policy slot, which has already written its targets with :meth:write_dofs_targets: the payload is then built from that buffer alone, with the action manager left out of it.

None before any such write is the third case — a caller that has nothing to send this step — and sends nothing rather than commanding a zero-initialised buffer, which on hardware is every joint driven to 0.0 rather than left alone. Hence the _direct_targets_written flag: an all-zero _processed_action is a legitimate command (every joint to its zero position) and cannot be told from an untouched buffer by inspecting it.

Every backend sends what the operator state machine wants: the hold while stopped, the INIT ramp, and the policy's command only under START, with the end-of-clip handover (on_motion_end) taking precedence over the policy. Sending nothing (the third case above) is :meth:_idle_tick: MuJoCo does not advance and hardware keeps its last command.

def step(self, action: Optional[torch.Tensor | dict[str, torch.Tensor]] = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Send one control step's command, then read and return the resulting observation.

    ``action`` is the policy's raw output, run through the env's action manager by
    :meth:`action_to_payload`. It is ``None`` for an extension-policy slot, which has
    already written its targets with :meth:`write_dofs_targets`: the payload is then
    built from that buffer alone, with the action manager left out of it.

    ``None`` before any such write is the third case — a caller that has nothing to
    send this step — and sends nothing rather than commanding a zero-initialised buffer,
    which on hardware is every joint driven to 0.0 rather than left alone. Hence the
    ``_direct_targets_written`` flag: an all-zero ``_processed_action`` is a legitimate
    command (every joint to its zero position) and cannot be told from an untouched
    buffer by inspecting it.

    Every backend sends what the operator state machine wants: the hold while stopped, the
    INIT ramp, and the policy's command only under START, with the end-of-clip handover
    (``on_motion_end``) taking precedence over the policy. Sending nothing (the third case
    above) is :meth:`_idle_tick`: MuJoCo does not advance and hardware keeps its last command.
    """
    if self.policy_seconds is not None and self._policy_ticks * self.control_dt >= self.policy_seconds - 1e-9:
        en.logger.info(f"[deploy] policy_seconds={self.policy_seconds:g} reached -- ending the run as KILL does.")
        raise KeyboardInterrupt
    self._before_step()
    self._advance_gain_ramp()
    payload = self._operator_payload(action)
    # Only a tick the policy drove advances its clocks: not STOP/hold, not INIT, and not the
    # START tick's hold, so the policy's first observation reads the clock at 0 and the clip
    # at frame 0, as after an env reset.
    driven = self._use_policy and not self._handover_pending
    self._handover_pending = False
    if payload is not None:
        self._sending_hold = not driven
        try:
            self.send_payload(payload)
        finally:
            self._sending_hold = False
    else:
        self._idle_tick()
    if not self._use_policy:
        self._policy_ticks = 0  # a later START runs policy_seconds afresh
    elif driven and payload is not None:
        self._policy_ticks += 1
    if self._rate is not None:
        self._rate.sleep()
    if self.advances_episode_clock and driven:
        self._env.episode_length_buf += 1
    if self.sync_before_commands:
        self.state = self.read_state()
        self._sync_state(self.state)
        self._update_commands(advance_reference=driven)
    else:
        self._update_commands(advance_reference=driven)
        self.state = self.read_state()
    # A control tick is a step, so stateful observation terms advance once here — the deploy
    # loop's phase 7. ``reset`` reads without advancing, as ``EnvBase.reset`` does.
    if not self._use_policy and payload is not None:
        self._watch_frozen_joints(payload, self.state)
    # Recorded after the observation, not straight after ``read_state``: this tick's velocity
    # estimate and foot contacts join ``state.extra`` inside ``state_to_observation``, and a
    # record taken before it would miss them. ``finally`` so a tick whose observation
    # raises -- the one a post-mortem most wants -- is still recorded, with whatever extras it
    # got as far as (``_record_step`` pads the rest).
    try:
        if self.sync_before_commands:  # synced above, once: sync_scene must not run twice a tick
            return self._observe(self.state, post_physics_refresh=True)
        return self.state_to_observation(self.state, post_physics_refresh=True)
    finally:
        if payload is not None:
            self._record_step(payload, self.state)

def reset(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Boot in STOP/hold and return the first observation: nothing moves until the operator says so.

    Every backend runs the same INIT/START/STOP/KILL state machine (see "The operator state
    machine" in ``docs/guides/deployment.md``). After this, :meth:`step` holds the measured pose
    until INIT ramps the joints to the ``init_target`` pose and START hands control to the
    policy -- from the robot's remote, the keyboard, or a script's :meth:`request_init` /
    :meth:`request_start`. With none of them open, a hardware backend holds in STOP for good.
    """
    # Drop the target low-pass state so the new episode warm-starts from its first command
    # instead of smoothing across the reset from the stale pre-reset target (no-op when
    # target_lpf == 1).
    self._lpf_prev = None
    self._policy_ticks = 0
    # A new episode: its first read starts every observation window afresh, as an env reset does.
    self._observations_stale = True
    self._enter_boot_hold()
    self._prepare_reset()
    self.state = self.read_state()
    # Rewind now so the clip waits at frame 0 through STOP and INIT; START rewinds again.
    self.reset_motion_reference()
    self._after_reset_read()
    self._setup_inputs()
    self._print_control_guide()
    return self.state_to_observation(self.state)

reset_motion_reference() -> None

Restart a motion-imitation reference cleanly at frame 0 (no-op for non-mimic envs).

Both reference paths are rewound, for the same reason :meth:_advance_motion_reference advances both: a task drives its reference through the motion manager, through a MotionCommand, or through both, and the deploy loop is the only thing that reaches either one.

  • the manager path — :meth:MotionManager.rewind_to_start for each env's currently-assigned clip, then a refill of the reference buffer;
  • the command path — :meth:CommandTerm.rewind_reference, the clock-only rewind.

Motion selection is NOT resampled on either (unlike :meth:MotionManager.reset): a deploy replays the same clip deterministically instead of the sim's random start phase (motion_start_from_middle_range), which is correct for a robot that begins from a stand. Called at deploy reset (before its INIT loop), at INIT, at START, and on every policy switch.

Rewinding the command path matters most at the handover the operator gate creates. The clip holds while the robot is in INIT or hold (:meth:step does not advance it), so without this a STOP at frame 500 followed by a START hands the policy a reference 500 frames into the motion while the robot is standing in its INIT stance — a mid-clip pose it is nowhere near, on a biped.

def reset_motion_reference(self) -> None:
    """Restart a motion-imitation reference cleanly at frame 0 (no-op for non-mimic envs).

    Both reference paths are rewound, for the same reason :meth:`_advance_motion_reference`
    advances both: a task drives its reference through the motion *manager*, through a
    ``MotionCommand``, or through both, and the deploy loop is the only thing that reaches
    either one.

    * the **manager** path — :meth:`MotionManager.rewind_to_start` for each env's
      currently-assigned clip, then a refill of the reference buffer;
    * the **command** path — :meth:`CommandTerm.rewind_reference`, the clock-only rewind.

    Motion selection is NOT resampled on either (unlike :meth:`MotionManager.reset`): a deploy
    replays the same clip deterministically instead of the sim's random start phase
    (``motion_start_from_middle_range``), which is correct for a robot that begins from a
    stand. Called at deploy reset (before its INIT loop), at INIT, at START, and on every
    policy switch.

    Rewinding the command path matters most at the handover the operator gate creates. The
    clip holds while the robot is in INIT or hold (:meth:`step` does not advance it), so
    without this a STOP at frame 500 followed by a START hands the policy a reference 500
    frames into the motion while the robot is standing in its INIT stance — a mid-clip pose it
    is nowhere near, on a biped.
    """
    if self._env.command_manager is not None:
        self._env.command_manager.rewind_reference()
    # Rewinding re-arms the clip, so a latched end-of-motion action ends and the policy
    # drives again -- the handover an operator START or a policy switch produces.
    self._standing_from = None
    self._stand_count = 0
    self._motion_end_switched = False
    mm = self._motion_manager
    if mm is None:
        return
    all_idx = torch.arange(self._env.num_envs, device=self._env.device)
    mm.rewind_to_start(all_idx)
    mm.fill_data()

state_to_observation(state: RobotState, *, post_physics_refresh: bool = False) -> dict[str, Any]

Sync state onto the env's robot entity and compute the policy's observation dict.

post_physics_refresh is the deploy loop's phase 7. :meth:step passes True so an observation term with per-step state (:meth:ObservationTerm.post_physics_refresh <eden.managers.observation_manager.ObservationTerm.post_physics_refresh>) advances exactly once per control tick, on the freshly synced robot state and before the read — the sim step runs it at phase 7 and a deploy that skipped it would hand the policy a value frozen at its last simulated step, silently (the class of bug _advance_motion_reference documents). The reset paths leave it False: EnvBase.reset runs no phase 7 either, so a term reads as zero there in both places. A command term's post_physics_refresh still does not run on this path (see :meth:CommandTerm.post_physics_refresh <eden.managers.command_manager.CommandTerm.post_physics_refresh>); the observation hook does because the policy's observations are the hardware path.

The first read of an episode -- after construction, :meth:reset or START -- also clears the observation manager's per-step state and the action manager's last actions, in the order an env reset does: this tick's phase 7, then reset(), then post_reset() (a term that rebuilds its state from the current frame, as ParkourProprio backfills its history, needs it), then the read, which backfills every history window from the robot. Without it the policy's first frames come from the training wrapper's env.reset() on the simulated robot at its spawn pose, or, at START, from the hold and INIT ramp in the yaw frame START just replaced. Clearing on the read rather than in each reset covers a backend override that does not chain to this class's, and a loop that drives :meth:step with no reset at all.

Overrides must accept the keyword (and forward it to super()); the constructor refuses one that does not (:meth:_check_state_to_observation_override).

One tick of skew relative to the sim, inherent to this loop's order: :meth:step publishes the new command (_update_commands) before read_state, so a term that integrates command − measured here pairs this tick's measurement with the command just published, where phase 7 in the sim pairs it with the command that was in effect during the physics.

    simulated step, silently (the class of bug ``_advance_motion_reference`` documents). The reset
    paths leave it ``False``: ``EnvBase.reset`` runs no phase 7 either, so a term reads as zero
    there in both places. A command term's ``post_physics_refresh`` still does not run on this path
    (see :meth:`CommandTerm.post_physics_refresh
    <eden.managers.command_manager.CommandTerm.post_physics_refresh>`); the observation hook does
    because the policy's observations *are* the hardware path.

    The first read of an episode -- after construction, :meth:`reset` or START -- also clears the
    observation manager's per-step state and the action manager's last actions, in the order an
    env reset does: this tick's phase 7, then ``reset()``, then ``post_reset()`` (a term that
    rebuilds its state from the current frame, as ``ParkourProprio`` backfills its history, needs
    it), then the read, which backfills every history window from the robot. Without it the
    policy's first frames come from the training wrapper's ``env.reset()`` on the *simulated*
    robot at its spawn pose, or, at START, from the hold and INIT ramp in the yaw frame START just
    replaced. Clearing
    on the read rather than in each ``reset`` covers a backend override that does not chain to
    this class's, and a loop that drives :meth:`step` with no reset at all.

    new command (``_update_commands``) *before* ``read_state``, so a term that integrates
    ``command − measured`` here pairs this tick's measurement with the command just published,
    where phase 7 in the sim pairs it with the command that was in effect during the physics.
    """
    self._sync_state(state)
    return self._observe(state, post_physics_refresh=post_physics_refresh)

The deploy loop calls it when it switches policy slots, so the policy switched in reads what an env reset would have handed it, with every history window backfilled from the robot as it is now, a fed-back last action of zero, and the motion reference the switch just rewound. def restart_observations(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Start every observation window afresh from the last reading, as START does; returns the observation.

    The deploy loop calls it when it switches policy slots, so the policy switched in reads what
    an env reset would have handed it, with every history window backfilled from the robot as it
    is now, a fed-back last action of zero, and the motion reference the switch just rewound.
    Without it the switched-in policy reads frames observed while another slot drove, with the
    reference still mid-clip, and its own last action from before it was switched out. The
    reading is not re-synced and the velocity estimator not re-run: the state is the one the last
    :meth:`step` already observed.
    """
    self._observations_stale = False
    self._restart_observed_episode()
    return self._env.observation_manager.compute(update_history=True)

docs.title: SoftShutdownMixin
docs.text:
SoftShutdownMixin(options: T)

Bases: ConfigurableMixin, ABC

Settle the robot into a damping state before a backend's close drops its link.

Dropping the link outright leaves the robot holding its last stiff PD target until an onboard comms watchdog trips, and a standing robot can lurch or collapse. :meth:_soft_shutdown instead sends shutdown_damping_steps ticks of kp=0, kd>0: the position servo is off, only velocity damping remains, and the joints settle gently.

With a :class:~eden.extensions.deployment.utils.republisher.CommandRepublisherMixin running, no watchdog can trip while the process lives: a control thread that stalls leaves the loop re-sending its last command at full gains, and the loop reports that rather than acting on it (see "A stalled control thread is reported, not acted on" in docs/guides/deployment.md). This ramp is then the only orderly way down, which is why such a backend's close runs it before _stop_publisher -- the damping command goes out at the same packet rate as any other.

Mixed in ahead of :class:DeploymentBase by the backends that run the ramp, which call :meth:_soft_shutdown from close and implement :meth:_shutdown_hold_pos. The two options live here rather than on :class:DeploymentBase so a backend without the ramp keeps rejecting them instead of accepting and ignoring them.

shutdown_damping_steps: int Control ticks to send the damping command before close releases the link. shutdown_damping_kd_scale: float Scale on kd during that soft shutdown.

def __init__(self, options: T) -> None:
    self._uid = gs.UID()
    self._options: T = options

    mirror_options_onto(self, self._options)

    # Deferred, not module-scope — see the NOTE above this module's imports.
    from eden.options._metadata import OPTION_METADATA_KEYS

    # check if there are unused parameters in the options. ``_extra_option_params`` are legitimate
    # options-only fields (not mirrored as attrs), so they are expected to be "unused" here.
    unused_params = set(self._options.keys()) - set(self.get_parameter_names())
    tolerated = {"name", "class_name"} | set(OPTION_METADATA_KEYS) | self._extra_option_params
    # ``params`` is a declared framework field on function-capable term options. An *empty* one is
    # legitimately unused when the same options class configures a class-based term; a non-empty
    # ``params`` on a class-based term would be silently ignored, so it stays invalid.
    if not getattr(self._options, "params", None):
        tolerated.add("params")
    invalid_params = unused_params - tolerated
    if invalid_params:
        # Name the term, not only the class: for a function term the class is the shared
        # ``*FuncWrapper``, which cannot tell the author which of a dozen terms is wrong.
        # Same wording as the construction-time check (``ManagerTermOptions._validate_param_names``).
        term_name = getattr(self._options, "name", None)
        subject = f"term '{term_name}' ({type(self).__name__})" if term_name else type(self).__name__
        raise ValueError(
            invalid_parameters_message(subject, invalid_params, self.get_configure_specs(), self._retired_params)
        )

def resolve_deployment_for(robot_options: RobotOptions | CompositeEntityOptions) -> type[DeploymentBase]:
    """Return the deployment class registered for ``type(robot_options)``.

    Walks the MRO to honor inheritance (a subclass with no binding falls
    back to its parent's). Raises ``KeyError`` if no ancestor is bound.

    A composite rig (:class:`~eden.options.entities.CompositeEntityOptions` — an arm with a hand
    welded on, a humanoid with hands) resolves to ``composite_deployment``, which drives each of
    its parts through that part's own binding.
    """
    if isinstance(robot_options, CompositeEntityOptions):
        return DEPLOYMENT_REGISTRY.get("composite_deployment")
    cls = type(robot_options)
    for ancestor in cls.__mro__:
        if ancestor in _ROBOT_DEPLOYMENT_BINDINGS:
            name = _ROBOT_DEPLOYMENT_BINDINGS[ancestor]
            return DEPLOYMENT_REGISTRY.get(name)
    available = sorted({k.__name__ for k in _ROBOT_DEPLOYMENT_BINDINGS}) or ["<none>"]
    raise KeyError(
        f"No deployment registered for robot {cls.__name__}. "
        f"Available bindings: {available}. Add one with "
        f"``bind_deployment({cls.__name__}, '<deployment_name>')``."
    )

A policy's pinned gains on the DOFs of dofs_name it names, as ({dof: kp}, {dof: kd}).

A default_dofs_kp / default_dofs_kd that robot leaves empty (G1Dofs23's, which trains on the asset's gains), or a robot with no dofs_name at all (None, a composite), resolves to {}: it declares no gains, and the deployed robot's apply. :meth:DeploymentBase.wire_gains builds a slot's wire gains from this.

Needs no deployment, so eden deploy runs it for every slot before constructing one: a raise here must land before the entity swap and before an operator device is opened.

Raises ValueError when a non-empty gain map leaves out a joint of dofs_name the robot has (and when a pattern in it matches none of the robot's joints): see "Each slot runs at its own PD gains" in docs/guides/deployment.md.

def resolve_pinned_gains(robot: Any, dofs_name: Sequence[str]) -> tuple[dict[str, float], dict[str, float]]:
    """A policy's pinned gains on the DOFs of ``dofs_name`` it names, as ``({dof: kp}, {dof: kd})``.

    A ``default_dofs_kp`` / ``default_dofs_kd`` that ``robot`` leaves empty (``G1Dofs23``'s,
    which trains on the asset's gains), or a ``robot`` with no ``dofs_name`` at all (``None``, a
    composite), resolves to ``{}``: it declares no gains, and the deployed robot's apply.
    :meth:`DeploymentBase.wire_gains` builds a slot's wire gains from this.

    Needs no deployment, so ``eden deploy`` runs it for every slot before constructing one: a
    raise here must land before the entity swap and before an operator device is opened.

    Raises ``ValueError`` when a non-empty gain map leaves out a joint of ``dofs_name`` the
    robot has (and when a pattern in it matches none of the robot's joints): see "Each slot
    runs at its own PD gains" in ``docs/guides/deployment.md``.
    """
    robot_dofs = getattr(robot, "dofs_name", None)
    if robot_dofs is None:
        return {}, {}
    robot_dofs = list(robot_dofs)
    deployed = set(dofs_name)
    driven = [name for name in robot_dofs if name in deployed]
    resolved: list[dict[str, float]] = []
    for field in ("default_dofs_kp", "default_dofs_kd"):
        pinned = getattr(robot, field, None)
        if not pinned:  # declares no gains: the deployed robot's
            resolved.append({})
            continue
        idx, _, values = resolve_matching_names_values(pinned, robot_dofs, preserve_order=True)
        covered = {robot_dofs[j]: float(value) for j, value in zip(idx, values, strict=True)}
        if uncovered := [name for name in driven if name not in covered]:
            owner = type(robot).__name__
            raise ValueError(
                f"{owner}'s {field} gives no value for {first_few(uncovered)}, which this deployment drives. A "
                "slot runs at its pinned robot's gains; a joint they leave out took the asset's own gain in "
                "training, which a deployment cannot read. Give every joint a value in the policy's "
                f"robot_options(), e.g. {field}={{**{owner}().{field}, ...}} (pydantic replaces the whole dict, "
                "it does not merge). Do not fall back to 0 or to the deployed robot's gain: either is a guess on "
                "a live robot."
            )
        resolved.append({name: covered[name] for name in driven})
    return resolved[0], resolved[1]

    scrambles any dict with wildcard keys. DOFs not covered by any pattern
    resolve to 0.0 (with a warning: a zero kp/kd reaching a real robot means a
    limp joint).
    """
    idx, _, values = resolve_matching_names_values(data, dofs_name, preserve_order=True)
    resolved = np.zeros(len(dofs_name), dtype=np.float64)
    resolved[idx] = values
    if len(idx) < len(dofs_name):
        missing = [name for i, name in enumerate(dofs_name) if i not in set(idx)]
        en.logger.warning(f"[deployment] No value matched for DOFs {missing}; defaulting to 0.0.")
    return resolved

Drive a Unitree G1 over the unitree_hg DDS low-level interface.

Configurable options (in addition to :class:~eden.extensions.deployment.unitree_dds._UnitreeDdsDeployment's):

publish_rate: float | None Rate at which the held LowCmd_ is re-sent between control ticks (default 500 Hz, Unitree's own low-level rate). None sends one packet per control tick.

The G1's ankle *and* -- on the 3-DOF-waist 29-DOF build -- waist roll/pitch are
parallel A/B linkages, driven here in PR (pitch/roll) mode via ``mode_pr``. That is
the same joint class whose per-packet PD made the LimX Oli's waist buzz at one
packet per 50 Hz tick: the derivative term acts on a 20 ms-old velocity,
which at 25 Hz is anti-damping. 500 Hz is what both vendor references use --
Unitree's own ``g1_low_level_example`` publishes at ``control_dt_ = 0.002``, and
NVIDIA's SONIC G1 deploy runs a dedicated 500 Hz ``LowCommandWriter`` thread beside
its 50 Hz control thread -- so it is the rate the robot is expected to be fed at,
independent of how fast any policy runs.

Unlike the Oli case this has **not** been measured on a G1: the mechanism and the
rate are taken from those two references, not from a hardware fit. ``--publish_rate 0``
sends one packet per tick, which is the A/B to run before concluding anything.

def connect(self) -> None:
    ensure_go1_sdk()

    self._udp = sdk.UDP(LOWLEVEL, self.local_port, self.robot_ip, self.robot_port)
    self._safe = sdk.Safety(sdk.LeggedType.Go1)
    self._cmd = sdk.LowCmd()
    self._state = sdk.LowState()
    self._udp.InitCmdData(self._cmd)
    self._init_low_cmd()

    # Prime the bidirectional UDP link and wait for the first valid low-state
    # packet. The robot only streams state back to a client it has already
    # heard from, so we must SEND while polling: the ``_init_low_cmd`` command
    # is limp (kp=kd=tau=0, so no torque / no motion) and safe to send before
    # we have any state. A Recv-only wait hangs forever whenever the robot
    # isn't already streaming (e.g. after a previous client closed).
    # ``tick`` (ms) stays 0 until the control board is heard from.
    start_time = time.time()
    while True:
        self._udp.SetSend(self._cmd)
        self._udp.Send()
        self._refresh_state()
        if self._state.tick != 0:
            break
        if time.time() - start_time > self.connect_timeout_s:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Timed out waiting for Unitree Go1 low state. Check the robot is powered, "
                "in low-level mode (L2+A → L2+B → L1+L2+start on the remote), and reachable "
                f"at {self.robot_ip}:{self.robot_port} from local UDP port {self.local_port}."
            )
        time.sleep(_PRIME_DT_S)

def read_state(self) -> RobotState:
    self._require_connected()
    self._refresh_state()
    state = self._state

    dofs_pos = np.zeros(self.num_dofs, dtype=np.float64)
    dofs_vel = np.zeros(self.num_dofs, dtype=np.float64)
    dofs_torque = np.zeros(self.num_dofs, dtype=np.float64)
    # Motor health (Eden dof order): recorded to --debug_record and used to warn on
    # thermal derating (a frozen/sagging leg is often an overheated motor cutting its
    # own torque, not a controller/policy issue).
    temps = np.zeros(self.num_dofs, dtype=np.float64)
    modes = np.zeros(self.num_dofs, dtype=np.float64)
    full_dofs_pos = np.zeros(self._num_full_dof, dtype=np.float64)

    for i, motor_idx in enumerate(self._dof_index):
        motor = state.motorState[motor_idx]
        dofs_pos[i] = motor.q
        dofs_vel[i] = motor.dq
        dofs_torque[i] = motor.tauEst
        temps[i] = motor.temperature
        modes[i] = motor.mode

    for i in range(self._num_full_dof):
        full_dofs_pos[i] = state.motorState[i].q

    self._warn_thermal(temps, modes)

    return RobotState(
        stamp=time.time(),
        base_quat=np.array(state.imu.quaternion, dtype=np.float64),  # wxyz
        base_ang_vel=np.array(state.imu.gyroscope, dtype=np.float64),  # body frame
        base_lin_acc=np.array(state.imu.accelerometer, dtype=np.float64),
        dofs_pos=dofs_pos,
        dofs_vel=dofs_vel,
        dofs_torque=dofs_torque,
        full_dofs_pos=full_dofs_pos,
        extra={"motor_temp": temps, "motor_mode": modes, **self._battery_extra()},
    )

def send_payload(self, payload: RobotCommand) -> None:
    self._require_connected()

    dofs_pos = self._apply_target_lpf(np.asarray(payload.dofs_pos, dtype=np.float64))

    for i, motor_idx in enumerate(self._dof_index):
        motor_cmd = self._cmd.motorCmd[motor_idx]
        motor_cmd.q = float(dofs_pos[i])
        motor_cmd.dq = float(payload.dofs_vel[i])
        motor_cmd.tau = float(payload.dofs_torque[i])
        if payload.dofs_kp is not None:
            motor_cmd.Kp = float(payload.dofs_kp[i])
        if payload.dofs_kd is not None:
            motor_cmd.Kd = float(payload.dofs_kd[i])

    # Refresh state first so PowerProtect compares against the current measurement,
    # not the one read at the end of the previous tick -- or none at all: the soft
    # shutdown ramp sends without reading.
    # CRC is computed inside SetSend (no manual CRC, unlike the DDS backends).
    self._refresh_state()
    self._safe.PowerProtect(self._cmd, self._state, self.power_protect_factor)
    self._udp.SetSend(self._cmd)
    self._udp.Send()

docs.title: LimX Oli
docs.text:
LimX Dynamics Oli (HU_D04) real-robot deployment backend.

Talks to the robot through the LimX low-level SDK (limxsdk, the Python wheel shipped in https://github.com/limxdynamics/limxsdk-lowlevel): joint state and IMU arrive on subscription callbacks, commands go out via publishRobotCmd. Command/state arrays are indexed in the robot's motor order, which the backend maps to/from Eden's dofs_name order by motor name read live from the robot (getMotorNames()) — LimX's own docs and shipped controller YAMLs disagree on the head-joint order, so a positional map would be silently wrong.

Commands are sent in PR (pitch/roll, serial-joint) space with the SDK's parallel_solve_required flag set, so the SDK converts to the physical A/B motors of the parallel ankle/waist linkages. This matches Eden's :class:~eden.options.robots.limx_oli.Oli model (the serial HU_D04_01.urdf) and LimX's own RL deployment stack; state read back in this mode is PR-space as well.

docs.text:
LimxOliDeployment(env: EnvBase, options: DeploymentOptions)

Bases: CommandRepublisherMixin, SoftShutdownMixin, DeploymentBase

LimX Oli deployment backend on top of :class:DeploymentBase.

Adds, on top of the base options:

  • robot_ip: IP the LimX SDK connects to. None (default) resolves to the ROBOT_IP environment variable, then to the real robot's 10.192.1.2; point it at 127.0.0.1 for the LimX MuJoCo simulator.
  • shutdown_damping_steps / shutdown_damping_kd_scale: soft shutdown — cycles to hold a damping (kp=0, kd) state before releasing.
  • soft_torque_limit: fraction of each joint's torque budget the position term of the implied PD torque may use; every commanded target is clamped to q ± soft_torque_limit * budget / kp around the measured pose. Same 0.95 default as LimX's own walk controller, but without the velocity term theirs includes -- see :meth:_clamp_torque_feasible for the hardware measurements behind that. 0 disables the clamp.
  • clamp_torque_limits: DOF-name pattern -> N·m overrides on top of the robot's default_dofs_force_limits for that budget. Defaults to LimX's deploy-time user_torque_limit where it differs from Eden's training limits: 80 N·m on the six parallel ankle/waist PR joints (two 42 N·m A/B motors each). Training keeps 42 -- the shipped action scale derives from it -- so this is a deploy-only budget.
  • publish_rate: rate at which the current wire command is re-sent between control ticks (default 1000 Hz, LimX's own rate). Load-bearing on this robot: in PR mode the robot evaluates the PD law of the six parallel-linkage joints (ankle pitch/roll, waist roll/pitch) once per received packet, on that packet's state -- measured on hardware, where their torque fits kp*(q_des-q) - kd*dq[previous packet] at R^2 0.92-0.99 while the serial joints fit the same-instant velocity. At 50 Hz that damping term acts on a 20 ms-old velocity, which is anti-damping at 25 Hz: the waist-roll linkage rings at exactly that frequency once a foot strike kicks it. None sends one packet per control tick, for A/B comparison only.
  • motor_name_map: Eden DOF name → SDK motor name overrides for robots whose getMotorNames() vocabulary doesn't match the URDF joint names (unmapped DOFs still match by suffix-normalized name).
  • verbose_diagnostics: also log warning/OK robot diagnostics as they change. By default only error-level (2) diagnostics are logged — the robot's diagnostic stream is chatty and the OK/warning transitions are commissioning detail, but a fault must never be silent.

def connect(self) -> None:
    ensure_limx_sdk()
    self._latest_state = None
    self._latest_imu = None
    self._latest_joy = None
    self._state_event.clear()
    self._imu_event.clear()

    ip = self.robot_ip or os.environ.get("ROBOT_IP") or _DEFAULT_ROBOT_IP
    robot = LimxRobot(LimxRobotType.Humanoid)
    if not robot.init(ip):
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Failed to connect to LimX Oli at {ip}. Check the robot is powered and reachable "
            "(real robot: 10.192.1.2 over the robot's network; LimX MuJoCo sim: 127.0.0.1), "
            "or override the target with the ROBOT_IP environment variable "
            "(or the robot_ip deployment option)."
        )

    motor_names = list(robot.getMotorNames())
    num_motors = int(robot.getMotorNumber())
    if len(motor_names) != num_motors:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"LimX SDK reports {num_motors} motors but {len(motor_names)} motor names: {motor_names}"
        )
    self._dof_index = self._build_dof_index(motor_names)
    self._num_motors = num_motors
    driven = set(self._dof_index)
    idle = [name for i, name in enumerate(motor_names) if i not in driven]
    if idle:
        en.logger.warning(
            f"[deploy] {len(idle)} robot motor(s) are not in the task's DOFs and will be held "
            f"limp (kp=kd=0): {idle}"
        )

    self._cmd = self._init_robot_cmd(motor_names)
    self._last_diagnostic.clear()
    robot.subscribeRobotState(self._on_robot_state)
    robot.subscribeImuData(self._on_imu_data)
    robot.subscribeSensorJoy(self._on_sensor_joy)
    robot.subscribeDiagnosticValue(self._on_diagnostic)
    self._robot = robot

    start_time = time.time()
    while not (self._state_event.is_set() and self._imu_event.is_set()):
        if time.time() - start_time > self.connect_timeout_s:
            missing = [
                name
                for name, event in (("robot state", self._state_event), ("IMU", self._imu_event))
                if not event.is_set()
            ]
            raise RuntimeError(f"Timed out waiting for LimX Oli {' and '.join(missing)} stream(s).")
        time.sleep(0.05)

    self._start_publisher()

def read_state(self) -> RobotState:
    if self._latest_state is None or self._latest_imu is None:
        raise RuntimeError("No LimX Oli robot state / IMU data received yet.")

    msg = self._latest_state
    imu = self._latest_imu
    q = np.asarray(msg.q, dtype=np.float64)
    dq = np.asarray(msg.dq, dtype=np.float64)
    tau = np.asarray(msg.tau, dtype=np.float64)
    if q.shape[0] != self._num_motors:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"LimX robot state carries {q.shape[0]} motors, expected {self._num_motors} "
            "(robot type / firmware mismatch?)."
        )

    return RobotState(
        stamp=time.time(),
        base_quat=np.asarray(imu.quat, dtype=np.float64),  # wxyz, same as Eden
        base_ang_vel=np.asarray(imu.gyro, dtype=np.float64),
        base_lin_acc=np.asarray(imu.acc, dtype=np.float64),
        dofs_pos=q[self._dof_index],
        dofs_vel=dq[self._dof_index],
        dofs_torque=tau[self._dof_index],
        full_dofs_pos=q,
    )

def send_payload(self, payload: RobotCommand) -> None:
    if self._robot is None or self._cmd is None:
        raise RuntimeError("LimX Oli deployment is not connected.")

    # Low-pass the commanded targets (no-op unless --target_lpf < 1) before
    # they hit the wire, so every path (init/hold/policy) is smoothed, then
    # clamp them to the position-torque budget (the clamp runs last so the
    # wire command is guaranteed within it).
    payload.dofs_pos = self._apply_target_lpf(np.asarray(payload.dofs_pos, dtype=np.float64))
    payload.dofs_pos = self._clamp_torque_feasible(payload.dofs_pos, payload.dofs_kp)

    with self._cmd_lock:
        cmd = self._cmd
        cmd.stamp = time.time_ns()
        for i, motor_idx in enumerate(self._dof_index):
            cmd.q[motor_idx] = float(payload.dofs_pos[i])
            cmd.dq[motor_idx] = float(payload.dofs_vel[i])
            cmd.tau[motor_idx] = float(payload.dofs_torque[i])
            if payload.dofs_kp is not None:
                cmd.Kp[motor_idx] = float(payload.dofs_kp[i])
            if payload.dofs_kd is not None:
                cmd.Kd[motor_idx] = float(payload.dofs_kd[i])
        self._robot.publishRobotCmd(cmd)
        self._note_command_published()

It is resolved on its own and scattered onto the force-limit array instead of being merged into one dict, because :func:~eden.utils.string.resolve_matching_names_values refuses a DOF matched by two patterns (waist_*_joint from the robot options and waist_roll_joint from the overrides would collide). def resolve_clamp_torque_limits(
    robot_options: RobotOptions, dofs_name: list[str], overrides: dict[str, float]
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Per-DOF torque budget for the deploy clamp: the robot's force limits with ``overrides`` on top.

    ``overrides`` maps DOF-name patterns to N·m. It is resolved on its own and scattered onto the
    force-limit array instead of being merged into one dict, because
    :func:`~eden.utils.string.resolve_matching_names_values` refuses a DOF matched by two patterns
    (``waist_*_joint`` from the robot options and ``waist_roll_joint`` from the overrides would
    collide). A pattern matching no DOF raises, so a typo cannot silently leave a joint at the
    robot's limit.
    """
    limits = resolve_dofs_values(robot_options.default_dofs_force_limits, dofs_name)
    if overrides:
        idx, _, values = resolve_matching_names_values(overrides, dofs_name)
        limits[idx] = values
    return limits

docs.title: FrankaPandaDeployment
docs.text:
FrankaPandaDeployment(env: EnvBase, options: DeploymentOptions)

Bases: DeploymentBase

Deployment backend for Franka Emika Panda / FR3 via panda-py.

The 7-DOF arm is driven through panda-py's real-time :class:controllers.JointPosition controller running at 1 kHz inside libfranka. The Franka Hand gripper is driven through libfranka's blocking Gripper API, dispatched from a worker thread so the per-step :meth:send_payload call never blocks the control loop.

The arm is fixed-base with no IMU, so :meth:read_state returns an identity base_quat, zero base angular velocity and zero linear acceleration.

Requirements
  • panda-python must be installed with a libfranka build that matches the controller's reported server version. See https://github.com/JeanElsner/panda-py/releases for per-firmware wheels.
  • FCI must be activated in Desk and the joint brakes released.
  • A PREEMPT_RT kernel is strongly recommended for stable 1 kHz control; without it expect occasional communication_constraints_violation.
PARAMETER DESCRIPTION robot_ip

IP address of the Franka Control box. Defaults to the factory IP.

arm_stiffness

Optional 7-element per-joint gains for the JointPosition controller. If None, panda-py's defaults are used.

arm_damping

Optional 7-element per-joint gains for the JointPosition controller. If None, panda-py's defaults are used.

arm_filter_coeff

Exponential low-pass coefficient applied to the JointPosition setpoint inside panda-py's 1 kHz control loop. 1.0 = no filtering (raw step inputs every set_control call); lower values smooth the trajectory. For policy/teleop at 30-100 Hz the controller sees abrupt setpoint changes between updates which cause the arm to buzz/shake under PD, so the default here is 0.05 (panda-py's value is 1.0). Drop further if you still see oscillation; raise toward 1.0 if you need maximum tracking responsiveness at the cost of smoothness.

velocity_safety_factor

Fraction of Panda's per-joint velocity limits that the deployment will allow per control step. send_payload clamps the commanded delta from current_q so the implied joint velocity is bounded by vel_limit * velocity_safety_factor. Direction is preserved by uniformly scaling the delta (rather than clipping per joint, which would distort EE motion). Without this clamp Differential IK near a high-Jacobian configuration can emit deltas that trigger libfranka's joint_velocity_violation reflex. Default 0.5 is conservative; raise toward 1.0 for more aggressive teleop on a PREEMPT_RT kernel.

use_grasp_on_close

When True, the gripper worker uses libfranka.Gripper.grasp (force-controlled) for closing commands and reserves Gripper.move for opening. grasp is more responsive on held objects (it returns as soon as firmware detects finger contact, instead of waiting out move's stall timeout) and applies continuous holding force, so objects don't slip during arm motion. The classification is by absolute target width: a command below close_width_threshold is treated as a close, anything at or above as an open. Disable to fall back to move-only behavior (e.g. if your task is purely position-mode finger control).

close_width_threshold

Target width (m) below which a command is treated as a close (uses grasp when use_grasp_on_close is set). Default 0.04 is roughly half the Franka Hand's max opening.

gripper_speed

Default gripper move speed (m/s).

gripper_force

Default grasp force (N) for the :meth:grasp helper.

gripper_epsilon_inner

Tolerance (m) for :meth:grasp success on the inner/outer side.

gripper_epsilon_outer

Tolerance (m) for :meth:grasp success on the inner/outer side.

skip_gripper_homing

If True, do not run gripper.homing() even when the encoder reports uncalibrated. Useful when an object is already held.

def connect(self) -> None:
    if panda_py is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "panda-python package is not installed. Install the libfranka-matched "
            "wheel from https://github.com/JeanElsner/panda-py/releases ."
        )

    self._panda = panda_py.Panda(self.robot_ip)
    # Clear any latched controller error from a prior session.
    self._panda.recover()

    if self._has_gripper:
        self._gripper = _libfranka.Gripper(self.robot_ip)
        state = self._gripper.read_once()
        # ``max_width`` reads as ~0 when the encoder hasn't been homed
        # this power cycle. Homing fully opens then closes the fingers
        # to calibrate, so it requires nothing be held.
        if not self.skip_gripper_homing and state.max_width <= 0.01:
            en.logger.info("[franka_panda] Homing gripper to calibrate encoder...")
            self._gripper.homing()
            state = self._gripper.read_once()
        if state.max_width > 0.0:
            self._gripper_max_width = float(state.max_width)

        self._gripper_stop.clear()
        self._gripper_thread = threading.Thread(target=self._gripper_worker, daemon=True)
        self._gripper_thread.start()

    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if self.arm_stiffness is not None:
        kwargs["stiffness"] = np.asarray(self.arm_stiffness, dtype=np.float64)
    if self.arm_damping is not None:
        kwargs["damping"] = np.asarray(self.arm_damping, dtype=np.float64)
    # Setpoint low-pass (see ``arm_filter_coeff``). Passed by keyword so a panda-py
    # build that names it differently raises instead of silently ignoring it.
    kwargs["filter_coeff"] = float(self.arm_filter_coeff)
    self._controller = _panda_controllers.JointPosition(**kwargs)

def close(self) -> None:
    self._teardown_common()
    if self._gripper_thread is not None:
        self._gripper_stop.set()
        self._gripper_thread.join(timeout=2.0)
    self._gripper_thread = None

    if self._panda is not None and self._controller_started:
        try:
            self._panda.stop_controller()
        except Exception as e:
            en.logger.warning(f"[franka_panda] stop_controller failed: {e}")
    self._controller_started = False

    if self._gripper is not None:
        try:
            self._gripper.stop()
        except Exception:
            pass

    self._controller = None
    self._gripper = None
    self._panda = None

def read_state(self) -> RobotState:
    if self._panda is None:
        raise RuntimeError("Franka Panda deployment is not connected.")

    s = self._panda.get_state()
    dofs_pos = np.zeros(self.num_dofs, dtype=np.float64)
    dofs_vel = np.zeros(self.num_dofs, dtype=np.float64)
    dofs_torque = np.zeros(self.num_dofs, dtype=np.float64)

    q = np.asarray(s.q, dtype=np.float64)
    dq = np.asarray(s.dq, dtype=np.float64)
    tau = np.asarray(s.tau_J, dtype=np.float64)
    for dof_i, joint_i in zip(self._arm_dof_indices, self._arm_joint_indices):
        dofs_pos[dof_i] = q[joint_i]
        dofs_vel[dof_i] = dq[joint_i]
        dofs_torque[dof_i] = tau[joint_i]

    extra: dict[str, Any] = {
        # O_T_EE is column-major (Fortran) in libfranka.
        "O_T_EE": np.asarray(s.O_T_EE, dtype=np.float64).reshape(4, 4, order="F"),
        "robot_mode": str(s.robot_mode),
    }

    if self._has_gripper and self._gripper is not None:
        g = self._gripper.read_once()
        width = float(g.width)
        # Symmetric split between the two finger joints (the Franka Hand
        # constraint ties them together at 2x the per-finger displacement).
        per_finger = 0.5 * width
        for dof_i in self._finger_dof_indices:
            dofs_pos[dof_i] = per_finger
        extra["gripper_width"] = width
        extra["gripper_is_grasped"] = bool(g.is_grasped)
        extra["gripper_max_width"] = float(g.max_width)

    return RobotState(
        stamp=time.time(),
        base_quat=np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),  # identity (wxyz) - fixed-base arm
        base_ang_vel=np.zeros(3),
        base_lin_acc=np.zeros(3),
        dofs_pos=dofs_pos,
        dofs_vel=dofs_vel,
        dofs_torque=dofs_torque,
        extra=extra,
    )

def send_payload(self, payload: RobotCommand) -> None:
    if self._panda is None or self._controller is None:
        raise RuntimeError("Franka Panda deployment is not connected.")
    if not self._controller_started:
        # The first payload is the boot STOP hold of the measured pose, so the controller
        # starts with the arm's own pose as its setpoint: no jerk.
        self._panda.start_controller(self._controller)
        self._controller_started = True

    # Low-pass the arm on every path (hold / INIT / policy); the payload carries what is sent. Not
    # the fingers: a filtered width ramps over many ticks, the gripper worker dispatches each step
    # of it as a new command, and every new command stops the one in flight -- a closing grasp
    # would be stopped and re-issued at the control rate (:meth:`_gripper_worker`).
    commanded = np.asarray(payload.dofs_pos, dtype=np.float64)
    sent = self._apply_target_lpf(commanded)
    sent[self._finger_dof_indices] = commanded[self._finger_dof_indices]
    payload.dofs_pos = sent
    target_q = self._extract_arm_target(payload.dofs_pos)
    target_q = self._clamp_arm_velocity(target_q)
    self._controller.set_control(target_q)

    # The hold, the INIT ramp and the START tick leave the gripper at the policy's last
    # command: a target from the measured width would stop a force-controlled grasp and
    # re-send it as a plain move, and INIT's default width would open it on what it holds.
    if self._has_gripper and not self.sending_hold:
        self._set_gripper_target(self._extract_target_width(payload.dofs_pos))

def grasp(self, width: float, force: float | None = None) -> bool:
    """Grasp (synchronously) an object of approximately ``width`` meters.

    Returns ``True`` when the firmware reports the fingers clamped on
    something within the configured tolerance. Sets the background
    gripper worker's target to ``width`` first, so the worker does not
    countermand the grasp with a ``move`` of its own.
    """
    if self._gripper is None:
        raise RuntimeError("Gripper is not configured for this deployment.")
    with self._gripper_command_lock:
        self._gripper_target_width = float(width)
    return bool(
        self._gripper.grasp(
            width=float(width),
            speed=self.gripper_speed,
            force=float(force if force is not None else self.gripper_force),
            epsilon_inner=self.gripper_epsilon_inner,
            epsilon_outer=self.gripper_epsilon_outer,
        )
    )

docs.text:
RoboTeraXHandDeployment(env: EnvBase, options: DeploymentOptions)

Bases: DeploymentBase

Deployment backend for the RoboTera XHand1 dexterous hand.

Supports both EtherCAT and RS485 communication protocols. For RS485 you must also set serial_port and baud_rate to match your hardware.

The hand is treated as a fixed-base robot: read_state returns an identity quaternion and zero angular velocity because the hand has no IMU.

Joint velocity is a finite difference. The SDK's FingerState_t has a position and no velocity, so read_state differences consecutive positions over the wall-clock time between the two reads (monotonic clock). The first read after connect has no previous sample and reports zero. It is a control-period average, not the instantaneous value the simulator reports, so expect it to be noisier and a period late.

The hand runs its own PD, with the gains below -- not the command's. finger_command carries kp / ki / kd as int16 values in firmware units, which have no known mapping to the N·m/rad of :attr:RobotCommand.dofs_kp (the xhand1 sysid example fits the effective sim-side gains for that reason). So send_payload forwards positions only: RobotCommand.dofs_kp / dofs_kd / dofs_vel / dofs_torque are not sent, and the firmware gains are set once at connect from dofs_kp / dofs_ki / dofs_kd. A payload with kp = 0 therefore changes nothing on the hand. The two base options that work through command gains, deploy_kp_kd_scale and disable_joints, are refused at construction rather than accepted and ignored. Change these options instead. connect logs the gains it programs.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION protocol

Bus to open. RS485 also needs serial_port and baud_rate.

RS485 device path.

def connect(self) -> None:
    if xhand_control is None:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "xhand_controller package is not installed. Install it before using RoboTeraXHandDeployment."
        )

    self._device = xhand_control.XHandControl()

    if self.protocol == "EtherCAT":
        ports = self._device.enumerate_devices("EtherCAT")
        if not ports:
            raise RuntimeError("No EtherCAT XHand devices found.")
        rsp = self._device.open_ethercat(ports[0])
    elif self.protocol == "RS485":
        rsp = self._device.open_serial(self.serial_port, self.baud_rate)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown protocol '{self.protocol}'. Expected 'RS485' or 'EtherCAT'.")

    if rsp.error_code != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to open XHand device: {rsp.error_message}")

    # Wait until the device enumerates at least one hand, then verify that the
    # configured hand_id is present.  When hand_id is 0 (default) we auto-select
    # the first discovered hand for single-hand setups.
    start_time = time.time()
    while True:
        ids = self._device.list_hands_id()
        if ids:
            if self.hand_id in ids:
                self._active_hand_id = self.hand_id
                break
            if self.hand_id == 0:
                self._active_hand_id = ids[0]
                break
            raise RuntimeError(f"Configured hand_id {self.hand_id} not found. Available hand IDs: {ids}")
        if time.time() - start_time > self.connect_timeout_s:
            raise RuntimeError("Timed out waiting for XHand device to enumerate hand IDs.")
        time.sleep(0.05)

    self._hand_cmd = xhand_control.HandCommand_t()
    for i in range(_NUM_JOINTS):
        fc = self._hand_cmd.finger_command[i]
        fc.id = i
        fc.kp = self.dofs_kp
        fc.ki = self.dofs_ki
        fc.kd = self.dofs_kd
        fc.position = 0.0
        fc.tor_max = self.tor_max
        fc.mode = self.finger_mode

    # A fresh link has no previous sample: the first read reports zero velocity.
    self._prev_dofs_pos = None
    self._prev_read_t = None
    en.logger.info(
        f"[deploy] XHand firmware PD: kp={self.dofs_kp} ki={self.dofs_ki} kd={self.dofs_kd} "
        f"tor_max={self.tor_max} (firmware units, on every finger). RobotCommand gains are not "
        "forwarded; set the dofs_kp / dofs_ki / dofs_kd deployment options to change these."
    )

def read_state(self) -> RobotState:
    if self._device is None:
        raise RuntimeError("XHand deployment is not connected.")

    for attempt in range(self.crc_retries):
        err, state = self._device.read_state(self._active_hand_id, True)
        if err.error_code == 0:
            break
        en.logger.warning(f"read_state CRC error (attempt {attempt + 1}/{self.crc_retries}): {err.error_message}")
    else:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to read XHand state after {self.crc_retries} attempts: {err.error_message}")
    read_t = time.perf_counter()

    dofs_pos = np.zeros(self.num_dofs, dtype=np.float64)
    dofs_torque = np.zeros(self.num_dofs, dtype=np.float64)

    joint_diagnostics: list[dict] = []
    for i, finger_idx in enumerate(self._dof_index):
        finger = state.finger_state[finger_idx]
        dofs_pos[i] = finger.position
        dofs_torque[i] = finger.torque
        joint_diagnostics.append(
            {
                "id": finger.id,
                "raw_position": finger.raw_position,
                "sensor_id": finger.sensor_id,
                "temperature": finger.temperature,
                "commboard_err": finger.commboard_err,
                "jonitboard_err": finger.jonitboard_err,
                "tipboard_err": finger.tipboard_err,
            }
        )

    # Collect fingertip tactile data for the five sensor-equipped fingers.
    fingertip_sensors: dict[int, dict] = {}
    for sensor_idx, finger_id in enumerate(_SENSOR_FINGERS):
        sensor_data = state.sensor_data[sensor_idx]
        fingertip_sensors[finger_id] = {
            "calc_pressure": np.array(
                [
                    sensor_data.calc_force.fx,
                    sensor_data.calc_force.fy,
                    sensor_data.calc_force.fz,
                ]
            ),
            "raw_pressure": np.array([[force.fx, force.fy, force.fz] for force in sensor_data.raw_force]),
            "sensor_temperature": sensor_data.calc_temperature,
        }

    dofs_vel = self._finite_difference_dofs_vel(dofs_pos, read_t)

    return RobotState(
        stamp=time.time(),
        # The XHand1 is a fixed-base end-effector with no on-board IMU.
        base_quat=np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0]),  # identity (wxyz)
        base_ang_vel=np.zeros(3),
        base_lin_acc=np.zeros(3),
        dofs_pos=dofs_pos,
        dofs_vel=dofs_vel,
        dofs_torque=dofs_torque,
        extra={
            "fingertip_sensors": fingertip_sensors,
            "joint_diagnostics": joint_diagnostics,
        },
    )

def send_payload(self, payload: RobotCommand) -> None:
    if self._device is None or self._hand_cmd is None:
        raise RuntimeError("XHand deployment is not connected.")

    # Low-pass every path (hold / INIT / policy); the payload carries what is sent.
    payload.dofs_pos = self._apply_target_lpf(np.asarray(payload.dofs_pos, dtype=np.float64))
    for i, finger_idx in enumerate(self._dof_index):
        fc = self._hand_cmd.finger_command[finger_idx]
        fc.id = finger_idx
        fc.position = float(payload.dofs_pos[i])

    for attempt in range(self.crc_retries):
        err = self._device.send_command(self._active_hand_id, self._hand_cmd)
        if err.error_code == 0:
            break
        en.logger.warning(f"send_command CRC error (attempt {attempt + 1}/{self.crc_retries}): {err.error_message}")
    else:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to send XHand command after {self.crc_retries} attempts: {err.error_message}")

docs.title: Wuji Hand
docs.text:
Wuji Hand 1 / Hand 2 real-robot deployment backend.

Both generations are 20-DOF hands (5 fingers x 4 joints) whose SDKs speak joint angles in radians, finger-major (thumb first), in the MJCF joint directions -- no sign or offset conversion. The SDK order is the same for a right and a left hand; the side is a property of the joint names, which :data:WUJI_JOINT_IDX maps for both sides and both naming schemes in Eden:

  • {right,left}_finger{1..5}_joint{1..4} (:class:~eden.options.robots.wuji_hand1.WujiHand1_R and the wuji-mjlab task models), and
  • {r,l}_{thumb_cmc_flex, ..., pinky_dip} (:class:~eden.options.robots.wuji_hand2beta2.WujiHand2Beta2_R), whose declaration order is the same finger-major order (upstream WUJI_HAND2_TASK_NAMES).

A :class:HandTransport is the wire to one hand: :class:Hand1Transport (wujihandpy) or :class:Hand2Transport (wuji_sdk). It streams targets the way upstream wuji-mjlab does:

  • "sync" (upstream reorient): :meth:HandTransport.command blocks for one control period, writing servo_hz linearly interpolated sub-targets from the previous command to the new one.
  • "thread" (upstream pen spin): :meth:HandTransport.command starts a new ramp and returns; a background thread streams it at servo_hz and holds the target once the ramp ends.

:class:WujiHandDeployment drives one hand through a transport it builds at :meth:connect, or one handed to it with :meth:WujiHandDeployment.use_transport (a simulator, for sim-to-sim).

def hold(self) -> None:
    """Let one control period pass with no new target, holding the last one.

    ``"sync"`` re-streams the last command across the period through :meth:`_ramp`, so a tick
    that sends nothing still lasts one control period (on a simulator's clock too); before any
    command there is nothing to hold, and it only waits. ``"thread"`` returns at once: the servo
    thread is already holding, and the base rate limiter paces the loop.
    """
    if self.stream.mode != "sync":
        self._raise_if_servo_failed()
        return
    if self._cmd is None:
        time.sleep(self.stream.interp_s)
        return
    self._ramp(self._cmd, self._cmd, self.stream.interp_s)

ease_to(goal: ndarray, duration_s: float, rate_hz: float, profile: str, guard: Callable[[], None] | None = None) -> None

Move from the measured pose to goal: upstream's home (cosine, 100 Hz) or start-pose smoothstep.

guard runs before every waypoint, so a safety check that raises stops a multi-second move where it is, holding the last waypoint, instead of only before it starts.

Source code in eden/extensions/deployment/wuji_hand.py 
def ease_to(
    self,
    goal: np.ndarray,
    duration_s: float,
    rate_hz: float,
    profile: str,
    guard: Callable[[], None] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Move from the measured pose to ``goal``: upstream's ``home`` (cosine, 100 Hz) or start-pose smoothstep.

    ``guard`` runs before every waypoint, so a safety check that raises stops a multi-second
    move where it is, holding the last waypoint, instead of only before it starts.
    """
    if not (duration_s >= 0.0 and rate_hz > 0.0):
        raise ValueError(f"ease_to needs duration_s >= 0 and rate_hz > 0; got {duration_s!r}, {rate_hz!r}.")
    goal = _checked(goal, self.joint_names)
    start = self.read().copy()
    n = max(1, round(duration_s * rate_hz))
    path = [start + ease(i / n, profile) * (goal - start) for i in range(1, n + 1)]
    if self.stream.mode == "sync":
        for prev, q in zip([start, *path], path):
            if guard is not None:
                guard()
            self._ramp(prev, q, 1.0 / rate_hz)
            self._cmd = q.copy()
        return
    if self._servo_thread is None:
        self._cmd = start
    for q in path:
        if guard is not None:
            guard()
        self._ensure_servo()
        self._set_segment(q, q)
        time.sleep(1.0 / rate_hz)

def connect(self) -> None:
    self._stale = None
    try:
        import wujihandpy
    except ImportError as e:
        raise ImportError(
            "Wuji Hand 1 needs wujihandpy (upstream pins 1.5.1): pip install wujihandpy==1.5.1"
        ) from e
    self._hand = wujihandpy.Hand()
    self._hand.write_joint_effort_limit(float(self.effort_limit_a))
    # Energized from here on: any failure must de-energize before propagating.
    try:
        self._hand.write_joint_enabled(True)
        self._ctrl_cm = self._hand.realtime_controller(
            enable_upstream=True, filter=wujihandpy.filter.LowPass(cutoff_freq=float(self.lowpass_cutoff_hz))
        )
        self._ctrl = self._ctrl_cm.__enter__()
    except BaseException:
        self.disconnect()
        raise
    en.logger.info(
        f"[wuji] Hand 1 enabled: current limit {self.effort_limit_a:g} A, target low-pass "
        f"{self.lowpass_cutoff_hz:g} Hz, {self.stream.mode} streaming at {self.stream.servo_hz:g} Hz"
    )

Source code in eden/extensions/deployment/wuji_hand.py 
def connect(self) -> None:
    from eden.utils.devices.wuji.glove import load_sdk

    self._sdk = wuji_sdk = load_sdk()
    self._mgr = wuji_sdk.SdkManager.instance()
    sn = self.serial_number or self._only_hand_on_the_bus()
    self._hand = self._mgr.connect(
        sn=sn, device_name=self.device_name, options=wuji_sdk.ConnectOptions(enable_bridge=False)
    )
    en.logger.info(f"[wuji] connected Wuji Hand 2 sn={self._hand.serial_number}")
    # Connected from here on: any failure must disable and release the link before propagating.
    try:
        n_online = self._hand.online_joints_count().get()
        if (self.require_all_joints and n_online != NUM_JOINTS) or n_online == 0:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Wuji Hand 2 {sn}: {n_online}/{NUM_JOINTS} joints online; refusing to move an incomplete "
                "hand (a missing joint reads back as its default pose). To run with the joints that are "
                "online, WujiHandDeployment.configure(require_all_joints=False)."
            )
        g = self.gains
        self._hand.effort_limit().set([float(a) for a in g.effort_limit_a])
        self._hand.mit_params().set(
            [wuji_sdk.MitParam(float(p), float(d)) for p, d in zip(g.kp, g.kd, strict=True)]
        )
        self._sub = self._hand.joint_states().subscribe_with_callback(self._on_state)
        try:
            self._diag_sub = self._hand.joint_diagnostics().subscribe_with_callback(self._on_diag)
        except Exception as e:
            en.logger.warning(f"[wuji] joint_diagnostics unavailable ({e}); faults limited to stale feedback")
        self._hand.enable()
        time.sleep(_HAND2_ARM_DELAY_S)
        self._pub = self._hand.joint_command().publish()
        self._await_feedback(n_online)
    except BaseException:
        self.disconnect()
        raise
    partial = "" if self._watched.all() else f", {int(self._watched.sum())}/{NUM_JOINTS} joints online"
    en.logger.info(
        f"[wuji] Hand 2 enabled: kp {min(g.kp):.3g}-{max(g.kp):.3g}, kd {min(g.kd):.3g}-{max(g.kd):.3g}, "
        f"current limit {min(g.effort_limit_a):g}-{max(g.effort_limit_a):g} A, "
        f"{self.stream.mode} streaming at {self.stream.servo_hz:g} Hz{partial}"
    )

def fault(self) -> str | None:
    for nid, code in list(self._errors):
        if (nid, code) in self._dismissed:
            continue
        i = _nid_index(nid)
        joint = f"joint {self.joint_names[i]!r} (nid={nid})" if i is not None else f"node nid={nid}"
        detail, severity = f"0x{code:04X}", ""
        try:
            d = self._hand.describe_error(code)
            if isinstance(d, dict):
                severity = str(d.get("severity", ""))
                detail = f"0x{code:04X} {d.get('name')} [{severity}] {d.get('desc')} ({d.get('resolution')})"
        except Exception:
            pass  # the bare code is still reported below
        if "warn" in severity.lower():
            en.logger.warning(f"[wuji] {joint} warning {detail}")
            self._dismissed.add((nid, code))
            continue
        return f"{joint} error {detail}"
    return None

def stale(self) -> str | None:
    now = time.monotonic()
    with self._state_lock:
        ages, last = now - self._joint_t, self._last_state_t
    if (feed_age := now - last) > self.stale_after_s:
        return f"joint_states feed stale for {feed_age:.1f} s (bus or link lost?)"
    if missing := [self.joint_names[i] for i in np.flatnonzero(self._watched & (ages > self.stale_after_s))]:
        return f"joint feedback stale for {missing}"
    return None

def disconnect(self) -> None:
    if self._hand is None:
        return
    try:
        self._hand.disable()
    except Exception as e:
        en.logger.warning(f"[wuji] Hand 2 disable failed: {e}")
    for sub in (self._diag_sub, self._sub):
        try:

        except Exception as e:
            en.logger.warning(f"[wuji] Hand 2 subscription close failed: {e}")

    try:

    except Exception as e:
        en.logger.warning(f"[wuji] Hand 2 disconnect failed: {e}")

docs.title: WujiHandDeployment
docs.text:
WujiHandDeployment(env: EnvBase, options: DeploymentOptions)

Bases: DeploymentBase

A Wuji Hand 1 or Hand 2, right or left, on a fixed mount.

The side comes from the robot's joint names (see :data:WUJI_JOINT_IDX); the deployment DOF order may be any permutation of the 20 joints, and is scattered into the SDK's order on the way out and gathered back on the way in. The hand has no IMU: :meth:read_state reports the mount orientation (the robot's default_root_quat) as the base's.

Joint velocity is a finite difference of consecutive reads over the transport's clock, like the XHand's (neither SDK reports one), optionally low-passed (vel_lowpass_hz).

Gains are programmed once at connect, never per command. Hand 2 takes MIT kp / kd (mit_kp / mit_kd, default the payload's nominal gains: the robot's default_dofs_kp / default_dofs_kd times deploy_kp_kd_scale). Hand 1 runs its own position loop and has no gain to set. So disable_joints (which works by zeroing command gains) is refused for both, and deploy_kp_kd_scale / mit_kp / mit_kd for Hand 1.

Loop order. The base control tick (:meth:DeploymentBase.step, the operator state machine every backend runs) with this backend's hooks: :meth:check_safety first, then the command is sent and the period waited out, then the env's episode clock advances (episode_length_buf: the scene is never stepped here, and action warm-ups and clip clocks read it), then the hand is read and :meth:sync_scene -- the hook a subclass uses to write anything else it observes (a camera-tracked object) into the scene -- runs, and only then do the commands publish (sync_before_commands), so a command that grades the new state sees it this tick. In stream_mode="sync" sending the command is the wait (it streams sub-targets across one control period, as upstream does), so the base's rate limiter is not used on top of it: a tick takes one control period, and the inference time is absorbed into it (each period's deadline is chained from the previous one, as upstream anchors its loop before inference). A tick with nothing to send (action=None before a slot has written targets) holds the last target for the period instead (:meth:HandTransport.hold), so it still lasts one period and the episode clock and the reference cannot race ahead at the speed of the loop.

Boot, INIT and START. :meth:reset restarts the episode clock and the velocity estimate and boots in STOP, holding the measured pose. The operator's INIT ramps from the pose measured at the press to init_target over init_steps ticks and holds it; START hands the hand to the policy. :meth:check_safety runs before every one of those ticks, and :meth:ease_to runs :meth:check_hand before every waypoint.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION hand

Hardware generation. None infers it from the robot options (WujiHand1* -> "hand1", WujiHand2Beta2* -> "hand2"); any other robot must set it.

TYPE: ('hand1', 'hand2') DEFAULT: "hand1"

serial_number

Hand 2 to connect; empty connects the only hand on the bus.

TYPE: str

stream_mode

How targets are streamed (see the module docstring).

TYPE: ('sync', 'thread') DEFAULT: "sync"

servo_hz

Rate of the interpolated sub-targets.

TYPE: float

effort_limit_a

Joint current limit, A. None: upstream's defaults, 0.5 (Hand 1) / 1.0 (Hand 2).

TYPE: float | None

lowpass_cutoff_hz

Hand 1's target low-pass cutoff.

TYPE: float

mit_kp

Hand 2's MIT gains: one value for every joint, or a pattern-keyed dict covering all 20. None: the payload's nominal gains.

TYPE: float | dict[str, float] | None

mit_kd

Hand 2's MIT gains: one value for every joint, or a pattern-keyed dict covering all 20. None: the payload's nominal gains.

TYPE: float | dict[str, float] | None

require_all_joints

TYPE: bool

:meth:check_hand raises :class:DeployStop on a latched hand fault. Stale joint feedback stops the run regardless: a policy must never run on a frozen reading.

TYPE: bool

def read_state(self) -> RobotState:
    q = self.from_sdk(self.transport.read())
    t = self.transport.clock()
    if self._prev_q is not None and t > self._prev_t:
        dt = t - self._prev_t
        vel = (q - self._prev_q) / dt
        if self.vel_lowpass_hz:
            a = dt / (dt + 1.0 / (2.0 * np.pi * self.vel_lowpass_hz))
            vel = a * vel + (1.0 - a) * self._vel
        self._vel = vel
    self._prev_q, self._prev_t = q.copy(), t
    return RobotState(
        stamp=t,
        base_quat=self._mount_quat,
        base_ang_vel=np.zeros(3),
        base_lin_acc=np.zeros(3),
        dofs_pos=q,
        dofs_vel=self._vel.copy(),
        dofs_torque=np.zeros(self.num_dofs),
    )

def ease_to(self, target: np.ndarray, duration_s: float, rate_hz: float, profile: str = "cosine") -> None:
    """Move the hand from its measured pose to ``target`` (deployment DOF order), ``"cosine"`` or ``"smoothstep"``.

    :meth:`check_hand` runs before every waypoint. The eased path is not low-passed (it is smooth
    already), but ``target_lpf`` restarts from ``target``, so the next command filters from where
    the hand was eased to rather than pulling it back toward the target before the ease.
    """
    self.check_hand()
    en.logger.info(f"[wuji] easing the hand to its target over {duration_s:g} s ({profile})")
    target = self._clip(np.asarray(target, dtype=np.float64))
    self.transport.ease_to(self.to_sdk(target), duration_s, rate_hz, profile, guard=self.check_hand)
    if self.target_lpf < 1.0:
        self._lpf_prev = target.copy()

def sdk_index_map(names: Sequence[str], owner: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """Each of ``names``' index in the SDK's joint array, raising (as ``owner``) unless they cover the 20 once each."""
    index = resolve_dof_index_map(names, WUJI_JOINT_IDX, owner=owner, what="Wuji SDK joint index", hint=_NAMING_HINT)
    if sorted(index) != list(range(NUM_JOINTS)):
        by_index = {i: [n for n, j in zip(names, index) if j == i] for i in sorted(set(index))}
        missing = sorted(set(range(NUM_JOINTS)) - set(index))
        twice = {i: dup for i, dup in by_index.items() if len(dup) > 1}
        raise ValueError(
            f"{owner}: the joints must cover each of the {NUM_JOINTS} Wuji SDK joints once; SDK joints {missing} "
            f"have no joint and {twice} have several (SDK index: joint names). {_NAMING_HINT}"
        )
    return np.asarray(index)
