robot_options() -> G1Dofs29

Return a G1Dofs29 carrying the standing pose and PD gains the checkpoint expects.

This is the robot a task-less eden deploy/inference --policy sonic builds its scene from, so it decides both where the robot stands before the policy takes over and — via :class:~eden.extensions.deployment.base.DeploymentBase, which resolves default_dofs_kp / default_dofs_kd once into the Kp/Kd sent on the wire — what PD loop tracks its targets.

Pose is :data:~eden.extensions.policies.sonic.joint_maps.SONIC_DOFS_POS, the default_angles[] the action transform is centred on. The stock G1's shallower stance would leave the robot 0.37 rad off at the knees and 0.9 rad at the elbows when SONIC's first target lands.

Gains differ from the stock G1 in the hip-pitch row alone: SONIC derives them from the same motor table by the same Raibert heuristic Eden does, and hip pitch is the one row where the tables disagree — SONIC's is a 7520-22, Eden's stock spec a 7520-14. The stock gains would run the hips at 0.41x the released checkpoint's stiffness (40.18 vs 99.10 N·m/rad) under the 7520-22 action scale, i.e. 2.4x less torque per unit action than trained.

Armature and effort limits stay on the stock spec: those describe the physical actuator, not the controller, and which motor a given G1 revision carries is a hardware question this port cannot settle. Note the consequence — Genesis builds hip pitch with the 7520-14 armature (0.0102 vs SONIC's 0.0251 kg·m²) and clamps its torque at 88 rather than 139 N·m, so a Genesis rollout is still not SONIC's training dynamics even with the gains fixed.

docs.text:
reset(envs_idx: slice | Tensor | None = None) -> None

Clear per-episode state at episode boundaries.

Resets: * History ring buffers (q, qdot, action, base_ang, gravity). Without clearing, the first decoder call after a reset sees the previous episode's last 10 frames and produces a discontinuous initial action. * The heading offset — re-captured per env on the next step() against whatever pose the motion was just resampled to. Critical for sampling_mode != "start" (where the motion frame index changes across episodes) and on motion wrap-around. Only the affected rows are marked for re-capture, so partial resets in batched rollouts leave the other envs' offsets intact.

Source code in eden/extensions/policies/sonic/policy.py 
def reset(self, envs_idx: (slice | torch.Tensor) | None = None) -> None:
    """Clear per-episode state at episode boundaries.

    Resets:
    * History ring buffers (``q``, ``qdot``, ``action``, ``base_ang``,
      ``gravity``). Without clearing, the first decoder call after a reset
      sees the previous episode's last 10 frames and produces a
      discontinuous initial action.
    * The heading offset — re-captured per env on the next ``step()``
      against whatever pose the motion was just resampled to. Critical for
      ``sampling_mode != "start"`` (where the motion frame index changes
      across episodes) and on motion wrap-around. Only the affected rows
      are marked for re-capture, so partial resets in batched rollouts
      leave the other envs' offsets intact.
    """
    for buf in self._hist_buffers:
        if envs_idx is None:
            buf.zero_()
        else:
            buf[envs_idx] = 0.0
    # Mark the affected envs for heading re-capture on their next step
    # against the fresh post-reset state.
    if envs_idx is None:
        self._needs_heading_capture.fill_(True)
        self._prev_time_steps = None
    else:
        self._needs_heading_capture[envs_idx] = True

def step(self, obs: dict[str, torch.Tensor | dict[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    # Read off the entity, not an observation group: this policy rides along as an extra deploy
    # slot on another policy's or task's env, whose groups are not its own (see the
    # "Declare the observation" section of docs/guides/policy-porting.md).
    del obs  # raw simulator state is read directly from the env
    robot = self.env.entities[self.entity_name]
    motion_cmd = self.env.command_manager.get_term("motion")

    pelvis_quat_wxyz = self._update_state_history(robot)

    # ---- motion future references (g1 mode encoder input) ----
    time_steps = motion_cmd.time_steps
    # Per-env motion length (multi-clip envs each track their own clip), so
    # the end-of-motion clamp is per-env. Single-clip: a constant vector.
    last_frame = motion_cmd.frame_total_per_env() - 1  # (N,)
    # NOTE: end-of-motion behavior is `clamp` (hold the last frame), not
    # `wrap` — matches the C++ deploy. If the motion wraps via
    # `_update_command`, the wrap-detection block below re-captures the
    # heading offset against the new motion-start pose.
    # `.minimum` (not `.clamp_max`) because the bound is a per-env tensor.
    future_t = (time_steps[:, None] + self._future_offsets[None, :]).minimum(last_frame[:, None])

    # Motion joint pos / vel are fed RAW (no default-angle subtraction) —
    # this matches both gear_sonic's `command_multi_future` (returns
    # `motion_lib.get_dof_pos(...)` directly) and the C++ deploy's
    # `GatherMotionJointPositionsMultiFrame` (raw memcpy from
    # `motion->JointPositions(frame)`). Only the robot's history obs
    # subtracts the default — see the q_rel computation in _update_state_history.
    # Motion data is stored in MJCF order (Eden's convention); reorder to IL.
    future_q_mj = motion_cmd.gather_motion_frames("dofs_pos", future_t)  # (N, F, 29)
    future_qdot_mj = motion_cmd.gather_motion_frames("dofs_vel", future_t)  # (N, F, 29)
    future_q_il = future_q_mj[..., self._mj_to_il]
    future_qdot_il = future_qdot_mj[..., self._mj_to_il]

    # ---- heading alignment (yaw-only) ----
    # `apply_delta_heading` in the C++ deploy =
    #   R(robot_init_yaw) · R(motion_init_yaw)^{-1}
    # Captured per env on the first step after that env's reset AND on that
    # env's motion wrap-around (when `MotionCommand._update_command`
    # resamples and its `time_steps` regresses). The same yaw offset is
    # applied to all future motion anchor quats until the env's next
    # reset/wrap. Without this, the robot's world heading drifts away from
    # the motion's heading and the anchor-orientation obs degrades.
    motion_pelvis_now_wxyz = motion_cmd.gather_motion_frames("links_quat_w", time_steps[:, None])[:, 0, 0]  # (N, 4)
    capture = self._needs_heading_capture.clone()
    if self._prev_time_steps is not None:
        capture |= time_steps < self._prev_time_steps  # per-env wrap detection
    # Compute the offset full-batch and write only the rows that need (re)capture.
    # No `bool(capture.any())` guard: that scalar read forces a per-step GPU→CPU
    # sync on the inference hot path. The masked `torch.where` is already a no-op
    # for the (usual) all-false case, matching CommandManager's unconditional-
    # masked-op convention.
    # `apply_delta_heading = robot_yaw * inv(motion_yaw)`, left-multiplied onto
    # the raw motion anchor quat.
    robot_yaw = yaw_quat(pelvis_quat_wxyz)
    motion_yaw = yaw_quat(motion_pelvis_now_wxyz)
    offset = transform_quat_by_quat(inv_quat(motion_yaw), robot_yaw)
    self._heading_offset_wxyz = torch.where(capture[:, None], offset, self._heading_offset_wxyz)
    self._needs_heading_capture &= ~capture
    self._prev_time_steps = time_steps.clone()

    # Future anchor (pelvis) orientation as 6D rotation in robot pelvis frame:
    #   corrected = apply_delta_heading · raw_ref
    #   rel       = inv(R(robot_pelvis_now)) · corrected
    # then convert to the 6D rep used by gear_sonic's motion_anchor_ori_b_mf.
    #
    # Both operands are (N, F, 4) — `transform_quat_by_quat` broadcasts on
    # the leading axes, so we skip the explicit `.expand(...).reshape(...)`
    # round-trips and only flatten once before the final `_quat_to_6d`.
    ref_pelvis_quat = motion_cmd.gather_motion_frames("links_quat_w", future_t)[..., 0, :]  # (N, F, 4)
    heading = self._heading_offset_wxyz[:, None, :]  # (N, 1, 4)
    cur_pelvis_inv = inv_quat(pelvis_quat_wxyz)[:, None, :]  # (N, 1, 4)
    corrected_ref = transform_quat_by_quat(ref_pelvis_quat, heading)  # (N, F, 4)
    rel_quat = transform_quat_by_quat(corrected_ref, cur_pelvis_inv)  # (N, F, 4)
    rel_anchor_6d = _quat_to_6d(rel_quat).reshape(-1, _FUTURE_LEN * 6)

    # ---- build encoder input (1762 dim, mostly zero for g1 mode) ----
    N = self._encoder_buf.shape[0]
    self._encoder_buf.zero_()
    self._write_slot(
        self._encoder_buf,
        _ENCODER_OFFSETS,
        "encoder_mode_4",
        self._encoder_mode_value.expand(N, -1),
    )
    self._write_slot(
        self._encoder_buf,
        _ENCODER_OFFSETS,
        "motion_joint_positions_10frame_step5",
        future_q_il.reshape(N, _FUTURE_LEN * _NUM_DOFS),
    )
    self._write_slot(
        self._encoder_buf,
        _ENCODER_OFFSETS,
        "motion_joint_velocities_10frame_step5",
        future_qdot_il.reshape(N, _FUTURE_LEN * _NUM_DOFS),
    )
    self._write_slot(self._encoder_buf, _ENCODER_OFFSETS, "motion_anchor_orientation_10frame_step5", rel_anchor_6d)
    # All other slots stay zero — they're for teleop / SMPL modes.

    # ---- encoder → token_state → decoder → action (IL order) ----
    action_il = self._decode(self._encode())
    self._push_action_history(action_il)

    # ---- isaaclab→mjcf permutation + action transform ----
    action_mj = action_il[..., self._il_to_mj]
    joint_pos_targets = self._default_angles_mj + self._action_scale_mj * action_mj
    return {"dofs_pos_controller": joint_pos_targets}

def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: PolicyOptions) -> None:
    super().__init__(env, options)

    self.device = env.device
    robot = self.require_entity(self.entity_name)
    # The joint observations and the action term read the robot's DOFs in its own order.
    if list(robot.dofs_name) != list(POLICY_JOINT_NAMES):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Twist2Policy drives the G1's 29 DOFs in {list(POLICY_JOINT_NAMES)} order; this robot's "
            f"dofs_name is {robot.dofs_name}. Build the robot from Twist2Policy.robot_options()."
        )

    # The built robot must carry the knees-bent keyframe in every env: the joint-position
    # observation and the action term are both relative to its default pose.
    expected_default = torch.tensor(DEFAULT_POS, device=env.device)
    built_default = robot.get_default_dofs_pos(POLICY_JOINT_NAMES).to(env.device)  # (num_envs, NUM_JOINTS)
    # ``allclose``'s tolerance, per env: the first env whose row is off is the one named.
    mismatched = ~torch.isclose(built_default, expected_default, atol=1e-6).all(dim=1)
    if mismatched.any().item():
        env_idx = int(mismatched.nonzero()[0].item())
        raise ValueError(
            f"Robot default_dofs_pos does not match TWIST2's knees-bent keyframe in env {env_idx}: "
            f"built={built_default[env_idx].tolist()} expected={expected_default.tolist()}. "
            "Build the robot from Twist2Policy.robot_options()."
        )

    # The env has to be the one this policy declares: a task env publishes its own
    # ``policy`` group, which the actor would read as garbage.
    expected_dim = ACTOR_HISTORY_LENGTH * ACTOR_CURRENT_DIM
    group_dims = env.observation_manager.group_obs_dim
    if group_dims.get(OBS_GROUP) != (expected_dim,):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Twist2Policy reads a {expected_dim}-dim '{OBS_GROUP}' observation group, but this env "
            f"publishes {group_dims}. Build the env from Twist2Policy.observation_options() (a task-less "
            f"`eden inference --policy twist2` does), not from another task's config."
        )

    self._actor = Twist2Actor(self.checkpoint_path, device=str(env.device))

def step(self, obs: dict[str, torch.Tensor | dict[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    history = obs[OBS_GROUP]  # (N, 11 * 127), oldest first, so the newest frame is the current one

def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: PolicyOptions) -> None:
    super().__init__(env, options)
    device = env.device
    self.device = device
    self._dtype = torch.float32
    N = env.num_envs

    self._actor = SimToolRealActor(self.checkpoint_path, device=str(device))
    self._state = self._actor.init_state(N)

    arm = self.require_entity(self.entity_name)
    hand = self.require_entity(self.hand_name)
    # Touched, not cached: ``step()`` re-resolves it (deployment hot-swaps entities), but a
    # scene without it must fail here, not one step into the rollout.
    self.require_entity(self.object_name)

    def _idx(values):
        return torch.as_tensor(values, dtype=torch.long, device=device)

    # Resolved at construction so a renamed joint/link raises here, not as a scrambled
    # obs vector on the first step.
    self._arm_dofs_idx = _idx(arm.find_named_dofs_idx_local(list(C.ARM_DOFS), preserve_order=True)[1])
    self._hand_dofs_idx = _idx(hand.find_named_dofs_idx_local(list(C.HAND_DOFS), preserve_order=True)[1])
    self._palm_link_idx = _idx(arm.find_named_links_idx_local([C.PALM_LINK], preserve_order=True)[1])
    self._ft_link_idx = _idx(hand.find_named_links_idx_local(list(C.FINGERTIP_LINKS), preserve_order=True)[1])

    def _t(x):
        return torch.as_tensor(x, dtype=self._dtype, device=device)

    self._q_lower = _t(C.Q_LOWER_LIMITS)
    self._q_upper = _t(C.Q_UPPER_LIMITS)
    self._palm_offset = _t(C.PALM_CENTER_OFFSET)
    self._ft_offset = _t(C.FINGERTIP_OFFSET)  # (3,) same for all 5
    self._kp_corners = _t(C.KEYPOINT_CORNERS)  # (4, 3)
    self._kp_scale = C.OBJECT_BASE_SIZE * C.KEYPOINT_SCALE / 2.0

    # Absolute target buffer (canonical order); prev_action_targets obs.
    self._prev_targets = torch.zeros(N, C.NUM_JOINTS, device=device, dtype=self._dtype)
    self._initialized = False

    # Per-env buffers; override via the setters or a ``goal_pose`` command term.
    self._object_scales = torch.tensor(self.object_scales, device=device, dtype=self._dtype).expand(N, 3).clone()
    self._goal_pos = torch.tensor(C.GOAL_START_POS, device=device, dtype=self._dtype).expand(N, 3).clone()
    self._goal_quat = torch.tensor(C.GOAL_START_QUAT_WXYZ, device=device, dtype=self._dtype).expand(N, 4).clone()

@classmethod
def robot_options(cls) -> KukaSharpa:
    """``KukaSharpa`` at SimToolReal's base placement, fingertips grippier than the palm.

    The composite already defaults to this port's home pose, gains, armature and gravity
    compensation. The fingertip friction reproduces the original's

@classmethod
def scene_entity_options(
    cls, *, object_asset: str | None = None, vis_mode: str = "visual"
) -> dict[str, EntityOptionsLike]:
    """The workspace the policy's observations are defined against: table, tool, goal ghost.

    The observation is object-centric (tool keypoints relative to the palm and the goal),
    so a robot-only scene cannot host this policy. Frictions and placements are
    SimToolReal's; see ``constants``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    object_asset : str | None
        :data:`~eden.options.objects.dextoolbench.DEXTOOLBENCH_REGISTRY` key to spawn.
        ``None`` reads :attr:`object_asset` — the base hook must stay callable with no
        arguments, and restating the literal here could drift from the attribute.
    vis_mode : str
        ``"collision"`` renders collision geometry instead of the visual meshes.
    """
    tool_cls = DEXTOOLBENCH_REGISTRY.get(object_asset or cls.object_asset)
    return {
        "table": BoxOptions(
            size=C.TABLE_SIZE,
            default_root_pos=C.TABLE_POS,
            fixed=True,
            vis_mode=vis_mode,
            material=RigidMaterialOptions(friction=C.TABLE_FRICTION),
        ),
        cls.object_name: tool_cls(
            default_root_pos=C.OBJECT_START_POS,
            default_root_quat=C.OBJECT_START_QUAT_WXYZ,
            vis_mode=vis_mode,
            material=RigidMaterialOptions(friction=C.OBJECT_FRICTION),
        ),
        # Collision-free and not physics-driven: a marker for the goal pose, re-posed each
        # step by whoever moves the goal (the example's sampler; a fixed goal stays put).
        "goal_ghost": tool_cls(
            default_root_pos=C.GOAL_START_POS,
            default_root_quat=C.GOAL_START_QUAT_WXYZ,
            is_fixed_base=True,
            collision=False,
            **dict(GHOST_DEFAULTS),
        ),
    }

def step(self, obs: dict[str, torch.Tensor | dict[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    # Read off the entity, not an observation group: this policy rides along as an extra deploy
    # slot on another policy's or task's env, whose groups are not its own (see the
    # "Declare the observation" section of docs/guides/policy-porting.md).
    del obs  # raw sim state + object/goal pose read directly
    env = self.env
    arm = env.entities[self.entity_name]
    hand = env.entities[self.hand_name]
    obj = env.entities[self.object_name]

    # LOAD-BEARING ``relative=True``: the default solver frame re-origins a rigid body
    # onto its inertial frame, 3-15 cm down these tools' handles. IsaacGym and MuJoCo
    # report the URDF-root pose, so that is what the policy trained on. See
    # docs/guides/entities.md.
    object_pos = obj.get_pos(relative=True)
    object_quat = obj.get_quat(relative=True)

    # Prefer a ``goal_pose`` command term if the task has one, else the ``set_goal`` buffer.
    try:
        goal_cmd = env.command_manager.get_term(self.goal_command)
        self._goal_pos, self._goal_quat = goal_cmd.goal_pos, goal_cmd.goal_quat
    except Exception:
        pass

    # Seed the EMA from where the robot actually is.
    if not self._initialized:
        self._prev_targets = self._read_q(arm, hand)[0].clone()
        self._initialized = True

    obs_vec = self._build_obs(
        arm, hand, object_pos, object_quat, self._goal_pos, self._goal_quat, self._object_scales
    )
    action, self._state = self._actor(obs_vec, self._state)
    targets = self._apply_action(action)
    # Split the canonical 29-vector back out to the two controllers.
    return {
        "dofs_pos_controller": targets[:, : C.NUM_ARM_JOINTS],
        "hand_dofs_pos_controller": targets[:, C.NUM_ARM_JOINTS :],
    }

def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: PolicyOptions):
    super().__init__(env, options)
    if not self.supports_batch and env.num_envs != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} has supports_batch=False and only supports "
            f"num_envs=1 (got {env.num_envs}). Set supports_batch=True on the "
            f"subclass if the remote server accepts batched requests."
        )
    if env.num_envs > 1 and type(self).reset is ClientMixin.reset:
        # The env resets its envs one by one; the default reset can only reset the shared
        # server state of all of them, so it would raise at the first episode end.
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} serves {env.num_envs} envs but keeps ClientMixin.reset, which "
            "refuses a partial reset because the server's episode state is shared by every env. Fix: "
            "override reset(envs_idx) with a per-env scheme (e.g. one server session per env), or "
            "run with num_envs=1."
        )
    self._num_envs: int = env.num_envs
    self._post_configure()
    self._scheduler = ActionChunkScheduler(
        num_envs=env.num_envs,
        mode=self.chunk_mode,
        pred_action_horizon=self.pred_action_horizon,
        exec_horizon=self.exec_horizon,
        short_chunk=self.short_chunk,
        ensemble_steps=self.chunk_temporal_ensemble_steps,
        ensemble_dims=self.chunk_temporal_ensemble_dims,
    )
    self.last_response_info: dict[str, Any] = {}
    self._transport: TransportBase = self.make_transport()
    self._post_connect()

Refuse an observation dict without a group the setup reads, then run the setup's per-step hook.

def observe(self, obs: dict) -> None:
    """Refuse an observation dict without a group the setup reads, then run the setup's per-step hook.

    Construction checks the env publishes every group in ``observation_groups``; this catches a dict the caller
    built by hand (a dropped ``wrist_image``, a renamed group) on the step it arrives, naming the fix.
    """
    missing = [group for group in self._setup.observation_groups if group not in obs]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(
            f"Gr00tPolicy.step() got observation groups {sorted(obs)}, without {missing}, which "
            f"policy_setup={self.policy_setup!r} reads. Fix: pass the dict env.reset() / env.step() return for an "
            f"env built from Gr00tPolicy.observation_options(policy_setup={self.policy_setup!r}). Do not fill a "
            "missing view with a copy of another camera: the checkpoint's schema has a distinct view per key."
        )
    super().observe(obs)

@classmethod
def observation_options(
    cls,
    camera_name: str = "camera",
    wrist_camera_name: str = "wrist_camera",
    secondary_camera_name: str | None = None,
    arm_entity_name: str = "robot",
    arm_dofs_name: list[str] | None = None,
    gripper_entity_name: str | None = None,
    gripper_dof_name: str = "left_driver_joint",
    gripper_close_pos: float = 0.8,
) -> dict[str, ObservationGroupOptions]:
    """Wire the DROID joint-state proprio + exterior/wrist camera groups.

    Mirrors OpenPI's ``droid_jointpos`` observation contract: an 8-D
    ``proprio`` vector ``[joint_pos(7), gripper(1)]`` plus an ``image``
    (exterior) and ``wrist_image`` group.  When ``secondary_camera_name``
    is given, an ``image_2`` group carries the second exterior view; pass
    the same value to ``Cosmos3Policy.configure()`` (the policy checks the
    two agree when it is constructed).
    """
    from eden.managers.terms.observations.camera import rgb_image
    from eden.options.managers.observations import ObservationGroupOptions
    from eden.terms import ObsTerm

    if arm_dofs_name is None:
        arm_dofs_name = list(DROID_ARM_DOFS)

    groups = make_image_groups(camera_name, use_wrist_image=True, wrist_camera_name=wrist_camera_name)
    if secondary_camera_name is not None:
        groups["image_2"] = ObservationGroupOptions(
            rgb=ObsTerm.configure(func=rgb_image, params={"camera_name": secondary_camera_name}),
        )

    groups["proprio"] = make_droid_joint_state_group(
        arm_entity_name,
        arm_dofs_name,
        gripper_entity_name=gripper_entity_name,
        gripper_dof_name=gripper_dof_name,
        gripper_close_pos=gripper_close_pos,
    )
    return groups

def pack_observations(self, obs: dict) -> dict:
    """Convert Eden obs tensors to the Cosmos3 RoboLab server payload dict."""
    if self.task_description is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "Cosmos3Policy sends 'prompt' with every request, but Cosmos3Policy.task_description is None. Fix: "
            "policy.set_task('<instruction>') before the first step, or "
            "Cosmos3Policy.configure(task_description='<instruction>'). Do not fill in a generic instruction: "
            "the checkpoint is language-conditioned and acts on whatever it is told."
        )
    proprio = to_numpy_unbatched(obs["proprio"])
    joint_pos = proprio[:7].astype(np.float32)
    gripper_closedness = proprio[7:8].astype(np.float32)

    payload: dict = {
        "prompt": self.task_description,
        "observation/joint_position": joint_pos,
        "observation/gripper_position": gripper_closedness,
    }

    # RoboArena concat view: wrist (top) + two exterior views (bottom), composed by the
    # server. The groups were checked against this policy at construction.
    exterior_img = prepare_image_padded(obs["image"], self.image_size)
    if self.secondary_camera_name is not None:
        exterior2_img = prepare_image_padded(obs["image_2"], self.image_size)
    else:  # duplicate_exterior_view=True
        exterior2_img = exterior_img
    payload["observation/wrist_image_left"] = prepare_image_padded(obs["wrist_image"], self.image_size)
    payload["observation/exterior_image_1_left"] = exterior_img
    payload["observation/exterior_image_2_left"] = exterior2_img

    return payload

    already re-applies its ``1 - x`` transform, so the scalar is closedness
    (``> 0.5`` ⇒ CLOSE). Delegated to ``JointPositionAdapter``.
    """
    return self._adapter(np.asarray(raw_action, dtype=np.float32).reshape(-1), env=self.env)

def pack_observations(
    self,
    obs: dict[str, torch.Tensor | dict[str, torch.Tensor]],
) -> dict:
    if self.task_description is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "MolmoAct2Policy sends 'instruction' with every request, but MolmoAct2Policy.task_description is "
            "None. Fix: policy.set_task('<instruction>') before the first step, or "
            "MolmoAct2Policy.configure(task_description='<instruction>'). Do not fill in a generic "
            "instruction: the checkpoint is language-conditioned and acts on whatever it is told."
        )
    missing = [group for group in ("image", "proprio") if group not in obs]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(
            f"MolmoAct2Policy reads the observation groups ['image', 'proprio'], but obs has no {missing} (its "
            f"groups are {sorted(obs)}). Fix: pass the observations of an env built from "
            "MolmoAct2Policy.observation_options(...) as they are. Do not fill a missing group with zeros: the "
            "server would act on a blank view or a zero joint state."
        )
    image_group = obs["image"]
    if not isinstance(image_group, dict):
        raise TypeError(
            f"MolmoAct2Policy expects obs['image'] to be a dict with 'external' and 'wrist' keys, but it is a "
            f"{type(image_group).__name__}. Fix: build the env's 'image' group from "
            "MolmoAct2Policy.observation_options(...), which keeps the two cameras apart (concatenate_terms=False)."
        )
    if "external" not in image_group or "wrist" not in image_group:
        raise KeyError(
            "MolmoAct2Policy sends obs['image']['external'] and obs['image']['wrist'] as its two views, but "
            f"obs['image'] holds {sorted(image_group)}. Fix: build the env's 'image' group from "
            "MolmoAct2Policy.observation_options(external_camera=..., wrist_camera=...), which names the env's "
            "cameras. Do not send one camera as both views: the checkpoint was trained on two."
        )

    proprio = to_numpy_unbatched(obs["proprio"]).astype(np.float32)
    if proprio.shape != (8,):
        raise ValueError(f"MolmoAct2 expects 8-D proprio [q1..q7, gripper], got {proprio.shape}.")

    payload = {
        "external_cam": to_uint8_hwc(image_group["external"]),
        "wrist_cam": to_uint8_hwc(image_group["wrist"]),
        "instruction": self.task_description,
        "state": proprio,
        "num_steps": int(self.num_steps),
    }
    if self.enable_cuda_graph:
        payload["enable_cuda_graph"] = True
    return payload

Every row of the reply is scanned, including any past the 15 that execute: a non-finite value anywhere means the server's output is broken, so the rows before it are not trusted either.

def accept_chunk(self, chunk: np.ndarray) -> None:
    """Refuse a chunk with any non-finite arm target before its first row executes, then queue it.

    Every row of the reply is scanned, including any past the 15 that execute: a non-finite value anywhere
    means the server's output is broken, so the rows before it are not trusted either.
    """
    chunk = self._normalize_action_shape(np.asarray(chunk, dtype=np.float32))
    self._check_action_width(chunk, self.action_dim, schema=type(self).__name__)
    # Arm columns only, on the whole (num_envs, T, 8) chunk: a NaN gripper alone holds the gripper.
    bad = ~np.isfinite(chunk[:, :, :7]).all(axis=2)
    if bad.any():
        env_idx, row_idx = (int(i) for i in np.argwhere(bad)[0])
        raise ValueError(
            f"MolmoAct2 server returned non-finite arm joint targets for env {env_idx} in row {row_idx} of its "
            f"{chunk.shape[1]}-row chunk: {[round(float(v), 6) for v in chunk[env_idx, row_idx]]} ([q1..q7, "
            f"gripper], rad). The whole chunk is refused before any row reaches the arm term {_ARM_TERM!r} "
            "(control_dofs_pos). Fix: check the served checkpoint and its norm_stats.json (franka_droid) on the "
            "server; a NaN gripper alone is allowed (it holds the gripper). Do not replace the bad values with "
            "the current or a default pose, or execute the rows before it: the whole chunk was predicted from "
            "the same broken output."
        )
    super().accept_chunk(chunk)

Decode an (num_envs, 8) MolmoAct2-DROID action row.

raw_action[:, :7] are absolute Franka joint targets in rad and are passed straight through to the arm ImplicitPDController (scale=1). raw_action[:, 7] is gripper closedness in [0, 1] (0=open, 1=closed), forwarded raw to the env's GripperDecisionController, which binarizes it at gripper_threshold (or follows it with binarize_gripper=False).

Stores self.last_diagnostics with the raw gripper scalar, threshold, and the intent the env's gripper term derives from it, so callers can record/plot gripper traces.

Source code in eden/extensions/policies/molmoact2/policy.py 
def unpack_actions(self, raw_action: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    """Decode an ``(num_envs, 8)`` MolmoAct2-DROID action row.

    ``raw_action[:, :7]`` are absolute Franka joint targets in rad and are
    passed straight through to the arm ``ImplicitPDController`` (scale=1).
    ``raw_action[:, 7]`` is gripper **closedness in ``[0, 1]``** (0=open,
    1=closed), forwarded raw to the env's ``GripperDecisionController``, which
    binarizes it at ``gripper_threshold`` (or follows it with ``binarize_gripper=False``).

    Stores ``self.last_diagnostics`` with the raw gripper scalar, threshold, and the intent
    the env's gripper term derives from it, so callers can record/plot gripper traces.
    """
    device = self.env.device
    arm = torch.as_tensor(raw_action[:, :7], dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    # The raw closedness goes to the env's GripperDecisionController, configured by
    # action_options() with the same flip / threshold / binarize semantics.
    gripper = torch.as_tensor(raw_action[:, 7:8], dtype=torch.float32, device=device)

    raw_g = float(raw_action[0, 7])
    self.last_diagnostics = {
        "raw_gripper_action": raw_g,
        "gripper_threshold": float(self.gripper_threshold),
        "gripper_intent": self._gripper_intent(raw_g),
        "gripper_command": raw_g,
        "binarize_gripper": bool(self.binarize_gripper),
        "flip_gripper": bool(self.flip_gripper),
    }
    return {_ARM_TERM: arm, "gripper_controller": gripper}

docs.text:
decode_response(response: dict) -> ndarray

Flatten Octo's two-dict reply into one (1, 1, 7) action row.

Uses raw_action["world_vector"] + raw_action["rotation_delta"] as the 6-D EE delta. RobotArena's Genesis default_test.py also uses the raw Euler rotation_delta for its target-pose transform, while action["gripper"] carries the processed WidowX open/close convention. The processed action["world_vector"] / action["rot_axangle"] are not a substitute: the server scales both by its action_scale, and rot_axangle is axis-angle.

Source code in eden/extensions/policies/octo/policy.py 
def decode_response(self, response: dict) -> np.ndarray:
    """Flatten Octo's two-dict reply into one ``(1, 1, 7)`` action row.

    Uses raw_action["world_vector"] + raw_action["rotation_delta"] as the
    6-D EE delta. RobotArena's Genesis default_test.py also uses the raw
    Euler rotation_delta for its target-pose transform, while action["gripper"]
    carries the processed WidowX open/close convention. The processed
    action["world_vector"] / action["rot_axangle"] are not a substitute: the
    server scales both by its action_scale, and rot_axangle is axis-angle.
    """
    try:
        raw_action = response["raw_action"]
        action = response["action"]
        world_vector = raw_action["world_vector"]
        rotation_delta = raw_action["rotation_delta"]
        gripper = action["gripper"]
    except (KeyError, TypeError) as e:
        if isinstance(response, dict):
            got = {k: list(v) if isinstance(v, dict) else type(v).__name__ for k, v in response.items()}
        else:
            got = type(response).__name__
        raise KeyError(
            "Octo reply must carry raw_action{world_vector, rotation_delta} and action{gripper}, as "
            f"RobotArena's server_octo.py /act sends them; got {got}. Do not fall back to "
            "action['world_vector'] / action['rot_axangle']: the server scales both by its action_scale "
            "and rot_axangle is axis-angle, not the raw Euler rotation_delta this client converts."
        ) from e

    flat_action = np.concatenate(
        [
            np.asarray(world_vector, dtype=np.float32).reshape(-1),  # (3,) translation delta
            np.asarray(rotation_delta, dtype=np.float32).reshape(-1),  # (3,) Euler rotation delta
            np.asarray(gripper, dtype=np.float32).reshape(-1)[:1],  # (1,) binarized +1=open/-1=close
        ]
    )  # (7,)
    if flat_action.shape != (7,):
        raise ValueError(f"Expected Octo action shape (7,), got {flat_action.shape}: {flat_action}")
    return self._normalize_action_shape(flat_action)

PoseEstimatorBase(options: T)

Bases: ConfigurableMixin[PoseEstimatorOptions]

Abstract base class for recovering human motion from video.

Takes no env, unlike the retargeting and grasp-sampling bases: estimation is offline preprocessing whose output is a motion clip, and the robot only enters at retargeting.

Backends expose the estimate at two levels — :meth:estimate keeps the backend's own frames and layout (so camera-space work and provenance survive), :meth:estimate_clip packs it into the AMASS-style Z-up SMPL clip the retargeting extensions consume.

No registry, as in retargeting: backends are chosen by CLI subcommand, never resolved by name from a config.

def __init__(self, options: T) -> None:
    self._uid = gs.UID()
    self._options: T = options

    mirror_options_onto(self, self._options)

    # Deferred, not module-scope — see the NOTE above this module's imports.
    from eden.options._metadata import OPTION_METADATA_KEYS

    # check if there are unused parameters in the options. ``_extra_option_params`` are legitimate
    # options-only fields (not mirrored as attrs), so they are expected to be "unused" here.
    unused_params = set(self._options.keys()) - set(self.get_parameter_names())
    tolerated = {"name", "class_name"} | set(OPTION_METADATA_KEYS) | self._extra_option_params
    # ``params`` is a declared framework field on function-capable term options. An *empty* one is
    # legitimately unused when the same options class configures a class-based term; a non-empty
    # ``params`` on a class-based term would be silently ignored, so it stays invalid.
    if not getattr(self._options, "params", None):
        tolerated.add("params")
    invalid_params = unused_params - tolerated
    if invalid_params:
        # Name the term, not only the class: for a function term the class is the shared
        # ``*FuncWrapper``, which cannot tell the author which of a dozen terms is wrong.
        # Same wording as the construction-time check (``ManagerTermOptions._validate_param_names``).
        term_name = getattr(self._options, "name", None)
        subject = f"term '{term_name}' ({type(self).__name__})" if term_name else type(self).__name__
        raise ValueError(
            invalid_parameters_message(subject, invalid_params, self.get_configure_specs(), self._retired_params)
        )

docs.title: GVHMR
docs.text:
Eden wrapper around GVHMR (world-grounded human motion recovery from monocular video).

GVHMR (zju3dv/GVHMR <https://github.com/zju3dv/GVHMR>, SIGGRAPH Asia 2024) is consumed through the packaged fork Kashu7100/eden_gvhmr <https://github.com/Kashu7100/eden_gvhmr> (import name hmr4d). :meth:GvhmrEstimator.estimate_clip writes what eden retarget soma --body-model smplx reads, so video → clip → robot qpos is two steps. See docs/guides/pose-estimation.md for setup.

In-process. The fork installs beside Eden: it drops upstream's pytorch3d requirement for inference, relaxes a stale numpy<1.24 cap, does not compose Hydra configs (so it does not fight a host that owns Hydra's global state), and carries no VCS dependency, so it ships on PyPI. pip install 'eden-world[pose]' resolves additively into Eden's environment and this class simply imports hmr4d.

One consequence worth knowing: GVHMR runs on Eden's video decoder and person detector rather than the versions its numerics were tuned against. Measured one change at a time on the bundled tennis clip, av 13 → 17 moves body joints by 3.6° max and ultralytics 8.2.42 → 8.4.113 moves the detected boxes by 8.5 px and body joints by 3.4°; numpy (including the 1.x/2.x jump), timm and imageio are all bit-identical. The estimate stays valid — it is just not bit-comparable with the published checkpoint's reference stack.

docs.text:
GvhmrEstimator(options: PoseEstimatorOptions)

Bases: PoseEstimatorBase

Monocular video → world-grounded SMPL-X motion.

The shared options (checkpoint_root, ckpt_path, output_root, motion_fps, verbose) are documented on :class:~eden.options.extensions.pose_estimation.PoseEstimatorOptions; the fields below are GVHMR's own and reach the options as extras.

The model is loaded once, on the first :meth:estimate call, and reused across videos. GVHMR is CUDA-only; select a GPU with CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES.

No overlay rendering. GVHMR can draw in-camera / world overlay videos, but that path needs two dependencies inference does not — pytorch3d (built against your torch/CUDA) and chumpy from git — neither of which can be declared, so the pose extra does not install them. Rather than offer a flag that fails after the whole pipeline has run, Eden does not expose rendering at all: the product here is the .npz. To eyeball an estimate, install those two and use GVHMR's own CLI (python -m hmr4d.demo). verbose still works — its bbox / keypoint overlays are drawn with cv2 and need nothing extra.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION static_cam

Skip visual odometry (assume the camera does not move). Much faster, and the right choice for tripod footage; wrong for handheld video, where camera motion would be absorbed into the body motion.

TYPE: bool

use_dpvo

Use DPVO instead of the default SimpleVO for camera motion. Requires GVHMR's dpvo extra and its checkpoint.

def __init__(self, options: PoseEstimatorOptions) -> None:
    # Set before anything that can raise, so close() is safe even on a failed construction.
    self._model = None
    self._skeleton_model = None
    super().__init__(options)
    if abs(self.motion_fps - _ASSUMED_VIDEO_FPS) > _FPS_TOLERANCE:
        raise ValueError(
            f"motion_fps={self.motion_fps:g} but GVHMR always expresses its output at "
            f"{_ASSUMED_VIDEO_FPS:g} fps — it relabels every input to that rate and integrates root motion "
            f"at it. Stamping any other rate mislabels the clip without changing the motion, which is worse "
            f"than the default. Re-encode the source video instead if you need a different rate."

docs.text:
estimate(video: str | Path, **overrides) -> dict

Recover the motion in video, verbatim in GVHMR's own frames.

**overrides take any of :data:_RECOVER_KEYS for this call only.

RETURNS DESCRIPTION dict

global — SMPL-X params in GVHMR's gravity-aligned Y-up world (global_orient (T, 3), body_pose (T, 63), betas (T, 10), transl (T, 3)); incam — the same in the camera frame; pelvis_j0 (T, 3); K_fullimg; output_dir; video_fps (the source rate). :meth:estimate_clip returns the Z-up, AMASS-style form Eden reads.

Source code in eden/extensions/pose_estimation/gvhmr/estimator.py 
def estimate(self, video: str | Path, **overrides) -> dict:
    """Recover the motion in ``video``, verbatim in GVHMR's own frames.

    ``**overrides`` take any of :data:`_RECOVER_KEYS` for this call only.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        ``global`` — SMPL-X params in GVHMR's gravity-aligned **Y-up** world
        (``global_orient (T, 3)``, ``body_pose (T, 63)``, ``betas (T, 10)``,
        ``transl (T, 3)``); ``incam`` — the same in the camera frame; ``pelvis_j0
        (T, 3)``; ``K_fullimg``; ``output_dir``; ``video_fps`` (the source rate).
        :meth:`estimate_clip` returns the Z-up, AMASS-style form Eden reads.
    """
    path = Path(video).expanduser()
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Video does not exist: {path}")
    unknown = set(overrides) - set(_RECOVER_KEYS)
    if unknown:
        raise TypeError(f"Unknown estimate() override(s) {sorted(unknown)}; expected {list(_RECOVER_KEYS)}.")

    kwargs = {key: getattr(self, key) for key in _RECOVER_KEYS}
    kwargs.update(overrides)
    kwargs["output_root"] = kwargs["output_root"] or None  # GVHMR keys its defaults on None

    video_path = str(path.resolve())
    with _checkpoint_root_env(self.checkpoint_root):
        # Load first: a missing backend must surface as _require_hmr4d's actionable
        # ImportError, not as `av` failing to import inside _video_fps.
        model = self._ensure_model()

        # Vet the source rate up front. Warning only after `recover()` would mean spending the
        # whole pipeline before telling the caller the clip they get is time-warped.
        fps = _video_fps(video_path)
        if fps is not None and abs(fps - _ASSUMED_VIDEO_FPS) > _FPS_TOLERANCE:
            en.logger.warning(
                f"{path.name} is {fps:g} fps, but GVHMR relabels every input to {_ASSUMED_VIDEO_FPS:g} fps "
                f"without resampling and integrates root motion at that rate — the recovered trajectory is "
                f"time-warped by {fps / _ASSUMED_VIDEO_FPS:.2f}x. Re-encode the video to "
                f"{_ASSUMED_VIDEO_FPS:g} fps for a physically correct clip."
            )

        out = model.recover(video_path, **kwargs)
        pelvis_j0 = self._pelvis_rest_offset(out["smpl_params_global"]["betas"])

    # Plain numpy on the way out: the caller should not have to care that GVHMR returns
    # CUDA tensors, and `convert` takes numpy so a saved clip stays framework-agnostic.
    return {
        "global": {key: _to_numpy(value) for key, value in out["smpl_params_global"].items()},
        "incam": {key: _to_numpy(value) for key, value in out["smpl_params_incam"].items()},
        "pelvis_j0": pelvis_j0,
        "K_fullimg": _to_numpy(out["K_fullimg"]),
        "output_dir": str(out["output_dir"]),
        "video_fps": fps,
    }

docs.title: Conversion to an AMASS-style clip
docs.text:
GVHMR's world-frame output is Y-up; these helpers rotate it to Eden's Z-up and write an AMASS-style SMPL-X .npz.

GVHMR's world-frame SMPL-X output → an AMASS-style, Z-up SMPL-X clip.

Two things change. Up axis: GVHMR predicts in a gravity-aligned frame whose +Y is up (its "ay" frame — hmr4d.utils.geo.hmr_global's "az"->"ay" is -90° about X), while Eden/Genesis/AMASS are Z-up. Pose layout: GVHMR returns global_orient (T, 3) + body_pose (T, 63); AMASS packs one poses (T, 165), whose jaw/eyes/hands tail stays zero because GVHMR does not estimate it.

Does not import GVHMR, so the conversion is testable without the backend installed.

docs.title: y_up_to_z_up_root
docs.text:
y_up_to_z_up_root(global_orient: ndarray, transl: ndarray, pelvis_j0: ndarray) -> tuple[ndarray, ndarray]

Rotate an SMPL-X root (global_orient, transl) pair from Y-up into Z-up.

body_pose is unaffected — SMPL joint rotations are parent-relative, so only the root sees a change of world frame.

The translation is not simply R @ transl: SMPL-X rotates the body about the rest-pose pelvis J0(betas) (BodyModelSMPLX.get_skeleton(betas)[..., 0, :]), which puts the pelvis at J0 + transl in the world, so rotating about the origin needs::

transl' = R @ (transl + J0) - J0

global_orient / transl are (T, 3), pelvis_j0 (T, 3) or (3,); returns the Z-up pair as float32.

Source code in eden/extensions/pose_estimation/gvhmr/convert.py 
def y_up_to_z_up_root(
    global_orient: np.ndarray, transl: np.ndarray, pelvis_j0: np.ndarray
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Rotate an SMPL-X root ``(global_orient, transl)`` pair from Y-up into Z-up.

    ``body_pose`` is unaffected — SMPL joint rotations are parent-relative, so only the root
    sees a change of world frame.

    The translation is **not** simply ``R @ transl``: SMPL-X rotates the body about the
    rest-pose pelvis ``J0(betas)`` (``BodyModelSMPLX.get_skeleton(betas)[..., 0, :]``), which
    puts the pelvis at ``J0 + transl`` in the world, so rotating about the origin needs::

        transl' = R @ (transl + J0) - J0

    ``global_orient`` / ``transl`` are ``(T, 3)``, ``pelvis_j0`` ``(T, 3)`` or ``(3,)``;
    returns the Z-up pair as float32.
    """
    orient = torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(global_orient), dtype=torch.float32)
    trans = torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(transl), dtype=torch.float32)
    if orient.ndim != 2 or orient.shape[-1] != 3 or trans.shape != orient.shape:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Expected per-frame (T, 3) arrays; got global_orient {tuple(orient.shape)}, transl {tuple(trans.shape)}."
        )
    j0 = torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(pelvis_j0), dtype=torch.float32).expand_as(trans)
    quat = y_up_to_z_up_quat()

    orient_z = axis_angle_from_quat(quat_mul(quat, quat_from_axis_angle(orient)))
    trans_z = transform_by_quat(trans + j0, quat) - j0
    return orient_z.numpy(), trans_z.numpy()

docs.title: to_amass_smplx_clip
docs.text:
to_amass_smplx_clip(result: dict, *, motion_fps: float, source_video: str | Path | None = None) -> dict[str, ndarray]

Pack one :meth:GvhmrEstimator.estimate result into AMASS-style SMPL-X npz fields.

Emits the AMASS fields Eden's retargeting path reads (poses, trans, betas, gender, mocap_frame_rate, surface_model_type) plus gvhmr_* copies of the raw Y-up estimate, so a saved clip stays traceable to what the model predicted.

betas is averaged over the clip — AMASS carries one shape vector per sequence, and GVHMR's per-frame betas are already a clip-average repeated per frame.

Source code in eden/extensions/pose_estimation/gvhmr/convert.py 
def to_amass_smplx_clip(
    result: dict, *, motion_fps: float, source_video: str | Path | None = None
) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Pack one :meth:`GvhmrEstimator.estimate` result into AMASS-style SMPL-X npz fields.

    Emits the AMASS fields Eden's retargeting path reads (``poses``, ``trans``, ``betas``,
    ``gender``, ``mocap_frame_rate``, ``surface_model_type``) plus ``gvhmr_*`` copies of the
    raw Y-up estimate, so a saved clip stays traceable to what the model predicted.

    ``betas`` is averaged over the clip — AMASS carries one shape vector per sequence, and
    GVHMR's per-frame betas are already a clip-average repeated per frame.
    """
    _require_keys(result, ("global", "pelvis_j0", "K_fullimg"), "GVHMR result")
    g = result["global"]
    _require_keys(g, ("global_orient", "body_pose", "betas", "transl"), "GVHMR result['global']")

    orient, body_pose, betas, transl = g["global_orient"], g["body_pose"], g["betas"], g["transl"]
    pelvis_j0 = result["pelvis_j0"]
    num_frames = orient.shape[0]
    for name, (array, shape) in {
        "global_orient": (orient, (num_frames, 3)),
        "body_pose": (body_pose, (num_frames, 63)),
        "betas": (betas, (num_frames, 10)),
        "transl": (transl, (num_frames, 3)),
        "pelvis_j0": (pelvis_j0, (num_frames, 3)),
    }.items():
        if array.shape != shape:
            raise ValueError(f"GVHMR result field {name!r} has shape {array.shape}, expected {shape}.")

    orient_z, trans_z = y_up_to_z_up_root(orient, transl, pelvis_j0)
    poses = np.zeros((num_frames, SMPLX_POSE_DIM), dtype=np.float32)
    poses[:, ROOT_ORIENT_SLICE] = orient_z
    poses[:, BODY_POSE_SLICE] = body_pose

    payload = {
        "poses": poses,
        "trans": trans_z,
        "betas": betas.mean(axis=0).astype(np.float32),
        "gender": np.array("neutral"),  # GVHMR predicts with the SMPL-X *neutral* model
        "mocap_frame_rate": np.float32(motion_fps),
        "surface_model_type": np.array("smplx"),
        "gvhmr_global_orient": orient,
        "gvhmr_transl": transl,
        "gvhmr_betas": betas,
        "gvhmr_pelvis_j0": pelvis_j0,
        "gvhmr_K_fullimg": result["K_fullimg"],
    }
    if result.get("video_fps") is not None:
        payload["gvhmr_video_fps"] = np.float32(result["video_fps"])
    if source_video is not None:
        payload["source_video"] = np.array(str(source_video))
    return payload

Retargeting maps motion captured on one morphology (human keypoints, SMPL-family bodies, MANO hands, interaction meshes) onto an Eden robot. The four solvers are RetargetingBase subclasses configured by a RetargeterOptions, and the FlashDexRetarget pipeline is a set of functions with its own options; each imports its backend lazily. docs.title: DexRetargeter
docs.text:
Eden RetargetingBase wrapper around the dex-retargeting port.

Combines one of three SLSQP optimizers (position / vector / dexpilot) with the upstream SeqRetargeting semantics (mean-of-limits warm start, output low-pass filter) into a single DexRetargeter entity-extension.

Typical usage:

.. code-block:: python

retargeter = DexRetargeter(
    env=env,
    options=DexRetargeter.configure(
        entity_name="robot",
        type="vector",
        target_origin_link_names=["wrist", "wrist", "wrist", "wrist"],
        target_task_link_names=["index_tip", "middle_tip", "ring_tip", "pinky_tip"],
        target_link_human_indices=np.array([[0, 0, 0, 0], [8, 12, 16, 20]]),
        scaling_factor=1.6,
    ),
)
qpos = retargeter.retarget(ref_value)              # one frame
qpos_seq = retargeter.retarget_motion(ref_seq)     # batch

SLSQP-based retargeting optimizers, Genesis-backed.

Ported from dex_retargeting.optimizer (AnyTeleop / DexPilot). The algorithm — Huber loss over keypoint positions or relative vectors, optimized with nlopt's SLSQP and analytic gradients built from positional Jacobians — is unchanged. Only the kinematics layer differs:

  • Forward kinematics is performed by calling entity.set_qpos(qpos).
  • Jacobians come from entity.get_jacobian(link) and are already in world frame (Genesis returns the spatial Jacobian), so the upstream link_rot @ body_jacobian step is dropped.
  • Column ordering follows entity.dofs_name (Eden reorders internally).

Free-joint detection and the MimicJointKinematicAdaptor from upstream are intentionally omitted; we expect hands with no base DOFs (fixed-base or welded onto an arm) with mimic constraints already baked into the URDF.

Bundled robot + retargeter presets for dex-retargeting.

Single source of truth shared by the eden retarget dex CLI and the examples/recipes/retargeting/dex_retargeter scripts. Each :class:HandPreset pairs a RobotOptions factory with a RetargeterOptions factory. The RetargeterOptions factories import DexRetargeter lazily (it pulls nlopt), so importing this module for :data:POSITION_PRESET_NAMES — used to build the CLI's --preset choices — stays free of the dex-retargeter extra.

Fingertip link names and MANO keypoint indices are read off the robot's MetadataOptions (target_hand_links / mano_hand_idx), so adding a hand only needs a new entry in :data:HAND_PRESETS.

URDF↔MANO frame alignment, derived from Eden's up / front fields.

A hand URDF's up and front declarations encode the same kind of "asset-frame → world-reference" rotation that :func:eden.utils.geom.align_up_and_front already produces for any Eden entity. For hand robots the convention is:

  • up = the URDF axis along which the fingers extend
  • front = the URDF axis along which the palm normal points (= the URDF axis that aligns with world +X after load)

Eden's defaults (up=(0,0,1), front=(1,0,0)) already match XHand1_R's URDF (fingers along URDF +Z, palm normal along URDF +X), so XHand1_R loads identity. MANO's right-hand canonical frame is the matching declaration in MANO-local axes:

  • fingers (= up) along -X in MANO local
  • palm normal (= front) along -Y in MANO local

Applying align_up_and_front twice (once for the robot, once for MANO) gives a URDF → canonical-world → MANO chain that the retargeter can compose into a single rotation — no per-robot urdf_to_mano_quat metadata needed.

This module exposes :func:urdf_to_mano_rot, which returns:

  • R_mano_to_world — used to rotate MANO-local keypoints into the retargeting (= canonical world) frame so the optimizer's targets line up with the robot's actually-loaded fingertip workspace.
  • q_urdf_to_mano — composed onto the per-frame MANO wrist quat to get the floating-base base_quat_w that places the robot at the right world orientation for the saved dofs_pos to reproduce MANO fingertips at viz time.

Constants for the dex-retargeting port.

Mirrors dex_retargeting.constants but trimmed to what the Eden port actually consumes. Robot-name enums upstream are tied to YAML config files shipped with the package; in Eden we plug in any RigidEntity directly, so those enums are not needed.

Helpers for the dex-retargeting port (e.g. low-pass filter).

def __init__(self, env: "EnvBase", options: RetargeterOptions) -> None:
    super().__init__(env, options)

    self.optimizer: Optimizer = self._build_optimizer()

    # Joint-limit bounds for the target DOFs. Either pull them from the
    # entity (and forward to nlopt) or use a wide band that effectively
    # disables the constraint.
    if self.has_joint_limits:
        # entity.get_dofs_limit() returns (lower, upper), each (n_envs, n_dofs).
        # Take env 0 and stack to (n_dofs, 2).
        entity_limits = torch.stack(self.entity.get_dofs_limit(), dim=-1)[0].cpu().numpy()
        self.joint_limits = entity_limits[self.optimizer.idx_target]
        self.optimizer.set_joint_limit(self.joint_limits)
    else:
        self.joint_limits = np.tile([-1e4, 1e4], (self.optimizer.opt_dof, 1)).astype(np.float64)

    self.last_qpos = self.joint_limits.mean(axis=1).astype(np.float32)

    self.filter: Optional[LPFilter] = LPFilter(self.low_pass_alpha) if 0 <= self.low_pass_alpha <= 1 else None

Retarget one frame and return a full-DOF qpos (in dofs_name order).

ref_value is the optimizer-specific Cartesian reference: positions (n, 3) for position; vectors (n, 3) for vector and dexpilot. fixed_qpos holds the non-target joints (optimizer.idx_fixed order; zeros when None).

Source code in eden/extensions/retargeting/dex_retargeter/retargeter.py 
def retarget(
    self,
    ref_value: np.ndarray,
    fixed_qpos: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Retarget one frame and return a full-DOF qpos (in ``dofs_name`` order).

    ``ref_value`` is the optimizer-specific Cartesian reference: positions
    ``(n, 3)`` for ``position``; vectors ``(n, 3)`` for ``vector`` and
    ``dexpilot``. ``fixed_qpos`` holds the non-target joints (``optimizer.idx_fixed`` order;
    zeros when ``None``).
    """
    if fixed_qpos is None:
        fixed_qpos = np.zeros(len(self.optimizer.idx_fixed), dtype=np.float32)

    qpos = self.optimizer.retarget(
        ref_value=np.asarray(ref_value, dtype=np.float32),
        fixed_qpos=np.asarray(fixed_qpos, dtype=np.float32),
        last_qpos=np.clip(self.last_qpos, self.joint_limits[:, 0], self.joint_limits[:, 1]),
    )
    self.last_qpos = qpos

    robot_qpos = np.zeros(self.optimizer.num_joints, dtype=np.float32)
    robot_qpos[self.optimizer.idx_fixed] = fixed_qpos
    robot_qpos[self.optimizer.idx_target] = qpos

    if self.filter is not None:
        robot_qpos = self.filter.next(robot_qpos)
    return robot_qpos

def retarget_motion(
    self,
    ref_sequence: np.ndarray,
    fixed_qpos_sequence: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Retarget a whole trajectory.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ref_sequence : np.ndarray
        ``(T, ...)`` — per-frame ``ref_value`` arrays.
    fixed_qpos_sequence : np.ndarray, optional
        ``(T, len(idx_fixed))`` if any joints are held fixed; otherwise
        ``None``.

    Returns
    -------
    qpos : np.ndarray, shape ``(T, n_dofs)``
        Full-DOF qpos per frame in ``entity.dofs_name`` order.
    """
    return np.stack(
        [
            self.retarget(
                ref_sequence[t],
                fixed_qpos=fixed_qpos_sequence[t] if fixed_qpos_sequence is not None else None,
            )
            for t in range(len(ref_sequence))
        ]
    )

@staticmethod
def extract_ref_value(
    joint_pos: np.ndarray,
    target_link_human_indices: np.ndarray,
    retargeting_type: str,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Build the optimizer's ``ref_value`` from a 21-keypoint MANO array.

    Same logic as upstream's ``detect_from_video.py`` snippet so existing
    MediaPipe pipelines drop in cleanly.
    """
    if retargeting_type == "POSITION":
        return joint_pos[target_link_human_indices, :]
    origin = target_link_human_indices[0, :]
    task = target_link_human_indices[1, :]
    return joint_pos[task, :] - joint_pos[origin, :]

def __init__(
    self,
    entity: "RigidEntity",
    target_joint_names: List[str],
    target_link_human_indices: Optional[np.ndarray],
) -> None:
    # The requirement is that the optimised qpos carries no base DOFs — true for a fixed
    # base and equally for a hand welded onto an arm (``attach`` removes its root joint),
    # so welded dexterous hands are supported here.
    if not entity.has_immobile_base:
        raise ValueError(
            "DexRetargeter optimizers require an entity with no base DOFs (fixed-base, or "
            "welded onto another entity). Floating-hand retargeting (upstream's "
            "`add_dummy_free_joint`) is not yet supported."
        )
    self.entity = entity
    self.device = entity.device
    self.dofs_name: list[str] = list(entity.dofs_name)
    self.num_joints: int = len(self.dofs_name)

    idx_target: list[int] = []
    for name in target_joint_names:
        if name not in self.dofs_name:
            raise ValueError(f"Joint {name!r} not in entity.dofs_name. Available: {self.dofs_name}")
        idx_target.append(self.dofs_name.index(name))
    target_set = set(idx_target)
    self.target_joint_names = target_joint_names
    self.idx_target = np.array(idx_target, dtype=int)
    self.idx_fixed = np.array([i for i in range(self.num_joints) if i not in target_set], dtype=int)

    self.opt = nlopt.opt(nlopt.LD_SLSQP, len(idx_target))
    self.opt_dof = len(idx_target)

    self.target_link_human_indices = target_link_human_indices

def retarget(
    self,
    ref_value: np.ndarray,
    fixed_qpos: np.ndarray,
    last_qpos: np.ndarray,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Run one SLSQP solve and return the optimized target-joint qpos.

    Parameters
    ----------
    ref_value
        Optimizer-specific Cartesian reference (positions or vectors).
    fixed_qpos
        Values for joints NOT in ``target_joint_names``, ordered to match
        ``self.idx_fixed`` (i.e. ``entity.dofs_name`` filtered by that index).
    last_qpos
        Initial guess and regularization target for this frame.
    """
    if len(fixed_qpos) != len(self.idx_fixed):
        raise ValueError(f"Optimizer expects {len(self.idx_fixed)} fixed joints, got {len(fixed_qpos)}.")
    objective_fn = self.get_objective_function(
        ref_value,
        fixed_qpos,
        np.asarray(last_qpos, dtype=np.float32),
    )
    self.opt.set_min_objective(objective_fn)
    try:
        qpos = self.opt.optimize(last_qpos)
        return np.asarray(qpos, dtype=np.float32)
    except RuntimeError as e:  # nlopt raises this on solver failure
        en.logger.warning(f"nlopt solver failure: {e}")
        return np.asarray(last_qpos, dtype=np.float32)

Source code in eden/extensions/retargeting/dex_retargeter/optimizer.py 
def get_objective_function(self, target_pos, fixed_qpos, last_qpos):
    expected = (len(self._target_links), 3)
    if target_pos.shape != expected:
        raise ValueError(
            f"PositionOptimizer: target_pos shape {target_pos.shape} does not match "
            f"{expected} (one (x, y, z) per target link). Did you pass the full "
            f"21-keypoint MANO array? Slice by target_link_human_indices first, "
            f"e.g. via DexRetargeter.extract_ref_value."
        )
    qpos = np.zeros(self.num_joints, dtype=np.float32)
    qpos[self.idx_fixed] = fixed_qpos
    torch_target_pos = torch.as_tensor(target_pos, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
    torch_target_pos.requires_grad_(False)

    def objective(x: np.ndarray, grad: np.ndarray) -> float:
        qpos[self.idx_target] = x
        self._set_qpos(qpos)
        body_pos = self._link_positions(self._target_links)

        torch_body_pos = torch.as_tensor(body_pos, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
        torch_body_pos.requires_grad_()
        huber_distance = self.huber_loss(torch_body_pos, torch_target_pos)
        result = float(huber_distance.detach().item())

        if grad.size > 0:
            self._write_grad(self._target_links, torch_body_pos, huber_distance, x, last_qpos, grad)
        return result

    return objective

Source code in eden/extensions/retargeting/dex_retargeter/optimizer.py 
def get_objective_function(self, target_vector, fixed_qpos, last_qpos):
    expected = (len(self.origin_link_indices), 3)
    if target_vector.shape != expected:
        raise ValueError(
            f"VectorOptimizer: target_vector shape {target_vector.shape} does not "
            f"match {expected} (one (dx, dy, dz) per origin/task link pair). Did "
            f"you pass the full 21-keypoint MANO array? Compute "
            f"`kp[task_idx] - kp[origin_idx]` first, e.g. via "
            f"DexRetargeter.extract_ref_value."
        )
    qpos = np.zeros(self.num_joints, dtype=np.float32)
    qpos[self.idx_fixed] = fixed_qpos
    torch_target_vec = torch.as_tensor(target_vector, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device) * self.scaling
    torch_target_vec.requires_grad_(False)

    def objective(x: np.ndarray, grad: np.ndarray) -> float:
        qpos[self.idx_target] = x
        self._set_qpos(qpos)
        body_pos = self._link_positions(self._computed_links)

        torch_body_pos = torch.as_tensor(body_pos, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
        torch_body_pos.requires_grad_()
        robot_vec = torch_body_pos[self.task_link_indices, :] - torch_body_pos[self.origin_link_indices, :]
        vec_dist = torch.norm(robot_vec - torch_target_vec, dim=1)
        huber_distance = self.huber_loss(vec_dist, torch.zeros_like(vec_dist))
        result = float(huber_distance.detach().item())

        if grad.size > 0:
            self._write_grad(self._computed_links, torch_body_pos, huber_distance, x, last_qpos, grad)
        return result

    return objective

DexPilot vector retargeting with thumb-to-fingertip projection.

A direct port of dex_retargeting.optimizer.DexPilotOptimizer. Generates its own link pairs (each fingertip-to-wrist + every fingertip-pair) and snaps thumb-to-fingertip distances inside project_dist to encourage pinch grasps. See https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.03135.

Source code in eden/extensions/retargeting/dex_retargeter/optimizer.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    entity: "RigidEntity",
    target_joint_names: List[str],
    finger_tip_link_names: List[str],
    wrist_link_name: str,
    target_link_human_indices: Optional[np.ndarray] = None,
    huber_delta: float = 0.03,
    norm_delta: float = 4e-3,
    project_dist: float = 0.03,
    escape_dist: float = 0.05,
    eta1: float = 1e-4,
    eta2: float = 3e-2,
    scaling: float = 1.0,
) -> None:
    if not (2 <= len(finger_tip_link_names) <= 5):
        raise ValueError(f"DexPilot supports 2..5 fingertips; got {len(finger_tip_link_names)}.")
    self.num_fingers = len(finger_tip_link_names)

    origin_link_index, task_link_index = self._generate_link_indices(self.num_fingers)
    if target_link_human_indices is None:
        target_link_human_indices = (np.stack([origin_link_index, task_link_index], axis=0) * 4).astype(int)

    links_name = [wrist_link_name] + list(finger_tip_link_names)
    origin_names = [links_name[i] for i in origin_link_index]
    task_names = [links_name[i] for i in task_link_index]

    super().__init__(entity, target_joint_names, target_link_human_indices)
    self.scaling = scaling
    self.huber_loss = torch.nn.SmoothL1Loss(beta=huber_delta, reduction="none")
    self.norm_delta = norm_delta
    self.project_dist = project_dist
    self.escape_dist = escape_dist
    self.eta1 = eta1
    self.eta2 = eta2

    self._setup_link_pairs(origin_names, task_names)
    self.opt.set_ftol_abs(1e-6)

    (
        self.projected,
        self.s2_project_index_origin,
        self.s2_project_index_task,
        self.projected_dist,
    ) = self._set_dexpilot_cache(self.num_fingers, eta1, eta2)

def get_objective_function(self, target_vector, fixed_qpos, last_qpos):
    qpos = np.zeros(self.num_joints, dtype=np.float32)
    qpos[self.idx_fixed] = fixed_qpos

    len_proj = len(self.projected)
    len_s2 = len(self.s2_project_index_task)
    len_s1 = len_proj - len_s2

    target_vec_dist = np.linalg.norm(target_vector[:len_proj], axis=1)
    self.projected[:len_s1][target_vec_dist[0:len_s1] < self.project_dist] = True
    self.projected[:len_s1][target_vec_dist[0:len_s1] > self.escape_dist] = False
    self.projected[len_s1:len_proj] = np.logical_and(
        self.projected[:len_s1][self.s2_project_index_origin],
        self.projected[:len_s1][self.s2_project_index_task],
    )
    self.projected[len_s1:len_proj] = np.logical_and(
        self.projected[len_s1:len_proj], target_vec_dist[len_s1:len_proj] <= _DEXPILOT_SECONDARY_PROJECT_DIST
    )

    normal_weight = np.ones(len_proj, dtype=np.float32)
    high_weight = np.array([200] * len_s1 + [400] * len_s2, dtype=np.float32)
    weight = np.where(self.projected, high_weight, normal_weight)
    # `as_tensor(..., device=self.device)`, not `from_numpy`: every tensor in this objective is built on
    # the entity's device, explicitly, since there is no torch default device (Genesis stopped setting one in
    # https://github.com/Genesis-Embodied-AI/Genesis/pull/3431). `from_numpy` aliases the numpy buffer, so it is
    # always CPU: on a GPU backend, multiplying the CUDA huber term by it raises inside nlopt, and `retarget`'s
    # `except RuntimeError` turns that into a per-frame warning while handing back `last_qpos` -- a robot hand
    # that silently never moves.
    weight = torch.as_tensor(
        np.concatenate([weight, np.ones(self.num_fingers, dtype=np.float32) * len_proj + self.num_fingers]),
        dtype=torch.float32,
        device=self.device,
    )

    normal_vec = target_vector * self.scaling
    dir_vec = target_vector[:len_proj] / (target_vec_dist[:, None] + 1e-6)
    projected_vec = dir_vec * self.projected_dist[:, None]
    reference_vec = np.where(self.projected[:, None], projected_vec, normal_vec[:len_proj])
    reference_vec = np.concatenate([reference_vec, normal_vec[len_proj:]], axis=0)
    torch_target_vec = torch.as_tensor(reference_vec, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
    torch_target_vec.requires_grad_(False)

    def objective(x: np.ndarray, grad: np.ndarray) -> float:
        qpos[self.idx_target] = x
        self._set_qpos(qpos)
        body_pos = self._link_positions(self._computed_links)

        torch_body_pos = torch.as_tensor(body_pos, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
        torch_body_pos.requires_grad_()
        robot_vec = torch_body_pos[self.task_link_indices, :] - torch_body_pos[self.origin_link_indices, :]
        vec_dist = torch.norm(robot_vec - torch_target_vec, dim=1)
        huber_distance = (self.huber_loss(vec_dist, torch.zeros_like(vec_dist)) * weight / robot_vec.shape[0]).sum()
        result = float(huber_distance.detach().item())

        if grad.size > 0:
            self._write_grad(self._computed_links, torch_body_pos, huber_distance, x, last_qpos, grad)
        return result

    return objective

urdf_to_mano_rot(robot: 'RigidEntity') -> tuple[ndarray, ndarray]

Derive the URDF↔MANO conversion from the robot's up / front.

Returns (R_mano_to_world, q_urdf_to_mano) where:

  • R_mano_to_world (3x3) — maps MANO-local vectors into the canonical world frame the robot is loaded into via align_up_and_front(robot.up, robot.front). Used at retargeting time to bring MANO keypoint targets into the robot's world frame.
  • q_urdf_to_mano (4,) wxyz — composed onto the per-frame MANO wrist quat to produce the floating-base base_quat_w for viz.

The robot's MANO side is read from metadata.side (defaults to right).

Source code in eden/extensions/retargeting/dex_retargeter/calibrate.py 
def urdf_to_mano_rot(robot: "RigidEntity") -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Derive the URDF↔MANO conversion from the robot's ``up`` / ``front``.

    Returns ``(R_mano_to_world, q_urdf_to_mano)`` where:

    - ``R_mano_to_world`` (3x3) — maps MANO-local vectors into the
      canonical world frame the robot is loaded into via
      ``align_up_and_front(robot.up, robot.front)``. Used at retargeting
      time to bring MANO keypoint targets into the robot's world frame.
    - ``q_urdf_to_mano`` (4,) wxyz — composed onto the per-frame MANO
      wrist quat to produce the floating-base ``base_quat_w`` for viz.

    The robot's MANO side is read from ``metadata.side`` (defaults to right).
    """
    from genesis.utils.geom import R_to_quat

    md = getattr(robot.options, "metadata", None)
    side = getattr(md, "side", "right") if md is not None else "right"
    mano_up, mano_front = _MANO_UP_FRONT[side]

    R_robot_to_world = align_up_and_front(robot.options.up, robot.options.front)
    R_mano_to_world = align_up_and_front(mano_up, mano_front)
    # R_urdf_to_mano = R_world_to_mano @ R_urdf_to_world = R_mano_to_world.T @ R_robot_to_world
    R_urdf_to_mano = (R_mano_to_world.T @ R_robot_to_world).astype(np.float32)
    q_urdf_to_mano = R_to_quat(R_urdf_to_mano).astype(np.float32)
    return R_mano_to_world.astype(np.float32), q_urdf_to_mano

def next(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    if not self.is_init:
        self.y = np.array(x, copy=True)
        self.is_init = True
        return self.y.copy()
    self.y = self.y + self.alpha * (x - self.y)
    return self.y.copy()

def __init__(self, env, options: RetargeterOptions) -> None:
    super().__init__(env, options)

    # -- normalize mutable fields ------------------------------------------
    if isinstance(self.foot_links, list):
        self.foot_links = {k: k for k in self.foot_links}
    for name in ("n_iter_init", "n_iter"):
        if getattr(self, name) < 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"OmniRetargeter: {name}={getattr(self, name)!r} runs no SQP iteration, so no frame would "
                f"be solved. Pass {name} >= 1 (the defaults are n_iter_init=50, n_iter=10)."
            )
    self._refuse_unknown(
        "laplacian_match_links keys",
        self.laplacian_match_links,
        self.demo_joints,
        "demo_joints (the demo's joint axis)",
    )
    self.smplh_mapped_joint_indices: list[int] = [
        self.demo_joints.index(name) for name in self.laplacian_match_links
    ]

    # -- validate link names against entity ---------------------------------
    available_links = [link.name for link in self.entity.links]
    self._refuse_unknown(
        "laplacian_match_links values",
        self.laplacian_match_links.values(),
        available_links,
        f"the links of entity '{self.entity_name}'",
    )
    self._refuse_unknown(
        "foot_links values", self.foot_links.values(), available_links, f"the links of entity '{self.entity_name}'"
    )
    self._refuse_unknown(
        "foot_sticking_map entries",
        [key for keys in self.foot_sticking_map.values() for key in keys],
        self.foot_links,
        "the foot_links keys",
    )

    # -- DOF layout --------------------------------------------------------
    #
    # Eden floating-base DOF layout:
    #   qpos:  [base_pos(3), base_quat(4), joints(N)]  → total 7 + N
    #   DOF:   [base_lin(3), base_ang(3),  joints(N)]  → total 6 + N
    #
    # The optimisation variable ``dqa`` lives in DOF (tangent) space.
    # ---------------------------------------------------------------
    self.dofs_name: list[str] = list(self.entity.dofs_name)
    self.n_joints: int = len(self.entity.dofs_name)
    self.nq_opt: int = self.entity.n_dofs
    # 6 base tangent DOFs only when a free root exists. ``has_immobile_base`` (not
    # ``is_fixed_base``) is the question: a welded child's root joint is removed by
    # ``attach``, so its qpos and DOF vectors have no base prefix either.
    self._joint_dof_start: int = 0 if self.entity.has_immobile_base else 6
    # The same split in qpos: ``[pos(3), quat_wxyz(4), joints]``, or just ``joints``.
    self._joint_q_start: int = 0 if self.entity.has_immobile_base else 7
    self.nq: int = self._joint_q_start + self.n_joints
    # ``_integrate_dqa`` adds a step to each joint q, which only holds when every joint has
    # one q and one DOF; a ball joint (4 q / 3 DOFs) or a ``dofs_name`` that leaves joints
    # out would put every slice past it in the wrong place.
    expected_n_dofs = self._joint_dof_start + self.n_joints
    if self.nq != self.entity.n_qs or expected_n_dofs != self.nq_opt:
        multi_dof = sorted({name for name in self.dofs_name if self.dofs_name.count(name) > 1})
        raise ValueError(
            f"OmniRetargeter: entity '{self.entity_name}' has n_qs={self.entity.n_qs} and "
            f"n_dofs={self.nq_opt}, but OmniRetarget handles only "
            f"{'a fixed base' if self.entity.has_immobile_base else 'a free root (7 q / 6 DOFs)'} plus "
            f"one-DOF hinge or slide joints, all listed in dofs_name ({self.n_joints} entries here), "
            f"which would give n_qs={self.nq} and n_dofs={expected_n_dofs}. "
            f"Joints with more than one DOF: {multi_dof or 'none (so dofs_name leaves joints out)'}. "
            f"Retarget an entity built from one-DOF joints, e.g. a ball joint split into three hinges."
        )

    for field in ("manual_lb", "manual_ub", "manual_cost", "nominal_tracking_dofs"):
        self._refuse_unknown(
            field, getattr(self, field), self.dofs_name, f"the dofs_name of entity '{self.entity_name}'"
        )

    # -- joint limits & cost weights (DOF space) ---------------------------
    self._init_limits_and_costs()

    # -- nominal tracking indices (joint DOFs only) ------------------------
    self.nominal_tracking_joint_indices = np.array(
        [self.dofs_name.index(name) for name in self.nominal_tracking_dofs], dtype=int
    )
    self.nominal_tracking_dof_indices = self._joint_dof_start + self.nominal_tracking_joint_indices
