def evaluate_retarget(
    retargeter: OTRetargeter,
    human: HumanSurfaceMotion,
    objects: list[InteractionObject],
    result: RetargetResult,
    eps_eval: float = 0.02,
    stance_height: float = 0.02,
    max_vertices_per_link: int = 1500,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Score a retarget against its demonstration.

    Parameters
    ----------
    retargeter : OTRetargeter
        The retargeter that produced ``result`` (after :meth:`~OTRetargeter.retarget_motion`, so its
        correspondence groups and channels match the demonstration).
    human : HumanSurfaceMotion
        The demonstration.
    objects : list[InteractionObject]
        Its objects (demonstrated poses).
    result : RetargetResult
        The retargeted motion.
    eps_eval : float
        Interaction threshold (20 mm).
    stance_height : float
        A foot is in stance when its lowest point is below this (m).
    max_vertices_per_link : int
        Robot visual-mesh vertices kept per link (evenly subsampled) to bound the cost.

    Returns
    -------
    dict[str, float]
        ``ground/*``, ``object/*`` and ``hand/*`` agreement and errors, ``clearance_mm``, ``skate_cm_s``,
        ``penetration_p95_mm``, ``hand/penetration_p95_mm``, ``rot_deg`` (``rot_body_deg`` over the root entity's
        links when hands are welded on), ``drift_cm``, and
        ``jitter_joint_deg`` (deg/frame^2), ``jitter_root_cm`` and ``jitter_human_pelvis_cm`` (cm/frame^2).
    """
    kin = retargeter.kin
    links = {link.name: link for ent in kin.entities for link in ent.links}
    groups = [retargeter._group(g) for g in retargeter.correspondences]
    # Robot units: visual-mesh vertices of each group's links, in link frames.
    unit_link, unit_local, unit_id = [], [], []
    for ui, (_, robot_links) in enumerate(groups):
        for name in robot_links:
            link = links[name]
            if len(link.vgeoms) == 0:
                continue
            v = np.asarray(get_link_mesh(link, use_visual_mesh=True).vertices)
            if len(v) > max_vertices_per_link:
                v = v[np.linspace(0, len(v) - 1, max_vertices_per_link).astype(int)]
            unit_link.append(np.full(len(v), kin.link_index(name)))
            unit_local.append(v)
            unit_id.append(np.full(len(v), ui))
    hand_links = {link.name for ent in kin.entities[1:] for link in ent.links}
    # All of a group's links, not any: the Wuji presets put the hand's mount link in the elbow group.
    hand_unit = np.array([bool(robot_links) and set(robot_links) <= hand_links for _, robot_links in groups])
    unit_link = np.concatenate(unit_link)
    unit_local = np.concatenate(unit_local)
    unit_id = np.concatenate(unit_id)
    # Human units: mesh vertices of each group's parts.
    vparts = human.vertex_parts
    human_unit = np.full(len(vparts), -1)
    for ui, (human_parts, _) in enumerate(groups):
        human_unit[np.isin(vparts, [human.joint_index(p) for p in human_parts])] = ui

    n_frames, n_units = len(result.qpos), len(groups)
    # Each unit's vertex indices, found once: rebuilding the masks per frame, channel and unit cost O(V * units).
    human_idx = [np.flatnonzero(human_unit == ui) for ui in range(n_units)]
    robot_idx = [np.flatnonzero(unit_id == ui) for ui in range(n_units)]
    channels = retargeter.channels
    d_hat = np.full((n_frames, n_units, len(channels)), np.inf)
    d_rob = np.full_like(d_hat, np.inf)
    w_hat = np.zeros((*d_hat.shape, 3))
    w_rob = np.zeros_like(w_hat)
    pen = np.zeros(n_frames)
    hand_pen = np.zeros(n_frames)
    hand_vertex = hand_unit[unit_id]
    foot_units = [ui for ui, (hp, _) in enumerate(groups) if any("ankle" in p or "Foot" in p for p in hp)]
    foot_low = np.full((n_frames, len(foot_units)), np.inf)
    foot_pts: list[list[np.ndarray]] = [[] for _ in foot_units]
    solved = {o.name: result.object_poses[o.name] for o in objects}
    rot_err = []
    for t in range(n_frames):
        kin.set_configuration(result.qpos[t])
        link_pos, link_rot = kin.link_poses()
        robot_world = link_pos[unit_link] + np.einsum("nab,nb->na", link_rot[unit_link], unit_local)
        human_world = human.vertices[t].astype(np.float64)
        for ci, channel in enumerate(channels):
            oi = retargeter._channel_object[ci]
            if oi < 0:
                R_demo = R_now = np.eye(3)
                tau_demo = tau_now = np.array([0.0, 0.0, retargeter.ground_height])
            else:
                R_demo = quat_to_R(objects[oi].poses[t, 3:])
                tau_demo = objects[oi].poses[t, :3]
                R_now = quat_to_R(solved[objects[oi].name][t, 3:])
                tau_now = solved[objects[oi].name][t, :3]
            demo_channel = retargeter._demo_channels.get(oi, channel)
            hd, hw = demo_channel.exact_distance((human_world - tau_demo) @ R_demo)
            rd, rw = channel.exact_distance((robot_world - tau_now) @ R_now)
            pen[t] = max(pen[t], float(np.clip(-rd, 0.0, None).max()))
            if oi >= 0 and hand_vertex.any():
                hand_pen[t] = max(hand_pen[t], float(np.clip(-rd[hand_vertex], 0.0, None).max()))
            for ui in range(n_units):
                if len(hi := human_idx[ui]):
                    k = hi[np.argmin(hd[hi])]
                    d_hat[t, ui, ci], w_hat[t, ui, ci] = hd[k], hw[k]
                if len(ri := robot_idx[ui]):
                    k = ri[np.argmin(rd[ri])]
                    d_rob[t, ui, ci], w_rob[t, ui, ci] = rd[k], rw[k]
            if oi in retargeter._witness_map:
                # The demonstrated witness lies on the demo mesh; the robot's on the scene mesh. Mapped after the
                # closest vertex is chosen, so only one witness per unit goes through the tree.
                tree, s_pts, _ = retargeter._witness_map[oi]
                w_hat[t, :, ci] = s_pts[tree.query(w_hat[t, :, ci])[1]]
        for k, ui in enumerate(foot_units):
            pts = robot_world[robot_idx[ui]]
            foot_low[t, k] = pts[:, 2].min() - retargeter.ground_height
            foot_pts[k].append(pts)
        # Style orientation error against the retargeter's own targets.
        _, style_rot = retargeter._style_targets(human, t)
        rel = np.einsum("lab,lcb->lac", link_rot[retargeter._style_link_idx], style_rot)
        cos = np.clip((np.trace(rel, axis1=1, axis2=2) - 1.0) / 2.0, -1.0, 1.0)
        rot_err.append(np.degrees(np.arccos(cos)))

    out: dict[str, float] = {}
    is_ground = np.array([retargeter._channel_object[ci] < 0 for ci in range(len(channels))])
    every_unit = np.ones(n_units, dtype=bool)
    for name, mask, units in (
        ("ground", is_ground, every_unit),
        ("object", ~is_ground, every_unit),
        ("hand", ~is_ground, hand_unit),
    ):
        if not mask.any() or not units.any():
            continue
        dh = d_hat[:, units][:, :, mask]
        dr = d_rob[:, units][:, :, mask]
        H = np.maximum(dh, 0.0) < eps_eval
        R = np.maximum(dr, 0.0) < eps_eval
        out |= {f"{name}/{k}": v for k, v in _agreement(H, R).items()}
        if H.any():
            out[f"{name}/depth_err_mm"] = 1e3 * float(np.abs(dr[H] - np.maximum(dh[H], 0.0)).mean())
            out[f"{name}/place_err_mm"] = 1e3 * float(
                np.linalg.norm(w_rob[:, units][:, :, mask][H] - w_hat[:, units][:, :, mask][H], axis=1).mean()
            )
    stance = foot_low < stance_height
    out["clearance_mm"] = 1e3 * float(np.median(foot_low[stance])) if stance.any() else float("nan")
    skate = []
    dt = 1.0 / result.fps
    for k in range(len(foot_units)):
        for t in range(n_frames - 1):
            if stance[t, k] and stance[t + 1, k]:
                # The vertices in contact at t: the least moving vertex of the whole foot read a foot yawing or
                # rolling heel-to-toe in place as no skate (any rigid motion has a point that barely moves).
                pts = foot_pts[k][t]
                down = pts[:, 2] - retargeter.ground_height < stance_height
                disp = np.linalg.norm((foot_pts[k][t + 1][down] - pts[down])[:, :2], axis=1)
                skate.append(disp.mean() / dt)
    out["skate_cm_s"] = 100.0 * float(np.median(skate)) if skate else float("nan")
    out["penetration_p95_mm"] = 1e3 * float(np.percentile(pen, 95))
    if hand_unit.any() and (~is_ground).any():
        out["hand/penetration_p95_mm"] = 1e3 * float(np.percentile(hand_pen, 95))
    if n_frames > 2:
        q = result.qpos
        out["jitter_joint_deg"] = float(np.degrees(np.abs(np.diff(q[:, kin.n_base_q :], 2, axis=0))).mean())
        if kin.floating:
            out["jitter_root_cm"] = 100.0 * float(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(q[:, :3], 2, axis=0), axis=1).mean())
            pelvis = human.joint_pos[:n_frames, retargeter._pelvis_joint]
            out["jitter_human_pelvis_cm"] = 100.0 * float(np.linalg.norm(np.diff(pelvis, 2, axis=0), axis=1).mean())
    rot_err = np.array(rot_err)  # (T, tracked links)
    out["rot_deg"] = float(rot_err.mean())
    # The same over the links of the root entity alone: the hand presets weigh finger style down on purpose.
    body = np.array([kin.link_names[li] not in hand_links for li in retargeter._style_link_idx])
    if body.any() and not body.all():
        out["rot_body_deg"] = float(rot_err[:, body].mean())
    if objects:
        out["drift_cm"] = 100.0 * float(
            np.mean([np.linalg.norm(solved[o.name][:, :3] - o.poses[:n_frames, :3], axis=1).mean() for o in objects])
        )
    return out

docs.title: SomaRetargeter
docs.text:
SomaRetargeter runs the eden-soma-retargeter library in a worker process. That extra pins a trimesh that only a checkout's uv override reconciles with Genesis, so install it with uv sync --inexact --extra soma-retargeter (it cannot be pip-installed).

Eden RetargetingBase wrapper around the eden-soma-retargeter library.

Retargets human motion — SMPL / SMPL-H / SMPL-X (fitted via py-soma-x) or native SOMA (arrays / save_soma_npz files / SOMA-skeleton BVH) — onto a floating-base robot (Unitree G1 29-DOF, LimX Oli 31-DOF), returning Genesis-compatible qpos.

Usage mirrors DexRetargeter / OmniRetargeter:

.. code-block:: python

retargeter = SomaRetargeter(
    env=env,
    options=SomaRetargeter.configure(
        entity_name="robot",
        body_model="smplx",
        body_model_path="/path/to/SMPLX_NEUTRAL.npz",
        target_fps=30.0,
    ),
)
qpos = retargeter.retarget_motion(poses=..., trans=..., betas=..., source_fps=120.0)
qpos_batch = retargeter.retarget_motions([clip0, clip1, ...])

Why a worker subprocess. Retargeting runs in a persistent Genesis-free worker process; this class streams clips to it and permutes results into entity.dofs_name order. The isolation is precautionary — it keeps the Warp fit's CUDA context and its several GB off the ones Genesis holds — and is an internal detail: the public API is the same in-process loop as the other retargeters.

Post-process each clip with one constant vertical offset so the lowest point of the robot's collision geometry over the whole motion touches the ground plane (z = 0) — lifts clips whose feet sink below the floor, lowers floating ones. def __init__(self, env: "EnvBase", options: RetargeterOptions) -> None:
    # Set before anything that can raise, so __del__ -> close() is always safe.
    self._proc: subprocess.Popen | None = None
    self._perm: np.ndarray | None = None
    self._perm_names: tuple[str, ...] | None = None

    super().__init__(env, options)

    if self.entity.has_immobile_base:
        reason = "is welded onto another entity" if self.entity.is_attached else "is fixed-base"
        raise ValueError(
            f"SomaRetargeter requires a floating-base entity (returns qpos with "
            f"[base_pos(3), base_quat(4), joints(N)]); '{self.entity.name}' {reason} and has "
            f"no base DOFs."
        )
    check_backend_available(self.body_model)

def close(self) -> None:
    """Terminate the worker subprocess (idempotent)."""
    proc, self._proc = getattr(self, "_proc", None), None
    if proc is None:
        return
    try:
        if proc.stdin is not None:
            proc.stdin.close()
        proc.wait(timeout=10)
    except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - best-effort teardown
        proc.kill()

def retarget_motion(
    self,
    poses: np.ndarray | None = None,
    trans: np.ndarray | None = None,
    transl: np.ndarray | None = None,
    betas: np.ndarray | None = None,
    gender: str | None = None,
    source_fps: float | None = None,
    **extra,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Retarget one clip to Genesis qpos ``(T, 7 + N)`` in ``entity.dofs_name`` order.

    Field names follow SOMA-X conventions. For the smpl family pass
    ``poses`` / ``trans`` / ``betas`` / ``source_fps`` (+ optional
    ``gender``); for native SOMA arrays pass ``poses`` / ``transl`` /
    ``source_fps``. Returned qpos is ``[x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz, joints...]``,
    Z-up, wxyz quaternion, radians.
    """
    clip: dict = {"source_fps": source_fps, **extra}
    if poses is not None:
        clip["poses"] = poses
    if trans is not None:
        clip["trans"] = trans
    if transl is not None:
        clip["transl"] = transl
    if betas is not None:
        clip["betas"] = betas
    if gender is not None:
        clip["gender"] = gender
    clip = {k: v for k, v in clip.items() if v is not None}
    return self._to_qpos(self._run([clip])[0])

docs.text:
build_dof_permutation(source_joint_names: Sequence[str], entity_dofs_name: Sequence[str]) -> ndarray

Permutation perm such that out[:, perm] = src maps each source DOF to its entity slot.

Resolves purely by name (independent of Genesis's internal link/DOF order, which changed BFS->DFS in genesis 1.2.0). A trailing _dof suffix on source names is tolerated. Raises ValueError on a length mismatch or a missing joint, listing both name sets.

Source code in eden/extensions/retargeting/soma_retargeter/retargeter.py 
def build_dof_permutation(source_joint_names: Sequence[str], entity_dofs_name: Sequence[str]) -> np.ndarray:
    """Permutation ``perm`` such that ``out[:, perm] = src`` maps each source DOF to its entity slot.

    Resolves purely by name (independent of Genesis's internal link/DOF order,
    which changed BFS->DFS in genesis 1.2.0). A trailing ``_dof`` suffix on
    source names is tolerated. Raises ``ValueError`` on a length mismatch or a
    missing joint, listing both name sets.
    """
    entity = list(entity_dofs_name)
    entity_index = {n: i for i, n in enumerate(entity)}
    # Strip the CSV '_dof' suffix only when doing so resolves a name.
    src = [
        n if n in entity_index else (n[:-4] if n.endswith("_dof") and n[:-4] in entity_index else n)
        for n in source_joint_names
    ]
    if len(src) != len(entity):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Retargeter emits {len(src)} DOFs but entity has {len(entity)}. Source: {src}. Entity: {entity}."
        )
    missing = [n for n in src if n not in entity_index]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f"Retargeter DOFs not in entity.dofs_name: {missing}. Entity DOFs: {entity}.")
    perm = [entity_index[n] for n in src]
    if len(set(perm)) != len(perm):
        raise ValueError(f"Retargeter DOF names are not a bijection onto entity.dofs_name (duplicates). Source: {src}.")
    return np.array(perm, dtype=np.int64)

docs.title: FlashDexRetarget
docs.text:
The kinematic half of FlashDexRetarget: import a released hand-object dataset, preprocess and filter its clips, retarget each with physics IK in MuJoCo, and pack the kept clips into motion.pt.

Options for the FlashDexRetarget kinematic-retargeting pipeline (human demos -> motion.pt).

Two stages, each driven by one options object:

  • :class:FDRImportOptions — a released dataset (TACO, OakInk2, HOT3D, DexYCB, each read by its :mod:eden.datasets loader) -> <dataset>/human_demo/<clip>.npz and <dataset>/objects/<id>/visual.obj.
  • :class:FDRKinematicRetargetingOptions — those clips -> support disks and reject rules (report.csv), convex object parts, MuJoCo physics IK onto the robot hand, and <dataset>/<robot>/motion.pt.

Defaults are FlashDexRetarget's (Holiday-Robot/FlashDexRetarget config/retarget/*.yaml); the Isaac-only usd step is gone. eden retarget flashdex builds these from --config / --override the way eden train does.

Import: a released dataset -> <dataset>/human_demo/<clip>.npz + <dataset>/objects/<id>/visual.obj.

The release is read by its :mod:eden.datasets loader (TacoDataset, OakInk2Dataset, Hot3dDataset, DexYCBDataset) with its MANO parameters (body_model_params), in the loader's z-up world at the release's frame rate; the loader cuts the clips and picks the object each hand holds. Per clip, this runs MANO, moves the surface the objects rest on to table_z, takes the wrist and fingertip reference the rewards compare against, and resamples to fps. A clip is skipped when an object flips more than max_obj_rot_step_deg in one source frame.

Kinematic retargeting: imported clips -> <dataset>/<robot>/motion.pt for one robot.

================= ================================================== =========================================== step does writes (under the dataset) ================= ================================================== =========================================== preprocess support disks, reject rules <robot>/report.csv convex convex decomposition (CoACD or CuACD) objects/<id>/convex/*.obj retarget MuJoCo physics IK <robot>/retargeted/<clip>.npz pack kept clips into one file <robot>/motion.pt urdf object URDFs for simulation objects/<id>/object.urdf sdf object SDF grids objects/<id>/.sdf_cache/ ================= ================================================== ===========================================

Preprocess: support disks and reject rules over every imported clip (writes only the report rows).

Retarget step: every IK attempt of every kept clip as a job of its own, the best attempt per clip saved to <robot>/retargeted/<clip>.npz and scored for the report.

A saved clip is a cache keyed (cache_key) on everything its IK read: the robot and its model files, the imported clip's bytes, its support disks, its objects' convex parts and the retarget options (force and the quality flags, which are scored afresh every run, aside), so a re-import, an updated asset, redone convex parts or a changed setting redoes it.

Pack: kept retargeted clips -> <dataset>/<robot>/motion.pt, with velocities and fingertip contact labels.

Per-frame arrays are concatenated over clips; clip i covers frames length_starts[i] to length_starts[i] + motion_num_frames[i]. joint_pos is in the robot MJCF's joint order, which joint_names lists; robot names the robot and fps the frame rate.

The imported-clip format (<dataset>/human_demo/<clip>.npz) and the object-mesh cache the pipeline shares.

All arrays are at the clip's fps, in a z-up world, in metres; s is right or left:

============================================ =========================== ============================================ key shape content ============================================ =========================== ============================================ fps () frame rate (one per dataset) mano_s_wrist_pos, mano_s_wrist_rot (T, 3), (T, 3, 3) MANO wrist, rotation in the robot palm's convention (see :func:mano_reference) mano_s_joints (T, 20, 3) MANO finger joints and tips, :data:MANO_JOINT_NAMES order obj_s_pose, obj_s_id (T, 4, 4), () object pose and its folder under objects/ obj_s_scale, obj_s_mass () optional mesh scale and mass ============================================ =========================== ============================================

Reject rules over imported clips: the per-clip features they test, and the verdict.

Quality flags of a retargeted clip, from a kinematic replay of its qpos (a flagged clip is still packed).

def open_dataset(cfg: FDRImportOptions) -> DatasetBase:
    """The :mod:`eden.datasets` loader of ``cfg.source``, built over ``cfg.raw`` with its MANO parameters."""
    from eden.datasets import DATASET_REGISTRY

    cls = DATASET_REGISTRY.get(SOURCE_DATASETS[cfg.source.name])
    params: dict[str, Any] = {
        "raw_data_path": cfg.raw,
        "body_model_params": True,
        "body_model_dir": cfg.mano_dir,
    }
    if cfg.source.name == "dexycb":
        from eden.datasets.dex_ycb_dataset import DEX_YCB_FRAMERATE

        raw = Path(cfg.raw)
        params |= {
            "target_framerate": DEX_YCB_FRAMERATE,
            "calibration_dir": str(raw / "calibration"),
            "models_dir": str(raw / "models"),
            # FlashDexRetarget fits its own support disks on the release's poses and meshes.
            "ground_initial_pose": False,
            "apply_mesh_correction": False,
        }
    else:
        params |= {"target_framerate": cls.source_framerate, "sides": cfg.sides}
    taken = sorted(set(cfg.source.dataset) & set(params))
    if taken:
        raise ValueError(
            f"source.dataset sets {taken}, which the import sets itself (from raw, mano_dir, sides and the release's "
            f"frame rate). Set them on the import options instead, or drop them from source.dataset."
        )
    return cls(cls.configure(**params, **cfg.source.dataset), torch.device("cpu"))

def import_demos(cfg: FDRImportOptions) -> list[dict]:
    """``cfg.raw`` (a released dataset, ``cfg.source``) -> ``<dataset>/human_demo/<clip>.npz`` and
    ``<dataset>/objects/<id>/visual.obj``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    cfg : FDRImportOptions
        Import settings.

    Returns
    -------
    list[dict]
        One row per clip: its name and frame count and objects, or the reason it was skipped (``skip``).
    """
    mano_dir = Path(cfg.mano_dir)
    for f in ("MANO_RIGHT.pkl", "MANO_LEFT.pkl"):
        if not (mano_dir / f).exists():
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                f"{mano_dir / f} missing. The import needs the MANO hand models, which are not redistributable: "
                "register at mano.is.tue.mpg.de, download 'Models & Code' (mano_v1_2.zip) and point `mano_dir` at "
                "its models/ directory."
            )
    en.logger.info(f"[import] {cfg.source.name}: reading {cfg.raw}")
    dataset = open_dataset(cfg)
    clips, skipped = _clips(dataset, cfg)
    out_dir = Path(cfg.dataset) / "human_demo"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    before = {p.stem for p in C.list_clips(out_dir)}
    rows = [{"clip": name, "skip": reason} for name, reason in skipped]
    done = 0
    for recording, group in itertools.groupby(sorted(clips, key=lambda c: c.recording), key=lambda c: c.recording):
        group = list(group)
        rec = _recording(dataset, recording, cfg, group[0].fps)
        rows += [_write(dataset, clip, cfg, out_dir, rec) for clip in group]
        if (done + len(group)) // 200 > done // 200 or done + len(group) == len(clips):
            en.logger.info(f"[import] {done + len(group)}/{len(clips)} clips")
        done += len(group)
    kept = [r for r in rows if "skip" not in r]
    reasons = count_reasons(r["skip"] for r in rows if "skip" in r)
    if not kept:
        # Before any earlier clip is removed below: an import that keeps nothing is a misconfiguration, not a release
        # whose clips all went away.
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"[import] every clip of {cfg.raw} was skipped ({len(rows)}: {reasons}), so nothing was written to "
            f"{out_dir} and its earlier clips are left as they are. First skips: {[r['skip'] for r in rows[:3]]}. "
            f"Check `sides` (now {cfg.sides!r}: each of those hands must hold an object) and the source's settings."
        )
    exported: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for oid in sorted({o for r in kept for k in ("objects", "context") if r.get(k) for o in r[k].split()}):
        status = _export_mesh(dataset, oid, Path(cfg.dataset) / "objects" / oid, cfg.textures)
        exported.setdefault(status, []).append(oid)
        if cfg.textures:
            # A trimesh mesh sits in reference cycles, so the textured one just exported is freed by the cycle
            # collector, which runs on object counts, not bytes: without this, the decoded textures (~50 MB each at
            # 4096^2) pile up, 1.5 GB over DexYCB's 20 objects.
            gc.collect()
    objects = Path(cfg.dataset) / "objects"
    changed, rewritten = exported.get("changed", []), exported.get("rewritten", [])
    retextured = exported.get("retextured", [])
    if retextured:
        en.logger.info(
            f"[import] {len(retextured)} objects already in {objects} got this release's materials and textures, their "
            f"visual.obj (and the convex parts and SDF grids made from it) unchanged, e.g. {retextured[:3]}"
        )
    if rewritten:
        en.logger.warning(
            f"[import] {len(rewritten)} objects already in {objects} have this release's geometry, but their "
            f"visual.obj was written again (other UVs, or another trimesh version's formatting), e.g. "
            f"{rewritten[:3]}; their convex parts, SDF grids and retargeted clips are redone."
        )
    if changed:
        en.logger.warning(
            f"[import] {len(changed)} objects already in {objects} had another mesh, now replaced "
            f"by this release's, e.g. {changed[:3]}; their convex parts, SDF grids and retargeted clips are redone."
        )
    en.logger.info(f"[import] {len(kept)} clips -> {out_dir}, skipped {len(rows) - len(kept)} {reasons}")
    # A clip this import skips but an earlier one wrote would still be retargeted: it goes.
    stale = sorted(before & {r["clip"] for r in rows if "skip" in r})
    for name in stale:
        (out_dir / f"{name}.npz").unlink()
    if stale:
        en.logger.info(
            f"[import] removed {len(stale)} clips of an earlier import that this one skips, e.g. {stale[:3]}"
        )
    others = sorted(before - {r["clip"] for r in rows})
    if others:
        en.logger.warning(
            f"[import] {out_dir} also holds {len(others)} clips this import did not write (another release or other "
            f"source settings), e.g. {others[:3]}; `eden retarget flashdex kinematic` retargets them too. Delete them "
            "if they are left over."
        )
    return rows

def run_kinematic_retargeting(cfg: FDRKinematicRetargetingOptions) -> Path | None:
    """Run the enabled steps over ``cfg.dataset``.

    The robot's outputs go to ``<dataset>/<robot>/`` (``report.csv``, ``retargeted/``, ``motion.pt``), so each robot
    retargeted from one import keeps its own; ``human_demo/`` and ``objects/`` are shared. A dataset without
    ``human_demo/`` but with the robot's ``motion.pt`` only gets its objects prepared (convex, sdf).

    Parameters
    ----------
    cfg : FDRKinematicRetargetingOptions
        Pipeline settings.

    Returns
    -------
    Path | None
        ``<dataset>/<robot>/motion.pt`` when it exists at the end, else ``None``.
    """
    workers = cfg.workers or max(1, (os.cpu_count() or 2) // 2)  # half the CPU cores by default
    steps = cfg.steps
    # What the last steps need, checked before the hours of IK ahead of them.
    if steps.convex and cfg.convex.name == "cuacd":
        check_cuacd(cfg.convex)
    if steps.sdf:
        check_sdf(cfg.sdf)
    dataset = Path(cfg.dataset)
    # Per robot: retargeting another robot keeps this one's results, and two robots' runs never share a file.
    demo, out = dataset / "human_demo", dataset / cfg.robot
    retargeted, motion, report = out / "retargeted", out / "motion.pt", out / "report.csv"
    old = [p for p in (dataset / "motion.pt", dataset / "report.csv", dataset / "retargeted") if p.exists()]
    if old:  # the layout before the per-robot directories: a training run pointed at them would load the stale ones
        en.logger.warning(
            f"[kinematic_retargeting] {dataset} still holds {[p.name for p in old]} of an earlier version, which wrote "
            f"one robot's outputs into the dataset itself; this run writes {out}/. Delete them."
        )
    from_clips = demo.is_dir()
    if from_clips:
        fps = clip_fps(list_clips(demo))
        en.logger.info(f"[kinematic_retargeting] preprocess: {demo} ({fps:g} Hz)")
        out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        rows, kept = preprocess_clips(demo, dataset, cfg, fps, workers)
        _write_report(report, rows)
        if not kept:
            raise RuntimeError(f"Every clip was rejected; the reasons are in {report} (column 'reject').")
        ids = object_ids(kept)
    elif motion.exists():
        en.logger.info(f"[kinematic_retargeting] no {demo}: preparing the objects of {motion}")
        packed = torch.load(motion, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
        ids = sorted({mesh.parent.name for mesh, _ in object_meshes(packed, motion.parent)})
    else:
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"{dataset} has neither human_demo/ nor {cfg.robot}/motion.pt; import a release into it first with "
            "`eden retarget flashdex import`."
        )

    if steps.convex:
        en.logger.info(f"[kinematic_retargeting] convex: {len(ids)} objects (<object>/convex/, {cfg.convex.name})")
        decompose_objects(dataset, ids, cfg.convex, workers)
    if from_clips and (steps.retarget or steps.pack):
        keys = _cache_keys(kept, dataset, cfg)
        names = set(keys)
        if steps.retarget:
            en.logger.info(f"[kinematic_retargeting] retarget: {len(kept)} clips -> {retargeted} ({cfg.robot})")
            ik = {
                r["clip"]: r
                for r in retarget_clips(
                    list(kept.items()), dataset, retargeted, cfg.robot, cfg.retarget, fps, workers, keys
                )
            }
            for r in rows:
                r.update(ik.get(r["clip"], {}))
            _write_report(report, rows)
            failed = {name for name, r in ik.items() if r.get("error")}
            if failed == names:
                raise RuntimeError(f"Every clip failed to retarget; the errors are in {report} (column 'error').")
            names -= failed
        if steps.pack:
            en.logger.info(f"[kinematic_retargeting] pack: {retargeted} -> {motion}")
            build(retargeted, dataset, motion, fps, cfg.pack, cfg.robot, {n: keys[n] for n in sorted(names)})
    if steps.urdf and motion.exists():
        packed = torch.load(motion, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
        write_object_urdfs(dataset, [(mesh.parent.name, scale) for mesh, scale in object_meshes(packed, motion.parent)])
    if steps.sdf and not motion.exists():
        en.logger.info(f"[kinematic_retargeting] sdf: skipped, no {motion} yet")
    elif steps.sdf:
        en.logger.info(f"[kinematic_retargeting] sdf: <object>/.sdf_cache/, {cfg.sdf.grid_n}^3")
        bake(motion, cfg.sdf, workers)
    return motion if motion.exists() else None

def preprocess_clips(
    clips: Path, pool: Path, cfg: FDRKinematicRetargetingOptions, fps: float, workers: int
) -> tuple[list[dict], dict[Path, np.ndarray | None]]:
    """Report rows of every clip, and the kept clips with their support disks.

    Parameters
    ----------
    clips : Path
        The ``human_demo/`` directory.
    pool : Path
        The dataset directory holding ``objects/``.
    cfg : FDRKinematicRetargetingOptions
        Pipeline settings (``desk``, ``filters``).
    fps : float
        The clips' frame rate.
    workers : int
        Processes.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[list[dict], dict[Path, np.ndarray | None]]
        One report row per clip (``reject`` empty when kept), and kept clip path -> its ``(K, 5)`` support disks.
    """
    paths = C.list_clips(clips)
    en.logger.info(f"[preprocess] {len(paths)} clips, desk={cfg.desk.mode}, filter={cfg.filters.enable}")
    jobs = [(str(p), str(pool), cfg, fps) for p in paths]
    with C.worker_pool(max(1, min(workers, len(jobs)))) as ex:
        results = list(ex.map(_process, *zip(*jobs))) if jobs else []

    rows = [r for r, _ in results]
    kept = {p: disks for p, (r, disks) in zip(paths, results) if not r["reject"]}
    counts: dict[str, int] = {}
    for r in rows:
        for reason in filter(None, r["reject"].split(";")):
            counts[reason] = counts.get(reason, 0) + 1
    en.logger.info(f"[preprocess] kept {len(kept)} / {len(rows)}  {counts}")
    return rows, kept

def cache_key(
    clip_path: Path, disks: np.ndarray | None, robot: str, robot_sha1: str, convex_sha1: dict[str, str], cfg
) -> dict:
    """What a retargeted clip was made from (cfg: retarget); compared field by field against a saved clip's.

    ``robot_sha1`` is :func:`~eden.extensions.retargeting.flashdexretarget.scene.robot_sha1` of the clip's hands and
    ``convex_sha1`` maps each of its objects to
    :func:`~eden.extensions.retargeting.flashdexretarget.convex.parts_sha1`.
    """
    return {
        "robot": robot,
        "robot_sha1": robot_sha1,
        "clip_sha1": hashlib.sha1(Path(clip_path).read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
        "support_disks_sha1": None
        if disks is None
        else hashlib.sha1(np.ascontiguousarray(disks, np.float64)).hexdigest(),
        "convex_sha1": dict(sorted(convex_sha1.items())),
        "retarget": cfg.model_dump(mode="json", exclude={"force", "quality"}),
    }

IK of (clip file, support disks) pairs into out, a cache: a clip whose saved result has its keys[stem] (:func:cache_key) is not redone unless cfg.force (cfg: retarget). Every IK run of every clip (cfg.attempts per clip) is a job of its own, so a long clip takes one run's time. Returns the report rows; retarget_seconds sums a clip's runs. A clip that fails has an error and no file in out.

Source code in eden/extensions/retargeting/flashdexretarget/retarget.py 
def retarget_clips(
    clips: list[tuple[Path, np.ndarray | None]],
    pool: Path,
    out: Path,
    robot: str,
    cfg,
    fps: float,
    workers: int,
    keys: dict[str, dict],
) -> list[dict]:
    """IK of (clip file, support disks) pairs into out, a cache: a clip whose saved result has its ``keys[stem]``
    (:func:`cache_key`) is not redone unless cfg.force (cfg: retarget). Every IK run of every clip (cfg.attempts per
    clip) is a job of its own, so a long clip takes one run's time. Returns the report rows; retarget_seconds sums a
    clip's runs. A clip that fails has an ``error`` and no file in out.
    """
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    en.logger.info(f"[retarget] {len(clips)} clips to {robot}")
    args = (str(pool), robot, cfg, fps)
    rows, runs, spent, jobs = [], {}, {}, {}

    def finish(p: Path, d, finished, seconds: float):
        return ex.submit(_finish, str(p), d, str(pool), str(out), robot, cfg, fps, finished, seconds, keys[p.stem])

    with C.worker_pool(max(1, workers)) as ex:
        for p, d in clips:
            try:
                check_length(C.num_frames(C.load_clip(p)), cfg.smooth)
            except ValueError as e:
                rows.append(_failed(out / p.name, {"clip": p.stem, "error": str(e)}, len(rows) + 1, len(clips)))
            else:
                if _needs_ik(keys[p.stem], out / p.name, cfg):
                    runs[p], spent[p] = [None] * cfg.attempts, 0.0
                    for k in range(cfg.attempts):
                        jobs[ex.submit(_attempt, str(p), d, *args, k)] = (p, d, k)
                else:
                    jobs[finish(p, d, None, 0.0)] = (p, d, None)
        while jobs:
            done, _ = wait(jobs, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED)
            for fut in done:
                p, d, k = jobs.pop(fut)
                if k is None:
                    r = fut.result()
                    if r.get("error"):
                        rows.append(_failed(out / p.name, r, len(rows) + 1, len(clips)))
                        continue
                    rows.append(r)
                    msg = f"{r['source']}, tip {r.get('ik_tip_err_mean_m', float('nan')) * 1e3:.1f} mm {r.get('flags') or 'ok'}"
                    en.logger.info(
                        f"[retarget] {len(rows)}/{len(clips)} {r['clip']} ({r['retarget_seconds']} s): {msg}"
                    )
                    continue
                runs[p][k], seconds = fut.result()
                spent[p] += seconds
                if any(r is None for r in runs[p]):
                    continue
                finished = runs.pop(p)
                failures = [(i, r) for i, r in enumerate(finished) if isinstance(r, _Failure)]
                if failures:
                    distinct = list(dict.fromkeys(r.error for _, r in failures))
                    row = {
                        "clip": p.stem,
                        "error": f"{len(failures)}/{len(finished)} IK attempts raised: " + "; ".join(distinct),
                        "traceback": f"attempt {failures[0][0]}:\n{failures[0][1].traceback}",
                        "retarget_seconds": round(spent[p], 1),
                    }
                    rows.append(_failed(out / p.name, row, len(rows) + 1, len(clips)))
                    continue
                jobs[finish(p, d, finished, spent[p])] = (p, d, None)
    errors = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("error"))
    flagged = sum(1 for r in rows if r.get("flags"))
    en.logger.info(f"[retarget] {len(rows) - errors} clips in {out} ({errors} errors, {flagged} flagged)")
    return rows

def velocity(x: np.ndarray, dt: float, sigma: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Finite difference, Gaussian-smoothed over time (sigma in frames)."""
    v = np.gradient(x, axis=0) / dt
    return gaussian_filter1d(v, sigma=sigma, axis=0, mode="nearest").astype(np.float32)

def angular_velocity(rot: np.ndarray, dt: float, sigma: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """World-frame angular velocity of a (T, 3, 3) rotation sequence."""
    w = Rotation.from_matrix(rot[1:] @ np.swapaxes(rot[:-1], -2, -1)).as_rotvec() / dt
    w = np.concatenate([w, w[-1:]], axis=0)
    return gaussian_filter1d(w, sigma=sigma, axis=0, mode="nearest").astype(np.float32)

tip_contacts(tips: ndarray, pose: ndarray, verts: ndarray, tree: cKDTree, threshold: float) -> tuple[ndarray, ndarray, ndarray]

Fingertips (T, 5, 3) vs the object: distance to the nearest of its surface points verts (tree over them; :class:~eden.extensions.retargeting.flashdexretarget.clips.ObjectMeshes surface) (T, 5), contact flags (distance < threshold, dilated by one frame), and that point in the object frame (T, 5, 3).

Source code in eden/extensions/retargeting/flashdexretarget/pack.py 
def tip_contacts(
    tips: np.ndarray, pose: np.ndarray, verts: np.ndarray, tree: cKDTree, threshold: float
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Fingertips (T, 5, 3) vs the object: distance to the nearest of its surface points ``verts`` (``tree`` over
    them; :class:`~eden.extensions.retargeting.flashdexretarget.clips.ObjectMeshes` ``surface``) (T, 5), contact
    flags (distance < threshold, dilated by one frame), and that point in the object frame (T, 5, 3).
    """
    rot, pos = pose[:, :3, :3], pose[:, :3, 3]
    local = np.einsum("tji,tkj->tki", rot, tips - pos[:, None])  # R^T (tip - p)
    dist, idx = tree.query(local.reshape(-1, 3))
    dist = dist.reshape(local.shape[:2]).astype(np.float32)
    near = dist < threshold
    flags = near.copy()
    flags[1:] |= near[:-1]
    flags[:-1] |= near[1:]
    return dist, flags.astype(np.float32), verts[idx].reshape(local.shape).astype(np.float32)

def load_clip(path: Path, meshes: C.ObjectMeshes, fps: float, cfg) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    clip = C.load_clip(path)
    dt, sigma = 1.0 / fps, cfg.vel_sigma
    qpos = clip["qpos"].astype(np.float32)
    T = len(qpos)
    if T < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"{path.name}: needs at least 2 frames")
    sides = C.sides(clip)
    if not sides:
        raise ValueError(f"{path.name}: no mano_right_* / mano_left_* arrays")
    d = {"joint_pos": qpos, "joint_vel": velocity(qpos, dt, sigma)}
    meta: dict = {"sides": sides, "support": clip.get("support_disks")}
    tip_cols = [C.MANO_JOINT_NAMES.index(f"{f}_tip") for f in C.FINGERS]
    for s in sides:
        joints = C.joints(clip, s).astype(np.float32)
        wrist_pos = clip[f"mano_{s}_wrist_pos"].astype(np.float32)
        wrist_rot = clip[f"mano_{s}_wrist_rot"].astype(np.float32)
        pose = C.obj_pose(clip, s)
        for key, arr in (
            ("mano_joints", joints),
            ("wrist_pos", wrist_pos),
            ("wrist_rot", wrist_rot),
            ("obj_pose", pose),
        ):
            if len(arr) != T:
                raise ValueError(f"{path.name}: {s} {key} has {len(arr)} frames, qpos {T}")
        obj_id, scale = C.obj_id(clip, s), C.obj_scale(clip, s)
        mass = float(clip[f"obj_{s}_mass"]) if f"obj_{s}_mass" in clip else 0.0
        d[f"mano_{s}_wrist_pos"] = wrist_pos
        d[f"mano_{s}_wrist_rot"] = wrist_rot
        d[f"mano_{s}_wrist_vel"] = velocity(wrist_pos, dt, sigma)
        d[f"mano_{s}_wrist_angvel"] = angular_velocity(wrist_rot.astype(np.float64), dt, sigma)
        d[f"mano_{s}_joints"] = joints
        d[f"mano_{s}_joints_vel"] = velocity(joints, dt, sigma)
        d[f"obj_{s}_pos"] = pose[:, :3, 3].astype(np.float32)
        d[f"obj_{s}_rotmat"] = pose[:, :3, :3].astype(np.float32)
        d[f"obj_{s}_vel"] = velocity(pose[:, :3, 3], dt, sigma)
        d[f"obj_{s}_angvel"] = angular_velocity(pose[:, :3, :3], dt, sigma)
        mesh = meshes.get(obj_id, scale)
        dist, flags, local = tip_contacts(
            joints[:, tip_cols].astype(np.float64), pose, mesh["surface"], mesh["tree"], cfg.contact_threshold
        )
        d[f"tips_distance_{s}"] = dist
        d[f"contact_contact_{s}"] = flags
        d[f"contact_contact_pos_full_{s}"] = local
        meta[s] = (obj_id, scale, mass)
    return d, meta

def joint_names(robot: str, sides: tuple[str, ...]) -> list[str]:
    """The robot MJCF's joints in qpos order: the columns of ``joint_pos``."""
    m = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path(str(robot_xml(robot, sides)))
    if m.nq != m.njnt:
        raise ValueError(f"{robot_xml(robot, sides)} has a joint with several qpos entries; joint_pos needs one each.")
    return [m.joint(j).name for j in np.argsort(m.jnt_qposadr)]

def build(clips: Path, dataset: Path, motion: Path, fps: float, cfg, robot: str, keys: dict[str, dict]) -> None:
    """Pack the retargeted clips of ``keys`` (clip name -> its
    :func:`~eden.extensions.retargeting.flashdexretarget.retarget.cache_key`) into ``motion`` (cfg: pack). Its object
    mesh directories are relative to ``motion``'s directory (``../objects/<id>`` for ``<dataset>/<robot>/motion.pt``).
    """
    files = _files(clips, keys)
    out = Path(motion).resolve()
    meshes = C.ObjectMeshes(dataset)
    rows, metas = [], []
    for f in files:
        d, m = load_clip(f, meshes, fps, cfg)
        rows.append(d)
        metas.append(m)
        en.logger.debug(f"[pack] {f.stem}: {len(d['joint_pos'])} frames, objects {[m[s] for s in m['sides']]}")
    sides = metas[0]["sides"]
    bad = [f.name for f, m in zip(files, metas) if m["sides"] != sides]
    if bad:
        raise ValueError(f"every clip needs the same hand sides {sides}; differs: {bad[:5]}")

    packed: dict = {k: torch.from_numpy(np.concatenate([r[k] for r in rows])) for k in rows[0]}
    frames = torch.tensor([len(r["joint_pos"]) for r in rows], dtype=torch.long)
    packed["motion_num_frames"] = frames
    packed["length_starts"] = torch.cumsum(frames, 0) - frames
    packed["motion_filename"] = [f.stem for f in files]
    for s in sides:
        packed[f"mano_{s}_joint_names"] = list(C.MANO_JOINT_NAMES)
    packed["robot"], packed["fps"] = robot, float(fps)
    packed["joint_names"] = joint_names(robot, sides)
    if len(packed["joint_names"]) != packed["joint_pos"].shape[1]:
        raise ValueError(
            f"joint_pos has {packed['joint_pos'].shape[1]} columns but {robot}'s MJCF for {sides} has "
            f"{len(packed['joint_names'])} joints."
        )

    # One object slot per distinct (right, left) object pair; a single-hand file has one per object.
    slots: dict[tuple, int] = {}
    slot_of = [slots.setdefault(tuple(m[s] for s in sides), len(slots)) for m in metas]
    for i, s in enumerate(sides):
        packed[f"{s}_object_mesh_dirs"] = [
            _relative(Path(dataset) / "objects" / key[i][0], out.parent) for key in slots
        ]
        packed[f"{s}_object_mesh_scales"] = [key[i][1] for key in slots]
        if any(key[i][2] > 0 for key in slots):
            packed[f"{s}_object_masses"] = [key[i][2] for key in slots]
        packed[f"motion_object_slot_{s}"] = torch.tensor(slot_of, dtype=torch.long)

    disks = [m["support"] for m in metas]
    if any(x is not None for x in disks):
        k = max(len(x) for x in disks if x is not None)
        table = np.zeros((len(rows), k, 5), np.float32)
        for i, x in enumerate(disks):
            if x is not None and len(x):
                table[i, : len(x)] = x
        packed["support_disks"] = torch.from_numpy(table)

    # Through a file of this process's own: an interrupted save never leaves a truncated motion.pt for the SDF step and
    # the training task to load.
    tmp = out.with_name(f"{out.name}.{os.getpid()}.tmp")
    torch.save(packed, tmp)
    os.replace(tmp, out)
    en.logger.info(f"[pack] {len(rows)} clips, {int(frames.sum())} frames, {len(slots)} object slots -> {out}")

def object_meshes(packed: dict, root: Path) -> list[tuple[Path, float]]:
    """Unique (visual.obj, scale) pairs a motion.pt references, in slot order; ``root`` is the motion.pt's directory,
    which its mesh directories are relative to.
    """
    seen: set[tuple[str, float]] = set()
    out: list[tuple[Path, float]] = []
    for side in ("right", "left"):
        dirs = list(packed.get(f"{side}_object_mesh_dirs") or [])
        scales = list(packed.get(f"{side}_object_mesh_scales") or [1.0] * len(dirs))
        if not dirs and packed.get(f"{side}_object_mesh_dir"):
            dirs, scales = [packed[f"{side}_object_mesh_dir"]], [packed.get(f"{side}_object_mesh_scale", 1.0)]
        for rel, scale in zip(dirs, scales):
            key = (str(rel), float(scale))
            if key not in seen:
                seen.add(key)
                out.append((Path(os.path.normpath(Path(root) / str(rel) / "visual.obj")), float(scale)))
    return out

def get(self, oid: str, scale: float = 1.0) -> dict:
    key = (oid, float(scale))
    if key not in self._cache:
        path = self.pool / "objects" / oid / "visual.obj"
        mesh = trimesh.load(path, force="mesh", process=False, skip_materials=True)
        mesh.apply_scale(scale)
        verts = np.asarray(mesh.vertices, dtype=np.float64)
        com = mesh.center_mass if mesh.is_watertight else verts.mean(0)
        surface, _ = trimesh.remesh.subdivide_to_size(verts, mesh.faces, max_edge=SURFACE_SPACING, max_iter=30)
        self._cache[key] = {
            "verts": verts,
            "surface": surface,
            "tree": cKDTree(surface),
            "hull": np.asarray(mesh.convex_hull.vertices, dtype=np.float64),
            "com": np.asarray(com, dtype=np.float64),
        }
    return self._cache[key]

def mano_reference(
    joints: np.ndarray, verts: np.ndarray, global_rot: np.ndarray, side: str
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """MANO layer output -> the clip's hand arrays.

    Parameters
    ----------
    joints : np.ndarray
        (T, 16, 3) MANO joints.
    verts : np.ndarray
        (T, 778, 3) MANO vertices.
    global_rot : np.ndarray
        (T, 3, 3) MANO global orientation.
    side : str
        ``right`` or ``left``.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
        Wrist position (T, 3), wrist rotation rebased to the robot palm frame (T, 3, 3), and the 20 named joints
        (T, 20, 3) in :data:`MANO_JOINT_NAMES` order, tips taken from
        :data:`eden.datasets.utils.body_model.CHORD_TIP_VERTICES`.
    """
    # Imported here: importing eden.datasets loads every dataset module, which only the import step needs.
    from eden.datasets.utils.body_model import CHORD_TIP_VERTICES

    first_joint = {"index": 1, "middle": 4, "pinky": 7, "ring": 10, "thumb": 13}
    wrist = joints[:, 0]
    named = {}
    for finger, j in first_joint.items():
        for k, part in enumerate(("proximal", "intermediate", "distal")):
            named[f"{finger}_{part}"] = joints[:, j + k]
        named[f"{finger}_tip"] = verts[:, CHORD_TIP_VERTICES[finger]]
    joints20 = np.stack([named[n] for n in MANO_JOINT_NAMES], axis=1)
    rebase = np.array([[-1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 1], [0, 1, 0]], dtype=np.float64)
    if side == "left":
        rebase = rebase @ np.diag([-1.0, -1.0, 1.0])
    rot = np.asarray(global_rot, dtype=np.float64) @ rebase
    return wrist.astype(np.float32), rot.astype(np.float32), joints20.astype(np.float32)

@contextlib.contextmanager
def single_threaded_workers() -> Iterator[None]:
    """Each of :data:`THREAD_VARS` the caller has not set is ``1`` while worker processes start inside, then removed
    again: a fresh worker process reads them as it loads numpy (or OpenMP), so N workers keep to N cores, and the
    caller's own environment is left as it was.
    """
    added = [v for v in THREAD_VARS if v not in os.environ]
    os.environ.update(dict.fromkeys(added, "1"))
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        for v in added:
            os.environ.pop(v, None)

workers processes for the CPU steps (preprocess, IK), each with one BLAS / OpenMP thread.

They fork from a forkserver, a fresh process that imports :data:WORKER_MODULES once under :func:single_threaded_workers, not from this one: a fork of this process would keep its thread pools as they are (numpy's sized to every core), and a spawned worker would spend seconds importing Eden. @contextlib.contextmanager
def worker_pool(workers: int) -> Iterator[ProcessPoolExecutor]:
    """``workers`` processes for the CPU steps (preprocess, IK), each with one BLAS / OpenMP thread.

    They fork from a ``forkserver``, a fresh process that imports :data:`WORKER_MODULES` once under
    :func:`single_threaded_workers`, not from this one: a fork of this process would keep its thread pools as they
    are (numpy's sized to every core), and a spawned worker would spend seconds importing Eden. The server lives as
    long as this process, so the thread counts are the ones of the first pool.
    """
    ctx = mp.get_context("forkserver")
    ctx.set_forkserver_preload(list(WORKER_MODULES))
    with single_threaded_workers(), ProcessPoolExecutor(workers, mp_context=ctx) as ex:
        yield ex

def features(clip: dict, meshes: C.ObjectMeshes, cfg, fps: float) -> dict:
    """Per-clip quantities the reject rules test; cfg: the filters config. Heights are of an object's lowest
    hull point above the lowest disk top; the floor and the disks under its centre of mass support it.
    """
    n = cfg.edge_frames
    disks = [d for d in np.asarray(clip.get("support_disks", np.zeros((0, 5)))).reshape(-1, 5) if d[3] > 0]
    z_desk = min(d[2] for d in disks) if disks else 0.0
    T = C.num_frames(clip)
    out: dict = {"frames": T, "seconds": T / fps, "disks": len(disks)}
    acc = [0.0]
    for s in C.sides(clip):
        w = _smooth(clip[f"mano_{s}_wrist_pos"].astype(np.float64), cfg.wrist_acc_spike.smooth)
        speed = np.linalg.norm(np.diff(w, axis=0), axis=1) * fps
        if len(speed) > 1:
            acc.append(float(np.abs(np.diff(speed)).max() * fps))
    out["wrist_acc_max"] = max(acc)
    offdisk, z_first, z_last, first_sup = 0, np.inf, np.inf, 1.0
    for s in C.objects(clip):
        mesh = meshes.get(C.obj_id(clip, s), C.obj_scale(clip, s))
        pose = C.obj_pose(clip, s)
        p, com = pose[:, :3, 3], np.einsum("tij,j->ti", pose[:, :3, :3], mesh["com"]) + pose[:, :3, 3]
        bottom = _bottom(mesh["hull"], pose)
        oz, on_floor = bottom - z_desk, bottom < cfg.contact
        supported = on_floor.copy()
        for x, y, _, r, _ in disks:
            supported |= np.hypot(com[:, 0] - x, com[:, 1] - y) < r
        free = ~_touched(clip, s, meshes, cfg.contact)
        low = free & (oz < cfg.obj_offdisk_untouched.max_height)  # higher up, an untouched object is held anyway
        offdisk = max(offdisk, int((low & ~supported).sum()))
        sunk = free & ~on_floor
        if sunk[:n].any():
            z_first = min(z_first, float(oz[:n][sunk[:n]].mean()))
        if sunk[-n:].any():
            z_last = min(z_last, float(oz[-n:][sunk[-n:]].mean()))
        sup = [
            _supported(
                mesh["hull"] @ pose[t, :3, :3].T + p[t],
                com[t],
                cfg.first_unsupported.base_band,
                cfg.first_unsupported.slack,
            )
            for t in range(min(n, T))
            if low[t]
        ]
        first_sup = min(first_sup, float(np.mean(sup)) if sup else 1.0)
    out.update(
        obj_offdisk_untouched_frames=offdisk,
        obj_z_first=float(z_first),
        obj_z_last=float(z_last),
        first_supported=first_sup,
    )
    return out

def reject_reasons(f: dict, cfg) -> list[str]:
    failed = {
        "obj_offdisk_untouched": f["obj_offdisk_untouched_frames"] >= cfg.obj_offdisk_untouched.frames,
        "wrist_acc_spike": f["wrist_acc_max"] > cfg.wrist_acc_spike.max_acc,
        "obj_below_desk": min(f["obj_z_first"], f["obj_z_last"]) < cfg.obj_below_desk.min_z,
        "too_short": f["seconds"] < cfg.too_short.min_sec,
        "first_unsupported": f["first_supported"] < 1.0,
    }
    return [rule for rule, bad in failed.items() if bad]

def flags(clip: dict, robot: str, pool, cfg, fps: float) -> dict:
    """Clip carries qpos (T, nq of the robot MJCF) aligned with its other arrays; cfg: retarget."""
    th = cfg.quality
    sides = C.sides(clip)
    objects = {s: (C.obj_id(clip, s), C.obj_scale(clip, s)) for s in sides}
    disks = np.asarray(clip.get("support_disks", np.zeros((0, 5)))).reshape(-1, 5)
    m = S.build(robot, sides, objects, pool, cfg.scene, disks, shared=C.shared_object(clip)).compile()
    d = mujoco.MjData(m)
    qpos = clip["qpos"]
    T, nq_robot = len(qpos), qpos.shape[1]
    z_desk = float(disks[:, 2].min()) if len(disks) else 0.0
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

    hand = {s: [] for s in sides}
    for g in range(m.ngeom):
        name = m.geom(g).name
        if name.startswith("collision_hand_") and m.geom_type[g] == mujoco.mjtGeom.mjGEOM_MESH:
            s = "left" if "left" in name else "right"
            if s in hand:
                mid = m.geom_dataid[g]
                v = m.mesh_vert[m.mesh_vertadr[mid] : m.mesh_vertadr[mid] + m.mesh_vertnum[mid]]
                hand[s].append((g, v[rng.choice(len(v), min(60, len(v)), replace=False)]))
    hand_ids = {g for g in range(m.ngeom) if m.geom(g).name.startswith("collision_hand_")}
    where = S.robot_xml(robot, sides)

    def find(objtype: mujoco.mjtObj, name: str) -> int:  # a missing name raises: -1 would read the last element
        return S.name_id(m, objtype, name, where)

    desk_ids = {find(mujoco.mjtObj.mjOBJ_GEOM, f"support_{k}") for k in range(len(disks))}
    obj_ids = {g for g in range(m.ngeom) if "_object_" in m.geom(g).name}
    tip_sites = {s: [find(mujoco.mjtObj.mjOBJ_SITE, f"{s}_{t}") for t in TIPS] for s in sides}
    mano_tips = {s: C.tips(clip, s) for s in sides}

    palm_body = {s: find(mujoco.mjtObj.mjOBJ_BODY, f"{s[0].upper()}_forearm_rot_y_link") for s in sides}
    palm = {s: np.zeros((T, 3)) for s in sides}
    tip_err, below_out, desk_pen, obj_pen = [], np.zeros(T), np.zeros(T), np.zeros(T)
    for t in range(T):
        d.qpos[:nq_robot] = qpos[t]
        for i, s in enumerate(sides):
            pose = C.obj_pose(clip, s)[t]
            q = np.zeros(4)
            mujoco.mju_mat2Quat(q, pose[:3, :3].reshape(-1))
            d.qpos[nq_robot + 7 * i : nq_robot + 7 * i + 7] = np.concatenate([pose[:3, 3], q])
        mujoco.mj_forward(m, d)
        for s in sides:
            palm[s][t] = d.xpos[palm_body[s]]
        tip_err.append(
            np.concatenate([np.linalg.norm(d.site_xpos[tip_sites[s]] - mano_tips[s][t], axis=1) for s in sides])
        )
        for c in d.contact[: d.ncon]:
            g1, g2, depth = c.geom1, c.geom2, max(0.0, -float(c.dist))
            pair = {g1, g2}
            if pair & hand_ids and pair & obj_ids:
                obj_pen[t] = max(obj_pen[t], depth)
            elif pair & hand_ids and pair & desk_ids:
                desk_pen[t] = max(desk_pen[t], depth)
        if len(disks):
            pts = np.concatenate(
                [v @ d.geom_xmat[g].reshape(3, 3).T + d.geom_xpos[g] for s in sides for g, v in hand[s]]
            )
            on = np.zeros(len(pts), dtype=bool)
            for x, y, _, r, _ in disks:
                on |= np.hypot(pts[:, 0] - x, pts[:, 1] - y) < r + 0.02
            if (~on).any():
                below_out[t] = max(0.0, float((z_desk - pts[~on, 2]).max()))
    tip_err = np.asarray(tip_err)
    acc = [0.0]
    for s in sides:
        v = np.linalg.norm(np.diff(palm[s], axis=0), axis=1) * fps
        if len(v) > 1:
            acc.append(float(np.abs(np.diff(v)).max() * fps))
    out = {
        "palm_acc_max": max(acc),
        "tip_err_median_m": float(np.median(tip_err)),
        "tip_far_frac": float((tip_err > th.tip_tracking.max_dist).mean()),
        "hand_below_desk_outside_max_m": float(below_out.max()),
        "hand_obj_pen_max_m": float(obj_pen.max()),
        "hand_desk_pen_frames": int(
            (desk_pen[th.hand_desk_penetration.after :] > th.hand_desk_penetration.max_depth).sum()
        ),
    }
    flagged = {
        "palm_acc_spike": out["palm_acc_max"] > th.palm_acc_spike.max_acc,
        "hand_far_below_desk": out["hand_below_desk_outside_max_m"] > th.hand_far_below_desk.max_depth,
        "tip_tracking": out["tip_far_frac"] > th.tip_tracking.max_frac,
        "hand_obj_penetration": out["hand_obj_pen_max_m"] > th.hand_obj_penetration.max_depth,
        "hand_desk_penetration": out["hand_desk_pen_frames"] >= th.hand_desk_penetration.frames,
    }
    out["flags"] = ";".join(name for name, bad in flagged.items() if bad)
    return out

docs.title: Scripted Demonstrations
docs.text:
Scripted demonstrators produce demo-like trajectories, the kind a person teleoperating would record: smooth minimum-jerk-timed motion through randomized keyframes, a per-episode speed, pauses, off-centre grasps, retries and deliberate mistakes the demonstrator recovers from. They are a port of OCBench's scripted policies onto Eden's batched envs. SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY says which demonstrator drives which task, and generate_demos (what eden datagen runs) rolls one out in parallel envs and records every episode. The scripted demonstrations guide covers eden datagen and writing a demonstrator.

from eden.extensions.scripted_demos.generate import generate_demos
from eden.extensions.scripted_demos.registry import SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY

docs.title: Generation and registry
docs.text:
Roll a task's scripted demonstrator out in parallel envs and record every episode (eden datagen).

OCBench's data_gen_scripts/generate_ocbench.py, on Eden's recorder: the env records itself (:class:~eden.managers.recorder_manager.RecorderManager), so a demonstration is written in the same HDF5 layout as a teleoperated one and eden lerobot convert reads either.

A demonstrator is either a keyframe controller (:class:~eden.extensions.scripted_demos.controller.ScriptedPickPlaceController) or a tool routine (:class:~eden.extensions.scripted_demos.routines.RoutineDemonstrator, or one per arm composed by a :class:~eden.extensions.scripted_demos.multi_arm.MultiArmDemonstrator); all expose reset / update_subgoals / act. A two-arm task records both arms' state, side by side. A routine demonstrator also keeps a per-episode trace, and the report carries the first failed episode's — the place to start when the success rate is low.

An episode ends when the demonstrator has finished the task — its success is the task's own success metric at that step — or when the env ends it (time limit, an object off the table). Every ended episode is exported with its success flag; export_mode decides whether the failed ones are kept. Generation stops once num_episodes have ended; the episodes still running then are dropped rather than written cut short.

Which scripted demonstrator drives which task: SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY, keyed by task name.

An entry is a factory (env, *, seed, p_mistake) -> demonstrator — a keyframe :class:~eden.extensions.scripted_demos.controller.ScriptedPickPlaceController, a tool-routine :class:~eden.extensions.scripted_demos.routines.RoutineDemonstrator, or a two-arm :class:~eden.extensions.scripted_demos.multi_arm.MultiArmDemonstrator — registered under the task's :data:~eden.tasks.registry.TASK_REGISTRY name, next to the task it scripts (eden/tasks/<suite>/scripted_demos.py) — list that module in populated_by below. A factory that also takes privileged has a camera-only mode (eden datagen --camera_only), and one whose episodes need longer than the generator's default declares an episode_length_s attribute.

def recorder_options(
    output_dir: str, filename: str, export_mode: DatasetExportMode, *, state_entity: str | list[str]
) -> RecorderManagerOptions:
    """What a demonstration records: observations, actions, rewards / dones / timestamps, the arm's state, and each
    episode's initial state.

    ``obs/<group>`` and ``action`` are the behavior-cloning pairs; ``state/*`` is ``state_entity``'s
    joint and root state — every arm's, concatenated in order, when it lists several — which
    ``eden lerobot convert`` reads as ``observation.state``; ``initial_state`` lets an episode be
    replayed from its first frame.
    """
    return RecorderManagerOptions(
        file_handler_options=HDF5FileHandler.configure(),
        dataset_export_dir_path=output_dir,
        dataset_filename=filename,
        dataset_export_mode=export_mode,
        override=True,
        observations=ObservationRecorder.configure(),
        actions=ActionRecorder.configure(),
        rl_step=RLStepRecorder.configure(),
        state=StateRecorder.configure(entity_name=state_entity),
        initial_state=InitialStateRecorder.configure(),
    )

def generate_demos(
    config: EdenRLConfig,
    task_name: str,
    *,
    num_episodes: int,
    output_dir: str,
    filename: str = "demos",
    export_mode: DatasetExportMode = DatasetExportMode.EXPORT_ALL,
    seed: int = 0,
    p_mistake: float | None = None,
    episode_length_s: float | None = None,
    camera_only: bool = False,
    show_viewer: bool = False,
) -> GenerationReport:
    """Generate ``num_episodes`` scripted demonstrations of ``task_name`` into ``output_dir/filename``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    config : EdenRLConfig
        The task config (mods applied); its recorder options and episode length are replaced.
    task_name : str
        Key of the task's demonstrator in :data:`~eden.extensions.scripted_demos.registry.SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY`.
    num_episodes : int
        Episodes to end before stopping.
    output_dir, filename : str
        Where the dataset goes (``filename`` without extension).
    export_mode : DatasetExportMode
        Keep every episode, the successful ones only, or both in separate files. Not
        ``EXPORT_NONE``: successes are counted off what is exported.
    seed : int
        Seeds the env and the demonstrator.
    p_mistake : float, optional
        Probability a subgoal is a deliberate mistake; the demonstrator's default when None.
    episode_length_s : float, optional
        Time limit [s] of an episode; the demonstrator's own ``episode_length_s`` (or
        :data:`DEFAULT_EPISODE_LENGTH_S`) when None.
    camera_only : bool
        Run the demonstrator without the simulator's object state (``privileged=False``): it sees
        through the task's cameras, which then render every env (``env_separate_rigid``). Only
        demonstrators that take a ``privileged`` argument can.
    show_viewer : bool
        Open the Genesis viewer.

    Returns
    -------
    GenerationReport
        Counts and where the dataset went.
    """
    if export_mode == DatasetExportMode.EXPORT_NONE:
        raise ValueError("export_mode=EXPORT_NONE would generate demonstrations and write none of them.")
    if num_episodes <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"num_episodes must be a positive integer, got {num_episodes}.")
    if task_name not in SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY:
        available = ", ".join(sorted(SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY.keys())) or "none"
        raise KeyError(
            f"Task '{task_name}' has no scripted demonstrator. Tasks with one: {available}. A demonstrator is a factory "
            f"registered in SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY under the task's name (see eden/tasks/robosuite/scripted_demos.py)."
        )
    from eden.envs.base import env_class_for_config

    factory = SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY.get(task_name)
    factory_kwargs = {"seed": seed}
    if p_mistake is not None:
        factory_kwargs["p_mistake"] = p_mistake
    if camera_only:
        if "privileged" not in inspect.signature(factory).parameters:
            camera_capable = sorted(
                name  # the registry iterates (name, factory) pairs
                for name, candidate in SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY
                if "privileged" in inspect.signature(candidate).parameters
            )
            raise ValueError(
                f"Task '{task_name}''s demonstrator reads the simulator's object state and has no camera-only mode; "
                f"tasks that do: {camera_capable or 'none'}. Drop --camera_only for this task."
            )
        factory_kwargs["privileged"] = False
        if config.env_options.num_envs > 1 and not config.env_options.env_separate_rigid:
            # A camera shared by the envs renders env 0 only; a camera-only demonstrator would see one scene everywhere.
            config.env_options.env_separate_rigid = True
            en.logger.info("--camera_only: rendering every env's own view (env_options.env_separate_rigid = True).")
    if episode_length_s is None:
        episode_length_s = getattr(factory, "episode_length_s", DEFAULT_EPISODE_LENGTH_S)
    if not episode_length_s > 0:
        raise ValueError(f"episode_length_s must be a positive number of seconds, got {episode_length_s}.")
    config.env_options.episode_length_s = episode_length_s
    arms = [rig.arm_name for rig in find_gripper_rigs(config.scene_options)]
    if not arms:
        raise TypeError(
            f"Task '{task_name}' holds no arm + two-finger gripper a scripted demonstrator could drive; scene entities: "
            f"{list(config.scene_options.keys())}."
        )
    state_entity = arms[0] if len(arms) == 1 else arms
    config.recorder_options = recorder_options(output_dir, filename, export_mode, state_entity=state_entity)
    env = env_class_for_config(config).from_config(config, show_viewer=show_viewer, eval_mode=True)
    env.build()
    env.reset(seed=seed)
    if env.metric_manager is None or not hasattr(env.metric_manager, "success_buf"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"Task '{task_name}' declares no success metric, so a generated episode cannot be labelled; give it a "
            f"metric term with contributes_to_success=True."
        )

    controller = factory(env, **factory_kwargs)
    controller.reset()

    recorder = env.recorder_manager
    report = GenerationReport(dataset_path=recorder_dataset_path(config.recorder_options))
    episode_steps = torch.zeros(env.num_envs, dtype=torch.long, device=env.device)
    # The generator's own time limit: a task need not declare a time_out termination (SIMPLER's
    # declare none), and a demonstrator that cannot finish must not hold its env forever.
    max_episode_steps = math.ceil(episode_length_s / env.dt)
    # Successful episodes exported per env so far: an env-ended episode's success is read off the
    # exporter, since the env clears its success buffer when it resets the env inside the step.
    exported_successes = [0] * env.num_envs
    recorder.start_recording()
    start = time.time()
    try:
        while report.episodes < num_episodes:
            done = controller.update_subgoals()
            timed_out = (episode_steps >= max_episode_steps) & ~done
            report.cut_short += int(timed_out.sum())
            ending = done | timed_out
            if bool(ending.any()):
                recorder.set_episode_success(ending, env.metric_manager.success_buf[ending])
                _keep_failure_trace(report, controller, ending & ~env.metric_manager.success_buf)
                _tally(report, ending, episode_steps)
                env.reset(ending)
                _count_exported_successes(recorder, ending, exported_successes)
                controller.reset(ending)
                episode_steps[ending] = 0
                if report.episodes >= num_episodes:
                    break

            try:
                env.step(controller.act())
            except gs.GenesisException as error:
                if "not finite" not in str(error) or not config.env_options.use_gjk_collision:
                    raise
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"Genesis's GJK narrowphase produced a non-finite contact while generating '{task_name}' demos. "
                    f"Thin convex collision geoms (a WidowX's finger pads, say) pressed against an object trigger "
                    f"it, so a long scripted rollout eventually does. Rerun with MPR collision: eden datagen "
                    f"--task {task_name} --override 'env_options: {{use_gjk_collision: false}}'. Catching this "
                    f"and resetting the env does not help: the solver state of every env is invalid after it."
                ) from error
            episode_steps += 1

            ended = env.reset_buf
            if bool(ended.any()):  # the env has already reset these, and exported them with their success
                succeeded = _count_exported_successes(recorder, ended, exported_successes)
                report.cut_short += int((ended & ~succeeded).sum())
                _keep_failure_trace(report, controller, ended & ~succeeded)
                _tally(report, ended, episode_steps)
                controller.reset(ended)
                episode_steps[ended] = 0
    finally:
        recorder.end_recording(export_unfinished=False)
        # Counted by the exporter: the env clears its success buffer when it resets an env, so the
        # flag an env-ended episode carried survives only in what was exported.
        report.successes = recorder.exported_successful_episode_count
        recorder.close()
    report.wall_s = time.time() - start
    report.subgoals = dict(controller.subgoal_counts)
    en.logger.info(f"Scripted demos for '{task_name}': {report.render()}")
    if report.failure_trace:
        en.logger.info("Trace of the first unsuccessful episode:\n" + "\n".join(report.failure_trace))
    return report

docs.title: Keyframe trajectories and pick-and-place primitives
docs.text:
Batched keyframe trajectories with demo-like timing: the motion layer of OCBench's scripted policies.

Port of ocbench/oracles/primitives/primitive.py (Primitive._compute_smooth_plan, _smooth_keyframe_times, current_plan_action), vectorized over environments.

A primitive samples a handful of keyframes — tool poses, times and a gripper value — and the trajectory between them is what makes a scripted rollout read like a human demonstration rather than a rule-based controller:

  • Position follows a cubic Hermite spline. The tangent is zero at stop keyframes (where a person pauses: before closing the gripper, at the place pose, at the end) and passes through the others at the neighbours' average velocity, clamped to 1.25x the faster neighbouring segment.
  • Rotation and gripper ease with the quintic smoothstep u^3 (10 - 15u + 6u^2).
  • Timing is stretched so no segment exceeds a peak speed: a minimum-jerk profile peaks at 1.875 d / T, so a segment of length d gets at least T = 1.875 d / v_peak.
  • Gates freeze the plan clock until the tool is within a tolerance of a keyframe, so the plan never runs ahead of an arm that lags behind it.
  • Wobble adds a small sideways bulge 16 u^2 (1 - u)^2 ((1 - u) c_1 + u c_2) to the vertical approach and retreat phases, which a human never executes as a straight line.

Every tensor is batched over environments in the first dimension and lives on the env device; a plan is written for a subset of environments with :meth:KeyframeTrajectory.assign and read for all of them with :meth:KeyframeTrajectory.evaluate.

Demo-like pick-and-place keyframes: a batched port of OCBench's CubePrimitive.

ocbench/oracles/primitives/cube.py (compute_keyframes). One call samples a whole pick -> carry -> place -> retreat plan for a batch of environments. Everything that makes it read like a person rather than a script is sampled per plan:

  • a grasp yaw that is usually the face nearest the current wrist yaw but sometimes a quarter turn off, a wrist tilt of up to 25 deg that carries (attenuated) into the place,
  • approach heights, contact offsets and a slightly off-centre place approach,
  • an optional pause before lifting, and when the fingers close (on arrival or after a beat),
  • a carry midpoint that bows to one side and, a third of the time, overshoots the target,
  • +-3 % jitter on every keyframe time.

A failed pick is retried from wherever the hand is (:attr:PickPlaceRequest.num_retries), and every random offset shrinks by 0.75 per retry — a person is more careful the second time.

Poses here are effector rotations in OCBench's sense — the rotation of a gripper that points straight down when it is the identity — so yaw, roll and pitch read as the wrist's heading and tilt. :func:tool_quat maps one to the tool link's world orientation through the rig's down_quat.

docs.text:
compacted() -> Keyframes

The valid keyframes first, the tail padded with the last valid one (so it adds no motion and no time).

Source code in eden/extensions/scripted_demos/trajectory.py 
def compacted(self) -> Keyframes:
    """The valid keyframes first, the tail padded with the last valid one (so it adds no motion and no time)."""
    num_kf = self.times.shape[1]
    # A stable sort on ``~valid`` keeps the valid keyframes in their authored order.
    order = torch.argsort((~self.valid).to(torch.int8), dim=1, stable=True)
    num_valid = self.valid.sum(dim=1)
    last = (num_valid - 1).clamp(min=0).unsqueeze(1)
    slots = torch.arange(num_kf, device=self.times.device).unsqueeze(0)
    # Tail slots read the last valid keyframe.
    gather = torch.where(slots < num_valid.unsqueeze(1), order, order.gather(1, last))

    def take(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        index = gather.view(*gather.shape, *([1] * (x.dim() - 2))).expand_as(x)
        return x.gather(1, index)

    tail = slots >= num_valid.unsqueeze(1)
    return Keyframes(
        times=take(self.times),
        pos=take(self.pos),
        quat=take(self.quat),
        grasp=take(self.grasp),
        stop=take(self.stop) | tail,
        valid=~tail,
    )

Every invalid keyframe replaced by the last valid one before it (time, pose and grasp).

Keeps the authored layout, so a primitive can still read a keyframe's time by its slot after :meth:retimed — an invalid slot then reports its predecessor's time.

Source code in eden/extensions/scripted_demos/trajectory.py 
def filled(self) -> Keyframes:
    """Every invalid keyframe replaced by the last valid one before it (time, pose and grasp).

    Keeps the authored layout, so a primitive can still read a keyframe's time by its slot
    after :meth:`retimed` — an invalid slot then reports its predecessor's time.
    """
    num_kf = self.times.shape[1]
    slots = torch.arange(num_kf, device=self.times.device).expand_as(self.times)
    source = torch.where(self.valid, slots, 0).cummax(dim=1).values

    def take(x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return x.gather(1, source.view(*source.shape, *([1] * (x.dim() - 2))).expand_as(x))

    return Keyframes(take(self.times), take(self.pos), take(self.quat), take(self.grasp), self.stop, self.valid)

retimed(peak_speed: Tensor) -> Keyframes

Stretch every segment that would exceed peak_speed ((B,) m/s) under a minimum-jerk profile.

OCBench Primitive._smooth_keyframe_times. Expects a :meth:filled or :meth:compacted plan, where an unused keyframe duplicates a used one: zero length and zero duration, so it stays put and the segments around it are timed as if it were absent.

Source code in eden/extensions/scripted_demos/trajectory.py 
def retimed(self, peak_speed: torch.Tensor) -> Keyframes:
    """Stretch every segment that would exceed ``peak_speed`` (``(B,)`` m/s) under a minimum-jerk profile.

    OCBench ``Primitive._smooth_keyframe_times``. Expects a :meth:`filled` or :meth:`compacted`
    plan, where an unused keyframe duplicates a used one: zero length and zero duration, so it
    stays put and the segments around it are timed as if it were absent.
    """
    dt = self.times.diff(dim=1)
    dist = (self.pos[:, 1:] - self.pos[:, :-1]).norm(dim=-1)
    min_dt = MIN_JERK_PEAK_TO_MEAN * dist / peak_speed.unsqueeze(1)
    dt = torch.maximum(dt, min_dt)
    times = torch.cat([self.times[:, :1], self.times[:, :1] + dt.cumsum(dim=1)], dim=1)
    return Keyframes(times, self.pos, self.quat, self.grasp, self.stop, self.valid)
