A parameter drives one of the per-DOF solver fields (damping, armature, stiffness, frictionloss) or one of the per-DOF PD gains (kp, kd) on the entity named entity_name for the listed dof_names.

def __init__(
    self,
    name: str,
    property: DofProperty,
    dof_names: Sequence[str],
    entity_name: str = "robot",
    per_dof: bool = False,
    nominal: float | Sequence[float] = 0.0,
    min_value: float | Sequence[float] = 0.0,
    max_value: float | Sequence[float] = 1.0,
    frozen: bool = False,
) -> None:
    if not dof_names:
        raise ValueError(f"Parameter '{name}' must target at least one DOF.")

    self.name = name
    self.property = property
    self.entity_name = entity_name
    self.dof_names = tuple(dof_names)
    self.per_dof = per_dof
    self.frozen = frozen

    expected_size = len(self.dof_names) if per_dof else 1
    self.nominal = _as_vector(nominal, expected_size, f"{name}.nominal")
    self.min_value = _as_vector(min_value, expected_size, f"{name}.min_value")
    self.max_value = _as_vector(max_value, expected_size, f"{name}.max_value")
    if np.any(self.min_value > self.max_value):
        raise ValueError(f"Parameter '{name}' has min_value > max_value.")
    if np.any(self.nominal < self.min_value) or np.any(self.nominal > self.max_value):
        raise ValueError(f"Parameter '{name}' nominal is outside [min, max].")
    self.value = self.nominal.copy()

def update_from_vector(self, vector: np.ndarray) -> None:
    vector = np.asarray(vector, dtype=np.float64).ravel()
    if vector.size != self.size:
        raise ValueError(f"Expected vector of size {self.size}, got {vector.size}.")
    start = 0
    for p in self:
        if p.frozen:
            continue
        end = start + p.size
        p.value = vector[start:end].reshape(p.nominal.shape).copy()
        start = end

Load a Trajectory from a RecorderManager npz produced by SysIDRecorder.

Reads only the sysid/* key schema. NPZFileHandler writes one or more episodes under demo_{n}/... keys; pass demo="demo_0" to pick a specific episode, or leave it to auto-select the first one. A flat npz whose keys are already under sysid/... (no demo_ prefix) is also supported.

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/trajectory.py 
@classmethod
def from_recorder_episode(
    cls,
    path: str | pathlib.Path,
    dof_names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
    demo: str | None = None,
) -> "Trajectory":
    """Load a Trajectory from a ``RecorderManager`` npz produced by ``SysIDRecorder``.

    Reads only the ``sysid/*`` key schema. ``NPZFileHandler`` writes one or
    more episodes under ``demo_{n}/...`` keys; pass ``demo="demo_0"`` to
    pick a specific episode, or leave it to auto-select the first one.
    A flat npz whose keys are already under ``sysid/...`` (no ``demo_``
    prefix) is also supported.
    """
    with np.load(path, allow_pickle=False) as npz:
        keys = set(npz.files)

        prefix = ""
        flat_stamp = _TIME_KEY
        if flat_stamp not in keys:
            # Recorder-manager output stores episodes under ``demo_N/``.
            demo_names = sorted({k.split("/", 1)[0] for k in keys if k.startswith("demo_")})
            if not demo_names:
                raise ValueError(f"Recorder episode {path} is missing '{_TIME_KEY}'.")
            chosen = demo if demo is not None else demo_names[0]
            if chosen not in demo_names:
                raise ValueError(f"{path} has no episode '{chosen}' (available: {demo_names}).")
            prefix = f"{chosen}/"
            if f"{prefix}{_TIME_KEY}" not in keys:
                raise ValueError(f"Recorder episode {path}:{chosen} is missing '{_TIME_KEY}'.")

        # ``times`` may arrive as (n_steps,), (n_steps, 1), (n_steps, num_envs),
        # or (n_steps, num_envs, 1) depending on which recorder layout produced
        # the npz. Squeeze trailing singletons and pick env 0 explicitly so a
        # blind reshape(-1) can't interleave envs and steps for multi-env runs.
        raw_times = np.asarray(npz[f"{prefix}{_TIME_KEY}"])
        env_axis_size = raw_times.shape[1] if raw_times.ndim >= 2 else 1
        if raw_times.ndim == 1:
            times = raw_times
        elif raw_times.ndim == 2:
            times = raw_times[:, 0] if raw_times.shape[1] >= 1 else raw_times.reshape(-1)
        else:  # ndim >= 3
            times = raw_times[:, 0, 0] if raw_times.shape[1] >= 1 else raw_times.reshape(-1)
        n_steps = int(times.shape[0])

        def _take(key: str) -> np.ndarray | None:
            full = f"{prefix}{key}"
            if full not in keys:
                return None
            arr = np.asarray(npz[full])
            # (n_steps, num_envs, dim) → take env 0; (n_steps, num_envs) where
            # num_envs > 1 → take env 0 column. Single-env (n_steps, 1) layouts
            # fall through unchanged and are 2-D-OK for the Trajectory dataclass.
            if arr.ndim == 3 and arr.shape[0] == n_steps:
                arr = arr[:, 0, :]
            elif arr.ndim == 2 and env_axis_size > 1 and arr.shape == (n_steps, env_axis_size):
                arr = arr[:, 0:1]
            return arr

        kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {"times": times}
        for name, candidates in _SIGNAL_KEYS.items():
            for candidate in candidates:
                arr = _take(candidate)
                if arr is not None:
                    kwargs[name] = arr
                    break
        action = _take(_ACTION_KEY)
        if action is not None:
            kwargs["action"] = action

        initial_state: dict[str, np.ndarray] = {}
        for key in _INITIAL_STATE_KEYS:
            full_key = f"{prefix}sysid/initial_state/{key}"
            if full_key not in keys:
                continue
            arr = np.asarray(npz[full_key])
            if arr.ndim == 2:
                arr = arr[0]
            initial_state[key] = arr
        kwargs["initial_state"] = initial_state

    if dof_names is not None:
        kwargs["dof_names"] = tuple(dof_names)
    return cls(**kwargs)

docs.title: CMAES
docs.text:
CMAES(env: 'EnvBase', options: SystemIdentificationOptions)

Bases: SystemIdentificationBase

CMA-ES identifier for noisy or contact-heavy residuals (e.g. dex hand).

By default evaluates candidates sequentially on the current env — each candidate ask() writes its own parameter vector across all envs and runs one replay per trajectory. This works with any env.num_envs and matches the serial assumption used by SciPyLeastSquares.

To enable batched candidate evaluation set batched=True and build the sysid env with env_options.num_envs == population_size; a single replay then scores the whole population, reducing the per-generation wall-clock by a factor close to the population size.

Extra options

sigma0: float Initial step size in the unit-hypercube reparameterisation. 0.25 explores ~50% of each bound interval on the first generation. population_size: int | None CMA population. Defaults to the library's recommendation 4 + floor(3*log(n)). batched: bool If True, score the whole population in one replay per trajectory; requires env.num_envs == population_size.

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/optimizers/cmaes.py 
def fit(
    self,
    params: ParameterSet,
    trajectories: Sequence[Trajectory],
) -> tuple[ParameterSet, FitResult]:
    try:
        import cma
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover
        raise RuntimeError("CMAES backend requires the 'cma' package.") from exc

    opt_params = params.copy()
    n = opt_params.size
    if n == 0:
        return opt_params, FitResult(cost=0.0, nfev=0, x=np.zeros(0), message="no free parameters")

    lo, hi = opt_params.get_bounds()
    x0 = opt_params.as_vector()
    x0_scaled = _to_unit(x0, lo, hi)

    pop = self.population_size or (4 + int(3 * np.log(max(n, 1))))
    if self.batched and pop != self._env.num_envs:
        raise ValueError(
            f"CMAES(batched=True) requires env.num_envs == population_size "
            f"(got num_envs={self._env.num_envs}, pop={pop})."
        )

    es = cma.CMAEvolutionStrategy(
        x0_scaled,
        self.sigma0,
        {
            "bounds": [[0.0] * n, [1.0] * n],
            "popsize": pop,
            "maxiter": self.max_iters,
            # Quiet cma's internal chatter — we print our own per-generation line below.
            "verbose": -9,
        },
    )

    history: list[float] = []
    score_fn = self._score_batched if self.batched else self._score_serial
    best_ever = float("inf")
    t_start = time.monotonic()
    if self.verbose:
        mode = "batched" if self.batched else "serial"
        en.logger.info(
            f"[CMAES] n_params={n}, popsize={pop}, mode={mode}, "
            f"num_envs={self._env.num_envs}, max_iters={self.max_iters}"
        )
        en.logger.info(f"{'gen':>4}  {'nfev':>7}  {'best':>12}  {'mean':>12}  {'sigma':>10}  {'elapsed':>8}")
    gen = 0
    while not es.stop():
        t_gen = time.monotonic()
        unit_candidates = np.asarray(es.ask())
        candidates = np.stack([_from_unit(c, lo, hi) for c in unit_candidates])
        if self.verbose:
            en.logger.info(
                f"[gen {gen + 1:>3d}] scoring {candidates.shape[0]} candidates "
                f"over {len(trajectories)} trajectories …"
            )
        costs = score_fn(opt_params, candidates, trajectories)
        es.tell(list(unit_candidates), list(costs.tolist()))
        gen_best = float(np.min(costs))
        history.append(gen_best)
        best_ever = min(best_ever, gen_best)
        gen += 1
        if self.verbose:
            gen_dt = time.monotonic() - t_gen
            elapsed = time.monotonic() - t_start
            en.logger.info(
                f"{gen:>4d}  {int(es.result.evaluations):>7d}  "
                f"{best_ever:>12.4g}  {float(np.mean(costs)):>12.4g}  "
                f"{float(es.sigma):>10.4g}  {elapsed:>6.1f}s  (+{gen_dt:.1f}s)"
            )

    best_unit = np.asarray(es.result.xbest)
    best = _from_unit(best_unit, lo, hi)
    opt_params.update_from_vector(best)

    return opt_params, FitResult(
        cost=float(es.result.fbest),
        nfev=int(es.result.evaluations),
        x=best,
        message="cma completed",
        history=np.asarray(history) if history else None,
    )

docs.title: SciPyLeastSquares
docs.text:
SciPyLeastSquares(env: 'EnvBase', options: SystemIdentificationOptions)

Bases: SystemIdentificationBase

Trust-Region Reflective least-squares with box bounds.

Operates on a unit-hypercube reparameterisation of the free parameters — decision variables live in [0, 1] regardless of their physical scale — so the finite-difference Jacobian uses a step of diff_step fraction of each parameter's bound range (not sqrt(eps) of its absolute value, which is below the sim's numerical floor for most solver fields). This is the same reparameterisation the CMA-ES backend uses.

Extra options

diff_step: float Relative FD step in unit space. 1e-2 = 1 % of each bound range. Too small → FD underflows to numerical noise and the optimiser terminates at xtol with no progress; too large → the Jacobian becomes a secant rather than a derivative. parallel_fd: bool If True, write n_params + 1 FD columns into as many envs and score them all in one replay per trajectory via :func:batched_candidate_rollout. Requires env.num_envs == n_params + 1 (the batched rollout writes one candidate per env). When False, scipy's serial 2-point FD is used.

def fit(
    self,
    params: ParameterSet,
    trajectories: Sequence[Trajectory],
) -> tuple[ParameterSet, FitResult]:
    opt_params = params.copy()
    n = opt_params.size
    if n == 0:
        return opt_params, FitResult(cost=0.0, nfev=0, x=np.zeros(0), message="no free parameters")

    lo, hi = opt_params.get_bounds()
    span = np.where(hi > lo, hi - lo, 1.0)
    x0 = opt_params.as_vector()
    x0_unit = np.clip((x0 - lo) / span, 0.0, 1.0)

    def _to_physical(x_unit: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        return lo + np.clip(x_unit, 0.0, 1.0) * span

    def residual_fn(x_unit: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        opt_params.update_from_vector(_to_physical(x_unit))
        return self.evaluate(opt_params, trajectories)

    jac_arg = "2-point"
    K = n + 1  # center + one perturbation per parameter
    if self.parallel_fd:
        if self._env.num_envs != K:
            raise ValueError(
                f"SciPyLeastSquares(parallel_fd=True) requires env.num_envs == {K} "
                f"(got {self._env.num_envs}). Build the sysid env with num_envs = n_params + 1."
            )
        jac_arg = self._build_parallel_jacobian(opt_params, trajectories, lo, span, K)

    result = least_squares(
        residual_fn,
        x0_unit,
        bounds=(np.zeros(n), np.ones(n)),
        max_nfev=self.max_iters,
        verbose=2 if self.verbose else 0,
        x_scale=1.0,
        diff_step=self.diff_step,
        jac=jac_arg,
    )

    x_star = _to_physical(result.x)
    opt_params.update_from_vector(x_star)

    return opt_params, FitResult(
        cost=float(result.cost),
        nfev=int(result.nfev),
        x=x_star,
        jacobian=getattr(result, "jac", None),
        message=str(result.message),
        extras={
            "optimality": float(result.optimality),
            "status": int(result.status),
            "x_unit": np.asarray(result.x),
        },
    )

docs.title: ChirpExcitation
docs.text:
ChirpExcitation(num_dofs: int, dof_indices: Sequence[int], f_start: float, f_end: float, duration: float, amplitude: float | Sequence[float], stagger_phase: float = 0.0)

Bases: Excitation

Linear-swept sine — the canonical sysid input for linear-system ID.

Produces amplitude * sin(2*pi * phase(t)) where the instantaneous frequency ramps from f_start to f_end over duration. When dof_indices lists multiple DOFs, each is phase-shifted by stagger_phase * (idx / num_active) so simultaneous excitation doesn't create degenerate rank-1 inputs.

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/excitation.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    num_dofs: int,
    dof_indices: Sequence[int],
    f_start: float,
    f_end: float,
    duration: float,
    amplitude: float | Sequence[float],
    stagger_phase: float = 0.0,
) -> None:
    self.num_dofs = num_dofs
    self.dof_indices = np.asarray(list(dof_indices), dtype=np.int64)
    self.f_start = float(f_start)
    self.f_end = float(f_end)
    self._duration = float(duration)
    self.stagger_phase = float(stagger_phase)
    amp = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(amplitude, dtype=np.float64))
    if amp.size == 1:
        amp = np.full(self.dof_indices.size, float(amp[0]))
    if amp.size != self.dof_indices.size:
        raise ValueError("amplitude size must be 1 or len(dof_indices).")
    self.amplitude = amp

PRBSExcitation(num_dofs: int, dof_indices: Sequence[int], period: float, duration: float, amplitude: float | Sequence[float], seed: int = 0)

Bases: Excitation

Pseudo-random binary sequence — good for stiction / friction characterisation.

Every period seconds each DOF's command takes a fresh random sign, +amplitude or -amplitude. The DOFs draw independent sequences (from one seed), which avoids correlated excitation.

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/excitation.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    num_dofs: int,
    dof_indices: Sequence[int],
    period: float,
    duration: float,
    amplitude: float | Sequence[float],
    seed: int = 0,
) -> None:
    self.num_dofs = num_dofs
    self.dof_indices = np.asarray(list(dof_indices), dtype=np.int64)
    self.period = float(period)
    self._duration = float(duration)
    amp = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(amplitude, dtype=np.float64))
    if amp.size == 1:
        amp = np.full(self.dof_indices.size, float(amp[0]))
    if amp.size != self.dof_indices.size:
        raise ValueError("amplitude size must be 1 or len(dof_indices).")
    self.amplitude = amp
    n_flips = max(int(np.ceil(self._duration / max(self.period, 1e-6))) + 1, 1)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    self._flips = rng.choice([-1.0, 1.0], size=(n_flips, self.dof_indices.size))

docs.title: reset_to_initial_state
docs.text:
reset_to_initial_state(env: 'EnvBase', trajectory: Trajectory, entity_name: str) -> None

Reset all envs to the measurement's initial state by writing entity state directly.

Bypasses _reset_idx on purpose: firing _RESET events would re-run domain-randomisation terms that may mutate the very parameters being identified. The caller is responsible for first placing the sysid parameters via :func:apply_parameters / :func:apply_candidates.

For floating-base entities, qpos from a sim-side recording already includes the 7-DOF base prefix (because :class:SysIDRecorder writes it using entity.qs_idx_local). Deployment recordings, however, store DOF positions only — pos and quat come through as separate initial_state keys, and we apply them after set_qpos so the base actually starts at the measured pose.

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/rollout.py 
def reset_to_initial_state(env: "EnvBase", trajectory: Trajectory, entity_name: str) -> None:
    """Reset all envs to the measurement's initial state by writing entity state directly.

    Bypasses ``_reset_idx`` on purpose: firing ``_RESET`` events would re-run
    domain-randomisation terms that may mutate the very parameters being
    identified. The caller is responsible for first placing the sysid
    parameters via :func:`apply_parameters` / :func:`apply_candidates`.

    For floating-base entities, ``qpos`` from a sim-side recording already
    includes the 7-DOF base prefix (because :class:`SysIDRecorder` writes it
    using ``entity.qs_idx_local``). Deployment recordings, however, store
    DOF positions only — ``pos`` and ``quat`` come through as separate
    ``initial_state`` keys, and we apply them after ``set_qpos`` so the
    base actually starts at the measured pose.
    """
    entity = env.entities[entity_name]
    if "qpos" not in trajectory.initial_state:
        raise ValueError("Trajectory.initial_state missing required 'qpos' field.")

    qpos = torch.as_tensor(trajectory.initial_state["qpos"], dtype=torch.float32, device=env.device)
    qpos = qpos.unsqueeze(0).expand(env.num_envs, -1).contiguous()
    entity.set_qpos(qpos, zero_velocity=True)

    if "dofs_vel" in trajectory.initial_state:
        dofs_vel = torch.as_tensor(trajectory.initial_state["dofs_vel"], dtype=torch.float32, device=env.device)
        dofs_vel = dofs_vel.unsqueeze(0).expand(env.num_envs, -1).contiguous()
        entity.set_dofs_vel(dofs_vel)

    # Apply base pose if it was recorded separately. Entities with no base DOFs don't accept
    # set_pos/set_quat — fixed-base ones reject it, and a welded child's pose is FK output that
    # discards the write — so guard on has_immobile_base when available.
    has_immobile_base = bool(getattr(entity, "has_immobile_base", False))
    if not has_immobile_base:
        if "pos" in trajectory.initial_state:
            pos = torch.as_tensor(trajectory.initial_state["pos"], dtype=torch.float32, device=env.device)
            if pos.ndim == 1:
                pos = pos.unsqueeze(0).expand(env.num_envs, -1).contiguous()
            entity.set_pos(pos)
        if "quat" in trajectory.initial_state:
            quat = torch.as_tensor(trajectory.initial_state["quat"], dtype=torch.float32, device=env.device)
            if quat.ndim == 1:
                quat = quat.unsqueeze(0).expand(env.num_envs, -1).contiguous()
            entity.set_quat(quat)

docs.title: replay_rollout
docs.text:
replay_rollout(env: 'EnvBase', trajectory: Trajectory, entity_name: str, signals: Sequence[str] = ('dofs_pos', 'dofs_vel', 'dofs_torque')) -> dict[str, Tensor]

Replay the measured action trajectory under the currently-applied parameters.

Uses the narrow physics-only stepper so that termination, reward, reset, command, event, and recorder managers do not fire — a measured trajectory longer than max_episode_length would otherwise be corrupted by auto-reset.

All env.num_envs envs step on every tick (Genesis steps the full batch). For K-candidate batched identification, build a dedicated env with env_options.num_envs = K and use :func:batched_candidate_rollout; otherwise all envs receive the same state (but may hold different parameters for Monte-Carlo variance estimation).

Returns a dict {signal_name: tensor(num_envs, n_steps, dim)}.

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/rollout.py 
def replay_rollout(
    env: "EnvBase",
    trajectory: Trajectory,
    entity_name: str,
    signals: Sequence[str] = ("dofs_pos", "dofs_vel", "dofs_torque"),
) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    """Replay the measured action trajectory under the currently-applied parameters.

    Uses the narrow physics-only stepper so that termination, reward,
    reset, command, event, and recorder managers do not fire — a measured
    trajectory longer than ``max_episode_length`` would otherwise be
    corrupted by auto-reset.

    All ``env.num_envs`` envs step on every tick (Genesis steps the full
    batch). For K-candidate batched identification, build a dedicated env
    with ``env_options.num_envs = K`` and use :func:`batched_candidate_rollout`;
    otherwise all envs receive the same state (but may hold different
    parameters for Monte-Carlo variance estimation).

    Returns a dict ``{signal_name: tensor(num_envs, n_steps, dim)}``.
    """
    if trajectory.action is None:
        raise ValueError("Trajectory.action is required for replay.")
    for s in signals:
        if s not in _SUPPORTED_SIGNALS:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported rollout signal: {s!r}. Expected one of {_SUPPORTED_SIGNALS}.")

    entity = env.entities[entity_name]
    n_steps = len(trajectory)
    signal_dims = {
        "dofs_pos": entity.num_dofs,
        "dofs_vel": entity.num_dofs,
        "dofs_torque": entity.num_dofs,
        "base_quat": 4,
        "base_ang_vel": 3,
    }
    buffers: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {
        s: torch.zeros(env.num_envs, n_steps, signal_dims[s], device=env.device) for s in signals
    }

    reset_to_initial_state(env, trajectory, entity_name)

    actions = torch.as_tensor(trajectory.action, dtype=torch.float32, device=env.device)
    for t in range(n_steps):
        action_batch = actions[t].unsqueeze(0).expand(env.num_envs, -1).contiguous()
        _physics_step(env, action_batch)
        if "dofs_pos" in buffers:
            buffers["dofs_pos"][:, t] = entity.get_dofs_pos()
        if "dofs_vel" in buffers:
            buffers["dofs_vel"][:, t] = entity.get_dofs_vel()
        if "dofs_torque" in buffers:
            buffers["dofs_torque"][:, t] = entity.get_dofs_control_force()
        if "base_quat" in buffers:
            buffers["base_quat"][:, t] = entity.get_quat()
        if "base_ang_vel" in buffers:
            buffers["base_ang_vel"][:, t] = entity.get_ang(frame="body")

    return buffers

def single_candidate_rollout(
    env: "EnvBase",
    params: ParameterSet,
    trajectory: Trajectory,
    entity_name: str,
    signals: Sequence[str] = ("dofs_pos", "dofs_vel", "dofs_torque"),
) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Apply every free parameter's ``value`` to all envs, replay once, return env-0 predictions.

    This is the serial primitive used by every optimiser that evaluates one
    parameter vector per step (scipy least-squares with FD Jacobian, and
    CMA-ES unless batched mode is opted into).
    """
    apply_parameters(env, params)
    pred = replay_rollout(env, trajectory, entity_name=entity_name, signals=signals)
    return {k: v[0].detach().cpu().numpy() for k, v in pred.items()}

Requires env.num_envs == K. Each candidate row is written into the matching env via per-env DOF setters; a single replay then produces predictions for all K candidates simultaneously.

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/rollout.py 
def batched_candidate_rollout(
    env: "EnvBase",
    params: ParameterSet,
    candidates: np.ndarray,
    trajectory: Trajectory,
    entity_name: str,
    signals: Sequence[str] = ("dofs_pos", "dofs_vel", "dofs_torque"),
) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Evaluate K candidates in one rollout on a K-sized env.

    Requires ``env.num_envs == K``. Each candidate row is written into the
    matching env via per-env DOF setters; a single replay then produces
    predictions for all K candidates simultaneously.

    Returns ``{signal_name: array(shape=(K, n_steps, dim))}``.
    """
    K = int(candidates.shape[0])
    if K != env.num_envs:
        raise ValueError(
            f"batched_candidate_rollout requires env.num_envs == K (got K={K}, "
            f"num_envs={env.num_envs}). Build the sysid env with "
            f"env_options.num_envs = K or use single_candidate_rollout."
        )
    apply_candidates(env, params, candidates)
    pred = replay_rollout(env, trajectory, entity_name=entity_name, signals=signals)
    return {k: v.detach().cpu().numpy() for k, v in pred.items()}

docs.text:
signal_residual(predicted: Mapping[str, ndarray], measured: Trajectory, signals: Sequence[str], weights: Mapping[str, float] | None = None, normalize: bool = True) -> ndarray

Flatten per-signal residuals into a single 1-D vector.

predicted[s] has shape (n_steps, dim). The measured value is read from measured.signal(s); the two are compared over the shorter of their lengths. A signal missing from either side is skipped. Each block is multiplied by its weight and, when normalize=True, divided by its measured RMS so heterogeneous units contribute comparably.

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/residual.py 
def signal_residual(
    predicted: Mapping[str, np.ndarray],
    measured: Trajectory,
    signals: Sequence[str],
    weights: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    normalize: bool = True,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Flatten per-signal residuals into a single 1-D vector.

    ``predicted[s]`` has shape ``(n_steps, dim)``. The measured value is read
    from ``measured.signal(s)``; the two are compared over the shorter of
    their lengths. A signal missing from either side is skipped. Each block is
    multiplied by its weight and, when ``normalize=True``, divided by its
    measured RMS so heterogeneous units contribute comparably.
    """
    weights = weights or {}
    pieces: list[np.ndarray] = []
    for s in signals:
        meas = measured.signal(s)
        if meas is None:
            continue
        pred = predicted.get(s)
        if pred is None:
            continue
        n = min(pred.shape[0], meas.shape[0])
        diff = pred[:n] - meas[:n]
        w = float(weights.get(s, 1.0))
        if w != 1.0:
            diff = diff * w
        if normalize:
            rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(meas[:n] ** 2)))
            if rms > 1e-8:
                diff = diff / rms
        pieces.append(diff.ravel())
    if not pieces:
        raise ValueError("No overlapping signals between predicted and measured.")
    return np.concatenate(pieces)

Concatenate residuals from multiple (predicted, measured) pairs.

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/residual.py 
def multi_trajectory_residual(
    predicted_trajectories: Sequence[Mapping[str, np.ndarray]],
    measured_trajectories: Sequence[Trajectory],
    signals: Sequence[str],
    weights: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    normalize: bool = True,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Concatenate residuals from multiple (predicted, measured) pairs."""
    if len(predicted_trajectories) != len(measured_trajectories):
        raise ValueError("predicted and measured trajectory lists have different lengths.")
    blocks = [
        signal_residual(p, m, signals=signals, weights=weights, normalize=normalize)
        for p, m in zip(predicted_trajectories, measured_trajectories)
    ]
    return np.concatenate(blocks)

docs.text:
make_parameter_from_default(env: 'EnvBase', name: str, property: str, dof_names: Sequence[str], entity_name: str = 'robot', min_scale: float = 0.1, max_scale: float = 10.0, per_dof: bool = False, frozen: bool = False) -> Parameter

Construct a Parameter using the entity's current value as the nominal.

Reads the current per-DOF value (env 0) via the entity getter and uses it as nominal — per DOF with per_dof, else their mean. Bounds are min_scale / max_scale times nominal, the natural parameterisation for the supported non-negative properties (damping, armature, stiffness, frictionloss, kp, kd). When the default is zero (e.g. frictionloss), the multiplicative bounds collapse — construct the Parameter explicitly in that case.

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/modifier.py 
def make_parameter_from_default(
    env: "EnvBase",
    name: str,
    property: str,
    dof_names: Sequence[str],
    entity_name: str = "robot",
    min_scale: float = 0.1,
    max_scale: float = 10.0,
    per_dof: bool = False,
    frozen: bool = False,
) -> Parameter:
    """Construct a Parameter using the entity's current value as the nominal.

    Reads the current per-DOF value (env 0) via the entity getter and uses it
    as ``nominal`` — per DOF with ``per_dof``, else their mean. Bounds are
    ``min_scale`` / ``max_scale`` times nominal, the natural parameterisation
    for the supported non-negative properties (``damping``, ``armature``,
    ``stiffness``, ``frictionloss``, ``kp``, ``kd``). When the default is zero
    (e.g. ``frictionloss``), the multiplicative bounds collapse — construct the
    ``Parameter`` explicitly in that case.
    """
    if property not in DOF_PROPERTY_GETTERS:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown DOF property: {property!r}. Expected one of {list(DOF_PROPERTY_GETTERS)}.")
    entity = env.entities[entity_name]
    _, dof_indices = entity.find_named_dofs_idx_local(list(dof_names), preserve_order=True)
    # Env 0 is the nominal: the getters carry an env axis, and nothing has randomized yet.
    values = getattr(entity, DOF_PROPERTY_GETTERS[property])(dofs_idx_local=dof_indices)[0]
    values_np = values.detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float64, copy=False)
    if per_dof:
        nominal = values_np
        lo = nominal * min_scale
        hi = nominal * max_scale
    else:
        nominal_scalar = float(values_np.mean())
        nominal = np.array([nominal_scalar], dtype=np.float64)
        lo = np.array([nominal_scalar * min_scale], dtype=np.float64)
        hi = np.array([nominal_scalar * max_scale], dtype=np.float64)
    return Parameter(
        name=name,
        property=property,
        dof_names=dof_names,
        entity_name=entity_name,
        per_dof=per_dof,
        nominal=nominal,
        min_value=lo,
        max_value=hi,
        frozen=frozen,
    )

def apply_parameters(env: "EnvBase", params: ParameterSet) -> None:
    """Write every free parameter's current value to all envs.

    Broadcasts the parameter vector to ``(num_envs, n_dofs)`` so the
    solver tensors are consistent across the batch.

docs.text:
apply_candidates(env: 'EnvBase', params: ParameterSet, candidates: ndarray) -> None

Write K distinct candidate parameter vectors into K environments.

candidates has shape (K, n_free_params) and requires K == env.num_envs. Each row is written to env k as the per-env value of the targeted solver tensor. Frozen parameters are untouched.

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/modifier.py 
def apply_candidates(env: "EnvBase", params: ParameterSet, candidates: np.ndarray) -> None:
    """Write K distinct candidate parameter vectors into K environments.

    ``candidates`` has shape ``(K, n_free_params)`` and requires
    ``K == env.num_envs``. Each row is written to env ``k`` as the per-env
    value of the targeted solver tensor. Frozen parameters are untouched.
    """
    K, n_free = candidates.shape
    if n_free != params.size:
        raise ValueError(f"Candidates width {n_free} != ParameterSet.size {params.size}.")
    if K != env.num_envs:
        raise ValueError(f"apply_candidates requires K == env.num_envs (got K={K}, num_envs={env.num_envs}).")

    original = params.as_vector()
    try:
        per_env = [candidates[k] for k in range(K)]
        start = 0
        for param in params:
            if param.frozen:
                continue
            end = start + param.size
            values = np.stack([vec[start:end] for vec in per_env])
            start = end
            _apply_one(env, param, envs_idx=None, per_env_values=values)
    finally:
        params.update_from_vector(original)

DeploymentRecorder(deployer: 'DeploymentBase', excitation: Excitation, kp_scale: float = 1.0, kd_scale: float = 1.0, safety_limits: ndarray | None = None, center_dofs_pos: ndarray | None = None, dofs_limit: tuple[ndarray, ndarray] | None = None)

Drive a DeploymentBase with an Excitation and record a Trajectory.

The loop writes the excitation offset on top of a center pose at every control tick, captures the returned RobotState, and after the duration serialises everything to a Trajectory compatible with the sysid rollout loader.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION deployer

Active deployment backend, connected and already at its start pose (an INIT that has finished: reset(), request_init(), then step(None) until init_done). The recorder writes the wire directly (send_payload / read_state), outside the operator state machine.

TYPE: 'DeploymentBase'

excitation

Excitation generator. Called once per control tick with the elapsed seconds since run was invoked.

TYPE: Excitation

kp_scale

Multipliers on deployer.default_dof_kp / ..._kd used for this recording. Lower kp is safer and surfaces compliance/damping in the response; higher kp stiffens the reference-tracking.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

kd_scale

Multipliers on deployer.default_dof_kp / ..._kd used for this recording. Lower kp is safer and surfaces compliance/damping in the response; higher kp stiffens the reference-tracking.

TYPE: float DEFAULT: 1.0

safety_limits

Optional per-DOF symmetric clamp on the excitation offset (radians). Defaults to no additional clamp beyond whatever the backend already enforces.

TYPE: ndarray | None DEFAULT: None

center_dofs_pos

Optional absolute joint-position center for the excitation. Defaults to the robot's actual position at recording start.

TYPE: ndarray | None DEFAULT: None

dofs_limit

Optional per-DOF lower and upper position limits used for diagnostics.

TYPE: tuple[ndarray, ndarray] | None DEFAULT: None

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/deployment_recorder.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    deployer: "DeploymentBase",
    excitation: Excitation,
    kp_scale: float = 1.0,
    kd_scale: float = 1.0,
    safety_limits: np.ndarray | None = None,
    center_dofs_pos: np.ndarray | None = None,
    dofs_limit: tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None = None,
) -> None:
    if excitation.num_dofs != deployer.num_dofs:
        raise ValueError(f"Excitation has {excitation.num_dofs} DOFs but deployer expects {deployer.num_dofs}.")
    self.deployer = deployer
    self.excitation = excitation
    self.kp = deployer.default_dof_kp * float(kp_scale)
    self.kd = deployer.default_dof_kd * float(kd_scale)
    self.safety_limits = np.asarray(safety_limits, dtype=np.float64) if safety_limits is not None else None
    if self.safety_limits is not None and self.safety_limits.size != deployer.num_dofs:
        raise ValueError("safety_limits size must equal deployer.num_dofs.")
    self.center_dofs_pos = np.asarray(center_dofs_pos, dtype=np.float64) if center_dofs_pos is not None else None
    if self.center_dofs_pos is not None and self.center_dofs_pos.size != deployer.num_dofs:
        raise ValueError("center_dofs_pos size must equal deployer.num_dofs.")
    if dofs_limit is None:
        self.dofs_limit = None
    else:
        lo, hi = dofs_limit
        self.dofs_limit = (np.asarray(lo, dtype=np.float64), np.asarray(hi, dtype=np.float64))
        if self.dofs_limit[0].size != deployer.num_dofs or self.dofs_limit[1].size != deployer.num_dofs:
            raise ValueError("dofs_limit arrays must equal deployer.num_dofs.")
    # Own our own rate limiter rather than reusing the deployer's, so that
    # data collection can run at its own cadence and does not race with
    # whatever other loop may hold the deployer's limiter.
    self._rate = RateLimiter(deployer.control_freq) if deployer.control_freq else None

Execute the excitation for excitation.duration seconds.

By default, the excitation offset is added on top of the robot's actual resting pose (read_state().dofs_pos). Callers can pass center_dofs_pos to use a known center pose instead, such as the midpoint of each joint's position limits.

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/deployment_recorder.py 
def run(self) -> Trajectory:
    """Execute the excitation for ``excitation.duration`` seconds.

    By default, the excitation offset is added on top of the robot's
    **actual resting pose** (``read_state().dofs_pos``). Callers can pass
    ``center_dofs_pos`` to use a known center pose instead, such as the
    midpoint of each joint's position limits.

    Returns the recorded Trajectory. The timestamp column starts at
    zero (relative to loop start); the caller can shift externally if
    absolute alignment with other logs is needed.
    """
    deployer = self.deployer
    duration = self.excitation.duration

    stamps: list[float] = []
    actions: list[np.ndarray] = []
    dofs_pos: list[np.ndarray] = []
    dofs_vel: list[np.ndarray] = []
    dofs_torque: list[np.ndarray] = []
    base_quat: list[np.ndarray] = []
    base_ang_vel: list[np.ndarray] = []
    base_lin_acc: list[np.ndarray] = []

    initial_state = deployer.read_state()
    q0 = np.asarray(initial_state.dofs_pos, dtype=np.float64).copy()
    center = q0 if self.center_dofs_pos is None else self.center_dofs_pos

    # Warn if the requested excitation range leaves the known joint limits.
    try:
        if self.dofs_limit is None:
            entity = deployer._env.entities[deployer.entity_name]
            q_lim_lo, q_lim_hi = entity.get_dofs_limit()
            q_lim_lo = q_lim_lo[0].detach().cpu().numpy()
            q_lim_hi = q_lim_hi[0].detach().cpu().numpy()
        else:
            q_lim_lo, q_lim_hi = self.dofs_limit
        # Peak excitation magnitude per DOF, sampled at 64 points over the duration (best-effort).
        peak = np.zeros(deployer.num_dofs, dtype=np.float64)
        for t in np.linspace(0.0, duration, 64):
            peak = np.maximum(peak, np.abs(self.excitation(t)))
        if self.safety_limits is not None:
            peak = np.minimum(peak, self.safety_limits)
        below = (center - peak) < q_lim_lo
        above = (center + peak) > q_lim_hi
        if np.any(below | above):
            names = list(deployer.dofs_name)
            for i in range(deployer.num_dofs):
                if below[i] or above[i]:
                    en.logger.warning(
                        f"DOF '{names[i]}' excitation range "
                        f"[{center[i] - peak[i]:+.3f}, {center[i] + peak[i]:+.3f}] "
                        f"exceeds URDF limits [{q_lim_lo[i]:+.3f}, {q_lim_hi[i]:+.3f}]. "
                        f"The real hand will clip at the mechanical stop and this joint "
                        f"will be hard to identify. Lower --dofs-range-ratio."
                    )
    except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover — diagnostic, don't crash collection
        en.logger.debug(f"joint-limit check skipped: {exc!r}")

    t0 = time.monotonic()
    while True:
        t = time.monotonic() - t0
        if t >= duration:
            break

        offset = self.excitation(t)
        if self.safety_limits is not None:
            offset = np.clip(offset, -self.safety_limits, self.safety_limits)
        target = center + offset

        cmd = RobotCommand(
            dofs_pos=target,
            dofs_vel=np.zeros(deployer.num_dofs),
            dofs_torque=np.zeros(deployer.num_dofs),
            dofs_kp=self.kp,
            dofs_kd=self.kd,
        )
        deployer.send_payload(cmd)
        if self._rate is not None:
            self._rate.sleep()
        state = deployer.read_state()

        stamps.append(t)
        actions.append(target.astype(np.float64, copy=True))
        dofs_pos.append(np.asarray(state.dofs_pos, dtype=np.float64))
        dofs_vel.append(np.asarray(state.dofs_vel, dtype=np.float64))
        dofs_torque.append(np.asarray(state.dofs_torque, dtype=np.float64))
        if state.base_quat is not None:
            base_quat.append(np.asarray(state.base_quat, dtype=np.float64))
        if state.base_ang_vel is not None:
            base_ang_vel.append(np.asarray(state.base_ang_vel, dtype=np.float64))
        if state.base_lin_acc is not None:
            base_lin_acc.append(np.asarray(state.base_lin_acc, dtype=np.float64))

    traj = Trajectory(
        times=np.asarray(stamps),
        action=_stack_or_none(actions),
        dofs_pos=_stack_or_none(dofs_pos),
        dofs_vel=_stack_or_none(dofs_vel),
        dofs_torque=_stack_or_none(dofs_torque),
        base_quat=_stack_or_none(base_quat),
        base_ang_vel=_stack_or_none(base_ang_vel),
        base_lin_acc=_stack_or_none(base_lin_acc),
        dof_names=tuple(deployer.dofs_name),
        initial_state={"qpos": q0, "dofs_vel": np.zeros_like(q0)},
    )
    return traj

def parameter_table(
    initial: ParameterSet,
    identified: ParameterSet,
    digits: int = 4,
) -> str:
    """Human-readable comparison of initial vs identified parameters."""
    lines = [f"{'name':<32}{'initial':>14}{'identified':>14}{'rel Δ':>10}"]
    for p in identified:
        init = initial[p.name].value
        for i in range(p.size):
            label = p.name if p.size == 1 else f"{p.name}[{i}]"
            v0, v1 = float(init.ravel()[i]), float(p.value.ravel()[i])
            rel = (v1 - v0) / v0 if abs(v0) > 1e-12 else float("nan")
            lines.append(f"{label:<32}{v0:>14.{digits}g}{v1:>14.{digits}g}{rel * 100:>9.1f}%")
    return "\n".join(lines)

Write per-signal matplotlib plots comparing one or more predictions against measurement.

predicted accepts two forms: - Single trace: {signal_name: array(n_steps, dim)} — one dashed "predicted" line is plotted alongside the measurement. - Multiple named traces: {label: {signal_name: array(...)}} — each label is drawn with its own line style, e.g. {"initial": pred0, "identified": pred1} to visualise the pre- vs post-optimisation fit on the same axes.

Each signal gets one figure with one subplot per DOF column. Requires matplotlib; returns the list of written file paths.

Source code in eden/extensions/sysid/report.py 
def signal_plots(
    predicted: Mapping[str, np.ndarray] | Mapping[str, Mapping[str, np.ndarray]],
    measured: Trajectory,
    signals: Sequence[str],
    save_dir: str | pathlib.Path,
    dof_names: Sequence[str] | None = None,
) -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    """Write per-signal matplotlib plots comparing one or more predictions against measurement.

    ``predicted`` accepts two forms:
    - **Single trace**: ``{signal_name: array(n_steps, dim)}`` — one
      dashed "predicted" line is plotted alongside the measurement.
    - **Multiple named traces**: ``{label: {signal_name: array(...)}}``
      — each label is drawn with its own line style, e.g.
      ``{"initial": pred0, "identified": pred1}`` to visualise the
      pre- vs post-optimisation fit on the same axes.

    Each signal gets one figure with one subplot per DOF column. Requires
    matplotlib; returns the list of written file paths.
    """
    try:
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover
        raise RuntimeError("signal_plots requires matplotlib.") from exc

    save_dir = pathlib.Path(save_dir)
    save_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    times = measured.times
    dof_names = tuple(dof_names) if dof_names is not None else measured.dof_names

    # Normalise predicted -> dict[label, dict[signal, array]].
    first_value = next(iter(predicted.values())) if predicted else None
    is_multi = isinstance(first_value, Mapping)
    if is_multi:
        traces: dict[str, Mapping[str, np.ndarray]] = dict(predicted)  # type: ignore[assignment]
    else:
        traces = {"predicted": predicted}  # type: ignore[dict-item]

    # Measurement = dotted reference. Predictions = continuous; semantically
    # meaningful labels get fixed colors so pre/post-fit are instantly
    # readable across runs. Unknown labels fall back to the default cycle.
    label_colors: dict[str, str] = {
        "initial": "lightblue",
        "baseline": "lightblue",
        "identified": "red",
    }
    written: list[pathlib.Path] = []

    for signal in signals:
        meas = measured.signal(signal)
        signal_traces = [(label, pred.get(signal)) for label, pred in traces.items()]
        signal_traces = [(label, arr) for label, arr in signal_traces if arr is not None]
        if meas is None or not signal_traces:
            continue
        n = min(min(arr.shape[0] for _, arr in signal_traces), meas.shape[0])
        dim = signal_traces[0][1].shape[-1]

        fig, axes = plt.subplots(dim, 1, figsize=(10, 1.2 * max(dim, 2)), sharex=True)
        if dim == 1:
            axes = [axes]
        for j in range(dim):
            axes[j].plot(
                times[:n],
                meas[:n, j],
                label="measured",
                linewidth=1.0,
                linestyle=":",
                color="black",
            )
            for label, pred in signal_traces:
                axes[j].plot(
                    times[:n],
                    pred[:n, j],
                    label=label,
                    linewidth=1.0,
                    linestyle="-",
                    color=label_colors.get(label),
                )
            title = dof_names[j] if dof_names and j < len(dof_names) else f"{signal}[{j}]"
            axes[j].set_ylabel(title, fontsize=8)
        axes[0].legend(loc="upper right", fontsize=8)
        axes[-1].set_xlabel("time [s]")
        fig.suptitle(signal)
        fig.tight_layout()
        out = save_dir / f"{signal}.png"
        fig.savefig(out, dpi=120)
        plt.close(fig)
        written.append(out)
    return written

def write_summary(
    save_dir: str | pathlib.Path,
    initial: ParameterSet,
    identified: ParameterSet,
    result: "FitResult",
) -> None:
    """Write identified parameters as YAML plus a human-readable summary.txt."""
    save_dir = pathlib.Path(save_dir)

    identified.save_yaml(save_dir / "params_identified.yaml")

docs.title: Teleoperation
docs.text:
Operator-side teleoperation stacks: the process an operator runs to stream commands to a robot process. A stack is a TeleopOperator built from a TeleopInputSource (what the operator wears or holds) and a TeleopStreamer (what it sends), configured by TeleopOptions. The stack that ships is SONIC whole-body teleoperation: PICO body tracking on the operator station, sent over ZMQ to the robot process that runs the SONIC policy. The input devices themselves (keyboard, gamepad, SpaceMouse, GELLO, Meta Quest, PICO, Wuji Glove) are on the devices page. The teleoperation guide covers every pipeline and its eden command.

from eden.extensions.teleop.base import TeleopInputSource, TeleopOperator, TeleopStreamer
from eden.options.extensions.teleop import TeleopOptions

docs.title: Base classes and options
docs.text:
Base classes for teleoperation operator stacks.

The interfaces a teleop stack implements, so future stacks (a different robot, a different tracker, a different wire protocol) share one shape:

  • :class:TeleopOperator — the operator-station lifecycle (setup -> loop -> teardown).
  • :class:TeleopInputSource — a tracked-input device reader.
  • :class:TeleopStreamer — a per-tick pipeline that packs and publishes one message.

:class:TeleopOperator is the configurable extension object, so it follows the Eden convention shared by every other extension base — ConfigurableMixin bound to a declarative :class:~eden.options.extensions.teleop.TeleopOptions (the same shape as DeploymentBase): its config is mirrored onto the instance from the options, and a concrete stack adds its device-specific parameters as class attributes.

:class:TeleopInputSource and :class:TeleopStreamer are plain :class:abc.ABC contracts instead, because they are dependency-injected internal components — constructed with live callables and sockets (send, a socket reader), not from a serializable options schema — so ConfigurableMixin (which exists to bind an Options instance) would not fit them. This mirrors sysid's split between SystemIdentificationBase (ConfigurableMixin) and its plain-ABC Excitation interface. The SONIC stack under teleop/sonic is the reference implementation of all three.

Configuration options for teleoperation operator stacks.

docs.title: TeleopOperator
docs.text:
TeleopOperator(options: T)

Bases: ConfigurableMixin[TeleopOptions], ABC

The operator-station lifecycle: build the stack, run the loop, tear down.

Configured by a :class:~eden.options.extensions.teleop.TeleopOptions (the fields below are mirrored onto the instance by ConfigurableMixin); a concrete stack adds its device-specific parameters as further class attributes. Construct it from an options instance built with configure().

run is the template method — setup once, then step until should_stop is true, then teardown in a finally (so it runs even on KeyboardInterrupt, which routes through on_interrupt). setup runs inside the same try — it can block for a long time (headset wait) — so teardown must cope with a partially built stack. The loop cadence is set by the streamers' own pacing inside step, not by this loop.

Source code in eden/utils/common.py 
def __init__(self, options: T) -> None:
    self._uid = gs.UID()
    self._options: T = options

    mirror_options_onto(self, self._options)

    # Deferred, not module-scope — see the NOTE above this module's imports.
    from eden.options._metadata import OPTION_METADATA_KEYS

    # check if there are unused parameters in the options. ``_extra_option_params`` are legitimate
    # options-only fields (not mirrored as attrs), so they are expected to be "unused" here.
    unused_params = set(self._options.keys()) - set(self.get_parameter_names())
    tolerated = {"name", "class_name"} | set(OPTION_METADATA_KEYS) | self._extra_option_params
    # ``params`` is a declared framework field on function-capable term options. An *empty* one is
    # legitimately unused when the same options class configures a class-based term; a non-empty
    # ``params`` on a class-based term would be silently ignored, so it stays invalid.
    if not getattr(self._options, "params", None):
        tolerated.add("params")
    invalid_params = unused_params - tolerated
    if invalid_params:
        # Name the term, not only the class: for a function term the class is the shared
        # ``*FuncWrapper``, which cannot tell the author which of a dozen terms is wrong.
        # Same wording as the construction-time check (``ManagerTermOptions._validate_param_names``).
        term_name = getattr(self._options, "name", None)
        subject = f"term '{term_name}' ({type(self).__name__})" if term_name else type(self).__name__
        raise ValueError(
            invalid_parameters_message(subject, invalid_params, self.get_configure_specs(), self._retired_params)
        )

def run(self) -> None:
    """Set up the stack, drive the control loop, and tear down on exit."""
    try:
        self.setup()
        while not self.should_stop():
            self.step()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        self.on_interrupt()
    finally:
        self.teardown()

def __init__(self, **data):
    # Seed type metadata as construction data so BaseModel validates it into
    # __pydantic_extra__ (no-op for extra="forbid" classes, which use
    # the serialization envelope instead).
    data.update(option_metadata(self))
    # NOTE: all of the option modifications/validations should be done in the __init__ method
    try:
        BaseModel.__init__(self, **data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        # A misspelled field on an extra="forbid" class should teach the field set, not just
        # name the typo. Only rewritten when every error is extra_forbidden.
        enriched = _enrich_extra_forbidden(type(self), exc)
        if enriched is None:
            raise
        raise enriched from None

docs.title: SONIC operator station
docs.text:
SONIC operator station: PICO body tracking -> ZMQ commands for the robot process.

The Eden counterpart of the reference stack's T3. One manager loop polls the controllers, advances the operator state machine, runs the active mode's streamer (POSE at ~50 Hz, planner modes at ~20 Hz), and publishes the command / manager_state messages. Run it with eden teleop sonic operator.

PICO input arrives through eden pico bridge, which this process spawns (pose-only, port --bridge-port) unless --bridge-host points at an external one or --no-bridge-start is given; --sdk reads the XRoboToolkit SDK in-process instead (the reference-parity path).

Controls (PICO): A+B+X+Y engage + calibrate (stand in the neutral pose) / stop + exit A+X toggle POSE <-> PLANNER B+Y toggle POSE <-> PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY L-stick click: toggle VR_3PT from either planner mode A+B/X+Y next / previous locomotion mode (planner modes) triggers close/open that hand menu hold pause the pose stream (re-align before releasing)

Operator state machine for SONIC teleoperation (pure logic, no I/O).

Port of the reference manager's mode table. Two chains share the VR_3PT sub-mode, which remembers its parent:

chain 1:  POSE <--(B+Y)--> PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY <--(L-stick click)--> PLANNER_VR_3PT
chain 2:  POSE <--(A+X)--> PLANNER                   <--(L-stick click)--> PLANNER_VR_3PT
VR_3PT --(A+X or B+Y)--> POSE;  A+B+X+Y engages from OFF / disengages from anywhere
POSE --(menu held)--> POSE_PAUSE --(menu released)--> POSE  (level-triggered)

Button combos are rising-edge except the menu pause. Each transition carries the side effects the manager must run before streaming the new mode's first tick, plus the command message to send after it.

Disengaging is an Eden deviation: the reference's A+B+X+Y from a live mode sends stop, which ends the robot process — on hardware a damping-only command, and an unsupported robot falls. Here it hands the robot to the planner's IDLE instead, so it keeps balancing in place; the robot session ends only from the robot side.

PICO body-tracking readers for the SONIC operator station.

Both readers hand the pipelines the raw XRoboToolkit service data — the (24, 7) full-body joint poses in the service's own frame (positions + scalar-last quaternions) plus controller buttons/sticks/triggers. The SONIC pipelines apply their own frame conversions (see smpl.py / three_point.py), so neither reader goes through :class:eden.utils.devices.pico.xr_client.PicoXrClient's robot-frame poses, whose conversion differs from the reference teleop math.

:class:BridgeReader (the default) subscribes to eden pico bridge's pose channel and consumes its lossless body_raw passthrough, so the SDK and its service-library linkage live in the bridge process. :class:PicoReader is the in-process port of the reference input_readers.PicoReader: a daemon thread spins on is_body_data_available, dedupes frames by device timestamp, keeps exactly one latest sample, and flags a disconnect after 5 s without fresh data. The bridge reader keeps the same sample semantics (dedupe on the same timestamp, identical dt/fps bookkeeping).

POSE-mode streamer: PICO body frames -> 50 Hz windowed SMPL pose messages.

Port of the reference PoseStreamer. Device frames (~90 Hz) are resampled onto a fixed 50 Hz virtual clock by interpolating between the two frames that bracket each virtual tick (nlerp for rotations), then the last five resampled frames are re-sent as an overlapping window on every tick — the robot's motion merger aligns them by frame index and rides out packet loss. Publishing is gated until the window is full after a mode entry.

Each message also carries: the wrist joint targets derived from the elbow twist/swing mapping, the calibrated VR 3-point pose of the current frame, Dex3 hand targets from the triggers, data-collection toggle edges, and the right-stick heading increment.

Planner-mode streamer: joystick -> locomotion commands (~20 Hz).

Port of the reference PlannerStreamer. The left stick sets the movement direction/speed (deadzone-rescaled, rotated into the world by the accumulated facing), the right stick turns, and A+B / X+Y cycle the locomotion mode. PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY attaches the frozen upper-body targets grabbed from the robot's feedback; PLANNER_VR_3PT attaches the calibrated 3-point pose and trigger-driven hand targets.

VR 3-point pose extraction and calibration (VR_3PT mode).

Port of the reference streamer's 3-point path. From the raw (24, 7) service body frame it takes root (0), left hand (22), right hand (23) and neck (12 — deliberately not the head, which moves too freely), converts them to the robot frame, applies per-joint alignment offsets, and expresses the three keypoints relative to the root. :class:ThreePointPose then calibrates them against G1 forward kinematics so the streamed targets live in the same pelvis-local frame the policy's teleop encoder was trained on:

  • full calibration (every engage): operator stands in the neutral pose == the G1's all-zero joint configuration; the neck orientation and both wrist offsets are captured against FK of q = 0.
  • wrist recalibration (every VR_3PT entry): only the wrist offsets are re-captured, against FK of the robot's measured joints; the neck calibration is preserved to avoid jumps from tracking noise.

The neck position is never measured: it is reconstructed from the calibrated neck orientation through a fixed two-link chain.

PICO full-body tracking -> SMPL parameters and root-local joints (POSE mode).

Port of the reference streamer's SMPL path:

  1. The service's 24 global joint rotations (scalar-last, service frame) become parent-local axis-angle after a per-joint Ry(180°) frame fix.
  2. The root orientation is re-based: pre-multiply Rx(+90°) (service Y-up -> robot Z-up), then post-multiply away SMPL's rest orientation (the 120° rotation about (1,1,1)).
  3. Joint positions come from an SMPL-X forward kinematics over the rest skeleton in sonic/smplx_joints_info.npz (fetched from the Kashu7100/eden_assets HF dataset; 55 joints; output = the 22 body joints
  4. the two thumb tips, SMPL-X indices 39 and 54 — NOT the SMPL left_hand/right_hand joints), expressed in the root-local frame.

No body-shape (betas) or operator-height scaling exists anywhere in this pipeline — the reference relies on calibration offsets and the policy itself.

SMPL elbow/wrist rotations -> G1 wrist joint targets (POSE mode).

The G1 elbow has a single pitch DOF, so the SMPL elbow's roll/yaw content is decomposed off (twist about the elbow axis vs. swing) and folded into the wrist joints, preserving the SMPL wrist's own rotation. Fills the six wrist entries of the 29-dim IsaacLab joint vector; everything else stays zero on the pose stream.

Trigger -> Dex3 hand joint targets (the reference's gripper gesture solver).

There is no Cartesian hand IK: the controller trigger fabricates synthetic fingertip positions (thumb tip fixed, the middle tip snapped onto it when the trigger passes 0.5), and the solver turns thumb-to-finger distances into a gesture choice plus a linear interpolation from the open pose to a preset closed pose. With trigger input only, the result is a binary open/close of the middle-finger power grasp.

Robot feedback for the operator station (g1_debug channel, polled on demand).

The operator polls the robot's state only at mode transitions: entering PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY grabs the measured upper-body joints as the frozen targets, and entering PLANNER_VR_3PT grabs the full measured configuration for wrist recalibration. :class:RobotResetWatcher is a separate per-tick subscriber for the robot's fall auto-reset counter — separate because :meth:FeedbackReader.poll_feedback drains the conflated socket, and the transition effects rely on finding a message there.

G1 key-frame forward kinematics for 3-point calibration (Genesis-backed).

Computes the poses of the two wrist frames and the torso frame — with the training-time local offsets applied — for a given 29-DOF joint configuration, root fixed at the origin with identity orientation. This is the reference frame the teleop encoder's vr_3point_local_* observations were trained against, so the offsets must match gear_sonic/config/manager_env/commands/terms/motion.yaml exactly.

The kinematics run on the same Genesis model the robot process simulates (:class:~eden.options.robots.unitree_g1.G1Dofs29Dex3), via a single-env kinematics-only scene (transient_robot_env) held open for the process lifetime. One subtlety: Genesis re-origins the base link onto its inertial frame, so with the FK root at identity the world origin is the solver base frame, not the MJCF pelvis body frame the reference (Pinocchio) uses. The key frames are therefore expressed relative to the pelvis body frame recovered via get_pos/get_quat(relative=True), which cancels the re-origin exactly — pinned against a MuJoCo reference in tests/extensions/teleop/sonic/test_g1_fk.py.

Operator visualization: calibrated VR 3-point pose, G1 mesh, SMPL body (PyVista).

Port of the reference VR3Pt visualizer's rendered content, in one window:

  • the three calibrated keypoints (left wrist light green, right wrist light blue, head orange) as balls with RGB frame triads,
  • the synthesized head chain (origin -> torso offset -> neck along its local Z),
  • a semi-transparent G1 mesh at the origin for spatial reference (geometry from the same MJCF asset the calibration FK loads); with waist tracking the three waist joints follow the calibrated neck orientation,
  • optionally the 24 SMPL joints (lower body blue, upper red) with bones, anchored beside the robot — a pre-engage check that the avatar mirrors the operator.

Requires pyvista (the sonic-viz extra). The window renders inline on the manager thread, exactly like the reference (visualization costs stream latency; run without --vis-vr3pt for the tightest loop).

The robot-side half (the SONIC policy runtime and its ZMQ server) is in eden.extensions.policies.sonic; its policy class is on the policies page.

The SONIC operator station as a :class:TeleopOperator.

setup builds the reader, publish socket, calibration FK, streamers and state machine (blocking until body data arrives); step runs one control tick (poll -> state machine -> effects -> stream -> publish); teardown releases everything, publish socket first. The loop cadence is set by the active streamer's own pacing sleep inside its run_once. Config is mirrored from a :class:~eden.options.extensions.teleop.TeleopOptions (build one with SonicTeleopOperator.configure(**vars(args))); the PICO/SONIC-specific parameters below ride along as options extras.

def __init__(self, options: TeleopOptions) -> None:
    super().__init__(options)
    self._stop = False
    self._final_command_queued = False  # a planner hand-off is queued: teardown must flush it
    # The robot was handed to the planner and kept its session: it is still engaged, with the
    # heading it captured at the first engage, so the next engage must not reset the facing.
    self._robot_kept_heading = False
    # Built by setup(); None until then, so teardown can release a partial stack.
    self._context = self._socket = self._reader = self._bridge_proc = None
    self._feedback = self._reset_watcher = self._fk = self._viz = self._sm = None

def setup(self) -> None:
    import genesis as gs
    import zmq

    import eden as en
    from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.feedback import FeedbackReader, RobotResetWatcher
    from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.g1_fk import G1KeyFrameFk
    from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.planner_streamer import PlannerStreamer
    from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.pose_streamer import PoseStreamer
    from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.three_point import ThreePointPose

    # CPU backend: the calibration FK is a single-env kinematics scene, and
    # the operator pipelines are numpy — claiming a GPU (and torch's default
    # device) here would only fight the robot process.
    en.init(backend=gs.cpu)

    # A --bridge-host bridge runs on another machine, next to its own service.
    self._bridge_proc = None
    if not self.no_service_start and not self.bridge_host and os.path.exists(_SERVICE_SCRIPT):
        subprocess.Popen(["bash", _SERVICE_SCRIPT])
        print(f"[sonic operator] started the XRoboToolkit PC service ({_SERVICE_SCRIPT})")

    if self.sdk:
        from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.inputs import PicoReader

        self._reader = PicoReader()
    else:
        from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.inputs import BridgeReader

        if not self.bridge_host and not self.no_bridge_start:
            # PR_SET_PDEATHSIG is Linux-only; elsewhere the bridge is reaped by teardown alone.
            preexec_fn = _die_with_parent if sys.platform.startswith("linux") else None
            self._bridge_proc = subprocess.Popen(_bridge_argv(self), preexec_fn=preexec_fn)  # noqa: PLW1509
            print(
                f"[sonic operator] started 'eden pico bridge' (pose port {self.bridge_port}, {self.bridge_fps:g} fps)"
            )
        self._reader = BridgeReader(host=self.bridge_host or "127.0.0.1", port=self.bridge_port)
    self._reader.start()

    # Bound before the slow startup (FK compile, headset wait) so a port
    # collision fails fast instead of minutes in. The command socket gets its
    # own context so teardown can term() it — the only call that waits for a
    # queued stop command to be written — without waiting on the feedback /
    # reader sockets that live on the shared instance.
    self._context = zmq.Context()
    self._socket = self._context.socket(zmq.PUB)
    try:
        self._socket.bind(f"tcp://*:{self.port}")
    except zmq.ZMQError as e:
        self._socket.close(linger=0)
        self._context.term()
        self._context = self._socket = None
        raise SystemExit(
            f"[sonic operator] cannot bind tcp://*:{self.port} ({e}) — a previous operator (or the "
            "reference streamer) is still running or still shutting down; stop it, or pass --port"
        ) from e
    print(f"[sonic operator] publishing on tcp://*:{self.port}")

    # Built eagerly, while the headset connects: the first calibration (the
    # engage press) must not stall on the kernel compile.
    print("[sonic operator] building the G1 kinematics scene (first run compiles, up to ~30 s)...")
    self._fk = G1KeyFrameFk()

    print("[sonic operator] waiting for body tracking data (headset in Full-body mode, service WORKING)...")
    while self._reader.get_latest() is None:
        if self._bridge_proc is not None and self._bridge_proc.poll() is not None:
            raise SystemExit(
                f"[sonic operator] the pico bridge exited with code {self._bridge_proc.returncode} — "
                f"check the xrobotoolkit_sdk build and that port {self.bridge_port} is free"
            )
        print("waiting for body data...")
        time.sleep(1)

    on_frame = None
    self._viz = None
    if self.vis_vr3pt:
        from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.viz import Vr3PtPoseVisualizer

        self._viz = Vr3PtPoseVisualizer(
            with_g1_robot=not self.no_g1,
            enable_waist_tracking=self.waist_tracking,
            enable_smpl_vis=self.vis_smpl,
        )
        on_frame = self._viz.on_frame

    self._three_point = ThreePointPose(self._fk)
    self._feedback = FeedbackReader(host=self.robot_host, port=self.feedback_port)
    self._reset_watcher = RobotResetWatcher(host=self.robot_host, port=self.feedback_port)
    self._pose_streamer = PoseStreamer(
        send=self._socket.send,
        three_point=self._three_point,
        num_frames_to_send=self.num_frames,
        target_fps=self.target_fps,
        record_dir=self.record_dir,
        on_frame=on_frame,
    )
    self._planner_streamer = PlannerStreamer(
        send=self._socket.send, three_point=self._three_point, feedback=self._feedback, on_frame=on_frame
    )
    self._sm = OperatorStateMachine()

    print("[sonic operator] A+B+X+Y engages (stand in the neutral pose: forearms bent 90° forward)")
    print(
        "[sonic operator] A+B+X+Y again disengages: the robot balances in place on the planner; "
        "Ctrl-C exits the operator (the robot keeps idling); end the robot session from its own terminal"
    )
    self._prev_toggle_dc = False
    self._prev_toggle_da = False
    self._bridge_died = False

def step(self) -> None:
    reader = self._reader
    socket = self._socket
    sm = self._sm

    if self._bridge_proc is not None and not self._bridge_died and self._bridge_proc.poll() is not None:
        self._bridge_died = True
        print(
            f"[sonic operator] WARNING: the pico bridge exited with code {self._bridge_proc.returncode}; "
            "the input stream is frozen — Ctrl-C to exit"
        )
    if input_lost(sm.mode, bridge_died=self._bridge_died, body_stale=reader.disconnected):
        # Frozen input would otherwise leave the robot on the last streamed pose
        # (POSE never times out robot-side) or the last VR 3-point target.
        forced = self._force_off("input lost", "A+B+X+Y re-engages once tracking is back")
        self._release_robot_to_planner(forced.previous)
        return
    controllers = reader.controllers()

    if self._reset_watcher.poll() and sm.mode != StreamMode.OFF:
        self._force_off("robot fell and auto-reset", "stand in the neutral pose and press A+B+X+Y to re-engage")
        self._robot_kept_heading = False  # the reset disengaged the robot: the next engage re-captures it
        return

    transition = sm.step(
        ButtonSnapshot(
            a=controllers.a,
            b=controllers.b,
            x=controllers.x,
            y=controllers.y,
            left_axis_click=controllers.left_axis_click,
            left_menu=controllers.left_menu,
        )
    )

    for effect in transition.effects:
        if effect == Effect.POSE_EXIT:
            self._pose_streamer.on_mode_exit()
        elif effect == Effect.CALIBRATE_FULL:
            sample = reader.get_latest()
            if sample is not None:
                self._three_point.calibrate_now(sample.body_poses)
            else:
                print("[sonic operator] WARNING: no body data available for calibration")
        elif effect == Effect.RESET_POSE_YAW:
            self._pose_streamer.reset_yaw()
        elif effect == Effect.RESET_PLANNER_YAW:
            if transition.previous == StreamMode.OFF and self._robot_kept_heading:
                # The robot stayed engaged on the planner, so it re-captures no heading on
                # this engage: the facing it is idling with must carry over, not snap to forward.
                self._robot_kept_heading = False
            else:
                self._planner_streamer.reset_yaw()
        elif effect == Effect.RELEASE_TO_PLANNER:
            self._release_robot_to_planner(transition.previous)
            print(
                "[sonic operator] disengaged — A+B+X+Y re-engages (full calibration: neutral pose, "
                "looking ahead); Ctrl-C exits the operator"
            )
        elif effect == Effect.SAVE_FROZEN_TARGETS:
            self._planner_streamer.save_upper_body_position_target()
        elif effect == Effect.RECALIBRATE_WRISTS:
            self._planner_streamer.recalibrate_for_vr3pt()

    # Run one tick of the new mode (its pacing sleep sets the loop rate).
    if transition.mode == StreamMode.POSE:
        self._pose_streamer.run_once(reader.get_latest(), controllers)
    elif transition.mode in PLANNER_MODES:
        self._planner_streamer.run_once(
            transition.mode, reader.get_latest(), controllers, reader.get_timestamp_ns()
        )
    else:
        time.sleep(0.005)  # OFF / POSE_PAUSE: idle poll (no hot spin)

    # Command messages go out after the first tick of the new mode, so its
    # data is already in flight when the robot switches.
    if transition.changed:
        print(f"[sonic operator] {transition.previous.name} -> {transition.mode.name}")
        if transition.command is not None:
            kind, planner_flag = transition.command
            socket.send(build_command_message(start=kind == "start", stop=False, planner=planner_flag))

    # manager_state every tick (consumed by data recorders, not the robot).
    toggle_dc_now = controllers.a and controllers.left_grip > 0.5
    toggle_da_now = controllers.b and controllers.left_grip > 0.5
    socket.send(
        build_manager_state_message(
            stream_mode=transition.mode.value,
            toggle_data_collection=toggle_dc_now and not self._prev_toggle_dc,
            toggle_data_abort=toggle_da_now and not self._prev_toggle_da,
        )
    )
    self._prev_toggle_dc = toggle_dc_now
    self._prev_toggle_da = toggle_da_now

def teardown(self) -> None:
    if self._socket is not None:
        # Leaving while engaged (Ctrl-C, an exception in step) without the stop
        # combo (which leaves the machine OFF): don't leave the robot holding the
        # last streamed pose.
        if self._sm is not None and self._sm.mode != StreamMode.OFF:
            self._release_robot_to_planner(self._sm.mode)
        # Release the command port first: the viz window and the FK scene can
        # take a while to tear down, and an immediate operator relaunch must not
        # find :5556 still bound to this dying process. linger=0 discards
        # whatever ZMQ has not yet written, though, and the last command is sent
        # microseconds before this — so after one, linger and term() (which
        # blocks until the queue is written or the linger expires) so the robot
        # actually receives it.
        self._socket.close(linger=_FINAL_COMMAND_LINGER_MS if self._final_command_queued else 0)
        self._context.term()
    if self._reader is not None:
        self._reader.stop()
    if self._feedback is not None:
        self._feedback.close()
    if self._reset_watcher is not None:
        self._reset_watcher.close()
    if self._bridge_proc is not None and self._bridge_proc.poll() is None:
        self._bridge_proc.terminate()
        try:
            self._bridge_proc.wait(timeout=3.0)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            self._bridge_proc.kill()
    if self._viz is not None:
        self._viz.close()
    if self._fk is not None:
        self._fk.close()
    print("[sonic operator] shutdown complete")

Whether an engaged operator has lost the input its current mode streams from.

A dead bridge freezes everything. Body staleness only matters to the modes that stream body poses: PLANNER / FROZEN_UPPER run on the controllers (whose stalls the robot's planner timeout already handles), so a tracker occlusion must not end joystick walking.

Source code in eden/extensions/teleop/sonic/manager.py 
def input_lost(mode: StreamMode, *, bridge_died: bool, body_stale: bool) -> bool:
    """Whether an engaged operator has lost the input its current mode streams from.

    A dead bridge freezes everything. Body staleness only matters to the modes that
    stream body poses: PLANNER / FROZEN_UPPER run on the controllers (whose stalls the
    robot's planner timeout already handles), so a tracker occlusion must not end
    joystick walking.
    """
    if mode == StreamMode.OFF:
        return False
    return bridge_died or (body_stale and mode in _BODY_STREAM_MODES)

def build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="eden teleop sonic operator", description="SONIC operator station (PICO body tracking -> robot commands)."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--robot-host", default="localhost", help="Host running 'eden teleop sonic robot' (g1_debug SUB)"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=5556, help="Command/planner/pose publish port (bound here)")
    parser.add_argument("--feedback-port", type=int, default=5557, help="Robot g1_debug port")
    parser.add_argument("--target-fps", type=int, default=50, help="Pose stream rate")
    parser.add_argument("--num-frames", type=int, default=5, help="Pose window size (frames per message)")
    parser.add_argument("--record-dir", default="", help="Record each sent pose message as .npz here")
    parser.add_argument("--no-service-start", action="store_true", help="Do not spawn the XRoboToolkit PC service")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--bridge-host",
        default="",
        help="Connect to an 'eden pico bridge' on this host (skips spawning the bridge and the PC service)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--bridge-port",
        type=int,
        default=SONIC_BRIDGE_POSE_PORT,
        help="Bridge pose PUB port (the default avoids the SONIC wire's 5556/5557)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--bridge-fps",
        type=float,
        default=120.0,
        help="Publish rate for the spawned bridge; keep it above the device body rate (~90 Hz)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--no-bridge-start", action="store_true", help="Do not spawn the bridge; connect to one already running locally"
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--sdk", action="store_true", help="Read the XRoboToolkit SDK in-process instead of via the bridge"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--vis-vr3pt", action="store_true", help="Visualize the calibrated VR 3-point pose")
    parser.add_argument("--vis-smpl", action="store_true", help="Also render the SMPL body (needs --vis-vr3pt)")
    parser.add_argument("--waist-tracking", action="store_true", help="Viz only: robot waist follows the neck")
    parser.add_argument("--no-g1", action="store_true", help="Viz only: hide the G1 mesh")
    return parser

def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    args = build_arg_parser().parse_args(argv)
    if args.vis_smpl and not args.vis_vr3pt:
        raise SystemExit("--vis-smpl requires --vis-vr3pt (they share one window)")
    # Every argparse dest is a configurable parameter of the operator, so the
    # namespace maps straight onto TeleopOptions via configure().
    options = SonicTeleopOperator.configure(**vars(args))
    SonicTeleopOperator(options).run()
