def step(self, buttons: ButtonSnapshot) -> Transition:
    """Advance one tick; returns the (possibly unchanged) mode and its effects."""
    ax = buttons.a and buttons.x
    by = buttons.b and buttons.y
    start_combo = buttons.a and buttons.b and buttons.x and buttons.y
    stick = buttons.left_axis_click

    ax_edge = ax and not self._prev_ax
    by_edge = by and not self._prev_by
    start_edge = start_combo and not self._prev_start
    stick_edge = stick and not self._prev_stick

    current = self.mode
    new_mode = current
    if current == StreamMode.OFF:
        if start_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.PLANNER
    elif current == StreamMode.PLANNER:
        if start_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.OFF
        elif ax_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.POSE
        elif stick_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.PLANNER_VR_3PT
    elif current == StreamMode.POSE:
        if start_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.OFF
        elif ax_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.PLANNER
        elif by_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY
        elif buttons.left_menu:  # level, not edge
            new_mode = StreamMode.POSE_PAUSE
    elif current == StreamMode.PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY:
        if start_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.OFF
        elif by_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.POSE
        elif stick_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.PLANNER_VR_3PT
    elif current == StreamMode.POSE_PAUSE:
        if start_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.OFF
        elif not buttons.left_menu:
            new_mode = StreamMode.POSE
    elif current == StreamMode.PLANNER_VR_3PT:
        if start_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.OFF
        elif stick_edge:
            new_mode = self.vr3pt_parent
        elif ax_edge or by_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.POSE

    self._prev_ax = ax
    self._prev_by = by
    self._prev_start = start_combo
    self._prev_stick = stick

    transition = Transition(previous=current, mode=new_mode, changed=new_mode != current)
    if transition.changed:
        self._collect_effects(transition)
    self.mode = new_mode
    return transition

def force_off(self) -> Transition:
    """External force-off (robot fall auto-reset, input loss): back to OFF, no effects but the pose exit.

    The caller decides what the robot needs: nothing after a fall auto-reset
    (it already reset itself), a planner hand-off after an input loss. The
    next A+B+X+Y re-engages through the normal OFF -> PLANNER edge with full
    calibration.
    """
    previous = self.mode
    self.mode = StreamMode.OFF
    transition = Transition(previous=previous, mode=StreamMode.OFF, changed=previous != StreamMode.OFF)
    if previous in (StreamMode.POSE, StreamMode.POSE_PAUSE):
        transition.effects.append(Effect.POSE_EXIT)
    return transition

def update(self, rx: float, dt: float) -> list[float]:
    """Integrate the stick's x-axis; returns the facing unit vector [x, y, 0]."""
    self.dyaw = self.yaw_gain * (-rx) * dt
    if abs(rx) >= self.deadzone:
        self.yaw_angle_rad += self.dyaw
        self.heading = [np.cos(self.yaw_angle_rad), np.sin(self.yaw_angle_rad), 0.0]
    return self.heading

def __init__(
    self,
    send: Callable[[bytes], None],
    three_point: ThreePointPose,
    fk: SmplFk | None = None,
    num_frames_to_send: int = 5,
    target_fps: int = 50,
    record_dir: str = "",
    on_frame: Callable[[np.ndarray, np.ndarray], None] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """``send`` publishes one packed message; ``on_frame(vr_3pt_pose,
    smpl_joints_local)`` is the visualization hook, called once per
    processed device frame.
    """
    self._send = send
    self._three_point = three_point
    self._fk = fk or SmplFk()
    self._on_frame = on_frame
    self.num_frames_to_send = num_frames_to_send
    self.target_fps = target_fps
    self.record_dir = record_dir
    self._record_idx = 0
    if record_dir:
        import os

        os.makedirs(record_dir, exist_ok=True)

    self.yaw_accumulator = YawAccumulator()
    # 95% of the frame period: the remaining 5% absorbs processing overhead.
    self.frame_time = 0.95 / max(1, target_fps)
    self._sleep = time.sleep

    self.step = 0
    self.frame_buffer: dict[str, deque] = defaultdict(lambda: deque(maxlen=num_frames_to_send))
    self.prev_stamp_ns: int | None = None
    self._last_seen_stamp_ns: int | None = None  # newest device frame run_once has processed
    self.prev_smpl_pose: np.ndarray | None = None
    self.prev_smpl_joints: np.ndarray | None = None
    self.prev_body_quat: np.ndarray | None = None
    self.next_target_ns: int | None = None
    self.frame_start = time.time()
    self.buffer_cleared = True  # publish only once the window refills
    self._toggle_dc_last = False
    self._toggle_da_last = False
    self._emit_count = 0
    self._rate_log_time = time.time()

def run_once(self, sample: BodySample | None, controllers: ControllerSample) -> None:
    """Process the latest device frame; publish when a virtual tick completes."""
    if sample is None:
        self._sleep(0.005)
        return
    if sample.timestamp_ns == self._last_seen_stamp_ns:
        # Same device frame as last tick: every path below would reach the same
        # result again, after a full SMPL-X FK. Without this wait the manager
        # loop would spin between device frames, re-running the FK and publishing
        # manager_state at kHz rates while competing with the reader thread.
        self._sleep(IDLE_POLL_S)
        return
    self._last_seen_stamp_ns = sample.timestamp_ns

    frame = process_body_poses(sample.body_poses, self._fk)
    smpl_pose = frame.body_pose[:63].reshape(21, 3).astype(np.float32)
    smpl_joints = frame.smpl_joints_local.astype(np.float32)
    body_quat = frame.global_orient_quat.astype(np.float32)

    toggle_dc_now = controllers.a and controllers.left_grip > 0.5
    toggle_da_now = controllers.b and controllers.left_grip > 0.5
    toggle_dc = toggle_dc_now and not self._toggle_dc_last
    toggle_da = toggle_da_now and not self._toggle_da_last
    self._toggle_dc_last = toggle_dc_now
    self._toggle_da_last = toggle_da_now

    left_hand, right_hand = hand_targets_from_triggers(controllers.left_trigger, controllers.right_trigger)

    # --- resample onto the 50 Hz virtual clock ---
    curr_stamp_ns = sample.timestamp_ns
    step_ns = int(1e9 / max(1, self.target_fps))
    if self.prev_stamp_ns is None:
        self.prev_stamp_ns = curr_stamp_ns
        self.prev_smpl_pose = smpl_pose
        self.prev_smpl_joints = smpl_joints
        self.prev_body_quat = body_quat
        self.next_target_ns = curr_stamp_ns
        return
    if curr_stamp_ns <= self.prev_stamp_ns:
        return  # duplicate device frame
    if self.next_target_ns is None:
        self.next_target_ns = self.prev_stamp_ns + step_ns
    self.next_target_ns = max(self.next_target_ns, self.prev_stamp_ns)
    if self.next_target_ns > curr_stamp_ns:
        return  # virtual tick not yet bracketed
    denom = float(curr_stamp_ns - self.prev_stamp_ns)
    alpha = float(np.clip((self.next_target_ns - self.prev_stamp_ns) / denom if denom > 0 else 1.0, 0.0, 1.0))

    use_joints = (1.0 - alpha) * self.prev_smpl_joints + alpha * smpl_joints
    # Per-joint NLERP of the (21, 3) axis-angle pose, via quaternions.
    prev_q = sRot.from_rotvec(self.prev_smpl_pose.reshape(-1, 3)).as_quat()
    curr_q = sRot.from_rotvec(smpl_pose.reshape(-1, 3)).as_quat()
    use_pose = (
        sRot.from_quat(quat_nlerp(prev_q, curr_q, alpha)).as_rotvec().reshape(smpl_pose.shape).astype(np.float32)
    )
    use_body_quat = quat_nlerp(self.prev_body_quat, body_quat, alpha).astype(np.float32)

    joint_pos = wrist_joints_from_body_pose(use_pose)

    # Calibrated VR 3-point pose of the current (raw) frame.
    vr_3pt_pose = self._three_point.process(sample.body_poses)
    if self._on_frame is not None:
        self._on_frame(vr_3pt_pose, frame.smpl_joints_local)

    self.frame_buffer["smpl_pose"].append(use_pose)
    self.frame_buffer["smpl_joints"].append(use_joints)
    self.frame_buffer["body_quat_w"].append(use_body_quat)
    self.frame_buffer["frame_index"].append(int(self.step))
    self.frame_buffer["joint_pos"].append(joint_pos)

    buffer_is_full = len(self.frame_buffer["frame_index"]) >= self.num_frames_to_send
    if buffer_is_full and self.buffer_cleared:
        self.buffer_cleared = False

    self.yaw_accumulator.update(controllers.right_axis[0], self.frame_time)

    if buffer_is_full and not self.buffer_cleared:
        n = len(self.frame_buffer["frame_index"])
        message_data = {
            "smpl_pose": np.stack(self.frame_buffer["smpl_pose"]),
            "smpl_joints": np.stack(self.frame_buffer["smpl_joints"]),
            "body_quat_w": np.stack(self.frame_buffer["body_quat_w"]),
            "joint_pos": np.stack(self.frame_buffer["joint_pos"]),
            "joint_vel": np.zeros((n, 29)),
            "vr_position": vr_3pt_pose[:, :3].flatten().astype(np.float32),
            "vr_orientation": vr_3pt_pose[:, 3:].flatten().astype(np.float32),
            "frame_index": np.array(self.frame_buffer["frame_index"], dtype=np.int64),
            "left_trigger": np.array([controllers.left_trigger], dtype=np.float32),
            "right_trigger": np.array([controllers.right_trigger], dtype=np.float32),
            "left_grip": np.array([controllers.left_grip], dtype=np.float32),
            "right_grip": np.array([controllers.right_grip], dtype=np.float32),
            "pico_dt": np.array([sample.dt], dtype=np.float32),
            "pico_fps": np.array([sample.fps], dtype=np.float32),
            "timestamp_realtime": np.array([sample.timestamp_realtime], dtype=np.float64),
            "timestamp_monotonic": np.array([sample.timestamp_monotonic], dtype=np.float64),
            "left_hand_joints": left_hand.astype(np.float32),
            "right_hand_joints": right_hand.astype(np.float32),
            "toggle_data_collection": np.array([toggle_dc], dtype=bool),
            "toggle_data_abort": np.array([toggle_da], dtype=bool),
            "heading_increment": np.array([self.yaw_accumulator.dyaw], dtype=np.float32),
        }
        self._send(pack_pose_message(message_data, topic="pose"))
        if self.record_dir:
            import os

            np.savez_compressed(os.path.join(self.record_dir, f"pose_{self._record_idx:06d}.npz"), **message_data)
            self._record_idx += 1

    self.step += 1
    self.next_target_ns += step_ns
    self.prev_stamp_ns = curr_stamp_ns
    self.prev_smpl_pose = smpl_pose
    self.prev_smpl_joints = smpl_joints
    self.prev_body_quat = body_quat

    # Reference parity ([PoseLoop] FPS/Step every 5 s). The resampler emits
    # at most one virtual frame per distinct device sample, so a sustained
    # rate below target means the input path is starving the robot's stream.
    self._emit_count += 1
    now = time.time()
    window = now - self._rate_log_time
    if window >= 5.0:
        rate = self._emit_count / window
        print(f"[PoseLoop] FPS: {rate:.1f} Step: {self.step}")
        if rate < 0.9 * self.target_fps:
            print(
                f"[PoseLoop] WARNING: emitting {rate:.1f} Hz < target {self.target_fps} — "
                "device/bridge rate too low, the robot-side stream will stall"
            )
        self._emit_count = 0
        self._rate_log_time = now

    elapsed = time.time() - self.frame_start
    if elapsed < self.frame_time:
        self._sleep(self.frame_time - elapsed)
    self.frame_start = time.time()

def send_idle(self) -> None:
    """Send one IDLE planner message, holding the current facing, with no optional fields.

    No upper-body, hand or VR 3-point fields: the robot reads their absence as "not
    operator-driven", so this drops VR 3-point control (back to the g1 encoder) and the
    frozen upper body. Used when the operator hands the robot back to the planner.
    """
    self._send(
        build_planner_message(
            mode=int(LocomotionMode.IDLE),
            movement=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            facing=np.asarray(self.yaw_accumulator.heading),
            speed=-1.0,
            height=-1.0,
        )
    )

Send one planner command (skipped while the headset stream is stalled).

Source code in eden/extensions/teleop/sonic/planner_streamer.py 
def run_once(
    self, stream_mode: StreamMode, sample: BodySample | None, controllers: ControllerSample, timestamp_ns: int
) -> None:
    """Send one planner command (skipped while the headset stream is stalled)."""
    if timestamp_ns == self._last_timestamp_ns:
        self._sleep(IDLE_POLL_S)  # stalled headset stream: poll, don't spin the manager loop
        return
    self._last_timestamp_ns = timestamp_ns
    self._retry_pending_feedback(stream_mode)

    # A+B -> next mode, X+Y -> previous (rising edges), clamped to the
    # modes the reference exposes (IDLE .. INJURED_WALK).
    ab_now = controllers.a and controllers.b
    xy_now = controllers.x and controllers.y
    if ab_now and not self._prev_ab:
        self.mode = LocomotionMode(min(int(LocomotionMode.INJURED_WALK), int(self.mode) + 1))
        print(f"[PlannerStreamer] mode -> {int(self.mode)}: {self.mode.name}")
    if xy_now and not self._prev_xy:
        self.mode = LocomotionMode(max(int(LocomotionMode.IDLE), int(self.mode) - 1))
        print(f"[PlannerStreamer] mode -> {int(self.mode)}: {self.mode.name}")
    self._prev_ab = ab_now
    self._prev_xy = xy_now

    lx, ly = controllers.left_axis
    rx, _ = controllers.right_axis
    facing = self.yaw_accumulator.update(rx, self.dt)

    raw_mag = float(np.clip(np.hypot(lx, ly), 0.0, 1.0))
    if raw_mag < JOYSTICK_DEADZONE:
        mag, speed = 0.0, -1.0
        mode_to_send = LocomotionMode.IDLE
    else:
        mag = min((raw_mag - JOYSTICK_DEADZONE) / (1.0 - JOYSTICK_DEADZONE), 1.0)
        mode_to_send = self.mode
        if self.mode == LocomotionMode.SLOW_WALK:
            speed = 0.1 + 0.5 * mag  # 0.1 .. 0.6 m/s
        elif self.mode == LocomotionMode.WALK:
            speed = -1.0  # mode default
        elif self.mode == LocomotionMode.RUN:
            speed = 1.5 + 3.0 * mag  # 1.5 .. 4.5 m/s
        else:
            speed = mag

    scale = mag / (raw_mag if raw_mag > 0.0 else 1.0)
    movement_local = np.array([-lx, ly]) * scale
    rotation_facing = np.array([[-facing[1], facing[0]], [facing[0], facing[1]]])
    movement_global = rotation_facing @ movement_local
    movement = [float(movement_global[0]), float(movement_global[1]), 0.0]

    upper_body_position = None
    left_hand = None
    right_hand = None
    if stream_mode == StreamMode.PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY:
        upper_body_position = self.feedback.upper_body_position_target
        left_hand = self.feedback.left_hand_position_target
        right_hand = self.feedback.right_hand_position_target

    vr_position = None
    vr_orientation = None
    if stream_mode == StreamMode.PLANNER_VR_3PT:
        if sample is not None and self._feedback_pending != StreamMode.PLANNER_VR_3PT:
            vr_pose = self._three_point.process(sample.body_poses)
            vr_position = vr_pose[:, :3].flatten()
            vr_orientation = vr_pose[:, 3:].flatten()
            if self._on_frame is not None:
                self._on_frame(vr_pose, None)
        left_hand, right_hand = hand_targets_from_triggers(controllers.left_trigger, controllers.right_trigger)

    self._send(
        build_planner_message(
            mode=int(mode_to_send),
            movement=movement,
            facing=np.asarray(facing),
            speed=float(speed),
            height=-1.0,
            upper_body_position=upper_body_position,
            left_hand_position=left_hand,
            right_hand_position=right_hand,
            vr_3pt_position=vr_position,
            vr_3pt_orientation=vr_orientation,
        )
    )

    # ~20 Hz pacing.
    now = time.time()
    sleep_t = self.dt - (now - self._last_send)
    if sleep_t > 0:
        self._sleep(sleep_t)
    self._last_send = time.time()

process_3pt_pose(body_poses: ndarray) -> ndarray

Raw (24, 7) service frame -> (3, 7) root-relative keypoints.

Rows are [left wrist, right wrist, neck], each [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz].

Source code in eden/extensions/teleop/sonic/three_point.py 
def process_3pt_pose(body_poses: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Raw ``(24, 7)`` service frame -> ``(3, 7)`` root-relative keypoints.

    Rows are [left wrist, right wrist, neck], each ``[x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz]``.
    """
    body_poses = np.asarray(body_poses, dtype=np.float64)
    kp = np.zeros((4, 7))
    for rel_i, joint in enumerate(_KEYPOINT_JOINTS):
        pos, quat = _service_pose_to_robot(body_poses[joint])
        rot = sRot.from_quat(quat, scalar_first=True) * _OFFSETS[rel_i]
        kp[rel_i, :3] = pos
        kp[rel_i, 3:] = rot.as_quat(scalar_first=True)

    root_pos = kp[0, :3].copy()
    root_rot = sRot.from_quat(kp[0, 3:], scalar_first=True)
    for i in range(1, 4):
        kp[i, :3] = root_rot.inv().apply(kp[i, :3] - root_pos)
        kp[i, 3:] = (root_rot.inv() * sRot.from_quat(kp[i, 3:], scalar_first=True)).as_quat(scalar_first=True)
    return kp[1:]

joints(global_orient: ndarray, body_pose: ndarray) -> ndarray

Posed joint positions (24, 3) for a root axis-angle + 63-dim body pose.

The full 55-joint pose is [global_orient, body_pose, zeros(99)]; the output gathers the 22 body joints plus the two thumb tips.

Source code in eden/extensions/teleop/sonic/smpl.py 
def joints(self, global_orient: np.ndarray, body_pose: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Posed joint positions ``(24, 3)`` for a root axis-angle + 63-dim body pose.

    The full 55-joint pose is ``[global_orient, body_pose, zeros(99)]``;
    the output gathers the 22 body joints plus the two thumb tips.
    """
    body_pose = np.asarray(body_pose, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1)[:63]
    full_pose = np.concatenate([np.asarray(global_orient, dtype=np.float64).reshape(3), body_pose, np.zeros(99)])
    rot_mats = sRot.from_rotvec(full_pose.reshape(55, 3)).as_matrix()  # (55, 3, 3)

    rel_joints = self._rest_joints.copy()
    rel_joints[1:] -= self._rest_joints[self._parents[1:]]

    transforms = np.zeros((55, 4, 4))
    transforms[:, :3, :3] = rot_mats
    transforms[:, :3, 3] = rel_joints
    transforms[:, 3, 3] = 1.0

    chain = [transforms[0]]
    for i in range(1, 55):
        chain.append(chain[self._parents[i]] @ transforms[i])
    positions = np.stack(chain)[:, :3, 3]
    return positions[_OUTPUT_JOINTS]

global_quats_to_local_aa(body_poses: ndarray) -> ndarray

Service-frame global joint rotations -> parent-local axis-angle (24, 3).

body_poses is the raw (24, 7) service array (scalar-last quats). Every joint is post-multiplied by Ry(180°) first (the service's joint frames are flipped relative to SMPL's).

Source code in eden/extensions/teleop/sonic/smpl.py 
def global_quats_to_local_aa(body_poses: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Service-frame global joint rotations -> parent-local axis-angle ``(24, 3)``.

    ``body_poses`` is the raw ``(24, 7)`` service array (scalar-last quats).
    Every joint is post-multiplied by ``Ry(180°)`` first (the service's joint
    frames are flipped relative to SMPL's).
    """
    global_quats = np.asarray(body_poses, dtype=np.float64)[:, [6, 3, 4, 5]]
    global_rots = sRot.from_quat(global_quats, scalar_first=True) * sRot.from_euler("y", 180, degrees=True)
    local = []
    for i in range(24):
        parent = SMPL_PARENTS[i]
        rot = global_rots[i] if parent == -1 else global_rots[parent].inv() * global_rots[i]
        local.append(rot.as_rotvec())
    return np.asarray(local)

Full POSE-mode conversion of one raw (24, 7) service frame.

def process_body_poses(body_poses: np.ndarray, fk: SmplFk) -> SmplFrame:
    """Full POSE-mode conversion of one raw ``(24, 7)`` service frame."""
    pose_aa = global_quats_to_local_aa(body_poses)
    body_pose = pose_aa[1:].reshape(-1)  # (69,)

    root_quat = sRot.from_rotvec(pose_aa[0]).as_quat(scalar_first=True)
    root_quat = smpl_root_ytoz_up(root_quat)
    global_orient_new = sRot.from_quat(root_quat, scalar_first=True).as_rotvec()

    joints = fk.joints(global_orient_new, body_pose[:63])

    root_quat = remove_smpl_base_rot(root_quat)
    joints_local = sRot.from_quat(root_quat, scalar_first=True).inv().apply(joints)
    return SmplFrame(body_pose=body_pose, global_orient_quat=root_quat, smpl_joints_local=joints_local)

The 29-dim IsaacLab joint vector for a pose-stream frame (wrists only).

body_pose is the frame's (21, 3) (or flat 63-dim) local axis-angle pose. All Euler readings are intrinsic XYZ; the per-side signs follow the reference mapping verbatim.

def wrist_joints_from_body_pose(body_pose: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """The 29-dim IsaacLab joint vector for a pose-stream frame (wrists only).

    ``body_pose`` is the frame's ``(21, 3)`` (or flat 63-dim) local axis-angle
    pose. All Euler readings are intrinsic XYZ; the per-side signs follow the
    reference mapping verbatim.
    """
    pose = np.asarray(body_pose, dtype=np.float64).reshape(21, 3)
    joint_pos = np.zeros(29)

    _, l_swing = decompose_rotation_aa(pose[SMPL_L_ELBOW][None], _ELBOW_AXIS)
    _, r_swing = decompose_rotation_aa(pose[SMPL_R_ELBOW][None], _ELBOW_AXIS)
    l_swing_euler = sRot.from_quat(l_swing[:, [1, 2, 3, 0]]).as_euler("XYZ")[0]
    r_swing_euler = sRot.from_quat(r_swing[:, [1, 2, 3, 0]]).as_euler("XYZ")[0]
    l_wrist_euler = sRot.from_rotvec(pose[SMPL_L_WRIST]).as_euler("XYZ")
    r_wrist_euler = sRot.from_rotvec(pose[SMPL_R_WRIST]).as_euler("XYZ")

    l_roll = l_swing_euler[0] + l_wrist_euler[0]
    l_pitch = -l_wrist_euler[1]
    l_yaw = l_swing_euler[2] + l_wrist_euler[2]
    r_roll = -(r_swing_euler[0] + r_wrist_euler[0])
    r_pitch = -r_wrist_euler[1]
    r_yaw = r_swing_euler[2] + r_wrist_euler[2]

    joint_pos[G1_L_WRIST_ROLL] = l_roll
    joint_pos[G1_L_WRIST_PITCH] = -l_pitch  # double negation kept verbatim from the reference
    joint_pos[G1_L_WRIST_YAW] = l_yaw
    joint_pos[G1_R_WRIST_ROLL] = r_roll
    joint_pos[G1_R_WRIST_PITCH] = r_pitch
    joint_pos[G1_R_WRIST_YAW] = r_yaw
    return joint_pos

def generate_finger_data(trigger: float, grip: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Synthesize ``(25, 4, 4)`` fingertip transforms from controller inputs.

    The thumb tip sits at x=1; the middle tip joins it when the trigger passes
    0.5 (closing the middle-gesture distance to zero). ``grip`` is accepted
    for interface parity but unused, exactly like the reference.
    """
    del grip
    fingertips = np.zeros((25, 4, 4))
    fingertips[_TIP["thumb"], 0, 3] = 1.0
    if trigger > 0.5:
        fingertips[_TIP["middle"], 0, 3] = 1.0
    return fingertips

def poll_feedback(self, quiet: bool = False) -> bool:
    """Read the newest robot state (if any) into the target fields.

    Returns whether the measured body configuration arrived. ``quiet`` skips the
    miss message, for callers that retry every tick and report once themselves.
    """
    data = self._poller.get_latest()
    if data is None:
        if not quiet:
            print("[FeedbackReader] no feedback data received")
        self.upper_body_position_target = None
        self.left_hand_position_target = None
        self.right_hand_position_target = None
        self.full_body_q_measured = None
        return False

    body_q = data.get("body_q_measured")
    if body_q is not None:
        full = np.asarray(body_q, dtype=np.float64)
        self.full_body_q_measured = full
        self.upper_body_position_target = full[list(UPPER_BODY_MJ_GATHER)]
    else:
        if not quiet:
            print("[FeedbackReader] body_q_measured not in feedback data")
        self.full_body_q_measured = None
        self.upper_body_position_target = None

    left = data.get("left_hand_q_measured")
    right = data.get("right_hand_q_measured")
    self.left_hand_position_target = None if left is None else np.asarray(left, dtype=np.float64)
    self.right_hand_position_target = None if right is None else np.asarray(right, dtype=np.float64)
    return self.full_body_q_measured is not None

def poll(self) -> bool:
    """True exactly when a previously-seen ``reset_count`` has increased."""
    data = self._poller.get_latest()
    count = None if data is None else data.get("reset_count")
    if count is None:

    count = int(count)
    increased = self._last_count is not None and count > self._last_count
    self._last_count = count
    return increased

def __init__(self, robot_options: G1Dofs29Dex3 | None = None) -> None:
    import torch

    from eden.utils.genesis_runtime import transient_robot_env

    self._torch = torch
    self._stack = ExitStack()
    self._env, self._robot = self._stack.enter_context(transient_robot_env(robot_options or G1Dofs29Dex3()))
    robot = self._robot
    if list(robot.dofs_name[:29]) != list(G1_DOFS29_NAME):
        self._stack.close()
        raise ValueError("the FK robot's dofs_name must start with the 29 body joints in MJCF order")
    # Raises (naming the available links) on a miss — same fail-fast as a
    # bad body name in the reference FK.
    _, self._links_idx = self._robot.find_named_links_idx_local([body for body, _ in G1_KEY_FRAMES.values()])
    self._offsets = torch.tensor(
        np.stack([offset for _, offset in G1_KEY_FRAMES.values()]), dtype=torch.float32, device=self._env.device
    )
    self._n_qs = 7 + len(robot.dofs_name)

Returns {key: {"position" (3,), "orientation_wxyz" (4,)}} with the local offsets folded into the positions.

Source code in eden/extensions/teleop/sonic/g1_fk.py 
def key_frame_poses(self, q_mj29: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, dict[str, np.ndarray]]:
    """Key-frame poses for a 29-joint configuration (MJCF order, radians).

    Returns ``{key: {"position" (3,), "orientation_wxyz" (4,)}}`` with the
    local offsets folded into the positions.
    """
    from genesis.utils.geom import transform_by_quat

    from eden.utils.geom import subtract_frame_transforms

    torch = self._torch
    q_mj29 = np.asarray(q_mj29, dtype=np.float64).reshape(29)
    qpos = torch.zeros((1, self._n_qs), dtype=torch.float32, device=self._env.device)
    qpos[0, 3] = 1.0  # free-base identity quaternion (wxyz), root at the origin
    qpos[0, 7:36] = torch.as_tensor(q_mj29, dtype=torch.float32, device=self._env.device)
    self._robot.set_qpos(qpos)  # hands stay at zero; refreshes link poses

    n = len(self._links_idx)
    # relative=True: the MJCF pelvis body frame (the reference's FK root),
    # not the re-origined solver frame the qpos root addresses.
    root_pos = self._robot.get_pos(relative=True)
    root_quat = self._robot.get_quat(relative=True)
    link_pos = self._robot.get_links_pos(ls_idx_local=self._links_idx)[0]
    link_quat = self._robot.get_links_quat(ls_idx_local=self._links_idx)[0]
    rel_pos, rel_quat = subtract_frame_transforms(
        root_pos.expand(n, -1), root_quat.expand(n, -1), link_pos, link_quat
    )
    rel_pos = rel_pos + transform_by_quat(self._offsets, rel_quat)

    return {
        key: {
            "position": rel_pos[i].detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float64),
            "orientation_wxyz": rel_quat[i].detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float64),
        }
        for i, key in enumerate(G1_KEY_FRAMES)
    }

    self,
    with_g1_robot: bool = True,
    enable_waist_tracking: bool = False,
    enable_smpl_vis: bool = False,
    axis_length: float = 0.08,
    ball_radius: float = 0.015,
    robot_opacity: float = 0.4,
    off_screen: bool = False,
) -> None:
    try:
        import pyvista as pv
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise ImportError(f"--vis-vr3pt needs pyvista: {install_hint('sonic-viz')}") from exc
    self._pv = pv
    self._waist_tracking = enable_waist_tracking
    self._smpl_vis = enable_smpl_vis

    self.plotter = pv.Plotter(window_size=(1100, 850), off_screen=off_screen)
    self.plotter.add_axes()
    self.plotter.add_mesh(pv.Plane(i_size=2.0, j_size=2.0), color="lightgray", opacity=0.3)
    for axis, color in zip(np.eye(3), ("red", "green", "blue")):
        self.plotter.add_mesh(pv.Line((0, 0, 0), tuple(0.2 * axis)), color=color, line_width=4)

    # VR keypoints: ball + RGB triad each, positioned via the actor matrix.
    self._kp_actors = []
    for color in VR_BALL_COLORS:
        ball = self.plotter.add_mesh(pv.Sphere(radius=ball_radius), color=color)
        triad = []
        for axis, axis_color in zip(np.eye(3), ("red", "green", "blue")):
            actor = self.plotter.add_mesh(
                pv.Line((0, 0, 0), tuple(axis_length * axis)), color=axis_color, line_width=3
            )
            triad.append(actor)
        self._kp_actors.append((ball, triad))

    # Synthesized head chain: origin -> torso offset -> neck.
    self._chain = pv.PolyData(np.zeros((3, 3)), lines=np.array([2, 0, 1, 2, 1, 2]), force_float=False)
    self.plotter.add_mesh(self._chain, color="orange", line_width=2)

    self._robot = _G1MeshView(self.plotter, robot_opacity) if with_g1_robot else None

    self._smpl_points = None
    if enable_smpl_vis:
        self._smpl_spheres = []
        for i in range(24):
            color = "steelblue" if i in SMPL_LOWER_BODY else "indianred"
            self._smpl_spheres.append(self.plotter.add_mesh(pv.Sphere(radius=0.02), color=color))
        lines = []
        for i in range(1, 24):
            lines.extend([2, SMPL_PARENTS_VIS[i], i])
        self._smpl_bones = pv.PolyData(np.zeros((24, 3)), lines=np.array(lines), force_float=False)
        self.plotter.add_mesh(self._smpl_bones, color="gray", line_width=2)

    self.plotter.show(interactive_update=True, auto_close=False)

def on_frame(self, vr_3pt_pose: np.ndarray, smpl_joints_local: np.ndarray | None) -> None:
    """Update the scene for one calibrated ``(3, 7)`` pose (+ optional SMPL joints)."""
    for row, (ball, triad) in enumerate(self._kp_actors):
        mat = _pose_matrix(vr_3pt_pose[row, :3], vr_3pt_pose[row, 3:])
        ball.user_matrix = mat
        for actor in triad:
            actor.user_matrix = mat

    neck_z = sRot.from_quat(vr_3pt_pose[2, 3:], scalar_first=True).apply([0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
    torso = np.array([0.0, 0.0, TORSO_LINK_OFFSET_Z])
    self._chain.points = np.stack([np.zeros(3), torso, torso + NECK_LINK_LENGTH * neck_z])

    if self._robot is not None and self._waist_tracking:
        # Waist follows the calibrated neck orientation. as_euler("ZYX")
        # returns [z, y, x] = [yaw, pitch, roll]; the waist joints are
        # yaw (q12), roll (q13), pitch (q14).
        yaw, pitch, roll = sRot.from_quat(vr_3pt_pose[2, 3:], scalar_first=True).as_euler("ZYX")
        q = np.zeros(29)
        q[12], q[13], q[14] = yaw, roll, pitch
        self._robot.set_pose(q)

    if self._smpl_vis and smpl_joints_local is not None:
        points = np.asarray(smpl_joints_local) + _SMPL_ANCHOR
        for i, sphere in enumerate(self._smpl_spheres):
            mat = np.eye(4)
            mat[:3, 3] = points[i]
            sphere.user_matrix = mat
        self._smpl_bones.points = points

    self.plotter.update()

start_recording(output_path: str | Path, fps: float | None = None) -> None

Record the current scene and subsequent updates to a .html or .viser file.

Each update advances playback by env.dt, or by 1 / fps when supplied. HTML exports include the interactive player and scene data. Call from the simulation thread, alongside update and stop_recording.

Everything knowable up front is checked here rather than at export time -- the suffix, the frame duration, that Viser can render the requested format, and that the output directory is writable. Viser's serializer is single-use, so an export that only fails once the run is over has lost the trajectory.

Source code in eden/extensions/visualization/viser.py 
def start_recording(self, output_path: str | Path, fps: float | None = None) -> None:
    """Record the current scene and subsequent updates to a .html or .viser file.

    Each update advances playback by ``env.dt``, or by ``1 / fps`` when
    supplied. HTML exports include the interactive player and scene data.
    Call from the simulation thread, alongside ``update`` and ``stop_recording``.

    Everything knowable up front is checked here rather than at export time --
    the suffix, the frame duration, that Viser can render the requested format,
    and that the output directory is writable. Viser's serializer is single-use,
    so an export that only fails once the run is over has lost the trajectory.
    """
    if self.is_recording:
        raise RuntimeError("A Viser recording is already active; call stop_recording() first.")
    path = Path(output_path)
    suffix = path.suffix.lower()
    if suffix not in {".html", ".viser"}:
        raise ValueError("Viser recording output must end in .html or .viser.")
    if fps is not None and (not math.isfinite(fps) or fps <= 0):
        raise ValueError("fps must be finite and positive.")
    dt = self.env.dt if fps is None else 1.0 / fps
    if not math.isfinite(dt) or dt <= 0:
        raise ValueError("Recording frame duration must be finite and positive.")
    if suffix == ".html":
        self._check_html_exporter()
    if path.is_dir():
        raise IsADirectoryError(path)
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    # Fail loudly now if the output directory is not writable, rather than losing a
    # whole recording when it is exported on stop. The directory is the only thing
    # that needs to be writable: ``stop_recording`` renames a sibling temporary file
    # into place, which never opens the destination itself. Mirrors the same check in
    # ``viewer_plugins/mesh_point_selector.py``.
    out_dir = path.parent.resolve()
    if not os.access(out_dir, os.W_OK):
        raise ValueError(f"Cannot record to '{path}': directory '{out_dir}' is not writable.")
    # Seed the initial frame with the current state. Deliberately not ``update()``:
    # that drains the GUI event state, so a reset clicked just before recording
    # started would be consumed here and never reported to the simulation loop.
    if not self._built:
        self.build()
    self._refresh_handles()
    self._recording_path = path
    self._recording_dt = dt
    self._recording = self.server.get_scene_serializer()

docs.text:
stop_recording() -> Path

Save the recording and return its path; fail if no recording is active.

The export is atomic: it writes a sibling temporary file and renames it into place, so a failure leaves the destination -- including a recording already saved there -- untouched instead of truncated. Viser's serializer is single-use, so a failed export ends the recording; that is what the checks in :meth:start_recording are there to make unlikely.

Source code in eden/extensions/visualization/viser.py 
def stop_recording(self) -> Path:
    """Save the recording and return its path; fail if no recording is active.

    The export is atomic: it writes a sibling temporary file and renames it into
    place, so a failure leaves the destination -- including a recording already
    saved there -- untouched instead of truncated. Viser's serializer is single-use,
    so a failed export ends the recording; that is what the checks in
    :meth:`start_recording` are there to make unlikely.
    """
    if self._recording is None:
        raise RuntimeError("No Viser recording is active; call start_recording() first.")
    # Retire the handle up front: ``as_html``/``serialize`` consume it, so nothing below
    # can be retried and leaving it in place would only turn a second call into a
    # confusing "serialize() was already called!" from inside Viser.
    recording, self._recording = self._recording, None
    path, self._recording_path = self._recording_path, None
    assert path is not None
    tmp = path.with_name(f"{path.name}.{os.getpid()}.tmp")
    try:
        if path.suffix.lower() == ".html":
            tmp.write_text(recording.as_html(), encoding="utf-8")
        else:
            tmp.write_bytes(recording.serialize())
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except OSError as e:
        tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Failed to save the Viser recording to '{path}': {e}. Viser's serializer is "
            "single-use, so this recording cannot be exported again."
        ) from e
    return path

docs.text:
Every configurable piece of Eden (the env, the scene and its entities, materials, sensors, managers and their terms, runners) is described by an options class: a Pydantic model that validates when you construct it and serializes into the run's saved config. This page documents the base classes; the pages in this section document each family.

from eden.options.envs import EnvOptions
from eden.options.entities import BoxOptions, SceneOptions

docs.title: Strict and dynamic options
docs.text:
ConfigurableOptions defaults to extra="forbid": a misspelled field raises at construction and names the fields the class does accept. Containers that hold named children (SceneOptions holds entities, *ManagerOptions hold terms, SensorsOptions and CamerasOptions hold sensors and cameras) subclass DynamicConfigurableOptions, which allows extra fields; each extra is one child, keyed by its name. Genesis' own options classes (gs.morphs.*, gs.sensors.*) keep Genesis' strict validation.

Copy an options object with clone() (or copy.deepcopy), not with Pydantic's model_copy(deep=True); and use updated(**changes) to get a validated copy with some fields changed. lock() freezes an options tree and unlock() thaws it. The task configuration guide covers serialization.

ConfigurableOptions: base class for all Eden options.

:class:ConfigurableOptions extends the Genesis Options Pydantic model with Eden conventions: lock()/unlock() to freeze/unfreeze a config, clone() for a lock-aware deep copy, and a best-effort __deepcopy__ that tolerates unpicklable objects (e.g. USD stages).

Copying. clone() is the canonical way to duplicate an options object — prefer it (or bare copy.deepcopy) over pydantic's model_copy(deep=True), because only the former routes through this class's __deepcopy__ and therefore inherits the unpicklable-safe fallback (a value that can't be deep-copied is shared by reference rather than raising). __deepcopy__ is faithful: the clone mirrors the source's lock state. clone(unlock=True) is the explicit "copy so I can edit it" path — it returns a mutable clone regardless of the source, leaving the source untouched. updated(**fields) is the copy-with-changes path: a deep copy with those fields replaced, whose names are validated like construction (so is model_copy(update=...)).

Locking. Locking is tree-scoped and downward-propagating: lock()/unlock() apply to the node they are called on and recurse into all nested options (through declared fields, extras, and any list/tuple/dict of options). They never walk upward, so a child can lock/unlock its own subtree without affecting its parent — reaching a mixed state (e.g. a locked config with one locally-unlocked child) is intentional and supported; the __setattr__ guard keys off each node's own _locked. Both calls are idempotent per node (a no-op if the node is already in the target state), so a redundant parent lock() does not clobber a child that was toggled locally. The lock is not part of an options object's value: a locked object == the same values unlocked.

The default is extra="forbid" so every fixed-schema options class (EnvOptions, entity/material/camera options, rsl_rl configs, ...) rejects misspelled fields loudly. Classes that legitimately carry dynamically-named children (scene entities, manager terms, observation terms, cameras, sensors, splat PCDs) or receive framework-injected .configure() params (name / params) as extras subclass :class:DynamicConfigurableOptions instead, which restores extra="allow".

def __init__(self, **data):
    # Seed type metadata as construction data so BaseModel validates it into
    # __pydantic_extra__ (no-op for extra="forbid" classes, which use
    # the serialization envelope instead).
    data.update(option_metadata(self))
    # NOTE: all of the option modifications/validations should be done in the __init__ method
    try:
        BaseModel.__init__(self, **data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        # A misspelled field on an extra="forbid" class should teach the field set, not just
        # name the typo. Only rewritten when every error is extra_forbidden.
        enriched = _enrich_extra_forbidden(type(self), exc)
        if enriched is None:
            raise
        raise enriched from None

Freeze this options node against further mutation, recursing into all children.

Tree-scoped and downward-propagating: applies to this node and every nested options object (declared fields, extras, and options inside list/tuple/dict). It never walks upward, so locking a child does not lock its parent. Idempotent (a no-op if already locked). See the module docstring for the full lock model.

Source code in eden/options/options.py 
def lock(self):
    """Freeze this options node against further mutation, recursing into all children.

    Tree-scoped and downward-propagating: applies to this node and every nested
    options object (declared fields, extras, and options inside list/tuple/dict).
    It never walks upward, so locking a child does not lock its parent. Idempotent
    (a no-op if already locked). See the module docstring for the full lock model.
    """
    if self._locked:
        return

    self._locked = True

    def lock_recursive(obj):
        if isinstance(obj, ConfigurableOptions):
            obj.lock()
        elif isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
            for item in obj:
                lock_recursive(item)
        elif isinstance(obj, dict):
            for item in obj.values():
                lock_recursive(item)

    for value in self.__dict__.values():
        lock_recursive(value)
    if self.__pydantic_extra__:
        for value in self.__pydantic_extra__.values():
            lock_recursive(value)

Exact mirror of :meth:lock (same downward propagation, no upward walk, same idempotency), so a child can unlock its own subtree without affecting its parent. _locked is exempt from the __setattr__ guard, so this clears it even on a currently-locked object.

Source code in eden/options/options.py 
def unlock(self):
    """Re-enable modification of this options node, recursing into all children.

    Exact mirror of :meth:`lock` (same downward propagation, no upward walk, same
    idempotency), so a child can unlock its own subtree without affecting its
    parent. ``_locked`` is exempt from the ``__setattr__`` guard, so this clears it
    even on a currently-locked object.
    """
    if not self._locked:
        return

    self._locked = False

    def unlock_recursive(obj):
        if isinstance(obj, ConfigurableOptions):
            obj.unlock()
        elif isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
            for item in obj:
                unlock_recursive(item)
        elif isinstance(obj, dict):
            for item in obj.values():
                unlock_recursive(item)

    for value in self.__dict__.values():
        unlock_recursive(value)

    if self.__pydantic_extra__:
        for value in self.__pydantic_extra__.values():
            unlock_recursive(value)

def clone(self, unlock: bool = False) -> "ConfigurableOptions":
    """Return a deep copy of this options object — the canonical way to duplicate options.

    Prefer this (or bare ``copy.deepcopy``) over ``model_copy(deep=True)``: only these
    route through :meth:`__deepcopy__` and thus tolerate unpicklable values (shared by
    reference instead of raising). By default the clone mirrors this object's lock
    state (a copy of a locked config stays locked). Pass ``unlock=True`` for a mutable
    clone regardless of the source — the explicit "copy so I can edit it" path, so
    re-enabling mutation is visible at the call site rather than a silent side effect
    of copying. The source is never modified.
    """
    new_obj = copy.deepcopy(self)
    if unlock:
        new_obj.unlock()
    return new_obj

def updated(self, **updates: Any) -> Self:
    """Return a deep copy with the given fields replaced — the way to override inherited options.

    ``base.track_linear_velocity.updated(weight=0.0)`` reads as what it does, and a misspelled
    name raises on that line (see :meth:`model_copy`, which this builds on: ``deep=True`` so the
    copy shares nothing with the inherited default, keywords so the names are not buried in a dict).

    The copy is always **unlocked**, even when this object is locked. A variant is made to be
    edited further, and the call already says "copy with changes" at the call site — the same
    visibility ``clone(unlock=True)`` asks for. There is no ``unlock=`` switch because every
    keyword here is a field name. ``model_copy`` stays faithful and mirrors the lock state; the
    source is never modified.

    Parameters
    ----------
    **updates
        Field values to change on the copy. Unknown names raise ``ValueError``.

    Returns
    -------
    Self
        The updated, unlocked deep copy.
    """
    copied = self.model_copy(update=updates, deep=True)
    copied.unlock()

def __init__(self, **data):
    # Seed type metadata as construction data so BaseModel validates it into
    # __pydantic_extra__ (no-op for extra="forbid" classes, which use
    # the serialization envelope instead).
    data.update(option_metadata(self))
    # NOTE: all of the option modifications/validations should be done in the __init__ method
    try:
        BaseModel.__init__(self, **data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        # A misspelled field on an extra="forbid" class should teach the field set, not just
        # name the typo. Only rewritten when every error is extra_forbidden.
        enriched = _enrich_extra_forbidden(type(self), exc)
        if enriched is None:
            raise
        raise enriched from None

docs.title: Resolving options classes by name
docs.text:
eden.options.catalog answers "which options class does this name mean?" for the eden view and eden snap commands and for robots: ROBOT_REGISTRY maps a robot key to its class, and the curated MANIFEST describes assets semantically (category, placement, tags).

Resolving entity Options classes by name — two layers over one "module:Class" pointer.

Eden assets (eden.options.objects.*, eden.options.robots.*) know how to load a mesh (their EntityOptions carry up/front/scale etc.) but the question "which Options class does this name mean?" is answered here, two ways, both lazily importing only the one module they need:

  • Auto-scan index (:func:find_entity_options / :func:entity_options_index) — exhaustive. A filesystem walk of the asset packages, cached on disk and keyed by a source fingerprint, maps every class name (RoboLabYcbBanana) and family-registry key (robolab/ycb/banana) to its "module:Class" pointer. This backs the eden view / eden snap CLI, where a warm lookup imports only the single defining module.

  • Curated manifest (:data:MANIFEST) — a hand-curated semantic subset. An asset is curated by decorating its Options class::

    @MANIFEST.curate("sofa", "furniture/seating", tags=("seating",), description="a couch")
@REPLICA_CAD_OBJECT_REGISTRY.register(name="frl_apartment_sofa")
class FRLApartmentSofa(ReplicaCADObjectOptions): ...

What's curated is semantic only (no EntityOptions field is re-declared): category (/-delimited taxonomy path), placement (floor | surface | wall | ceiling), support_surface (place-on target), container (place-in target), tags, description. Physical pose stays on the Options class (up/front/scale); AssetSpec.movable is derived at curation time from the constructed Options (not is_fixed_base), never hand-curated, so it can't drift from the class.

Variant families (one Options class serving many mesh variants, e.g. Objaverse) curate each variant with the direct-call form and make_kwargs — the variant selector baked into :meth:AssetSpec.make (explicit make() overrides still win)::

    MANIFEST.curate("apple_3", "food/fruit", make_kwargs={"variant": 3})(ObjaverseApple)

Population is never eager — so importing Eden stays cheap no matter how many assets exist: a @curate decorator registers its asset only when that family module is imported, and re-import is idempotent (a true name collision raises); :meth:AssetManifest.build imports the known families on demand; :meth:ensure is the build-if-empty entry point for consumers.

Both layers share one "module:Class" spelling and one lazy resolver (:func:_resolve): AssetSpec stores options_path (so :meth:AssetManifest.summary rows are JSON-ready and :meth:make imports only the one class it constructs), and the auto-scan index stores the same.

from eden.options.catalog import MANIFEST, find_entity_options
MANIFEST.ensure()                                  # populate (imports asset families)
MANIFEST.facets()                                  # what can I query? axes → valid values
MANIFEST.names(category="furniture/seating")       # drill down → ['armchair','chair','sofa']
MANIFEST.search("mug")                             # free text → ['coffee_cup', ...]
opts = MANIFEST.make("sofa", default_root_pos=(0, 0, 0))   # lazily imports + constructs
cls = find_entity_options("RoboLabYcbBanana")      # exhaustive auto-scan lookup

curate(name: str, category: str, *, placement: Placement = 'floor', support_surface: bool = False, container: bool = False, tags=(), description: str = '', make_kwargs: dict | None = None)

Curate the decorated EntityOptions subclass as an asset.

Usable as a stacked decorator, or in direct-call form for variant families (one class, many curated names): curate("apple_3", ..., make_kwargs={"variant": 3})(cls).

Source code in eden/options/catalog.py 
def curate(
    self,
    name: str,
    category: str,
    *,
    placement: Placement = "floor",
    support_surface: bool = False,
    container: bool = False,
    tags=(),
    description: str = "",
    make_kwargs: dict | None = None,
):
    """Curate the decorated ``EntityOptions`` subclass as an asset.

    Usable as a stacked decorator, or in direct-call form for variant families
    (one class, many curated names): ``curate("apple_3", ..., make_kwargs={"variant": 3})(cls)``.
    """
    kwargs = dict(make_kwargs or {})

    def deco(cls):
        # Construct the Options once, here where the class is in hand, to derive `movable`
        # the way make() actually builds it (running model_post_init's fixed/is_fixed_base
        # unification). This also fail-fasts at the curation site if make_kwargs is wrong,
        # rather than at a downstream make()/query. Options construction is offline (no
        # mesh load — that happens at entity build) and cheap.
        try:
            movable = not cls(**kwargs).is_fixed_base
        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — re-raise with the curation site attached
            raise ValueError(f"curate({name!r}): cannot construct {cls.__name__}(**{kwargs!r}): {exc}") from exc
        self._curate(
            AssetSpec(
                name=name,
                options_path=f"{cls.__module__}:{cls.__name__}",
                category=category,
                placement=placement,
                support_surface=support_surface,
                container=container,
                tags=tuple(tags),
                description=description,
                make_kwargs=kwargs,
                movable=movable,
            )
        )
        return cls

    return deco

names(*, category: str | None = None, placement: str | None = None, tag: str | None = None, support_surface: bool | None = None, container: bool | None = None, movable: bool | None = None) -> list[str]

Asset names matching every given filter. Filter axes/values come from :meth:facets.

Source code in eden/options/catalog.py 
def names(
    self,
    *,
    category: str | None = None,
    placement: str | None = None,
    tag: str | None = None,
    support_surface: bool | None = None,
    container: bool | None = None,
    movable: bool | None = None,
) -> list[str]:
    """Asset names matching every given filter. Filter axes/values come from :meth:`facets`."""
    # string axes treat ""/None as "no filter"; the boolean axes need `is not None` since
    # False is a real filter value.
    out = []
    for name, spec in self:
        if category and not _is_under(spec.category_path, category):
            continue
        if placement and spec.placement != placement:
            continue
        if tag and tag not in spec.tags:
            continue
        if support_surface is not None and spec.support_surface != support_surface:
            continue
        if container is not None and spec.container != container:
            continue
        if movable is not None and spec.movable != movable:
            continue
        out.append(name)
    return sorted(out)

Find asset names by free text.

Case-insensitive substring match over each asset's name, category path, tags, and description — the loosest entry point for an agent resolving task language ("a mug", "trash") to catalog names. An empty query raises (use :meth:names or :meth:summary to list the whole catalog).

def search(self, query: str) -> list[str]:
    """Find asset names by free text.

    Case-insensitive substring match over each asset's name, category path, tags, and
    description — the loosest entry point for an agent resolving task language
    ("a mug", "trash") to catalog names. An empty query raises (use :meth:`names` or
    :meth:`summary` to list the whole catalog).
    """
    q = query.strip().lower()
    if not q:
        raise ValueError("search() needs a non-empty query; use names() or summary() to list everything")
    return sorted(
        name for name, spec in self if q in " ".join((name, spec.category, *spec.tags, spec.description)).lower()
    )

def facets(self) -> dict[str, list]:
    """Describe the available queries: each filter axis :meth:`names` accepts → its present values."""
    cats, places, tags, supports, containers, movables = set(), set(), set(), set(), set(), set()
    for _, spec in self:
        cats.add(spec.category)
        places.add(spec.placement)
        tags.update(spec.tags)
        supports.add(spec.support_surface)
        containers.add(spec.container)
        movables.add(spec.movable)
    return {
        "category": sorted(cats),
        "placement": sorted(places),
        "tag": sorted(tags),
        "support_surface": sorted(supports),
        "container": sorted(containers),
        "movable": sorted(movables),
    }

def tree(self) -> dict:
    """Nested taxonomy: ``{node: {child: {...}, '__assets__': [names]}}`` from category paths."""

def find_entity_options(name: str) -> type[BaseEntityOptions]:
    """Resolve an Options class by class name (``RoboLabYcbBanana``) or registry
    key (``robolab/ycb/banana``). Warm lookups import only the defining module.
    """
    index = entity_options_index()
    target = index.get(name)
    if target is None:
        close = difflib.get_close_matches(name, list(index), n=5)
        hint = f" Did you mean: {', '.join(close)}?" if close else ""
        raise ValueError(f"No entity options found for {name}.{hint}")
    return _resolve(target)

Actuator options describe a physical motor (rotor inertia, gear ratio, effort and velocity limits, ...) so a robot preset can derive its armature and PD gains from the hardware instead of hand-tuned numbers. ActuatorSpecOptions is the base; the presets below model the motors of the built-in Unitree, DAMIAO and LimX robots. The robots guide shows how a robot preset uses them.

from eden.options.actuators import Unitree7520_14

The helpers that turn a motor spec into armature and gains (reflected_inertia, raibert_heuristic_kp, ...) are on the robotics utilities page.

@classmethod
def ARMATURE(cls) -> float:
    if isinstance(cls.ROTOR_INERTIA, float):
        assert isinstance(cls.GEAR_RATIO, float), "Expected single-stage gearbox (1 gear ratio)"
        return reflected_inertia(cls.ROTOR_INERTIA, cls.GEAR_RATIO)
    elif isinstance(cls.ROTOR_INERTIA, tuple):
        assert isinstance(cls.GEAR_RATIO, tuple), "Expected two-stage planetary gearbox (3 gear ratios)"
        assert len(cls.ROTOR_INERTIA) == len(cls.GEAR_RATIO)
        assert len(cls.GEAR_RATIO) == 3, "Expected two-stage planetary gearbox (3 gear ratios)"
        return reflected_inertia_from_two_stage_planetary(cls.ROTOR_INERTIA, cls.GEAR_RATIO)
    else:
        return 0.0

Entity options describe one thing in the scene: a mesh or URDF/MJCF asset (EntityOptions, RobotOptions), a primitive shape, a terrain, a bank of per-env variants (GroupedEntityOptions) or a multi-entity rig (CompositeEntityOptions). SceneOptions holds them as named children; each name becomes the key of env.entities. The entities guide explains pose frames, DOF fields and contact parameters; the scenes guide covers scenes and terrain.

from eden.options.entities import BoxOptions, SceneOptions

scene_options = SceneOptions(box=BoxOptions(size=(0.1, 0.1, 0.1), default_root_pos=(0.0, 0.0, 0.6)))

def named_entities(self) -> dict[str, BaseEntityOptions]:
    """Every entity the scene will build, keyed by final entity name (composites expanded)."""
    out: dict[str, BaseEntityOptions] = {}
    for key, entity in (self.__pydantic_extra__ or {}).items():
        if key.startswith("_option_"):
            continue
        if isinstance(entity, CompositeEntityOptions):
            out.update(entity.entity_options())
        elif isinstance(entity, BaseEntityOptions):
            out[key] = entity
    return out

docs.title: remove_entity
docs.text:
remove_entity(name: str) -> None

Remove the entity placed under scene key name, together with its own attachment.

The supported way for a task variant to drop an entity (see eden/tasks/robosuite/variants.py::drop_object). Only an entity added by name (an extra) is removable; one declared as a field of a SceneOptions subclass (DroidSceneOptions.robot) is part of that scene class. An attachments_dict entry that welds the removed entity onto a parent goes with it. An entity that other entities are welded onto cannot be removed — remove the children first. Nothing else that names the entity is touched — manager terms, cameras, sensors — so update those too, otherwise they fail to resolve the entity at build time.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION name

Scene key of the entity. A composite is removed whole, under its placement key; one of its bodies cannot be removed on its own.

TYPE: str

RAISES DESCRIPTION RuntimeError

If the scene options are locked (checked before anything else).

KeyError

If the scene has no entity name (the message lists the removable entities), or name cannot be removed: a declared field, or a body of a composite (the message says which).

ValueError

If another entity is attached to the one being removed.

def remove_entity(self, name: str) -> None:
    """Remove the entity placed under scene key ``name``, together with its own attachment.

    The supported way for a task variant to drop an entity (see
    ``eden/tasks/robosuite/variants.py::drop_object``). Only an entity added by
    name (an extra) is removable; one declared as a field of a ``SceneOptions`` subclass
    (``DroidSceneOptions.robot``) is part of that scene class. An ``attachments_dict`` entry
    that welds the removed entity onto a parent goes with it. An entity that *other* entities
    are welded onto cannot be removed — remove the children first. Nothing else that names
    the entity is touched — manager terms, cameras, sensors — so update those too, otherwise
    they fail to resolve the entity at build time.

    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        Scene key of the entity. A composite is removed whole, under its placement key; one of
        its bodies cannot be removed on its own.

    Raises
    ------
    RuntimeError
        If the scene options are locked (checked before anything else).
    KeyError
        If the scene has no entity ``name`` (the message lists the removable entities), or
        ``name`` cannot be removed: a declared field, or a body of a composite (the message
        says which).
    ValueError
        If another entity is attached to the one being removed.
    """
    try:
        entity = self._removable_child(name, noun="entity")
    except KeyError as err:
        # The generic "not found" would be wrong for an entity that exists but is not an extra.
        reason = self._unremovable_entity_reason(name)
        if reason is None:
            raise
        raise KeyError(reason) from err
    # A composite produces several scene entities (arm + gripper); all of them go with it.
    removed_names = set(entity.entity_names) if isinstance(entity, CompositeEntityOptions) else {name}
    dependents = sorted(
        child
        for child, spec in self.attachments_dict.items()
        if spec[0] in removed_names and child not in removed_names
    )
    if dependents:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Cannot remove entity '{name}': {dependents} are attached to it via attachments_dict. "
            f"Remove those entities first."
        )

    self._remove_named_child(name, noun="entity")
    # Rebuilt, not edited in place: a shallow model_copy() shares the dict with its source scene,
    # which would silently lose its own welds.
    self.attachments_dict = {
        child: spec for child, spec in self.attachments_dict.items() if child not in removed_names
    }

Entity options for Eden, wrapping Genesis' Entity related options.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION up

The object's up direction in its own coordinate system (use gs view to visualize that coordinate system). On loading, the object is rotated so this axis becomes world +z.

front

The object's front direction in its own coordinate system (use gs view to visualize that coordinate system). On loading, the object is rotated so this axis becomes world +x.

local_dir

Where the asset is cached. Unset, it is the family's assets_subdir under the asset root, resolved at load time by :meth:resolve_local_dir; :meth:fetch_asset downloads into it.

file

Path to the entity file.

scale

Scale of the entity: uniform, or along each axis of the asset's frame (a scanned mesh measured to a real object's size, say). Unequal axes need a mesh file (:data:MESH_FILE_SUFFIXES); URDF, MJCF and USD assets scale uniformly.

collision

Whether the entity needs to be considered for collision checking. Defaults to True.

decimate

Whether to decimate (simplify) the mesh. Defaults to True. This is only used for RigidEntity.

TYPE: bool

decimate_face_num

The number of faces to decimate to. Defaults to 1000. This is only used for RigidEntity.

TYPE: int

decimate_aggressiveness

How hard the decimation process will try to match the target number of faces, as an integer ranging from 0 to 8. 0 is lossless. 2 preserves all features of the original geometry. 5 may significantly alter the original geometry if necessary. 8 does what needs to be done at all costs. Defaults to 3. This is only used for RigidEntity.

TYPE: int

convexify

Whether to convexify the entity. When convexify is True, all the meshes in the entity will each be converted to a set of convex hulls. The mesh will be decomposed into multiple convex components if the convex hull is not sufficient to meet the desired accuracy (see 'decompose_(robot|object)_error_threshold' documentation). The module 'coacd' is used for this decomposition process. If not given, it defaults to True for RigidEntity and False for other deformable entities.

TYPE: bool

decompose_object_error_threshold

For basic rigid objects (mug, table...), skip convex decomposition if the relative difference between the volume of original mesh and its convex hull is lower than this threshold. 0.0 to enforce decomposition, float("inf") to disable it completely. Defaults to 0.15 (15%).

TYPE: float

decompose_robot_error_threshold

For poly-articulated robots, skip convex decomposition if the relative difference between the volume of original mesh and its convex hull is lower than this threshold. 0.0 to enforce decomposition, float("inf") to disable it completely. Defaults to float("inf").

TYPE: float

coacd_threshold

The threshold for the CoACD algorithm. Defaults to 0.05.

TYPE: float

coacd_preprocess_resolution

The resolution for the CoACD algorithm. Defaults to 100.

TYPE: int

links_to_keep

A list of link names that should not be skipped during link merging. Defaults to [].

TYPE: list of str

align

Whether Genesis re-frames a floating root link onto its centre of mass and principal axes. None (default) lets Genesis decide: on for a basic rigid object (one free root body, nothing articulated under it), off otherwise. An aligned link's centre of mass and inertia belong to the solver and cannot be written after build, so set False on an object whose inertial properties a task randomizes per env (a COM offset, a per-env inertia); its free joint then sits at the authored body frame, as in MuJoCo, so for a single-body free object get_pos() equals get_pos(relative=True) (and likewise get_quat). The cost: the unaligned free body loses its diagonal mass block (linear and angular motion couple through the COM offset), the numerical-stability benefit alignment exists for.

TYPE: bool | None

default_armature

Rotor inertia Genesis fills in at scene.build() for every DOF of a body moved by a single hinge or slide joint whose armature the asset leaves at zero: every URDF joint (URDF has no armature element) and any MJCF joint that omits armature or authors it as 0. Ball, free and multi-joint bodies are skipped, and a nonzero authored value is kept. 0.0 disables the fill. Defaults to 0.1, usually far too high for low-stiffness joints, so set default_dofs_armature from the source asset instead of inheriting it.

TYPE: float

is_fixed_base

Whether the entity is fixed in the environment. A URDF, USD or mesh asset is built to match. An MJCF is not — Genesis has no fixed switch for it — so declare what the file says: False when its base body carries a <freejoint/>, True when it has no joint or any other joint of its own (hinge, slide or ball). A mismatch raises at build.

Whether the entity is articulated.

is_actuated

Whether the entity is actuated.

default_root_pos

The default position of the loaded entity's root link. Will not take effect if the entity is attached to another entity.

default_root_quat

The default orientation of the loaded entity's root link (w, x, y, z). Will not take effect if the entity is attached to another entity.

dofs_name

The names of the DOFs to be treated as controllable DOFs.

Class-level default actuator specification map for entity DOFs.

The default velocities of the DOFs of the entity.

The default control position gains of the DOFs of the entity.

The default control velocity gains of the DOFs of the entity.

The default stiffnesses of the DOFs of the entity. If provided, the value will be used over the stiffness in dofs_spec.

The default dampings of the DOFs of the entity. If provided, the value will be used over the damping in dofs_spec.

The default armatures of the DOFs of the entity. If provided, the value will be used over the armature in dofs_spec.

def resolve_local_dir(self) -> str:
    """Where this entity's asset is cached: ``local_dir``, else ``assets_subdir`` under the asset root.

def fetch_asset(self, file: str | None = None) -> str:
    """The local path of ``file`` (default: ``self.file``) from this entity's Hub dataset, downloaded if missing.

    Fetches with this entity's ``registry``, ``dataset`` and :meth:`resolve_local_dir`. Call this rather
    than ``get_asset_path(..., local_dir=options.local_dir)``: an unset ``local_dir`` passed on raw would
    fetch into the asset root instead of the family's ``assets_subdir``, and nothing would fail.
    """
    return get_asset_path(
        self.file if file is None else file,
        registry=self.registry,
        dataset=self.dataset,
        local_dir=self.resolve_local_dir(),
    )

@classmethod
def fetch_family_asset(cls, file: str) -> str:
    """The local path of ``file`` from this family's default Hub dataset, downloaded if missing.

    For a file the family's dataset ships that no entity is built from (a task catalogue's BDDL file, a
    background image), so there is no options instance to call :meth:`fetch_asset` on: fetches with the
    class's default ``registry``/``dataset``/``local_dir``, the last resolved like :meth:`resolve_local_dir`.
    Nothing is validated as an entity, so the file may be of any type.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        When the family declares no Hub ``registry``/``dataset`` default, so there is no dataset to fetch from.
    """
    fields = cls.model_fields
    registry, dataset = fields["registry"].default, fields["dataset"].default
    if registry is None or dataset is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{cls.__name__}.fetch_family_asset({file!r}): the family has no Hub dataset to fetch from "
            f"(registry={registry!r}, dataset={dataset!r}). Give {cls.__name__} registry and dataset defaults, "
            f"or open a local file directly instead of fetching it."
        )
    return get_asset_path(
        file,
        registry=registry,
        dataset=dataset,
        local_dir=resolve_local_dir(fields["local_dir"].default, cls.assets_subdir),
    )

def get_morph(self) -> Rod:
    # ``eden.engine.solvers.mochi.morphs.Rod`` inherits only ``Morph`` (no ``fixed`` / ``contype`` /
    # ``conaffinity`` / ``batch_fixed_verts``), and genesis options forbid extras, so the generic

    kwargs: dict[str, object] = {

        "radius": self.radius,
        "n_cross_section_segments": self.n_cross_section_segments,
        "is_closed_loop": self.is_closed_loop,
        "pos": self.default_root_pos,
        "quat": self.default_root_quat,
        "collision": self.collision,
        "visualization": self.visualization,
    }
    if isinstance(self.morph, dict):
        kwargs.update(**self.morph)
    elif isinstance(self.morph, Morph):
        kwargs.update(**self.morph.model_dump())
    return Rod(**kwargs)

docs.text:
GroupedEntityOptions(**data)

Bases: BaseEntityOptions

Grouped entity used for heterogeneous batching.

Supports both non-articulated entities (Mesh, Primitive) and articulated entities (URDF) that share the same joint structure (same number of links, joints, and DOFs).

Each variant contributes its morph (file or shape, mesh processing, its own default_root_pos / default_root_quat), and may hold its own value for some of the group's fields. A variant holds a value when it differs from the field's default, whether passed in or its catalog class's default.

  • Per variant (variant_values(), variant_materials): the geom fields (default_geoms_friction*, default_geoms_sol_params), the per-DOF ones (default_dofs_* and soft_dofs_pos_limits) and the material's rho / friction*. Each env takes its variant's own value, else the group's. Variants that differ in a simulated DOF field (gains, stiffness, damping, armature, frictionloss, force limits) need EnvOptions(batch_dofs_info=True). A per-variant rho rescales each env's mass after the build, so it needs a mesh or primitive variant, whose mass Genesis computes from its density.
  • Shared (shared_dof_fields(), shared_dofs_spec): dofs_name and default_dofs_spring_ref, the group's own or, when it sets none, that of the first variant that sets one; a variant's own different value is refused. So is a variant class's dofs_spec that differs from another's.
  • Group only: every other field (surface, color, is_fixed_base, the support and collision mask fields, the other material fields): a variant's own different value is refused.

A variant overrides the group's own value for a per-variant field only with a value other than its class's default: one equal to the class default is read as inherited and refused, as the group's value would silently skip it. The group's value is also refused when every variant overrides it, as it would apply to none of them. check_variants runs these checks; the entity runs it again before the build.

def check_variants(self) -> None:
    """Refuse what the variants hold that the entity cannot apply as configured (raises ``ValueError``).

    Run at construction, and again by the entity before the scene is built: a TaskMod or any other code
    that assigns a field of the group or of a variant after construction never re-runs
    ``model_post_init``, so its edit would otherwise go unchecked.
    """
    self._refuse_variant_group_only_values()
    self._refuse_variant_shared_dof_values()
    for i, variant in enumerate(self.grouped_entities):
        if variant.material is not None:
            self._refuse_variant_material(i, variant.material)
    self._refuse_implicit_variant_overrides()
    self._refuse_unused_group_values()

docs.title: CompositeEntityOptions
docs.text:
CompositeEntityOptions(**data)

Bases: ConfigurableOptions

A composite of several entities added to a scene as a single unit.

A composite is a real, validated Options (it round-trips through the config system and declares its own fields). It stays in :class:SceneOptions as-is — a task adds it by name like any other entity, SceneOptions(robot=Droid(...)) — and the env build loop expands it into ordinary entities + weld wiring (see RLEnvBase scene construction). A composite adds no runtime behaviour of its own beyond "these named entities + these welds", which env.entities + attach_to already provide, so there is deliberately no composite runtime entity.

Subclasses describe the rig by implementing :meth:entity_parts (the ordered (name, sub-entity Options) pairs) and, when parts are welded, :meth:attachments; :meth:entity_options keys those parts by name, refusing a collision that would otherwise cost the rig a body silently. The scene placement key must equal :attr:primary_name (the root body), so the key is meaningful (not silently discarded) and downstream terms can reference the sub-entities by the composite's own names. Concrete composites — an arm + gripper (a manipulator), a humanoid + hands — live in eden/options/robots/composite.

The named sub-entities keyed by name (uncopied), and where a name collision is caught.

Framework-owned: subclasses implement :meth:entity_parts instead, so this check cannot be bypassed by method dispatch.

Two bodies under one name collapse to a single entry, leaving the composite one body short with nothing downstream noticing: :attr:entity_names, :meth:expand and the cross-composite check in :meth:SceneOptions.model_post_init all read this dict, so none of them can see what has already been overwritten. def entity_options(self) -> dict[str, "BaseEntityOptions"]:
    """The named sub-entities keyed by name (uncopied), and where a name collision is caught.

    Framework-owned: subclasses implement :meth:`entity_parts` instead, so this check cannot
    be bypassed by method dispatch.

    Two bodies under one name collapse to a single entry, leaving the composite one body
    short with nothing downstream noticing: :attr:`entity_names`, :meth:`expand` and the
    cross-composite check in :meth:`SceneOptions.model_post_init` all read *this* dict, so
    none of them can see what has already been overwritten. Checked here, on every call, not
    only at construction (:meth:`model_post_init` calls this) — these Options do not
    ``validate_assignment``, so a ``*_name`` reassigned after construction would slip past a
    construction-time-only guard.
    """
    parts = self.entity_parts()
    names = [name for name, _ in parts]
    collisions = sorted({name for name in names if names.count(name) > 1})
    if collisions:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{type(self).__name__} gives two bodies the same name {collisions}, but a "
            f"composite's entity names ARE the scene's entity names, so each body needs its "
            f"own; got {names}. Set the colliding '*_name' field(s) to something distinct."
        )
    return dict(parts)

def expand(self) -> tuple[dict[str, "BaseEntityOptions"], dict[str, tuple[str, str]]]:
    """Return ``(named_entities, attachments)`` for the scene build loop.

    The sub-entity Options are deep-copied so one composite instance can be placed in
    several scenes (or reused from the registry) without the scenes aliasing — and
    mutating — the same Options. (``copy.deepcopy`` — not pydantic ``model_copy`` —
    because genesis' Options define ``__deepcopy__(self, memo)``.)
    """
    entities = {name: copy.deepcopy(opts) for name, opts in self.entity_options().items()}
    return entities, dict(self.attachments())
