docs.title: EnvOptions
docs.text:
EnvOptions(**data)

Bases: ConfigurableOptions

Top-level environment configuration (sim, solvers, batching).

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION num_envs

Number of environments to run in parallel.

sim_dt

Simulation time step.

sim_substeps

Number of simulation substeps.

decimation

Physics steps per control (env) step. The control step is sim_dt * decimation.

requires_grad

Whether to enable differentiable mode. Defaults to False.

TYPE: bool

episode_length_s

Length of the episode in seconds.

use_gjk_collision

Whether to use GJK collision detection. Defaults to True. If False, MPR+GJK will be used.

solver

Constraint solver (Newton or conjugate gradient).

integrator

Rigid-body integrator. "approximate_implicitfast" (default) is Genesis' own fast scheme. "implicitfast" and "euler" are MuJoCo's integrators of the same name, for tasks ported from a MuJoCo stack: "implicitfast" integrates joint damping and the position actuators' velocity gain implicitly, as MuJoCo does, and "euler" integrates the PD controller explicitly, which is why an actuated entity then folds kd * substep_dt into its armature. Only damping Genesis itself applies is ever implicit: a torque-mode action term (control_dofs_force, e.g. ExplicitPDController) computes -kd * qdot itself, and it stays explicit under all three (see "Implicit Damping" in docs/guides/entities.md).

impratio

Ratio of frictional to normal constraint impedance at contacts (MuJoCo's impratio); must be positive. None (default) lets Genesis resolve it: 100 with the elliptic cone, 1 otherwise.

constraint_timeconst

Time constant for the constraint solver. If None, it will be computed as max(0.01, 2 * sim_dt / sim_substeps).

max_collision_pairs

Maximum number of collision pairs.

iterations

Maximum constraint-solver iterations.

tolerance

Convergence tolerance for the constraint solver, as a ratio against the scene's free-motion cost. If None, Genesis resolves it from the floating-point precision (1e-6 for single, 1e-9 for double). Defaults to None — pinning a literal here means a Genesis release that re-scales what the ratio is quoted against (as https://github.com/Genesis-Embodied-AI/Genesis/pull/3194 did) silently moves Eden's convergence gate.

ls_iterations

Maximum line-search iterations per constraint-solver iteration.

ls_tolerance

Line-search convergence tolerance.

enable_self_collision

Whether to enable self collision detection. Defaults to True.

enable_neutral_collision

Keep self-collision pairs that already overlap in an entity's neutral configuration (qpos0). Defaults to False, where Genesis drops every such pair for good. Its overlap test is a voxel approximation, so it can drop a pair that only comes within millimetres at qpos0 -- set True to keep the MJCF's full collision set. The switch is scene-wide (a rigid-solver option, not a per-entity one): True keeps the pairs that overlap at qpos0 on every articulated entity in the scene, so a second robot whose collision meshes genuinely interpenetrate at qpos0 then fights itself from the first step.

batch_links_info

Whether to batch links information. Defaults to False.

batch_joints_info

Whether to batch joints information. Defaults to False.

batch_dofs_info

Whether to batch DOFs information. Defaults to True.

enable_multi_contact

Whether to enable multi-contact detection. Defaults to True.

enable_torsional_friction

Opt-in torsional friction: whether contacts also resist relative spin about their normal (one extra constraint axis per contact). Defaults to False. Enable it when spin resistance matters (e.g. a peg twisting in a hole, an object twisting inside a grasp). This switch only adds the axis — its strength is per geom, from RigidMaterialOptions.friction_torsional or default_geoms_friction_torsional, and an MJCF geom that does not declare condim >= 4 parses to 0, i.e. no spin resistance until a coefficient is set. See docs/guides/entities.md.

enable_rolling_friction

Opt-in rolling friction: whether contacts also resist rolling about their tangent axes (two extra constraint axes per contact). Requires enable_torsional_friction. Strength is per geom like the torsional axis, from RigidMaterialOptions.friction_rolling or default_geoms_friction_rolling. Defaults to False. Enable it when rolling resistance matters (e.g. a ball settling on a plane).

friction_cone

Shape of the friction cone. "pyramidal" (default) is robust and easy to solve; "elliptic" is the exact isotropic cone, harder to solve but the only one that supports contact_resolution="signorini". Unsupported with the noslip solver (noslip_iterations > 0) or requires_grad.

contact_resolution

How a contact's normal force and friction force are resolved against each other. "signorini" bounds friction against the normal force the contact has developed, so sliding never inflates it — a body launched horizontally decelerates at mu * g instead of lifting off — at the cost of extra solver iterations. It requires friction_cone="elliptic" and solver="newton". "convex" poses the contact as a single convex program, which converges more predictably on stiff scenes but lets fast sliding buy normal force. Defaults to None, which resolves to "signorini" with the elliptic cone and the Newton solver, and "convex" otherwise.

noslip_iterations

Number of iterations for the noslip solver. Defaults to 0 (disabled). noslip is a post-processing step after the main solver to suppress slip/drift. Recommended to set this value to 5 for manipulation tasks or when slip/drift is a big problem.

env_spacing

Spacing between environments. Defaults to (0.0, 0.0).

center_envs_at_origin

Whether to center environments at the origin. Defaults to False.

show_link_frame

Whether to show link frames. Defaults to False.

show_world_frame

Whether to show world frames. Defaults to False.

show_camera_frustums

Whether to show camera frustums. Defaults to False.

segmentation_level

Level of segmentation. Defaults to "entity".

show_FPS

Whether to show FPS for profiling. Defaults to False.

enable_default_keybinds

Whether to enable the default viewer keyboard shortcuts. Defaults to True.

background_color

RGB background color (each component in [0, 1]) for the viewer/renderer. Defaults to (0.04, 0.08, 0.12).

rasterizer_shadows

Whether Rasterizer viewers and camera sensors render shadows. Defaults to True.

update_sensors_every_substep

If False (default), Genesis's SensorManager.step() runs only on the last sub-step of the env decimation loop. Intermediate sub-step sensor readings would be discarded by the next call before anything reads them (observation_manager.compute() reads from the sensor cache once at the end of step()), so updating them is pure waste — for ray-casting depth cameras at perceptive_mimic scale this is a ~2.3× end-to-end env.step() speedup at decimation=4.

The skip auto-disables on a per-step basis when any sensor declares Genesis-level SensorOptions.history_length or delay (i.e. the SensorManager allocates timeline / return rings) — those rings need sim-rate fresh writes to stay correct, so leaving the optimisation on by default is safe even for sensor-history users.

Set True to force per-sub-step updates unconditionally (mostly useful for an A/B comparison against per-sub-step updates).

record_final_observations

Snapshot pre-reset observations for done envs into extras['final_observations'].

Off by default. When on, RLEnvBase.step() runs one extra observation_manager.compute(update_history=False) every step. The returned extras dict gains a 'final_observations' entry shaped (num_envs, *obs_shape) per group; rows for non-done envs are zero, and on a no-termination step every row is zero. For groups with history_length > 0 the row is history-shaped with the freshly- computed post-physics frame in the most-recent slot (composed via CircularBuffer.peek_buffer; the canonical once-per-step advance still happens in the post-reset compute).

No per-step GPU→CPU sync. Both the gating logic and the snapshot copy stay on-device. Cost: one extra observation_manager.compute(update_history=False) per step plus one torch.where per observation group.

rsl_rl PPO does not consume this, by design — rsl_rl 5.x reads only the "time_outs", "log" and "episode" extras keys. rsl_rl bootstraps time-out V-targets from V(s_t) via extras['time_outs'] (a deliberate approximation; not something this flag changes). Leaving this flag off in pure rsl_rl runs costs nothing.

Turn it on for off-policy algorithms whose replay buffers need the actual s' for time-out transitions (FastSAC), eval-recording callbacks that segment trajectories on done and need the real terminal frame for visualization / per-trajectory metrics, or a future Holosoma-style PPO runner that bootstraps from V(s_{t+1}^{phys}) instead of rsl_rl's V(s_t) proxy.

cuda_graph_options

Replay the graded phase of RLEnvBase.step — metric_manager.compute, the observation terms' post_physics_refresh, termination_manager.compute and reward_manager.compute — from a CUDA graph instead of launching its kernels one by one; None (the default) runs it eagerly. CudaGraphOptions() turns it on with the default capture and validation settings, documented there.

These managers only read the post-physics state and write their own buffers, but they do it in hundreds of small kernels, and on a host-bound step the launches are the cost: on BeyondMimic at 4096 envs the phase takes ~3 ms of host time eagerly, against ~5 µs for the replay plus ~70 µs for the checks before it (see docs/guides/environments.md). CUDA only (a CPU or Metal backend raises at build), and only an RLEnvBase has a graded phase (any other env raises at construction). A training-throughput switch: the replay commands (eden inference, eden export, eden deploy) reset it in a run's config (see :attr:training_only_fields).

The options configuring the fem_solver. Defaults to None.

The options configuring the sph_solver. Defaults to None.

The options configuring the mochi_solver (Meta's implicit multi-physics solver: rigid/articulated bodies, tetrahedral solids, shells and rods in one Newton system with penalty contact). A scene with a Mochi entity may hold only Mochi and kinematic entities, and cannot be differentiable. Leave MochiOptions.dt unset — the solver substep is sim_dt / sim_substeps like every other solver. Run with en.init(precision="64") unless every penalty_coefficient is lowered. Defaults to None.

def reset_training_only_fields(self) -> list[str]:
    """Reset every field in :attr:`training_only_fields` to its default; return the names of those it changed."""
    changed = []
    for name in self.training_only_fields:
        default = type(self).model_fields[name].get_default(call_default_factory=True)
        if getattr(self, name) != default:
            setattr(self, name, default)
            changed.append(name)
    return changed

docs.title: CudaGraphOptions
docs.text:
CudaGraphOptions(**data)

Bases: ConfigurableOptions

How EnvOptions.cuda_graph_options captures, validates and re-captures the graded phase's CUDA graph.

The graph is captured after warmup_steps eager steps. That step and the next validation_steps are each run eagerly too and compared bit for bit with the graph over every tensor the phase leaves behind: a term the graph cannot reproduce raises, naming the tensors that differ, rather than training on stale values. A change to a graded term's configured fields (a curriculum moving a termination threshold), to the env's dt, max_episode_length or training, or a tensor the graph reads rebound to a new one, re-captures and re-validates; reward weights are read from the device and need none. Reading env.common_step_counter during the capture raises, naming the term's line. Not watched: any other Python value a term reads from outside its own fields (another manager's term, a module global), which the graph replays as it was at capture.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION warmup_steps

Eager graded steps before the first capture. A term builds its lazy caches (index tensors, resolved link ids) on its first calls, and building one inside a capture is a host-to-device copy, which fails. These steps already read contacts padded, as the capture will, so a cache sized by the contact width fits it. Defaults to 2.

validation_steps

How many replays after each capture are checked against an eager run of the same step. A validated replay runs the graph before the eager phase, which is what catches work a capture could not record (a kernel launched outside torch's stream), so at least one is required. Each costs about one eager graded phase plus a copy of the tensors the phase writes. Defaults to 3.

recapture_window

The span, in graded steps, that max_recaptures_per_window counts re-captures over. Defaults to 100.

max_recaptures_per_window

Re-captures allowed within recapture_window steps; one more raises, naming what changed. A one-off change (a curriculum switching stage) re-captures once, but something that changes a baked-in value on nearly every step would re-capture and re-validate every step, which costs more than the eager phase. Defaults to 2.

Configuration for a state-independent Gaussian distribution.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION class_name

The distribution class name.

init_std

Initial standard deviation.

std_type

Parameterisation of the standard deviation.

std_range

Hard (min, max) clamp on the standard deviation. The floor is what keeps a policy exploring once its advantage signal flattens out -- without one, a task whose reward briefly stops depending on the action can drive the std to zero and never recover. Defaults to (1e-6, 1e6), rsl-rl's own effectively-unclamped range -- a concrete default rather than None because rsl-rl splats this whole dict into the distribution constructor (dist_class(output_dim, **dist_cfg)), where a None placeholder raises 'NoneType' object is not iterable instead of meaning "unset".

rsl-rl >= 5 only. The v3.2 and v4 translators (:mod:eden.options.learning.rsl_rl.translate) forward only init_std and std_type, so on an older rsl-rl this field is dropped and the clamp simply does not apply -- set it as insurance, not as something a run depends on.

RslRlSymmetryOptions(**data)

Bases: ConfigurableOptions

Configuration for the symmetry-augmentation in the training.

When use_data_augmentation is True, the data_augmentation_func is used to generate augmented observations and actions. These are then used to train the model.

When use_mirror_loss is True, the mirror_loss_coeff is used to weight the symmetry-mirror loss. This loss is directly added to the agent's loss function.

If both use_data_augmentation and use_mirror_loss are False, then no symmetry-based training is enabled. However, the data_augmentation_func is called to compute and log symmetry metrics. This is useful for performing ablations.

For more information, please check the work from :cite:mittal2024symmetry.

Whether to use the symmetry-augmentation loss.

Not declared as a field yet (commented out below), so these options reject it; an algorithm that takes one declares its own (HIMPPOAlgorithmOptions.data_augmentation_func). The symmetry data augmentation function, with signature func(env, obs, action) -> (obs, action) where:

  • obs (tensordict.TensorDict | None): the observation dictionary; if None, the observation is not used.
  • action (torch.Tensor | None): the action tensor; if None, the action is not used.

It returns a tuple of the augmented observation dictionary and action tensors, either of which can be None if its respective input was None.

docs.title: Spatial-softmax CNN
docs.text:
CNN policy head with a spatial-softmax pooling layer.

Spatial softmax (Levine et al. 2016, "End-to-End Training of Deep Visuomotor Policies") replaces the flatten at the end of a conv stack with a soft-argmax over each channel's feature map, returning the expected (x, y) location of every channel — i.e. explicit 2D keypoint coordinates. For a grasp/lift task this hands the policy the object's image-space position directly instead of forcing the MLP trunk to recover it from a flattened feature vector, which is what makes vision manipulation learnable from scratch.

:class:SpatialSoftmaxCNNModel is a drop-in replacement for rsl_rl's CNNModel: point an actor/critic class_name at eden.options.learning.rsl_rl.spatial_softmax:SpatialSoftmaxCNNModel and pass a cnn_cfg with spatial_softmax: True (see eden/tasks/manipulation/lift_box_rgb/config.py). Built on the stock rsl_rl.modules.CNN / rsl_rl.models.{CNNModel,MLPModel} APIs, so it tracks whatever rsl_rl version eden resolves.

docs.title: SpatialSoftmax
docs.text:
SpatialSoftmax(height: int, width: int, temperature: float = 1.0)

Bases: Module

Spatial soft-argmax over feature maps.

Given input of shape (B, C, H, W), computes a softmax over each channel's spatial locations and returns the expected (x, y) coordinates, yielding output shape (B, C * 2).

Args: height: Height of the input feature maps. width: Width of the input feature maps. temperature: Temperature for the spatial softmax. Lower values produce sharper distributions.

Source code in eden/options/learning/rsl_rl/spatial_softmax.py 
def __init__(self, height: int, width: int, temperature: float = 1.0) -> None:
    super().__init__()
    # Normalised coordinate grids in [-1, 1].
    pos_x, pos_y = torch.meshgrid(
        torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, height),
        torch.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, width),
        indexing="ij",
    )
    # Register as buffers so they move with the module's device.
    self.register_buffer("pos_x", pos_x.reshape(1, 1, -1))
    self.register_buffer("pos_y", pos_y.reshape(1, 1, -1))
    self.temperature = temperature

docs.title: forward
docs.text:
forward(x: Tensor) -> Tensor
Source code in eden/options/learning/rsl_rl/spatial_softmax.py 
def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    B, C, H, W = x.shape
    features = x.reshape(B, C, -1)
    weights = torch.softmax(features / self.temperature, dim=-1)
    pos_x: torch.Tensor = self.pos_x  # type: ignore[assignment]
    pos_y: torch.Tensor = self.pos_y  # type: ignore[assignment]
    expected_x = (weights * pos_x).sum(dim=-1)
    expected_y = (weights * pos_y).sum(dim=-1)
    return torch.stack([expected_x, expected_y], dim=-1).reshape(B, C * 2)

CNN encoder with spatial-softmax pooling.

Wraps rsl_rl.modules.CNN (created with global_pool="none" and flatten=False) followed by :class:SpatialSoftmax. Exposes the same interface as CNN: :attr:output_dim (int) and :attr:output_channels (None, signalling flattened output).

Source code in eden/options/learning/rsl_rl/spatial_softmax.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    input_dim: tuple[int, int],
    input_channels: int,
    temperature: float = 1.0,
    **cnn_kwargs: Any,
) -> None:
    super().__init__()
    # Spatial softmax replaces pooling/flatten.
    cnn_kwargs.pop("global_pool", None)
    cnn_kwargs.pop("flatten", None)
    self.cnn = CNN(
        input_dim=input_dim,
        input_channels=input_channels,
        global_pool="none",
        flatten=False,
        **cnn_kwargs,
    )
    # cnn.output_dim is (H, W) when flatten=False.
    out_h, out_w = self.cnn.output_dim  # type: ignore[misc]
    num_channels: int = self.cnn.output_channels  # type: ignore[assignment]
    self.spatial_softmax = SpatialSoftmax(out_h, out_w, temperature)
    self._output_dim = num_channels * 2

CNN model that uses spatial-softmax pooling.

Drop-in replacement for rsl_rl.models.CNNModel. The only difference is that each CNN encoder is wrapped with :class:SpatialSoftmaxCNN instead of a plain CNN. The spatial_softmax / spatial_softmax_temperature keys are stripped from cnn_cfg before the rest is forwarded to the CNN.

Source code in eden/options/learning/rsl_rl/spatial_softmax.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    obs: TensorDict,
    obs_groups: dict[str, list[str]],
    obs_set: str,
    output_dim: int,
    cnn_cfg: dict[str, dict] | dict[str, Any],
    cnns: nn.ModuleDict | None = None,
    hidden_dims: tuple[int] | list[int] = [256, 256, 256],  # noqa: B006
    activation: str = "elu",
    obs_normalization: bool = False,
    distribution_cfg: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> None:
    # Separate 1D / 2D observation groups (sets self.obs_groups_2d,
    # obs_dims_2d, obs_channels_2d; returns 1D info for MLPModel).
    self._get_obs_dim(obs, obs_groups, obs_set)

    if cnns is not None:
        if set(cnns.keys()) != set(self.obs_groups_2d):
            raise ValueError("The 2D observations must be identical for all models sharing CNN encoders.")
        print("Sharing CNN encoders between models, the CNN configurations of the receiving model are ignored.")
        _cnns = cnns
    else:
        # Expand a single flat config to per-group configs.
        if not all(isinstance(v, dict) for v in cnn_cfg.values()):
            cnn_cfg = {group: cnn_cfg for group in self.obs_groups_2d}
        assert len(cnn_cfg) == len(self.obs_groups_2d), (
            "The number of CNN configurations must match the number of 2D observation groups."
        )
        _cnns = {}
        for idx, obs_group in enumerate(self.obs_groups_2d):
            group_cfg = dict(cnn_cfg[obs_group])
            group_cfg.pop("spatial_softmax", None)
            temperature = group_cfg.pop("spatial_softmax_temperature", 1.0)
            _cnns[obs_group] = SpatialSoftmaxCNN(
                input_dim=self.obs_dims_2d[idx],
                input_channels=self.obs_channels_2d[idx],
                temperature=temperature,
                **group_cfg,
            )

    self.cnn_latent_dim = 0
    for cnn in _cnns.values():
        if cnn.output_channels is not None:
            raise ValueError("The output of the CNN must be flattened before passing it to the MLP.")
        self.cnn_latent_dim += int(cnn.output_dim)  # type: ignore[arg-type]

    MLPModel.__init__(
        self,
        obs=obs,
        obs_groups=obs_groups,
        obs_set=obs_set,
        output_dim=output_dim,
        hidden_dims=hidden_dims,
        activation=activation,
        obs_normalization=obs_normalization,
        distribution_cfg=distribution_cfg,
    )

    if isinstance(_cnns, nn.ModuleDict):
        self.cnns = _cnns
    else:
        self.cnns = nn.ModuleDict(_cnns)

Helpers that detect the installed rsl-rl-lib version and translate the typed options into the runner dict it expects.

Translation functions between rsl_rl config versions.

These functions convert the canonical v5-style runner dict (separate actor / critic with distribution_cfg) into the formats expected by older rsl_rl versions.

Typical usage::

from eden.options.learning.rsl_rl.translate import translate_runner_dict

runner_dict = translate_runner_dict(config.runner_options.dict())  # auto-detect
runner = OnPolicyRunner(env, runner_dict, ...)

def require_rsl_rl_version(minimum: tuple[int, ...], module: str, needs: str) -> None:
    """Raise an ``ImportError`` that names the upgrade when the installed ``rsl-rl-lib`` is older than ``minimum``.

    Called at the top of a module before its ``rsl_rl`` imports, so an older install reads "upgrade to X" rather than
    ``cannot import name ...`` from inside rsl_rl.

    Parameters
    ----------
    minimum : tuple[int, ...]
        The oldest release the module runs on.
    module : str
        The module's dotted name, for the message.
    needs : str
        What it uses that older releases lack, for the message.
    """
    installed = detect_rsl_rl_version()
    if installed < minimum:
        wanted = ".".join(map(str, minimum))
        raise ImportError(
            f"{module} needs rsl-rl-lib >= {wanted} ({needs}); the installed version is "
            f"{'.'.join(map(str, installed))}. Upgrade with `uv pip install 'rsl-rl-lib>={wanted}'`."
        )

def translate_runner_dict(runner_dict: dict, algorithm: Any = None) -> dict:
    """Translate *runner_dict* to whatever the installed rsl_rl version expects.

    Auto-detects the installed rsl_rl version and translates from the canonical
    v5 format to whatever that version expects.

    Parameters
    ----------
    runner_dict : dict
        A runner configuration dict (v5-style with ``actor`` / ``critic`` keys).
        **Not modified in-place** — a deep copy is returned.
    algorithm : ConfigurableOptions, optional
        The runner's algorithm options. When they define ``adapt_runner_dict(runner_dict, major)``,
        it runs on the translated dict, so an algorithm outside rsl_rl (an
        ``eden.learning.wrappers.rsl_rl`` one) adapts its own entries for the installed major
        — the generic translation only knows rsl_rl's own models.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A runner dict compatible with the installed rsl_rl version.
    """
    major = detect_rsl_rl_major_version()
    if major < 3:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Detected rsl_rl version {major}.X is not supported. Only versions 3, 4, and 5 are supported."
        )
    elif major == 3:
        en.logger.info("Detected rsl_rl version 3.X. Translating runner dict to v3 format.")
        out = translate_runner_dict_to_v3(runner_dict)
    elif major == 4:
        en.logger.info("Detected rsl_rl version 4.X. Translating runner dict to v4 format.")
        out = translate_runner_dict_to_v4(runner_dict)
    else:  # v5+
        out = copy.deepcopy(runner_dict)
    adapt = getattr(algorithm, "adapt_runner_dict", None)  # an optional hook, not a required field
    return adapt(out, major) if adapt is not None else out

translate_runner_dict_to_v3(runner_dict: dict) -> dict

Convert a v5-style runner dict to the v3.2 format.

v3.2 expects: - A single "policy" dict with combined actor/critic fields (actor_hidden_dims, critic_hidden_dims, init_noise_std, …). - The actor observation set keyed as "policy" in obs_groups. - No share_cnn_encoders or check_for_nan in the algorithm.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION runner_dict

A runner configuration dict produced by RslRlOnPolicyRunnerOptions.dict(). Not modified in-place — a deep copy is returned.

TYPE: dict

RETURNS DESCRIPTION dict

A v3.2-compatible runner dict.

Source code in eden/options/learning/rsl_rl/translate.py 
def translate_runner_dict_to_v3(runner_dict: dict) -> dict:
    """Convert a v5-style runner dict to the v3.2 format.

    v3.2 expects:
    - A single ``"policy"`` dict with combined actor/critic fields
      (``actor_hidden_dims``, ``critic_hidden_dims``, ``init_noise_std``, …).
    - The actor observation set keyed as ``"policy"`` in ``obs_groups``.
    - No ``share_cnn_encoders`` or ``check_for_nan`` in the algorithm.

    Parameters
    ----------
    runner_dict : dict
        A runner configuration dict produced by ``RslRlOnPolicyRunnerOptions.dict()``.
        **Not modified in-place** — a deep copy is returned.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A v3.2-compatible runner dict.
    """
    out = copy.deepcopy(runner_dict)

    # If already in v3.2 format, return as-is
    if "policy" in out and "actor" not in out:
        return out

    actor = out.pop("actor", {})
    critic = out.pop("critic", {})

    # --- build combined policy dict ------------------------------------------
    dist_cfg = actor.pop("distribution_cfg", None)
    class_name = _model_class_to_v3(actor.get("class_name", "MLPModel"))

    policy: dict[str, Any] = {
        "class_name": class_name,
        "actor_hidden_dims": actor.get("hidden_dims", [256, 256, 256]),
        "critic_hidden_dims": critic.get("hidden_dims", [256, 256, 256]),
        "activation": actor.get("activation", "elu"),
        "actor_obs_normalization": actor.get("obs_normalization", False),
        "critic_obs_normalization": critic.get("obs_normalization", False),
    }

    # Distribution → noise params
    if dist_cfg is not None:
        policy["init_noise_std"] = dist_cfg.get("init_std", 1.0)
        policy["noise_std_type"] = dist_cfg.get("std_type", "scalar")

    # Forward RNN fields
    for key in ("rnn_type", "rnn_hidden_dim", "rnn_num_layers"):
        if key in actor:
            policy[key] = actor[key]

    # CNN: v3's ``ActorCriticCNN`` takes separate ``actor_cnn_cfg`` / ``critic_cnn_cfg``
    # (one conv stack per 2D obs group per side), not the v5 single ``cnn_cfg`` — a
    # bare ``cnn_cfg`` lands in its ``**kwargs`` and is silently ignored, leaving
    # the model with no CNN for its image obs.
    if class_name == "ActorCriticCNN":
        if actor.get("cnn_cfg") is not None:
            policy["actor_cnn_cfg"] = actor["cnn_cfg"]
        if critic.get("cnn_cfg") is not None:
            policy["critic_cnn_cfg"] = critic["cnn_cfg"]
    elif actor.get("cnn_cfg") is not None:
        policy["cnn_cfg"] = actor["cnn_cfg"]

    # --- obs_groups: rename "actor" → "policy" --------------------------------
    obs_groups = out.get("obs_groups", {})
    if "actor" in obs_groups and "policy" not in obs_groups:
        obs_groups["policy"] = obs_groups.pop("actor")
    out["obs_groups"] = obs_groups

    # --- algorithm: strip v5-only fields -------------------------------------
    alg = out.get("algorithm", {})
    alg.pop("share_cnn_encoders", None)
    alg.pop("check_for_nan", None)

    # --- runner: strip v5-only fields ----------------------------------------
    out.pop("check_for_nan", None)

    # --- runner: add deprecated field for compat -----------------------------
    out.setdefault("empirical_normalization", None)

    out["policy"] = policy
    return out

docs.text:
translate_runner_dict_to_v4(runner_dict: dict) -> dict

Convert a v5-style runner dict to the v4 format.

v4 uses separated model dicts (like v5) — actor / critic for PPO, student / teacher for distillation — but a model takes stochastic, init_noise_std, noise_std_type, state_dependent_std instead of distribution_cfg. Both v4 runners splat each model dict straight into MLPModel.__init__, so an untranslated distribution_cfg is a TypeError there.

def translate_runner_dict_to_v4(runner_dict: dict) -> dict:
    """Convert a v5-style runner dict to the v4 format.

    v4 uses separated model dicts (like v5) — ``actor`` / ``critic`` for PPO,
    ``student`` / ``teacher`` for distillation — but a model takes
    ``stochastic``, ``init_noise_std``, ``noise_std_type``,
    ``state_dependent_std`` instead of ``distribution_cfg``. Both v4 runners
    splat each model dict straight into ``MLPModel.__init__``, so an
    untranslated ``distribution_cfg`` is a ``TypeError`` there.

    Parameters
    ----------
    runner_dict : dict
        A runner configuration dict produced by ``RslRlOnPolicyRunnerOptions.dict()``
        or ``RslRlDistillationRunnerOptions.dict()``.
        **Not modified in-place** — a deep copy is returned.

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        A v4-compatible runner dict.
    """
    out = copy.deepcopy(runner_dict)

    # --- convert distribution_cfg to v4 noise params -------------------------
    # Only the heads the dict has: a distillation dict gains no ``actor``.
    for head in ("actor", "student", "teacher"):
        if isinstance(out.get(head), dict):
            _model_to_v4(out[head])

    # --- critic: strip distribution_cfg if present (shouldn't be, but safe) --
    if isinstance(out.get("critic"), dict):
        out["critic"].pop("distribution_cfg", None)

    # --- algorithm: strip v5-only fields -------------------------------------
    alg = out.get("algorithm", {})
    alg.pop("check_for_nan", None)

    # --- runner: strip v5-only fields ----------------------------------------
    out.pop("check_for_nan", None)

    return out

def check_agents_options(agents: list[str], obs_groups: dict[str, list[str]]) -> None:
    """Raise ``ValueError`` if ``agents`` repeats a name or is set together with ``obs_groups``.

    Shared by the options validator and :class:`~eden.envs.wrappers.rl_games_env.RlGamesVecEnvWrapper`,
    which re-checks because a field assigned after construction skips the validator.
    """
    if not agents:
        return
    if obs_groups:
        raise ValueError(
            f"RlGamesPpoRunnerOptions sets both `agents={agents!r}` and `obs_groups={obs_groups!r}`; "
            "they are mutually exclusive.\n"
            "In multi-agent mode each agent's observation is the observation group named after it, "
            "and there is no central-value critic to give `obs_groups['critic']` to.\n"
            "Fix: drop `obs_groups` (set it to `{}`) to train the agents, or drop `agents` (set it to `[]`) "
            "for a single-agent run."
        )
    repeated = sorted({name for name in agents if agents.count(name) > 1})
    if repeated:
        raise ValueError(
            f"RlGamesPpoRunnerOptions.agents names {repeated!r} more than once: {agents!r}.\n"
            "Each agent owns one observation group, one reward group and one action term.\n"
            "Fix: list every agent exactly once, in the action manager's term order."
        )

def translate_runner_dict(runner_dict: dict[str, Any], *, num_envs: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Convert a flat Eden options dict into the nested ``params`` dict rl_games expects.

    The output matches what ``rl_games.torch_runner.Runner.load()`` expects.

    Parameters
    ----------
    runner_dict:
        A dict produced by ``RlGamesPpoRunnerOptions.dict()``.
    num_envs:
        Number of parallel environments (injected by the wrapper).

    Returns
    -------
    dict
        The full ``{"params": {...}}`` dict ready for ``Runner.load()``.
    """
    from eden.utils.torch import resolve_device

    d = runner_dict
    net = d.get("network", {})

    minibatch_size = d.get("minibatch_size")
    if minibatch_size is None:
        # Full batch. A multi-agent env (`agents`) gives rl_games `num_envs * len(agents)` rows a step;
        # `agents` itself is a wrapper concern rl_games never reads, so it is not forwarded.
        minibatch_size = d.get("horizon_length", 24) * num_envs * max(len(d.get("agents") or ()), 1)

    lr_schedule = d.get("lr_schedule", "adaptive")
    if lr_schedule == "None":
        lr_schedule = None

    return {
        "params": {
            "seed": d.get("seed", 7100),
            "algo": {"name": "a2c_continuous"},
            "model": {"name": "continuous_a2c_logstd"},
            "network": {
                "name": net.get("name", "actor_critic"),
                "separate": net.get("separate", True),
                "space": {
                    "continuous": {
                        "mu_activation": net.get("mu_activation", "None"),
                        "sigma_activation": net.get("sigma_activation", "None"),
                        "mu_init": {"name": net.get("mu_init_name", "default")},
                        "sigma_init": {
                            "name": "const_initializer",
                            "val": net.get("init_sigma_val", 0.0),
                        },
                        "fixed_sigma": net.get("fixed_sigma", True),
                    },
                },
                "mlp": {
                    "units": list(net.get("units", [512, 256, 128])),
                    "activation": net.get("activation", "elu"),
                    "initializer": {"name": "default"},
                },
            },
            "config": {
                "name": d.get("experiment_name", ""),
                "env_name": "eden",
                "device": resolve_device(d.get("device", "auto")),
                "num_actors": num_envs,
                "horizon_length": d.get("horizon_length", 24),
                "minibatch_size": minibatch_size,
                "mini_epochs": d.get("mini_epochs", 5),
                "learning_rate": d.get("learning_rate", 1e-3),
                "lr_schedule": lr_schedule,
                "kl_threshold": d.get("kl_threshold", 0.01),
                "gamma": d.get("gamma", 0.99),
                "tau": d.get("tau", 0.95),
                "e_clip": d.get("e_clip", 0.2),
                "clip_value": d.get("clip_value", True),
                "entropy_coef": d.get("entropy_coef", 0.01),
                "critic_coef": d.get("critic_coef", 1.0),
                "grad_norm": d.get("grad_norm", 1.0),
                "truncate_grads": d.get("truncate_grads", True),
                "normalize_input": d.get("normalize_input", False),
                "normalize_value": d.get("normalize_value", False),
                "normalize_advantage": d.get("normalize_advantage", True),
                "value_bootstrap": d.get("value_bootstrap", True),
                "reward_shaper": {"scale_value": d.get("reward_scale", 1.0)},
                "bounds_loss_coef": d.get("bounds_loss_coef", 0.0),
                # Disable rl_games' built-in action rescaling — Eden
                # handles action scaling internally via controllers.
                "clip_actions": False,
                "max_epochs": d.get("max_epochs", 30000),
                "save_frequency": d.get("save_frequency", 500),
                "torch_compile": d.get("torch_compile", True),
                "print_stats": True,
            },
        },
    }

Return clip_actions if it is a finite positive bound, raising otherwise.

Source code in eden/options/learning/clip_actions.py 
def validate_clip_actions(clip_actions: float, field: str = "clip_actions") -> float:
    """Return ``clip_actions`` if it is a finite positive bound, raising otherwise.

    Actions are clamped to ``[-clip_actions, clip_actions]``: zero would clamp every action to zero, a
    negative bound inverts the interval, and an infinite or NaN one bounds nothing while promising a
    bound to a library that reads the action space. ``field`` is where the caller set it, for the message.
    """
    if not (0 < clip_actions < math.inf):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{field}={clip_actions!r} must be a finite positive bound, or None to leave actions unclamped."
        )
    return clip_actions

docs.title: ManagerTermOptions
docs.text:
ManagerTermOptions(**data)

Bases: DynamicConfigurableOptions

Base for all per-term options (RewardTermOptions, EventTermOptions, ...).

Term options stay extra="allow" because class-based terms carry their per-term parameters as extras (the options class is shared by every term of the kind). Typo protection comes from validating those extras against the registered term instead:

  • At construction and on attribute assignment (model_post_init / __setattr__): when name resolves in the kind's term registry — stamped onto this class as _term_registry_ by TermRegistry.__init__ — extras must be parameters of the registered term, and for function terms the params keys must be arguments of the registered function. RewardTermOptions(name="upright", wieght=2.0) and options.wieght = 2.0 both raise in the config file that contains the typo (a rejected assignment is rolled back).
  • On copy-with-changes (updated(...) / model_copy(update=...)): the same check runs on the copy — pydantic's update= is otherwise unvalidated and would park {"wieght": 2.0} as an extra next to the untouched weight.
  • At build (ConfigurableMixin.__init__): the pre-existing invalid-parameter check backstops options whose name was missing or not yet registered at construction time.

def term_keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    """Return only the registered ``ManagerTerm`` entry names.

    These are the extras validated by :meth:`model_post_init` to be
    ``_term_options_class_`` instances.

    This is intentionally distinct from :meth:`ConfigurableOptions.keys`,
    which returns every named child of the options object — including
    declared model fields that are config knobs (e.g.
    ``RecorderManagerOptions.dataset_filename``), not terms.
    """
    extra = self.__pydantic_extra__ or {}
    return tuple(key for key in extra if not key.startswith("_option_"))

ObservationTermOptions(**data)

Bases: FunctionTermOptions

Observation term specification.

The manager processes each frame of the term's output in this order: modifiers, noise, clip, scale, then the group's nan_policy, and last the history window.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION modifiers

Transforms applied to the term's output in list order, before noise (default=[], none). Each entry is a registered :class:~eden.managers.modifiers.base.ObservationModifier configured with <ModifierClass>.configure(...), e.g. ExponentialMovingAverage.configure(alpha=0.2) or ObservationDelay.configure(control_steps=2). Unlike noise, modifiers run in every mode: training, eval and deployment. A modifier must return the shape, dtype and device it receives.

noise

Noise model applied to the observation, in training only (default=None, no noise).

clip

Range to clip the observation values (default=None, no clipping).

scale

Scaling factor applied to the observation (default=1.0). A list gives a per-component scale matched against the term's feature dim — the last dimension of its raw compute() output — validated at env-construction time and applied before history stacking.

history_length

Number of previous observations to include (default=0, no history).

flatten_history_dim

Whether to flatten the history into the feature axis, giving (num_envs, history_length * dim) instead of (num_envs, history_length, dim) (default=True, the same as the group's).

backfill

Whether to backfill the history with the first observation (default=True). If False, the history will be filled with zeros.

Whether to allow adding noise to each term in the group (default=True). False is a group-level master switch: it disables the noise of every term in the group, whatever each term configured, so one term dict can serve a noisy policy and a clean critic. The terms keep their noise in the config — the group does not edit what it adopts — and the observation manager drops it when it builds the group, logging one info line that names the group and the terms, so noise that does not reach the policy is stated rather than silent.

history_length

The history length enforced for all terms in the group (default=None).

flatten_history_dim

Whether to flatten the history dimension (default=True).

backfill

Whether to backfill the history with the first observation (default=True). If False, the history will be filled with zeros.

nan_policy

What to do when a term delivers a non-finite value (NaN or ±Inf) (default="disabled", no check). The check is on each term's frame after its modifiers, noise, clip and scale, just before the history window, so a report names the term. A clip that bounds an infinity is therefore never reported. "sanitize" replaces each non-finite entry with 0.0 in what the policy receives. "warn" does the same and also logs the first occurrence for each term, naming the envs. "error" raises FloatingPointError. The check runs in every mode (training, eval, deployment) and on every computation, including the final-observation snapshot. It cannot clean a stateful modifier upstream of it: a NaN that reaches an ExponentialMovingAverage stays in the average until the env resets. "sanitize" stays on the device. "error", and "warn" for terms that have not warned yet, cost one GPU sync per group per observation compute.

def disable_term(self, name: str) -> None:
    """Remove a term from this group by name, and from ``terms_order`` when the group declares one.

    ``terms_order`` must list exactly the group's terms, so a name left behind there would fail
    the next load or the observation manager's build, far from this call.

    Raises ``KeyError`` (listing the terms that exist) for an unknown name and
    ``RuntimeError`` on a locked config.
    """
    self._remove_named_child(name, noun="term")
    if self.terms_order is not None:
        # Rebuilt, not edited in place: assignment on an options model is unvalidated, so the
        # list may be shared with another group or with the code that assigned it.
        self.terms_order = [term for term in self.terms_order if term != name]

docs.text:
disable_term(name: str) -> None

Remove a flat term, a whole group, or a term nested inside exactly one group, by name.

The name must resolve unambiguously. If it matches more than one entry (a term declared in several groups, or a top-level entry and a nested term), this raises ValueError — disable through the owning group instead: getattr(options, group).disable_term(name). Ambiguity here is name-based, not activity-based: a weight-0 (inert) duplicate still counts as a match, unlike the manager's build-time uniqueness check, because options can't know final weights.

Source code in eden/options/managers/rewards.py 
def disable_term(self, name: str) -> None:
    """Remove a flat term, a whole group, or a term nested inside exactly one group, by name.

    The name must resolve unambiguously. If it matches more than one entry (a term
    declared in several groups, or a top-level entry and a nested term), this raises
    ``ValueError`` — disable through the owning group instead:
    ``getattr(options, group).disable_term(name)``. Ambiguity here is name-based, not
    activity-based: a weight-0 (inert) duplicate still counts as a match, unlike the
    manager's build-time uniqueness check, because options can't know final weights.
    """
    owner_groups = self._groups_containing(name)
    places = (["top level"] if name in self.term_keys() else []) + [f"group '{g}'" for g in owner_groups]
    if len(places) > 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Name '{name}' is ambiguous ({' and '.join(places)}). To remove a nested term, call "
            f"disable_term on its group: getattr(options, group).disable_term({name!r})."
        )
    if owner_groups:
        getattr(self, owner_groups[0]).disable_term(name)
        return
    # Top-level hit (flat term or whole group), or the canonical KeyError.
    self._remove_named_child(name, noun="term")

A heterogeneous entity (GroupedEntityOptions) gives each env one variant for the whole run — one object mesh out of a bank. MotionTermOptions(**data)

Bases: ManagerTermOptions

Configuration for the motion buffer.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION dataset_options

The options for the dataset.

entities_map

Maps each environment entity name (key) to its motion sequence key in the dataset (value).

target_dofs_name

Per entity, the names of the degrees of freedom to target. The reference's DOF columns follow this list's order, which need not match the dataset's.

target_links_name

Per entity, the names of the links to target. The reference's link rows follow this list's order, which need not match the dataset's.

env_starting_stub_sampling_strategy

How a motion and its start time are drawn. "independent" (default) draws the motion, then its start time. "concat_motion_bins" draws one motion_bin_length_s bin from all motions' bins concatenated (so a longer motion is proportionally likelier) and starts inside it; requires motion_bin_length_s.

motion_start_from_middle_range

(min, max) fractions of the clip duration the start time is drawn uniformly from. Used only when max > 0 and motion_bin_length_s is None (bin sampling takes priority). Defaults to (0.0, 0.0): every clip starts at its first frame.

motion_bin_length_s

Width [s] of the start-time bins. Setting it enables bin-weighted start sampling; required by adaptive_sampling and "concat_motion_bins". Defaults to None.

adaptive_sampling

Master toggle for adaptive start-time (intra-motion bin) sampling. Defaults to False.

adaptive_kernel_size

Temporal smoothing kernel width K. Smooths each failure onto the bin it died in and the K - 1 bins before it, so starts move onto the run-up to a hard moment (BeyondMimic's look-ahead kernel). 1 disables smoothing. Defaults to 1.

adaptive_lambda

Exponential decay for kernel weights: the death bin weighs 1, the bin i before it adaptive_lambda ** i, normalised to sum to 1. Defaults to 0.8.

adaptive_uniform_ratio

Minimum uniform floor in sampling probabilities. Defaults to 0.1.

adaptive_alpha

EMA blend rate for failure counts. Defaults to 0.001.

adaptive_failure_rate_max_over_mean

Per-START-bin concentration clamp for adaptive start-time sampling. A bin whose (smoothed) failure rate exceeds mean * this (per-motion mean over its bins) is clipped to that ceiling before normalization, so no single bin can absorb arbitrarily much probability mass even if its failure rate is pathologically high (e.g. a momentarily impossible frame). Bin-level analogue of motion_weight_failure_rate_max_over_mean; without it the uniform mix alone only bounds the floor, not the peak, so the start distribution can still collapse onto one bin. <= 0 disables the clamp. Defaults to 10.0.

motion_weights

Initial per-motion-id sampling weights, one entry per loaded trajectory in motion-id order. None (default) weights every motion equally. A list[float] supplies the weights inline; a str is a path to a text/JSON file (loaded via load_text) holding a "motion_weights" key with that list — convenient for large clip libraries. The length must equal the number of loaded trajectories or build raises. When adaptive_motion_weights is True these are the starting weights the curriculum then rewrites.

adaptive_motion_weights

Master toggle for adaptive per-motion-id sampling (hard-motion mining). Orthogonal to adaptive_sampling (which controls intra-motion start-time bins). When True, _motion_weights is updated each training iteration based on per-motion success / early-termination outcomes during rollouts. Defaults to False.

motion_weight_success_discount

Per-success multiplicative decay applied to a motion's weight when its motion plays to its natural end (regardless of whether the env also terminated this step). < 1.0 shrinks the weight of easy motions; = 1.0 disables decay. Defaults to 0.999 (matches ProtoMotions reference).

motion_weight_failure_amplify

Per-failure multiplicative gain applied to a motion's weight when an episode terminates early without the motion completing. > 1.0 boosts the weight of hard motions; = 1.0 disables amplification. Defaults to 2.0 (matches ProtoMotions reference). For a gentler, symmetric per-iter pressure, set this to a value just above 1 (e.g. 1.001) alongside motion_weight_success_discount=0.999.

motion_weight_floor

Lower clamp on per-motion weight (before re-normalization), so no motion can be permanently zeroed out. Defaults to 1e-3. Only consulted by motion_weight_update_mode="compound"; the snapshot mode bounds weights via motion_weight_failure_rate_max_over_mean + motion_weight_uniform_mix instead.

motion_weight_update_mode

How _motion_weights is rewritten from the drained outcome counts:

  • "snapshot" (default): stateless rate-proportional formulation ported from SONIC's update_adaptive_sampling_probabilities (motion_lib_base.py:2570-2585). Computes failure_rate = n_failure / (n_success + n_failure), clamps outliers at mean_failure_rate * failure_rate_max_over_mean, normalises, then blends with uniform via uniform_mix. The result is always the same function of the current drained counts — no history compounds. success_discount / failure_amplify / floor are ignored under this mode.
  • "compound" (opt-in): log-space additive update log_w += n_success * log(success_discount) + n_failure * log(failure_amplify). Integrates all historical outcomes forever; any persistent failure-rate bias compounds exponentially until a motion saturates at the floor or at 1.0. Observed to collapse to a single motion at LAFAN1 scale; kept only for ablation runs.

motion_weight_uniform_mix

Applied AFTER the curriculum update under either mode: w := (1 - α) * w + α / N. Caps maximum concentration at (1 - α) + α/N and floors minimum at α/N, independent of the update mode's own dynamics. Defaults to 0.0 (off).

motion_weight_failure_rate_max_over_mean

Snapshot-mode-only outlier clamp. A motion with failure rate greater than mean * this is clipped to that ceiling before being converted to a probability. With N=12 and clamp=200, the worst case is one motion captures up to ~95% of the pre-mix probability mass; combined with uniform_mix=0.1 the worst-case cap becomes ~85%. Defaults to 200.0 (matches SONIC's adp_samp_failure_rate_max_over_mean).

motion_weight_update_every_n_iters

Apply the curriculum update every N PPO iterations. Outcomes accumulate in between. Defaults to 1.

log_per_motion_metrics

Emit per-motion-id distributions as wandb.Histogram panels under MotionPerMotion/Weights (current sampling weights) and MotionPerMotion/Outcome/{success_count, failure_count, total, success_rate} (per-drain counts). One histogram per metric per iter — independent of motion count.

Useful for diagnosing curriculum collapse: a long tail forming in the weight distribution shows up immediately as a skewed histogram. One scalar series per motion-id would be ~47k series per iteration at AMASS scale (~9.4k motions × 5 fields), which overwhelms the wandb backend and slows rsl-rl's logger; histograms keep the diagnostic at constant cost. MotionWeights/argmax_motion_id (a single int) stays on the aggregate panel and is always emitted — that's the cheapest way to identify the dominant clip and works at any scale. Defaults to False.

log_motion_id_to_filename

When True, additionally emit MotionWeights/argmax_motion_filename as a wandb string field — the basename of the dataset file corresponding to the current argmax motion-id. Resolved against the dataset's all_motion_files list (the post-select_trajectories per-rank slice), so DDP-sharded runs may emit "<not_local>" when the argmax is held by another rank. Off by default because the integer argmax_motion_id is enough to identify the clip via the dataset's saved file order, and the string field is heavier to handle (wandb plot-by-string is awkward; mostly useful in the wandb run table for at-a-glance correlation with the integer time series).

start_at_timestep_zero_prob

On reset, with this probability force the start time to 0 instead of sampling via motion_start_from_middle_range / bin-weighted sampling. Useful for eval-mode determinism and curriculum warm-ups where every clip should begin at frame 0. Defaults to 0.0.

freeze_at_timestep_zero_prob

Per-step probability that MotionManager.compute(dt) does NOT advance _timestamp for envs currently at timestamp 0. Re-rolled every step (mirrors Holosoma's WBT semantic), so a setting of 0.5 gives an env at t=0 a 50% chance of advancing each step — useful for mild start-time jitter, NOT for permanent freeze (an env frozen on step N can advance on step N+1). Defaults to 0.0.

compute_per_motion_metrics

When True, accumulate per-step tracking error against the reference (MPJPE in world frame, root position L2 error, root quaternion geodesic error) into per-env running sums, then scatter to per-motion-id aggregators at episode reset. Drained alongside the success/failure curriculum counts (same all_reduce_fn across DDP ranks; same cadence as motion_weight_update_every_n_iters). Aggregate scalars (Mimic/mpjpe_{mean,p50,p95} etc.) flow into extras["log"]; per-motion tensors are available via summarize_per_motion_metrics() for CSV dump.

Hot-path cost when enabled: one extra get_links_pos per step + 3 per-env reductions + 3 in-place adds. No CPU↔GPU sync. When disabled (default), buffers are unallocated and the accumulator is a single early-return check. Defaults to False.

metric_anchor_link_name

Optional anchor link (e.g. "torso_link"). When set together with compute_per_motion_metrics=True, additionally accumulates G-MPJPE — link MPJPE measured in the anchor frame (subtract the anchor link's world-frame position from all tracked link positions before the L2 norm). Surfaces Mimic/g_mpjpe_* scalars in extras["log"]. None → don't compute G-MPJPE, keep the baseline 3-metric set (MPJPE, root_pos_err, root_quat_err) only. Adds one extra entity find_named_links_idx_local lookup at first compute, then one get_links_pos row (for the anchor) and one subtract on the hot path. Defaults to None.

env_motion_groups

Per-env clip groups keyed on a heterogeneous entity's variant (see :class:MotionGroupOptions), for a reference that is only valid with one variant of that entity — an object-manipulation clip and the object it manipulates. None (the default) samples every env from the whole library.

How the motion library is split across DDP ranks: "None" (default) gives every rank all of it, "Even" splits it evenly (round-robin), "Segment" assigns each rank a contiguous segment.

Whether to enable symmetric augmentation of motion data (mirroring across the x-z plane). When True, the required mapping fields below must also be provided.

The joint index permutation for symmetric augmentation. Maps each joint to its mirrored counterpart.

symmetric_augmentation_joint_reverse_buf

Per-joint sign multipliers for symmetric augmentation (e.g., -1.0 for joints that flip sign when mirrored). Required when symmetric_augmentation is True.

symmetric_augmentation_links_mapping

Link index permutation for symmetric augmentation (in the order of links_of_interests). Required when symmetric_augmentation is True and links are referenced.

reference_prim_path

Not read by the motion manager.

resync_on_motion_end

When True, an env whose reference reaches the end of its clip is soft-reset mid-episode: a fresh start phase is resampled and the robot is teleported onto the new reference start (via the ReferenceStateInitialization event term), WITHOUT ending the episode. Mirrors the clip-wrap behavior of MotionCommand (used by the beyondmimic example). Default False: the reference freezes at the last frame (velocities zeroed) and the robot is not re-synced.

def to_genesis_material(self):
    cls = self._genesis_material_cls
    if cls is None:
        raise NotImplementedError(f"{type(self).__name__} does not implement to_genesis_material()")
    # Drop None-valued fields so Genesis applies its own (often lazily-resolved)
    # defaults rather than seeing an explicit ``None``. Several Genesis materials
    # reject an explicit ``sampler=None`` even though it is their ``__init__``
    # default (e.g. ``gs.materials.MPM.Elastic``), so forwarding None would make
    # ``MPMElasticMaterialOptions()`` unusable.
    return cls(**{k: v for k, v in self.dict().items() if v is not None})

RigidMaterialOptions(**data)

Bases: MaterialOptions

Options for Genesis rigid materials.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION rho

The density of the material used to compute mass. Default is 200.0.

TYPE: float

friction

Friction coefficient within the rigid solver. If None, a default of 1.0 may be used or parsed from file.

TYPE: float

friction_torsional

Torsional friction coefficient: how strongly a contact resists relative spin about its normal. Expressed in meters — it is the effective contact-patch radius, and it bounds the resisting torque at friction_torsional * normal_force. Requires EnvOptions.enable_torsional_friction (Eden raises at build if the switch is off) and costs one extra constraint axis per contact. If None, parsed from the asset when available (MJCF friction[1], only for geoms declaring condim >= 4), otherwise genesis' 0.005. Default is None.

TYPE: float

friction_rolling

Rolling friction coefficient: how strongly a contact resists rolling about its two tangent axes. In meters like friction_torsional. Requires EnvOptions.enable_rolling_friction (which itself requires enable_torsional_friction) and costs two extra constraint axes per contact. If None, parsed from the asset when available (MJCF friction[2], only for geoms declaring condim >= 6), otherwise genesis' 0.0001. Default is None.

TYPE: float

needs_coup

Whether the material participates in coupling with other solvers. Default is True.

TYPE: bool

coup_friction

Friction used during coupling. Must be non-negative. Default is 0.1.

TYPE: float

coup_softness

Softness of coupling interaction. Must be non-negative. Default is 0.002.

TYPE: float

coup_restitution

Restitution coefficient in collision coupling. Should be between 0 and 1. Default is 0.0.

TYPE: float

sdf_cell_size

Cell size in SDF grid in meters. Defines grid resolution. Default is 0.005.

TYPE: float

sdf_min_res

Minimum resolution of the SDF grid. Must be at least 16. Default is 32.

TYPE: int

sdf_max_res

Maximum resolution of the SDF grid. Must be >= sdf_min_res. Default is 128.

TYPE: int

gravity_compensation

Compensation factor for gravity. 1.0 cancels gravity. Default is 0.

TYPE: float

coup_type

Coupling mode for this entity. Only used by the IPC coupler. Requires needs_coup=True. If None, auto-selected based on entity type: 'external_articulation' for fixed-base articulated robots, 'two_way_soft_constraint' for floating-base robots, and 'ipc_only' for non-articulated objects. Valid values: - 'two_way_soft_constraint': Two-way soft coupling. - 'external_articulation': Joint-level coupling for articulated bodies. Joint positions will be coupled at the DOF level. - 'ipc_only': IPC controls entity, transforms copied to Genesis (one-way). Only supported by rigid non-articulated objects. Default is None.

TYPE: str or None

coup_links

Link names to include in coupling. When set, only the named links participate in coupling; other links are excluded. Only supported with needs_coup=True and two_way_soft_constraint type in IPC. Default is None.

TYPE: list of str or None

enable_coup_collision

Whether coupler collision is enabled for this entity's links. Only used by the IPC coupler. Unlike needs_coup=False (which removes the entity from the coupler entirely), setting this to False keeps the entity in the coupler for coupling forces but disables contact response. Default is True.

TYPE: bool

coup_collision_links

Link names whose geoms participate in coupler collision. Only used by the IPC coupler. Only effective when enable_coup_collision=True. If None, all coupled links have collision. When set, only the named links get coupler collision; other links are marked no-collision. Default is None.

TYPE: list of str or None

contact_resistance

IPC coupling contact resistance/stiffness override for this entity. None means use IPCCouplerOptions.contact_resistance. Default is None.

TYPE: float or None

MochiShellMaterialOptions(**data)

Bases: MochiMaterialOptions

Options for Mochi thin shells / cloth (eden.engine.solvers.mochi.materials.Shell).

The surface triangles of a Mesh (or primitive) morph become a Saint Venant-Kirchhoff membrane plus a Koiter-type bending term, both thickness-integrated from E, nu, rho and thickness unless overridden. Shells act as colliders through spheres of collider_radius at their vertices, which only other point-cloud bodies (cloths, rods) and — with self_contact — the shell itself feel; rigid bodies and solids touch the shell through its own contact samples. Consistently wound meshes are required. Light cloth has little inertia: use penalty_coefficient=1e7. Entities build as :class:~eden.entities.mochi.MochiSoftEntity.

docs.title: MochiRodMaterialOptions
docs.text:
MochiRodMaterialOptions(**data)

Bases: MochiMaterialOptions

Options for Mochi discrete elastic rods (eden.engine.solvers.mochi.materials.Rod).

A Kirchhoff rod (stretch, bend, twist; no shear) on the polyline of a :class:~eden.options.entities.RodOptions morph — the only morph this material accepts. The five stiffness / inertia quantities derive from E, nu, rho and the rod radius unless given explicitly. Clamp a rod by fixing its first two nodes. Rods collide through samples on their centerline and act as colliders through node spheres of the rod radius, which only other point-cloud bodies (and the rod itself under self_contact) feel. Entities build as :class:~eden.entities.mochi.MochiSoftEntity.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION use_visual_raycasting

See :class:MaterialOptions. Default is False.

TYPE: bool

E

Young's modulus (Pa). Default is 1e7.

TYPE: float

nu

Poisson ratio (shear modulus G = E / (2 (1 + nu))). Default is 0.3.

TYPE: float

rho

Density (kg/m^3). Default is 1000.0.

TYPE: float

axial_stiffness

E * A override. Default is None.

TYPE: float or None

flexural_stiffness

E * I override. Default is None.

TYPE: float or None

torsional_stiffness

G * J override. Default is None.

TYPE: float or None

linear_density

rho * A override (kg/m). Default is None.

TYPE: float or None

linear_rotational_inertia

rho * J override (kg m). Default is None.

TYPE: float or None

mass_damping

Rayleigh mass-proportional damping (1/s). Default is 0.0.

TYPE: float

stiffness_damping

Rayleigh stiffness-proportional damping (s). Default is 0.0.

TYPE: float

collider_type

Whether the rod carries node spheres other point-cloud bodies collide with. Default is "auto".

TYPE: ('auto', 'point_cloud', 'none') DEFAULT: "auto"

self_contact

Let the rod's samples collide with its own node spheres. Default is False.

TYPE: bool

self_contact_exclusion_ratio

Nodes within radius * ratio (plus the penalty threshold) of a sample in the rest configuration are excluded from self-contact; e.g. 3 for segments twice the radius. Default is 1.5.

TYPE: float

docs.text:
Robot presets are RobotOptions subclasses with the asset, DOF order, PD gains, armature and limits of one robot already filled in; construct one and put it in a scene. Composite rigs bundle several presets (an arm and a gripper, a humanoid and two hands) into one validated options object. The robots guide covers the catalog, composite rigs and adding a robot.

import eden as en
from eden.options.robots import COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY, ROBOT_REGISTRY, Droid

robot = en.robots.Go1()
rig = Droid(base_pos=(0.0, 0.0, 0.4))           # hand-less Panda + Robotiq 2F-85
cls = COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY.get("ur5e_2f85")  # -> UR5eRobotiq

docs.title: OliNoHands
docs.text:
OliNoHands(**data)

Bases: Oli

Oli with its moulded rubber hands removed, for welding a real end effector.

Teleoperating a Dex3 / XHand / Dex1 gripper (or a Wuji Hand2 — see :class:~eden.options.robots.composite.oli_wuji.OliWuji) means welding that end effector onto the wrist, and the stock moulded hand would then sit stacked inside it. This variant points at HU_D04_01_no_hand.urdf; every joint and every other link is identical to the stock URDF, so DOFs, gains and pose are inherited unchanged from :class:Oli. Four things differ:

  • *_wrist_roll_link points at *_wrist_roll_link_nohand.STL. This is what removes the hand: it is baked into the stock wrist mesh, not carried on a link, and so is the silver end-cap it bolted onto. Dropping both leaves 72 of 322 cm^3 and exposes the real flange.
  • The wrist inertial is recomputed for the bare metal — 0.205 kg with its CoM 2.9 cm down, against the stock 0.581 kg at 8.9 cm, which was dominated by the rubber hand. So the arm carries the end effector you weld on, not that plus a phantom 0.38 kg per wrist.
  • Two *_hand_mount frames are added on the exposed flange (z = -0.058 in *_wrist_roll_link, the plane upstream's own stock URDF puts *_hand_contact on). They carry no mass and no geometry; welding an end effector to them needs no offset.
  • The four fixed *_hand_{manip,contact} links/joints are dropped. Despite the names these are not the hand, just 1 cm / 1 g marker boxes for the grasp and contact frames LimX's stack targets; they are fixed children Genesis merges away regardless.

The :class:SmplHumanoid skeleton (same bodies, joints, geoms and DOF order) generated with the robot options PHC trained phc_3 with (real_weight_porpotion_boxes=True, so the five box geoms carry their real-weight densities instead of 1000) and with the floor, light and motors stripped (examples/projects/mimic/assistmimic/scripts/generate_smpl_xml.py). From MuJoCo Menagerie's franka_fr3 (Apache-2.0), which derives it from Franka's own franka_description, with two Eden edits baked into the shipped asset: its links and joints are renamed link0…link7 / joint1…joint7 (the naming every other arm here uses, and what this class's DOF maps and the composite rigs address), and the bare attachment_site becomes an attachment body carrying the same mount frame as panda_nohand.xml — 0.107 m up from link7, rotated 135 degrees about z — so a gripper welds onto either Franka arm unchanged.

The FR3 is the same arm mechanically as the Panda (identical link frames, identical collision hulls, 855 mm reach, 3 kg payload, ±87 / ±12 N·m joint torques), and differs in what it declares: its own joint limits (A6 is shifted by 26 degrees, so a Panda home pose is not automatically reachable), Franka's published inertials, and joint friction identified in torque control (armature 0.195 / 0.074, damping 0.21, frictionloss 1.137 … 0.248) where the Panda model has none.

The Panda counterpart of :class:FrankaResearch3, and what a composite rig wants when the end-effector is a separate entity — :class:~eden.options.robots.FrankaEmikaPanda is one MJCF with the fingers inside it, so its hand cannot be swapped or welded to. The Panda's own gains and joint limits, which are not the FR3's: see :class:FrankaResearch3 for what differs between the two robots.

docs.title: OmniReset UR5e rig
docs.text:
UWLab's OmniReset rig: a calibrated UR5e carrying a Robotiq 2F-85 with a D415 mount.

Converted once from UWLab's USD (UW-Lab/uwlab-assets), which Genesis cannot load: the gripper's parallel linkage is a PhysX articulation with two parents per inner knuckle, coupled by physxMimicJoint constraints. The MJCF rebuilds it as a tree. Each body is placed from its PhysX joint frames at q = 0, so every joint reads PhysX's coordinate; the five mimic joints become joint equalities and the two loop-closing joints are dropped. One authored gearing is corrected: right_inner_knuckle_joint says -1, but its hinge is flipped relative to its mirror, which opens a 72 mm gap in the right finger's loop when closed; +1 closes it to 0.08 mm, and it matches Isaac Lab's recorded states, which read that joint as -finger_joint. Kinematics match UWLab's calibrated analytic model (uwlab_assets.robots.ur5e_robotiq_gripper.kinematics) to 1e-7 m; joint values are PhysX's, so a pose reads what Isaac Lab reports for it.

One asset rather than a ManipulatorOptions composite of :class:UR5e and :class:Robotiq2f85, because neither part is the same robot: UR5e carries rounded nominal link lengths, putting its flange 1.2 mm (max 2.3 mm) from this calibrated one across random poses — the size of OmniReset's 2.5 mm success tolerance — and Robotiq2f85 is MuJoCo Menagerie's loop-closed 2F-85 (other joints, pad-only colliders, sub-millisecond substeps, no D415 mount), not the mimic linkage whose six joint angles the policy observes.

Inertials are PhysX's. The arm links' are authored in the USD; the gripper links have none, so the ones here are what Isaac Sim 6.1 derives for UWLab's robot (measured), including 1 kg on each collider-less outer knuckle. With them the arm's mass matrix matches PhysX's to 0.01 %, and UWLab's 120 Hz explicit controller is stable.

The dynamics are UWLab's implicit-actuator training/eval configuration (IMPLICIT_UR5E_ROBOTIQ_2F85): the arm is torque-driven by an operational-space controller (kp = kd = 0 here; efforts capped at 150/28 N·m), the gripper's finger_joint is a PD servo (kp 17, kd 5, 60 N·m) and the five passive linkage joints follow it through joint equalities. Every link floats (disable_gravity in the USD), which gravity compensation reproduces, and no DOF carries armature or friction — the USD authors none and the stage-1 policy never had the sysid values the finetune stage randomizes.

docs.title: Robotiq2f85
docs.text:
Robotiq2f85(**data)

Bases: RobotOptions

Robotiq 2F85 parallel-jaw gripper, tuned for stable grasping.

The 2F85 is an underactuated four-bar linkage: MuJoCo closes it with <equality><connect> constraints and drives it through a <tendon> actuator. Genesis has no runtime tendon (the actuator is approximated per driver joint at parse time) and solves the loop closures softly, so the stock asset penetrates/oscillates instead of pinching. These options bake in the validated compensation (tuned by SpaceMouse-teleop A/B against the loop-free Franka Hand; pinned by the grasp-and-lift regression in tests/options/robots/test_robotiq_2f85.py):

  • Pads: flat box collision geoms with high friction (a face contact that resists rotation), instead of the original 5-sphere cluster. Pair with collision_link_patterns=[".*pad"] so only the pads collide and the object isn't wedged against the inner linkage.
  • Drive (default_dofs_force_limits): the kp=100 servo commanded to the closed target would develop ~40 N·m and crush through a small object; the cap reproduces MuJoCo's tendon forcerange -5 5 × wrap coef 0.485 = 2.4 N·m per driver.
  • Loop closure (default_equalities_sol_params): the connects + driver coupling are stiffened to near-rigid so grip force transmits through the four-bar to the pads instead of flexing it.
  • Contact (default_geoms_sol_params): pad contact stiffened to match. Genesis mixes a pair's params as the mean of its two geoms (geom priority is ignored), so graspable objects should carry comparable sol params via their own default_geoms_sol_params — never via a global EnvOptions.constraint_timeconst, which over-stiffens every rigid contact and ejects mesh objects on contact.
  • Spring preload (default_dofs_spring_ref): Genesis drops MJCF springref; re-anchoring the spring-link springs at 2.62 rad restores the preload that keeps the passive pad chain taut.
  • Dissipation (damping/frictionloss/armature): at contact the drivers are torque-saturated, so kp/kd have no authority over contact chatter; always-on joint damping (~critical for the pinch mode) and a dry frictionloss stick band absorb it instead.

Full constraint stiffness needs an effective substep dt <= 0.001 (e.g. sim_dt=0.004, sim_substeps=4); Genesis clamps solref timeconst to 2*substep_dt otherwise.

docs.title: Inspire RH56
docs.text:
Inspire RH56 dexterous hands (left/right): the stock RH56 and the RH56DFQ variant Unitree mounts on the G1.

Both are the same hand: link tree, joint frames and axes, and every link's inertial (0.1918 kg in all) are identical. What differs is the asset each is published with, and so the joint ranges, the coupling ratios and the meshes:

========================== ================================== ========================================= asset InspireRH56_* InspireRH56DFQ_* (Weave's G1 rig) ========================== ================================== ========================================= finger proximal range 0 – 1.47 rad 0 – 1.7 rad thumb distal range 0 – 0.4 rad 0 – 1.2 rad couplings URDF <mimic> (Genesis equality) software, via mimic_dofs (no tags) thumb int. / distal ratio 1.334 / 0.667 1.6 / 2.4 finger intermediate ratio 1.06399, offset -0.04545 1.0 ========================== ================================== =========================================

Six of the twelve joints are mimic followers of the six drivers (actuated_dofs_name). metadata.mimic_dofs publishes the couplings as follower -> (driver, multiplier, offset) for both. The RH56 asset keeps its <mimic> tags, so Genesis couples its followers itself and the mapping is descriptive; the DFQ asset has them stripped, and a task passes the mapping to the joint PD action term, which then commands each follower at driver_target * multiplier + offset (Weave's MimicJointPositionAction)::

ImplicitPDController.configure(entity_name="left_hand", dofs_name=InspireRH56DFQ_L.actuated_dofs_name,
                               mimic_dofs=InspireRH56DFQ_L.metadata.mimic_dofs)

docs.title: Wuji Hand 1
docs.text:
Wuji Hand 1 dexterous hand configurations (left/right, full-mesh or primitive collision).

Twenty-DOF anthropomorphic hand from Wuji Technology (5 fingers x 4 DOF) with a silicone pad on the thumb -- the hand/body-with-soft package, i.e. the hand the upstream in-hand cube-reorientation RL task (wuji-technology/wuji-mjlab) is built around. The successor generation is :mod:eden.options.robots.wuji_hand2beta2; the two are different hands, not variants (different link names, joint names and kinematics).

Two collision flavours per side:

  • WujiHand1_{R,L} -- one full visual mesh per link, reused as the collision mesh. Genesis convexifies each, so the palm becomes a single convex hull that bulges over the finger sockets. Fine for visualization, retargeting and teleop.
  • WujiHand1Simplified_{R,L} -- primitive collision (cylinder + end spheres on the proximal links, simplified meshes for the palm, the thumb pad and the five distal links). This reproduces the collision model the upstream MJCF -- and therefore the upstream RL task -- was tuned against, and is much cheaper at thousands of envs. Use this flavour for contact-rich manipulation.

Assets (URDF + STL meshes, MIT-licensed) live under hands/wuji_hand1 in the Kashu7100/eden_assets dataset, converted from the upstream wuji-technology/wuji-description hand/body-with-soft package.

Not to be confused with the older, unreferenced hands/wuji_hand directory in the same dataset: that is the upstream hand/body package at v1.0.1 -- same kinematics, but no thumb pad, no simplified-collision flavour, unprefixed link/joint names, and looser joint limits and effort ceilings. Nothing in Eden loads it.

docs.title: Composite robots
docs.text: A composite is a CompositeEntityOptions: it round-trips through the config system and is added to a scene by name like any other entity, and the scene expands it into its unit robots plus the welds that join them. It exposes the controller metadata as properties (arm_dofs on every arm rig, plus gripper_dofs, gripper_open, gripper_close, ... on a ManipulatorOptions and hand_dofs on a DexManipulatorOptions; robot_dofs, left_hand_dofs, right_hand_dofs on a humanoid rig). ManipulatorOptions carries a two-finger gripper, DexManipulatorOptions a dexterous hand, and HumanoidOptions one end-effector per wrist.

docs.title: Composite base classes
docs.text:
Base options for composite robots (an arm + an attached gripper, and kin).

A composite robot bundles several unit-robot :class:RobotOptions into one rig that a scene expands into its constituent entities + welds. Unlike the unit robots in eden/options/robots, a composite is itself a validated Options (a :class:~eden.options.entities.CompositeEntityOptions), so it round-trips through the config system, can declare its own fields, and is added to a scene by name like any other entity::

from eden.options.robots import Droid

droid = Droid(base_pos=(0.0, 0.0, 0.4))
scene = en.scenes.Empty(is_support_enabled=True, robot=droid)   # -> robot (arm) + gripper + weld
# ...the same object exposes the controller metadata as shortcut properties:
DifferentialIKController.configure(entity_name=droid.arm_name,
                                   ee_link_name=droid.ee_link,
                                   dofs_name=droid.arm_dofs)

Two end-effector cases share one arm base (:class:_ArmCompositeOptions): :class:ManipulatorOptions bolts on a two-finger gripper (the manipulator); :class:DexManipulatorOptions bolts on a multi-DOF dexterous hand. Concrete rigs (Franka + Robotiq, UR5e, Franka + XHand, …) subclass one of these with default fields and register in :data:COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY. A humanoid carrying an end-effector per wrist is the third shape, :class:HumanoidOptions — a sibling of the arm base rather than a subclass, because its root is a humanoid with two welds instead of an arm with one (see :mod:eden.options.robots.composite.oli_wuji). mjlab attaches the end-effector to each arm at a tool frame via with_gripper; Eden's equivalent is the scene attachments_dict, which the composite fills in from :meth:expand.
