def apply_actions(self) -> None:
    entity = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)
    current_pos, current_quat = self._control_point_pose(entity)
    full_jacobian = entity.get_jacobian(link=entity.links[self._ee_link_idx], local_point=self._ee_local_pos)[
        :, : self.action_dim
    ]
    jacobian = full_jacobian.index_select(-1, self._dofs_idx_name_order)
    full_dofs_vel = entity.get_dofs_vel()
    task_velocity = (full_jacobian @ full_dofs_vel.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
    if self.control_mode == "position":
        task_error = self._goal_pos - current_pos
    else:
        task_error = torch.cat(
            [self._goal_pos - current_pos, self._orientation_error(self._goal_quat, current_quat)],
            dim=-1,
        )
    desired_acceleration = self._kp * task_error - self._kd * task_velocity
    invalid_envs = (
        ~torch.isfinite(full_jacobian).all(dim=(-2, -1))
        | ~torch.isfinite(full_dofs_vel).all(dim=-1)
        | ~torch.isfinite(desired_acceleration).all(dim=-1)
    )

    if self._needs_mass_matrix:
        mass_matrix = entity.get_mass_mat()
        mass_matrix = mass_matrix.index_select(1, self.dofs_idx_local).index_select(2, self.dofs_idx_local)
        mass_solve_jacobian_t, invalid_mass_solve = _solve_mass_matrix_jacobian_transpose(
            mass_matrix,
            jacobian,
        )
        invalid_envs |= invalid_mass_solve
        mass_solve_jacobian_t.masked_fill_(invalid_envs[:, None, None], 0.0)
        if self.inertial_decoupling == "full" or self.control_mode == "position" or self.nullspace_kp is not None:
            task_inertia, invalid_task_inertia = _damped_pseudoinverse(
                jacobian @ mass_solve_jacobian_t,
                self._task_identity,
                self.operational_inertia_damping,
            )
            invalid_envs |= invalid_task_inertia
        if self.nullspace_kp is not None:
            jacobian_bar = mass_solve_jacobian_t @ task_inertia
            nullspace = self._dofs_identity - jacobian_bar @ jacobian
    if self.inertial_decoupling == "none":
        desired_wrench = desired_acceleration
    elif self.inertial_decoupling == "full" or self.control_mode == "position":
        desired_wrench = (task_inertia @ desired_acceleration.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)
    else:
        block_identity = self._task_identity[:, :3, :3]
        position_inertia, invalid_position_inertia = _damped_pseudoinverse(
            jacobian[:, :3] @ mass_solve_jacobian_t[:, :, :3],
            block_identity,
            self.operational_inertia_damping,
        )
        orientation_inertia, invalid_orientation_inertia = _damped_pseudoinverse(
            jacobian[:, 3:] @ mass_solve_jacobian_t[:, :, 3:],
            block_identity,
            self.operational_inertia_damping,
        )
        invalid_envs |= invalid_position_inertia | invalid_orientation_inertia
        desired_wrench = torch.cat(
            [
                (position_inertia @ desired_acceleration[:, :3].unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1),
                (orientation_inertia @ desired_acceleration[:, 3:].unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1),
            ],
            dim=-1,
        )
    dofs_force = (jacobian.transpose(-2, -1) @ desired_wrench.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)

    if self.nullspace_kp is not None:
        dofs_pos = entity.get_dofs_pos(dofs_idx_local=self.genesis_dofs_idx)
        dofs_vel = entity.get_dofs_vel(dofs_idx_local=self.genesis_dofs_idx)
        self._nullspace_acceleration[:] = (
            self.nullspace_kp * (self._nullspace_reference_pos - dofs_pos) - self._nullspace_kd * dofs_vel
        )
        nullspace_force = mass_matrix @ self._nullspace_acceleration.unsqueeze(-1)
        dofs_force += (nullspace.transpose(-2, -1) @ nullspace_force).squeeze(-1)

    invalid_envs |= ~torch.isfinite(dofs_force).all(dim=-1)
    dofs_force.masked_fill_(invalid_envs[:, None], 0.0)
    self._processed_action.copy_(dofs_force)
    self.verify_command_shape(self._processed_action)
    entity.control_dofs_force(self._processed_action, dofs_idx_local=self.genesis_dofs_idx)

IKPoseController(env: EnvBase, options: ActionTermOptions)

Bases: ActionTerm

Absolute task-space pose controller: solve IK for a base-frame target pose each step.

The action is a base-frame target pose [x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz] (wxyz) for the end-effector link, optionally expressed at a virtual tool frame offset from that link. Each control step the target is transformed to the world frame, the tool offset is removed, and Genesis' IK is solved from the measured joint configuration so the resulting joint targets stay on the current elbow branch. Policies that emit accumulated Cartesian targets (RobotArena-style delta accumulation, DROID Cartesian velocity effectors) drive this term; a policy that emits per-step deltas relative to the measured pose should use :class:DifferentialIKController instead.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION entity_name

The name of the entity to control.

dofs_name

The arm DOFs the IK solution is applied to.

ee_link_name

The end-effector link the target pose refers to.

ee_link_offset_pos

Position of the virtual tool frame in the end-effector link frame. The link is driven to the pose that places this offset frame at the target.

ee_link_offset_quat

Orientation (wxyz) of the virtual tool frame in the end-effector link frame.

max_joint_delta

Per-step clamp (rad) on every joint's change from its measured position; also turns an IK branch discontinuity into a bounded step. None disables it.

joint_limit_margin

Keep commanded joints at least this far (rad) inside their limits.

max_ik_position_error

Reject an IK solution whose position residual (m) exceeds this and hold the measured arm pose instead. None disables the check.

max_ik_rotation_error

Same for the rotation residual (rad).

def build(self) -> None:
    super().build()
    if self.entity.n_qs != self.entity.n_dofs:
        # The IK seed and solution are full Genesis qpos vectors; indexing them by DOF index
        # is only valid when qpos and DOF indices coincide (no free/ball joints).
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)} requires a fixed-base entity with one qpos per DOF; "
            f"it has n_qs={self.entity.n_qs}, n_dofs={self.entity.n_dofs}."
        )
    self._all_qs_idx = torch.arange(self.entity.n_qs, device=self.device)
    self._ee_link = self.entity.get_link(self.ee_link_name)
    offset_pos = torch.as_tensor(self.ee_link_offset_pos, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device).unsqueeze(0)
    offset_quat = torch.as_tensor(self.ee_link_offset_quat, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device).unsqueeze(0)
    offset_quat = offset_quat / offset_quat.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-8)
    self._ee_link_offset_quat_inv = inv_quat(offset_quat)
    self._ee_link_offset_pos_inv = transform_by_quat(-offset_pos, self._ee_link_offset_quat_inv)

def compute(self, actions: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    assert actions.shape == (
        self.num_envs,
        self.action_dim,
    ), f"Expected actions shape: (num_envs, {self.action_dim}), got {actions.shape=}"
    self._prev_action[:] = self._raw_action
    self._raw_action[:] = actions

    target_pos_b = actions[:, :3]
    target_quat_b = actions[:, 3:7]
    target_quat_b = target_quat_b / target_quat_b.norm(dim=-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-8)
    # The target refers to the virtual tool frame; drive the EE link to the
    # pose that places that offset frame at the requested target.
    target_pos_w, target_quat_w = combine_frame_transforms(
        self.entity.get_pos(),
        self.entity.get_quat(),
        target_pos_b,
        target_quat_b,
    )
    target_pos_w, target_quat_w = combine_frame_transforms(
        target_pos_w,
        target_quat_w,
        self._ee_link_offset_pos_inv,
        self._ee_link_offset_quat_inv,
    )

    # Genesis-local indices: read through dofs_idx_local, never index a dofs_name-ordered array.
    current_arm = self.entity.get_dofs_pos(dofs_idx_local=self.genesis_dofs_idx)
    # Full qpos in Genesis-native order, the layout inverse_kinematics expects for init_qpos.
    current_qpos = self.entity.get_qpos(qs_idx_local=self._all_qs_idx)
    ik_result = self.entity.inverse_kinematics(
        self.ee_link_name,
        poss=target_pos_w,
        quats=target_quat_w,
        # Explicitly seed from the measured configuration. This prevents
        # random-restart IK from selecting a distant Franka elbow branch.
        init_qpos=current_qpos,
        dofs_idx_local=self.genesis_dofs_idx,
        return_error=True,
    )
    target_q, ik_error = ik_result
    if not isinstance(target_q, torch.Tensor):
        target_q = torch.as_tensor(target_q, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
    target_q = target_q.to(device=self.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    if target_q.ndim == 1:
        target_q = target_q.unsqueeze(0)

    # inverse_kinematics returns the full Genesis-native qpos (n_qs == n_dofs, checked in build()).
    processed = target_q[:, self.dofs_idx_local]
    if not isinstance(ik_error, torch.Tensor):
        ik_error = torch.as_tensor(ik_error, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
    ik_error = ik_error.to(device=self.device, dtype=torch.float32)
    if ik_error.ndim == 1:
        ik_error = ik_error.unsqueeze(0)

    finite = torch.isfinite(processed).all(dim=-1) & torch.isfinite(ik_error).all(dim=-1)
    acceptable = finite.clone()
    if self.max_ik_position_error is not None:
        acceptable &= ik_error[..., :3].norm(dim=-1) <= float(self.max_ik_position_error)
    if self.max_ik_rotation_error is not None:
        acceptable &= ik_error[..., 3:6].norm(dim=-1) <= float(self.max_ik_rotation_error)
    if not acceptable.all():
        # Never pass a failed IK result into the rigid solver: one NaN
        # position target permanently poisons the simulation state. Hold
        # the affected arm at its measured joints and continue instead.
        processed = torch.where(acceptable.unsqueeze(-1), processed, current_arm)
        rejected = ~acceptable
        position_residual = ik_error[..., :3].norm(dim=-1)
        rotation_residual = ik_error[..., 3:6].norm(dim=-1)
        rejected_position_residual = position_residual[rejected].detach().cpu().tolist()
        rejected_rotation_residual = rotation_residual[rejected].detach().cpu().tolist()
        rejected_target_pos_b = target_pos_b[rejected].detach().cpu().tolist()
        rejected_target_quat_b = target_quat_b[rejected].detach().cpu().tolist()
        en.logger.warning(
            f"{term_subject(self)} rejected an invalid or excessive-residual IK target; "
            f"holding the current arm pose for {int(rejected.sum().item())} environment(s). "
            f"position_residual_m={rejected_position_residual} "
            f"(limit={self.max_ik_position_error}), "
            f"rotation_residual_rad={rejected_rotation_residual} "
            f"(limit={self.max_ik_rotation_error}), "
            f"target_pos_base_m={rejected_target_pos_b}, "
            f"target_quat_base_wxyz={rejected_target_quat_b}."
        )

    # DROID's RobotIKSolver limits every Franka joint to 0.2 rad per
    # Cartesian command. Applying the same bound here also makes an IK
    # branch discontinuity harmless instead of a full-arm jump.
    if self.max_joint_delta is not None:
        max_delta = float(self.max_joint_delta)
        processed = current_arm + torch.clamp(processed - current_arm, -max_delta, max_delta)

    # DROID's dm_robotics Cartesian effector keeps 0.3 rad away from joint
    # limits. Clamp the commanded target to the same interior band. If the
    # measured state is already outside it, max_joint_delta above moves it
    # back gradually rather than teleporting it.
    if self.joint_limit_margin > 0.0:
        lower, upper = self.entity.get_dofs_limit(dofs_idx_local=self.genesis_dofs_idx)
        lower = torch.as_tensor(lower, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
        upper = torch.as_tensor(upper, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device)
        safe_lower = lower + float(self.joint_limit_margin)
        safe_upper = upper - float(self.joint_limit_margin)
        processed = torch.maximum(safe_lower, torch.minimum(processed, safe_upper))
        if self.max_joint_delta is not None:
            max_delta = float(self.max_joint_delta)
            processed = current_arm + torch.clamp(processed - current_arm, -max_delta, max_delta)
    self._processed_action = processed

docs.title: FreeBasePoseController
docs.text:
FreeBasePoseController(env: EnvBase, options: ActionTermOptions)

Bases: ActionTerm

Drive a floating base to a pose near its default root pose (Genesis free-joint PD).

For an entity that stands on nothing (a dexterous hand or a gripper with no arm: a "flying" end effector), this term is the arm. Its action is six numbers per environment: a translation along the world axes, at position_scale metres per unit, then a rotation vector about the world axes, at orientation_scale radians per unit. Both are applied to the entity's default root pose, about its authored origin (a hand's wrist), so the target is absolute: a zero action holds the default pose.

The target orientation is composed as a quaternion and only then written as the free joint's intrinsic xyz Euler angles, which Genesis turns straight back into a quaternion to take a rotation-vector error. Nothing is added in Euler space, so a default orientation at the Euler singularity (pitch at 90 degrees, which a palm-down hand is) costs nothing.

Genesis position control places the solver frame, which for a re-origined body is not the authored frame that default_root_pos / default_root_quat describe (see docs/guides/entities.md). The offset between them is measured once at build and applied to every target.

The gains below are written to the six free-joint DOFs at build. Nothing else sets them: Eden applies default_dofs_kp / default_dofs_kd to the joints in dofs_name only, and Genesis leaves a free joint at zero gain with an unbounded force range. Gravity is not in the loop. Give the entity RigidMaterialOptions(gravity_compensation=1.0), as a real arm's controller would, or it hangs m * g / position_kp below its target and the orientation loop carries the weight's moment about the origin.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION entity_name

The floating-base entity. It must have exactly one free joint and must not be attached to another entity.

TYPE: str

position_scale

Metres per unit of translation action, scalar or per world axis.

TYPE: float | tuple[float, float, float]

orientation_scale

Radians per unit of rotation-vector action, scalar or per world axis.

TYPE: float | tuple[float, float, float]

position_kp

Translational stiffness, N/m.

TYPE: float

position_kd

Translational damping, N·s/m.

TYPE: float

orientation_kp

Rotational stiffness, N·m/rad.

TYPE: float

orientation_kd

Rotational damping, N·m·s/rad.

TYPE: float

force_limit

Bound on each translational DOF's control force, N.

TYPE: float

torque_limit

Bound on each rotational DOF's control torque, N·m.

def build(self) -> None:
    if self.dofs_name:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)} drives the entity's free joint, so it takes no "
            f"`dofs_name`; got {self.dofs_name!r}. Drive the other joints with a joint controller of their own."
        )
    gains = {
        "position_kp": self.position_kp,
        "position_kd": self.position_kd,
        "orientation_kp": self.orientation_kp,
        "orientation_kd": self.orientation_kd,
        "force_limit": self.force_limit,
        "torque_limit": self.torque_limit,
    }
    negative = {name: value for name, value in gains.items() if value < 0.0}
    if negative:
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)}: gains must be >= 0, got {negative}.")

    self._entity = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)
    entity: RigidEntity = self._entity
    # Raises, naming the joints, unless there is exactly one free joint: a fixed or attached base has none.
    base_dofs = entity.find_free_base_dofs_idx_local()
    self.dofs_idx_local = torch.as_tensor(base_dofs, dtype=gs.tc_int, device=self.device)
    self._n_dofs = len(base_dofs)

    self._position_scale = self._per_axis(self.position_scale, "position_scale")
    self._orientation_scale = self._per_axis(self.orientation_scale, "orientation_scale")

    kp = torch.tensor([self.position_kp] * 3 + [self.orientation_kp] * 3, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=self.device)
    kd = torch.tensor([self.position_kd] * 3 + [self.orientation_kd] * 3, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=self.device)
    limit = torch.tensor([self.force_limit] * 3 + [self.torque_limit] * 3, dtype=gs.tc_float, device=self.device)
    if entity.has_batched_dofs_info:
        kp, kd, limit = (value.expand(self.num_envs, -1) for value in (kp, kd, limit))
    entity.set_dofs_kp(kp, dofs_idx_local=self.genesis_dofs_idx)
    entity.set_dofs_kd(kd, dofs_idx_local=self.genesis_dofs_idx)
    entity.set_dofs_force_range(-limit, limit, dofs_idx_local=self.genesis_dofs_idx)
    if entity._needs_explicit_damping_armature:
        # The same first-order implicit damping Eden folds into an actuated joint's armature (see RigidEntity).
        armature = entity.get_dofs_armature(dofs_idx_local=self.genesis_dofs_idx)
        substep_dt = self._env.scene.sim._substep_dt
        entity.set_dofs_armature(
            (armature if entity.has_batched_dofs_info else armature[0]) + kd * substep_dt,
            dofs_idx_local=self.genesis_dofs_idx,
        )

    # Solver frame relative to the authored frame, in the authored frame: a rigid offset of the body, so reading
    # it wherever the entity happens to be is exact.
    authored_pos, authored_quat = entity.get_pos(relative=True), entity.get_quat(relative=True)
    self._offset_pos = inv_transform_by_quat(entity.get_pos() - authored_pos, authored_quat)
    self._offset_quat = quat_mul(inv_quat(authored_quat), entity.get_quat())
    self._default_pos, self._default_quat = entity.get_default_root_pose()

    self._raw_action = torch.zeros(self.num_envs, self.action_dim, device=self.device)
    self._prev_action = torch.zeros(self.num_envs, self.action_dim, device=self.device)
    self._processed_action = torch.zeros(self.num_envs, self._n_dofs, device=self.device)

def target_pose(self, actions: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """The authored-frame pose ``actions`` asks for: the default root pose, moved and then turned.

    Parameters
    ----------
    actions : torch.Tensor
        ``(num_envs, 6)``: translation, then rotation vector, in action units.

    Returns
    -------
    tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]
        Position ``(num_envs, 3)`` and wxyz quaternion ``(num_envs, 4)``.
    """
    pos = self._default_pos + actions[:, :3] * self._position_scale
    quat = quat_mul(quat_from_axis_angle(actions[:, 3:] * self._orientation_scale), self._default_quat)
    return pos, quat

def compute(self, actions: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    self._prev_action[:] = self._raw_action
    self._raw_action[:] = actions
    pos, quat = self.target_pose(self._raw_action)
    solver_pos = pos + transform_by_quat(self._offset_pos, quat)
    solver_quat = quat_mul(quat, self._offset_quat)
    # A free joint's DOF positions are its position and its intrinsic xyz Euler angles.
    self._processed_action = torch.cat((solver_pos, quat_to_xyz(solver_quat, rpy=False)), dim=-1)

def build(self) -> None:
    super().build()

    self._open_action = torch.zeros(1, self.num_dofs, device=self.device)
    self._close_action = torch.zeros(1, self.num_dofs, device=self.device)

    # Keys resolve to positions in this term's own `dofs_name` (the layout of the two rows), but a key that is
    # exactly a joint's name is literal against every joint of the entity: another term's or a passive
    # `pin.1` selects nothing here, rather than this term's `pin_1` as a regex.
    every_joint = [joint.name for joint in self.entity.joints]

    if isinstance(self.open_action, float):
        self._open_action[:] = self.open_action
    elif isinstance(self.open_action, dict):
        for dofs_name, open_action in self.open_action.items():
            term_idx, _ = resolve_matching_names(
                dofs_name, self.dofs_name, preserve_order=True, literal_names=every_joint
            )
            self._open_action[:, term_idx] = open_action
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)}: unsupported open_action type {type(self.open_action)}.")

    if isinstance(self.close_action, float):
        self._close_action[:] = self.close_action
    elif isinstance(self.close_action, dict):
        for dofs_name, close_action in self.close_action.items():
            term_idx, _ = resolve_matching_names(
                dofs_name, self.dofs_name, preserve_order=True, literal_names=every_joint
            )
            self._close_action[:, term_idx] = close_action
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)}: unsupported close_action type {type(self.close_action)}.")

    self._raw_action[:] = actions
    if actions.dtype == torch.bool:
        close_mask = actions
    else:
        close_mask = (actions * self.scale) > 0
    self._processed_action = (
        self._open_action.repeat(self.num_envs, 1) * (~close_mask)
        + self._close_action.repeat(self.num_envs, 1) * close_mask
    )

docs.title: GripperDecisionController
docs.text:
GripperDecisionController(env: EnvBase, options: ActionTermOptions)

Bases: BinaryJointController

Gripper controller that decides open/close from a policy scalar.

Policy servers describe the gripper in different units and conventions (> 0 means close for some, open for others; a closedness or an openness in [0, 1] for others), often with noise that wants hysteresis, a hold, or a latch. This term takes the raw scalar and decides, so a client only slices its action vector. With the defaults it behaves exactly like :class:BinaryJointController.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION input

Meaning of the scalar: sign closes on > 0 (parent behaviour), open_sign opens on > 0, closedness / openness are [0, 1] amounts.

threshold

Binarisation point for closedness / openness: a closedness strictly above it closes; an openness strictly above it opens.

open_threshold

Hysteresis on closedness: once closed, open only below open_threshold; once open, close only above close_threshold. Set both to enable (they replace threshold); a value exactly on a threshold keeps the current state.

close_threshold

Hysteresis on closedness: once closed, open only below open_threshold; once open, close only above close_threshold. Set both to enable (they replace threshold); a value exactly on a threshold keeps the current state.

hold_steps

After a state change, the new state lasts at least this many decisions, counting the one that changed it (hysteresis mode only; 0 and 1 do not hold).

sticky_repeats

Fractal / Google-robot latch (SimplerEnv CogACT / SpatialVLA google_robot): the relative command is prev - openness (> 0 closes), with prev taken from the first command and updated only when the latch triggers. A jump of more than 0.5 triggers the latch, which repeats the jump for this many steps; otherwise the small relative command itself is sent. The command then drives ManiSkill's gripper_pd_joint_target_delta_pos controller: the target (in closedness) starts at the measured gripper, moves by 1.31 * clip(command, -1, 1) / 1.3 per step, clipped to the joint range [-0.0101, 1.31] / 1.3, and holds when the move is below 1e-3 / 1.3. The fingers follow that target continuously. Needs an openness / closedness input. 0 disables.

zero_holds

With a sign / open_sign input, a command of exactly 0 keeps the previous state instead of opening (robosuite's gripper steps by sign(action)).

continuous

Interpolate the DOF targets between open_action and close_action by the closedness instead of binarising; snap_threshold promotes closedness above it to fully closed.

snap_threshold

See continuous.

on_missing

What a NaN command (the server omitted the gripper) does: hold keeps the previous target; measured commands the gripper's measured closedness every such step, as the DROID Galaxea reference client does.

Notes

Under on_missing="hold", a NaN before any command was received is seeded from the measured DOF position (the gripper is where it physically is). In place of a NaN, :attr:action (and so the ActionManager's buffers) records the command acted on, in the input's units: that measured seed, or the held previous command. Per-env decision state resets with the env (reset(envs_idx)).

def build(self) -> None:
    super().build()
    if self.input not in ("sign", "open_sign", "closedness", "openness"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)}: input={self.input!r}; expected sign, open_sign, closedness or openness."
        )
    if (self.open_threshold is None) != (self.close_threshold is None):
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)}: set both open_threshold and close_threshold or neither.")
    if self.open_threshold is not None and self.close_threshold < self.open_threshold:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)}: close_threshold ({self.close_threshold}) must be >= "
            f"open_threshold ({self.open_threshold})."
        )
    if self.hold_steps < 0 or self.sticky_repeats < 0:
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)}: hold_steps and sticky_repeats must be non-negative.")
    if self.continuous and self.input in ("sign", "open_sign"):
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)}: continuous mode needs a closedness or openness input.")
    if self.snap_threshold is not None and not 0.0 <= self.snap_threshold <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)}: snap_threshold must be in [0, 1].")
    if self.on_missing not in ("hold", "measured"):
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)}: on_missing={self.on_missing!r}; expected hold or measured.")
    # Settings that the selected mode would silently ignore.
    hysteresis = self.open_threshold is not None
    if self.hold_steps > 0 and not hysteresis:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)}: hold_steps only applies with open_threshold/close_threshold (hysteresis)."
        )
    if hysteresis and self.input in ("sign", "open_sign"):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)}: hysteresis thresholds need a closedness or openness input, not {self.input!r}."
        )
    if self.snap_threshold is not None and not self.continuous:
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)}: snap_threshold only applies with continuous=True.")
    if self.continuous and (hysteresis or self.sticky_repeats > 0):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)}: continuous mode cannot be combined with hysteresis or sticky_repeats."
        )
    if self.sticky_repeats > 0 and (hysteresis or self.input in ("sign", "open_sign")):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)}: sticky_repeats needs an openness/closedness input and no hysteresis."
        )
    if self.zero_holds and self.input not in ("sign", "open_sign"):
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)}: zero_holds only applies to a sign or open_sign input.")
    if self.on_missing == "measured" and not self.continuous:
        # Re-deciding from a stalled grasp's measured position would re-binarize (or re-latch) it open.
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)}: on_missing='measured' needs continuous=True.")
    n = self.num_envs
    dev = self.device
    self._closed = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=dev)  # starts open
    self._hold_remaining = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.long, device=dev)
    self._sticky_prev = torch.full((n,), float("nan"), device=dev)  # unset until the first command
    self._sticky_on = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=dev)
    self._sticky_count = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.long, device=dev)
    self._sticky_action = torch.zeros(n, device=dev)
    self._sticky_target = torch.zeros(n, device=dev)  # delta-controller target, in closedness
    self._seen_command = torch.zeros(n, dtype=torch.bool, device=dev)
    self._last_processed = self._open_action.repeat(n, 1).clone()
    # Fixed at build time; resolved once so the per-step measured read never syncs with the device.
    self._measure_span_zero = bool(torch.isclose(self._open_action[0, 0], self._close_action[0, 0]))
    self.last_closedness = torch.zeros(n, device=dev)
    self._last_raw: torch.Tensor | None = None
    self._last_valid: torch.Tensor | None = None

def compute(self, actions: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    if actions.dtype == torch.bool:
        actions = actions.float() * 2.0 - 1.0  # True -> +1 (close), False -> -1 (open) in sign terms
        if self.input != "sign":
            raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)}: boolean commands are only valid with input='sign'.")
    raw = actions[:, 0].to(torch.float32)
    self._prev_action[:] = self._raw_action
    valid = ~torch.isnan(raw)
    missing = ~valid

    # Missing command: the gripper is wherever it physically is (first miss, or every miss
    # under on_missing="measured"). Computed unconditionally to avoid a host sync per step.
    seed = ~valid if self.on_missing == "measured" else ~valid & ~self._seen_command
    measured = self._measured_closedness()
    if self.input == "closedness":
        seeded = measured
    elif self.input == "openness":
        seeded = 1.0 - measured
    else:  # sign conventions: raw * scale > 0 means close for "sign", open for "open_sign"
        closed_sign = torch.where(measured > 0.5, torch.ones_like(raw), -torch.ones_like(raw))
        closed_sign = closed_sign if self.scale >= 0 else -closed_sign
        seeded = closed_sign if self.input == "sign" else -closed_sign
    raw = torch.where(seed, seeded, raw)
    valid = valid | seed
    self._seen_command |= valid
    # Record the command acted on, in the input's units: the seeded measured value, else (a held
    # miss) the previous command. The ActionManager stores this in place of the NaN
    # (_accepts_missing_command_), so last-action observations and recorders see what was done.
    self._raw_action[:, 0] = torch.where(missing & ~seed, self._prev_action[:, 0], raw)

    closedness = self._closedness_from_input(raw)
    if self.sticky_repeats > 0:
        cmd = torch.where(valid, self._sticky_step(closedness, measured, valid), self.last_closedness)
        processed = self._open_action + (self._close_action - self._open_action) * cmd.unsqueeze(-1)
        self._closed = cmd > 0.5
    elif self.continuous:
        cmd = closedness.clamp(0.0, 1.0)
        if self.snap_threshold is not None:
            cmd = torch.where(cmd > self.snap_threshold, torch.ones_like(cmd), cmd)
        cmd = torch.where(valid, cmd, self.last_closedness)
        processed = self._open_action + (self._close_action - self._open_action) * cmd.unsqueeze(-1)
        self._closed = cmd > 0.5
    else:
        self._closed = self._decide(raw, closedness, valid)
        cmd = self._closed.float()
        mask = self._closed.unsqueeze(-1)
        processed = torch.where(
            mask, self._close_action.expand(self.num_envs, -1), self._open_action.expand(self.num_envs, -1)
        )
    processed = torch.where(valid.unsqueeze(-1), processed, self._last_processed)
    self._last_processed = processed.clone()
    self.last_closedness = cmd
    self._processed_action = processed
    self._last_raw = raw
    self._last_valid = valid

Bases: _WeldingBase

Collision-aware welding of an object link to the suction-cup end-effector link.

When the action is applied and the end-effector link is in contact with an object link, the end-effector link and the object link are welded together.

Note

action is a boolean tensor, True: suction, False: release if float is used, >0: suction, <=0: release

def apply_actions(self) -> None:
    contact_info = self._entity.get_contacts(exclude_self_contact=True)
    link_a = contact_info["link_a"]
    link_b = contact_info["link_b"]
    valid_mask = contact_info["valid_mask"]
    # NOTE: get object links in contact
    objects_link_idx = torch.unique(
        torch.cat(
            [
                link_a[(link_b == self._ee_link_idx) & valid_mask],
                link_b[(link_a == self._ee_link_idx) & valid_mask],
            ]
        )
    )
    suction_mask = self._processed_action & ~self._welded
    if not suction_mask.any():
        return
    for link_idx in self._weldable(objects_link_idx):
        # NOTE: only add weld constraint if the object is not welded and the action is true
        envs_weld = suction_mask & (
            ((link_a == link_idx) & (link_b == self._ee_link_idx) & valid_mask).any(dim=1)
            | ((link_b == link_idx) & (link_a == self._ee_link_idx) & valid_mask).any(dim=1)
        )
        if not envs_weld.any():
            continue
        self._env.rigid_solver.add_weld_constraint(link_idx, self._ee_link_idx, envs_idx=envs_weld)
        self._welded[envs_weld] = True

docs.text:
ParallelJawWelding(env: EnvBase, options: ActionTermOptions)

Bases: _WeldingBase

Weld the link a parallel-jaw gripper is squeezing to the end-effector link.

While the action is on, an env with no weld welds a link to ee_link_name once both pads press that same link with contact force along the closing direction above grasp_force_threshold (:func:~eden.managers.terms.utils.parallel_jaw_is_grasping with object_link_idx). A link touching only one pad is never welded, and neither are two links each pressed by one pad: a grasp that spans two links of a multi-link object welds nothing. Releasing the action deletes the weld. An env holds at most one weld; if several links pass in the same step, the one with the lowest solver index is welded.

The force test is sign-agnostic, so both pads scraping the same surface while closing can pass it: list support surfaces (table, floor) in ignore_entities_name.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION entity_name

The name of the entity to control. (e.g., "robot")

ee_link_name

The name of the end-effector link. (e.g., "hand")

ignore_entities_name

The names of the entities to exclude from welding (e.g., "table", "floor").

ignore_links_idx

The rigid-solver (scene-global) link indices to exclude from welding, e.g. env.entities["table"].get_link("top").idx; an entity-local idx_local excludes the wrong link.

left_gripper_link_name

The name of the left gripper link. (e.g., "left_gripper_pad")

right_gripper_link_name

The name of the right gripper link. (e.g., "right_gripper_pad")

grasp_force_threshold

Minimum projected contact force (N) on each pad from the candidate link; >= 0.

def build(self) -> None:
    super().build()
    if not self.grasp_force_threshold >= 0.0:
        # The force test compares |projected force| > threshold, so a negative threshold passes every
        # contact, and NaN passes none: either way the weld no longer depends on a grasp.
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)}: grasp_force_threshold={self.grasp_force_threshold!r} must be >= 0 "
            "(newtons of contact force each pad must carry from the squeezed link). Use 0.0 to weld "
            "on any two-pad contact with that link."
        )

    self._left_gripper_link_idx = self._entity.get_link(self.left_gripper_link_name).idx
    self._right_gripper_link_idx = self._entity.get_link(self.right_gripper_link_name).idx
    self._gripper_idx_local = [

def apply_actions(self) -> None:
    # Only an env whose action is on and that holds no weld yet can weld this step.
    if not (self._processed_action & ~self._welded).any():
        return
    contact_info = self._entity.get_contacts(exclude_self_contact=True)
    link_a = contact_info["link_a"]
    link_b = contact_info["link_b"]
    valid_mask = contact_info["valid_mask"]

    # Candidates: every external link either pad touches. The grasp is checked per candidate below,
    # from that link's contacts alone, so contacts with different links never add up to one grasp.
    pad_a = (link_a == self._left_gripper_link_idx) | (link_a == self._right_gripper_link_idx)
    pad_b = (link_b == self._left_gripper_link_idx) | (link_b == self._right_gripper_link_idx)
    objects_link_idx = torch.unique(torch.cat([link_a[pad_b & valid_mask], link_b[pad_a & valid_mask]]))
    for link_idx in self._weldable(objects_link_idx):
        # Both pads carry force above the threshold (>= 0, checked in build) from this link, which
        # implies both touch it. Re-read _welded each time: an env welds at most one link per step.
        squeezed = parallel_jaw_is_grasping(
            self._entity,
            contact_info,
            self._left_gripper_link_idx,
            self._right_gripper_link_idx,
            self._gripper_idx_local,
            self.grasp_force_threshold,
            object_link_idx=link_idx,
        )
        envs_weld = self._processed_action & ~self._welded & squeezed
        if not envs_weld.any():
            continue

        self._env.rigid_solver.add_weld_constraint(link_idx, self._ee_link_idx, envs_idx=envs_weld)
        self._welded[envs_weld] = True

docs.title: Command Terms
docs.text:
Command terms produce the goal a policy is conditioned on (a base velocity, a target pose, a gait phase, a motion clip) and resample it on their own schedule. Other terms read a command by its config key through env.command_manager. The commands guide covers resampling and debug visualization; the term catalog lists every parameter.

from eden import commands

The base class CommandTerm is on the managers page.

docs.title: UniformVelocityCommand
docs.text:
UniformVelocityCommand(env: EnvBase, options: CommandTermOptions)

Bases: CommandTerm

SE(2) velocity command sampled from a uniform distribution.

The command comprises a linear velocity in x and y direction and an angular velocity around the z-axis. It is given in the robot's base frame.

If the heading_command attribute is set to True, the angular velocity is computed from the heading error similar to doing a proportional control on the heading error. The target heading is sampled uniformly from the provided range. Otherwise, the angular velocity is sampled uniformly from the provided range.

def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: CommandTermOptions):

docs.title: ConstantVelocityCommand
docs.text:
ConstantVelocityCommand(env: EnvBase, options: CommandTermOptions)

Bases: CommandTerm

SE(2) velocity command held at a fixed value instead of resampled.

Same command as :class:UniformVelocityCommand -- (vx, vy, wz) in the robot's base frame -- with the random generator taken out: the value is whatever :attr:command_value says, or whatever :meth:set_command was last given, and it never changes on its own.

This is the term a deployment substitutes for the trained one. A policy deployed from its training config keeps resampling the command it was trained against, which on a robot reads as the machine wandering off on its own; holding a value the operator chose is what a deploy actually wants. It is equally the right term for an evaluation that has to hold one command for a whole episode.

The value is clamped into lin_vel_x_range / lin_vel_y_range / ang_vel_z_range, which a deploy fills from the term it replaces, so the held command cannot leave the distribution the policy was trained on. A degenerate range — move_forward's lin_vel_x_range=(0.5, 0.5) — pins its axis: the policy only ever saw one velocity there, so that axis is not controllable and the clamp holds the single trained value whatever it is asked for. The clamp is logged.

Source code in eden/managers/terms/commands/velocity.py 
def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: CommandTermOptions):
    super().__init__(env, options)
    self.robot: Entity | None = None
    self.vel_command_b = torch.zeros(self.num_envs, 3, device=self.device)
    self._limits_key: tuple[tuple[float, float], ...] | None = None
    self._low: torch.Tensor | None = None
    self._high: torch.Tensor | None = None

def build(self) -> None:
    # Resolve the named entity and *keep* it, exactly as UniformVelocityCommand does:
    # consumers reach through the command term for it (``eden/managers/terms/metrics/
    # error.py`` reads ``command.robot.get_vel()``), so a substitute that only resolved
    # and discarded would not be interchangeable with the term it replaces. Resolving
    # here also means a bad name fails at setup rather than on the robot. An unnamed
    # entity is legitimate: a command term standing alone, driving no particular entity,
    # is what the task-less deploy path builds.
    if self.entity_name:
        self.robot = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)
    self._seed_command()

docs.text:
set_command(command, *, warn_on_clamp: bool = True) -> Tensor

Hold (vx, vy, wz) from now on, clamped into the configured ranges.

Returns the clamped command, and warns when clamping actually bit — a value outside the trained ranges is worth seeing rather than silently trimming.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION command

(vx, vy, wz) in the robot's base frame.

warn_on_clamp

Whether to log a clamp. Off for a value nothing will hold long enough to matter — :class:OperatorVelocityCommand seeds the buffer with command_value only so the first observation is in range, and the device overwrites it on the first compute.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: True

Source code in eden/managers/terms/commands/velocity.py 
def set_command(self, command, *, warn_on_clamp: bool = True) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Hold ``(vx, vy, wz)`` from now on, clamped into the configured ranges.

    Returns the clamped command, and warns when clamping actually bit — a value
    outside the trained ranges is worth seeing rather than silently trimming.

    Parameters
    ----------
    command
        ``(vx, vy, wz)`` in the robot's base frame.
    warn_on_clamp
        Whether to log a clamp. Off for a value nothing will hold long enough to
        matter — :class:`OperatorVelocityCommand` seeds the buffer with
        ``command_value`` only so the first observation is in range, and the device
        overwrites it on the first ``compute``.
    """
    value = torch.as_tensor(command, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device).flatten()
    if value.numel() != 3:
        raise ValueError(f"A velocity command is (vx, vy, wz); got {value.numel()} value(s): {command}.")
    low, high = self._limits()
    clamped = torch.clamp(value, min=low, max=high)
    if warn_on_clamp and not torch.equal(clamped, value):
        # Reported from ``_limits_key``, not the fields, so the range named here is
        # always the one that was actually applied.
        vx_range, vy_range, wz_range = self._limits_key
        en.logger.warning(
            f"[commands] Velocity command {value.tolist()} is outside the trained ranges "
            f"(vx {vx_range}, vy {vy_range}, wz {wz_range}); holding {clamped.tolist()} instead."
        )
    self.vel_command_b[:] = clamped
    return clamped

OperatorVelocityCommand(env: EnvBase, options: CommandTermOptions)

Bases: ConstantVelocityCommand

SE(2) velocity command driven live by a human, from a keyboard or a gamepad.

A :class:ConstantVelocityCommand whose held value is re-read from an input device every control step. Deploy a locomotion policy with this term substituted for its trained :class:UniformVelocityCommand and the robot goes where the operator says instead of where the training distribution says.

The device emits a normalized deflection; it is scaled into the same lin_vel_*_range / ang_vel_z_range and clamped there, so full deflection is the fastest command the policy was trained on and the operator cannot ask for more. See :mod:eden.utils.devices.se2 for the bindings.

For deployment and interactive evaluation, not for training: it reads a physical device, so a training run would sit at whatever the sticks happen to say.

def build(self) -> None:
    from eden.utils.devices.se2 import make_se2_device, scale_se2_deflection

    super().build()
    # The device is opened in build(), not __init__: build() is the last step of term
    # construction, so one that cannot be opened (no display for pynput, no gamepad
    # plugged in) leaves the term unusable rather than half-alive.
    self._device = make_se2_device(self.device_name, self.device_options)
    # Bound once rather than imported per control step.
    self._scale = scale_se2_deflection
    en.logger.info(
        f"[commands] Operator velocity command via {self.device_name}: "
        f"vx {self.lin_vel_x_range}, vy {self.lin_vel_y_range}, wz {self.ang_vel_z_range}."
    )

def draw_vis(self) -> None:
    # Goal marker (eval/inference only; gated on debug_vis by the manager).
    pos = self.oracle_pos_b
    if self.marker_frame_entity:
        ent = self.resolve_entity(self.marker_frame_entity)
        pos = ent.get_pos() + transform_by_quat(pos, ent.get_quat())
    marker = (
        self._env.entities[self.marker_entity_name]
        if self.marker_entity_name and self.marker_entity_name in self._env.entities
        else None
    )
    if marker is not None:
        # Move a real (non-colliding) entity to the goal — renders in cameras,
        # unlike draw_debug_* which only shows in the interactive viewer.
        marker.set_pos(pos.detach())
    else:
        self._env.clear_debug_objects()
        self._env.draw_debug_spheres(pos.detach().cpu().numpy(), radius=self.marker_radius, color=self.marker_color)

docs.text: Gait phase command term for bipedal locomotion.

docs.title: GaitPhaseCommand
docs.text:
GaitPhaseCommand(env: EnvBase, options: CommandTermOptions)

Bases: CommandTerm

Command generator that maintains a cyclic gait phase for each foot.

Generates a per-foot phase signal that advances at a configurable frequency. The left foot starts at phase 0 and the right foot starts at phase_offset (default pi for an alternating gait).

The command property returns the raw phase angles (num_envs, num_feet). Use the sin_phase / cos_phase observation terms to feed these into the policy.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION gait_frequency

Gait cycle frequency in Hz (cycles per second). Default 1.25 Hz.

phase_offset

Phase offset between left and right foot in radians. Default pi (alternating).

num_feet

Number of feet. Default 2.

velocity_command_name

Optional name of a velocity-style command term (e.g. UniformVelocityCommand) whose command tensor has shape (num_envs, ≥3) interpreted as [lin_x, lin_y, ang_z] in the base frame. When set, the gait phase is pinned to stand_phase_value for environments whose commanded velocities are below stand_velocity_threshold — so downstream alternating-gait rewards stop enforcing a step cycle while the policy is commanded to stand. None (default) keeps the phase always cycling.

stand_velocity_threshold

Velocity-magnitude threshold (m/s for linear, rad/s for angular) below which a command is treated as "stand". Default 0.01.

stand_phase_value

Phase value (radians) assigned to all feet for stand-mode envs. Setting both feet to the same phase means the gait reward stops penalizing alternation while standing. Default pi matches the common contact-schedule formulation where cos(phase) > 0 is stance.

Source code in eden/managers/terms/commands/gait.py 
def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: CommandTermOptions):
    super().__init__(env, options)
    self._phase = torch.zeros(self.num_envs, self.num_feet, device=self.device)
    # Initialize with offsets (left=0, right=phase_offset, ...)
    for i in range(self.num_feet):
        self._phase[:, i] = i * self.phase_offset
    self._stand_shape_validated = False

docs.title: Motion clips
docs.text:
MotionCommand plays .npz motion clips on a plain RLEnvBase, for frozen-policy inference and single-clip tracking. Training-grade motion tracking goes through MimicRLEnvBase and the motion manager instead.

Motion-clip command term (single- and multi-clip) and npz loaders.

A :class:CommandTerm that drives motion-imitation / tracking policies from one or more BeyondMimic-format .npz clips. Single-clip is the M == 1 case of the multi-clip library. Shared by the frozen ONNX policy ports (sonic, twist2, humanoid_gpt, protomotionv3, beyondmimic_moves) and the beyondmimic example.

Which motion path to use

Eden has two motion-reference systems; pick by use case:

  • This command-term path (MotionCommand) — lightweight, for frozen-policy inference / single-clip tracking on a plain RLEnvBase. Loads npz clips verbatim and exposes the current frame (plus arbitrary future frames via :meth:MotionCommand.gather_motion_frames) directly off the command term. No dataset pipeline.
  • The manager path (eden.managers.motion_manager.MotionManager + eden.utils.motion_reference) — training-grade: dataset adapters, continuous-time interpolation, a future-frame window, symmetry augmentation, and motion-id / start-time curricula. Owned by MimicRLEnvBase and consumed by the tracking reward / observation / termination terms. See docs/guides/motion-tracking.md.

Both expose the same world-frame vocabulary — links_*_w (tracked-link poses) and base_*_w (floating-base root) — so reward / metric code reads the same field names regardless of source.

Config vs data vocabulary

The configurable links_name list names the tracked links; their per-frame data is read as links_*_w. Two links_name members are special: the floating-base body (base_link_name, default links_name[0]; exposed as base_*_w, used to reset the robot root) and anchor_link_name (the yaw-warp reference, exposed as anchor_*_w). Both are resolved and validated against links_name in :meth:build. The npz on-disk keys stay body_*_w (file format); only the Python accessors are links_*.

def __init__(
    self,
    motion_file: str,
    links_idx: torch.Tensor,
    device: torch.device = torch.device("cpu"),
    links_name: list[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    data = np.load(motion_file)
    body_cols = resolve_body_cols(data, links_idx, links_name)

    def _load(key: str) -> torch.Tensor:
        return torch.tensor(data[key], dtype=torch.float32, device=device)

    self.dofs_pos = _load("joint_pos")
    self.dofs_vel = _load("joint_vel")
    self.time_step_total = self.dofs_pos.shape[0]
    # Body axes are sliced to the requested links; quats are wxyz (MuJoCo convention).
    self.links_pos_w = _load("body_pos_w")[:, body_cols]
    self.links_quat_w = _load("body_quat_w")[:, body_cols]
    self.links_lin_vel_w = _load("body_lin_vel_w")[:, body_cols]
    self.links_ang_vel_w = _load("body_ang_vel_w")[:, body_cols]

docs.title: MultiMotionLoader
docs.text:
MultiMotionLoader(motion_files: list[str], links_idx: Tensor, device: device, links_name: list[str] | None = None)

Batched verbatim loader for a list of BeyondMimic .npz clips.

Mirrors :class:MotionLoader field-for-field, but stacks M clips of possibly different lengths into padded (M, T_max, ...) tensors plus a per-clip frame_total (M,). Fields are loaded VERBATIM (no interpolation, no velocity recompute) so each clip is bit-identical to the single-clip path. With M == 1 (the single-clip case) T_max == T and no padding occurs, so library[0, t] is plain single-clip indexing.

Padding edge-replicates each clip's last valid frame (never zeros): a zero quaternion would NaN yaw_quat, and an over-read then degrades to a "hold last frame" end-of-motion behavior (the per-env wrap keeps reads in range anyway).

Source code in eden/managers/terms/commands/mimic.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    motion_files: list[str],
    links_idx: torch.Tensor,
    device: torch.device,
    links_name: list[str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    if not motion_files:
        raise ValueError("MultiMotionLoader: motion_files is empty")
    self.motion_refs = [os.path.splitext(os.path.basename(f))[0] for f in motion_files]
    clips = [np.load(f) for f in motion_files]
    lengths = [int(c["joint_pos"].shape[0]) for c in clips]
    # All fields of a clip must share its frame count; otherwise the per-field
    # padding below would misalign body vs joint frames silently.
    for f, c in zip(motion_files, clips):
        for k in ("joint_vel", "body_pos_w", "body_quat_w", "body_lin_vel_w", "body_ang_vel_w"):
            if k in c and int(c[k].shape[0]) != int(c["joint_pos"].shape[0]):
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{f}: field '{k}' has {c[k].shape[0]} frames but joint_pos has {c['joint_pos'].shape[0]}"
                )
    # Resolve each clip's body columns by name (order-independent of Genesis) when the npz
    # provides ``body_names``, else fall back to the Genesis idx_local in ``links_idx``.
    body_cols = [resolve_body_cols(c, links_idx, links_name) for c in clips]
    m, t_max = len(clips), max(lengths)
    self.frame_total = torch.tensor(lengths, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    self.time_step_total = t_max  # nominal; per-clip lengths live in frame_total

    def _stack(key: str, link_sliced: bool) -> torch.Tensor:
        out: torch.Tensor | None = None
        for i, clip in enumerate(clips):
            t = torch.tensor(clip[key], dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
            if link_sliced:
                t = t[:, body_cols[i]]
            if out is None:
                out = t.new_zeros((m, t_max, *t.shape[1:]))
            length = t.shape[0]
            out[i, :length] = t
            if length < t_max:  # edge-replicate the last valid frame
                out[i, length:] = t[length - 1]
        return out

    self.dofs_pos = _stack("joint_pos", False)  # (M, T_max, 29)
    self.dofs_vel = _stack("joint_vel", False)  # (M, T_max, 29)
    self.links_pos_w = _stack("body_pos_w", True)  # (M, T_max, n_bodies, 3)
    self.links_quat_w = _stack("body_quat_w", True)  # (M, T_max, n_bodies, 4)
    self.links_lin_vel_w = _stack("body_lin_vel_w", True)
    self.links_ang_vel_w = _stack("body_ang_vel_w", True)

MotionCommand(env: EnvBase, options: CommandTermOptions)

Bases: CommandTerm

Motion command for mimicking one or more motion clips.

Backed by a :class:MultiMotionLoader clip library and a per-env (motion_id, time_steps) gather. A single clip is just the M == 1 case: every env stays on clip 0 and the gather reduces to plain single-clip indexing. Passing motion_files=[...] (or a list to :func:motion_command_options) assigns each env its own clip, re-sampled on every reset/wrap so all clips are exercised regardless of num_envs vs num_clips.

Sampling modes: start / uniform work for any clip count; adaptive (the failure-bin start-time curriculum) requires a single clip, since the bins partition one clip's timeline.

def build(self) -> None:
    self.robot = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)

    # NOTE: avoid tensor indexing by passing int
    robot_base_dofs_index = self.robot.find_free_base_dofs_idx_local(self.base_joint_name)
    self.robot_base_dofs_index = torch.as_tensor(
        robot_base_dofs_index, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device
    ).contiguous()
    self.base_and_dofs_index = torch.cat([self.robot_base_dofs_index, self.robot.dofs_idx_local]).contiguous()

    # Resolve a links_name member to its row in ``links_*_w``, failing loudly on a mistyped or reordered
    # name instead of a bare index error or (for the base) a silent wrong-link root reset.
    def links_index(link_name: str, field_name: str) -> int:
        if link_name not in self.links_name:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{term_subject(self)}: {field_name}={link_name!r} must be a member "
                f"of links_name; got links_name={self.links_name}"
            )
        return self.links_name.index(link_name)

    self.motion_anchor_link_index = links_index(self.anchor_link_name, "anchor_link_name")
    self.base_link_index = 0 if self.base_link_name is None else links_index(self.base_link_name, "base_link_name")

    self.links_idx = torch.tensor(
        self.robot.find_named_links_idx_local(self.links_name, preserve_order=True)[1],
        dtype=torch.long,
        device=self.device,
    )

    # Single-clip is the M=1 case of the clip library: ``motion_file`` is the
    # single-clip shorthand for ``motion_files=[motion_file]``.
    motion_files = list(self.motion_files) if self.motion_files else [self.motion_file]
    self.num_clips = len(motion_files)
    if self.num_clips > 1 and self.sampling_mode == "adaptive":
        raise ValueError(
            "adaptive sampling requires a single clip (the failure-bin curriculum partitions "
            f"one clip's timeline); got {self.num_clips} clips. Use sampling_mode 'start' or 'uniform'."
        )

    self.motion = MultiMotionLoader(motion_files, self.links_idx, device=self.device, links_name=self.links_name)
    self.time_steps = torch.zeros(self.num_envs, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)
    self.motion_id = torch.zeros(self.num_envs, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)
    self.frame_total = self.motion.frame_total[self.motion_id]  # (N,) per-env clip length
    self.links_pos_relative_w = torch.zeros(self.num_envs, len(self.links_name), 3, device=self.device)
    self.links_quat_relative_w = torch.zeros(self.num_envs, len(self.links_name), 4, device=self.device)
    self.links_quat_relative_w[:, :, 0].fill_(1.0)

    # Adaptive failure-bin curriculum state. The bins partition the (single)
    # clip's timeline; for multi-clip these stay allocated but unused
    # (``sampling_mode == "adaptive"`` is rejected above for M > 1).
    self.bin_count = int(self.motion.time_step_total // (1 / self._env.dt)) + 1
    self.bin_failed_count = torch.zeros(self.bin_count, dtype=torch.float, device=self.device)
    self._current_bin_failed = torch.zeros(self.bin_count, dtype=torch.float, device=self.device)
    self.bin_starts_count = torch.zeros(self.bin_count, dtype=torch.float, device=self.device)
    self._current_bin_starts = torch.zeros(self.bin_count, dtype=torch.float, device=self.device)
    self.start_bin = torch.zeros(self.num_envs, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)
    self.kernel = torch.tensor(
        [self.adaptive_lambda**i for i in range(self.adaptive_kernel_size)],
        device=self.device,
    )
    self.kernel = self.kernel / self.kernel.sum()

    # How `_resample_command` hands the reset state to Genesis. Where its setters can keep the
    # bool env mask on the device — a `torch.where` into the state and a masked
    # forward-kinematics kernel — they take every env's row and a `range` for each DOF axis
    # (`RigidEntity.setters_take_every_row`). Otherwise, e.g. under a `dofs_name` reordered away from the
    # asset's or with hibernation on, they take the selected rows and the DOF indices: Genesis'
    # indexed path, which pays a `nonzero()` GPU->CPU sync per setter to turn the mask into indices.
    dofs_range = contiguous_range(self.base_and_dofs_index)
    qs_range = contiguous_range(self.robot.qs_idx_local)
    self._reset_through_mask = self.robot.setters_take_every_row and dofs_range is not None and qs_range is not None
    self._reset_dofs_idx = dofs_range if self._reset_through_mask else self.base_and_dofs_index
    self._reset_qs_idx = qs_range if self._reset_through_mask else self.robot.qs_idx_local

    self._init_sampling_stats()
    # Initial per-env clip assignment. Gated on M > 1 so the single-clip path
    # draws no RNG here (motion_id is already all-zeros) and its sampling
    # stream does not depend on the clip library.
    if self.num_clips > 1:
        self._sample_motions(torch.ones(self.num_envs, dtype=torch.bool, device=self.device))
    self._update_robot_state_cache()

def post_physics_refresh(self) -> None:
    # The robot-state cache is refreshed at TWO distinct points per control step, by
    # design — they snapshot different states:
    #   1. here (post-physics, before reward) so reward/termination grade S_N, the
    #      pre-reset post-physics state;
    #   2. in compute() (which the command manager runs AFTER _reset_idx) so the
    #      cache then reflects the POST-reset state of just-reset envs, which the
    #      command and the end-of-step observation read.
    # Dropping either leaves one of those consumers a control step stale. See RLEnvBase.step.
    self._update_robot_state_cache()
    # Advance-then-grade: the clip clock was advanced (and wrapped) in
    # pre_physics_advance, so recompute the anchor-relative transforms against
    # the advanced reference and the just-refreshed post-physics robot cache.
    # This is what makes reward/termination grade the temporally-aligned frame.
    self._update_relative_transforms()

def clip_finished(self) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Per-env ``(N,)`` bool: has this env's clip reached its final frame?

    The command path's answer to "is the motion over", and the counterpart of
    :meth:`~eden.managers.motion_manager.MotionManager.get_motion_phase` ``>= 1`` on the
    manager path. It is only meaningful because :meth:`advance_reference` *holds* the clock
    at ``frame_total - 1`` instead of wrapping: in simulation
    :meth:`pre_physics_advance` resamples at the boundary, so the clock regresses and this
    goes ``False`` again, which is correct — a wrapped clip is not a finished one.

    ``DeploymentBase.motion_finished`` reduces this for the deploy loop's end-of-clip
    handover; nothing in the training loop reads it.
    """
    return self.time_steps >= self.frame_total - 1

def gather_motion_frames(self, field_name: str, frame_idx: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Gather motion field ``field_name`` at per-env frame indices.

    ``frame_idx`` is ``(N, K)`` long -> returns ``(N, K, ...)``. Each env
    indexes its own assigned clip (``motion_id``); with a single clip every
    env indexes the one shared clip's time axis.
    """
    field = getattr(self.motion, field_name)  # (M, T_max, ...)
    n, k = frame_idx.shape
    mid = self.motion_id[:, None].expand(n, k)
    return field[mid, frame_idx]  # (N, K, ...)

Advance the clip clock (+ wrap-teleport) BEFORE the physics sub-steps.

Advance-then-grade: the reference frame is advanced before physics so the post-physics robot (graded at reward/termination time) is compared against the temporally-aligned frame — matching :class:MotionManager, whose clock advances at the start of MimicRLEnvBase.step. Advancing in :meth:compute (after reward) would grade against a one-control-step-stale reference. def pre_physics_advance(self) -> None:
    """Advance the clip clock (+ wrap-teleport) BEFORE the physics sub-steps.

    Advance-then-grade: the reference frame is advanced before physics so the
    post-physics robot (graded at reward/termination time) is compared against
    the temporally-aligned frame — matching :class:`MotionManager`, whose clock
    advances at the start of ``MimicRLEnvBase.step``. Advancing in
    :meth:`compute` (after reward) would grade against a
    one-control-step-stale reference. Wrap-teleport runs here, before physics,
    so the teleported robot is forward-stepped and its forward kinematics stay
    fresh at reward time (no stale-FK spurious terminations).
    """
    self.time_steps += 1
    wrapped = self.time_steps >= self.frame_total  # per-env clip length
    # The bool mask `_resample_command` gets from `_resample` too, so the wrap costs no sync of
    # its own. The `.any()` gate is one: an all-False mask would write nothing, but the
    # full-batch reset draws, math and setter calls still cost ~1 ms at 4096 envs, far more
    # than the sync.
    if wrapped.any():
        self._resample_command(wrapped)

def rewind_reference(self) -> None:
    """Rewind the clip clock to frame 0 for every env — the deploy path's handover.

    Clock only: no :meth:`_resample_command`, so the robot is neither teleported nor
    pose-randomized and the clip assignment stands. That is the whole point on hardware,
    where the sim's reset-state initialization has nothing to act on, and it mirrors what
    ``MotionManager.rewind_to_start`` does for the manager path.
    """
    if self.time_steps is not None:
        self.time_steps.zero_()
        # Deployment restarts only on reset/START, not on the training timer.
        # Otherwise compute() can still resample and initialize the robot pose.
        self.time_left.fill_(float("inf"))

def resolve_body_cols(clip, links_idx, links_name) -> "torch.Tensor | list[int]":
    """Column indices into a clip's ``body_*_w`` arrays for the requested links.

    Resolution order:

    1. If the npz stores ``body_names``, resolve by name — independent of Genesis's internal link
       ordering (which changed breadth-first -> depth-first in genesis 1.2.0).
    2. Else, if the canonical G1 breadth-first link list (``G1_DOFS29_TRACKED_LINKS_NAME``) covers
       every requested link, resolve against that order. Every ``body_names``-less npz predates
       genesis 1.2.0 and was therefore written in the old breadth-first order, so this makes legacy
       G1 clips correct under a depth-first runtime instead of silently mis-sliced by ``idx_local``.
    3. Else (unrecognized body set, e.g. a non-G1 clip) fall back to the Genesis ``idx_local`` in
       ``links_idx`` — order-coupled, correct only when generated under the runtime's ordering.
    """
    if links_name is not None:
        if "body_names" in clip:
            return columns_by_name(clip["body_names"], links_name, what="motion npz 'body_names'")
        if all(n in G1_DOFS29_TRACKED_LINKS_NAME for n in links_name):
            en.logger.warning(_LEGACY_BFS_WARNING)
            return columns_by_name(G1_DOFS29_TRACKED_LINKS_NAME, links_name, what="G1_DOFS29_TRACKED_LINKS_NAME")
    en.logger.warning(_LEGACY_NPZ_WARNING)
    return links_idx

def motion_command_options(
    motion_file: str | list[str],
    *,
    anchor_link_name: str,
    links_name: list[str],
    entity_name: str = "robot",
    ghost_entity_name: str = "",
    debug_vis: bool = False,
    sampling_mode: str = "start",
    **overrides,
) -> dict[str, "CommandTermOptions"]:
    """Build the ``{"motion": <term>}`` command_options for a motion-tracking policy.

    Always builds a single :class:`MotionCommand`; a list of clip paths populates
    its ``motion_files`` (each env rolls its own assigned clip) and a single path
    populates ``motion_file`` (the M=1 case). The accessor interface is identical
    either way, so a policy reads motion source-agnostically — a new ONNX motion
    policy reuses this helper by passing only its body/anchor names. ``overrides``
    replace shared term fields.
    """
    shared = dict(
        resampling_time_range=(1.0e9, 1.0e9),
        debug_vis=debug_vis,
        entity_name=entity_name,
        ghost_entity_name=ghost_entity_name,
        anchor_link_name=anchor_link_name,
        links_name=links_name,
        pose_range={},
        velocity_range={},
        dofs_position_range=(0.0, 0.0),
        sampling_mode=sampling_mode,
    )
    shared.update(overrides)
    if isinstance(motion_file, (list, tuple)):
        return dict(motion=MotionCommand.configure(motion_files=list(motion_file), **shared))
    return dict(motion=MotionCommand.configure(motion_file=motion_file, **shared))

docs.title: AverageEpisodeLengthTracker
docs.text:
AverageEpisodeLengthTracker(env: RLEnvBase, options: CurriculumTermOptions)

Bases: CurriculumTerm

Track the running mean of episode length.

Maintains a single device-side scalar updated with an EMA whose effective time-constant is num_compute_average_epl episodes' worth of resets at the reference env count BASE_NUM_ENVS, scaled linearly with env.num_envs.

Other curriculum terms read the current estimate via env.curriculum_manager.get_state(<this term's name>). The state dict carries both average_episode_length and an is_primed flag — the latter is False until at least one reset() call has actually fed episode lengths into the EMA, so consumers can avoid acting on the initial-zero estimate before any episode has finished.

Declare this term before any consumer in curriculum_options so the consumer's compute() sees a fresh value on the same step. Declared after, get_state raises and names the ordering rather than reading as "no value yet".

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION num_compute_average_epl

Reference EMA window in number of resets, expressed at BASE_NUM_ENVS. The effective window scales as max(1, int(num_compute_average_epl * num_envs / BASE_NUM_ENVS)).

def __init__(self, env: RLEnvBase, options: CurriculumTermOptions):
    super().__init__(env=env, options=options)
    self._scaled_window = max(1, int(self.num_compute_average_epl * self._env.num_envs / BASE_NUM_ENVS))
    self.average_episode_length = torch.tensor(0.0, device=self.device, dtype=torch.float)
    self._is_primed = False

reset(envs_idx: Tensor | None = None) -> None
Source code in eden/managers/terms/curricula/locomotion.py 
def reset(self, envs_idx: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> None:
    # ``envs_idx is None`` is treated as "no episodes to record" rather than
    # "all envs". CurriculumManager always passes the indices of envs that
    # just terminated; a None here would mean a startup-style call where
    # ``episode_length_buf`` is all-zero (or mid-episode), and feeding that
    # into the EMA would corrupt the running mean. Same semantics as
    # PenaltyCurriculum.reset().
    if envs_idx is None:
        return
    ep_lens = self._env.episode_length_buf[envs_idx].float()
    n = ep_lens.numel()
    if n == 0:
        return
    weight = min(n / self._scaled_window, 1.0)
    current_average = ep_lens.mean()
    # Device-side EMA update. ``lerp_`` is in-place: it avoids per-reset
    # tensor allocation on the running estimate.
    self.average_episode_length.lerp_(current_average, weight)
    self._is_primed = True

def compute(self, *args, **kwargs) -> dict[str, float]:
    # NOTE: the stages are sorted in descending order, so we can break the loop
    for stage_step, stage_weight in self.weight_stages:
        if self._env.common_step_counter >= stage_step:
            self._reward_term.weight = stage_weight

    # first stage's step is reached, the applied stage after. Returning nothing would read back
    # through ``CurriculumManager.get_state`` as ``None`` (indistinguishable from "never computed")
    # and log no ``Curriculum/`` key at all.
    return {"weight": float(self._reward_term.weight)}

docs.text:
PenaltyCurriculum(env: RLEnvBase, options: CurriculumTermOptions)

Bases: CurriculumTerm

Curriculum that gradually scales reward weights for a set of reward terms.

Monitors average episode length and adjusts a scale factor applied to all targeted reward terms. When episodes are short (agent struggling), the scale decreases to ease penalties. When episodes are long (agent succeeding), the scale increases to enforce stricter behaviour.

The scale factor multiplies the configured weight of each term, so the effective weight is configured_weight * scale.

Targets can be specified by name OR by tag — exactly one entry path must be used per curriculum instance. Mixing the two would split intent across two fields and make refactors error-prone (e.g. renaming a term forgets the name-list, but the tag-list still matches). Prefer reward_term_tags when the same curriculum should apply to a group of penalties whose roster may grow (just tag new terms); use reward_term_names for explicit, audited targets.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION reward_term_names

Explicit names of reward terms to scale. Mutually exclusive with reward_term_tags.

reward_term_tags

Tags to match on RewardTermOptions.tags. A term is selected if any of its tags appears in this list. Mutually exclusive with reward_term_names.

initial_scale

Starting scale factor. Default 0.1 (10% of configured weight).

min_scale

Minimum allowed scale. Default 0.0.

max_scale

Maximum allowed scale. Default 1.0.

level_up_threshold

Average episode length (in steps) above which the scale increases.

level_down_threshold

Average episode length (in steps) below which the scale decreases.

degree

Amount to adjust the scale per curriculum compute call.

num_episode_average

Number of most recent episode lengths to average over. Ignored when tracker_name is set (the named tracker owns the EMA).

tracker_name

Optional name of an AverageEpisodeLengthTracker curriculum term whose average_episode_length should drive this curriculum instead of the per-instance buffer. The tracker must be declared before this PenaltyCurriculum in curriculum_options so the tracker's compute() runs first within a step. When None (default), a per-instance CPU buffer of the last num_episode_average lengths is used.

def __init__(self, env: RLEnvBase, options: CurriculumTermOptions):
    super().__init__(env=env, options=options)
    if not self.reward_term_names and not self.reward_term_tags:
        raise ValueError("PenaltyCurriculum requires either `reward_term_names` or `reward_term_tags` to be set.")
    if self.reward_term_names and self.reward_term_tags:
        raise ValueError(
            "PenaltyCurriculum: `reward_term_names` and `reward_term_tags` are mutually exclusive — "
            "set exactly one. Use names for explicit targets, tags for groups whose roster may grow."
        )
    self._scale = self.initial_scale
    self._targeted_terms: list = []
    self._base_weights: list[float] = []
    if self.tracker_name is None:
        # Rolling buffer for episode lengths. Kept on CPU on purpose: the running
        # mean is consumed by compute() every env step and used to branch on
        # ``level_up_threshold`` / ``level_down_threshold``. A device-side mean
        # would force a GPU→CPU sync per step, defeating async kernel launch.
        # Episode lengths are tiny ints; the CPU buffer is cheap.
        self._episode_lengths = torch.zeros(self.num_episode_average, device="cpu")
        self._ep_cursor = 0
        self._ep_count = 0

The reward manager is built before the curricula (EnvBase._manager_order), so an unknown reward_term_names entry raises at env construction rather than on the first reset. Installing the scale here — rather than on whichever of reset() / compute() runs first — is also what keeps the initial scale applied at eval: CurriculumManager freezes both of those there, so a term that only ever installed its starting level from one of them would grade an eval rollout at the unscaled configured weights.

def build(self) -> None:
    """Resolve the targeted reward terms and install ``initial_scale`` on them.

    The reward manager is built before the curricula (``EnvBase._manager_order``), so an
    unknown ``reward_term_names`` entry raises at env construction rather than on the first
    reset. Installing the scale here — rather than on whichever of ``reset()`` / ``compute()``
    runs first — is also what keeps the initial scale applied at eval:
    ``CurriculumManager`` freezes both of those there, so a term that only ever installed its
    starting level from one of them would grade an eval rollout at the *unscaled* configured
    weights.
    """
    reward_manager = self._env.reward_manager
    if self.reward_term_names:
        # Explicit names: error if any is missing.
        self._targeted_terms = [reward_manager.get_term(name) for name in self.reward_term_names]
    else:
        # Tag match: scan all terms and keep those carrying any listed tag.
        tag_set = set(self.reward_term_tags)
        self._targeted_terms = [
            term
            for _, term in reward_manager.iter_terms()
            if tag_set.intersection(getattr(term, "tags", None) or [])
        ]
    self._base_weights = [term.weight for term in self._targeted_terms]
    # Empty resolution is allowed (e.g. tag-based curriculum on a task that doesn't
    # use that tag yet) but warn loudly so it isn't a silent no-op.
    if not self._targeted_terms:
        en.logger.warning(
            "PenaltyCurriculum resolved zero target reward terms "
            f"(reward_term_names={self.reward_term_names!r}, reward_term_tags={self.reward_term_tags!r}). "
            "The curriculum will be a no-op — check that names exist and that target terms carry the listed tags."
        )
    self._apply_scale()

def reset(self, envs_idx: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> None:
    if self.tracker_name is not None:
        # The named tracker owns the EMA; nothing to update here.
        return
    if envs_idx is None:
        return
    # Pull episode lengths to CPU once per reset and update the running mean
    # incrementally (avoids per-step ``.mean().item()`` syncs in compute()).
    ep_lens = self._env.episode_length_buf[envs_idx].float().cpu()
    n = ep_lens.shape[0]
    if n == 0:
        return
    buf_size = self.num_episode_average
    indices = (torch.arange(n, device=self._episode_lengths.device) + self._ep_cursor) % buf_size
    self._episode_lengths[indices] = ep_lens
    self._ep_cursor = (self._ep_cursor + n) % buf_size
    self._ep_count = min(self._ep_count + n, buf_size)
    # Refresh cached running mean as a Python float — no per-step sync below.
    self._avg_ep_len = float(self._episode_lengths[: self._ep_count].mean())

def compute(self, *args, **kwargs) -> dict[str, float]:
    if self.tracker_name is not None:
        # A tracker that is registered but hasn't computed yet raises inside get_state: it must
        # be declared *before* this term in curriculum_options, and the manager says so.
        avg_ep_len, is_primed = self._read_tracker_state()
        # Same gate as the buffer path's ``_ep_count > 0``: only move the scale once
        # the tracker has actually consumed at least one reset. Otherwise the
        # initial-zero estimate would push ``_scale`` toward ``min_scale`` on
        # every pre-first-reset step.
        if is_primed:
            if avg_ep_len > self.level_up_threshold:
                self._scale = min(self._scale + self.degree, self.max_scale)
            elif avg_ep_len < self.level_down_threshold:
                self._scale = max(self._scale - self.degree, self.min_scale)
            self._apply_scale()
        return {"scale": self._scale, "avg_episode_length": avg_ep_len}

    avg_ep_len = getattr(self, "_avg_ep_len", 0.0)

    # Only update the scale once we have at least one recorded episode length.
    # Otherwise compute() runs every env.step() from start of training and the
    # default avg_ep_len=0.0 would push _scale toward min_scale before any
    # real episode data exists.
    if self._ep_count > 0:
        if avg_ep_len > self.level_up_threshold:
            self._scale = min(self._scale + self.degree, self.max_scale)
        elif avg_ep_len < self.level_down_threshold:
            self._scale = max(self._scale - self.degree, self.min_scale)
        self._apply_scale()
    return {"scale": self._scale, "avg_episode_length": avg_ep_len}
