docs.title: MotionBasePoseThresholdCurriculum
docs.text:
MotionBasePoseThresholdCurriculum(env: EnvBase, options: _TermOptionsT)

Bases: CurriculumTerm

Tighten a :class:MotionBasePoseTrackingBreak gate as success rises.

ConTrack's "threshold curriculum": an EMA of the per-episode success rate linearly interpolates the paired termination term's pos_threshold / rot_threshold from their *_max (lenient) values to their *_min (tight) ones as the EMA moves across [success_rate_low, success_rate_high]. An episode counts as a success when it ends with the motion clip exhausted (validity[:, 0] false at reset time) rather than via the pose gate.

This lives in a curriculum term rather than inside the termination term so it gets the three things curriculum state needs and a termination term cannot provide: CurriculumManager logs :meth:compute's return under Curriculum/<name>/*, it freezes curricula at eval (eval_mode=True) so an eval rollout is graded at a fixed tolerance, and the state has one obvious home if/when term checkpointing lands (nothing calls state_dict() on manager terms today, so a resumed run still restarts the EMA at 0 — i.e. at the lenient thresholds).

Declaration order matters only against other curriculum terms; the thresholds this writes are consumed by the next step's termination_manager.compute().

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION termination_term_name

Name of the MotionBasePoseTrackingBreak term to drive, as declared in termination_options.

entity_name

Entity whose motion-reference validity defines episode success. Must match the termination term's own entity_name.

pos_threshold_max

Position tolerance (m) at success_rate_low / success_rate_high.

rot_threshold_max

Orientation tolerance (rad) at success_rate_low / success_rate_high.

success_ema_alpha

Per-episode EMA rate. The update is applied once per reset batch with an effective rate of 1 - (1 - alpha) ** n for a batch of n episodes, which is exactly n successive per-episode updates. Without that correction the EMA's time constant would scale with num_envs (at 4096 envs some env resets almost every step, so a per-batch alpha converges within a fraction of one episode).

success_rate_low

EMA values at which the thresholds sit at *_max and *_min respectively.

def build(self) -> None:
    # Fail fast on the degenerate spans: `high == low` would make the interpolation
    # weight 0/0 -> nan, which propagates through clamp into both thresholds and turns
    # `err > threshold` permanently False — the gate would silently never fire.
    if not self.success_rate_high > self.success_rate_low:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)} requires success_rate_high > success_rate_low; got "
            f"success_rate_low={self.success_rate_low}, success_rate_high={self.success_rate_high}."
        )
    if not 0.0 < self.success_ema_alpha <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)} requires 0 < success_ema_alpha <= 1; got {self.success_ema_alpha}.")
    for name in ("pos", "rot"):
        lo, hi = getattr(self, f"{name}_threshold_min"), getattr(self, f"{name}_threshold_max")
        if lo > hi:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{term_subject(self)}: {name}_threshold_min ({lo}) must not exceed "
                f"{name}_threshold_max ({hi}) — the curriculum tightens from max to min."
            )
    # The reset grades the episode that ended, whose window is refilled before the manager resets
    # run; a wrong entity_name raises here, not on the first reset.
    self._env.motion_manager.record_ended_episode_validity(self.entity_name)
    self._success_ema = torch.zeros((), device=self.device)
    # The termination manager is built before the curricula (``EnvBase._manager_order``), so
    # the term this curriculum drives resolves here — a wrong name or a mismatched entity
    # raises at env construction rather than on the first compute().
    self._term = self._env.termination_manager.get_term(self.termination_term_name)
    if not isinstance(self._term, MotionBasePoseTrackingBreak):
        raise TypeError(
            f"{term_subject(self)} drives termination term '{self.termination_term_name}', a "
            f"{type(self._term).__name__}, but it can only move a MotionBasePoseTrackingBreak gate (through its "
            "set_thresholds). Point termination_term_name at one."
        )
    if self._term.entity_name != self.entity_name:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)} drives termination term '{self.termination_term_name}' on entity "
            f"'{self._term.entity_name}' but grades success on '{self.entity_name}'. Point both at "
            f"the same entity, or the tolerance would track a different clip's progress."
        )

Source code in eden/managers/terms/curricula/motion.py 
def reset(self, envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None = None) -> None:
    env: MimicRLEnvBase = self._env
    # Both reads below describe the episode that just ended: the validity the motion manager took
    # as it ended (the window itself already holds the new episode's), and `episode_length_buf`,
    # which `_reset_idx` zeroes after the manager resets. An exhausted clip (the episode ran to
    # the end instead of breaking) reads as validity False.
    success = (~env.motion_manager.ended_episode_validity(self.entity_name)).to(torch.float32)
    # Never-stepped envs (the build-time bootstrap reset) still hold the all-invalid
    # make_empty default, which would read as instant success and bias the EMA.
    stepped = (env.episode_length_buf > 0).to(torch.float32)
    # Kept entirely device-side: no `.item()`/`bool()`/mask-index — the auto-reset hands a bool
    # mask, which as an index is a sync per gather, so the sums reduce through it instead (they
    # count whole numbers, so they match the gathered ones exactly). n == 0 makes `weight` 0,
    # i.e. a no-op update.
    envs_idx = slice(None) if envs_idx is None else envs_idx
    n = sum_over_envs(stepped, envs_idx)
    mean_success = sum_over_envs(success * stepped, envs_idx) / n.clamp(min=1.0)
    weight = 1.0 - (1.0 - self.success_ema_alpha) ** n
    self._success_ema += weight * (mean_success - self._success_ema)

def compute(self, *args, **kwargs) -> dict[str, float]:
    w = torch.clamp(
        (self._success_ema - self.success_rate_low) / (self.success_rate_high - self.success_rate_low),
        0.0,
        1.0,
    )
    pos_threshold = self.pos_threshold_max * (1.0 - w) + self.pos_threshold_min * w
    rot_threshold = self.rot_threshold_max * (1.0 - w) + self.rot_threshold_min * w
    self._term.set_thresholds(pos_threshold, rot_threshold)
    return {
        "success_ema": self._success_ema,
        "pos_threshold": pos_threshold,
        "rot_threshold": rot_threshold,
    }

docs.title: Success Guided Sampling
docs.text:
Success Guided Sampling (SGS): choose each episode's reset configuration from its recent success rate.

Zhang et al., "A Balanced Data Diet: Addressing the Exploration Bottleneck in Mega-Scale RL for Robot Control" (CoRL 2026, arXiv:2610.12465), Sec. 3.2 and Appendix B.2. A task owns a fixed set of N reset configurations. SGS keeps the last history success/failure outcomes of every configuration, scores each configuration's success rate p with a Beta-shaped kernel peaked at target, and draws the next configuration of every resetting env from a softmax over those scores. Most episodes go to configurations the policy solves sometimes; every configuration keeps a non-zero probability, so the estimates of the ones it cannot solve yet (or has mastered) keep being refreshed.

The term is a :class:~eden.managers.resets.sampling.ResetConfigSampler: the RESET event that owns the configuration set binds it and calls :meth:SuccessGuidedSampling.sample, because the RESET events run before any manager's reset() (see :mod:eden.managers.resets.sampling). sample grades the episode that just ended before it draws the next one -- the termination manager still holds the finished step's verdicts then, since its own reset() comes later in the same walk.

docs.title: SuccessGuidedSampling
docs.text:
SuccessGuidedSampling(env: EnvBase, options: _TermOptionsT)

Bases: CurriculumTerm, ResetConfigSampler

Draw each resetting env's reset configuration with probability peaked at a target success rate.

A reset event that owns a configuration set names this term (its sampler parameter), binds it to the set size in its build() and calls :meth:sample from every reset. A term no reset event binds fails env construction. A configuration never graded reads p = 0, so before any outcome is in, sampling is uniform.

An outcome is recorded for an env when its episode ended: it is in the reset selection, the termination manager has it done, and it ran at least one step. A success is the success_term termination having fired on that last step. Not graded: an env's first spawn, an env.reset() that cut an episode short, and an episode the simulator flagged as corrupt (termination_manager.solver_errors) -- that one ended on the solver, not on the task. When more than history envs finish one configuration in the same reset, a uniformly random history of them are recorded.

At eval (env.training False) configurations are drawn uniformly and nothing is recorded: evaluation grades the policy on the task distribution, not on the sampler's current emphasis.

The defaults are the paper's locomotion settings; it uses target=0.5, concentration=1.0, floor=1e-4 for manipulation.

ATTRIBUTE DESCRIPTION success_term

Termination term whose firing marks an episode a success (e.g. all_goals_reached).

TYPE: str | None

history

Outcomes kept per configuration (a ring buffer); p is their mean.

TYPE: int

target

Success rate the kernel peaks at, in [0, 1].

TYPE: float

concentration

Kernel sharpness k >= 0; 0 samples uniformly.

TYPE: float

temperature

Softmax temperature, effective value max(temperature, 1).

TYPE: float

floor

eps > 0: keeps the kernel finite at p in {0, 1} and every probability non-zero.

def compute(self) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    """Publish the sampler's state; device tensors, so logging it costs no sync.

    ``mean_success`` averages ``p`` over the configurations graded at least once;
    ``frontier_frac`` is the share of the whole set with ``0 < p < 1`` -- solved sometimes, the
    configurations SGS exists to find; ``sampling_ess_frac`` is the effective sample size of the
    sampling distribution as a fraction of the set (1 = uniform).
    """
    self._require_bound("compute()")
    visited = self.num_outcomes > 0
    num_visited = visited.sum()
    p = self._success_rate
    return {
        "mean_success": (p * visited).sum() / num_visited.clamp(min=1),
        "visited_frac": num_visited / self._num_configs,
        "frontier_frac": ((p > 0.0) & (p < 1.0)).float().mean(),
        "sampling_ess_frac": 1.0 / (self._probs.square().sum() * self._num_configs),
    }

success_guided_probabilities(success_rate: Tensor, *, target: float, concentration: float, temperature: float, floor: float) -> Tensor

Sampling probability of each configuration given its success rate (paper Eq. 1-2, Appendix B.2).

w = (p + eps)^(k t) * (1 - p + eps)^(k (1 - t)) -- the Beta(1 + k t, 1 + k (1 - t)) density in mode-concentration form, up to a constant -- floored at eps; the logit is log(w + eps) and the probabilities a softmax over the logits at temperature max(temperature, 1).

Source code in eden/managers/terms/curricula/success_guided.py 
def success_guided_probabilities(
    success_rate: torch.Tensor, *, target: float, concentration: float, temperature: float, floor: float
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Sampling probability of each configuration given its success rate (paper Eq. 1-2, Appendix B.2).

    ``w = (p + eps)^(k t) * (1 - p + eps)^(k (1 - t))`` -- the Beta(1 + k t, 1 + k (1 - t)) density in
    mode-concentration form, up to a constant -- floored at ``eps``; the logit is ``log(w + eps)`` and the
    probabilities a softmax over the logits at temperature ``max(temperature, 1)``.
    """
    p = success_rate.float()
    weight = (p + floor).pow(concentration * target) * (1.0 - p + floor).pow(concentration * (1.0 - target))
    logits = torch.log(weight.clamp(min=floor) + floor)
    return torch.softmax(logits / max(temperature, 1.0), dim=-1)

Reset the base to its default pose, offset and rotated at random.

The offsets are added to the entity's default root position, and the sampled roll / pitch / yaw (world x-y-z, R_rpy = Rz @ Ry @ Rx) rotate the default orientation — R_rpy @ R_default — so an object authored lying on its side stays on its side. Both writes use the authored frame (relative=True), the frame default_root_pos is specified in: the asset's declared root origin lands on the target, not the centre of mass Genesis re-origins a free body onto. A heterogeneous entity's per-variant default poses are honored (Entity.get_default_root_pose). Similar to mjlab's reset_root_state_uniform, which composes its rotation in the body frame instead (R_default @ R_rpy); the two agree for an identity default orientation or a pure yaw about an upright default.

Rigid-only: relies on set_pos/set_quat, which raise on :class:ParticleEntity (MPM/SPH). For deformable entities, bake pose into the morph at creation time.

@EVENT_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def reset_base_state_uniform(
    env: EnvBase,
    envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None,
    *,
    entity_name: str,
    pos_x_range: Vec2FType = (-0.5, 0.5),
    pos_y_range: Vec2FType = (-0.5, 0.5),
    pos_z_range: Vec2FType = (0.0, 0.0),
    roll_range: Vec2FType = (0.0, 0.0),
    pitch_range: Vec2FType = (0.0, 0.0),
    yaw_range: Vec2FType = (-3.14, 3.14),
):
    """Reset the base to its default pose, offset and rotated at random.

    The offsets are added to the entity's default root position, and the sampled roll / pitch / yaw (world
    x-y-z, ``R_rpy = Rz @ Ry @ Rx``) rotate the default orientation — ``R_rpy @ R_default`` — so an object
    authored lying on its side stays on its side. Both writes use the authored frame (``relative=True``),
    the frame ``default_root_pos`` is specified in: the asset's declared root origin lands on the target,
    not the centre of mass Genesis re-origins a free body onto. A heterogeneous entity's per-variant default
    poses are honored (``Entity.get_default_root_pose``). Similar to mjlab's ``reset_root_state_uniform``,
    which composes its rotation in the body frame instead (``R_default @ R_rpy``); the two agree for an
    identity default orientation or a pure yaw about an upright default.

    Rigid-only: relies on ``set_pos``/``set_quat``, which raise on
    :class:`ParticleEntity` (MPM/SPH). For deformable entities, bake pose into
    the morph at creation time.
    """
    from eden.entities.rigid import RigidEntity

    envs_idx = sanitize_envs_idx(envs_idx, env.num_envs)

    entity = env.get_entity(entity_name)
    if not isinstance(entity, RigidEntity):
        raise TypeError(
            f"reset_base_state_uniform requires a RigidEntity for '{entity_name}', got {type(entity).__name__}."
        )

    default_pos, default_quat = entity.get_default_root_pose()  # fresh (num_envs, 3) / (num_envs, 4)

    ranges = (pos_x_range, pos_y_range, pos_z_range, roll_range, pitch_range, yaw_range)
    sampled = sample_uniform_ranges(ranges, env.num_envs, env.device)
    new_pos = default_pos + sampled[:, :3]
    new_quat = transform_quat_by_quat(default_quat, xyz_to_quat(sampled[:, 3:], rpy=True))

    if entity.root_qpos_is_authored_pose:
        # One write of the 7 root coordinates, which are the authored pose here. Velocities are zeroed as
        # Genesis' `set_pos` / `set_quat` zero them: a simulated entity's, not a kinematic one's.
        root_qpos = _rows_to_write(torch.cat([new_pos, new_quat], dim=-1), envs_idx)
        entity.set_qpos(root_qpos, qs_idx_local=_ROOT_QS, envs_idx=envs_idx, zero_velocity=not entity.is_kinematic)
        return

    # ``relative=True`` takes Genesis' general path, which wants the selected rows under every
    # ``envs_idx`` form (slice, index tensor or bool mask). Orientation first, as the build write does:
    # the solver position of a re-origined body depends on its orientation. One `nonzero()` for the
    # auto-reset's mask covers both gathers and both setters (`env_indices`).
    envs_idx = env_indices(envs_idx)
    entity.set_quat(new_quat[envs_idx], envs_idx=envs_idx, relative=True)
    entity.set_pos(new_pos[envs_idx], envs_idx=envs_idx, relative=True)

Reset DOFs to default + U(offset), clamped to soft limits.

The offset is drawn per env and DOF. Velocities are zeroed (the base's too), then set to U(dofs_vel_range) when that is given. Rigid-only: requires a :class:RigidEntity (DOFs are not defined on :class:ParticleEntity).

@EVENT_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def reset_dofs_by_offset(
    env: EnvBase,
    envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None,
    *,
    entity_name: str,
    dofs_pos_range: Vec2FType = (-0.1, 0.1),
    dofs_vel_range: Vec2FType | None = None,
):
    """Reset DOFs to ``default + U(offset)``, clamped to soft limits.

    The offset is drawn per env and DOF. Velocities are zeroed (the base's too), then set to
    ``U(dofs_vel_range)`` when that is given.
    Rigid-only: requires a :class:`RigidEntity` (DOFs are not defined on
    :class:`ParticleEntity`).
    """
    from eden.entities.rigid import RigidEntity

    envs_idx = sanitize_envs_idx(envs_idx, env.num_envs)

    entity = env.get_entity(entity_name)
    if not isinstance(entity, RigidEntity):
        raise TypeError(
            f"reset_dofs_by_offset requires a RigidEntity for '{entity_name}', got {type(entity).__name__}."
        )
    dofs_pos = entity.default_dofs_pos.clone() + sample_uniform(
        dofs_pos_range[0],
        dofs_pos_range[1],
        (env.num_envs, entity.num_dofs),
        device=env.device,
    )
    dofs_pos = dofs_pos.clamp(entity.soft_dofs_pos_limits[:, :, 0], entity.soft_dofs_pos_limits[:, :, 1])
    dofs_pos = _rows_to_write(dofs_pos, envs_idx)
    if dofs_vel_range is None:
        # `set_dofs_pos` zeroes every dof's velocity (the base's too) and runs forward kinematics once.
        entity.set_dofs_pos(dofs_pos, envs_idx=envs_idx)
        return

    # Velocities first, without forward kinematics: the position write below runs the one pass over these envs,
    # and that pass refreshes link velocities from the dof velocities written here; writing velocities after
    # the positions would run a second pass. Final state: every dof's velocity zero (the base's too, as
    # `set_dofs_pos`' default zeroing would leave it), then the sampled joint velocities.
    dofs_vel = _rows_to_write(
        sample_uniform(dofs_vel_range[0], dofs_vel_range[1], (env.num_envs, entity.num_dofs), device=env.device),
        envs_idx,
    )
    entity.zero_all_dofs_velocity(envs_idx=envs_idx, skip_forward=True)
    entity.set_dofs_vel(dofs_vel, envs_idx=envs_idx, skip_forward=True)
    entity.set_dofs_pos(dofs_pos, envs_idx=envs_idx, zero_velocity=False)

@EVENT_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def reset_dofs_by_scale_and_offset(
    env: EnvBase,
    envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None,
    *,
    entity_name: str,
    dofs_scale_range: Vec2FType = (0.8, 1.2),
    dofs_offset_range: Vec2FType = (-0.1, 0.1),
):
    """Reset DOFs to ``default * U(scale) + U(offset)``; velocities to 0.

    Sampled per env and DOF, then clamped to the soft limits. OpenHomie's ``_reset_dofs``:
    :func:`reset_dofs_by_scale` and :func:`reset_dofs_by_offset` composed.
    Rigid-only: requires a :class:`RigidEntity`.
    """
    from eden.entities.rigid import RigidEntity

    envs_idx = sanitize_envs_idx(envs_idx, env.num_envs)

    entity = env.get_entity(entity_name)
    if not isinstance(entity, RigidEntity):
        raise TypeError(
            f"reset_dofs_by_scale_and_offset requires a RigidEntity for '{entity_name}', got {type(entity).__name__}."
        )
    shape = (env.num_envs, entity.num_dofs)
    scale = sample_uniform(dofs_scale_range[0], dofs_scale_range[1], shape, device=env.device)
    offset = sample_uniform(dofs_offset_range[0], dofs_offset_range[1], shape, device=env.device)
    limits = entity.soft_dofs_pos_limits
    dofs_pos = (entity.default_dofs_pos * scale + offset).clamp(limits[..., 0], limits[..., 1])
    # `set_dofs_pos` zeroes every dof's velocity, the base's too.
    entity.set_dofs_pos(_rows_to_write(dofs_pos, envs_idx), envs_idx=envs_idx)

def compute(self, envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None = None) -> None:
    if envs_idx is None:
        envs_idx = slice(None)
    rows = _push_rows(envs_idx, self._write_every_row)
    lin_vel_w = self.entity.get_vel(envs_idx=rows)
    ang_vel_w = self.entity.get_ang(envs_idx=rows)
    quat_w = self.entity.get_quat(envs_idx=rows)

    rand_vel = sample_uniform(
        self.ranges[:, 0],
        self.ranges[:, 1],
        (self._env.num_envs, 6),
        device=self._env.device,
    )[rows]
    lin_vel_w += rand_vel[:, :3]
    # Genesis stores a free joint's rotational DOF velocity in the base BODY frame (MuJoCo
    # qvel convention). Convert the current world ang-vel to body, add the (body-frame)
    # perturbation, and write the BODY-frame result straight into DOFs 3-5 — do NOT rotate
    # back to world first. Linear DOFs are world-frame and left as-is.
    ang_vel_b = inv_transform_by_quat(ang_vel_w, quat_w)
    ang_vel_b += rand_vel[:, 3:]
    self.entity.set_dofs_vel(
        torch.cat([lin_vel_w, ang_vel_b], dim=1),
        dofs_idx_local=self._genesis_base_dofs_idx,
        envs_idx=envs_idx,
    )

RandomizeDofsPosOffset(env: EnvBase, options: _TermOptionsT)

Bases: EventTerm

Per-env joint-position offset on joint position controllers (encoder bias).

Each selected controller draws its own offsets, one per env and controlled DOF, and takes them through :meth:~eden.managers.terms.actions.joint_actions._JointPDControllerBase.set_dofs_pos_offset. The draw adds to the controller's position target on top of its configured offset and its reference_source reference, and replaces neither, so it composes with a static offset and, in either order, with :class:RandomizeStartupDofsPosBias.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION entity_name

The name of the entity to control.

action_term_name

The joint position controller(s) to randomize: one term name, a list of them, or None (the default) for every joint position controller on entity_name — see :func:~eden.managers.terms.actions.joint_actions.is_joint_position_controller. None keeps a config that splits the entity's joints across several controllers (a per-limb scale or delay) from having to list, and so depend on, each term's name. A named term must be a joint position controller on entity_name, and None raises if the entity has none.

docs.title: RandomizeStartupDofsPosBias
docs.text:
RandomizeStartupDofsPosBias(env: EnvBase, options: _TermOptionsT)

Bases: EventTerm

Bake a per-env joint-zero bias into entity.default_dofs_pos at startup.

Simulates motor calibration drift: each env gets a small fixed offset on every DOF of the entity, sampled once at startup and held constant for the lifetime of the env. The bias persists across resets, unlike the per-reset jitter from :class:RandomizeDofsPosOffset. The two compose: a calibration drift baked in at startup + small per-episode jitter on top.

When action_terms_name lists one or more PD controllers, each controller's _offset cache (folded once at build time as default_offset + configured_offset, see _JointPDControllerBase._build_scale_and_offset) is updated in lockstep by adding the same per-env bias delta on the DOFs that controller owns. This avoids the "stale cache" trap where mutating entity.default_dofs_pos would diverge from a controller's pre-folded static offset.

Build-time contract. build() performs strict validation so that any stale-cache footgun surfaces loudly at startup rather than as silent drift at runtime:

  1. action_terms_name must contain no duplicates.
  2. Each listed term must be a :class:_JointPDControllerBase instance, target the same entity, and have reference_source == ReferenceSource.DEFAULT.

  3. Every same-entity action term that caches default_dofs_pos at build must be either listed (and updated in lockstep) or rejected with a clear error. Specifically:

  4. _JointPDControllerBase with reference_source=DEFAULT not in the listed set: error (its _offset would silently go stale).

  5. :class:NullJointAction caches a copy of default_dofs_pos at build with no refresh path; if it is present on the same entity, build() errors out. OperationalSpaceController refreshes its declared nullspace reference at reset and therefore does not need this rejection.
PARAMETER DESCRIPTION entity_name

The entity to bias.

action_terms_name

Names of PD controller action terms whose _offset caches should be kept in sync with the bias. Each must be a :class:_JointPDControllerBase on entity_name with reference_source=DEFAULT. Must list every such controller on the entity — see the build-time contract above. Empty list is fine if and only if no DEFAULT-source PD controllers exist on this entity.

dofs_pos_range

Per-DOF bias range, sampled uniformly. Default ±1 degree.

def compute(self, envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None = None) -> None:
    # Idempotence: startup terms are invoked once today, but make the contract explicit.
    if self._applied:
        return
    self._applied = True

    if envs_idx is None:
        envs_idx = slice(None)

    if self.entity.default_dofs_pos.shape[0] == 1 and self._env.num_envs != 1:
        self.entity.default_dofs_pos = self.entity.default_dofs_pos.repeat(self._env.num_envs, 1)
    elif self.entity.default_dofs_pos.shape[0] != self._env.num_envs:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)} expected default_dofs_pos batch size 1 or {self._env.num_envs}, "
            f"got {self.entity.default_dofs_pos.shape[0]}"
        )

    bias_full = sample_uniform(
        self.dofs_pos_range[0],
        self.dofs_pos_range[1],
        (self._env.num_envs, self.entity.default_dofs_pos.shape[1]),
        device=self._env.device,
    )[envs_idx]

    # 1. Bake the bias into the entity's default DOF positions (additive).
    self.entity.default_dofs_pos[envs_idx] = self.entity.default_dofs_pos[envs_idx] + bias_full

    # 2. Keep each listed PD controller's pre-folded `_offset` cache in lockstep,
    #    on the subset of DOFs that controller owns.
    for term, columns in self._targets:
        term._offset[envs_idx] = term._offset[envs_idx] + bias_full[:, columns]

docs.title: RandomizeKpKdGains
docs.text:
RandomizeKpKdGains(env: EnvBase, options: _TermOptionsT)

Bases: EventTerm

Scale an entity's joint PD gains by a random factor.

With action_term_name set, the draw goes into that controller's own gain caches, over the controller's DOFs in its dofs_name order: each cache becomes the entity's current gains times the drawn factor. Writing them only in :meth:compute is not enough: the controller's reset() re-reads its caches from the entity, and in both reset and startup mode that re-read lands after the draw (the ordering :class:_ResetModeActuatorDR describes), leaving the randomization silently inert. So the term keeps each env's factors and applies them again in :meth:reset, which runs after action_manager.reset(); a draw in any mode then holds until that env's next draw. Keeping factors rather than gains is what lets it compose with anything else that changes the entity's gains (an entity-path RandomizeKpKdGains, a gain curriculum): each reset scales whatever the entity holds then, and an env not yet drawn keeps the entity's gains unchanged (factor 1).

Requires

env_options.batch_dofs_info=True to support per-env PD gain randomization.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION entity_name

The name of the entity to control.

action_term_name

If set, the name of an ExplicitPDController or VelocityFeedforwardPDController on entity_name, whose _kp / _kd caches receive the gains; the entity is left untouched. If None, the gains are written directly to the entity via set_dofs_kp / set_dofs_kd (the path Genesis' built-in PD, ImplicitPDController, reads).

kp_range

Multiplicative range, sampled uniformly per env and DOF. On the entity path it multiplies entity.default_dofs_kp; on the controller path (action_term_name set) it multiplies the entity's current kp, which is default_dofs_kp unless something else changed it.

kd_range

As kp_range, for kd (entity.default_dofs_kd on the entity path).

def build(self) -> None:
    self.entity = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)
    self.term = None
    if self.action_term_name is None:
        return

    from eden.managers.terms.actions.joint_actions import ExplicitPDController, VelocityFeedforwardPDController

    term = self._env.action_manager.get_term(self.action_term_name)
    if not isinstance(term, (ExplicitPDController, VelocityFeedforwardPDController)):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)} (action_term_name={self.action_term_name!r}) writes the joint gain caches of an "
            f"ExplicitPDController or VelocityFeedforwardPDController, but action term "
            f"{self.action_term_name!r} is of type {type(term).__name__}, which has none. For Genesis' built-in PD "
            "(ImplicitPDController) set action_term_name=None: the gains then go to the entity "
            "(set_dofs_kp / set_dofs_kd), which is what that controller reads."
        )
    if term.entity_name != self.entity_name:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)} (action_term_name={self.action_term_name!r}): "
            f"action term {self.action_term_name!r} controls entity {term.entity_name!r}, so its gains would be "
            f"scaled from the wrong entity's default_dofs_kp / default_dofs_kd. Set "
            f"entity_name={term.entity_name!r}."
        )
    self.term = term
    # Each env's factors in the controller's layout, re-applied to the entity's gains by `reset()`.
    # Identity until the first draw.
    self._kp_factor = torch.ones_like(term._kp)
    self._kd_factor = torch.ones_like(term._kd)

def compute(self, envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None = None) -> None:
    if envs_idx is None:
        envs_idx = slice(None)
    if self.term is not None:
        self._draw_into_term(envs_idx)
        return
    n_dofs = len(self.entity.dofs_name)

    kp_factor = sample_uniform(
        self.kp_range[0],
        self.kp_range[1],
        (self._env.num_envs, n_dofs),
        device=self._env.device,
    )[envs_idx]
    kd_factor = sample_uniform(
        self.kd_range[0],
        self.kd_range[1],
        (self._env.num_envs, n_dofs),
        device=self._env.device,
    )[envs_idx]

    # NOTE: default_dofs_kp/kd may be (1, n_dofs) even with batch_dofs_info=True
    base_kp = self.entity.default_dofs_kp.expand(self._env.num_envs, -1)[envs_idx]
    base_kd = self.entity.default_dofs_kd.expand(self._env.num_envs, -1)[envs_idx]

    self.entity.set_dofs_kp(
        base_kp * kp_factor,
        dofs_idx_local=self.entity.dofs_idx_local,
        envs_idx=envs_idx,
    )
    self.entity.set_dofs_kd(
        base_kd * kd_factor,
        dofs_idx_local=self.entity.dofs_idx_local,
        envs_idx=envs_idx,
    )

docs.title: RandomizeFrictionRatio
docs.text:
RandomizeFrictionRatio(env: EnvBase, options: EventTermOptions)

Bases: EventTerm

Randomize sliding friction on links_name to absolute values, not a scale.

Every compute() first pins the whole entity's base friction to 1.0 (set_friction(1.0), entity-wide — this discards any authored default_geoms_friction, including on links outside links_name, which are left at a flat 1.0) and then writes per-link ratios on links_name. friction_range is therefore an absolute coefficient range, regardless of what the asset authored; a source config expressed as "scale x authored value" must be converted to the resulting absolute range. Genesis multiplies the same ratio into the torsional and rolling coefficients where those axes are enabled, so this term randomizes spin resistance too.

Genesis resolves a contact pair's friction as max(a, b), so the randomized coefficient only takes effect against surfaces whose friction is below the sampled value — author the ground plane low (e.g. PlaneOptions(default_geoms_friction={"*": 0.01})) so the robot side always wins. Overlapping link sets (a whole-robot pass plus a tighter feet range) are ordered by the events' priority field (ascending). mode defaults to reset, but friction DR is usually a per-env-lifetime property — every in-tree task uses mode="startup". The full porting recipe lives in docs/guides/entities.md ("Porting a friction-randomization setup").

def compute(self, envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None = None) -> None:
    if envs_idx is None:
        envs_idx = slice(None)
    # NOTE: set the friction of the terrain and objects small so that the robot geometry can decide the friction
    # NOTE: the friction between the object A and B is defined by the maximum friction of the two objects
    # NOTE: friction_a = geoms_info.friction[i_ga] * geoms_state.friction_ratio[i_ga, i_b]
    # NOTE: friction_b = geoms_info.friction[i_gb] * geoms_state.friction_ratio[i_gb, i_a]
    # NOTE: contact_data.friction[i_c, i_b] = ti.max(ti.max(friction_a, friction_b), 1e-2)
    # NOTE: geoms_info.friction defaults to 1.0 and has to be in range [1e-2, 5.0] for simulation stability.

    friction_ratio = sample_uniform(
        self.friction_range[0],
        self.friction_range[1],
        (
            self._env.num_envs,
            len(self.links_name),
        ),
        device=self._env.device,
    )[envs_idx]

    self.entity.set_friction(1.0)
    self.entity.set_friction_ratio(
        friction_ratio,
        ls_idx_local=self.ls_idx_local,
        envs_idx=envs_idx,
    )

Requires EnvOptions(batch_links_info=True), and rejects a range whose lower bound could drive a selected link's mass non-positive — the write itself is unchecked (Genesis skips the device-side check for speed), so it would otherwise silently produce unphysical dynamics. It also rejects a link fixed to the world, whose mass the solver never reads.

def build(self) -> None:
    resolved_names, ls_idx_local = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name).find_named_links_idx_local(self.links_name)
    assert len(ls_idx_local) > 0, f"No links found for {self.links_name} in {self.__class__.__name__}"
    self.ls_idx_local = torch.as_tensor(ls_idx_local, dtype=gs.tc_int, device=self.device).contiguous()
    self.entity = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)
    _reject_world_fixed_links(self, self.entity, self.links_name, resolved_names, ls_idx_local, "mass")
    _refuse_anchored_inertials(self, "mass")
    # The worst-case sampled mass is nominal + range lower bound. A one-time device sync
    # at build is the earliest well-defined point to reject a range that could go
    # non-positive mid-training.
    nominal = self.entity.get_links_inertial_mass(self.ls_idx_local)  # (num_envs, n_selected)
    lightest = nominal.min(dim=0).values
    if float(lightest.min()) + self.mass_shift_range[0] <= 0.0:
        offender = int(lightest.argmin())
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)}: mass_shift_range[0]={self.mass_shift_range[0]} can drive link "
            f"'{resolved_names[offender]}' ({float(lightest[offender]):.3g} kg) non-positive. Narrow the "
            f"range or drop the link from links_name."
        )

Bases: EventTerm

Multiplicative per-link mass randomization.

Scales each specified link's mass by a random factor sampled from [mass_scale_range[0], mass_scale_range[1]]. Internally uses set_mass_shift with shift = mass * (scale - 1). Requires EnvOptions(batch_links_info=True), and rejects a non-positive lower scale bound — the write itself is unchecked, so a scale of zero or below would silently produce a massless or negative-mass link.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION entity_name

The entity to randomize.

links_name

Link name patterns to randomize. ["*"] selects every link, so it suits only an entity with no link fixed to the world. On a fixed-base arm, a mounted hand or a fixed=True prop, name the moving links: a fixed link is rejected at build, since its mass is never read, and the error gives a links_name that selects exactly the moving ones.

mass_scale_range

Multiplicative scale range, e.g. (0.9, 1.2) for 90-120%.

    self.ls_idx_local = torch.as_tensor(ls_idx_local, dtype=gs.tc_int, device=self.device).contiguous()

def compute(self, envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None = None) -> None:
    if envs_idx is None:
        envs_idx = slice(None)
    # Sample at full env count and index — mirrors the rest of this module
    # and avoids shape mismatches when ``envs_idx`` is a slice subset.
    scale = sample_uniform(

        self.mass_scale_range[1],
        (self._env.num_envs, len(self.ls_idx_local)),
        device=self._env.device,

docs.text:
ERFI50(env: EnvBase, options: _TermOptionsT)

Bases: EventTerm

ERFI-50 noise: 50% Random Actuation Offset (RAO) + 50% Random Force Injection (RFI).

For each environment, a random value r in [0, 1] is drawn at reset:

  • r < erfi_ratio (RAO): a fixed scalar offset r * 3 * upper_bound is broadcast to all DOFs and held constant for the entire episode.
  • r >= erfi_ratio (RFI): independent per-DOF torque noise drawn uniformly from [lower_bound, upper_bound].
Requires

The action term must have a TorqueOffset modifier.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION interval_range_s

The interval range in seconds. Expected to be set to the control timestep.

action_term_name

The name of the action term to apply the noise to.

lower_bound

The lower bound of the torque noise (N·m).

upper_bound

The upper bound of the torque noise (N·m).

erfi_ratio

The fraction of envs that use RAO instead of RFI.

Reference
  • Learning and Deploying Robust Locomotion Policies with Minimal Dynamics Randomization (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2209.12878)

def build(self) -> None:
    from eden.managers.modifiers.actions.actuators import TorqueOffset

    self.term = self._env.action_manager.get_term(self.action_term_name)
    self.modifier = _require_modifier(self.term, TorqueOffset, type(self).__name__, self.action_term_name)
    self._erfi_random = sample_uniform(0.0, 1.0, (self._env.num_envs,), device=self._env.device)
    self._is_rao = (self._erfi_random < self.erfi_ratio).unsqueeze(1)
    self._rao_noise = (self._erfi_random * 3.0 * self.upper_bound).unsqueeze(1).repeat(1, self.term._n_dofs)

def reset(self, envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None = None) -> None:
    if envs_idx is None:
        envs_idx = slice(None)
    # Full-batch draws written into the selected rows (`assign_over_envs`): the auto-reset hands a
    # bool mask, and gathering or writing through it as an index is a GPU->CPU sync per op.
    # Resample per-env RAO / RFI selector.
    erfi_random = sample_uniform(0.0, 1.0, (self._env.num_envs,), device=self._env.device)
    assign_over_envs(self._erfi_random, envs_idx, erfi_random)
    assign_over_envs(self._is_rao, envs_idx, (erfi_random < self.erfi_ratio).unsqueeze(1))

    # RAO: fixed scalar noise broadcast to all DOFs.
    rao_noise = (erfi_random * 3.0 * self.upper_bound).unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, self.term._n_dofs)
    assign_over_envs(self._rao_noise, envs_idx, rao_noise)

    # Apply initial offset so first post-reset step is consistent.
    rfi_noise = sample_uniform(
        self.lower_bound, self.upper_bound, (self._env.num_envs, self.term._n_dofs), device=self._env.device
    )
    assign_over_envs(self.modifier._torque_offset, envs_idx, torch.where(self._is_rao, self._rao_noise, rfi_noise))

def __init__(self, mu_x: float, mu_y: float, var_x: float, var_y: float):
    self.mu_x = float(mu_x)
    self.mu_y = float(mu_y)
    # Pre-calculate the normalization constant: 1 / (2 * pi * sigma_x * sigma_y)
    sigma_x = math.sqrt(var_x)
    sigma_y = math.sqrt(var_y)
    self.norm_const = 1.0 / (2 * math.pi * sigma_x * sigma_y)

    # Pre-calculate the inverse denominator for the exponent: 1 / (2 * var)
    # We multiply by this later instead of dividing for speed
    self.inv_var_x_2 = 0.5 / var_x
    self.inv_var_y_2 = 0.5 / var_y

def get_probs(self, points):
    """Compute the Gaussian weights for the given points.

PlaceFromLayouts(env: EnvBase, options: EventTermOptions)

Bases: EventTerm

Each reset env draws one of a fixed list of layouts and places every entity the layout names.

A layout maps entity names to (x, y, yaw_deg): the world-frame xy on the support surface (z comes off the surface) and a yaw in degrees on top of the entity's default root orientation. Drawing all the entities' poses as one layout is what keeps them apart: two entities placed by independent ranges over the same area can start overlapping, and physics then throws them apart on the first step.

def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: EventTermOptions):
    super().__init__(env=env, options=options)
    if not self.layouts:
        raise ValueError(
            "PlaceFromLayouts needs at least one layout: pass layouts=[{'<entity>': (x, y, yaw_deg), ...}, ...]."
        )
    self.entity_names = list(self.layouts[0])
    for i, layout in enumerate(self.layouts):
        if sorted(layout) != sorted(self.entity_names):
            raise ValueError(
                f"PlaceFromLayouts layout {i} names {sorted(layout)}, but layout 0 names "
                f"{sorted(self.entity_names)}; every layout must place the same entities."
            )
    poses = torch.tensor(
        [[layout[name] for name in self.entity_names] for layout in self.layouts],
        dtype=gs.tc_float,
        device=env.device,
    )  # (layouts, entities, 3)
    self._xy = poses[..., :2]
    rpy = torch.zeros_like(poses)
    rpy[..., 2] = torch.deg2rad(poses[..., 2])
    self._yaw_quat = xyz_to_quat(rpy.reshape(-1, 3), rpy=True).reshape(*poses.shape[:2], 4)

def constant_xy_sampler(
    support_data: list[ExtendedSupportData],
    asset_AABB: torch.Tensor,
    batch_size: int = 1,
    *,
    pos_xy: tuple[float, float],
    support_idx: int | None = None,
    frame: Literal["world", "local"] = "world",
    **kwargs,
):
    """Sample a constant xy placement position on the support surface.

    Parameters
    ----------
    support_data: list[ExtendedSupportData]
        the support data of the asset to place
    asset_AABB: torch.Tensor
        the AABB of the asset to place
    batch_size: int
        the number of placement positions to sample (one per environment).
    pos_xy: tuple[float, float]
        the xy position of the object to place, interpreted in ``frame`` (see below).
    support_idx: int | None
        which of the support entity's surfaces to place onto. ``None`` (the default) is the first that can hold
        the object. An integer indexes all of the support's surfaces, link by link and each link's largest
        first, like a Python list; out of range raises ``IndexError``, and a surface that cannot hold the
        object raises ``ValueError``. Both errors list the surfaces with their heights, centres and areas.
    frame: Literal["world", "local"]
        coordinate frame for ``pos_xy``. ``"world"`` (default) treats it as world-frame
        xy and reads z off the support plane at that xy. ``"local"`` treats it in the
        support facet's local frame (origin at an arbitrary mesh corner, axes possibly
        rotated) and maps it through ``d.transform``.
    **kwargs
        additional keyword arguments, ignored by this sampler.

    NOTE: This sampler aligns z-level to the support surface but *no guarantee* on the given pos_xy is on the surface.
    NOTE: This sampler does *not* check collisions.
          It is a user's responsibility to ensure the specified pos_xy is free from collision.
    """
    del asset_AABB  # unused
    d = _support_surface(support_data, support_idx)
    res_dir = d.normal

    if frame == "local":
        vertices_3d_on_plane = torch.zeros((batch_size, 1, 3), device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)  # (B, N, 3)
        if isinstance(pos_xy, tuple):
            vertices_3d_on_plane[:, :, 0] = pos_xy[0]
            vertices_3d_on_plane[:, :, 1] = pos_xy[1]
        else:
            vertices_3d_on_plane[:, :, :2] = pos_xy
        return transform_by_T(vertices_3d_on_plane, d.transform).squeeze(1), res_dir, None

    if frame != "world":
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown frame {frame!r}; expected 'world' or 'local'.")
    # NOTE: pos_xy is in *world* coordinates; the support plane only sets the z level
    # (the facet-local frame's origin is an arbitrary mesh corner, not the world origin).
    res_pos = torch.zeros((batch_size, 3), device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)  # (B, 3)
    if isinstance(pos_xy, tuple):
        res_pos[:, 0] = pos_xy[0]
        res_pos[:, 1] = pos_xy[1]
    else:
        res_pos[:, :2] = pos_xy
    res_pos[:, 2] = _z_on_support(res_pos, d)
    return res_pos, res_dir, None

def range_xy_sampler(
    support_data: list[ExtendedSupportData],
    asset_AABB: torch.Tensor,
    batch_size: int = 1,
    *,
    range_x: tuple[float, float] | torch.Tensor,
    range_y: tuple[float, float] | torch.Tensor,
    support_idx: int | None = None,
    frame: Literal["world", "local"] = "world",
    **kwargs,
):
    """Sample an xy placement position uniformly from a rectangular range on the support surface.

    Parameters
    ----------
    support_data: list[ExtendedSupportData]
        the support data of the asset to place
    asset_AABB: torch.Tensor
        the AABB of the asset to place
    batch_size: int
        the number of placement positions to sample (one per environment).
    range_x: tuple[float, float] | torch.Tensor
        the range of the x-coordinate of the object to place, interpreted in ``frame``.
    range_y: tuple[float, float] | torch.Tensor
        the range of the y-coordinate of the object to place, interpreted in ``frame``.
    support_idx: int | None
        which of the support entity's surfaces to place onto. ``None`` (the default) is the first that can hold
        the object. An integer indexes all of the support's surfaces, link by link and each link's largest
        first, like a Python list; out of range raises ``IndexError``, and a surface that cannot hold the
        object raises ``ValueError``. Both errors list the surfaces with their heights, centres and areas.
    frame: Literal["world", "local"]
        coordinate frame for the ranges. ``"world"`` (default) samples world-frame xy
        and reads z off the support plane; ``"local"`` samples in the support facet's
        local frame and maps through ``d.transform``.
    **kwargs
        additional keyword arguments, ignored by this sampler.

    NOTE: This sampler aligns z-level to the support surface but *no guarantee* on the given pos_xy is on the surface.
    NOTE: This sampler does *not* check collisions.
          It is a user's responsibility to ensure the specified pos_xy is free from collision.
    """
    del asset_AABB  # unused
    d = _support_surface(support_data, support_idx)
    res_dir = d.normal

    if frame == "local":
        lower = torch.zeros(batch_size, 3, device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)
        upper = torch.zeros(batch_size, 3, device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)
        lower[:, 0], lower[:, 1] = range_x[0], range_y[0]
        upper[:, 0], upper[:, 1] = range_x[1], range_y[1]
        vertices_3d_on_plane = sample_uniform(lower, upper, (batch_size, 3), device=gs.device)  # (B, 3)
        return transform_by_T(vertices_3d_on_plane, d.transform).squeeze(1), res_dir, None

    if frame != "world":
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown frame {frame!r}; expected 'world' or 'local'.")
    # NOTE: range_x/range_y are in *world* coordinates; the support plane only sets the z level.
    lower = torch.zeros(batch_size, 2, device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)
    upper = torch.zeros(batch_size, 2, device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)
    lower[:, 0], lower[:, 1] = range_x[0], range_y[0]
    upper[:, 0], upper[:, 1] = range_x[1], range_y[1]
    res_pos = torch.zeros((batch_size, 3), device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)  # (B, 3)
    res_pos[:, :2] = sample_uniform(lower, upper, (batch_size, 2), device=gs.device)
    res_pos[:, 2] = _z_on_support(res_pos, d)
    return res_pos, res_dir, None

def uniform_sampler(
    support_data: list[ExtendedSupportData],
    asset_AABB: torch.Tensor,
    holes: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    **kwargs,
):
    """Sample a placement position uniformly from the pre-sampled support points.

    Parameters
    ----------
    support_data: list[ExtendedSupportData]
        the support data of the asset to place
    asset_AABB: torch.Tensor
        the AABB of the asset to place (B, 2, 3)
    holes: torch.Tensor | None
        the AABBs of existing objects concatenated in dim=1, e.g., (B, L, 2, 3) for L holes
    **kwargs
        additional keyword arguments, ignored by this sampler.
    """
    offset = (asset_AABB[:, 1] - asset_AABB[:, 0]) / 2  # (B, 3)
    # consider only supports that are valid for current gravity
    support_data = [d for d in support_data if d.valid_mask.any()]

    res_pos = []
    res_dir = []
    res_valid_mask = []

    for d in support_data:
        if d.sample_points is not None:
            vertices_3d_on_plane = torch.zeros((1, d.num_sample_points, 3), device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)
            vertices_3d_on_plane[0, :, :2] = d.sample_points
            res_pos.append(transform_by_T(vertices_3d_on_plane, d.transform))  # B, N, 3
            res_dir.append(d.normal.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, d.num_sample_points, 3))
            res_valid_mask.append(d.valid_mask.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, d.num_sample_points))  # B, N

    if len(res_pos) > 0:
        res_pos = torch.cat(res_pos, dim=1)  # (B, sum(N), 3)
        res_dir = torch.cat(res_dir, dim=1)  # (B, sum(N), 3)
        res_valid_mask = torch.cat(res_valid_mask, dim=1)  # (B, sum(N),)

        # NOTE: filter out points inside holes
        if holes is not None:
            assert holes.ndim == 4, f"Unexpected holes shape {holes.shape}"
            if holes.shape[1] > 0:
                min_occ = holes[..., 0, :2] - offset[:, None, :2]
                max_occ = holes[..., 1, :2] + offset[:, None, :2]
                is_inside_tmp = torch.all(
                    (min_occ[:, None] <= res_pos[..., None, :2]) & (res_pos[..., None, :2] < max_occ[:, None]),
                    dim=-1,
                ).any(dim=-1)  # (B, sum(N))
                res_valid_mask = res_valid_mask & torch.logical_not(is_inside_tmp)

        valid_mask = res_valid_mask.any(dim=1)  # (B, )
        # multinomial rejects all-zero rows; make them uniform so sampling never
        # raises — the returned valid_mask flags those envs as failures downstream.
        probs = res_valid_mask.float()
        probs[probs.sum(dim=1) == 0] = 1.0
        random_true_indices = torch.multinomial(probs, 1).flatten()
        res_pos = res_pos[torch.arange(res_pos.shape[0], device=res_pos.device), random_true_indices]  # (B', 3)
        res_dir = res_dir[torch.arange(res_dir.shape[0], device=res_dir.device), random_true_indices]  # (B', 3)
        return res_pos, res_dir, valid_mask
    else:
        raise ValueError("No pre-sampled points found for the support data")

def gaussian_sampler(
    support_data: list[ExtendedSupportData],
    asset_AABB: torch.Tensor,
    holes: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    gaussian_weights: Callable | None = None,
    **kwargs,
):
    """Sample a placement position from the support points weighted by a Gaussian.

    Parameters
    ----------
    support_data: list[ExtendedSupportData]
        the support data of the asset to place
    asset_AABB: torch.Tensor
        the AABB of the asset to place
    holes: torch.Tensor | None
        the AABBs of existing objects concatenated in dim=1, e.g., (B, L, 2, 3) for L holes
    gaussian_weights: Callable | None
        callable mapping candidate points to per-point sampling weights. If None, a default is used.
    **kwargs
        additional keyword arguments, ignored by this sampler.
    """
    offset = (asset_AABB[:, 1] - asset_AABB[:, 0]) / 2  # (B, 3)
    # consider only supports that are valid for current gravity
    support_data = [d for d in support_data if d.valid_mask.any()]

    res_pos = []
    res_dir = []
    res_valid_mask = []
    res_weights = []

    for d in support_data:
        if d.sample_points is not None:
            vertices_3d_on_plane = torch.zeros((1, d.num_sample_points, 3), device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)
            vertices_3d_on_plane[0, :, :2] = d.sample_points
            pos = transform_by_T(vertices_3d_on_plane, d.transform)
            res_pos.append(pos)  # B, N, 3
            res_dir.append(d.normal.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, d.num_sample_points, 3))

            res_weights.append(gaussian_weights(pos[..., :2]))  # B, N
            res_valid_mask.append(d.valid_mask.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, d.num_sample_points))  # B, N

    if len(res_pos) > 0:
        res_pos = torch.cat(res_pos, dim=1)  # (B, sum(N), 3)
        res_dir = torch.cat(res_dir, dim=1)  # (B, sum(N), 3)
        res_valid_mask = torch.cat(res_valid_mask, dim=1)  # (B, sum(N),)
        res_weights = torch.cat(res_weights, dim=1)  # (B, sum(N),)

        # NOTE: filter out points inside holes
        if holes is not None:
            assert holes.ndim == 4, f"Unexpected holes shape {holes.shape}"
            if holes.shape[1] > 0:
                min_occ = holes[..., 0, :2] - offset[:, None, :2]
                max_occ = holes[..., 1, :2] + offset[:, None, :2]
                is_inside_tmp = torch.all(
                    (min_occ[:, None] <= res_pos[..., None, :2]) & (res_pos[..., None, :2] < max_occ[:, None]),
                    dim=-1,
                ).any(dim=-1)  # (B, sum(N))
                res_valid_mask = res_valid_mask & torch.logical_not(is_inside_tmp)

        valid_mask = res_valid_mask.any(dim=1)  # (B, )
        # multinomial rejects all-zero rows, which happen two ways: (1) the row has valid points
        # but their Gaussian weights underflowed to 0 — fall back to a uniform draw over just those
        # valid points (never invalid ones, e.g. inside a hole); (2) the row has no valid point at
        # all — give it all-ones so sampling doesn't raise (valid_mask flags it as a failure).
        probs = res_weights * res_valid_mask.float()
        zero_rows = probs.sum(dim=1) == 0
        probs[zero_rows] = res_valid_mask.float()[zero_rows]
        probs[~valid_mask] = 1.0
        random_true_indices = torch.multinomial(probs, 1).flatten()
        res_pos = res_pos[torch.arange(res_pos.shape[0], device=res_pos.device), random_true_indices]  # (B', 3)
        res_dir = res_dir[torch.arange(res_dir.shape[0], device=res_dir.device), random_true_indices]  # (B', 3)
        return res_pos, res_dir, valid_mask
    else:
        raise ValueError("No pre-sampled points found for the support data")

docs.text:
ResetFromStateBuffer(env: EnvBase, options: _TermOptionsT)

Bases: EventTerm

Restore each resetting env to one stored row of a reset-state buffer file.

The buffer (:class:~eden.utils.buffers.reset_states.ResetStateBuffer, written by save()) names the entities it covers. Each reset writes those entities' full state, meaning the root pose and velocity in the authored frame and every joint by name, through one staged write; a fixed base built with batch_fixed_verts=True (a robot mount or fixture placed per row) gets its root pose too. Entities it does not name keep what the scene reset and the other RESET events leave. Which row each env gets is the sampler's call: uniform by default, or the curriculum term named by sampler (e.g. Success Guided Sampling), bound to this buffer's size at build.

RESET events run in ascending priority number, so give it a larger priority number than any RESET event that writes the same entities; one that runs after it overwrites the restored state. Task data stored with the rows (a goal) is read with :meth:current_column.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION path

The buffer file (ResetStateBuffer.save). Loaded and checked against the built entities in build().

sampler

Config key of a curriculum term subclassing ResetConfigSampler, or None for uniform sampling.

category_weights

Draw a row's category by these weights (keyed by buffer.category_names; a category left out is never drawn), then the row uniformly within it: :class:CategoryWeightedSampler. Needs a labelled buffer (ResetStateBuffer.from_families) and no sampler.

def build(self) -> None:
    if not self.path:
        raise ValueError(
            "ResetFromStateBuffer needs path=: the reset-state buffer file to restore from. "
            "Fix: ResetFromStateBuffer.configure(path='<buffer>.pt'); write one with ResetStateBuffer.save()."
        )
    # In the solver's float dtype, so the reset math never mixes precisions (``precision='64'``).
    self.buffer = ResetStateBuffer.load(self.path, device=self.device).to(self.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)
    self._plans = [self._plan(name, states) for name, states in self.buffer.entities.items()]
    self._dry_run_stage()
    consumer = f"ResetFromStateBuffer(path='{self.path}')"
    self._sampler: ResetConfigSampler = self._resolve_sampler(consumer)
    self._sampler.bind(self.buffer.num_states, consumer=consumer)
    self._buffer_generation = self.buffer.generation
    #: Each env's current row. Our own copy: the sampler's buffer is live and only valid at the call.
    self._current = torch.zeros(self.num_envs, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)

def compute(self, envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None = None) -> None:
    envs_idx = sanitize_envs_idx(envs_idx, self.num_envs, prefer_slice=False)
    if self.buffer.generation != self._buffer_generation:
        # write_rows may have relabelled rows: regroup, or the weighted sampler draws by the old families.
        if isinstance(self._sampler, CategoryWeightedSampler):
            self._sampler.relabel(self.buffer.category)
        self._buffer_generation = self.buffer.generation
    assignment = self._sampler.sample(envs_idx)
    if is_env_mask(envs_idx):
        torch.where(envs_idx, assignment, self._current, out=self._current)
        rows = slice(None)  # every env's row; the mask picks which are written, on the device
    else:
        self._current[envs_idx] = assignment[envs_idx]
        rows = envs_idx
    # Fixed roots first: the staged write's forward pass then places their links from the new base pose.
    self._write_fixed_roots(self._current, envs_idx)
    write = StagedStateWrite()
    self._stage(write, self._current, rows)
    write.apply(envs_idx)

def current_column(self, name: str) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Task column ``name`` at each env's current row, ``(num_envs, ...)``; a goal stored with the states."""
    if name not in self.buffer.columns:
        raise KeyError(

            f"Columns: {', '.join(self.buffer.columns) or '(none)'}."

Set constraint-solver (solref/solimp) parameters on selected entity geoms.

A STARTUP event: applies sol_params — (timeconst, dampratio, dmin, dmax, width, mid, power), see the MuJoCo "Solver parameters" docs — to the collision geoms of the named entities, leaving every other geom (and all joint/limit constraints) at defaults. entity_links maps entity name to the link names whose geoms to modify (None = all of the entity's geoms).

Note genesis mixes a contact pair's parameters as the mean of its two geoms' values, so a stiffened geom mildly stiffens every pair it participates in (e.g. an object also contacts the table), not only the pair of interest.

envs_idx must be None: genesis stores geom sol_params unbatched, so a per-env selection would be silently ignored (the write always applies to all envs) — rejected loudly here to keep the term out of per-env randomization.

@EVENT_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def set_contact_sol_params(
    env: EnvBase,
    envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None,
    *,
    sol_params: tuple[float, ...],
    entity_links: dict[str, list[str] | None],
) -> None:
    """Set constraint-solver (solref/solimp) parameters on selected entity geoms.

    A ``STARTUP`` event: applies ``sol_params`` — ``(timeconst, dampratio, dmin,
    dmax, width, mid, power)``, see the MuJoCo "Solver parameters" docs — to the
    collision geoms of the named entities, leaving every other geom (and all
    joint/limit constraints) at defaults. ``entity_links`` maps entity name to
    the link names whose geoms to modify (``None`` = all of the entity's geoms).

    Note genesis mixes a contact pair's parameters as the mean of its two geoms'
    values, so a stiffened geom mildly stiffens *every* pair it participates in
    (e.g. an object also contacts the table), not only the pair of interest.

    ``envs_idx`` must be ``None``: genesis stores geom sol_params unbatched, so a
    per-env selection would be silently ignored (the write always applies to all
    envs) — rejected loudly here to keep the term out of per-env randomization.
    """
    if len(sol_params) != 7:
        raise ValueError(
            "sol_params must have 7 elements (timeconst, dampratio, dmin, dmax, width, mid, power); "
            f"got {len(sol_params)}"
        )
    if not (envs_idx is None or (isinstance(envs_idx, slice) and envs_idx == slice(None))):
        raise ValueError(
            "set_contact_sol_params only supports envs_idx=None: geom sol_params are unbatched in genesis, "
            "so a per-env selection would silently apply to ALL envs."
        )
    geoms_idx: list[int] = []
    for entity_name, links in entity_links.items():
        geoms = env.get_entity(entity_name).geoms
        if links is None:
            matched = [g.idx for g in geoms]
        else:
            link_names = {g.link.name for g in geoms}
            unmatched = [name for name in links if name not in link_names]
            if unmatched:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"entity '{entity_name}' has no collision geoms on links {unmatched}; "
                    f"available links with geoms: {sorted(link_names)}"
                )
            matched = [g.idx for g in geoms if g.link.name in links]
        if not matched:
            raise ValueError(f"entity '{entity_name}' has no collision geoms to apply sol_params to")
        geoms_idx += matched
    env.set_sol_params(sol_params, geoms_idx=geoms_idx)

docs.title: ReferenceStateInitializationBase
docs.text:
ReferenceStateInitializationBase(env: EnvBase, options: _TermOptionsT)

Bases: EventTerm

Shared base for the motion-reference RSI (reference-state-initialization) events.

Two concrete flavours seed initial state from the motion reference at RESET: :class:ReferenceStateInitialization (the robot — a floating or immobile base) and :class:ObjectReferenceStateInitialization (a free rigid object). This base exists so the motion-end resync path can find every flavour by isinstance (not by matching one exact class name) and ask each to seed itself onto a resampled reference via :meth:teleport — so the branch knowledge lives in the term, in one place, instead of being re-derived in :class:~eden.managers.motion.resync.MotionEndResync.

A flavour does not write the simulator itself: it stages its entity's writes (:meth:_stage_reset, :meth:_stage_teleport) into a shared :class:~eden.entities.rigid.StagedStateWrite, and :meth:compute_batch / :meth:teleport_batch apply every term's writes at once. The event manager fires adjacent RSI terms through one :meth:compute_batch, so a reset seeding N entities gathers the reference once and pays one Genesis write per kind and one forward-kinematics pass, not N of each.

compute_batch(terms: Sequence[ReferenceStateInitializationBase], envs_idx: slice | Tensor | None) -> None

Seed every term's entity from the init reference state, in one write (see the class docstring).

The terms draw their perturbation noise in order, as they would one by one, and write disjoint state, so the result is what firing them one after another leaves.

Source code in eden/managers/terms/events/motion.py 
@classmethod
def compute_batch(
    cls, terms: Sequence[ReferenceStateInitializationBase], envs_idx: slice | torch.Tensor | None
) -> None:
    """Seed every term's entity from the init reference state, in one write (see the class docstring).

    The terms draw their perturbation noise in order, as they would one by one, and write disjoint
    state, so the result is what firing them one after another leaves.
    """
    env = terms[0]._env
    if envs_idx is None or isinstance(envs_idx, slice):
        envs_idx = sanitize_envs_idx(envs_idx, env.num_envs, prefer_slice=False)
    # The reference is gathered for the selected rows, through int ids: a sync per op through a mask and
    # none through ids. The auto-reset's mask has its ids taken once for the whole reset, so this
    # costs nothing. The write itself takes the mask, which Genesis applies on the device.
    envs_ids = env_indices(envs_idx)
    init_states = env.motion_manager.get_reset_reference_state(envs_ids, [term.entity_name for term in terms])
    write = StagedStateWrite()
    for term in terms:
        term._stage_reset(write, envs_ids, init_states[term.entity_name])
    write.apply(envs_idx)
    for term in terms:
        term._arm_depenetration(envs_ids)

@classmethod
def teleport_batch(
    cls,
    terms: Sequence[ReferenceStateInitializationBase],
    wrap_idx: torch.Tensor,
    refs: Mapping[str, MotionReferenceData],
) -> None:
    """:meth:`teleport` every term's entity onto ``refs[entity_name]``, in one write.

    ``wrap_idx`` is int env ids, or a ``(num_envs,)`` bool mask: then every env's frame 0 is staged
    and the mask picks which are written, which Genesis does on the device — no ``nonzero()``, so a
    mask that selects no env costs no GPU->CPU sync either (the motion-end resync calls this every step).
    """
    rows = slice(None) if is_env_mask(wrap_idx) else wrap_idx
    write = StagedStateWrite()
    for term in terms:
        term._stage_teleport(write, rows, refs[term.entity_name])
    write.apply(wrap_idx)
    for term in terms:
        term._arm_depenetration(wrap_idx)

def build(self):
    self.robot = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)
    # ``has_immobile_base`` covers both a fixed-base entity and one welded onto another
    # (a composite's dexterous hand): Genesis ``attach`` removes the child's root joint,
    # so there is no base to seed there either.
    if self.robot.has_immobile_base:
        if self.max_depenetration_velocity is not None:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{term_subject(self)} sets max_depenetration_velocity, but "
                f"the entity has no base to cap (it is fixed or welded to another entity). Drop the option here; "
                f"set it on the RSI term of the entity carrying the free base."
            )
        # No floating base joint to seed — only the actuated DOFs are
        # written (see the immobile-base branch in ``_stage_reset``). The write
        # goes through name-resolved Genesis indices in the MOTION dof
        # order, so no qpos-declaration-order assumption is needed.
        from eden.utils.motion_reference.lookup import get_robot_dofs_idx, untracked_entity_error

        motion_dofs_name = self._env.motion_manager.get_target_dofs_name(self.entity_name)
        if motion_dofs_name is None:
            raise untracked_entity_error(self._env, self.entity_name)
        if not motion_dofs_name:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{term_subject(self)} (immobile base) requires the motion reference to expose DOFs for it."
            )
        self._motion_dofs_idx = get_robot_dofs_idx(self._env, self.entity_name, motion_dofs_name)
        # Host copies for the staged write, which reads its indices in Python every reset.
        self._motion_dofs_host = self._motion_dofs_idx.tolist()
        # A ball joint's three DOFs make one quaternion, so the reference covers all of them or none.
        StagedStateWrite.check_dofs_pos(self.robot, self._motion_dofs_host)
        self._entity_dofs_host = range(self.robot.n_dofs)
        # See ``_soft_limits_cols``: gather the rows matching the motion DOF order so the
        # clip in ``_dofs_pos_with_noise`` can't silently apply another joint's range.
        self._soft_limits_cols = self.robot.find_named_dofs(motion_dofs_name).columns
    else:
        from eden.utils.motion_reference.lookup import assert_motion_field_present

        # The base is seeded from the reference's base pose, so an untracked entity, or a sequence
        # without one, is a config error: raise it here rather than at the first reset.
        assert_motion_field_present(self._env, self.entity_name, "base_pos_w")
        assert_motion_field_present(self._env, self.entity_name, "base_quat_w")
        base_dofs_index = self.robot.find_free_base_dofs_idx_local(self.base_joint_name)
        # Host lists for the staged write, which reads its indices in Python every reset: the free base's
        # six DOFs then the actuated ones, and the qs ``set_qpos`` writes by default (dofs_name order).
        self._base_and_dofs_host = [*base_dofs_index, *self.robot.dofs_idx_local.tolist()]
        self._qs_host = self.robot.qs_idx_local.tolist()
        self._build_depenetration(self.robot, base_dofs_index)

    range_list = [self.pose_range.get(key, (0.0, 0.0)) for key in ["x", "y", "z", "roll", "pitch", "yaw"]]
    self.pose_ranges = torch.tensor(range_list, device=self.device)
    range_list = [self.velocity_range.get(key, (0.0, 0.0)) for key in ["x", "y", "z", "roll", "pitch", "yaw"]]
    self.velocity_ranges = torch.tensor(range_list, device=self.device)

def build(self):
    from eden.utils.motion_reference.lookup import assert_motion_field_present

    self.obj = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)
    if self.obj.has_immobile_base:
        reason = "is welded to another entity" if self.obj.is_attached else "is fixed-base"

            f"free-floating entity; it {reason} and has no base DOFs."

    assert_motion_field_present(self._env, self.entity_name, "base_quat_w")

    self._base_dofs_host = range(6)
    self._base_qs_host = range(7)

def compute(self) -> torch.Tensor:

@TERMINATION_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
@METRIC_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def object_a_is_on_b(
    env: EnvBase,
    *,
    entity_a_name: str,
    entity_b_name: str,
    xy_threshold: float = 0.03,
    height_threshold: float = 0.04,
    height_diff: float = 0.0,
):
    """Check if object_a is on object_b by comparing height and xy distance of object origins.

    This function can be used as a termination term or a metric term.

    Parameters
    ----------
    env: EnvBase
        The environment instance.
    entity_a_name: str
        The name of the entity_a.
    entity_b_name: str
        The name of the entity_b.
    xy_threshold: float
        The threshold for the xy distance.
    height_threshold: float
        The threshold for the height distance.
    height_diff: float
        The expected height difference.

    Returns
    -------
    success: torch.Tensor
        A boolean tensor indicating if the object_a is on the object_b.
    """
    object_a: Entity = env.get_entity(entity_a_name)
    object_b: Entity = env.get_entity(entity_b_name)

    pos_diff = object_a.get_pos() - object_b.get_pos()
    height_dist = torch.linalg.vector_norm(pos_diff[:, 2:], dim=1)
    xy_dist = torch.linalg.vector_norm(pos_diff[:, :2], dim=1)

    success = torch.logical_and(
        pos_diff[:, 2] > 0.0,  # object_a is above object_b
        torch.logical_and(xy_dist < xy_threshold, (height_dist - height_diff) < height_threshold),
    )
    return success

Both footprints are the xy extent of the entity's world-frame bounding box (its collision geometry), so a cup over a cutting board, or a scissor dropped into a container, passes whatever its height: pair it with a height or contact check to require that it rests there. PolaRiS's is_within_xy rubric checker (eden.tasks.polaris) is this test.

@METRIC_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def object_a_within_b_xy(
    env: EnvBase,
    *,
    entity_a_name: str,
    entity_b_name: str,
    min_fraction: float = 0.8,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """*min_fraction* of entity_a's footprint lies over entity_b's.

    Both footprints are the xy extent of the entity's world-frame bounding box (its collision geometry),
    so a cup over a cutting board, or a scissor dropped into a container, passes whatever its height:
    pair it with a height or contact check to require that it rests there. PolaRiS's ``is_within_xy``
    rubric checker (``eden.tasks.polaris``) is this test.

    Parameters
    ----------
    env: EnvBase
        The environment instance.
    entity_a_name: str
        The entity that must lie over the other.
    entity_b_name: str
        The entity it must lie over.
    min_fraction: float
        Smallest share of entity_a's footprint area that must overlap entity_b's, in ``(0, 1]``.
    """
    a = env.get_entity(entity_a_name).get_AABB()[..., :2]  # (num_envs, 2 [low, high], 2)
    b = env.get_entity(entity_b_name).get_AABB()[..., :2]
    overlap = (torch.minimum(a[:, 1], b[:, 1]) - torch.maximum(a[:, 0], b[:, 0])).clamp(min=0.0).prod(dim=1)
    area = (a[:, 1] - a[:, 0]).prod(dim=1)
    return overlap >= min_fraction * area

def entity_near_target(
    env: EnvBase,
    *,
    entity_name: str,
    target_pos: Vec3FType | torch.Tensor,
    threshold: float = 0.05,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Check if an entity is within *threshold* of a fixed world position.

    Returns a per-env bool tensor (True if within threshold).

    Parameters
    ----------
    env: EnvBase
        The environment instance.
    entity_name: str
        Name of the entity to check.
    target_pos: list[float] | Tensor
        Target world position ``[x, y, z]``.  A plain list is converted to a
        tensor once per distinct value (``device_constant``) and reused.
    threshold: float
        Maximum allowed distance.
    """
    entity: Entity = env.get_entity(entity_name)
    if not isinstance(target_pos, torch.Tensor):
        target_pos = device_constant(target_pos, env.device).unsqueeze(0)
    dist = torch.linalg.vector_norm(entity.get_pos() - target_pos, dim=1)
    return dist < threshold

    entity_a: Entity = env.get_entity(entity_a_name)
    entity_b: Entity = env.get_entity(entity_b_name)
    pos_diff = entity_a.get_pos()[:, :2] - entity_b.get_pos()[:, :2]
    dist = torch.linalg.vector_norm(pos_diff, dim=1)
    return dist < threshold

@TERMINATION_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
@METRIC_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def object_in_region(
    env: EnvBase,
    *,
    entity_name: str,
    region_min: list[float],
    region_max: list[float],
    relative: bool = False,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Check if an entity's root position is inside an axis-aligned box.

    Returns a per-env bool tensor (True if inside, bounds inclusive).

    Parameters
    ----------
    env: EnvBase
        The environment instance.
    entity_name: str
        Name of the entity.
    region_min: list[float]
        Lower corner of the box ``[x_min, y_min, z_min]``.
    region_max: list[float]
        Upper corner of the box ``[x_max, y_max, z_max]``.
    relative: bool
        Frame the box is expressed in — see :func:`object_above_height`, including why ``True``
        needs a rigid entity and only says so on step 1. Pass ``True`` when the corners were
        reasoned from the asset's own geometry rather than measured in the solver frame.
    """
    entity: Entity = env.get_entity(entity_name)
    pos = entity.get_pos(relative=relative)
    # Built once per distinct box, not per call: an upload per step is a GPU->CPU sync.
    lo = device_constant(region_min, env.device).unsqueeze(0)
    hi = device_constant(region_max, env.device).unsqueeze(0)
    inside = (pos >= lo).all(dim=1) & (pos <= hi).all(dim=1)
    return inside

Bases: MetricTerm

Detect a parallel-jaw grasp via contact force alignment.

Returns a per-env bool, True when both gripper pads have contact forces aligned with their closing direction above force_threshold. This correctly detects a grasp even when the fingers cannot fully close (e.g. when an object is between them).

A grasp spanning two links of one object counts, and so do pads pressing two different objects. The weld action instead requires both pads on the one link it would weld, so this metric can read True in a step that welds nothing.

@TERMINATION_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
@METRIC_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def joint_angle_at_target(
    env: EnvBase,
    *,
    entity_name: str,
    joint_name: str,
    target_angle: float,
    threshold: float = 0.05,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Check if a single DOF is within *threshold* of *target_angle*.

    Returns a per-env bool tensor, True when the joint position satisfies
    ``|current - target_angle| < threshold``.

    Parameters
    ----------
    env: EnvBase
        The environment instance.
    entity_name: str
        Name of the articulated entity.
    joint_name: str
        Name of the DOF to query.
    target_angle: float
        Target joint position (radians or meters depending on joint type).
    threshold: float
        Maximum allowed deviation.
    """
    entity: Entity = env.get_entity(entity_name)
    _, dof_idx = entity.find_named_dofs_idx_local([joint_name], preserve_order=True)
    dof_pos = entity.get_dofs_pos(dofs_idx_local=dof_idx)  # (num_envs, 1)
    error = torch.abs(dof_pos[:, 0] - target_angle)
    return error < threshold
