docs.title: SequentialMetricTerm
docs.text:
SequentialMetricTerm(env: EnvBase, options: MetricTermOptions)

Bases: MetricTerm

Metric that tracks ordered sub-goals (phases).

Each phase is a predicate that must be satisfied before the next phase is evaluated. The metric value is the fraction of phases completed (completed / total). With the default success_threshold=1.0 and direction="hib", the episode is considered successful once all phases are complete.

Phase advancement is per-environment -- different parallel environments can be in different phases.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION phases

Ordered list of phase definitions. Each PhaseOptions must contain one of:

  • term -- a MetricTermOptions from .configure().
  • ref -- a string referencing a sibling term in MetricManagerOptions.

And optionally:

  • threshold -- (default 1.0) minimum value returned by the phase predicate that counts as "passed".
  • hold -- if True, reuse the phase's own term as hold predicate.
  • hold_term -- a separate MetricTermOptions for the hold predicate (overrides hold).
  • hold_until -- the last phase (name or index, inclusive) through which the hold stays active; default: until the task completes.
  • hold_guard -- name of another held phase; this hold is enforced only where that phase's hold is also failing.

TYPE: list[PhaseOptions]

allow_skip

If True, an env may advance through multiple phases in a single compute() call. If False (default), at most one phase transition happens per call.

TYPE: bool

Example

::

SequentialMetricTerm.configure(
    phases=[
        PhaseOptions(
            name="reach",
            term=EeNearEntity.configure(
                robot_name="robot",
                ee_link_names=["finger_l", "finger_r"],
                entity_name="apple",
                threshold=0.15,
            ),
            threshold=0.5,
        ),
        PhaseOptions(
            name="grasp",
            term=IsGrasping.configure(
                robot_name="robot",
                left_gripper_link_name="left_gripper_pad",
                right_gripper_link_name="right_gripper_pad",
                force_threshold=0.5,
            ),
            threshold=1.0,
            hold=True,
            hold_until="place",
        ),
        PhaseOptions(
            name="place",
            term=entity_near_target.configure(entity_name="apple", target_pos=[0.5, 0.0, 0.8]),
        ),
    ],
    allow_skip=False,
)

def resolve_refs(self, manager_options) -> None:
    """Resolve ``ref`` phases by looking up sibling MetricTermOptions.

    Called by ``MetricManager._prepare_terms()`` in a second pass after
    all terms have been built.
    """
    for i, phase in enumerate(self.phases):
        if phase.ref is not None and self._resolved_phases[i][0] is None:
            sibling_options = getattr(manager_options, phase.ref, None)
            if sibling_options is None:
                raise ValueError(f"Phase {i} ref='{phase.ref}' not found in MetricManagerOptions")
            term_instance = self._instantiate_term(sibling_options, f"phases[{i}].ref ('{phase.ref}')")
            self._resolved_phases[i] = (term_instance, phase.threshold)

    # Now resolve hold conditions (requires all phases to be resolved)
    self._resolve_all_holds()

def build(self):
    for i, phase in enumerate(self.phases):
        if not isinstance(phase, PhaseOptions):
            raise TypeError(
                f"Phase {i} must be a PhaseOptions instance, got {type(phase).__name__}. "
                f"Use PhaseOptions(term=MyTerm.configure(...), ...) instead of dict."
            )

        if phase.term is not None and phase.ref is not None:
            raise ValueError(f"Phase {i}: 'term' and 'ref' are mutually exclusive")
        if phase.term is None and phase.ref is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Phase {i}: must specify either 'term' or 'ref'")

        # Derive phase name
        name = phase.name
        if not name:
            if phase.term is not None:
                name = phase.term.name
            elif phase.ref is not None:
                name = phase.ref
            else:
                name = f"phase_{i}"
        self._phase_names.append(name)
        self._phase_name_to_idx[name] = i

        # Instantiate term (or defer if ref)
        if phase.term is not None:
            term_instance = self._instantiate_term(phase.term, f"phases[{i}].term")
            self._resolved_phases.append((term_instance, phase.threshold))
        else:
            # ref — will be resolved in resolve_refs()
            self._resolved_phases.append((None, phase.threshold))

    # If no refs, resolve holds now; otherwise MetricManager will call resolve_refs()
    has_refs = any(p.ref is not None for p in self.phases)
    if not has_refs:
        self._resolve_all_holds()

def compute(self) -> torch.Tensor:
    num_phases = len(self._resolved_phases)
    if num_phases == 0:
        return torch.ones(self._env.num_envs, device=self.device)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Hold-condition check: revert to earliest failing hold
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    if self._has_any_holds:
        # Track the earliest failing phase per env (num_phases = "no failure")
        revert_target = torch.full((self._env.num_envs,), num_phases, dtype=torch.long, device=self.device)

        # Pre-compute hold values so guards can reference them.
        # hold_failed[p] is a per-env bool tensor (True = hold failing).
        hold_failed: list[torch.Tensor | None] = [None] * num_phases
        for p, hold in enumerate(self._hold_conditions):
            if hold is None:
                continue
            candidates = (self._phase_buf > p) & (self._phase_buf < hold.until_idx)
            if not candidates.any():
                continue
            h_value = hold.term.compute()
            h_failed = h_value < hold.threshold
            hold_failed[p] = candidates & h_failed

            if en.logger.level <= logging.DEBUG:
                for e in range(self._env.num_envs):
                    if candidates[e]:
                        en.logger.debug(
                            f"  [env {e}] hold check phase {p} ({self._phase_names[p]}): "
                            f"value={h_value[e].item():.4f}  threshold={hold.threshold}  "
                            f"failed={bool(h_failed[e])}"
                        )

        # Apply hold failures, respecting guards.
        for p, hold in enumerate(self._hold_conditions):
            if hold is None or hold_failed[p] is None:
                continue
            failing = hold_failed[p]
            if not failing.any():
                continue

            # If this hold has a guard, suppress it for envs where the
            # guard's hold is still passing (i.e. guard not failing).
            if hold.guard_idx is not None:
                guard_failing = hold_failed[hold.guard_idx]
                if guard_failing is None:
                    # Guard hold wasn't even evaluated (no envs in window) → guard is passing → suppress all
                    if en.logger.level <= logging.DEBUG:
                        en.logger.debug(
                            f"  hold on phase {p} ({self._phase_names[p]}) fully suppressed "
                            f"by guard '{self._phase_names[hold.guard_idx]}' (guard passing)"
                        )
                    continue
                # Only enforce this hold where the guard is also failing
                failing = failing & guard_failing
                if not failing.any():
                    if en.logger.level <= logging.DEBUG:
                        en.logger.debug(
                            f"  hold on phase {p} ({self._phase_names[p]}) suppressed "
                            f"by guard '{self._phase_names[hold.guard_idx]}' (guard passing for all envs)"
                        )
                    continue

            revert_target = torch.where(failing & (p < revert_target), self._phase_tensors[p], revert_target)

        # Apply reverts
        needs_revert = revert_target < num_phases
        if needs_revert.any():
            if en.logger.level <= logging.INFO:
                for e in range(self._env.num_envs):
                    if needs_revert[e]:
                        old_p = self._phase_buf[e].item()
                        new_p = revert_target[e].item()
                        en.logger.info(
                            f"[env {e}] HOLD FAILED: reverting from phase {old_p} ({self._phase_names[old_p]}) "
                            f"→ phase {new_p} ({self._phase_names[new_p]})"
                        )
            self._phase_buf = torch.where(needs_revert, revert_target, self._phase_buf)

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Phase advancement
    # ------------------------------------------------------------------
    prev_phases = self._phase_buf.clone()

    # When allow_skip is False, use a snapshot so each env advances at
    # most one phase per compute().  When True, read _phase_buf directly
    # so envs that just advanced are re-evaluated for the next phase.
    phase_view = self._phase_buf if self.allow_skip else prev_phases

    for p, (term_instance, threshold) in enumerate(self._resolved_phases):
        mask = phase_view == p
        if not mask.any():
            continue
        value = term_instance.compute()
        passed = value >= threshold
        advance = mask & passed
        self._phase_buf[advance] = p + 1

        if en.logger.level <= logging.DEBUG:
            for e in range(self._env.num_envs):
                if mask[e]:
                    en.logger.debug(
                        f"  [env {e}] phase {p} ({self._phase_names[p]}): "
                        f"value={value[e].item():.4f}  threshold={threshold}  "
                        f"passed={bool(passed[e])}"
                    )

    # Clamp to [0, num_phases]
    self._phase_buf.clamp_(max=num_phases)

    if en.logger.level <= logging.INFO:
        for e in range(self._env.num_envs):
            if self._phase_buf[e] != prev_phases[e]:
                old_p = prev_phases[e].item()
                new_p = self._phase_buf[e].item()
                old_name = self._phase_names[old_p]
                if new_p >= num_phases:
                    en.logger.info(
                        f"[env {e}] Phase {old_p} ({old_name}) DONE → task COMPLETE ({new_p}/{num_phases})"
                    )
                else:
                    en.logger.info(
                        f"[env {e}] Phase {old_p} ({old_name}) DONE → now at phase {new_p} ({self._phase_names[new_p]})  [{new_p}/{num_phases}]"
                    )

    return self._phase_buf.float() / num_phases

docs.text:
RubricMetricTerm(env: EnvBase, options: MetricTermOptions)

Bases: MetricTerm

Fraction of rubric criteria met, each after its dependencies.

A criterion is reached the first step its predicate succeeds — by the term's own is_success, so its direction and success_threshold decide (entity_distance with success_threshold=0.05 is met within 5 cm) — while every criterion in its after list has already been reached, and stays reached until the env resets: a cube let go over the tray counts even if it bounces off later. The value is the fraction of criteria reached, so with the default success_threshold=1.0 the task succeeds once all of them are. Unlike :class:SequentialMetricTerm, criteria with no dependency between them are reached in any order (both cubes' "reach" before either "lift", or one cube's whole chain first) — the progress score of PolaRiS's Rubric, which :mod:eden.tasks.polaris reproduces.

Criteria are evaluated in list order every step, so after names earlier criteria only, and a criterion can be reached in the same step as the ones it depends on.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION criteria

The criteria, each a named predicate (term) and the earlier criteria it needs (after).

TYPE: list[CriterionOptions]

Example

::

RubricMetricTerm.configure(
    criteria=[
        CriterionOptions(name="reach", term=EeNearEntity.configure(robot_name="gripper", ...)),
        CriterionOptions(name="lift", term=object_above_height.configure(...), after=["reach"]),
        CriterionOptions(name="in_bowl", term=object_a_within_b_xy.configure(...), after=["lift"]),
    ]
)

    super().__init__(env=env, options=options)
    self._terms: list[MetricTerm] = []

def build(self):
    if not self.criteria:
        raise ValueError(
            "RubricMetricTerm needs at least one criterion: pass criteria=[CriterionOptions(...), ...]."
        )
    index: dict[str, int] = {}
    for i, criterion in enumerate(self.criteria):
        if not isinstance(criterion, CriterionOptions):
            raise TypeError(
                f"criteria[{i}] must be a CriterionOptions, got {type(criterion).__name__}; write "
                f"CriterionOptions(name=..., term=MyTerm.configure(...)) rather than a dict."
            )
        if criterion.name in index:
            raise ValueError(
                f"RubricMetricTerm criterion name '{criterion.name}' is used twice; names must be unique."
            )
        unknown = [name for name in criterion.after if name not in index]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"RubricMetricTerm criterion '{criterion.name}' lists after={unknown}, which are not earlier "
                f"criteria; earlier ones: {list(index) or 'none'}. Move the criterion below the ones it depends on."
            )
        term = build_term(
            METRIC_TERM_REGISTRY, self._env, criterion.term, label=f"{type(self).__name__}.criteria[{i}]"
        )
        if term.is_cumulative:
            raise ValueError(
                f"RubricMetricTerm criterion '{criterion.name}' has is_cumulative=True, but a criterion is "
                f"judged on each step's value, never on a sum over the episode; configure its term with "
                f"is_cumulative=False."
            )
        self._after.append([index[name] for name in criterion.after])
        self._terms.append(term)
        index[criterion.name] = i

def compute(self) -> torch.Tensor:
    for i, (term, after) in enumerate(zip(self._terms, self._after)):
        met = term.is_success(term.compute())
        if after:
            met &= self._reached[:, after].all(dim=1)
        self._reached[:, i] |= met
    return self._reached.float().mean(dim=1)

Bases: ConfigurableTermBase[ActionModifierOptions]

Base class for composable action modifiers.

Action modifiers intercept and transform processed actions (target positions/velocities) and/or control torques. They are designed to be composed together using :class:~eden.managers.modifiers.actions.actuators.Compose.

Subclasses override any of three hooks, which run at two different rates:

docs.title: ObservationModifier
docs.text:
ObservationModifier(env: EnvBase, options: _TermOptionsT)

Bases: ConfigurableTermBase[ObservationModifierOptions]

Base class for a transform the observation manager applies to one term's output, frame by frame.

Listed on an observation term as modifiers=[...]. Each frame of the term goes through its modifiers in list order, then noise, clip and scale, then the group's nan_policy, and last the history window. Unlike noise, a modifier runs in every mode (training, eval, deployment). Each term instance owns its modifier instances, so the same modifier on a policy and a critic copy of a term keeps two independent states.

compute(frame) is a read, the same rule as for an observation term. The manager calls it every time the observation is computed, which can be several times per control step: from EnvBase.reset(), at phase 19, at phase 12 for the final-observation snapshot, from get_observations(), and once at build to check the output. It returns the output for frame given the modifier's current state and changes nothing.

advance(frame) is the commit. A stateful modifier (a filter, a delay) folds frame into its state here. The manager calls it right after compute(frame), with the same frame, on the pass that also pushes the history windows (compute(update_history=True)). That pass runs once per control step (phase 19 of RLEnvBase.step, EnvBase.step, each deploy tick) and once per EnvBase.reset(). A partial env.reset(envs_idx) therefore advances every env, the same way it pushes every env's history window. So a modifier's state moves together with the history window, and a delay of k is k pushes. A read that comes after the push and before the next step (get_observations() between steps) applies the current frame once more, as the history window's read does. With backfill, right after a reset, that gives the same value; otherwise it runs one push ahead. A stateless modifier leaves advance as the no-op it is here.

Two rules keep reads and commits apart:

  • compute returns a tensor it does not write afterwards. The manager uses the output after calling advance, so a view of state that advance updates in place would change under it. Return a fresh tensor, or .clone() the state.
  • Neither method writes into frame, and advance copies what it keeps (self._last.copy_(frame), not self._last = frame). frame may be the raw output that another group's copy of the term also reads (the manager's cross-group cache), the term's own buffer, or a view of simulator state.

The other hooks: build(frame) allocates the state from a sample frame, before the env steps (allocate here, then write in place: see "Term state lifecycle" in docs/guides/terms.md). reset(envs_idx) restarts the rows of the envs whose episode restarts. It is called with the same indices as the term's history window: None for every env, otherwise an index or boolean-mask tensor to index with.

A modifier returns a frame of the shape, dtype and device it received. The manager checks this at build, because scale, history and concatenation are all sized from the term's raw output.

docs.title: Action modifiers
docs.text:
Composable action modifiers for action terms.

Action modifiers sit between action terms and the physics engine. They intercept and transform processed actions (target positions/velocities) and/or control torques via composable operations like clipping, delay, friction, and motor strength scaling.

Modifiers are designed to be composed together using :class:Compose, similar to torchvision.transforms.Compose::

modifiers = Compose.configure(
    modifiers=[
        ActionDelay.configure(delay_range_steps=(1, 3)),
        FrictionModel.configure(),
        EffortClip.configure(),
    ]
)

Each modifier implements up to three hooks:

  • modify_processed_action: transforms the target positions/velocities once per control step, before PD control (e.g., envelope clip, backlash).
  • modify_applied_target: transforms the command the actuator acts on, once per physics step (e.g., delay).
  • modify_ctrl_torque: transforms the computed torques after PD control (e.g., friction, effort clipping, motor strength scaling).

Modifiers that need motor spec parameters (friction, T-N curve limits) read them automatically from the entity's actuator spec (dofs_spec) at build time. Explicit overrides can still be passed to use custom values.

docs.title: Compose
docs.text:
Compose(env: EnvBase, options: ActionModifierOptions)

Bases: ActionModifier

Chains multiple action modifiers in sequence.

Each hook calls the children in list order, but the three hooks run at different points of a step (see :class:~eden.managers.modifiers.ActionModifier): every modify_processed_action once per control step in compute(), then every modify_applied_target once per physics step in apply_actions(), then every modify_ctrl_torque after the control law. A physics-step modifier such as :class:ActionDelay therefore acts after every control-step one such as :class:EnvelopeClip, wherever each is listed. Listing it first logs a warning, since the list would then read in a different order from the one that runs.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION modifiers

Ordered sequence of modifier configurations.

TYPE: tuple[ActionModifierOptions, ...] | list[ActionModifierOptions]

Example

::

Compose.configure(
    modifiers=[
        ActionDelay.configure(delay_range_steps=(1, 3)),
        FrictionModel.configure(),
        EffortClip.configure(),
    ]
)
Source code in eden/managers/modifiers/actions/actuators.py 
def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: ActionModifierOptions):
    super().__init__(env=env, options=options)
    self._modifiers: list[ActionModifier] = []
    for mod_options in self.modifiers:
        # Normalize plain dicts (e.g. from YAML/JSON config loading) to ActionModifierOptions.
        if isinstance(mod_options, dict):
            mod_options = ActionModifierOptions(**mod_options)
        mod = ACTION_MODIFIER_REGISTRY.get(mod_options.name)(env=env, options=mod_options)
        self._modifiers.append(mod)
    self._warn_if_listed_out_of_run_order()

def get(self, cls: type) -> ActionModifier | None:
    """Return the first child modifier that is an instance of ``cls``, or ``None``.

    Recurses into nested ``Compose`` chains via each child's ``get``.
    """
    for mod in self._modifiers:
        found = mod.get(cls)
        if found is not None:
            return found
    return None

Bases: ActionModifier

Delays the command the actuator acts on by a random number of physics steps, drawn per episode.

The delay is applied at the actuator, once per physics step (sim_dt), not once per control step: every apply_actions() pushes the controller's command into a history and drives the actuator with the entry d physics steps old. So a latency shorter than a control step can be expressed — at sim_dt=0.005, decimation=4, d=2 keeps the first two physics steps of every control step on the previous command. This matches the physics-step unit of Isaac Lab's DelayedPDActuatorCfg and mjlab's actuator delay_* fields.

Each env draws d uniformly from the inclusive range when it resets and keeps it until its next reset. The range is given either in physics steps (delay_range_steps) or in seconds (delay_range_s), but not both; with neither, commands pass through. After a reset the history is backfilled with the first new command, so the actuator never acts on a command from before the reset.

processed_action stays undelayed. It is the command the policy issued, and what a deployment sends. The delay acts only inside apply_actions(), after every modify_processed_action modifier wherever it sits in a :class:Compose chain (which warns when it is listed before one). It models the simulated actuator's latency, and no deployment applies it: eden deploy never calls apply_actions(), so a real robot has only its own latency, and the MuJoCo sim-to-sim robot has none. A policy trained against a delay therefore runs there with less latency than it trained with. With both ends of the range equal, the lag was fixed, so it expects that lag on every step, and a MuJoCo sim-to-sim run does not reproduce it.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION delay_range_steps

The inclusive delay range (min, max) in physics steps — the unit of Isaac Lab's min_delay / max_delay.

TYPE: tuple[int, int] | None

delay_range_s

The inclusive delay range in seconds instead. Converted to physics steps at build, so each end must be a whole multiple of sim_dt.

TYPE: tuple[float, float] | None

def build(self, num_envs: int, device: str, entity=None, dofs_idx_local=None) -> None:

        raise ValueError("ConstantTorqueKick requires dofs_idx_local to be passed in build().")

        raise ValueError("ConstantTorqueKick direction_source must be 'pos_err' or 'ctrl_torque'.")

        self.activation_epsilon,

        param_name="activation_epsilon",

    self._torque_kick = self._torque_kick_row.unsqueeze(0).repeat(num_envs, 1)

def modify_ctrl_torque(
    self,
    ctrl_torque: torch.Tensor,
    dofs_vel: torch.Tensor,
    pos_err: torch.Tensor | None = None,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    if self.direction_source == "pos_err" and pos_err is not None:
        direction_signal = pos_err
        active = pos_err.abs() > self._activation_epsilon
    else:
        direction_signal = ctrl_torque
        active = direction_signal != 0.0
    return ctrl_torque + torch.sign(direction_signal) * self._torque_kick * active.to(ctrl_torque.dtype)

docs.text:
GearBacklash(env: EnvBase, options: _TermOptionsT)

Bases: ActionModifier

Adds direction-dependent gear slop to position targets before PD control.

This models lost motion in the drivetrain, where the load settles on the side of the gear gap selected by the latest commanded motion. After a positive target move the effective motor-side target becomes target + backlash; after a negative move it becomes target - backlash. Small target changes below reversal_threshold do not change the selected side, which prevents command noise from flipping the gap state.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION backlash

One-sided position offset in radians. A scalar broadcasts to all controlled DOFs; an iterable must match len(dofs_idx_local).

TYPE: LaxFArrayType

reversal_threshold

Minimum target-position change in radians required to select a new backlash side.

TYPE: LaxFArrayType

takeup_rate

Fraction of the remaining gap state to take up on each action update. 1.0 switches sides instantly; values in [0, 1) create a smooth slosh transition over multiple control updates.

TYPE: LaxFArrayType

initial_side

Initial gap side on reset. 0.0 starts centered until the first command movement selects a side.

TYPE: LaxFArrayType

def build(self, num_envs: int, device: str, entity=None, dofs_idx_local=None) -> None:
    if dofs_idx_local is None:
        raise ValueError("GearBacklash requires dofs_idx_local to be passed in build().")
    n_dof = len(dofs_idx_local)
    self._backlash_row = _per_dof_float_row(self.backlash, n_dof, device, param_name="backlash")
    if (self._backlash_row < 0.0).any().item():
        raise ValueError("GearBacklash backlash must be nonnegative.")
    self._reversal_threshold_row = _per_dof_float_row(
        self.reversal_threshold,
        n_dof,
        device,
        param_name="reversal_threshold",
    ).abs()
    self._takeup_rate_row = _per_dof_float_row(self.takeup_rate, n_dof, device, param_name="takeup_rate")
    if ((self._takeup_rate_row < 0.0) | (self._takeup_rate_row > 1.0)).any().item():
        raise ValueError("GearBacklash takeup_rate must be in [0, 1].")
    self._initial_side_row = _per_dof_float_row(self.initial_side, n_dof, device, param_name="initial_side").clamp(
        min=-1.0,
        max=1.0,
    )

    self._backlash = self._backlash_row.unsqueeze(0).repeat(num_envs, 1)
    self._reversal_threshold = self._reversal_threshold_row.unsqueeze(0).repeat(num_envs, 1)
    self._takeup_rate = self._takeup_rate_row.unsqueeze(0).repeat(num_envs, 1)
    self._initial_side = self._initial_side_row.unsqueeze(0).repeat(num_envs, 1)
    self._backlash_side = self._initial_side.clone()
    self._prev_target = torch.zeros(num_envs, n_dof, device=device)
    self._initialized = torch.zeros(num_envs, n_dof, dtype=torch.bool, device=device)

modify_processed_action(processed_action: Tensor) -> Tensor
Source code in eden/managers/modifiers/actions/actuators.py 
def modify_processed_action(self, processed_action: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    first_update = ~self._initialized
    delta = processed_action - self._prev_target
    moving_positive = delta > self._reversal_threshold
    moving_negative = delta < -self._reversal_threshold
    requested_side = torch.where(
        moving_positive,
        torch.ones_like(self._backlash_side),
        torch.where(moving_negative, -torch.ones_like(self._backlash_side), self._backlash_side),
    )
    requested_side = torch.where(first_update, self._initial_side, requested_side)
    self._backlash_side += (requested_side - self._backlash_side) * self._takeup_rate
    self._prev_target[:] = processed_action
    self._initialized[:] = True
    return processed_action + self._backlash_side * self._backlash

Bases: ActionModifier

Clips target positions so PD torques stay within the motor torque-speed envelope.

Back-solves the motor torque-speed curve to find the range of target positions that yield feasible torques, then clips targets into that range. This ensures the PD controller never commands torques outside the motor's physical capability.

The torque-speed envelope is defined by four parameters::

    Torque, N·m
        ^
Y2──────|
        |──────────────Y1
        |              │\\
        |              │ \\
        |              │  \\
        |              |   \\
--------+--------------|------> velocity, rad/s
                      X1   X2

Given current joint state (q, dq) and PD gains (kp, kd), the modifier computes the maximum and minimum feasible torques from the T-N curve, then back-solves for the corresponding target position bounds::

target_low  = (tau_low  + kd * dq) / kp + q
target_high = (tau_high + kd * dq) / kp + q

By default, T-N curve parameters are read from the entity's actuator spec (dofs_spec). Explicit values override the entity defaults.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION driving_torque_limit

(Y1) Maximum torque when torque and velocity are in the same direction. None → read from entity spec.

TYPE: LaxFArrayType | None

braking_torque_limit

(Y2) Maximum torque when torque and velocity are in opposite directions. None → read from entity spec.

TYPE: LaxFArrayType | None

full_torque_speed

(X1) Speed below which full torque is available [rad/s]. None → read from entity spec.

TYPE: LaxFArrayType | None

no_load_speed

(X2) Speed at which available torque drops to zero [rad/s]. None → read from entity spec.

TYPE: LaxFArrayType | None

def build(self, num_envs: int, device: str, entity=None, dofs_idx_local=None) -> None:
    if entity is None:
        raise ValueError("EnvelopeClip requires entity to be passed in build().")
    self._entity = entity
    # The selector for the entity getters below: a `range` when the DOFs are contiguous, Genesis'
    # sync-free slice path — `modify_processed_action` reads the joint state every control step.
    self._dofs_idx_local = None if dofs_idx_local is None else as_genesis_index(dofs_idx_local)

    # Cache PD gains
    self._kp = entity.get_dofs_kp(dofs_idx_local=self._dofs_idx_local)
    self._kd = entity.get_dofs_kd(dofs_idx_local=self._dofs_idx_local)

    # T-N curve parameters — read from entity spec unless explicitly overridden
    def _resolve(param_value, spec_attr):
        return _get_param_tensor_from_entity(
            param_value,
            spec_attr=spec_attr,
            entity=entity,
            dofs_idx_local=dofs_idx_local,
            device=device,
        )

    self._motor_y1 = _resolve(self.driving_torque_limit, "driving_torque_limit")
    self._motor_y2 = _resolve(self.braking_torque_limit, "braking_torque_limit")
    self._motor_x1 = _resolve(self.full_torque_speed, "full_torque_speed")
    self._motor_x2 = _resolve(self.no_load_speed, "no_load_speed")

modify_processed_action(processed_action: Tensor) -> Tensor
Source code in eden/managers/modifiers/actions/actuators.py 
def modify_processed_action(self, processed_action: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    joint_pos = self._entity.get_dofs_pos(dofs_idx_local=self._dofs_idx_local)
    joint_vel = self._entity.get_dofs_vel(dofs_idx_local=self._dofs_idx_local)

    abs_dq = joint_vel.abs()
    over = torch.clamp(abs_dq - self._motor_x1, min=0.0)
    denom = torch.clamp(self._motor_x2 - self._motor_x1, min=CURVE_SPEED_DENOM_MIN)

    # Positive torque limit (tau_high >= 0)
    base_pos = torch.where(
        abs_dq <= MOTOR_STALL_VEL_THRESHOLD,
        self._motor_y2,
        torch.where(joint_vel >= 0.0, self._motor_y1, self._motor_y2),
    )
    tau_high = torch.clamp(base_pos - (base_pos / denom) * over, min=0.0)

    # Negative torque limit (tau_low <= 0)
    base_neg = torch.where(
        abs_dq <= MOTOR_STALL_VEL_THRESHOLD,
        -self._motor_y2,
        torch.where(joint_vel >= 0.0, -self._motor_y2, -self._motor_y1),
    )
    tau_low = torch.clamp(base_neg + (-base_neg / denom) * over, max=0.0)

    # Back-solve: tau = kp * (target - q) - kd * dq
    kd_dq = self._kd * joint_vel
    target_low = (tau_low + kd_dq) / self._kp + joint_pos
    target_high = (tau_high + kd_dq) / self._kp + joint_pos

    return torch.clip(processed_action, target_low, target_high)

def compute(self, data: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    # Generate uniform noise in [0, 1) and scale to [n_min, n_max).
    noise = torch.rand_like(data) * (self.n_max - self.n_min) + self.n_min
    match self.operation:
        case NoiseOperation.ADD:
            return data + noise
        case NoiseOperation.SCALE:
            return data * noise
        case _:
            return noise

docs.title: ExponentialMovingAverage
docs.text:
ExponentialMovingAverage(env: EnvBase, options: ObservationModifierOptions)

Bases: ObservationModifier

Exponential moving average, updated once per control step.

y(t) = alpha * x(t) + (1 - alpha) * y(t - 1).

alpha is the weight of the newest frame, as in pandas' ewm(alpha=...). Some filter libraries write the complement, so check that before porting a value. The term's frame must be floating-point — the weights are held in its dtype, so an integer one would truncate them to zero; :class:ObservationDelay is the modifier that carries any dtype.

A non-finite frame keeps its kind: an infinity entering the average stays an infinity, so a clip on the term still bounds it — a raycast's +inf for "no hit" reaches the policy as the clip's far end, not as a NaN that no clip bounds — and a NaN stays a NaN. Either one stays in the average until the env resets. The group's nan_policy checks the term's output after its modifiers, so it replaces what the policy receives but cannot clean the average itself. The one frame that still averages to NaN is a component that sees both +inf and -inf, their weighted sum being genuinely undefined.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION alpha

Weight of the newest frame, in (0, 1]. Required. alpha=1 passes each frame through unchanged; a smaller alpha smooths more.

TYPE: float

backfill

What the average starts from after a reset (default True). True: the first frame after the reset starts the average, so it is delivered unchanged, as if every earlier frame had equalled it. False: the average starts from zero, so the first frame delivers alpha * x.

TYPE: bool

Source code in eden/managers/modifiers/observations/temporal.py 
def __init__(self, env: EnvBase, options: ObservationModifierOptions):
    super().__init__(env=env, options=options)
    if self.alpha is None:
        raise ValueError("ExponentialMovingAverage: alpha is required (the weight of the newest frame, in (0, 1]).")
    if not 0.0 < self.alpha <= 1.0:
        raise ValueError(f"ExponentialMovingAverage: alpha must be in (0, 1], got {self.alpha}.")
    # The weight a row's first frame after a reset gets. With backfill it is 1, so that frame replaces
    # the zeroed average instead of being blended with it.
    self._first_frame_weight = 1.0 if self.backfill else self.alpha

docs.text:
build(frame: Tensor) -> None
Source code in eden/managers/modifiers/observations/temporal.py 
def build(self, frame: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    if not frame.is_floating_point():
        # The weights live in the frame's dtype, and ``torch.full(..., 0.2, dtype=torch.int64)`` is 0
        # without raising, so an integer frame would deliver zeros from its second frame on.
        raise ValueError(
            f"ExponentialMovingAverage: needs a floating-point frame, got {frame.dtype}. Average a float "
            f"term — a count, an index or a flag has no meaningful average — or drop the modifier. "
            f"ObservationDelay carries a frame of any dtype unchanged."
        )
    self._average = torch.zeros_like(frame)
    # One weight per env, broadcast over the feature dims: ``_first_frame_weight`` on a row whose
    # first frame since the reset is still to come, ``alpha`` once that frame has been advanced in.
    # ``_hold``, the weight of the stored average, is carried alongside rather than computed as
    # ``1 - _weight`` per read, so the pair is written together everywhere it changes.
    weight_shape = (frame.shape[0],) + (1,) * (frame.dim() - 1)
    self._weight = torch.full(weight_shape, self._first_frame_weight, dtype=frame.dtype, device=frame.device)
    self._hold = torch.full(weight_shape, 1.0 - self._first_frame_weight, dtype=frame.dtype, device=frame.device)

docs.text:
reset(envs_idx: Tensor | None = None) -> None
Source code in eden/managers/modifiers/observations/temporal.py 
def reset(self, envs_idx: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> None:
    if is_env_mask(envs_idx):
        # Auto-reset passes a mask every step; ``masked_fill_`` applies it on the device, as
        # ``CircularBuffer.reset`` does.
        rows = envs_idx.view(self._weight.shape)
        self._average.masked_fill_(rows, 0.0)
        self._weight.masked_fill_(rows, self._first_frame_weight)
        self._hold.masked_fill_(rows, 1.0 - self._first_frame_weight)
    else:
        rows = slice(None) if envs_idx is None else envs_idx
        self._average[rows] = 0.0
        self._weight[rows] = self._first_frame_weight
        self._hold[rows] = 1.0 - self._first_frame_weight

docs.title: compute
docs.text:
compute(frame: Tensor) -> Tensor
Source code in eden/managers/modifiers/observations/temporal.py 
def compute(self, frame: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    # ``(1 - w) * y + w * x``, written out rather than as ``torch.lerp(y, x, w)``: lerp evaluates
    # ``y + w * (x - y)`` (``x - (x - y) * (1 - w)`` for ``w >= 0.5``), so an infinite frame meets
    # ``inf - inf`` and comes out NaN — which ``clip`` passes through, since ``clamp`` does, and
    # which then reaches the policy. This form turns an infinity into an infinity, so the term's
    # clip still bounds it. Its one indeterminate product, ``(1 - w) * y``, needs ``y`` to be zero
    # wherever ``1 - w`` is; :meth:`advance` is what keeps that true.
    return torch.addcmul(self._hold * self._average, self._weight, frame)

docs.title: advance
docs.text:
advance(frame: Tensor) -> None
Source code in eden/managers/modifiers/observations/temporal.py 
def advance(self, frame: torch.Tensor) -> None:
    if self.alpha < 1.0:
        self._average.copy_(self.compute(frame))
    # ``alpha == 1`` is pass-through: ``_hold`` is zero everywhere and the average is never read
    # again, so it is left zeroed rather than written. Storing an infinite frame in it would make
    # the next ``(1 - w) * y`` a ``0 * inf``, and so a NaN, for a modifier that changes nothing.
    self._weight.fill_(self.alpha)
    self._hold.fill_(1.0 - self.alpha)

Delivers the frame the term produced control_steps control steps earlier.

The delay is counted in pushes of the observation window (see :class:~eden.managers.modifiers.base.ObservationModifier), which happen once per control step. That is the same clock as history_length, so a delayed term with a history window holds the delayed frames.

TYPE: int

backfill

def build(self, frame: torch.Tensor) -> None:

    # delayed frame. ``CircularBuffer`` owns backfill, per-row reset and the read without an append.

docs.title: ScaledCommands
docs.text:
ScaledCommands(env: EnvBase, options: ObservationTermOptions)

Bases: ObservationTerm

Command vector multiplied by a per-component scale; prefer the built-in scale=[...] modifier.

For plain per-component scaling prefer the built-in scale=[...] post-compute modifier (ObsTerm.configure(func=..., scale=[2.0, 1.0])). command_scale is the per-component multiplier (named to avoid colliding with the inherited post-compute scale modifier). Both the command ref and the scale tensor are resolved once in :meth:build.

The swap is exact only when the term configures no noise and no clip. This class scales inside compute(), so the manager's noise and clip see the scaled command; the scale modifier is applied after both (compute_group runs noise -> clip -> scale). So migrating a term that also sets noise divides the effective noise std by the per-component factor, and one that sets clip reinterprets the bounds from scaled units into raw ones. Rescale those two alongside the swap, or keep this class.

docs.title: VelocityTrackingErrorIntegral
docs.text:
VelocityTrackingErrorIntegral(env: EnvBase, options: ObservationTermOptions)

Bases: ObservationTerm

Running integral of the base-velocity tracking error (N, 3).

The worked example of a stateful observation term.

∫ (commanded − measured) dt over [vx, vy, wz] in the base frame, against a velocity command laid out [vx, vy, wz] (:class:~eden.managers.terms.commands.velocity.UniformVelocityCommand). Zero at reset, exactly k increments after k control steps, and clamped per component to ±max_abs so a persistent error (a robot that cannot reach the commanded speed) saturates the feature instead of growing without bound — the anti-windup clamp of a PI controller.

This term exists as much to be copied as to be used. It is the reference for per-step state on an observation term, which the manager's compute() cannot hold because that call is a read and runs several times a step (:class:~eden.managers.observation_manager.ObservationTerm):

  • :meth:build resolves the command (a bad name raises at env construction), touches the entity, and allocates the buffer — outside any inference-mode region, so every hook may write it.
  • :meth:post_physics_refresh is the once-per-step tick: it reads the post-physics robot and adds the increment in place. It runs at phase 7 — after the command caches and metrics, above the graded layer and the auto-reset — so the final-observation snapshot carries this step's increment and reset() zeroes it for the envs that restart before their first fresh observation. The deploy loop ticks it once per control tick.
  • :meth:reset zeroes the rows of the restarting envs.
  • :meth:compute returns the buffer, live — like a metric buffer, not a copy; the manager's snapshot paths copy what they keep. Nothing else.

The entity is resolved in the hook, not cached in build — the deployment swaps env.entities[name] for a RobotStateEntity and a cached handle would keep integrating the simulated robot on hardware. self._env.dt is the control dt, so the integral is in m / rad regardless of decimation.

def build(self) -> None:
    # ``getattr``: a plain ``EnvBase`` has no command manager attribute at all, and that is the
    # same misconfiguration as an RL env with none — one message for both.
    command_manager = getattr(self._env, "command_manager", None)
    if command_manager is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)} requires a command manager with a '{self.command_name}' term.")
    # ``get_term`` raises naming the available commands; touching the entity does the same for
    # ``entity_name``. Both fail here, at env construction, rather than on the first tick.
    self._command = command_manager.get_term(self.command_name)
    self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)
    # The command buffer exists at build (the command manager is constructed first), so its width
    # is checked here: a narrower command would otherwise fail on the first tick as a broadcasting
    # error in ``post_physics_refresh``, not at env construction.
    command_dim = self._command.command.shape[-1]
    if command_dim < 3:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)}: command '{self.command_name}' publishes {command_dim} component(s); this term "
            f"integrates the first three as [vx, vy, wz] and needs at least 3 (UniformVelocityCommand's layout)."
        )
    if self.max_abs <= 0.0:
        raise ValueError(f"{term_subject(self)}: max_abs must be positive, got {self.max_abs}.")
    self._integral = torch.zeros(self.num_envs, 3, device=self.device)

def post_physics_refresh(self) -> None:
    entity = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)
    measured = torch.cat([entity.get_vel(frame="body")[:, :2], entity.get_ang(frame="body")[:, 2:3]], dim=-1)
    # In place: the buffer was allocated in build(), and this may run under inference mode.
    self._integral.add_((self._command.command[:, :3] - measured) * self._env.dt).clamp_(
        -self.max_abs, self.max_abs
    )

def build(self) -> None:
    # Cache only grid buffers; resolve entities lazily in compute() (see ManagerTermBase.resolve_entity).
    entity = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)
    if entity.has_immobile_base:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{term_subject(self)} needs an entity whose base moves through the world; "
            f"it has an immobile base (fixed, or welded onto another entity)."
        )
    _ = self.resolve_entity(self.terrain_entity_name)  # fail fast if the terrain entity is missing
    self._grid_buffer = torch.zeros(
        (
            self._env.num_envs,
            len(self.measured_points_x),
            len(self.measured_points_y),
            3,
        ),
        device=gs.device,
        dtype=gs.tc_float,
    )
    measured_points_x = torch.tensor(self.measured_points_x, device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)
    measured_points_y = torch.tensor(self.measured_points_y, device=gs.device, dtype=gs.tc_float)
    grid_x, grid_y = torch.meshgrid(measured_points_x, measured_points_y, indexing="ij")
    self._grid_buffer[..., 0] = grid_x
    self._grid_buffer[..., 1] = grid_y
    self.num_measured_points = grid_x.numel()
    self.num_measured_points_x = len(self.measured_points_x)
    self.num_measured_points_y = len(self.measured_points_y)
    self.grid = torch.zeros(
        (
            self._env.num_envs,
            len(self.measured_points_x),
            len(self.measured_points_y),
            2,
        ),
        device=gs.device,
        dtype=gs.tc_float,
    )

docs.title: compute
docs.text:
compute(*args, **kwargs)
Source code in eden/managers/terms/observations/locomotion.py 
def compute(self, *args, **kwargs):
    base_pose = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name).get_qpos(slice(0, 7))
    self.grid = transform_by_quat_yaw_approx(
        self._grid_buffer.view(-1, 3),
        base_pose[:, 3:7].view(-1, 4).repeat_interleave(self.num_measured_points, dim=0),
    ).view(-1, self.num_measured_points_x, self.num_measured_points_y, 3)[..., :2]
    self.grid += base_pose[:, :2].view(-1, 1, 1, 2)
    scan_dots = self.resolve_entity(self.terrain_entity_name).get_height(self.grid)  # B, h_out, w_out

    if self.offset_from_base:
        scan_dots -= base_pose[:, 2].view(-1, 1, 1)
        min_clamp, max_clamp = self.clamp_offset_range
        scan_dots = torch.nan_to_num(scan_dots, nan=0.0, posinf=max_clamp, neginf=min_clamp).clamp(
            min=min_clamp, max=max_clamp
        )

    if self.flatten_measured_points:
        return scan_dots.view(-1, self.num_measured_points)
    else:
        return scan_dots

@OBSERVATION_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def base_height(
    env: EnvBase,
    *,
    entity_name: str = "robot",
    terrain_entity_name: str | None = None,
    relative: bool = False,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Height of the entity's base above the ground, shape ``(num_envs, 1)``.

    The locomotion counterpart of Isaac Lab's ``base_pos_z``, and the observation half of
    :func:`~eden.managers.terms.terminations.locomotion.root_height_below_minimum` — the two read the
    same :func:`~eden.managers.terms.utils.base_height_above_ground` helper, so an observation and a
    termination configured alike cannot disagree about what "height" means.

    Parameters
    ----------
    env : EnvBase
        The environment instance.
    entity_name : str, optional
        Entity whose base height is reported. Defaults to ``"robot"``.
    terrain_entity_name : str | None, optional
        Terrain entity to measure *against*. ``None`` (the default) reports the world-frame ``z``,
        which is the height above the ground only on flat terrain; naming a
        :class:`~eden.entities.terrain.Terrain` subtracts the terrain height under the base's ``xy``
        so the feature means the same thing everywhere on a heightfield.
    relative : bool, optional
        Frame the base pose is read in — see
        :func:`~eden.managers.terms.observations.proprio.base_pos`. Defaults to ``False`` (the solver
        frame), matching the other base-pose observations and
        :func:`~eden.managers.terms.rewards.locomotion.base_height_l2`.
    """
    terrain = resolve_terrain(env.entities, terrain_entity_name)
    height = base_height_above_ground(resolve_named_entity(env.entities, entity_name), terrain, relative=relative)
    return height.unsqueeze(-1)

MetricObservation(env: EnvBase, options: ObservationTermOptions)

Bases: ObservationTerm

Expose a :class:~eden.managers.metric_manager.MetricTerm's cached value as a (num_envs, 1) observation.

Pulls the per-env value the metric manager computed this step (metric_manager runs before the observation manager in env.step()). Same rationale as metric_reward: compute a shared quantity once as a metric and read it here by name rather than recomputing it or stashing it on env. The standard obs modifiers (scale/clip/noise/ history) still apply. Observations are computed after env resets, so an environment that reset this step reads the metric's post-reset value (0 until its next compute), consistent with Eden's post-reset observation convention.

A missing metric manager or an unset or unknown metric_name (the error lists the active metrics) raises in :meth:build, i.e. at env construction. :meth:compute is a pure read of the manager-owned buffer, so the extra calls an observation term receives (build-time shape probe, reset(), the final-observation snapshot) are harmless.

@OBSERVATION_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def episode_phase(
    env: RLEnvBase,
    *,
    centered: bool = False,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Return normalized episode time as a ``(num_envs, 1)`` tensor.

    ``centered=False`` (default): ``t / max_episode_length`` in ``[0, 1]``.
    ``centered=True``: ``2 * t / max_episode_length - 1`` in ``[-1, 1]``.
    """
    phase = env.episode_length_buf.float() / env.max_episode_length
    if centered:
        phase = 2.0 * phase - 1.0
    return phase.unsqueeze(-1)

docs.title: Privileged dynamics
docs.text:
Per-env domain-randomized quantities (gain and motor-strength scales, added mass, foot friction, CoM offset) for a critic or a teacher policy.

Privileged observation terms exposing per-env domain-randomized dynamics.

These read the realized randomized physical parameters relative to their nominal defaults, so an asymmetric (privileged) critic can condition on the domain randomization the actor cannot observe — the standard sim-to-real privileged-critic technique. The actor sees only proprioception; the critic additionally sees terms like these.

Each term reads back exactly one domain_rand event:

=========================== ======================================================================= term event it reads back =========================== ======================================================================= :class:GainScale :class:~eden.managers.terms.events.domain_rand.RandomizeKpKdGains :class:MotorStrengthScale :class:~eden.managers.terms.events.domain_rand.RandomizeMotorStrength :class:AddedMass :class:~eden.managers.terms.events.domain_rand.RandomizeMassShift :class:FootFriction :class:~eden.managers.terms.events.domain_rand.RandomizeFrictionRatio :class:ComOffset :class:~eden.managers.terms.events.domain_rand.RandomizeComShift =========================== =======================================================================

Convention: the shift/deviation terms are 0 at nominal (GainScale, MotorStrengthScale, AddedMass, ComOffset); FootFriction is a ratio, 1.0 at nominal.

Inspired by TWIST2's critic_extras (critic_motor_scales / critic_added_mass / critic_foot_friction / critic_base_com_offset).

docs.title: GainScale
docs.text:
GainScale(env: EnvBase, options: ObservationTermOptions)

Bases: ObservationTerm

Per-DOF relative deviation of the realized PD gains from their defaults.

Returns concat([kp/kp0 - 1, kd/kd0 - 1]) over the entity's actuated DOFs (in dofs_name order); 0 means nominal, so it is all zeros when there is no gain randomization. Pairs with :class:~eden.managers.terms.events.domain_rand.RandomizeKpKdGains. Output shape (num_envs, 2 * num_dofs).

Notes

Reads the gains held on the entity (get_dofs_kp / get_dofs_kd), so it only reflects gain randomization written to the entity — i.e. RandomizeKpKdGains with action_term_name=None (the default, Genesis built-in PD path). RandomizeKpKdGains with action_term_name set writes the PD-controller's _kp / _kd caches instead and never touches the entity, so this term would read all zeros; :meth:build raises if such an event targets the same entity. (The controller mirrors the entity gains into its caches on every action reset, but that mirror is one-way entity→controller, so it does not carry controller-side randomization back to the entity.) Per-env gains require batch_dofs_info=True in env_options; otherwise the gains are shared across envs and the term is uniformly zero (still valid, just uninformative).

This is the gain deviation, distinct from :class:MotorStrengthScale (the actuator torque-scale modifier).

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION entity_name

Name of the articulated entity whose actuator gains to read.

def build(self) -> None:
    entity = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)
    # Baselines are build-time constants (the nominal per-DOF gains). Cache
    # them plus the derived zero-masks / safe denominators so compute() does
    # no per-step allocation. Clone so the cache never aliases
    # ``default_dofs_kp`` (``as_tensor`` returns the same tensor when it is
    # already float32 on-device).
    self._kp0 = self._ensure_2d(entity.default_dofs_kp).clone()
    self._kd0 = self._ensure_2d(entity.default_dofs_kd).clone()
    self._kp_zero, self._kp_safe = self._zero_mask_and_safe(self._kp0)
    self._kd_zero, self._kd_safe = self._zero_mask_and_safe(self._kd0)
    self._guard_conflicting_gain_events()
    self._warn_zero_baseline_dofs(entity)

def compute(self) -> torch.Tensor:
    entity = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)
    # The getters already reach the full env count, which fixes the output shape; the
    # ``(1, ndof)`` denominators then broadcast against them.
    kp = entity.get_dofs_kp()
    kd = entity.get_dofs_kd()
    dev = torch.cat(
        [self._rel_dev(kp, self._kp_zero, self._kp_safe), self._rel_dev(kd, self._kd_zero, self._kd_safe)],
        dim=-1,
    )
    return dev.float()

Express a batch of wxyz quaternions (N, 4) in rotation format.

euler_xyz is extrinsic roll/pitch/yaw (scipy "xyz"), axis_angle a rotation vector, rot6d the first two rows of the rotation matrix (Zhou et al.).

def rotation_as(quat_wxyz: torch.Tensor, rotation: RotationFormat) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Express a batch of wxyz quaternions ``(N, 4)`` in ``rotation`` format.

    ``euler_xyz`` is extrinsic roll/pitch/yaw (scipy ``"xyz"``), ``axis_angle`` a rotation
    vector, ``rot6d`` the first two rows of the rotation matrix (Zhou et al.).
    """
    if rotation == "quat":
        return quat_wxyz
    if rotation == "euler_xyz":
        roll, pitch, yaw = euler_xyz_from_quat(quat_wxyz)
        return torch.stack([roll, pitch, yaw], dim=-1)
    if rotation == "axis_angle":
        return axis_angle_from_quat(quat_wxyz)
    if rotation == "rot6d":
        return R_to_rot6d(quat_to_R(quat_wxyz))
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown rotation format {rotation!r}; expected quat, euler_xyz, axis_angle or rot6d.")

(pos (N, 3), quat_wxyz (N, 4)) of one link, optionally re-expressed and corrected.

offset_pos / offset_quat (1, 3) / (1, 4) place a virtual tool frame on the link (RobotArena's ee_gripper_link sits 9.36 cm ahead of WidowX's gripper_link). frame="base" expresses the result in the entity's base frame. correction_quat (1, 4) is a fixed rotation right-multiplied onto the orientation (R_out = R @ R_corr), as the DROID rot6d convention or a hardware tool-frame yaw offset require.

def end_effector_pose(
    entity,
    link_idx: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    frame: Literal["base", "world"] = "base",
    offset_pos: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    offset_quat: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    correction_quat: torch.Tensor | None = None,
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """``(pos (N, 3), quat_wxyz (N, 4))`` of one link, optionally re-expressed and corrected.

    ``offset_pos`` / ``offset_quat`` ``(1, 3)`` / ``(1, 4)`` place a virtual tool frame on
    the link (RobotArena's ``ee_gripper_link`` sits 9.36 cm ahead of WidowX's
    ``gripper_link``). ``frame="base"`` expresses the result in the entity's base frame.
    ``correction_quat`` ``(1, 4)`` is a fixed rotation right-multiplied onto the
    orientation (``R_out = R @ R_corr``), as the DROID rot6d convention or a hardware
    tool-frame yaw offset require.
    """
    pos_w = entity.get_links_pos(ls_idx_local=link_idx)[:, 0, :]
    quat_w = entity.get_links_quat(ls_idx_local=link_idx)[:, 0, :]
    if offset_pos is not None or offset_quat is not None:
        pos_w, quat_w = combine_frame_transforms(pos_w, quat_w, offset_pos, offset_quat)
    if frame == "base":
        pos, quat = subtract_frame_transforms(entity.get_pos(), entity.get_quat(), pos_w, quat_w)
    elif frame == "world":
        pos, quat = pos_w, quat_w
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid frame {frame!r}. Expected 'base' or 'world'.")
    if correction_quat is not None:
        quat = quat_mul(quat, correction_quat.expand_as(quat))
    return pos, quat

gripper_state(dofs_pos: Tensor, *, normalize: GripperNormalize = 'raw', open_pos: float | None = None, close_pos: float | None = None, scale: float = 1.0) -> Tensor

Map gripper DOF positions (N, k) to raw (scaled) values, openness or closedness.

closedness = (pos - open_pos) / (close_pos - open_pos) and openness = 1 - closedness, so a WidowX finger (open at 0.037, closed at 0) and a Robotiq driver (open at 0, closed at 0.8) both read 0 = open, 1 = closed for closedness without per-robot special cases.

Source code in eden/managers/terms/observations/manipulation.py 
def gripper_state(
    dofs_pos: torch.Tensor,
    *,
    normalize: GripperNormalize = "raw",
    open_pos: float | None = None,
    close_pos: float | None = None,
    scale: float = 1.0,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Map gripper DOF positions ``(N, k)`` to raw (scaled) values, openness or closedness.

    ``closedness = (pos - open_pos) / (close_pos - open_pos)`` and
    ``openness = 1 - closedness``, so a WidowX finger (open at 0.037, closed at 0) and a
    Robotiq driver (open at 0, closed at 0.8) both read 0 = open, 1 = closed for
    ``closedness`` without per-robot special cases.
    """
    if normalize == "raw":
        return dofs_pos * scale
    if open_pos is None or close_pos is None or open_pos == close_pos:
        raise ValueError(
            f"normalize={normalize!r} needs distinct open_pos and close_pos, got open_pos={open_pos}, close_pos={close_pos}."
        )
    closedness = (dofs_pos - open_pos) / (close_pos - open_pos)
    if normalize == "closedness":
        return closedness
    if normalize == "openness":
        return 1.0 - closedness
    raise ValueError(f"Unknown gripper normalize {normalize!r}; expected raw, openness or closedness.")

Per-link contact-force-norm observation.

Reads :meth:RigidEntity.get_links_net_contact_force (Genesis-aggregated per-link net force; (num_envs, n_links, 3) in world frame), slices to the configured link set, and returns the per-link force magnitude.

Trade-off vs. gs.sensors.ContactForce: the Genesis sensor binds to one link per SensorOptions declaration, so a 14-link hand needs 14 sensor entries plus 14 obs-term entries to do what :class:ContactForceNorm does in a single declaration. The cost is no NoisySensorMixin noise / delay / decimation modeling; that path is reachable via the :class:~eden.managers.terms.observations.sensors.SensorRead term plus a per-link sensor declaration if a config wants noise on a small subset of links.

ContactForceNorm(env: EnvBase, options: ObservationTermOptions)

Bases: ObservationTerm

Per-link contact-force magnitude (Euclidean, world frame).

Returns (num_envs, K) where K = len(matched links), each entry being ‖f_link‖ at the most recent scene.step().

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION entity_name

Entity to read forces from (must be a RigidEntity).

links_name

:func:resolve_matching_names-compatible patterns selecting which links contribute. Empty list raises in :meth:build — this term is per-link by design; use :func:self_collision_cost for a global "any contact" scalar.

Notes

Output scaling, noise, clipping, and history are controlled via the inherited :class:ObservationTermOptions fields (scale, noise, clip, history_length) — pass e.g. scale=0.01 on the term options when forces are in newtons and the policy expects roughly-unit observations.

The underlying force is in world frame — Genesis's get_links_net_contact_force returns the world-frame net force per link. gs.sensors.ContactForce (the noise-aware path reachable via the generic :class:~eden.managers.terms.observations.sensors.SensorRead obs term) returns the same vector in the link's local frame. Magnitudes are equal under any choice of frame, so this term's per-link norm is unaffected by the choice; a config swapping between this term and a sensor-reading-plus-norm composition gets identical scalar values but watch the frame if a downstream consumer uses the raw force vector.

def compute(self) -> torch.Tensor:
    contacts = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name).get_grouped_contacts(
        self.resolve_entity(self.object_entity_name),
        links_a_idx_local=self._links_idx,
        links_b_idx_local=self._object_links_idx,

def build(self) -> None:
    all_sensor_names = list(self._env.sensors.keys())

    else:
        _, matched_sensor_names = resolve_matching_names(

def compute(self, *args, **kwargs) -> torch.Tensor:
    sensor_readings = []
    for sensor in self._sensors:
        data = sensor.read_ground_truth() if self.read_ground_truth else sensor.read()
        if self.post_process_func is not None:
            data = self.post_process_func(data)
        if not isinstance(data, tuple):
            data = (data,)

        for tensor in data:
            if tensor.ndim > 2:
                tensor = tensor.flatten(start_dim=1)
            sensor_readings.append(tensor.float())

    self._cached = torch.cat(sensor_readings, dim=-1)
    return self._cached

For feeding a CNN policy (rsl_rl's ActorCriticCNN expects float (N, C, H, W)), set normalize=True (uint8 -> float in [0, 1]) and channels_first=True. @OBSERVATION_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def rgb_image(
    env: RLEnvBase,
    *,
    camera_name: str,
    normalize: bool = False,
    channels_first: bool = False,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """RGB image from a camera, optionally CNN-ready.

    By default returns the renderer's native output (``(N, H, W, C)``, uint8).
    For feeding a CNN policy (rsl_rl's ``ActorCriticCNN`` expects float
    ``(N, C, H, W)``), set ``normalize=True`` (uint8 -> float in [0, 1]) and
    ``channels_first=True``. Either flag also drops an alpha channel (the
    madrona batch renderer returns RGBA).
    """
    rgb = env.cameras[camera_name].render_rgb()
    if normalize or channels_first:
        rgb = rgb[..., :3]
    if normalize:
        rgb = rgb.float() / 255.0 if rgb.dtype == torch.uint8 else rgb.float()
    if channels_first:
        rgb = rgb.permute(0, 3, 1, 2).contiguous()
    return rgb

docs.title: Motion tracking
docs.text:
Terms that expose env.motion_manager reference state on a MimicRLEnvBase.

Observation terms exposing motion-reference state to the policy.

Reads env.motion_manager.data[entity_name] (filled per step at the start of MimicRLEnvBase.step() and refilled per env on reset) — NOT reference_frame, which would force a recompute pass and a GPU sync.

Current vs future frames

The motion-reference buffer is shaped (num_envs, num_frames, ...) where num_frames comes from :attr:MotionManagerOptions.num_frames. Terms in this module split into two families:

  • Current-frame terms (motion_base_*_w, motion_dofs_*, motion_links_*_b) index [:, 0, ...]. With the default data_start_from="one_frame_interval" frame 0 is one tick ahead; with data_start_from="current_time" frame 0 is the current step.
  • Future-frame terms (motion_future_*) index a caller-supplied frame_offsets tuple into the same buffer. They are intended for policies that consume a short lookahead (e.g. ProtoMotions' (1, 2, 4, 8)-step target poses on top of the current frame). The caller must size num_frames to cover max(frame_offsets) + 1; the term raises a clear error on the first call otherwise.
Shape convention
  • Single-target terms (motion_base_*_w, motion_dofs_*) return (num_envs, F).
  • Multi-link terms (motion_links_*) return (num_envs, K*F) by default — flat, so they slot into rank-2 obs concat groups (the common case for MLP policies) without the caller having to pass flatten=True every time. Pass flatten=False to keep the link axis as a separate (num_envs, K, F) dimension for structured policies (transformer / per-link MLP).
  • Future-frame terms add a leading K = len(frame_offsets) axis: (num_envs, K*D) flat / (num_envs, K, D) unflattened for DOF terms; (num_envs, K*L*F) / (num_envs, K, L, F) for link terms.

Each term calls :func:assert_motion_field_present for the field(s) it actually reads, so a dataset that doesn't supply the required field (e.g. a fixed-base motion sequence with no base_pos_w, or a hand sequence with no links_quat_w) fails fast on first read instead of silently feeding the MotionReferenceData.make_empty default (zeros / identity quat) to the policy. Position-only and orientation-only terms intentionally assert only on the field they consume — a dataset with only positions can still feed motion_links_pos_w / motion_links_pos_b.

    reproduces the original anchor-vs-anchor numerics and the

    anchor_robot_idx = get_robot_link_idx(env, entity_name, [anchor_link_name])
    motion_idx = get_motion_link_idx(env, entity_name, links_name)

    entity = env.get_entity(entity_name)
    anchor_pos = entity.get_links_pos(ls_idx_local=anchor_robot_idx)[:, 0]  # (N, 3)
    anchor_quat = entity.get_links_quat(ls_idx_local=anchor_robot_idx)[:, 0]  # (N, 4)

    ref = env.motion_manager.data[entity_name]
    motion_pos = current_motion_frame(ref.links_pos_w, motion_idx)  # (N, L, 3)

    pos_b = links_pos_in_anchor_frame(anchor_pos, anchor_quat, motion_pos)  # (N, L, 3)
    return _maybe_flatten(pos_b, flatten)

@OBSERVATION_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def motion_future_dofs_pos(
    env: MimicRLEnvBase,
    *,
    entity_name: str,
    frame_offsets: Sequence[int],
    dofs_name: list[str] | None = None,
    flatten: bool = True,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Return motion-ref qpos at multiple future buffer frames.

    Shape ``(N, K*D)`` (or ``(N, K, D)`` if ``flatten=False``).

    ``frame_offsets`` are interpreted as **buffer indices** into
    ``env.motion_manager.data[entity_name].dofs_pos`` (shape ``(N, F, D)``).
    With ``data_start_from="current_time"`` offset 0 is the current step
    and ``(1, 2, 4, 8)`` are 1/2/4/8 buffer ticks ahead; with the default
    ``data_start_from="one_frame_interval"`` offset 0 is already one tick
    ahead. The per-tick wall-clock duration is
    :attr:`MotionManagerOptions.frame_interval_s_range`.

    ``dofs_name=None`` returns every motion-ref DOF for the entity.

    assert_motion_field_present(env, entity_name, "dofs_pos")
    ref = env.motion_manager.data[entity_name]
    offsets = resolve_frame_offsets(env, "dofs_pos", frame_offsets, ref.dofs_pos.shape[1])
    sel = None if dofs_name is None else get_motion_dofs_idx(env, entity_name, dofs_name)
    future = select_motion_frames(ref.dofs_pos, offsets, sel)  # (N, K, D)
    return _maybe_flatten(future, flatten)

motion_future_links_ori_b(env: MimicRLEnvBase, *, entity_name: str, links_name: list[str], anchor_link_name: str, frame_offsets: Sequence[int], representation: Literal['rot6d', 'tan_norm'] = 'rot6d', flatten: bool = True) -> Tensor

Return future-frame motion-ref link orientations in the robot's current anchor frame.

Shape (N, K*L*6) (or (N, K, L, 6) if flatten=False).

The relative rotation is R_rel = R_robot_anchor⁻¹ · R_motion_future — i.e. the motion future orientation is brought into the robot's current anchor frame, matching the ProtoMotions reduced-coords target pose formulation. Two output representations:

  • representation="rot6d": 2-column rotation matrix [R_rel·x̂, R_rel·ŷ] (Zhou et al. 2019). Same convention as :func:motion_links_ori_b, so a config can swap the current-frame and future-frame variants without retraining the head.
  • representation="tan_norm": ProtoMotions quat_to_tan_norm output [R_rel·x̂, R_rel·ẑ]. Use this when feeding a checkpoint trained against ProtoMotions' target-poses obs (e.g. the g1-bones-deploy actor).

Set links_name=[anchor_link_name] to reproduce the ProtoMotions "anchor-relative anchor future rotation" channel (single link, K futures).

@OBSERVATION_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def motion_future_links_ori_b(
    env: MimicRLEnvBase,
    *,
    entity_name: str,
    links_name: list[str],
    anchor_link_name: str,
    frame_offsets: Sequence[int],
    representation: Literal["rot6d", "tan_norm"] = "rot6d",
    flatten: bool = True,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Return future-frame motion-ref link orientations in the robot's current anchor frame.

    Shape ``(N, K*L*6)`` (or ``(N, K, L, 6)`` if ``flatten=False``).

    The relative rotation is ``R_rel = R_robot_anchor⁻¹ · R_motion_future``
    — i.e. the motion future orientation is brought into the robot's
    *current* anchor frame, matching the ProtoMotions reduced-coords target
    pose formulation. Two output representations:

    * ``representation="rot6d"``: 2-column rotation matrix
      ``[R_rel·x̂, R_rel·ŷ]`` (Zhou et al. 2019). Same convention as
      :func:`motion_links_ori_b`, so a config can swap the current-frame
      and future-frame variants without retraining the head.
    * ``representation="tan_norm"``: ProtoMotions ``quat_to_tan_norm``
      output ``[R_rel·x̂, R_rel·ẑ]``. Use this when feeding a checkpoint
      trained against ProtoMotions' target-poses obs (e.g. the
      ``g1-bones-deploy`` actor).

    Set ``links_name=[anchor_link_name]`` to reproduce the ProtoMotions
    "anchor-relative anchor future rotation" channel (single link, K
    futures).
    """
    assert_motion_field_present(env, entity_name, "links_quat_w")

    ref = env.motion_manager.data[entity_name]
    offsets = resolve_frame_offsets(env, "links_quat_w", frame_offsets, ref.links_quat_w.shape[1])
    motion_idx = get_motion_link_idx(env, entity_name, links_name)
    anchor_robot_idx = get_robot_link_idx(env, entity_name, [anchor_link_name])

    # (N, K, L_all, 4) → (N, K, L, 4): pick K frames, then L motion links.
    motion_future_quat = select_motion_frames(ref.links_quat_w, offsets, motion_idx)

    entity = env.get_entity(entity_name)
    # Robot anchor quat is read at the current sim step (no future axis on the
    # robot side; only the motion ref looks ahead).
    anchor_quat = entity.get_links_quat(ls_idx_local=anchor_robot_idx)[:, 0]  # (N, 4)

    # Robot anchor has no future axis; broadcast it over the K motion futures so
    # (N, K) is the batch and L the link axis for the shared transform.
    K = offsets.shape[0]
    anchor_quat_k = anchor_quat[:, None, :].expand(-1, K, -1)  # (N, K, 4)
    quat_b = links_quat_in_anchor_frame(anchor_quat_k, motion_future_quat)  # (N, K, L, 4)
    return _maybe_flatten(_orientation_6d(quat_b, representation), flatten)  # (N, K, L, 6)

@OBSERVATION_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def entity_base_pos_b(
    env: MimicRLEnvBase,
    *,
    entity_name: str,
    anchor_entity_name: str,
    anchor_link_name: str,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Live base position of ``entity_name`` in another entity's live anchor-link frame. Shape ``(N, 3)``.

    The simulated counterpart of :func:`motion_future_base_pos_b` — e.g. where the object is relative to the
    humanoid's pelvis. Reads ``get_pos()``, the entity's solver root frame: for a free rigid object that is its
    centre of mass unless the object is built with ``align=False`` (then the authored body frame, the frame a
    reference object pose is recorded in).

def record_post_step(self) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    out: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
    if self.include_reward and hasattr(self._env, "reward_buf"):
        out["reward"] = self._env.reward_buf.unsqueeze(-1)
    if self.include_done and hasattr(self._env, "reset_buf"):
        out["done"] = self._env.reset_buf.to(dtype=torch.bool).unsqueeze(-1)
    if self.include_terminated and hasattr(self._env, "reset_terminated"):
        out["terminated"] = self._env.reset_terminated.to(dtype=torch.bool).unsqueeze(-1)
    if self.include_timeout and hasattr(self._env, "reset_timeouts"):
        out["timeout"] = self._env.reset_timeouts.to(dtype=torch.bool).unsqueeze(-1)
    if self.include_timestamp and hasattr(self._env, "episode_length_buf") and hasattr(self._env, "dt"):
        out["timestamp"] = self._env.episode_length_buf.to(dtype=torch.float32).unsqueeze(-1) * float(self._env.dt)
    return out

def record_post_reset(self, envs_idx=None) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor | dict]:
    if not self._env.entities:
        return {}

    entities_state: dict[str, dict[str, torch.Tensor]] = {}
    for entity_name, entity in self._env.entities.items():
        entity_state: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}

        if self.include_qpos:
            entity_state["qpos"] = entity.get_qpos(qs_idx_local=entity.qs_idx_local, envs_idx=envs_idx).clone()
        if self.include_dofs_vel:
            entity_state["dofs_vel"] = entity.get_dofs_vel(envs_idx=envs_idx).clone()
        if self.include_pos_quat:
            entity_state["pos"] = entity.get_pos(envs_idx=envs_idx).clone()
            entity_state["quat"] = entity.get_quat(envs_idx=envs_idx).clone()

        if entity_state:
            entities_state[entity_name] = entity_state

    if not entities_state:
        return {}

    return {"initial_state": {"entities": entities_state}}

def compute(self, envs_idx: torch.Tensor | None = None) -> torch.Tensor:
    entity = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)

def build(self) -> None:
    # The action manager is built before the reward manager (``EnvBase._manager_order``), so
    # both the handle and the action width are known here: an unknown ``action_term_name``
    # raises at env construction, and the buffer is sized once against the real shape instead
    # of on the first ``compute()``.
    _, prev_action = self._action_and_prev()
    # ``inference_mode(False)`` states the invariant rather than inheriting it from whoever
    # called ``env.build()``: the buffer must be a *normal* tensor, because ``compute()`` runs
    # under ``RewardManager.compute``'s ``torch.inference_mode`` while ``reset()`` may be
    # called outside it (`eden smoke`'s plain step loop), and mutating an inference tensor
    # from a normal path raises.
    with torch.inference_mode(False):
        self._prev_prev_action: torch.Tensor = torch.zeros_like(prev_action)

def compute(self) -> torch.Tensor:
    action, prev_action = self._action_and_prev()
    out = _compute_action_rate_l2_smooth(action, prev_action, self._prev_prev_action)
    # This step's ``prev_action`` is two-steps-old next step.
    self._prev_prev_action.copy_(prev_action)
    return out

docs.text:
MetricReward(env: EnvBase, options: _TermOptionsT)

Bases: RewardTerm

Use a :class:~eden.managers.metric_manager.MetricTerm's cached value as the reward.

Reads the per-env value the metric manager already computed this step (metric_manager runs before the reward manager in env.step()), so a quantity shared across reward / observation / termination terms is computed once as a metric and pulled here by name — instead of being recomputed in every term or stashed on the env object. The configured reward weight scales it as usual (use a negative weight for a penalty).

Rejects a cumulative metric by default: its value is the running episode sum, so using it directly as a per-step reward re-integrates that sum and balloons over the episode — almost never intended. Pass allow_cumulative=True to opt in if you really want the running sum as the reward.

A missing metric manager, an unset or unknown metric_name (the error lists the active metrics) and a rejected cumulative metric all raise in :meth:build, i.e. at env construction.

docs.title: VariablePosture
docs.text:
VariablePosture(env: EnvBase, options: _TermOptionsT)

Bases: RewardTerm

Speed-dependent posture reward.

Uses per-joint standard deviations to control how much each joint can deviate from default pose. The reward is exp(-mean(error^2 / std^2)). Three speed regimes select the std set:

  • standing (speed < walking_threshold)
  • walking (walking_threshold <= speed < running_threshold)
  • running (speed >= running_threshold)

Each std dict must cover every DOF of the robot (a ".*" entry is the explicit "everything else" catch-all); DOFs no pattern matches raise at :meth:build instead of silently training against a default tolerance.

def build(self) -> None:
    self._robot = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)
    self._command = self._env.command_manager.get_term(self.command_name)
    term = type(self).__name__
    self._std_standing = resolve_per_dof_std(
        self.std_standing, self._robot, self.device, field=f"{term}.std_standing"
    )
    self._std_walking = resolve_per_dof_std(self.std_walking, self._robot, self.device, field=f"{term}.std_walking")
    self._std_running = resolve_per_dof_std(self.std_running, self._robot, self.device, field=f"{term}.std_running")

docs.title: compute
docs.text:
compute() -> Tensor
Source code in eden/managers/terms/rewards/locomotion.py 
def compute(self) -> torch.Tensor:
    command = self._command.command
    linear_speed = torch.norm(command[:, :2], dim=1)
    angular_speed = torch.abs(command[:, 2])
    total_speed = linear_speed + angular_speed

    standing_mask = (total_speed < self.walking_threshold).float()
    walking_mask = ((total_speed >= self.walking_threshold) & (total_speed < self.running_threshold)).float()
    running_mask = (total_speed >= self.running_threshold).float()

    std = (
        self._std_standing * standing_mask.unsqueeze(1)
        + self._std_walking * walking_mask.unsqueeze(1)
        + self._std_running * running_mask.unsqueeze(1)
    )

    current_dofs_pos = self._robot.get_dofs_pos()
    error_squared = torch.square(current_dofs_pos - self._robot.default_dofs_pos)
    return torch.exp(-torch.mean(error_squared / (std**2), dim=1))

def compute(self) -> torch.Tensor:
    foot_pos = self._robot.get_links_pos(ls_idx_local=self._ls_idx)  # (num_envs, N, 3)
    foot_vel = self._robot.get_links_vel(ls_idx_local=self._ls_idx)  # (num_envs, N, 3)

    foot_z = foot_pos[:, :, 2]  # (num_envs, N)
    vel_norm = torch.norm(foot_vel[:, :, :2], dim=-1)  # (num_envs, N)
    delta = torch.abs(foot_z - self.target_height)
    cost = torch.sum(delta * vel_norm, dim=1)

    command = self._command.command
    total_command = torch.norm(command[:, :2], dim=1) + torch.abs(command[:, 2])
    active = (total_command > self.command_threshold).float()
    return torch.mul(cost, active)
