def calibrate_gello_leader(argv: list[str] | None = None):
    from argparse import ArgumentParser
    from pathlib import Path

    from eden.utils.devices.gello.dynamixel_driver import DynamixelDriver
    from eden.utils.devices.gello.leader import GelloLeaderConfig

    description = (
        f"{colorize('Gello leader arm calibration tool.', ANSI_BOLD, ANSI_CYAN)}\n"
        "\n"
        "Hold the leader arm at a known joint configuration (passed via "
        f"{colorize('--start-dofs', ANSI_GREEN)},\n"
        "in radians), then run this tool to compute per-joint offsets and a gripper\n"
        "open/close range. The result is printed as a ready-to-paste\n"
        f"{colorize('GelloLeaderConfig(...)', ANSI_MAGENTA)}."
    )
    epilog = (
        f"{colorize('Examples:', ANSI_BOLD, ANSI_YELLOW)}\n"
        f"  {colorize('# 6-DoF arm (IDs 1..6) at zero pose, with a gripper on ID 7 (default N+1):', ANSI_DIM)}\n"
        "  eden gello calibrate \\\n"
        f"      {colorize('--port', ANSI_GREEN)} /dev/ttyUSB0 \\\n"
        f"      {colorize('--start-dofs', ANSI_GREEN)} 0 0 0 0 0 0 \\\n"
        f"      {colorize('--signs', ANSI_GREEN)} 1 1 -1 1 1 1 \\\n"
        f"      {colorize('--gripper', ANSI_GREEN)}\\\n"
        f"      {colorize('--output', ANSI_GREEN)} configs/gello_ur5e.yaml\n"
        "\n"
        f"  {colorize('# Custom Dynamixel IDs and high-speed baudrate, no gripper:', ANSI_DIM)}\n"
        "  eden gello calibrate \\\n"
        f"      {colorize('--port', ANSI_GREEN)} /dev/ttyUSB0 \\\n"
        f"      {colorize('--start-dofs', ANSI_GREEN)} 0 0 0 0 0 0 \\\n"
        f"      {colorize('--signs', ANSI_GREEN)} 1 1 1 1 1 1 \\\n"
        f"      {colorize('--joint-ids', ANSI_GREEN)} 1 2 4 6 7 8 \\\n"
        f"      {colorize('--baudrate', ANSI_GREEN)} 1000000"
    )
    parser = ArgumentParser(
        prog="eden gello calibrate",
        description=description,
        epilog=epilog,
        formatter_class=ColorHelpFormatter,
    )
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=str, required=True, help="Dynamixel serial port (e.g. /dev/ttyUSB0).")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--start-dofs", type=float, nargs="+", required=True, help="Known arm DOFs (rad) at calibration pose."
    )
    parser.add_argument("--signs", type=float, nargs="+", required=True, help="Sign (-1 or 1) per arm DOF.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--joint-ids", type=int, nargs="+", default=None, help="Dynamixel IDs for arm DOFs. Default: 1..N."
    )
    parser.add_argument("--gripper", action="store_true", help="Whether the gripper is attached.")
    parser.add_argument("--gripper-id", type=int, default=None, help="Dynamixel ID for the gripper. Default: N+1.")
    parser.add_argument("--baudrate", type=int, default=57600)
    parser.add_argument("--warmup-reads", type=int, default=10, help="Read iterations before sampling offsets.")
    parser.add_argument("--max-pi-multiple", type=int, default=8)
    parser.add_argument("--gripper-open-delta-deg", type=float, default=-0.2)
    parser.add_argument("--gripper-close-delta-deg", type=float, default=-42.0)
    parser.add_argument(
        "-o",
        "--output",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help="Save the resulting GelloLeaderConfig to this path (format inferred from .json, .yaml, or .yml).",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.output is not None and args.output.suffix.lower() not in (".json", ".yaml", ".yml"):
        parser.error(f"--output must end in .json, .yaml, or .yml (got {args.output.suffix!r}).")

    start_dofs = np.asarray(args.start_dofs, dtype=np.float64)
    signs = np.asarray(args.signs, dtype=np.float64)
    if start_dofs.size != signs.size:
        raise ValueError("'--start-dofs' and '--signs' must have the same length.")

    num_arm = start_dofs.size
    joint_ids = args.joint_ids if args.joint_ids is not None else list(range(1, num_arm + 1))
    if len(joint_ids) != num_arm:
        raise ValueError(f"'--joint-ids' must have length {num_arm}, got {len(joint_ids)}.")

    ids = list(joint_ids)
    if args.gripper:
        gripper_id = int(args.gripper_id) if args.gripper_id is not None else num_arm + 1
        if gripper_id in ids:
            raise ValueError("'--gripper-id' must not overlap with arm joint IDs.")
        ids.append(gripper_id)

    driver = DynamixelDriver(ids=ids, port=args.port, baudrate=args.baudrate)
    try:
        for _ in range(max(0, args.warmup_reads)):
            driver.get_positions()

        positions = driver.get_positions()
        arm_positions = positions[:num_arm]
        offsets = get_offset(
            current_dofs=arm_positions,
            start_dofs=start_dofs,
            signs=signs,
            max_pi_multiple=args.max_pi_multiple,
        )

        def _label(text: str) -> str:
            return colorize(text, ANSI_CYAN)

        def _value(text: str) -> str:
            return colorize(text, ANSI_YELLOW)

        def _key(text: str) -> str:
            return colorize(text, ANSI_GREEN)

        print(f"{_label('current arm dofs (rad)    :')} {_value(str([f'{v:.6f}' for v in arm_positions.tolist()]))}")
        print(f"{_label('best offsets (rad)        :')} {_value(str([f'{v:.6f}' for v in offsets.tolist()]))}")
        print(f"{_label('best offsets (pi/2 terms) :')} {_value(str(format_offsets_as_pi_half_terms(offsets)))}")

        gripper_block = ""
        if args.gripper:
            open_deg, close_deg = estimate_gripper_range_deg(
                current_gripper_rad=float(positions[-1]),
                open_delta_deg=args.gripper_open_delta_deg,
                close_delta_deg=args.gripper_close_delta_deg,
            )
            print(f"{_label('gripper current (deg)     :')} {_value(f'{np.rad2deg(positions[-1]):.6f}')}")
            print(f"{_label('gripper open (deg)        :')} {_value(f'{open_deg:.6f}')}")
            print(f"{_label('gripper close (deg)       :')} {_value(f'{close_deg:.6f}')}")
            gripper_block = (
                f"    {_key('gripper_id')}={_value(str(gripper_id))},\n"
                f"    {_key('gripper_open_deg')}={_value(f'{open_deg:.6f}')},\n"
                f"    {_key('gripper_close_deg')}={_value(f'{close_deg:.6f}')},\n"
            )

        config = GelloLeaderConfig(
            joint_ids=[int(v) for v in joint_ids],
            joint_offsets_rad=[float(v) for v in offsets],
            joint_signs=[int(s) for s in signs],
            gripper_id=gripper_id if args.gripper else None,
            gripper_open_deg=(open_deg if args.gripper else None),
            gripper_close_deg=(close_deg if args.gripper else None),
            baudrate=args.baudrate,
        )

        print(f"\n{colorize('GelloLeaderConfig(', ANSI_BOLD, ANSI_MAGENTA)}")
        print(f"    {_key('joint_ids')}={_value(str(tuple(config.joint_ids)))},")
        print(f"    {_key('joint_offsets_rad')}={_value(str(tuple(config.joint_offsets_rad)))},")
        print(f"    {_key('joint_signs')}={_value(str(tuple(config.joint_signs)))},")
        if gripper_block:
            print(gripper_block, end="")
        print(f"    {_key('baudrate')}={_value(str(config.baudrate))},")
        print(colorize(")", ANSI_BOLD, ANSI_MAGENTA))

        if args.output is not None:
            saved = config.save(args.output)
            print(f"\n{colorize('Saved config to:', ANSI_BOLD, ANSI_GREEN)} {saved}")
    finally:
        driver.close()

def __init__(self, ids: Sequence[int], port: str, baudrate: int = 57600):
    if len(ids) == 0:
        raise ValueError("'ids' must not be empty.")

    try:
        from dynamixel_sdk.group_sync_read import GroupSyncRead
        from dynamixel_sdk.group_sync_write import GroupSyncWrite
        from dynamixel_sdk.packet_handler import PacketHandler
        from dynamixel_sdk.port_handler import PortHandler
        from dynamixel_sdk.robotis_def import COMM_SUCCESS
        from dynamixel_sdk.robotis_def import DXL_HIBYTE, DXL_HIWORD, DXL_LOBYTE, DXL_LOWORD
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise ImportError("dynamixel_sdk is required. Install with `pip install dynamixel-sdk`.") from exc

    self._ids = tuple(int(i) for i in ids)
    self._port_handler = PortHandler(port)
    self._packet_handler = PacketHandler(2.0)
    self._group_read = GroupSyncRead(
        self._port_handler, self._packet_handler, ADDR_PRESENT_POSITION, LEN_PRESENT_POSITION
    )
    self._group_write = GroupSyncWrite(
        self._port_handler, self._packet_handler, ADDR_GOAL_POSITION, LEN_GOAL_POSITION
    )
    self._comm_success = COMM_SUCCESS
    self._byte_pack = (DXL_LOBYTE, DXL_HIBYTE, DXL_LOWORD, DXL_HIWORD)
    self._torque_enabled = False

    if not self._port_handler.openPort():
        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to open Dynamixel port: {port}")
    if not self._port_handler.setBaudRate(int(baudrate)):
        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to set Dynamixel baudrate: {baudrate}")

    for dxl_id in self._ids:
        if not self._group_read.addParam(dxl_id):
            raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to add group read param for ID {dxl_id}")

def get_positions(self) -> np.ndarray:
    comm_result = self._group_read.txRxPacket()
    if comm_result != self._comm_success:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to read joint positions: {self._packet_handler.getTxRxResult(comm_result)}")

    positions = np.zeros(len(self._ids), dtype=np.float64)
    for i, dxl_id in enumerate(self._ids):
        if not self._group_read.isAvailable(dxl_id, ADDR_PRESENT_POSITION, LEN_PRESENT_POSITION):
            raise RuntimeError(f"Position data is not available for ID {dxl_id}")
        raw = self._group_read.getData(dxl_id, ADDR_PRESENT_POSITION, LEN_PRESENT_POSITION)
        signed = raw - (1 << 32) if raw & (1 << 31) else raw
        positions[i] = signed * np.pi / 2048.0
    return positions

def set_positions(self, joint_angles: Sequence[float]):
    if not self._torque_enabled:
        raise RuntimeError("Torque must be enabled before commanding joint positions.")

    joint_angles_arr = np.asarray(joint_angles, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1)
    if joint_angles_arr.size != len(self._ids):
        raise ValueError(f"Expected {len(self._ids)} joint angles, got {joint_angles_arr.size}.")

    lo_byte, hi_byte, lo_word, hi_word = self._byte_pack
    try:
        for dxl_id, angle in zip(self._ids, joint_angles_arr):
            value = int(np.round(angle * 2048.0 / np.pi)) & 0xFFFFFFFF
            data = [
                lo_byte(lo_word(value)),
                hi_byte(lo_word(value)),
                lo_byte(hi_word(value)),
                hi_byte(hi_word(value)),
            ]
            if not self._group_write.addParam(dxl_id, data):
                raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to add write param for ID {dxl_id}")
        comm_result = self._group_write.txPacket()
    finally:
        self._group_write.clearParam()

    if comm_result != self._comm_success:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to write joint positions: {self._packet_handler.getTxRxResult(comm_result)}")

def __init__(
    self,
    env: EnvBase,
    arm_entity_name: str,
    arm_dofs_name: list[str],
    ee_link_name: str,
    *,
    gripper_entity_name: str | None = None,
    gripper_dofs_name: list[str] | None = None,
    host: str = "localhost",
    port: int = 5001,
    verbose: bool = False,
):
    if not ZMQ_AVAILABLE:
        raise ImportError(
            "pyzmq (import name `zmq`) is not installed. "
            f"Install it with Eden's 'gello' extra, {install_hint('gello')}; or alone with `pip install pyzmq`."
        )

    self._host = host
    self._port = port
    self._verbose = verbose

    self._env = env
    self._arm_entity: RigidEntity = env.entities[arm_entity_name]
    _, self._arm_dofs_idx = self._arm_entity.find_named_dofs_idx_local(arm_dofs_name, preserve_order=True)
    self._ee_link: RigidLink = self._arm_entity.get_link(ee_link_name)
    if gripper_entity_name is not None:
        self._gripper_entity: RigidEntity = env.entities[gripper_entity_name]
        gripper_dofs_name, self._gripper_dofs_idx = self._gripper_entity.find_named_dofs_idx_local(
            gripper_dofs_name, preserve_order=True
        )
        assert len(self._gripper_dofs_idx) == 2, "Gripper must have exactly 2 DOFs."

        gripper_open = torch.zeros(2)
        gripper_close = torch.zeros(2)
        open_dofs_pos = getattr(self._gripper_entity._options, "open_dofs_pos", None)
        close_dofs_pos = getattr(self._gripper_entity._options, "close_dofs_pos", None)

        if isinstance(open_dofs_pos, float):
            gripper_open[:] = open_dofs_pos
        elif isinstance(open_dofs_pos, dict):
            for dofs_name, pos in open_dofs_pos.items():
                # Robot-level configs may include both left/right gripper keys. Skip entries that do not
                # match this server's gripper scope, as decided by the lookup itself (an exact joint name is
                # literal against every joint, which a separate probe over the scope alone would not see).
                try:
                    _dofs_name, dofs_idx = self._gripper_entity.find_named_dofs_idx_local(
                        dofs_name, name_scope=gripper_dofs_name
                    )
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                dofs_idx = [gripper_dofs_name.index(name) for name in _dofs_name]
                gripper_open[dofs_idx] = pos
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported open_dofs_pos type: {type(open_dofs_pos)}.")

        if isinstance(close_dofs_pos, float):
            gripper_close[:] = close_dofs_pos
        elif isinstance(close_dofs_pos, dict):
            for dofs_name, pos in close_dofs_pos.items():
                # Robot-level configs may include both left/right gripper keys. Skip entries that do not
                # match this server's gripper scope, as decided by the lookup itself (an exact joint name is
                # literal against every joint, which a separate probe over the scope alone would not see).
                try:
                    _dofs_name, dofs_idx = self._gripper_entity.find_named_dofs_idx_local(
                        dofs_name, name_scope=gripper_dofs_name
                    )
                except ValueError:
                    continue
                dofs_idx = [gripper_dofs_name.index(name) for name in _dofs_name]
                gripper_close[dofs_idx] = pos
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported close_dofs_pos type: {type(close_dofs_pos)}.")

        self._gripper_open = gripper_open
        self.max_opening = (gripper_close - gripper_open).abs().sum(dim=-1)
    else:
        self._gripper_entity = None

    self._num_dofs = len(self._arm_dofs_idx) + int(self._gripper_entity is not None)

    self._lifecycle_lock = threading.Lock()
    self._stop_event = threading.Event()
    self._server_ready = threading.Event()
    self._server_startup_done = threading.Event()
    self._server_thread: threading.Thread | None = None
    self._server_startup_error: Exception | None = None
    self._server_state: _ServerState = _ServerState.IDLE
    self._command_lock = threading.Lock()
    self._command = (
        np.asarray(self._get_observations_for_rpc(dofs_pos_only=True), dtype=np.float32).reshape(-1).copy()
    )

def start(self):
    startup_timeout_seconds = 10.0

    with self._lifecycle_lock:
        if self._server_state == _ServerState.STOPPED:
            raise RuntimeError("Gello RPC server has already been stopped and cannot be restarted.")

        if self._server_state == _ServerState.RUNNING:
            thread = self._server_thread
            if thread is not None and thread.is_alive() and self._server_ready.is_set():
                return
            self._server_state = _ServerState.IDLE
            self._server_thread = None

        if self._server_state == _ServerState.IDLE:
            self._server_startup_error = None
            self._server_startup_done.clear()
            self._server_ready.clear()
            self._stop_event.clear()
            self._server_state = _ServerState.STARTING

            thread = threading.Thread(target=self._serve, daemon=True)
            try:
                thread.start()
            except Exception:
                self._server_state = _ServerState.IDLE
                raise
            self._server_thread = thread

    if not self._server_startup_done.wait(timeout=startup_timeout_seconds):
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Gello RPC server startup timed out after {startup_timeout_seconds} seconds "
            f"for endpoint {self.endpoint!r}."
        )

    with self._lifecycle_lock:
        if self._server_state == _ServerState.STOPPED:
            raise RuntimeError("Gello RPC server was stopped during startup.")
        if self._server_startup_error is not None:
            self._server_state = _ServerState.IDLE
            self._server_thread = None
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"Failed to start Gello RPC server on {self.endpoint}."
            ) from self._server_startup_error
        if not self._server_ready.is_set():
            self._server_state = _ServerState.IDLE
            self._server_thread = None
            raise RuntimeError("Gello RPC server thread exited before becoming ready.")
        self._server_state = _ServerState.RUNNING

def stop(self):
    with self._lifecycle_lock:
        if self._server_state == _ServerState.STOPPED:
            return
        self._server_state = _ServerState.STOPPED
        self._stop_event.set()
        thread = self._server_thread

def __init__(self, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = 6001, timeout_ms: int = 2000):
    if not ZMQ_AVAILABLE:
        raise ImportError("pyzmq is not installed. Install it with `pip install pyzmq`.")
    if timeout_ms <= 0:
        raise ValueError("'timeout_ms' must be greater than 0.")

    self._context = zmq.Context()
    self._socket = self._context.socket(zmq.REQ)
    self._socket.setsockopt(zmq.LINGER, 0)
    self._socket.setsockopt(zmq.RCVTIMEO, int(timeout_ms))
    self._socket.setsockopt(zmq.SNDTIMEO, int(timeout_ms))
    self._socket.connect(f"tcp://{host}:{port}")

docs.title: Meta Quest
docs.text:
A WebXR bridge process (televuer) streams controller poses to Eden over ZMQ.

XR bridge process for Meta Quest teleoperation.

Owns the televuer XR session: it spins up a Vuer WebXR server that the Meta Quest connects to over Wi-Fi, captures head / wrist poses plus either the hand-joint poses or the motion-controller state, and displays the stereo frames that Eden renders.

WebXR exposes hand tracking and motion controllers as mutually exclusive input sources, so the bridge runs in one of two modes (--tracking): * hand : head/wrist poses + 25 hand-joint positions + pinch/squeeze * controller : head/wrist poses + per-hand trigger / grip / A,B buttons / thumbstick (button + 2D axis)

Data flow (see protocol.py): * publishes head/wrist + hand-or-controller state -> Eden (PUB on POSE_PORT) * receives stereo RGB frames <- Eden (PULL on FRAME_PORT) -> headset

Each published dict carries a "mode" key ("hand" or "controller") so the Eden side knows which fields to expect.

All published poses are converted from the OpenXR basis (x right, y up, z back) into the Genesis/robot basis (x forward, y left, z up) so Eden can consume them directly in its world frame.

Requires the metaquest extra and televuer, which is not on PyPI (uv sync --inexact --extra metaquest --group metaquest-git in a checkout).

Run: eden metaquest bridge # hand tracking (default) eden metaquest bridge --tracking controller # motion controllers # or, equivalently: uv run python -m eden.utils.devices.metaquest.xr_bridge

Wire protocol for the Eden <-> XR (televuer) ZMQ bridge.

Two localhost channels, both single-part so ZMQ_CONFLATE (keep-latest) works:

  • frames : Eden PUSH -> bridge PULL (FRAME_PORT) stereo RGB uint8 (H, W, 3)
  • poses : bridge PUB -> Eden SUB (POSE_PORT) head/wrist/hand JSON state

This module is imported by both processes (the XR bridge and Eden), so it must depend only on numpy + pyzmq -- never on televuer or eden.

Pose matrices published here are already expressed in the Genesis/robot world frame: z up, x forward, y left, metres, origin at the XR tracking origin.

Clutch-relative pose mapping: XR controller pose -> end-effector target.

Ported from Dream-Machines-Robotics/vr-teleop-kit (Apache-2.0), with the upstream mujoco quaternion calls swapped for Genesis' numpy-backed wxyz helpers (genesis.utils.geom) — no quaternion math is reimplemented here. The algorithm and its hardware-tuned defaults are unchanged; see tests/utils/devices/metaquest/test_pose_mapping.py for the ported sanity checks (T1-T11).

ClutchPoseMapper holds the "engage" state — the controller pose and the EE pose captured at the moment the operator pressed the clutch (grip) button. While the clutch is held, the EE target is the engaged EE pose composed with an effective controller delta, rotated from the XR world frame into the arm's base frame. On release the mapper disengages and target() returns None until the next engage, so the operator can reposition their hand without moving the robot (clutch-relative mapping, like lifting a mouse off the desk).

Reach limit (the interesting part). When the caller passes the arm's current EE pose into target(), the position/orientation channels become INCREMENTAL: per-tick controller deltas accumulate into an effective delta, and anything past pos_reach_limit / rot_reach_limit of the current EE pose is absorbed (a "slipping clutch"). This kills two failure modes the upstream authors hit on hardware:

  • an absolute orientation map pushed far past a joint stop builds up the ~180° error where the shortest-way direction flips sign -> cap-speed shaking;
  • 350° CW and 10° CCW are the same orientation, so an absolute map eventually "snaps" the wrist around the other way. The incremental one never can.

The absorbed overshoot does not come back when the operator reverses (mouse at the edge of the screen: reversing bites immediately). Trade-off: with scale_rotation != 1 the per-increment gain is a rate gain, so curved hand paths are path-dependent on SO(3); re-clutching realigns. 0/None on either reach limit restores the legacy absolute-delta-since-engage mapping.

Frames: all quaternions are wxyz. R maps XR-world vectors into the arm base (v_armbase = R @ v_xr); for an Eden bridge that already publishes poses in the Genesis/robot world frame, R is identity.

def build_pose_msg(tv: TeleVuer):
    """Snapshot the current hand-tracking XR state into a JSON dict (robot frame)."""
    msg = {
        "mode": "hand",
        "ready": bool(tv.motion_data_ready),
        "head": to_robot_se3(tv.head_pose).tolist(),
        "left_wrist": to_robot_se3(tv.left_arm_pose).tolist(),
        "right_wrist": to_robot_se3(tv.right_arm_pose).tolist(),
        "left_hand_pos": to_robot_points(tv.left_hand_positions).tolist(),
        "right_hand_pos": to_robot_points(tv.right_hand_positions).tolist(),
        # pinchValue is a distance (~0 when pinching); expose both the bool and value.
        "left_pinch": bool(tv.left_hand_pinch),
        "right_pinch": bool(tv.right_hand_pinch),
        "left_pinch_value": float(tv.left_hand_pinchValue),
        "right_pinch_value": float(tv.right_hand_pinchValue),
        "left_squeeze": float(tv.left_hand_squeezeValue),
        "right_squeeze": float(tv.right_hand_squeezeValue),
    }
    return msg

left_wrist / right_wrist are the controller grip poses (already in the robot frame). Button / trigger / grip booleans and analog values plus the thumbstick click + 2D axis come straight from the WebXR gamepad mapping:

  • *_trigger_value / *_squeeze_value: 0.0 (released) -> 1.0 (fully pressed)
  • *_thumbstick_value: (x, y) in [-1, 1], +x right, +y back (see televuer)
Source code in eden/utils/devices/metaquest/xr_bridge.py 
def build_controller_msg(tv: TeleVuer):
    """Snapshot the current motion-controller XR state into a JSON dict (robot frame).

    ``left_wrist`` / ``right_wrist`` are the controller grip poses (already in the
    robot frame). Button / trigger / grip booleans and analog values plus the
    thumbstick click + 2D axis come straight from the WebXR gamepad mapping:

      * ``*_trigger_value`` / ``*_squeeze_value``: 0.0 (released) -> 1.0 (fully pressed)
      * ``*_thumbstick_value``: (x, y) in [-1, 1], +x right, +y back (see televuer)
    """
    msg = {
        "mode": "controller",
        "ready": bool(tv.motion_data_ready),
        "head": to_robot_se3(tv.head_pose).tolist(),
        "left_wrist": to_robot_se3(tv.left_arm_pose).tolist(),
        "right_wrist": to_robot_se3(tv.right_arm_pose).tolist(),
    }
    for side in ("left", "right"):
        msg.update(
            {
                f"{side}_trigger": bool(getattr(tv, f"{side}_ctrl_trigger")),
                f"{side}_trigger_value": float(getattr(tv, f"{side}_ctrl_triggerValue")),
                f"{side}_squeeze": bool(getattr(tv, f"{side}_ctrl_squeeze")),
                f"{side}_squeeze_value": float(getattr(tv, f"{side}_ctrl_squeezeValue")),
                f"{side}_a_button": bool(getattr(tv, f"{side}_ctrl_aButton")),
                f"{side}_b_button": bool(getattr(tv, f"{side}_ctrl_bButton")),
                f"{side}_thumbstick": bool(getattr(tv, f"{side}_ctrl_thumbstick")),
                f"{side}_thumbstick_value": [float(x) for x in getattr(tv, f"{side}_ctrl_thumbstickValue")],
            }
        )
    return msg

def main(argv=None):
    """Run the XR bridge loop (parses ``argv`` or ``sys.argv`` when ``None``)."""
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Eden <-> Quest XR bridge (televuer side)")
    ap.add_argument("--width", type=int, default=1280, help="full stereo frame width (both eyes)")
    ap.add_argument("--height", type=int, default=480, help="frame height")
    ap.add_argument("--fps", type=float, default=30.0, help="headset display fps")
    ap.add_argument("--display-mode", default="immersive", choices=["immersive", "ego", "pass-through"])
    ap.add_argument(
        "--tracking",
        default="hand",
        choices=["hand", "controller"],
        help="XR input source: hand joints (default) or motion controllers (mutually exclusive in WebXR)",
    )
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    use_hand_tracking = args.tracking == "hand"
    build_msg = build_pose_msg if use_hand_tracking else build_controller_msg

    # The bridge runs televuer, not Genesis, so en.init() (and its en.logger) never
    # runs here -- stand up Eden's logger directly.
    logger = getattr(en, "logger", None) or en.Logger("INFO")

    tv = TeleVuer(
        use_hand_tracking=use_hand_tracking,
        binocular=True,
        img_shape=(args.height, args.width),
        display_fps=args.fps,
        display_mode=args.display_mode,
        zmq=True,  # in-process shared-memory frame display (no external image server)
        webrtc=False,
    )

    ctx = zmq.Context.instance()
    frame_sock = P.frame_pull(ctx)
    pose_sock = P.pose_pub(ctx)

    # Eden-styled banner: ~<...>~ mint, ~~<...>~~ mint-underline, ~~~~<...>~~~~ bold.
    rule = "━" * 64
    logger.info(f"~<{rule}>~")
    logger.info(f" 🍏 ~~~~<Meta Quest XR bridge>~~~~  ({args.tracking} tracking)  —  waiting for the headset")
    logger.info(" On the Quest: join this host's Wi-Fi, then open in the browser ~<→>~")
    for ip in list_host_ips() or ["<host-ip>"]:
        logger.info(f"     ~~<https://{ip}:8012/?ws=wss://{ip}:8012>~~")
    logger.info(" Tap ~<Virtual Reality>~ and allow all prompts")
    logger.info(" (first run: accept the self-signed cert — Advanced ~<→>~ Proceed)")
    logger.info(f" ZMQ   poses PUB ~<:{P.POSE_PORT}>~   frames PULL ~<:{P.FRAME_PORT}>~")
    logger.info(f"~<{rule}>~")

    running = {"v": True}

    def stop(*_):
        running["v"] = False

    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, stop)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)

    period = 1.0 / max(args.fps, 1.0)
    frames_shown = 0
    last_log = time.time()
    try:
        while running["v"]:
            loop_start = time.time()

            # Newest frame from Eden -> headset. Eden sends RGB; render_to_xr treats
            # its input as BGR (it does BGR2RGB internally), so flip channels here.
            frame = P.recv_frame(frame_sock, flags=zmq.NOBLOCK)
            if frame is not None:
                tv.render_to_xr(np.ascontiguousarray(frame[:, :, ::-1]))
                frames_shown += 1

            # Publish current XR pose state to Eden.
            P.send_pose(pose_sock, build_msg(tv))

            now = time.time()
            if now - last_log > 5.0:
                state = "tracking" if tv.motion_data_ready else "waiting for headset"
                logger.info(f"{state} | frames shown: {frames_shown}")
                last_log = now

            dt = time.time() - loop_start
            if dt < period:
                time.sleep(period - dt)
    finally:
        logger.info("shutting down...")
        tv.close()

def send_frame(sock, rgb):
    """Send one stereo RGB frame. ``rgb`` is (H, W, 3) uint8 (left|right halves)."""
    rgb = np.ascontiguousarray(rgb, dtype=np.uint8)
    h, w = rgb.shape[:2]
    header = np.array([h, w], dtype=np.uint32).tobytes()
    sock.send(header + rgb.tobytes(), copy=False)

def recv_frame(sock, flags=0):
    """Receive one frame, or return None if ``flags=zmq.NOBLOCK`` and none waiting."""
    try:
        buf = sock.recv(flags=flags)
    except zmq.Again:
        return None
    h, w = np.frombuffer(buf[:8], dtype=np.uint32)
    return np.frombuffer(buf[8:], dtype=np.uint8).reshape(int(h), int(w), 3)

def frame_pull(ctx, port=FRAME_PORT):
    """Bridge side: PULL that keeps only the newest frame."""
    s = ctx.socket(zmq.PULL)
    s.setsockopt(zmq.CONFLATE, 1)
    s.setsockopt(zmq.RCVHWM, 1)
    s.bind(f"tcp://*:{port}")

def set_R(self, R: np.ndarray) -> None:
    """Replace the XR->arm-base rotation. Typically called per engage with a
    yaw-corrected R so the operator can turn their body between engagements and
    still have 'controller forward' mean 'robot forward'.
    """
    self.R = np.asarray(R, dtype=float).copy()

Source code in eden/utils/devices/metaquest/pose_mapping.py 
def engage(
    self,
    controller_pos_xr: np.ndarray,
    controller_quat_xr: np.ndarray,
    ee_pos_armbase: np.ndarray,
    ee_quat_armbase: np.ndarray,
    pivot_armbase: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Capture the engage frame. Call on the rising clutch edge. If
    ``pivot_armbase`` is supplied, rotation deltas during this engagement
    pivot around that point instead of around the EE.
    """
    self._ctrl_engage_pos = np.array(controller_pos_xr, float, copy=True)
    self._ctrl_engage_quat = np.array(controller_quat_xr, float, copy=True)
    self._ee_engage_pos = np.array(ee_pos_armbase, float, copy=True)
    self._ee_engage_quat = np.array(ee_quat_armbase, float, copy=True)
    self.rotation_pivot = None if pivot_armbase is None else np.array(pivot_armbase, float, copy=True)
    self._ctrl_prev_quat = self._ctrl_engage_quat.copy()
    self._ctrl_prev_pos = self._ctrl_engage_pos.copy()
    self._d_quat_eff = np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])
    self._d_pos_eff = np.zeros(3)
    self._engaged = True

Compute the current EE target in arm-base frame, or None if disengaged.

ee_pos_armbase / ee_quat_armbase are the arm's CURRENT EE pose; passing them enables the pos/rot reach limits (see the class docstring). Without them the legacy absolute mapping applies unchanged.

Source code in eden/utils/devices/metaquest/pose_mapping.py 
def target(
    self,
    controller_pos_xr: np.ndarray,
    controller_quat_xr: np.ndarray,
    ee_pos_armbase: np.ndarray | None = None,
    ee_quat_armbase: np.ndarray | None = None,
) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None:
    """Compute the current EE target in arm-base frame, or None if disengaged.

    ``ee_pos_armbase`` / ``ee_quat_armbase`` are the arm's CURRENT EE pose;
    passing them enables the pos/rot reach limits (see the class docstring).
    Without them the legacy absolute mapping applies unchanged.
    """
    if not self._engaged:
        return None
    assert self._ctrl_engage_pos is not None
    assert self._ctrl_engage_quat is not None
    assert self._ee_engage_pos is not None
    assert self._ee_engage_quat is not None

    # Position delta. Reach-limited path accumulates per-tick increments
    # (vectors commute, so per-tick-scaled increments compose to exactly the
    # absolute scaled delta until the reach limit absorbs). Legacy path: the
    # absolute delta from the engage frame.
    p_now = np.asarray(controller_pos_xr, float)
    pos_limited = ee_pos_armbase is not None and bool(self.pos_reach_limit)
    if pos_limited:
        assert self._ctrl_prev_pos is not None
        self._d_pos_eff = self._d_pos_eff + self.R @ (self.scale * (p_now - self._ctrl_prev_pos))
        d_pos_arm = self._d_pos_eff
    else:
        d_pos_arm = self.R @ (self.scale * (p_now - self._ctrl_engage_pos))
    self._ctrl_prev_pos = p_now.copy()

    q_now = np.asarray(controller_quat_xr, float)
    rot_limited = ee_quat_armbase is not None and bool(self.rot_reach_limit)
    if rot_limited:
        # Incremental path: accumulate this tick's controller rotation
        # increment (a degree or two — never direction-ambiguous) into the
        # effective delta. At scale_rotation=1 the increments telescope to
        # exactly the absolute delta until the reach limit clamps; at other
        # scales it is a rate gain (path-dependent on curved SO(3) loops).
        assert self._ctrl_prev_quat is not None
        if float(np.dot(q_now, self._ctrl_prev_quat)) < 0.0:
            q_now = -q_now  # hemisphere-align: q and -q are the same rotation
        inc = transform_quat_by_quat(inv_quat(self._ctrl_prev_quat), q_now)  # q_now ⊗ prev⁻¹
        self._ctrl_prev_quat = q_now.copy()
        if self.scale_rotation != 1.0:
            inc = rotvec_to_quat(self.scale_rotation * quat_to_rotvec(inc))
        # express the XR-frame increment in arm frame: R ⊗ inc ⊗ R⁻¹
        inc_arm = transform_quat_by_quat(self._R_quat_conj, transform_quat_by_quat(inc, self._R_quat))
        d_quat_arm = transform_quat_by_quat(self._d_quat_eff, inc_arm)  # inc_arm ⊗ d_quat_eff
        d_quat_arm /= np.linalg.norm(d_quat_arm)
        self._d_quat_eff = d_quat_arm
    else:
        # Legacy absolute path: rotation delta in XR world (now * engage⁻¹),
        # conjugated by R_quat to express in arm base. Keep the incremental
        # state fresh so a live reach-limit toggle doesn't see stale prev.
        if self._ctrl_prev_quat is not None:
            if float(np.dot(q_now, self._ctrl_prev_quat)) < 0.0:
                q_now = -q_now
            self._ctrl_prev_quat = q_now.copy()
        d_quat_xr = transform_quat_by_quat(inv_quat(self._ctrl_engage_quat), q_now)  # q_now ⊗ engage⁻¹
        if self.scale_rotation != 1.0:
            d_quat_xr = rotvec_to_quat(self.scale_rotation * quat_to_rotvec(d_quat_xr))
        # R ⊗ d_quat_xr ⊗ R⁻¹
        d_quat_arm = transform_quat_by_quat(self._R_quat_conj, transform_quat_by_quat(d_quat_xr, self._R_quat))

    target_quat = transform_quat_by_quat(self._ee_engage_quat, d_quat_arm)  # d_quat_arm ⊗ ee_engage

    if rot_limited:
        # Clamp the target to within rot_reach_limit of the arm's current
        # orientation and ABSORB the excess into the effective delta.
        ee_q = np.asarray(ee_quat_armbase, float)
        e = quat_to_rotvec(transform_quat_by_quat(inv_quat(ee_q), target_quat))  # target ⊗ ee⁻¹
        e_norm = float(np.linalg.norm(e))
        if e_norm > self.rot_reach_limit:
            e *= self.rot_reach_limit / e_norm
            target_quat = transform_quat_by_quat(ee_q, rotvec_to_quat(e))  # rotvec_to_quat(e) ⊗ ee
            self._d_quat_eff = transform_quat_by_quat(inv_quat(self._ee_engage_quat), target_quat)
            d_quat_arm = self._d_quat_eff

    # A pivot turns the rotation into a swing of the EE around it; with
    # rotation_pivot None the offset term vanishes (legacy in-place rotation).
    if self.rotation_pivot is not None:
        offset = self._ee_engage_pos - self.rotation_pivot
        target_pos = self.rotation_pivot + transform_by_quat(offset, d_quat_arm) + d_pos_arm
    else:
        target_pos = self._ee_engage_pos + d_pos_arm

    # Position reach limit: clamp toward the current EE position and ABSORB
    # the excess (mouse-at-screen-edge: reversal moves the target immediately
    # instead of after retracing the overshoot).
    if pos_limited:
        ee_p = np.asarray(ee_pos_armbase, float)
        dp = target_pos - ee_p
        dp_norm = float(np.linalg.norm(dp))
        if dp_norm > self.pos_reach_limit:
            clamped = ee_p + dp * (self.pos_reach_limit / dp_norm)
            self._d_pos_eff = self._d_pos_eff + (clamped - target_pos)
            target_pos = clamped

    return target_pos, target_quat

docs.title: PICO
docs.text:
The XRoboToolkit tracking client, the bridge process, and the Remote Vision video link that streams Eden's stereo frames to the headset.

PICO tracking client: XRoboToolkit PC Service state -> Genesis/robot frame.

The PICO headset does not talk to Eden directly. It streams its tracking state to the XRoboToolkit PC Service running on this host, and the service exposes it through the xrobotoolkit_sdk extension module. :class:PicoXrClient wraps that module and hands Eden ready-to-use state:

  • poses as 4x4 matrices in the Genesis/robot world frame (z up, x forward, y left, metres, origin at the headset's tracking origin),
  • controller buttons / triggers / grips / thumbsticks by name,
  • the PICO-only extras: paired motion trackers and, in Full-body mode, the 24 SMPL-ordered body joints.

The service reports poses in the OpenXR basis (x right, y up, -z forward), so every pose is conjugated into the robot basis exactly as Eden's Meta Quest bridge does — :data:R_ROBOT_XR here is the same matrix as televuer's R_ROBOT_OPENXR and as XRoboToolkit's own R_HEADSET_TO_WORLD.

:func:xr_pose_to_se3 and friends are module-level and SDK-free so the frame conversion is testable without a headset; only :class:PicoXrClient needs the extension module, which it imports on construction.

Install: build xrobotoolkit_sdk from https://github.com/XR-Robotics/XRoboToolkit-PC-Service-Pybind (it needs the PC Service's libPXREARobotSDK.so; setup_ubuntu.sh fetches and builds both). The service's shared library is preloaded from its install directory when the dynamic linker can't find it, so no LD_LIBRARY_PATH export is needed.

PICO teleoperation bridge: XRoboToolkit PC Service <-> Eden.

Owns everything device-side of a PICO teleop session so the Eden process only speaks ZMQ: it reads the headset's tracking state from the PC Service (via xrobotoolkit_sdk), publishes it in the Genesis/robot world frame, and streams Eden's rendered stereo frames back to the headset as H.264 over the app's Remote Vision link.

Data flow (see :mod:eden.utils.devices.pico.protocol for the headset link and :mod:eden.utils.devices.metaquest.protocol for the ZMQ channels)::

PICO ──Wi-Fi──▶ XRoboToolkit PC Service ──▶ eden pico bridge
                                             │  poses  (PUB :5557) ──▶ Eden
  headset decoder ◀──H.264 / TCP─────────────┤  frames (PULL :5556) ◀──┘

The published state dict uses the same schema as eden metaquest bridge --tracking controller, so an Eden-side teleop loop runs against either headset unchanged; PICO's extras (menu buttons, motion trackers, full-body joints) are additive keys. See :meth:eden.utils.devices.pico.xr_client.PicoXrClient.state.

Requires the pico extra (uv sync --inexact --extra pico) plus a locally built xrobotoolkit_sdk — see :mod:eden.utils.devices.pico.xr_client.

Run: eden pico bridge # or, equivalently: uv run python -m eden.utils.devices.pico.bridge

Stream Eden's rendered stereo frames to a PICO headset over the Remote Vision link.

:class:PicoVideoLink owns both sockets of the link documented in :mod:eden.utils.devices.pico.protocol:

  • it listens on :13579 for the OPEN_CAMERA / CLOSE_CAMERA commands the XRoboToolkit app sends when the operator taps Listen / stops,
  • on OPEN_CAMERA it connects out to the decoder address the request names and pushes H.264 (or H.265) frames until the app closes the stream.

Two daemon threads do the work — one accepting control connections, one encoding — so the caller only ever does::

link = PicoVideoLink()
link.start()
while ...:
    link.push(rgb)   # (H, W, 3) uint8 RGB, left|right side-by-side
link.stop()

push() is non-blocking and latest-frame-wins: it drops into a single slot that the encoder thread drains, so a slow encoder never stalls the sim loop and the headset always shows the newest frame rather than a growing backlog.

Frames are encoded at the size the headset asked for; a differently sized frame is rescaled (with a one-time warning) because the app's decoder is configured from the OPEN_CAMERA request, not from the stream.

The encoder/sender half is ported from SIMPLE's src/simple/teleop/pico/ (MIT, https://github.com/physical-superintelligence-lab/SIMPLE).

Wire protocol of the Eden <-> PICO (XRoboToolkit) Remote Vision video link.

The XRoboToolkit PICO app drives both directions; Eden is the server on the control channel and the client on the video channel:

  • control (headset -> Eden), TCP :13579::

    [4B BE uint32 body_len][body]

    where body is a little-endian NetworkDataProtocol record::

    [4B LE int32 cmd_len][command][4B LE int32 data_len][data]

    The app sends OPEN_CAMERA (data = a CameraRequestData payload, see below) when the operator taps Listen, and CLOSE_CAMERA (no data) when they stop. Eden acknowledges each command with the same framing, echoing the command name and an empty data field.

  • video (Eden -> headset), TCP to the ip/port the OPEN_CAMERA request names — that is where the app's MediaDecoder listens::

    [4B BE uint32 frame_size][H.264 / H.265 NAL data]

CameraRequestData (the OPEN_CAMERA payload) is::

    [0xCA 0xFE]        magic
    [0x01]             version
    [7 x 4B LE int32]  width, height, fps, bitrate, enable_mv_hevc,
                       render_mode, port
    [1B len + bytes]   camera   (the app's source profile, e.g. "ZED")
    [1B len + bytes]   ip       (the headset's own address)

This module is pure bytes <-> objects (stdlib only), so the framing is unit-testable without a headset; the sockets and the encoder live in :mod:eden.utils.devices.pico.video.

Ported from SIMPLE's src/simple/teleop/pico/protocol.py (MIT, https://github.com/physical-superintelligence-lab/SIMPLE), which is where the byte layout above was reverse-engineered from the PICO app.

PicoXrClient(tracker_roles: dict[str, str] | None = None)

Live PICO tracking state, converted into Eden's world frame.

Constructing the client initialises the SDK (which connects to the PC Service on this host); call :meth:close when done. Every getter is a cheap read of the state the service pushes in the background, so calling them once per sim step is fine.

Source code in eden/utils/devices/pico/xr_client.py 
def __init__(self, tracker_roles: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> None:
    """Parameters
    ----------
        tracker_roles: optional ``{serial_number: role}`` map that labels motion
            trackers by body placement (e.g. ``{"PA123...": "waist"}``). The
            service reports trackers only by serial, so this is how a tracker
            becomes ``left_foot`` / ``waist`` / ... in :meth:`trackers`. Unmapped
            trackers fall back to their serial.
    """
    self._sdk = load_sdk()
    self._sdk.init()
    self._tracker_roles = dict(tracker_roles or {})

    sdk = self._sdk
    # Name -> getter tables. The names match XRoboToolkit's own vocabulary
    # (XrClient.get_*_by_name) so recipes written against the upstream
    # samples carry over unchanged.
    self._poses = {
        "head": sdk.get_headset_pose,
        "left_controller": sdk.get_left_controller_pose,
        "right_controller": sdk.get_right_controller_pose,
    }
    self._values = {
        "left_trigger": sdk.get_left_trigger,
        "right_trigger": sdk.get_right_trigger,
        "left_grip": sdk.get_left_grip,
        "right_grip": sdk.get_right_grip,
    }
    self._buttons = {
        "X": sdk.get_X_button,
        "Y": sdk.get_Y_button,
        "A": sdk.get_A_button,
        "B": sdk.get_B_button,
        "left_menu_button": sdk.get_left_menu_button,
        "right_menu_button": sdk.get_right_menu_button,
        "left_axis_click": sdk.get_left_axis_click,
        "right_axis_click": sdk.get_right_axis_click,
    }
    self._axes = {"left": sdk.get_left_axis, "right": sdk.get_right_axis}
    self._hand_active = {"left": sdk.get_left_hand_is_active, "right": sdk.get_right_hand_is_active}
    self._hand_states = {"left": sdk.get_left_hand_tracking_state, "right": sdk.get_right_hand_tracking_state}

def hand_joints(self, side: str) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64] | None:
    """Robot-frame ``(26, 3)`` hand-joint positions, or None when hand tracking is off.

    This is the OpenXR 26-joint layout (palm included), *not* the 25-joint
    WebXR one the Meta Quest bridge publishes — index it with the OpenXR
    ``XrHandJointEXT`` order.
    """
    if not self._get(self._hand_active, side, "hand")():
        return None
    state = np.asarray(self._hand_states[side](), dtype=float)
    if state.shape != (N_HAND_JOINTS, 7):
        raise ValueError(f"expected ({N_HAND_JOINTS}, 7) hand joint poses from the service, got {state.shape}")
    return xr_points_to_robot(state[:, :3])

Each value is {"serial", "role", "pos" (3), "quat" (4), "vel" (6), "acc" (6)}; role is None for a tracker with no tracker_roles entry, and such a tracker is keyed by its serial instead. vel/acc are (vx, vy, vz, wx, wy, wz) in the robot frame.

def trackers(self) -> dict[str, dict]:
    """PICO motion trackers (up to 5) in the robot frame, keyed by role or serial.

    Each value is ``{"serial", "role", "pos" (3), "quat" (4), "vel" (6),
    "acc" (6)}``; ``role`` is ``None`` for a tracker with no ``tracker_roles``
    entry, and such a tracker is keyed by its serial instead. ``vel``/``acc`` are
    ``(vx, vy, vz, wx, wy, wz)`` in the robot frame.
    """
    count = int(self._sdk.num_motion_data_available())
    if count == 0:
        return {}
    poses = self._sdk.get_motion_tracker_pose()
    vels = self._sdk.get_motion_tracker_velocity()
    accs = self._sdk.get_motion_tracker_acceleration()
    serials = self._sdk.get_motion_tracker_serial_numbers()
    out: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for i in range(count):
        pq = xr_pose_to_pos_quat(poses[i])
        if pq is None:
            continue
        serial = str(serials[i])
        role = self._tracker_roles.get(serial)
        out[role or serial] = {
            "serial": serial,
            "role": role,
            "pos": pq[0].tolist(),
            "quat": pq[1].tolist(),
            "vel": xr_vel6_to_robot(vels[i]).tolist(),
            "acc": xr_vel6_to_robot(accs[i]).tolist(),
        }
    return out

body_joints(poses: ndarray | None = None) -> dict[str, dict] | None

Full-body joints as {name: {pos, quat, vel, acc}}, or None when unavailable.

Requires Full-body mode in the PICO app with calibrated motion trackers; keys are :data:BODY_JOINT_NAMES (left_wrist, left_ankle, left_foot, pelvis, ...). vel/acc are (linear, angular) 6-vectors in the robot frame. A joint the service has not solved yet reports a degenerate quaternion and is published as identity at the origin. poses reuses an already-read (24, 7) service-frame array so one snapshot needs a single SDK pose read; velocities/accelerations are always read live.

Source code in eden/utils/devices/pico/xr_client.py 
def body_joints(self, poses: np.ndarray | None = None) -> dict[str, dict] | None:
    """Full-body joints as ``{name: {pos, quat, vel, acc}}``, or None when unavailable.

    Requires Full-body mode in the PICO app with calibrated motion trackers;
    keys are :data:`BODY_JOINT_NAMES` (``left_wrist``, ``left_ankle``,
    ``left_foot``, ``pelvis``, ...). ``vel``/``acc`` are ``(linear, angular)``
    6-vectors in the robot frame. A joint the service has not solved yet reports
    a degenerate quaternion and is published as identity at the origin.
    ``poses`` reuses an already-read ``(24, 7)`` service-frame array so one
    snapshot needs a single SDK pose read; velocities/accelerations are
    always read live.
    """
    if poses is None:
        if not self._sdk.is_body_data_available():
            return None
        poses = np.asarray(self._sdk.get_body_joints_pose(), dtype=float)
    vels = np.asarray(self._sdk.get_body_joints_velocity(), dtype=float)
    accs = np.asarray(self._sdk.get_body_joints_acceleration(), dtype=float)
    for name, arr, cols in (("pose", poses, 7), ("velocity", vels, 6), ("acceleration", accs, 6)):
        if arr.shape != (N_BODY_JOINTS, cols):
            raise ValueError(f"expected ({N_BODY_JOINTS}, {cols}) body {name} from the service, got {arr.shape}")
    body: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for i, joint in enumerate(BODY_JOINT_NAMES):
        pq = xr_pose_to_pos_quat(poses[i])
        body[joint] = {
            "pos": (pq[0] if pq is not None else np.zeros(3)).tolist(),
            "quat": (pq[1] if pq is not None else np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0])).tolist(),
            "vel": xr_vel6_to_robot(vels[i]).tolist(),
            "acc": xr_vel6_to_robot(accs[i]).tolist(),
        }
    return body

def body_raw(self) -> tuple[int, list[list[float]]] | None:
    """Untouched service-frame body poses: ``(timestamp_ns, (24, 7) xyz+xyzw lists)``.

    Deliberately no frame conversion, no untracked-joint substitution, no
    wxyz flip — for consumers that apply their own frame math to exactly
    what the SDK reports (the SONIC teleop pipelines). The timestamp is
    ``get_time_stamp_ns`` (not the body-specific stamp) read immediately
    before the poses, matching the in-process reader's dedupe order
    (``eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.inputs.PicoReader``).
    """
    if not self._sdk.is_body_data_available():
        return None
    stamp_ns = int(self._sdk.get_time_stamp_ns())
    poses = np.asarray(self._sdk.get_body_joints_pose(), dtype=float)
    if poses.shape != (N_BODY_JOINTS, 7):
        raise ValueError(f"expected ({N_BODY_JOINTS}, 7) body poses from the service, got {poses.shape}")
    return stamp_ns, poses.tolist()

docs.text:
state(derived_body: bool = True) -> dict

Snapshot every input as a JSON-safe dict, in the Genesis/robot frame.

The controller keys deliberately match what eden metaquest bridge --tracking controller publishes (head, {side}_wrist, {side}_trigger[_value], {side}_squeeze[_value], {side}_a_button/_b_button, {side}_thumbstick[_value]), so an Eden-side teleop loop runs against either headset unchanged. PICO's extras are additive: {side}_menu_button, trackers (see :meth:trackers), body_ready and body (see :meth:body_joints), plus the lossless body_raw / body_raw_timestamp_ns passthrough (see :meth:body_raw).

derived_body=False skips the per-joint body dict and trackers (a consumer that only reads body_raw — the SONIC operator — saves most of the per-snapshot SDK work; body_ready then reflects the raw read).

Source code in eden/utils/devices/pico/xr_client.py 
def state(self, derived_body: bool = True) -> dict:
    """Snapshot every input as a JSON-safe dict, in the Genesis/robot frame.

    The controller keys deliberately match what ``eden metaquest bridge
    --tracking controller`` publishes (``head``, ``{side}_wrist``,
    ``{side}_trigger[_value]``, ``{side}_squeeze[_value]``,
    ``{side}_a_button``/``_b_button``, ``{side}_thumbstick[_value]``), so an
    Eden-side teleop loop runs against either headset unchanged. PICO's extras
    are additive: ``{side}_menu_button``, ``trackers`` (see :meth:`trackers`),
    ``body_ready`` and ``body`` (see :meth:`body_joints`), plus the lossless
    ``body_raw`` / ``body_raw_timestamp_ns`` passthrough (see :meth:`body_raw`).

    ``derived_body=False`` skips the per-joint ``body`` dict and ``trackers``
    (a consumer that only reads ``body_raw`` — the SONIC operator — saves
    most of the per-snapshot SDK work; ``body_ready`` then reflects the raw
    read).
    """
    # Read the head pose once so ``ready`` describes the matrix we publish.
    head = self.pose("head")
    state = {
        "device": "pico",
        "mode": "controller",
        "ready": bool(np.abs(head).sum() > 1e-6),
        "head": head.tolist(),
        "left_wrist": self.pose("left_controller").tolist(),
        "right_wrist": self.pose("right_controller").tolist(),
        "timestamp_ns": self.timestamp_ns(),
    }
    # X/Y (left) and A/B (right) are the primary/secondary buttons of their
    # controller, which is what the Meta Quest bridge calls a/b per side.
    primary = {"left": "X", "right": "A"}
    secondary = {"left": "Y", "right": "B"}
    for side in ("left", "right"):
        trigger = self.value(f"{side}_trigger")
        squeeze = self.value(f"{side}_grip")
        state.update(
            {
                f"{side}_trigger": trigger > 0.5,
                f"{side}_trigger_value": trigger,
                f"{side}_squeeze": squeeze > 0.5,
                f"{side}_squeeze_value": squeeze,
                f"{side}_a_button": self.button(primary[side]),
                f"{side}_b_button": self.button(secondary[side]),
                f"{side}_menu_button": self.button(f"{side}_menu_button"),
                f"{side}_thumbstick": self.button(f"{side}_axis_click"),
                f"{side}_thumbstick_value": list(self.axis(side)),
            }
        )

    raw = self.body_raw()
    if raw is not None:
        state["body_raw_timestamp_ns"], state["body_raw"] = raw
    if derived_body:
        state["trackers"] = self.trackers()
        # Reuse the raw read: one SDK pose read per snapshot.
        body = self.body_joints(poses=None if raw is None else np.asarray(raw[1], dtype=float))
        state["body_ready"] = body is not None
        if body is not None:
            state["body"] = body  # {joint_name: {pos, quat, vel, acc}}
    else:
        state["body_ready"] = raw is not None
    return state

def load_sdk():
    """Import ``xrobotoolkit_sdk``, raising a build hint instead of a bare ImportError.

    The pybind module links against the PC Service's ``libPXREARobotSDK.so``,
    which lives outside the default loader path. When the import fails on that
    library, it is preloaded from the service's install directory and the
    import retried — no ``LD_LIBRARY_PATH`` export needed.
    """
    try:
        return _import_sdk()
    except ImportError as exc:
        if _PXREA_LIB in str(exc) and _preload_pxrea():
            try:
                return _import_sdk()
            except ImportError as exc2:  # pragma: no cover - depends on the local build
                raise ImportError(_SDK_HINT) from exc2
        raise ImportError(_SDK_HINT) from exc

def xr_pose_to_se3(pose: npt.ArrayLike) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]:
    """Convert one service pose ``(x, y, z, qx, qy, qz, qw)`` to a robot-frame 4x4.

    Returns :data:`UNTRACKED` (all zeros) when the quaternion is degenerate, which
    is what the service reports for a device it has not seen yet. Eden-side
    consumers test ``np.abs(mat).sum() < 1e-6`` for "tracking dropped".
    """
    values = np.asarray(pose, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    if values.shape != (7,):
        raise ValueError(f"expected a 7-element (x, y, z, qx, qy, qz, qw) pose, got shape {values.shape}")
    quat = values[[6, 3, 4, 5]]  # the service reports xyzw; Genesis is wxyz
    norm = float(np.linalg.norm(quat))
    if norm < 1e-8:
        return UNTRACKED.copy()
    return T_ROBOT_XR @ trans_quat_to_T(values[:3], quat / norm) @ T_XR_ROBOT

def xr_pose_to_pos_quat(pose: npt.ArrayLike) -> tuple[npt.NDArray[np.float64], npt.NDArray[np.float64]] | None:
    """Robot-frame ``(pos (3,), wxyz quat (4,))`` for one service pose, or None if untracked."""
    mat = xr_pose_to_se3(pose)
    if np.abs(mat).sum() < 1e-6:
        return None

def xr_points_to_robot(points: npt.ArrayLike) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]:

def xr_vel6_to_robot(vel6: npt.ArrayLike) -> npt.NDArray[np.float64]:
    """Rotate a 6-vector ``(vx, vy, vz, wx, wy, wz)`` velocity/accel into the robot frame.

    Both the linear and angular halves are free vectors, so each rotates by
    :data:`R_ROBOT_XR` (a proper rotation, so angular pseudovectors transform the
    same way). Used for the motion-tracker and body-joint velocities/accelerations.
    """
    v = np.asarray(vel6, dtype=float).reshape(-1)
    if v.shape != (6,):
        raise ValueError(f"expected a 6-element (linear, angular) vector, got shape {v.shape}")
    return np.concatenate([R_ROBOT_XR @ v[:3], R_ROBOT_XR @ v[3:]])

def main(argv=None):
    """Run the PICO bridge loop (parses ``argv`` or ``sys.argv`` when ``None``)."""
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Eden <-> PICO teleop bridge (XRoboToolkit side)")
    ap.add_argument("--fps", type=float, default=30.0, help="pose publish rate (frames are forwarded as they arrive)")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--control-address",
        default=f"0.0.0.0:{CONTROL_PORT}",
        help="host:port to listen on for the app's OPEN_CAMERA / CLOSE_CAMERA commands",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--pose-port", type=int, default=P.POSE_PORT, help="ZMQ PUB port for the tracking state")
    ap.add_argument("--frame-port", type=int, default=P.FRAME_PORT, help="ZMQ PULL port for Eden's rendered frames")
    ap.add_argument("--no-video", action="store_true", help="publish tracking only; do not stream frames back")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--no-derived-body",
        action="store_true",
        help="skip the derived per-joint body dict and trackers; publish the lossless body_raw only",
    )
    ap.add_argument(
        "--tracker-role",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        metavar="SERIAL=ROLE",
        help="label a motion tracker by serial, e.g. --tracker-role PA1234=waist "
        "(repeatable; unmapped trackers are logged so you can add them)",
    )
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    tracker_roles = {}
    for spec in args.tracker_role:
        serial, sep, role = spec.partition("=")
        if not (serial and sep and role):
            ap.error(f"--tracker-role expects SERIAL=ROLE, got {spec!r}")
        tracker_roles[serial] = role

    # The bridge does not run Genesis, so en.init() (and its en.logger) never
    # runs here -- stand up Eden's logger directly.
    logger = getattr(en, "logger", None) or en.Logger("INFO")

    client = PicoXrClient(tracker_roles=tracker_roles)  # raises with a build hint if the SDK is missing
    video = None if args.no_video else PicoVideoLink(args.control_address, logger=logger)

    ctx = zmq.Context.instance()
    # No video, no frame channel: nothing would consume the frames, and not
    # binding keeps the port free for whoever shares this host (the SONIC
    # operator's command PUB uses the same default number, 5556).
    frame_sock = None if video is None else P.frame_pull(ctx, port=args.frame_port)
    pose_sock = P.pose_pub(ctx, port=args.pose_port)

    # Eden-styled banner: ~<...>~ mint, ~~<...>~~ mint-underline, ~~~~<...>~~~~ bold.
    rule = "━" * 64
    logger.info(f"~<{rule}>~")
    logger.info(" 🥽 ~~~~<PICO XR bridge>~~~~  (XRoboToolkit)  —  waiting for the headset")
    logger.info(" On the PICO: open ~<XRoboToolkit>~, point it at this host and tap ~<Connect>~")
    for ip in list_host_ips() or ["<host-ip>"]:
        logger.info(f"     ~~<{ip}>~~")
    logger.info(" Status must read ~<Working>~; then enable ~<Send>~ under Data & Control")
    if video is not None:
        logger.info(f" Stereo view: ~<Remote Vision>~ ~<→>~ ~<Listen>~ (Eden listens on {args.control_address})")
    frames_note = "frames off (--no-video)" if frame_sock is None else f"frames PULL ~<:{args.frame_port}>~"
    logger.info(f" ZMQ   poses PUB ~<:{args.pose_port}>~   {frames_note}")
    logger.info(f"~<{rule}>~")

    if video is not None:
        video.start()

    running = {"v": True}

    def stop(*_):
        running["v"] = False

    signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, stop)
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, stop)

    period = 1.0 / max(args.fps, 1.0)
    frames_forwarded = 0
    last_log = time.time()
    warned_at = 0.0
    seen_serials: set[str] = set()
    # Probe once up front: a fundamentally wrong SDK contract fails loud here, at
    # startup, rather than deep in the loop below.
    derived_body = not args.no_derived_body
    last_state = client.state(derived_body=derived_body)
    try:
        while running["v"]:
            loop_start = time.time()

            # Newest frame from Eden -> headset. Eden renders RGB and the encoder
            # takes RGB, so no channel flip is needed here.
            if video is not None:
                frame = P.recv_frame(frame_sock, flags=zmq.NOBLOCK)
                if frame is not None:
                    video.push(frame)
                    frames_forwarded += 1

            # Transient device noise (a momentarily malformed read) must not tear
            # down a live teleop session: log it at most every few seconds and
            # republish the last good state (the consumers CONFLATE to latest).
            try:
                last_state = client.state(derived_body=derived_body)
            except (ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
                now = time.time()
                if now - warned_at > 5.0:
                    logger.warning(f"skipping a bad PICO read: {exc}")
                    warned_at = now
            P.send_pose(pose_sock, last_state)

            # Surface each new unlabeled tracker once so the operator can map it.
            for tr in last_state.get("trackers", {}).values():
                if tr.get("role") is None and tr["serial"] not in seen_serials:
                    seen_serials.add(tr["serial"])
                    logger.info(
                        f"motion tracker {tr['serial']} is unlabeled — map it with --tracker-role {tr['serial']}=<role>"
                    )

            now = time.time()
            if now - last_log > 5.0:
                logger.info(_status(last_state, video, frames_forwarded))
                last_log = now

            dt = time.time() - loop_start
            if dt < period:
                time.sleep(period - dt)
    finally:
        logger.info("shutting down...")
        if video is not None:
            video.stop()
        client.close()

def encode_message(command: str, data: bytes = b"") -> bytes:
    """Frame one control message (length header included) ready to ``sendall``."""
    cmd = command.encode("utf-8")
    body = struct.pack("<i", len(cmd)) + cmd + struct.pack("<i", len(data)) + data
    return struct.pack(_FRAME_HEADER, len(body)) + body

def decode_message(body: bytes) -> tuple[str, bytes]:
    """Split a control-message body into ``(command, data)``.

    ``body`` is the payload *after* the 4-byte length header (see
    :func:`unpack_length`). Raises ``ValueError`` on a malformed record — the
    caller should log it and keep reading rather than tear the connection down,
    since the next message may be fine.
    """
    if len(body) < 8:
        raise ValueError(f"control body too small: {len(body)} bytes (need >= 8)")

    (cmd_len,) = struct.unpack_from("<i", body, 0)
    if cmd_len < 0 or 4 + cmd_len > len(body):
        raise ValueError(f"invalid command length {cmd_len} in a {len(body)}-byte body")
    command = body[4 : 4 + cmd_len].decode("utf-8").rstrip("\x00")

    offset = 4 + cmd_len
    if offset + 4 > len(body):
        raise ValueError(f"command {command!r} is missing its data-length field")
    (data_len,) = struct.unpack_from("<i", body, offset)
    offset += 4
    if data_len < 0 or offset + data_len > len(body):
        raise ValueError(f"invalid data length {data_len} for command {command!r}")

    return command, body[offset : offset + data_len]

def decode_camera_request(data: bytes) -> CameraRequest:
    """Decode an ``OPEN_CAMERA`` payload. Raises ``ValueError`` if malformed."""
    if len(data) < 3 + 28:
        raise ValueError(f"camera request too small: {len(data)} bytes (need >= 31)")
    if data[:2] != MAGIC:
        raise ValueError(f"bad camera-request magic: {data[:2].hex()} (expected {MAGIC.hex()})")
    if data[2] != VERSION:
        raise ValueError(f"unsupported camera-request version: {data[2]} (expected {VERSION})")

    width, height, fps, bitrate, enable_mv_hevc, render_mode, port = struct.unpack_from("<7i", data, 3)
    camera, offset = _decode_string(data, 3 + 28)
    ip, offset = _decode_string(data, offset)
    return CameraRequest(
        width=width,
        height=height,
        fps=fps,
        bitrate=bitrate,
        hevc=bool(enable_mv_hevc),
        render_mode=render_mode,
        port=port,
        camera=camera,
        ip=ip,
    )

def encode_camera_request(request: CameraRequest) -> bytes:
    """Encode a :class:`CameraRequest` back into its wire payload.

    Eden never sends this — the PICO app does. It exists so tests (and a fake
    headset client) can exercise the decoder against the documented layout.
    """
    head = MAGIC + bytes([VERSION])
    ints = struct.pack(
        "<7i",
        request.width,
        request.height,
        request.fps,
        request.bitrate,
        int(request.hevc),
        request.render_mode,
        request.port,
    )
    return head + ints + _encode_string(request.camera) + _encode_string(request.ip)

docs.title: Wuji Glove
docs.text:
Wuji Glove teleoperation device: live hand pose + tactile, in Eden's hand frame.

The glove is a plain SDK device — it streams over USB/Ethernet to wuji_sdk running in this process, so unlike the Meta Quest / PICO headsets there is no bridge process to stand up. :class:WujiGlove connects, subscribes to the streams you ask for, and keeps the newest frame of each so every getter is a cheap read that a sim loop can call once per step.

What it exposes
  • hand pose — the 21 MediaPipe landmarks (:func:~eden.utils.devices.wuji.protocol.skeleton_to_arrays), the IK solver's 21 joint angles, and the 5 fingertip poses.
  • tactile — the 24x31 palm-and-finger pressure sheet, its zone-grouped view, the calibrated binary/residual contact streams, and the 3D tactile point cloud.

Poses are returned in Eden's hand frame (x forward along the fingers, y left, z up out of the back of the hand) by default, so an axis means the same physical direction on either glove — the vendor's +y flips between dorsal and ventral by side. See :mod:eden.utils.devices.wuji.protocol for the basis change and the data layouts. Pass frame="wuji" to any getter for the vendor's raw wrist frame instead.

Install the SDK with the wuji extra (uv sync --inexact --extra wuji); it ships manylinux wheels only, so this is Linux x86_64 / aarch64.

Example

.. code-block:: python

from eden.utils.devices.wuji import WujiGlove

glove = WujiGlove(side="right", streams=("hand_skeleton", "tactile"))
keypoints = glove.get_command()          # (21, 3) torch tensor, Eden hand frame
pressure = glove.tactile()               # (24, 31), masked taxels are nan
glove.close()

Wuji Glove data layout: stream shapes, landmark tables, and the basis change into Eden.

Everything here is pure numpy and duck-typed over the SDK message objects, so the whole decode path is testable without a glove (or without wuji_sdk installed). :mod:eden.utils.devices.wuji.glove owns the connection and the subscriptions.

Frames

Wuji publishes hand data in the wrist frame (l_wrist / r_wrist), which the vendor defines anatomically (docs, Coordinate Frames)::

x = radial     (ulnar -> radial, i.e. toward the thumb)
z = proximal   (distal -> proximal, i.e. along the bone toward the elbow)
y = right-hand rule, so it MIRRORS between hands:
    left glove  +y = dorsal (back of the hand)
    right glove +y = ventral (palm)

So +y means the opposite physical direction on the two gloves. Eden pins every axis to anatomy instead, in the Genesis basis — x forward along the fingers, y left, z up — so :data:R_HAND_WUJI maps::

x_eden = -z_wuji                                  (distal, out along the fingers)
z_eden = +y_wuji (left) / -y_wuji (right)         (dorsal, out of the back of the hand)
y_eden = z_eden x x_eden = -x_wuji (left) / +x_wuji (right)

Both per-side matrices are proper rotations (det = +1), and the per-side sign flip is exactly the vendor's own note that "left-hand glove data is mirrored from the right hand, with the Y direction inverted". Note what this does not buy: y is radial on a right hand and ulnar on a left one, because a left hand is a mirrored right hand and no right-handed frame can make the two agree. x (distal) and z (dorsal) do agree, which is what a retargeter and a pose-plotting recipe actually read.

Tactile

The tactile matrix is a fixed 24 x 31 row-major grid of 744 taxels, only some of which are real; the rest are permanently pinned to :data:TACTILE_INVALID (-1.0). Two counts describe "real" and they disagree by eight — read :data:N_ACTIVE_TAXELS and :data:N_UNMASKED_TAXELS before hard-coding either, here or in prose. That sentinel is a number, so grid.mean() over a raw frame is silently wrong — :func:tactile_grid therefore turns masked taxels into nan, which fails loudly instead. Use :func:tactile_valid for the boolean mask, or :func:tactile_taxels for the node-wise view: one (index, value) entry per taxel that actually measured something, with the dead ones dropped rather than masked.

eden wuji — find a Wuji Glove and watch its hand-pose / tactile streams live.

The first thing to run after plugging a glove in: it proves the SDK sees the device, that the glove is solving a hand pose, and that the tactile sheet responds to a touch, without building a Genesis scene.

Run::

eden wuji scan                                  # list the gloves on the bus
eden wuji monitor                               # live status, Ctrl-C to stop
eden wuji monitor --side right --seconds 30
eden wuji monitor --streams hand_skeleton tactile_zones --rate-hz 30
# or, equivalently:
uv run python -m eden.utils.devices.wuji.monitor monitor

docs.text:
WujiGlove(*, sn: str | None = None, side: str | None = None, device_name: str | None = None, streams: Sequence[str] = DEFAULT_STREAMS, rate_hz: int | None = None, hand_model_path: str | None = None, exclusive: bool = False)

Bases: DeviceBase

A connected Wuji Glove, streaming hand pose and tactile into Eden.

Constructing the device scans for gloves, connects to one, and opens a background subscription per requested stream; call :meth:close when done (or use it as a context manager). Every getter returns None until that stream's first frame has arrived, so a teleop loop can hold its last pose instead of blocking.

PARAMETER DESCRIPTION sn

Serial number of the glove to connect to. None scans and picks the only glove on the bus (or the one matching side).

TYPE: str | None DEFAULT: None

side

"left" or "right". Used to pick between two connected gloves, and checked against the glove's own hand_side either way, so a mismatch raises at construction rather than silently flipping the radial axis of every pose.

TYPE: str | None DEFAULT: None

device_name

Handle this connection is registered under inside the SDK. It selects no particular glove, but it does identify the connection to disconnect, so it must be unique per live device — None (the default) takes a fresh one from :func:_next_device_name. Pass your own only if something outside Eden has to resolve the same connection.

TYPE: str | None DEFAULT: None

streams

Which of :data:STREAMS to subscribe to. Defaults to :data:DEFAULT_STREAMS.

TYPE: Sequence[str] DEFAULT: DEFAULT_STREAMS

rate_hz

Lower the device push rate of the rate-adjustable sources (:data:RATE_SOURCES) that streams needs. None keeps the device default (120 Hz). The device quantizes the request and the applied rate is logged.

TYPE: int | None DEFAULT: None

hand_model_path

Custom hand URDF for the glove's online IK, applied before subscribing. Needs a named (non-default) SDK user; without one the SDK's built-in model is used.

TYPE: str | None DEFAULT: None

exclusive

Take the glove for this process alone. By default the SDK bridges the device so Wuji Studio / a recorder can read it at the same time.

TYPE: bool DEFAULT: False

Notes

tactile_binary and tactile_residual are produced by a contact model trained per SDK user and glove serial. Subscribing to them before running the vendor's tactile calibration yields an all-zero sheet, not an error, so this device logs a warning when you ask for one.

Source code in eden/utils/devices/wuji/glove.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    sn: str | None = None,
    side: str | None = None,
    device_name: str | None = None,
    streams: Sequence[str] = DEFAULT_STREAMS,
    rate_hz: int | None = None,
    hand_model_path: str | None = None,
    exclusive: bool = False,
):
    super().__init__()

    if not streams:
        raise ValueError(
            f"'streams' is empty — the device would carry no data; pass at least one of {list(STREAMS)}"
        )
    unknown = [s for s in streams if s not in STREAMS]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown glove stream(s) {unknown}; expected a subset of {list(STREAMS)}")
    if side is not None:
        P.check_side(side)
    if rate_hz is not None and rate_hz <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"'rate_hz' must be positive (or None for the device default), got {rate_hz}")

    self._sdk = load_sdk()
    self._manager = self._sdk.SdkManager.instance()
    self._device_name = _next_device_name() if device_name is None else device_name
    # Seeded before the connect so teardown and __str__ can read them unconditionally,
    # including on the paths where the connect itself is what failed.
    self._sn = "?"
    self._side = "?"
    self._streams = tuple(dict.fromkeys(streams))  # de-duplicate, keep order
    self._latest: dict[str, Any] = {}
    self._lock = threading.Lock()
    self._subscriptions: list[Any] = []
    self._rate_handles: list[Any] = []
    self._closed = False
    self._connected = False

    options = self._sdk.ConnectOptions(enable_bridge=not exclusive)
    self._glove = self._connect(sn, side, options)
    self._sn = str(self._glove.serial_number)
    self._side = P.check_side(str(self._glove.hand_side().get()).lower())
    if side is not None and self._side != side:
        self.close()  # not `disconnect`: mark the device closed so __del__ doesn't retry
        raise RuntimeError(f"glove {self._sn} reports hand_side {self._side!r}, but {side!r} was requested")

    en.logger.info(f"Wuji Glove {self._sn} connected ({self._side} hand, FW {self._glove.version().get()})")

    if hand_model_path is not None:
        self._glove.hand_model_path().set(str(hand_model_path))
        en.logger.info(f"Wuji Glove {self._sn} online-IK hand model: {self._glove.hand_model_path().get()}")

    for stream in CALIBRATED_STREAMS:
        if stream in self._streams:
            en.logger.warning(
                f"'{stream}' comes from a contact model trained per SDK user and glove serial. "
                "Without a tactile calibration for this pair the stream stays at zero — run the "
                "vendor's tactile calibration (wuji-sdk examples/python/wuji_glove/7.tactile_calibration.py)."
            )

    try:
        if rate_hz is not None:
            self._set_rate(rate_hz)
        for stream in self._streams:
            resource = getattr(self._glove, stream)()
            self._subscriptions.append(resource.subscribe_with_callback(partial(self._on_frame, stream)))
    except BaseException:
        self.close()
        raise

def tactile_taxels(self, stream: str = "tactile", flat: bool = False) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None:
    """``(index, value)`` for just the taxels ``stream`` actually measured, or None.

    The node-wise view: one entry per live taxel, dead ones dropped rather than
    ``nan``-masked. ``index`` is ``(N, 2)`` ``(row, col)`` into the ``24 x 31`` sheet,
    or ``(N,)`` row-major ids when ``flat=True``; ``value`` is that taxel's reading.
    ``stream`` picks which sheet to read — ``tactile``, ``tactile_binary`` or
    ``tactile_residual`` — and must be one this device subscribed to.

    See :func:`~eden.utils.devices.wuji.protocol.tactile_taxels` for why ``N`` is not
    the point cloud's point count.
    """
    if stream not in TACTILE_SHEETS:
        raise ValueError(f"'{stream}' is not a tactile sheet; expected one of {list(TACTILE_SHEETS)}")
    frame = self._take(stream)
    if frame is None:
        return None
    index, value = P.tactile_taxels(frame.data, flat)
    return torch.from_numpy(index), torch.from_numpy(value).float()

def tactile_points(self, frame: str = "hand") -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor] | None:
    """``(points (N, 3), pressure (N,))`` for the 3D tactile point cloud, or None.

    The 526 real taxels placed on the live hand skeleton, so contact can be drawn in
    the scene or fed to a contact-conditioned policy.
    """
    cloud = self._take("tactile_point_cloud")
    if cloud is None:
        return None
    points, pressure = P.decode_point_cloud(cloud)
    if P.check_frame(frame) == "hand":
        points = P.wuji_points_to_hand(points, self._side)
    return torch.from_numpy(points).float(), torch.from_numpy(pressure).float()

JSON-safe snapshot of every subscribed stream, for logging or a ZMQ bridge.

Only the streams this device subscribed to appear. Tactile sheets are published as the raw flat 744-value payload with the vendor's :data:~eden.utils.devices.wuji.protocol.TACTILE_INVALID sentinel intact rather than the nan-masked grid, because nan is not valid JSON.
