  • API reference: EventManager, event terms, options.

docs.title: Adding a Policy to the Zoo
docs.text: A policy extension packages a frozen controller (an ONNX graph, a TorchScript module, a torch network, or a client for a remote server) so that eden inference --policy <name> and eden deploy --policy <name> can run it. This page covers the package layout, the PolicyBase contract, how weights are fetched, and the mistakes that produce a policy that builds and then acts on the wrong input. Faithfully reproducing a policy from another stack is its own checklist: Porting a Pretrained Policy. Server-backed policies add a transport layer on top: Remote Policy Clients.

docs.title: What a policy is
docs.text:
A policy is any object that takes the env's observations and returns actions. In Eden every policy:

  • subclasses PolicyBase (eden.extensions.policies.base) and is registered with @POLICY_REGISTRY.register();
  • declares the world it was trained in through classmethods: the robot, the other scene entities, the env options, and the observation, action and command terms;
  • implements step(obs) -> {action_term_name: tensor}, and reset(envs_idx) if it holds per-env state.

The registry key is to_snake_case(ClassName) (Twist2Policy → twist2_policy). --policy also accepts the key without _policy and the package name, as long as the package registers one policy. Policy packages are imported on demand: the CLI imports eden.extensions.policies.<pkg>.policy when it resolves a name, so a package with optional dependencies does not slow down or break the others.

docs.title: Package layout
docs.text:
One package per policy under eden/extensions/policies/<name>/:

File Contents policy.py The registered PolicyBase subclass. Required: the CLI discovers a package by this file. constants.py The frozen I/O contract: joint-name order, observation scales, default pose, gains. onnx_wrapper.py / network.py / modules.py The actor, when it is not a plain ONNX graph. custom_terms/ Observation, action or command terms only this policy needs. setups.py Per-embodiment setups, for a server-backed client that serves several robots.

Keep the package to the policy, its network and its contract. When Eden also has a training task for the policy, reuse that task's terms and scene from eden/tasks/<name>/ rather than copying them: husky builds its observation and action from eden/tasks/husky/config.py, and omnireset its scene from eden/tasks/omnireset/. A released checkpoint and a policy trained in Eden then share one layout.

Add a runnable example under examples/policies/<name>/main.py with the metadata header described in examples/AGENTS.md (tier: policy, its capabilities, hardware, optional_deps and run command), and tests under tests/extensions/policies/<name>/.

docs.title: A worked example: TWIST2
docs.text:
eden/extensions/policies/twist2/policy.py is a compact, complete policy that reads the env's observations. Its skeleton, with the class constants and the __init__ checks trimmed:

from eden import actions, observations
from eden.constants import ReferenceSource
from eden.extensions.policies.base import POLICY_REGISTRY, PolicyBase, PolicyOptions
from eden.managers.terms.commands.mimic import MotionCommand
from eden.options.managers.observations import ObservationGroupOptions
from eden.options.robots.unitree_g1 import G1Dofs29
from eden.terms import ObsTerm

# Importing the custom terms registers them before any env is built.
from eden.extensions.policies.twist2.custom_terms.observations import (
    twist2_imu_roll_pitch, twist2_motion_dofs_pos, twist2_motion_root,
)
from eden.extensions.policies.twist2.onnx_wrapper import Twist2Actor
# POLICY_JOINT_NAMES, KNEES_BENT_DOFS_POS, JOINT_SCALES, ... come from eden.extensions.policies.twist2.constants


@POLICY_REGISTRY.register()
class Twist2Policy(PolicyBase):
    """TWIST2 whole-body motion-tracking controller (G1 29-DOF, ONNX backend)."""

    reads_env_observations = True          # step() reads the observation dict the env publishes
    entity_name: str = "robot"
    checkpoint_path: str = "twist2/pretrained.onnx"
    md5_hash: str | None = "a045b72bd49ce0993aa145f8958a5564"

    def __init__(self, env, options: PolicyOptions) -> None:
        super().__init__(env, options)      # resolves and verifies checkpoint_path
        robot = self.require_entity(self.entity_name)
        # ... check robot.dofs_name, the built default pose and the observation width here ...
        self._actor = Twist2Actor(self.checkpoint_path, device=str(env.device))

    @classmethod
    def robot_options(cls) -> G1Dofs29:
        return G1Dofs29(default_dofs_pos=dict(KNEES_BENT_DOFS_POS), default_root_pos=(0.0, 0.0, 0.76))

    @classmethod
    def env_options(cls) -> dict:
        return dict(sim_dt=0.01, sim_substeps=2, decimation=2, ...)   # 50 Hz control

    @classmethod
    def action_options(cls, entity_name: str = "robot") -> dict:
        return dict(
            dofs_pos_controller=actions.ImplicitPDController.configure(
                entity_name=entity_name,
                dofs_name=list(POLICY_JOINT_NAMES),
                scale=dict(zip(POLICY_JOINT_NAMES, JOINT_SCALES)),
                reference_source=ReferenceSource.DEFAULT,
            ),
        )

    @classmethod
    def command_options(cls, motion_file: str = "motion.npz", entity_name: str = "robot", ...) -> dict:
        return dict(motion=MotionCommand.configure(motion_file=motion_file, entity_name=entity_name, ...))

    @classmethod
    def observation_options(cls, entity_name: str = "robot") -> dict:
        entity = {"entity_name": entity_name}
        return {
            "policy": ObservationGroupOptions(
                enable_corruption=False,
                history_length=ACTOR_HISTORY_LENGTH,
                flatten_history_dim=True,
                motion_root=ObsTerm.configure(func=twist2_motion_root),
                motion_dofs_pos=ObsTerm.configure(func=twist2_motion_dofs_pos),
                base_ang_vel=ObsTerm.configure(
                    func=observations.base_ang_vel, params={**entity, "frame": "body"}, scale=BASE_ANG_VEL_SCALE
                ),
                imu_roll_pitch=ObsTerm.configure(func=twist2_imu_roll_pitch, params=entity),
                dofs_pos=observations.DofsPos.configure(entity_name=entity_name, offset_from_default=True),
                dofs_vel=observations.DofsVel.configure(entity_name=entity_name, scale=list(JOINT_VEL_SCALES)),
                last_action=ObsTerm.configure(func=observations.last_action),
            )
        }

    def step(self, obs):
        history = obs["policy"]             # (N, 11 * 127), oldest frame first
        actor_obs = torch.cat([history[:, -ACTOR_CURRENT_DIM:], history], dim=-1)
        return {"dofs_pos_controller": self._actor(actor_obs)}

docs.title: Class attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Default Meaning checkpoint_path None The main checkpoint, relative to the policy's Hugging Face dataset. __init__ replaces it with the local path, downloading on first use. md5_hash None The MD5 the downloaded file must match; None skips the check. registry Eden's policy repository owner The Hugging Face owner of the dataset (a class constant). dataset "eden_policies" The Hugging Face dataset holding the weights (a class constant). local_dir None The cache directory; None means assets_subdir under the asset root (a class constant). assets_subdir "policies" The subdirectory of the asset root an unset local_dir means. reads_env_observations False Whether step() consumes the env's observation dict (see below).

Any other annotated class attribute (entity_name, hand_name, pair, …) is a configurable parameter: MyPolicy.configure(entity_name="g1") sets it, and the spec classmethods can read it (next section).

docs.title: Classmethods: the world the policy was trained in
docs.text:
Classmethod Required Returns robot_options() no The robot options with the training pose, gains and armature, or None to use --robot. Takes no arguments. scene_entity_options() no {name: entity options} for every non-robot entity step() or the observations read. A plane entity replaces the flat ground. env_options() no EnvOptions fields: at least sim_dt and decimation. Takes no arguments. action_options() yes {term_name: action term options}. observation_options() yes {group_name: ObservationGroupOptions}. May be {}. command_options() no {term_name: command term options}.

In action_options, observation_options and scene_entity_options, a parameter named after one of the policy's configurable attributes is filled from that attribute: declare hand_name: str = "hand" on the class and action_options(cls, entity_name="robot", hand_name="hand") receives cls.hand_name. So a name is declared once, instead of restated as a literal that can drift from it. entity_name is the caller's (--entity_name wins), and any other parameter keeps its default, which means a knob that must keep its literal default needs a name no attribute uses.

command_options is filled by the CLI instead: entity_name, motion_file (from --motion_file, and required whenever the signature takes it), and clip_name (from --clip_name, when the signature takes it).

docs.title: env_options: match the control rate
docs.text:
sim_dt × decimation is the time per policy step, and it must match the training setup. A policy that does not override env_options() runs at the env's defaults and will very likely perform poorly. The shipped values:

Policy sim_dt decimation Control rate amo 0.002 s 10 50 Hz gmt 0.001 s 20 50 Hz holosoma, husky 0.005 s 4 50 Hz sonic, twist2, protomotionv3, humanoid_gpt 0.01 s 2 50 Hz omnixtreme 0.004 s 5 50 Hz metamotivo 1/450 s 15 30 Hz

Solver settings (iterations, substeps, contact options) belong here too when the training simulator's differ.

docs.title: step() and reset()
docs.text:
• obs keys are the group names from observation_options(). A group with concatenate_terms=False arrives as a dict of its terms (obs["wrist_image"]["image"]), which is how camera images are delivered.
  • The returned dict's keys must be the term names from action_options(). An unknown key raises a KeyError. A term the dict leaves out is not an error: it keeps its previous action, silently. Return every term on every step.
  • Return tensors on self.env.device, and run inference under torch.no_grad() (or torch.inference_mode()).
  • Override reset(envs_idx) when the policy holds per-env state across steps (a recurrent state, a last-action history it builds itself, an action-chunk queue). eden inference calls it with the envs that just ended an episode; envs_idx=None means all envs.

docs.title: Observations: declare them, or read raw state
docs.text:
reads_env_observations says which side of the env boundary step() sits on, and eden deploy arranges a run around the answer, so treat it as a contract:

  • True: the policy owns the env. The env is built from its observation groups and action terms, and its action goes through the env's action manager, which keeps env-computed observations such as last_action in step with what the robot was commanded. This is the preferred form: the layout is explicit, and the observation manager handles history, scale, NaN policy and resets. Only one such policy can be loaded at a time, and not alongside a task, since one env publishes one observation layout.
  • False: the policy reads raw state. step() reads the robot's state off the entity and builds the input itself (holosoma, homie, sonic). Such a policy can ride along as an extra slot on another policy's env, converting its own actions; its observation_options() may return {}.

Rules that keep an observation correct:

  • The term order is the layout. Terms concatenate in declaration order (or terms_order, when set), and the network only sees numbers: a wrong order is dimensionally valid and silently wrong.
  • History is oldest first. With history_length=H and flatten_history_dim=True, a group of frame width D arrives as (N, H * D) with the newest frame last (obs[g][:, -D:]). With flatten_history_dim=False it is (N, H, D). At an episode start the window is filled with the first frame when backfill=True (the default), or with zeros when backfill=False.
  • Turn training noise off. Pass enable_corruption=False on a group whose term definitions carry noise (for example terms shared with a training task), as husky and twist2 do.
  • A declared group needs at least one term. No groups at all builds fine; a concatenate_terms=True group with no terms fails at construction with Unable to concatenate observation terms in group `<name>`.

docs.title: Entities and commands
docs.text:
• Resolve every entity in __init__ with self.require_entity(name). A scene without it then fails at construction with a message that says where the entity should come from (the policy's scene_entity_options() in a task-less run, the task's scene with --task). In step(), read self.env.entities[name] instead of caching the handle: deployment swaps the entity for a live-robot stand-in.
  • Check the built robot against the contract in __init__. The shipped ports refuse a robot whose dofs_name is not the policy's joint order, or whose built default pose differs from the training keyframe in any env (robot.get_default_dofs_pos(POLICY_JOINT_NAMES) is (num_envs, n) in that order), and an env whose observation group has the wrong width. Copy those checks; they turn a silent wrong-input rollout into an error.
  • A command-driven policy defines set_command(command) and a _commands buffer. --base_command VX VY WZ is padded with zeros or truncated to the width of policy._commands (HOMIE's is 4-D, HUSKY's 2-D) before set_command is called. A policy whose command lives on a command term exposes _commands as a property that reads the term, as HuskyPolicy does.
  • A command term a frozen policy observes must tick in pre_physics_advance, never in post_physics_refresh, which a deployment does not run.

docs.title: Custom terms
docs.text:
A term only the policy needs goes in custom_terms/, registered like any other term (see Writing Terms):

# eden/extensions/policies/mypolicy/custom_terms/observations.py
import torch

from eden.envs.base import EnvBase
from eden.managers.observation_manager import OBSERVATION_TERM_REGISTRY


@OBSERVATION_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def mypolicy_root_height(env: EnvBase, *, entity_name: str = "robot") -> torch.Tensor:
    return env.entities[entity_name].get_pos()[:, 2:3]

The built-in term registries find their terms by importing the modules they list, and a policy's custom_terms/ is not among them, so import every custom term module in policy.py (at module level). The CLI imports policy.py before it builds the env, and the import registers the terms. Prefix a policy-only term's name with the policy's (twist2_imu_roll_pitch): term keys share one namespace across Eden.

A custom action term is needed when the robot's actuators differ from Eden's controllers (MetaMotivo's SMPL humanoid uses MuJoCo-style affine actuators, MujocoSMPLActuator); a custom command term when the policy consumes a signal no built-in command produces (AMOCommand, GMT's GMTMotionLibCommand).

docs.title: Weights
docs.text:
PolicyBase.__init__ fetches checkpoint_path with the class's fetch_asset(), which downloads from the registry/dataset Hugging Face dataset into resolve_local_dir() (local_dir, else assets_subdir under the asset root), and checks md5_hash. Fetch every further file the same way, with self.fetch_asset(path):

  • Never call get_asset_path(..., local_dir=self.local_dir) yourself. An unset local_dir is None and means "assets_subdir under the asset root", resolved at load time; passing the raw None fetches into the asset root instead.
  • registry, dataset, local_dir and assets_subdir are class constants, not options: passing one to configure() raises. That keeps a lookup made before any instance exists (a clip catalog read by command_options(), a file an observation term loads) on the same path as __init__: call MyPolicy.fetch_asset(path) on the class.
Scenario What to do One .pt / .onnx file Set checkpoint_path and md5_hash. Several files Keep the main one in checkpoint_path; name the others <prefix>checkpoint_path / <prefix>md5_hash (decoder_checkpoint_path, residual_checkpoint_path) and fetch and verify them in __init__. The naming lets use_local_checkpoint(path, checkpoint_attr=...) redirect any of them. A model loaded from Hugging Face by its own library (metamotivo) Set checkpoint_path = None, registry = None, dataset = None, and load in __init__. Weights from another dataset (beyondmimic_moves) Override registry and dataset on the class. No released weights (limx_oli_loco) checkpoint_path = None, registry = None, dataset = None, and raise in __init__ when no local file was given.

To run local weights, call MyPolicy.use_local_checkpoint(path) before constructing the policy: it sets the path and clears the MD5 pinned to the released file together. To fetch from a mirror, export EDEN_ASSETS_DIR=/data/mirror (policies then cache under /data/mirror/policies/), or set MyPolicy.local_dir = "/data/mirror" on the class before anything reads it.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
eden inference --policy mypolicy --vis                 # task-less: the policy's own world
eden inference --policy mypolicy --async --vis         # deployment-style timing
eden deploy --policy mypolicy --mujoco --vis           # MuJoCo sim-to-sim (see Deployment)

From Python, build the env from the policy's spec the way a task-less run does:

import eden as en
import genesis as gs

from eden.envs.base import RLEnvBase
from eden.extensions.policies.twist2.policy import Twist2Policy
from eden.options.envs import EnvOptions
from eden.options.managers.actions import ActionManagerOptions
from eden.options.managers.commands import CommandManagerOptions
from eden.options.managers.observations import ObservationManagerOptions
from eden.utils.configs import EdenRLConfig

en.init(backend=gs.gpu)

cfg = EdenRLConfig(
    env_options=EnvOptions(num_envs=1, **Twist2Policy.env_options()),
    scene_options=en.scenes.Empty(robot=Twist2Policy.robot_options(), **Twist2Policy.scene_entity_options()),
    action_options=ActionManagerOptions(**Twist2Policy.action_options()),
    observation_options=ObservationManagerOptions(**Twist2Policy.observation_options()),
    command_options=CommandManagerOptions(**Twist2Policy.command_options(motion_file="motion.npz")),
)
env = RLEnvBase.from_config(cfg, eval_mode=True)
env.build()
policy = Twist2Policy(env=env, options=Twist2Policy.configure())

obs, _ = env.reset()
policy.reset()
for _ in range(1000):
    obs, *_ = env.step(policy.step(obs))

The CLI's version of this is _build_extension_env in eden/utils/cli/tasks.py, which the policy tests use too. Calling the spec classmethods directly skips the CLI's attribute filling, so pass any parameter that names a configured attribute yourself.

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
• PolicyBase subclass in eden/extensions/policies/<name>/policy.py, decorated with @POLICY_REGISTRY.register().
  • checkpoint_path and md5_hash set, or the weight source handled as in Weights.
  • robot_options() with the training pose, gains and armature; scene_entity_options() for every other entity the policy reads.
  • env_options() with the training sim_dt and decimation (and solver settings that differ).
  • action_options() keys equal the keys step() returns, on every step.
  • Observation groups in the training order, history oldest first, training noise off.
  • reads_env_observations set to match what step() reads.
  • __init__ resolves every entity with require_entity and checks the built robot and the observation width.
  • Every custom term module imported in policy.py.
  • An example in examples/policies/<name>/main.py with its metadata header, and tests in tests/extensions/policies/<name>/ that pin the observation and action contract.
  • Verified layer by layer as in Porting a Pretrained Policy.

docs.title: Grasp sampling
docs.text:
A grasp sampler turns the point cloud of one entity into ranked 6-DoF grasp poses that you can hand straight to inverse kinematics. Eden wraps two learned backends behind one interface, GraspSamplerBase (eden/extensions/grasp_sampling/base.py). This page covers installing them, sampling, the frame each pose places (the part that is easy to get wrong), where the object's points come from, checking grasps against the scene, and adding a backend.

Backend Model Grippers Collision filter GraspGenXSampler (eden.extensions.grasp_sampling.graspgenx) GraspGenX: one model, conditioned on a gripper description every gripper GraspGenX has a description of, picked by name (GraspGenXGripper) — parallel jaws and dexterous hands no (see below) GraspGenSampler (eden.extensions.grasp_sampling.graspgen) GraspGen: one model per gripper franka_panda, robotiq_2f_140, suction_cup_30mm yes

docs.title: Sample grasps
docs.text:
from eden.extensions.grasp_sampling.graspgenx import GraspGenXSampler

sampler = GraspGenXSampler(env, GraspGenXSampler.configure(end_effector="FrankaEmikaPanda"))
result = sampler.sample_grasps("mustard")        # GraspResult, best first
robot = env.entities["robot"]
qpos = robot.inverse_kinematics(sampler.pose_link_name, result.pos[:1], result.quat[:1])

env is a built env holding the target entity and, for the default object_cloud="camera", a camera named by camera_name (default "camera"). The model loads at construction and runs on CUDA only; the Eden env itself may stay on gs.cpu.

A GraspResult holds world-frame pos (n, 3), wxyz quat (n, 4) and confidences (n,) on the env's device, in descending confidence, so they go straight into inverse_kinematics or a setter. result.success is false when no grasp cleared grasp_threshold (or the collision filter). Each pose places the link sampler.pose_link_name — see Which link a pose places.

Runnable versions:

  • examples/recipes/planning/grasp_sampling_graspgenx.py — the Franka hand or a UR5e with a Robotiq 2F-85, IK onto the grasps, and a collision check in simulation.
  • examples/recipes/planning/grasp_sampling_graspgenx_hands.py — every GraspGenX end-effector Eden pairs (the parallel jaws and the dexterous hands) placed at its grasps on YCB objects, the fingers closed, and the contacts reported.
  • examples/recipes/planning/grasp_sampling_graspgen.py — GraspGen with its collision filter on a Franka.

docs.title: Batched envs
docs.text:
sample_grasps(name, env_idx=0) samples one env. sample_grasps_batch(name, envs_idx=None) samples several (all of them by default) with one render and one model call, where a call per env would render the whole batch each time; a scripted demonstrator running one routine per env samples every env there first.

With num_envs > 1, a camera the sampler reads must render each env on its own — EnvOptions(env_separate_rigid=True) or the batch renderer — because a shared view holds every env's copy of the target under one segmentation id. The sampler checks this at construction. object_cloud="surface" reads no camera.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
Each backend is an extra; they install side by side:

pip install 'eden-world[graspgenx]'    # or, in a checkout: uv sync --inexact --extra graspgenx
pip install 'eden-world[graspgen]'     # then run `grasp_gen download` and export GRASPGEN_CHECKPOINT_DIR as it prints
  • graspgenx installs eden-graspgenx (import name graspgenx), an inference-only packaging of GraspGenX. Its checkpoints and gripper descriptions download from Hugging Face on first use. To run offline, point GRASPGENX_CHECKPOINT_DIR (a directory holding gen/ and dis/) and GRASPGENX_GRIPPER_CFG_DIR at local copies, or pass checkpoint_dir=.
  • graspgen installs eden-grasp-gen (import name grasp_gen), under NVIDIA's non-commercial license. gripper_config= is a path, or a path relative to GRASPGEN_CHECKPOINT_DIR.
  • Both are pure-Python wheels with floor-only pins, so neither downgrades Eden's dependencies.

A missing package raises an ImportError carrying the install command.

docs.title: Which link a pose places
docs.text:
Both models return grasp frames: z is the approach direction and x the direction the fingers close along, whatever the gripper. A grasp frame is generally no link of the real gripper, and driving a link to it anyway fails quietly — a parallel jaw closes 90° off its intended axis, a hand lands upside down — while the poses look plausible until the fingers close. So each pose places a named link, sampler.pose_link_name:

  • With end_effector= — the Eden robot that executes the grasps, by its options class name. It picks the backend's gripper (gripper_name for GraspGenX, gripper_config for GraspGen) and makes each pose a pose of that robot's link. Only pairings checked against the Eden robot are offered: each backend's END_EFFECTORS, typed as a Literal (GraspGenXEndEffector, GraspGenEndEffector). Passing end_effector= together with a different gripper option raises.
  • Without it, GraspGenX's poses place the description's base link (its URDF welds that link to the grasp frame through a fixed world_joint, which the sampler applies), and GraspGen's are its bare grasp frame (pose_link_name is None). Mapping either onto an Eden link is then yours, and needs the check below first.
end_effector Backend gripper Eden link the pose places FrankaEmikaPanda, FrankaHand GraspGenX franka_panda hand FrankaEmikaPanda, FrankaHand GraspGen graspgen_franka_panda.yml hand: the grasp frame turned 90° about z Robotiq2f85 GraspGenX robotiq_2f_85 the root, world (not the gripper's base link) SharpaWave_R GraspGenX sharpa_wave the root, right_hand_C_MC WujiHand1_R GraspGenX wuji_hand the root, right_palm_link (WujiHand2Beta2_R is a different hand) InspireRH56_R GraspGenX inspire_hand the root, base: the description's base after a half turn about (0, 1, −1)/√2

tests/extensions/grasp_sampling/test_end_effectors.py checks every row on the built Eden robot: a parallel jaw's pads, open, must straddle the TCP along the closing axis (within 1 cm), and a dexterous hand's links must sit where its GraspGenX description puts them. For GraspGen on YCB objects, the bare grasp frame put the Franka hand into the cracker box and the mustard bottle on all ten best grasps; turned the quarter turn, 7 and 9 of them cleared and the best pinched (recorded next to GraspGenSampler.END_EFFECTORS).

A new pairing is an EndEffectorPairing(gripper, link_name, link_in_frame) in the backend's END_EFFECTORS, where link_in_frame is the Eden link's pose in the frame the backend's poses place without a pairing. Add it to that test as well.

Besides the pose, the sampler exposes what executing a grasp needs, all in the posed link's frame: sampler.tcp_offset (the point the grasp puts on the object), sampler.closing_axis, and sampler.approach_axis (to back off a pregrasp along). GraspGenX also gives the description's open_dofs_pos / close_dofs_pos, by joint name. Eden's dexterous hands share those joint names (sharpa_wave with SharpaWave_R, inspire_hand with InspireRH56_R), so the configuration a grasp assumes applies to them as is.

gripper_name is typed as GraspGenXGripper, a Literal of the descriptions GraspGenX ships, grouped by kind (parallel_2f, revolute_2f, revolute_3f), so an editor offers them. The descriptions found on disk at construction are what is checked, so a custom description under GRASPGENX_GRIPPER_CFG_DIR works too.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Shared options (GraspSamplerOptions, eden/options/extensions/grasp_sampling.py), passed to <Backend>.configure(...):

Option Default Meaning camera_name "camera" Camera whose point cloud is read (for object_cloud="camera" and the collision filter). It must use the legacy camera backend — no sensor_options — which renders point clouds and segmentation. object_cloud "camera" "camera" or "surface"; see below. surface_points 2048 Points sampled over the surface when object_cloud="surface". grasp_threshold 0.8 (GraspGenX: 0.7) Confidence a grasp needs to be returned. GraspGenX's confidences run lower than GraspGen's. num_grasps 200 Grasps proposed per inference pass, before thresholding. max_grasps None Keep at most this many of the best grasps. filter_collisions False Drop grasps whose gripper collision mesh comes within collision_threshold (0.02 m) of the obstacle cloud. collision_ignore_entities None Entities left out of the obstacle cloud. None leaves out every actuated entity (the arm about to move); [] keeps all. Names are checked at construction. max_scene_points 8192 The obstacle cloud is downsampled to this many points. end_effector None See above.

GraspGenX adds gripper_name, checkpoint_dir, planner and graspmoe. planner="graspmoe" (the default) scores the diffusion model's grasps together with grasps swept over the object's oriented bounding box, which helps on boxy objects; "diffusion" returns the diffusion model's grasps alone. graspmoe is a GraspMoEOptions holding the bounding-box sweep's knobs. GraspGen adds gripper_config.

docs.title: Where the object's points come from
docs.text:
object_cloud picks the cloud the model sees:

  • "camera" (default) — the pixels of the entity that camera_name sees, through its segmentation. That is what a real robot has. The model centres its grasps on the visible part, so on a round object seen from one side the grasp centre is offset toward the camera — an offset a parallel jaw with little spare stroke may not absorb.
  • "surface" — points sampled over the entity's whole surface (no camera needed). Grasps are centred on the true object, but the hidden underside is included, so the model also proposes grasps from below whatever the object rests on; the reachability and collision checks below reject those.

A camera that sees none of the entity raises a ValueError instead of returning an empty result: "nothing to sample from" and "the model found no grasp" (result.success is False) are different failures.

docs.title: Checking a grasp against the scene
docs.text:
filter_collisions=True drops grasps whose gripper collision mesh comes within collision_threshold of the camera's obstacle cloud — every entity but the target and the ignored ones. Only GraspGen supports it. GraspGenX refuses it at construction: none of its descriptions ships a collision mesh (coll_mesh.obj), and GraspGenX substitutes a 1 cm box that every grasp clears.

Check a GraspGenX grasp in simulation instead: IK the arm onto it, set the fingers open, and call detect_collision() on the arm and gripper entities. That runs the narrow phase on the posed geometry without stepping, against the real collision geometry of everything in the scene. Subtract the pairs already in contact at the home pose (a gripper welded onto its flange) and ignore pairs with the target. examples/recipes/planning/grasp_sampling_graspgenx.py does exactly this.

docs.title: Adding a backend
docs.text:
1. Subclass GraspSamplerBase and implement _infer(object_points) -> (grasp frames (k, 4, 4), confidences (k,)) in world frame. Override _infer_batch(clouds) too if the model batches. The base class reads the clouds, filters, places the posed link, ranks, applies max_grasps and packs the result.
  2. At the end of __init__, call _set_pose_frame(link_name, grasp_T_frame, tcp_in_grasp) to name the frame the poses place without a pairing.
  3. List the verified pairings in END_EFFECTORS and name the option that selects the gripper in _gripper_option.
  4. If the backend's grippers carry collision geometry, implement _collision_free(grasps, scene_points) -> mask on grasp frames. Otherwise leave it: the base class then refuses filter_collisions=True at construction, quoting _no_collision_filter_reason, which you can override to say why.
  5. Register it with @GRASP_SAMPLER_REGISTRY.register() and add its module to the registry's populated_by.

  • Scripted demonstrations — routines that execute grasps.

  • Sensors and rendering — cameras, segmentation and the batch renderer.

docs.title: Metrics and recorders
docs.text:
The metric manager measures how well each env is doing: it computes named quantities once per step, decides whether the task succeeded, and logs per-episode means such as Metrics/Success. The recorder manager writes rollouts to disk: actions, observations, states and RL buffers, one episode per file entry. This page covers both, for task authors who need a success signal or a quantity shared by several terms, and for anyone recording demonstrations or system-identification data.

Every environment class supports both managers, configured through metric_options and recorder_options (fields of EdenConfig); a task that declares no metric terms has env.metric_manager is None.

docs.title: A first example
docs.text:
A pick-and-place task declares success as "the source object rests on the target" (eden/tasks/simpler/bridge_table/config.py):

from eden.managers.terms.metrics.proximity import object_a_is_on_b
from eden.options.managers.metrics import MetricManagerOptions
from eden.terms import MetricTerm

metric_options = MetricManagerOptions(
    placement=MetricTerm.configure(
        func=object_a_is_on_b,
        params={"entity_a_name": "source", "entity_b_name": "target"},
    ),
)

object_a_is_on_b returns 1.0 or 0.0 per env. With the defaults below (higher is better, threshold 1.0, judged every step), an episode counts as a success when the object is on the target on its last step. The env logs Metrics/placement, Metrics/Success and Metrics/Progress for every finished episode, and the on_success termination can end the episode as soon as it happens.

A task with no metric terms has env.metric_manager is None.

docs.title: Fields every metric term has
How success is decided
docs.text:
Each step (phase 6, after physics and before terminations and rewards), the manager computes every term, then:

  • success_buf is True for an env when every INTERVAL term that contributes to success succeeds on this step's value. RESET-mode terms never enter it, and with no contributing INTERVAL term it is never True. The on_success termination, the TaskSuccess reward and the recorder's per-episode success label all read it.

When an env's episode ends (phase 13), the manager judges the episode:

  • each INTERVAL term counts if it succeeded on the episode's last step;
  • each RESET-mode term counts if its episode value succeeds (the last step's value, or the per-step mean for a cumulative term);
  • Metrics/Progress is the fraction of contributing terms that counted, and Metrics/Success is 1 when all of them did;
  • Metrics/<name> is each term's episode value.

The Metrics/* values are means over the envs that ended an episode in that step, returned in the step's extras["log"] (the RSL-RL runner logs them every step). An env whose physics Genesis flagged as corrupt in that step (a NaN contact, a diverged solve) has its metric values zeroed and is left out of every success check and every mean.

metric_mode="reset" does not exclude a term from Metrics/Success

A RESET-mode term is still judged, only at the end of the episode instead of every step, and Metrics/Success requires it. For a metric that exists for monitoring or to feed other terms and has no notion of success, set contributes_to_success=False: it is then left out of success_buf, Metrics/Success, Metrics/Progress and the recorder's success label, and its threshold and direction are unused.

A diagnostic error metric left at the defaults pins Metrics/Success at 0

The defaults are higher-is-better with threshold 1.0. A tracking error of a few centimetres never reaches 1.0, so it fails every episode and drags Metrics/Success to zero with it. Give such a term direction="lib" and a meaningful threshold, or contributes_to_success=False.

eden inference prints the mean of every Metrics/* key over the finished episodes when the rollout ends, reading each env's last episode from metric_manager.last_episode(). With --episodes N it counts each env's first ceil(N / num_envs) episodes and runs until every env has finished them.

docs.title: Using a metric from other terms
docs.text:
Compute a quantity once as a metric and pull it by name wherever it is needed, instead of recomputing it in each term or storing it on env. The metric manager runs at phase 6, before the observation tick (7), terminations (8) and rewards (9), so what they pull is this step's value.

Term Kind Reads rewards.MetricReward(metric_name=...) reward The metric's value, times the reward weight. Rejects a cumulative metric unless allow_cumulative=True. observations.MetricObservation(metric_name=...) observation The value as a (num_envs, 1) observation. terminations.OnMetricSuccess(metric_name=...) termination The metric's own success check on this step (INTERVAL, success-contributing metrics only). terminations.MetricAbove(metric_name=..., threshold=...) termination value > threshold; accepts a contributes_to_success=False metric, such as a collision flag. terminations.on_success termination success_buf: every success metric holds this step. rewards.TaskSuccess reward 1 on a step where success_buf holds; raises at build when there is no INTERVAL success metric. 
from eden import observations, rewards
from eden.options import ObservationGroupOptions
from eden.options.managers.rewards import RewardManagerOptions

reward_options = RewardManagerOptions(
    score=rewards.MetricReward.configure(metric_name="my_score", weight=1.0),
)
policy = ObservationGroupOptions(
    score=observations.MetricObservation.configure(metric_name="my_score"),
)

All of these resolve the metric in build(), so a missing metric manager or an unknown name raises at env construction with the active metrics listed. In your own terms, the accessors are:

  • env.metric_manager.get_value(name) — the per-env value buffer, updated in place every step (hold on to it if you like; treat it as read-only). For a cumulative metric it is the running episode sum.
  • is_cumulative(name), is_current_step_success(name), success_buf, progress_buf, num_step_success_terms.
  • last_episode() — each env's last finished episode as Metrics/* values plus a healthy mask, for evaluations that pick which episodes to count.

For an intermediate shared by several terms that is not itself a metric, use env.compute_once(key, producer); see Terms.

docs.title: Built-in metric terms
docs.text:
All built-ins live in eden.managers.terms.metrics (also eden.metrics). eden terms --kind metric prints them with every parameter, and the generated term catalog has the same list.

Group Terms Proximity entity_distance, entity_distance_xy (lower is better), entity_near_target, entity_near_entity_xy, EeNearEntity (mean end-effector position within threshold of an entity), object_a_is_on_b, object_a_within_b_xy Containment object_above_height, object_bottom_above_height, object_in_region Grasp object_lifted, IsGrasping (parallel-jaw grasp from contact-force alignment) Articulation joint_angle_at_target Velocity tracking error_vel_xy, error_vel_yaw (cumulative, lower is better, judged at reset; read a velocity command term) Composition MetricTermAND, MetricTermOR, MetricTermNOT, SequentialMetricTerm, RubricMetricTerm

The boolean combinators work on the child terms' raw values: AND is the element-wise minimum, OR the maximum, NOT is 1.0 - value. The children's own thresholds and directions are not consulted, so combine predicates that already return 0 or 1.

docs.title: Ordered sub-goals
docs.text:
SequentialMetricTerm tracks phases that must be completed in order, per env; its value is the fraction of phases completed. Each PhaseOptions gives either an inline term or a ref to a sibling metric by its key, a threshold (default 1.0) the phase's value must reach, and optionally a hold: with hold=True the phase's own predicate (or hold_term) must keep holding while later phases run, until the phase named by hold_until, or the env reverts to it. hold_guard suppresses a hold while another phase's hold still passes (lowering an object while still grasping it is not a failure). allow_skip=True lets an env advance through several phases in one step. From examples/recipes/teleop/keyboard/teleoperation_keyboard_metrics.py, trimmed:

from eden.managers.terms.metrics import IsGrasping, SequentialMetricTerm, object_a_is_on_b
from eden.options.managers.metrics import MetricManagerOptions, PhaseOptions
from eden.terms import MetricTerm

metric_options = MetricManagerOptions(
    is_grasping=IsGrasping.configure(
        robot_name="robot",
        left_gripper_link_name="left_gripper_pad",
        right_gripper_link_name="right_gripper_pad",
        contributes_to_success=False,
    ),
    task_progress=SequentialMetricTerm.configure(
        phases=[
            PhaseOptions(name="grasp", ref="is_grasping", hold=True, hold_until="place"),
            PhaseOptions(
                name="place",
                term=MetricTerm.configure(
                    func=object_a_is_on_b, params={"entity_a_name": "apple", "entity_b_name": "plate"}
                ),
            ),
        ],
    ),
)

(The example script marks its helper metrics metric_mode=MetricMode.RESET instead; per the warning above, contributes_to_success=False is what keeps them out of Metrics/Success.)

RubricMetricTerm scores a list of CriterionOptions(name=..., term=..., after=[...]). A criterion is reached the first step its term succeeds (by the term's own direction and threshold) while every criterion in its after list has been reached, and it stays reached until the env resets. Criteria without a dependency between them are reached in any order. The value is the fraction reached. eden/tasks/polaris uses it.

docs.title: Writing a metric term
docs.text:
A function metric takes the env and keyword parameters and returns one value per env:

import torch

from eden.managers import METRIC_TERM_REGISTRY


@METRIC_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def entity_speed(env, *, entity_name: str) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Linear speed of an entity's root, in m/s."""
    return torch.linalg.vector_norm(env.get_entity(entity_name).get_vel(), dim=-1)

from eden.terms import MetricTerm

cup_at_rest = MetricTerm.configure(
    func=entity_speed, params={"entity_name": "cup"}, direction="lib", success_threshold=0.01
)

The value is cast to float. For state across steps, a build() to resolve names, or a custom reset(), subclass eden.managers.MetricTerm and implement compute(self); IsGrasping in eden/managers/terms/metrics/grasp.py is a short example. A class term may also override is_success(value, envs_idx=None) for a custom success rule. The general rules (resolve names in build(), no state on env, no GPU→CPU syncs) are in Terms.

docs.title: Recording a rollout
docs.text:
The recorder manager is idle until you start it. Configure the recorder terms you want, then bracket the steps to record (eden/extensions/scripted_demos/generate.py does exactly this):

from eden.constants import DatasetExportMode
from eden.managers.terms.recorders import (
    ActionRecorder,
    InitialStateRecorder,
    ObservationRecorder,
    RLStepRecorder,
    StateRecorder,
)
from eden.options.managers.recorders import RecorderManagerOptions
from eden.utils.file_handler.hdf5_file_handler import HDF5FileHandler

config.recorder_options = RecorderManagerOptions(
    file_handler_options=HDF5FileHandler.configure(),
    dataset_export_dir_path="datasets",
    dataset_filename="demos",
    dataset_export_mode=DatasetExportMode.EXPORT_ALL,
    override=True,
    observations=ObservationRecorder.configure(),
    actions=ActionRecorder.configure(),
    rl_step=RLStepRecorder.configure(),
    state=StateRecorder.configure(entity_name="robot"),
    initial_state=InitialStateRecorder.configure(),
)

# ... build and reset the env ...
recorder = env.recorder_manager
recorder.start_recording()
for _ in range(num_steps):
    env.step(policy(obs))
recorder.end_recording()
recorder.close()
  • start_recording(reset_scene=False) opens the dataset file and starts an episode per env from the current state; with reset_scene=True it resets the env first. It does nothing (with a warning) when no recorder term is configured.
  • Every episode that ends while recording is exported when it ends.
  • end_recording(export_unfinished=True) stops recording and, by default, exports the episodes still in progress as they stand. Pass export_unfinished=False to drop them when only complete episodes belong in the dataset.
  • close() ends a running recording and closes the file.

eden datagen, the teleoperation tools and eden lerobot convert build on this; see Scripted demonstrations, Teleoperation and Datasets and recording for the HDF5 layout and conversion.

docs.title: Recorder manager options
docs.text:
Field Default Meaning file_handler_options NPZFileHandler.configure() The file format: NPZFileHandler (.npz) or HDF5FileHandler (.hdf5), both in eden.utils.file_handler. dataset_export_dir_path <system temp dir>/eden/logs Directory the dataset is written to. dataset_filename "dataset" File name without extension. dataset_export_mode DatasetExportMode.EXPORT_ALL Which episodes are written (below). override False Replace an existing file instead of appending to it. <term name> — Any number of recorder terms.

DatasetExportMode (eden.constants): EXPORT_ALL writes every episode to one file; EXPORT_SUCCEEDED_ONLY writes successful ones and drops the rest; EXPORT_SUCCEEDED_FAILED_IN_SEPARATE_FILES writes failures to <dataset_filename>_failed; EXPORT_NONE writes nothing.

An existing dataset is appended to by default

With override=False, a file already at dataset_export_dir_path/dataset_filename is opened in append mode and new episodes are added after the ones it holds. Set override=True for a fresh file, and change the default directory: the system temp directory may not survive a reboot.

An episode's success label is metric_manager.success_buf on its last step, set by RLEnvBase.step. It therefore reflects only the INTERVAL metrics that contribute to success; a task whose success metrics are all RESET-mode records every episode as unsuccessful, an env with no metric manager records no label (treated as a failure), and EXPORT_SUCCEEDED_ONLY then writes nothing.

docs.title: Built-in recorder terms
docs.text:
All built-ins live in eden.managers.terms.recorders (also eden.recorders).

Term Keys written When ActionRecorder action every step, at its start ObservationRecorder(groups=None) obs/<group> (every group, or the listed ones) every step, at its start StateRecorder(entity_name="robot") state/qpos, state/dofs_vel, state/pos, state/quat (several entities are concatenated along the last axis) every step, at its start RLStepRecorder reward, done, terminated, timeout, timestamp (each optional) every step, after rewards and terminations SensorRecorder sensor/<sensor name> (use_ground_truth=True reads ground truth) every step, at its start, and once per new episode InitialStateRecorder initial_state/entities/<entity>/{qpos,dofs_vel,pos,quat} for every entity once per new episode SysIDRecorder(entity_name="robot") sysid/...: initial state, action and time stamp, joint positions, velocities and torques, base orientation per episode and every step

Row t of action and of obs/<group> form one (o_t, a_t) pair: the observation the action was chosen from and the action itself, which is the shape a behaviour-cloning dataset needs. SysIDRecorder records what eden.extensions.sysid.Trajectory.from_recorder_episode reloads; see Planning and system identification.

docs.title: When recorder hooks run
docs.text:
A recorder term implements any of four hooks, each returning a dict of (num_envs, ...) tensors (nested dicts become slash-separated keys). The step positions refer to the table in Environments.

Hook Runs Recorded as record_pre_step() phase 2, after the action is processed and before physics one row of the step record_post_step() phase 11, after terminations and rewards, before done envs are reset one row of the step record_pre_reset(envs_idx) phase 11 for the envs whose episode ends this step, and at the start of a manual env.reset() part of that last step record_post_reset(envs_idx) after a reset (phase 15, the end of env.reset()) and at start_recording() episode-level data

record_post_step() runs before the INTERVAL events (phase 18), so an event that perturbs the robot for the next step never shows up as the outcome of this step's action.

docs.title: Writing a recorder term
docs.text:
import torch

from eden.managers import RECORDER_TERM_REGISTRY, RecorderTerm


@RECORDER_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
class BaseHeightRecorder(RecorderTerm):
    entity_name: str = "robot"

    def build(self) -> None:
        self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name)  # fail at build on a bad name

    def record_post_step(self) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        pos = self.resolve_entity(self.entity_name).get_pos()
        return {"base_height": pos[:, 2:3].clone()}

Return clones, or values you will not modify in place, and leave compute() alone: recorder terms are driven only by the hooks. close(file_path) is called when the manager closes, while the dataset file is still open.

docs.title: Motion Datasets
docs.text: Eden reads motion libraries (human motion capture, robot retargets, hand-object recordings) through dataset loaders that all produce the same in-memory format. This page lists the loaders that ship, says where each one expects its data and what you must obtain yourself, documents the motion fields they fill, the offline modifiers you can stack on top, and how to write a loader for a new library. How a loaded dataset drives a training environment is in Motion tracking.

docs.title: Loading a dataset
docs.text:
Every loader is a DatasetBase subclass, constructed from its options and a device. The LAFAN1 replay recipe (examples/recipes/datasets/lafan1.py):

import genesis as gs

import eden as en
from eden.datasets.lafan1_dataset import LAFAN1RetargetedG1Dataset

en.init(backend=gs.gpu)

dataset = LAFAN1RetargetedG1Dataset(
    options=LAFAN1RetargetedG1Dataset.configure(
        raw_data_path=data_path,   # None downloads the dataset from HuggingFace
        target_framerate=50.0,
    ),
    device=gs.device,
)

robot_seq = dataset.motion_sequences["g1"]          # a BatchMotionSequence
robot_seq.base_pos_w[0, 0]                          # clip 0, frame 0
robot_seq.buffer_length                             # frames per clip
dataset.metadata["all_motion_files"]                # source file per clip

dataset.motion_sequences maps each motion sequence key (one per actor) to a BatchMotionSequence holding every clip; len(dataset) is the number of clips. In a task you never construct the dataset yourself: you pass SomeDataset.configure(...) as a MotionTerm's dataset_options (see Motion tracking). Each loader under examples/recipes/datasets/ replays one library on a robot in the viewer.

docs.title: Shipped loaders
docs.text:
All of these are importable from eden.datasets and registered in DATASET_REGISTRY under the snake-case key shown.

loader registry key sequence keys content data source AMASSRetargetedG1Dataset amass_retargeted_g1_dataset g1 AMASS retargeted to a 29-DOF G1, IsaacLab AMP .npz with link poses included HuggingFace ember-lab-berkeley/AMASS_Retargeted_for_G1, auto-download LAFAN1RetargetedG1Dataset lafan1_retargeted_g1_dataset g1 Ubisoft LAFAN1 retargeted to G1, CSV (30 fps) HuggingFace, auto-download (g1/ only) SEEDRetargetedG1Dataset seed_retargeted_g1_dataset g1 BONES Studio SEED, G1 CSV split (120 fps) HuggingFace bones-studio/seed, gated PHUMADataset phuma_dataset g1 PHUMA physically grounded humanoid motion, G1 split HuggingFace DAVIAN-Robotics/PHUMA, auto-download OMOMOHolosomaDataset omomo_holosoma_dataset human, object OMOMO processed by the Holosoma pipeline: root pose, 52 SMPL-H joint positions, object pose (30 fps) HuggingFace, auto-download ArcticDataset arctic_dataset object, left_hand, right_hand ARCTIC bimanual manipulation: two MANO hands (21 keypoints each) and a 1-DOF articulated object HuggingFace, auto-download HHIAssistDataset hhi_assist_dataset caregiver, recipient HHI-Assist paired BVH of a caregiver and a care recipient (link poses only) HuggingFace, auto-download DexYCBDataset dex_ycb_dataset hand, object DexYCB single-hand grasps of YCB objects (30 fps) manual download, gated TacoDataset taco_dataset right_hand, object_right, left_hand, object_left TACO bimanual tool use (30 fps) manual download + MANO OakInk2Dataset oak_ink2_dataset as TACO OakInk2 bimanual manipulation, one clip per program stage (120 fps) manual download + MANO Hot3dDataset hot3d_dataset as TACO HOT3D egocentric recordings cut into hand-object segments (30 fps) manual download + MANO WeaveG1InspireHOIDataset weave_g1_inspire_hoi_dataset robot, left_hand, right_hand, object Weave reference clips: a G1 with two Inspire hands moving an OMOMO object HuggingFace, auto-download

Three more loaders live with the task that uses them: BvhCsvG1Dataset (eden/tasks/beyondmimic/dataset.py, G1 CSV in BeyondMimic's layout), DexterHandDataset (eden/tasks/contrack/dataset.py, ConTrack xArm7 + XHand clips) and FlashDexRetargetDataset (eden/tasks/flashdexretarget/dataset.py, the motion.pt that eden retarget flashdex writes).

The datasets' own licences and citations are in eden/datasets/README.md. Check each licence before using a library or anything trained on it.

docs.title: Automatic download
docs.text:
With raw_data_path=None, a loader that names a HuggingFace repo downloads it into the HuggingFace cache on first use and reads it from there. Some repos hold more than the loader reads, so a loader may fetch only part of the repo (_hf_allow_patterns), unpack an archive in place (_post_download_process), and read a subdirectory (_hf_data_subdir):

  • LAFAN1 fetches and reads only the g1/ CSVs; the repo also holds h1/ and h1_2/ retargets with other DOF counts.
  • SEED fetches only g1.tar.gz and unpacks it to g1/csv/. The repo is gated: request access on its HuggingFace page and run huggingface-cli login first.
  • PHUMA downloads one data.zip, unzips it, and reads data/g1.
  • Weave downloads only the files of the split ("train" or "test", default "test") and objects you ask for.

A finished unpack is marked with a .eden_extracted file inside the unpacked directory (g1/ for SEED, data/ for PHUMA), so an interrupted unpack is redone on the next run; delete that directory to force it. An upstream revision bump downloads and unpacks into a fresh snapshot directory and leaves the old one behind. Set raw_data_path to a directory you manage if you want a stable location. Where downloads go in general is covered in Assets.

docs.title: An explicit raw_data_path
docs.text:
An explicit raw_data_path is used exactly as given and must already exist. A missing path raises (listing the sibling directories, so a typo is visible) rather than downloading. Because the download stages only run on the download path, an explicit path must point at what the narrowing would have produced: for LAFAN1 the g1/ directory itself, since mixing robots' CSVs fails with a shape mismatch.

SEED is the one exception: its raw_data_path may be the directory holding g1.tar.gz (it extracts it there, so that directory must be writable), the extracted g1/, or g1/csv/. For a read-only copy, point at g1/csv.

docs.title: Licence-gated data you must obtain yourself
docs.text:
Eden never ships the SMPL, SMPL-H, SMPL-X or MANO model files, raw AMASS data, or the gated releases. You need:

what needed by where to get it where the loader expects it DexYCB DexYCBDataset dex-ycb.github.io (Google Drive consent form) raw_data_path: the extracted root holding <YYYYMMDD-subject-NN>/<sequence>/; calibration_dir: its calibration/ directory TACO TacoDataset github.com/Satorinal/TACO raw_data_path holding Hand_Poses/, Object_Poses/, object_models_released/ OakInk2 OakInk2Dataset oakink.net/v2 raw_data_path holding anno_preview/, program/program_info/, object_repair/align_ds/ HOT3D Hot3dDataset HOT3D raw_data_path holding dataset/<recording>/, _assets/assets/ MANO models TACO, OakInk2, HOT3D always; DexYCB with body_model_params=True mano.is.tue.mpg.de, Models & Code (mano_v1_2.zip) body_model_dir: its models/ directory (MANO_RIGHT.pkl, MANO_LEFT.pkl) SEED access SEEDRetargetedG1Dataset request access on HuggingFace huggingface-cli login, then auto-download

The MANO, SMPL and SMPL-H .pkl files pickle chumpy arrays. Eden reads them without chumpy (eden.utils.chumpy_pickle), so they need no extra package; a .npz next to the .pkl is read instead when present.

docs.title: Dataset notes
docs.text:
AMASS. The clips are already retargeted to the G1, with link poses precomputed. This is the retargeted split only; the raw AMASS SMPL clips (for eden retarget soma) come from amass.is.tue.mpg.de.

SEED. The CSV root rotation columns are Euler angles in degrees composed in intrinsic ZYX order (the Maya export convention); translation is in centimetres and joints in degrees. The loader handles all three. At about 142k clips, use the file filters and GroundFirstFrame(chunk_size=...) to keep memory bounded.

ARCTIC. The object's one DOF is rotation, and its links are bottom and top; each hand's links are the 21 MANO keypoints (eden.datasets.constants.MANO_KEYPOINTS_NAME). This loader does not trim clips, so drop_first_n_frames / drop_last_n_frames raise; use the TrimFrames modifier.

DexYCB. calibration_dir is required: each clip's master-camera extrinsic is applied so poses land in DexYCB's AprilTag world frame (z-up, origin on the table tag), and a missing or nonexistent calibration_dir raises FileNotFoundError. The hand's base is the labelled MANO wrist keypoint (MANO's transl is a shape-dependent offset of about 9 cm away from it), and its links are the 21 labelled keypoints. Only the grasped object (meta.yml::ycb_grasp_ind) is kept. Leading frames without a MANO annotation are trimmed, and a clip whose unannotated frames are not all at its start is skipped with a warning. Per-clip metadata: objects (YCB folder name) and sides. Further options: ground_initial_pose (default True), apply_mesh_correction (default True; set False when rendering against a non-Eden YCB asset, and provide models_dir), and retargeted_label, which also loads a retargeted_<label>.npz written next to each clip by examples/recipes/retargeting/dex_retargeter/dex_ycb_position_retargeting.py as a third key, robot.

from eden.datasets import DexYCBDataset

ds = DexYCBDataset(
    options=DexYCBDataset.configure(
        raw_data_path="/data/dex_ycb",
        calibration_dir="/data/dex_ycb/calibration",
        target_framerate=30.0,
    ),
    device="cuda",
)

TACO, OakInk2, HOT3D (shared base HandObjectDatasetBase). Each clip holds <side>_hand (the MANO wrist as base, the 21 MANO keypoints as links) and object_<side> (the object that hand holds) for the hands in sides ("both", "right" or "left"). A clip where a loaded hand holds nothing, or whose reader rejects it, is left out and named in metadata["skipped"]. Per-clip metadata: clip_names, recordings, objects_<side>; object_mesh(obj_id) and recording_object_poses(recording) read meshes and every object's poses from the release. World frames follow CHORD's conventions (z-up). Pass the release's rate as target_framerate (the class attribute source_framerate) to keep the clips unretimed. Release-specific options: OakInk2's contact (default 0.01 m), and HOT3D's segmentation settings tip_contact, link_contact, gap_frames, min_frames, pad_frames and modes (default ("B",): both hands on one object). File filters match each clip's <unit>/<clip name> path.

from eden.datasets import TacoDataset

ds = TacoDataset(
    options=TacoDataset.configure(
        raw_data_path="/data/taco", body_model_dir="/data/mano_v1_2/models", target_framerate=30.0
    ),
    device="cpu",
)
print(ds.metadata["clip_names"][:3], ds.metadata["objects_right"][:3])

HHI-Assist. Paired caregiver and recipient BVH files (120 Hz), parsed by eden.datasets.utils.bvh.parse_bvh. Both actors are link-only (no DOFs), so they are tracked with link and base terms.

OMOMO (Holosoma). The human is link-only: 52 SMPL-H joint positions in SMPLH_KEYPOINTS_NAME order. The object is a base pose only. metadata["human_height"] holds each subject's height, which eden retarget omniretarget uses to scale.

docs.title: Common options
docs.text:
Every loader accepts these (DatasetOptions); each loader's own options are listed in its docstring and its API entry.

option default effect raw_data_path None source data; None downloads when the loader has a repo processed_data_path None cache file; None keeps nothing on disk, except for a loader that derives its own default path (BeyondMimic's BvhCsvG1Dataset) (see the cache) target_framerate 50.0 every clip is resampled to this rate at load. Match the env's control rate. drop_first_n_frames, drop_last_n_frames 0 trim each raw clip at read time. A loader that cannot (ARCTIC) refuses a non-zero value; use TrimFrames. include_pattern, exclude_pattern None regex (re.search) on each file's basename include_list_file, exclude_list_file None YAML/JSON list of files to keep/drop: a flat list, a list of {file: ...} dicts (ProtoMotions' amass_*_train.yaml shape), or either under a motions: key. Matched on basename without extension, so CMU/45/45_01_stageii.motion matches 45_01_stageii.npz. modifiers () offline transforms applied after load (Modifiers) recalculate_velocities True re-estimate velocities by finite differences of the resampled positions instead of interpolating source velocities strict_cache_identity True refuse a cache whose record omits a setting this loader tracks; False accepts it with a warning body_model_params False also load body-model pose and shape (below) body_model_dir None directory of the licence-gated model files

Filters run before preparation, so excluded files are never read, and again on every cache load, so one cached full library can serve several subsets.

docs.title: The motion fields
docs.text:
A loader fills a MotionSequence per clip (fields [num_frames, ...]) and batches them into a BatchMotionSequence per key (each field a concatenated tensor indexed [clip, frame, ...]). Both live in eden.utils.motion_reference.motion_data. Only framerate is required; fill what your source has.

field per-frame shape notes framerate, buffer_length scalar clip rate (Hz) and frame count dofs_pos, dofs_vel (D,) joint positions / velocities in the loader's motion_dofs_name order base_pos_w, base_quat_w (3,), (4,) floating-base pose; quaternion wxyz base_lin_vel_w, base_ang_vel_w (3,) estimated from the poses when not given links_pos_w, links_quat_w (L, 3), (L, 4) tracked-link poses, rows in motion_links_name order; computed by forward kinematics when the source has only base and joints links_lin_vel_w, links_ang_vel_w (L, 3) estimated when not given links_pos_b, links_quat_b, links_lin_vel_b, links_ang_vel_b (L, ...) the link fields in the base frame, derived from the world ones. A large library may skip all four (derive_body_frame=False), which halves per-link memory; no tracking term reads them, but base-frame link distances do and refuse such a dataset. contact_points_w, contact_points_valid (L, P, 3), (L, P) demonstrated contact points per (link, partner link), opt-in; contact_points_valid alone is a per-link binary contact flag contact_label (L,) int8 +1 must touch, -1 must not touch, 0 no label, opt-in body_pose_quat, body_shape, body_model (J, 4), (B,), str body-model parameters, opt-in (below)

Quaternions are wxyz everywhere. Loaders whose source is xyzw (LAFAN1, DexYCB, PHUMA, HHI-Assist BVH, OMOMO's object) convert on read with eden.utils.geom.xyzw_to_wxyz, and MotionSequence renormalizes every quaternion field when it is constructed. Contact fields and labels are resampled nearest-neighbour, never blended.

A BatchMotionSequence also carries is_free_floating (default True) and entity_kind (advisory); see several actors.

docs.title: Body-model parameters
docs.text:
With body_model_params=True (off by default), DexYCB, TACO, OakInk2 and HOT3D also store the MANO pose and shape of each hand: body_pose_quat (the local rotation of every joint below the root, wxyz, relative to the flat hand), body_shape (the betas) and body_model ("mano_right" / "mano_left"). The root is the sequence's base: base_pos_w is the root joint, not MANO's transl. Any other loader refuses the flag. With it off nothing extra is read, stored or cached, and no simulation buffer ever holds these fields. A cache prepared without them is refused when the flag asks for them.

eden.datasets.utils.body_model turns them back into geometry:

from eden.datasets.utils.body_model import body_model_forward

hand = ds.motion_sequences["right_hand"]
joints, vertices = body_model_forward(
    hand.body_model[0],                 # e.g. "mano_right"
    "/data/mano_v1_2/models",
    hand.base_pos_w[0], hand.base_quat_w[0],
    hand.body_pose_quat[0], hand.body_shape[0],
)

BODY_MODELS names every supported model: mano_right, mano_left, and smpl_*, smplh_*, smplx_* for neutral, male and female. A model file is found under its BODY_MODELS spelling (SMPLH_MALE.pkl), the official download's (SMPLH_male.pkl), or AMASS's <gender>/model.npz. The models run on SkinnedBodyModel, a numpy linear-blend-skinning rig, so the smplx package is not needed.

docs.title: Modifiers
docs.text:
Modifiers are offline transforms applied to the loaded clips after the cache is loaded or prepared, in the order listed. They are not stored in the cache, so changing them needs no rebuild.

from eden.datasets.modifiers import GroundFirstFrame, SmoothStartTransition
from eden.options.robots.unitree_g1 import G1_IK_PROFILE

dataset_options = LAFAN1RetargetedG1Dataset.configure(
    raw_data_path="/data/lafan1/g1",
    modifiers=[
        GroundFirstFrame.configure(robot_options=en.robots.G1Dofs29()),
        SmoothStartTransition.configure(
            ik_profile=G1_IK_PROFILE,
            motion_links_name_per_key=dict(LAFAN1RetargetedG1Dataset.motion_links_name),
        ),
    ],
)
modifier registry key does Translate translate add offset to base_pos_w and links_pos_w Rotate rotate rotate every world-frame field by angle_deg about axis through the world origin. Order with Translate matters. MirrorLR mirror_lr mirror across the plane normal to axis (default 1, y) and relabel sides with dofs_swap, dofs_sign_flip, links_swap (indices in the original order) SpeedScale speed_scale play speed times faster by resampling, keeping the framerate; velocities are scaled TrimFrames trim_frames drop trim_first / trim_last frames Jitter jitter add Gaussian (std) or uniform (low, high) noise to fields. Prefer Rotate for orientations: noise breaks unit quaternions. GroundFirstFrame ground_first_frame lift each clip so frame 0's robot AABB sits at or above z = 0 (+ safety_margin_m), by forward kinematics of robot_options. One env per clip unless chunk_size is set. SmoothStartTransition smooth_start_transition prepend a stand-still, an IK-synthesized step and a blend into frame 0, so a reset from the default pose is not a teleport. Needs ik_profile (G1_IK_PROFILE for the G1). TCRSTerrainAdapt tcrs_terrain_adapt adapt flat-ground clips to a terrain; see TCRS terrain adaptation Compose compose run a nested list of modifiers as one, optionally scoped to keys

Rules that apply to all of them:

  • Scope with motion_sequence_keys. None (the default) applies a modifier to every key; an empty tuple applies it to none. A key that is not in the dataset raises.
  • Robot-only modifiers need one key. GroundFirstFrame and SmoothStartTransition drive one robot; on a dataset with a robot and an object, set motion_sequence_keys=("robot_key",), and shift the object to match yourself, or the two drift apart.
  • Keep keys the same length. TrimFrames and SpeedScale change clip lengths. Applied to only some keys of a multi-key dataset, they leave the keys with different lengths, which raises after the stack runs.
  • Body-model fields. MirrorLR, SmoothStartTransition and TCRSTerrainAdapt cannot keep body_pose_quat consistent and refuse a sequence that carries it.
  • Not idempotent. Each modifier mutates the clips in place and runs once per load. Reload the dataset to rerun the stack.

docs.title: Writing a loader
docs.text:
A loader declares its actors and their names as class attributes and implements prepare(). LAFAN1's (eden/datasets/lafan1_dataset.py, lightly trimmed) is a complete example:

from typing import Any, ClassVar

import numpy as np

import eden as en
from eden.datasets.base import DATASET_REGISTRY, DatasetBase
from eden.options.robots.unitree_g1 import G1_DOFS29_NAME, G1_DOFS29_TRACKED_LINKS_NAME
from eden.utils.geom import xyzw_to_wxyz
from eden.utils.motion_reference.motion_data import BatchMotionSequence, MotionSequence


@DATASET_REGISTRY.register()
class LAFAN1RetargetedG1Dataset(DatasetBase):
    _applies_frame_window: ClassVar[bool] = True

    registry: str = "<hf-namespace>"           # the HuggingFace repo <registry>/<dataset>
    dataset: str = "LAFAN1_Retargeting_Dataset"
    _hf_allow_patterns: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("g1/*", "LICENSE", "README.md")
    _hf_data_subdir: ClassVar[str] = "g1"

    file_extension: ClassVar[str] = ".csv"
    motion_sequence_keys: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]] = ("g1",)
    motion_dofs_name: ClassVar[dict[str, list[str]]] = {"g1": G1_DOFS29_NAME}
    motion_links_name: ClassVar[dict[str, list[str]]] = {"g1": G1_DOFS29_TRACKED_LINKS_NAME}

    def prepare(self) -> tuple[dict[str, BatchMotionSequence], dict[str, Any]]:
        # The CSVs carry base + DOFs only, so links come from forward kinematics of this robot.
        return self._prepare_single_key(
            self._read_single_sequence,
            desc="LAFAN1: reading raw csv",
            robot=en.robots.G1Dofs29(dofs_name=self.motion_dofs_name["g1"]),
        )

    def _read_single_sequence(self, file_path: str) -> MotionSequence:
        motion = np.loadtxt(file_path, delimiter=",")[self._frame_window()]
        return self._pack_motion_sequence(
            framerate=30.0,
            base_pos_w=motion[:, :3],
            base_quat_w=xyzw_to_wxyz(motion[:, 3:7]),
            dofs_pos=motion[:, 7:],
        )

What each piece is for:

  • motion_sequence_keys, motion_dofs_name, motion_links_name are required; the class fails to define without them. Every key needs an entry in both name maps ([] when the actor has none).
  • file_extension is globbed recursively under raw_data_path. prepare() reads self.all_motion_files, already filtered.
  • _pack_motion_sequence(framerate, base_pos_w, base_quat_w, ...) builds one clip: it resamples to target_framerate, estimates missing velocities, derives the base-frame link fields (unless derive_body_frame=False) and refuses a clip under 2 frames.
  • _prepare_single_key(read_fn, desc, robot=...) covers the one-actor, one-file-per-clip case: parallel reads, batching, and, with robot, forward kinematics for the link fields. Multi-actor loaders call _parallel_read_motion_files and BatchMotionSequence.from_motion_sequences themselves and return ({key: batch, ...}, metadata); every key must end up with the same clip lengths.
  • registry / dataset name a HuggingFace dataset repo for the automatic download; _hf_allow_patterns, _post_download_process and _hf_data_subdir narrow it. A subclass for another robot replaces the pattern tuple rather than extending it.
  • _applies_frame_window = True declares that the reader slices with self._frame_window(); without it, a non-zero drop_first_n_frames / drop_last_n_frames raises instead of being silently ignored.
  • _cache_identity_fields lists the loader's own options that change the prepared data. They are recorded in the cache and checked on load; an option missing from the list lets a stale cache survive a setting change.
  • _PER_CLIP_METADATA_KEYS lists metadata lists with one entry per clip, so they stay aligned when clips are filtered or split across ranks (required for env_motion_groups).
  • _supports_body_model_params = True for a loader that can fill the body-model fields.

  • Retargeting: turning human motion into robot motion these loaders can read.
