docs.title: Motion Tracking
docs.text: This page explains the machinery behind Eden's motion-imitation tasks: the EdenMimicConfig config leaf, the motion manager that serves a reference trajectory to every environment, the data layout that reference uses, and the dataset cache that eden preprocess builds. Read it when you write or tune a tracking task, a tracking term, or a new motion source. The shipped tracking tasks themselves (BeyondMimic, general_mimic, Weave HOI, ...) are described in Motion-tracking tasks; the dataset loaders are in Motion datasets.

docs.title: The pieces
docs.text:
A tracking task has four layers. Each layer only talks to the one below it:

flowchart LR
    D["Dataset loader<br/>(DatasetBase)"] -->|BatchMotionSequence per key| T["MotionTerm"]
    T -->|fills per-env window| M["MotionManager<br/>env.motion_manager"]
    M -->|"data[entity_name]"| R["Tracking terms<br/>(observations, rewards,<br/>terminations, RSI events)"]
  • A dataset (a DatasetBase subclass) reads a motion library once, resamples every clip to target_framerate, fills the fields of a BatchMotionSequence per motion sequence key (one key per actor: "g1", "human", "object", "left_hand", ...), and caches the result.
  • A motion term (MotionTerm, in eden.managers.motion_manager) owns one dataset, picks a clip and a start time for each of its environments at every reset, and maps the dataset's sequence keys to scene entity names.
  • The motion manager (MotionManager, created by MimicRLEnvBase as env.motion_manager) advances a clock per environment and, once per step, copies a short window of reference frames into one MotionReferenceData buffer per tracked entity.
  • Tracking terms read env.motion_manager.data[entity_name] and compare it with the simulated entity.

docs.title: A minimal tracking config
docs.text:
A tracking task subclasses EdenMimicConfig (in eden.utils.configs), which is EdenRLConfig plus one field, motion_options: MotionManagerOptions | None. env_class_for_config maps it to MimicRLEnvBase; building it with RLEnvBase.from_config raises a TypeError instead of silently building an env with no reference (see Environments).

The motion section of the BeyondMimic task (eden/tasks/beyondmimic/config.py, set by its BeyondMimicDataMod):

from eden.managers.motion_manager import MotionTerm
from eden.options.managers.motions import MotionManagerOptions
from eden.tasks.beyondmimic.dataset import BvhCsvG1Dataset

config.motion_options = MotionManagerOptions(
    num_frames=1,
    data_start_from="current_time",
    frame_interval_s_range=(0.02, 0.02),
    # At clip end, soft-reset (resample start phase + teleport onto the reference)
    # instead of freezing at the last frame
    resync_on_motion_end=True,
    default=MotionTerm.configure(
        dataset_options=BvhCsvG1Dataset.configure(
            raw_data_path=self.raw_data_path,
            processed_data_path=self.processed_data_path,
            target_framerate=self.target_framerate,
        ),
        entities_map={"robot": "g1"},
        target_dofs_name={"g1": _G1Options.dofs_name},
        target_links_name={"g1": BvhCsvG1Dataset.motion_links_name["g1"]},
        motion_bin_length_s=1.0,
        adaptive_sampling=False,
        motion_start_from_middle_range=(0.0, 1.0),
    ),
)

Three things in that snippet are easy to get wrong:

  • default= is a term name. Every extra keyword on MotionManagerOptions is a motion term, as on every other manager. Most tasks have exactly one, named default.
  • entities_map goes from scene entity to dataset key ({"robot": "g1"}: the scene's robot tracks the dataset's g1 sequence). A key that is not one of the dataset's motion_sequence_keys raises at construction and lists the available keys.
  • target_dofs_name and target_links_name are keyed by dataset key, not by entity name, and need an entry for every key the dataset has (use [] for an actor with no DOFs, such as a rigid object). Names are matched with resolve_matching_names, so regex patterns work. The reference's DOF columns and link rows follow the order of these lists, which need not match the dataset's own order.

The rest of the config is ordinary RL: observation, reward and termination terms that read the reference, plus a reset event that puts the robot onto it (next sections).

docs.title: What a step does
docs.text:
MimicRLEnvBase.step() calls motion_manager.compute(dt) before RLEnvBase.step(). That call:

  1. advances each environment's motion clock by the control dt;
  2. fills data[entity] for every tracked entity with num_frames reference frames;
  3. if resync_on_motion_end=True, soft-resets environments whose clip just ran out (see Clip ends);
  4. accumulates per-motion metrics when compute_per_motion_metrics=True.

Every reward, termination, metric and observation computed later in that step sees the same, fresh window.

docs.title: The reference window
docs.text:
data[entity_name] is a MotionReferenceData whose fields have shape (num_envs, num_frames, ...):

field shape meaning dofs_pos, dofs_vel (N, F, D) joint positions / velocities, columns in target_dofs_name order base_pos_w, base_quat_w (N, F, 3), (N, F, 4) floating-base pose, world frame, quaternion wxyz base_lin_vel_w, base_ang_vel_w (N, F, 3) floating-base velocities, world frame links_pos_w, links_quat_w (N, F, L, 3), (N, F, L, 4) tracked-link poses, rows in target_links_name order links_lin_vel_w, links_ang_vel_w (N, F, L, 3) tracked-link velocities, world frame links_pos_b, links_quat_b, links_*_vel_b (N, F, L, ...) the same in the reference's base frame contact_points_w, contact_points_valid (N, F, L, P, 3), (N, F, L, P) demonstrated contact points per (link, partner link) contact_label (N, F, L) int8 per-link label: +1 must touch, -1 must not, 0 no label validity (N, F) bool False where the frame lies past the end of the clip time_to_target_frame (N, F) seconds from now to each frame; -1 for an invalid frame

World-frame positions already include the environment's env_origins, so they compare directly with entity.get_pos() / get_links_pos().

Which times the F frames sample is set on MotionManagerOptions:

option default effect num_frames 1 frames in the window. Size it to cover the largest frame_offsets any term reads: an offset >= num_frames raises with the fix. frame_interval_s_range (0.1, 0.1) spacing between window frames in seconds, drawn per environment at reset from this range. The shipped tasks set it to the control dt ((0.02, 0.02) at 50 Hz). data_start_from "one_frame_interval" "current_time": frame 0 is now. "one_frame_interval": frame 0 is one interval ahead.

The default window starts one frame ahead

With the default data_start_from="one_frame_interval", frame 0 is the next reference frame, so motion_ends fires one step before the policy sees the missing frame and "current frame" terms score against the future. Every shipped tracking task sets data_start_from="current_time".

The frame read at a given time is floor((start_time + t) * framerate) of the clip. There is no interpolation at lookup: clips are resampled once, at load, to the dataset's target_framerate. Set target_framerate to the control rate (1 / (sim_dt * decimation)) so one step advances exactly one frame, as the shipped tasks do.

Frames past the end of a clip are marked invalid, hold the last valid pose, and have their velocities zeroed. Tracking rewards that take frame_offsets average only over valid frames.

docs.title: Reading the reference in a term
docs.text:
The built-in terms show the pattern; motion_link_position_tracking_exp (eden/managers/terms/rewards/tracking.py) reads:

assert_motion_field_present(env, entity_name, "links_pos_w")
motion_idx = get_motion_link_idx(env, entity_name, links_name)
robot_idx = get_robot_link_idx(env, entity_name, links_name)
ref = env.motion_manager.data[entity_name]
offsets = resolve_frame_offsets(env, "links_pos_w", frame_offsets, ref.links_pos_w.shape[1])
motion_pos = select_motion_frames(ref.links_pos_w, offsets, motion_idx)   # (N, K, L, 3)
robot_pos = env.get_entity(entity_name).get_links_pos(ls_idx_local=robot_idx)  # (N, L, 3)

The helpers live in eden.utils.motion_reference.lookup:

  • get_motion_link_idx / get_motion_dofs_idx resolve names to rows/columns of the reference; get_robot_link_idx / get_robot_dofs_idx resolve the same names on the simulated entity. They are different index spaces: never index one with the other.
  • current_motion_frame(field, sel_idx) reads frame 0; select_motion_frames(field, frames, sel_idx) reads a set of frames, and resolve_frame_offsets validates and caches the offsets.
  • assert_motion_field_present(env, entity_name, field) raises when the dataset never filled field.

An unfilled field is not None

MotionReferenceData allocates every field (zeros, identity quaternions), so a field the dataset does not provide reads as plausible-looking zeros forever. Call assert_motion_field_present for every field a term reads; the built-in terms do (class terms in build(), function terms on their first call). It also refuses a base_* field on a sequence flagged is_free_floating=False.

For general guidance on writing terms (function vs class, build() vs compute(), caching) see Terms.

docs.title: Built-in tracking terms
docs.text:
Run eden terms --grep motion for the full list with parameters. The main families:

kind terms reads observation motion_dofs_pos, motion_dofs_vel, motion_base_pos_w, motion_base_quat_w, motion_links_pos_w, motion_links_quat_w, motion_phase current frame observation motion_links_pos_b, motion_links_ori_b reference links in the robot's live anchor-link frame observation motion_future_dofs_pos, motion_future_dofs_vel, motion_future_links_pos_b, motion_future_links_ori_b, motion_future_base_pos_w, motion_future_base_quat_w several window frames (frame_offsets) observation motion_future_base_pos_b, motion_future_base_ori_b another entity's reference base in this entity's live anchor frame (anchor_entity_name, anchor_link_name) observation motion_contact_flags, motion_future_contact_label demonstrated contacts reward motion_base_position_tracking_exp, motion_base_orientation_tracking_exp, motion_link_position_tracking_exp, motion_link_orientation_tracking_exp, motion_dofs_pos_tracking_exp world-frame poses / joint positions reward MotionRelativeBodyPositionErrorExp, MotionRelativeBodyOrientationErrorExp link poses relative to a yaw-aligned anchor link reward MotionGlobalBodyLinearVelocityErrorExp, MotionGlobalBodyAngularVelocityErrorExp links_lin_vel_w / links_ang_vel_w reward MotionContactChamferReward, MotionContactDistanceReward, MotionContactMatchReward contact_points_* termination motion_ends validity[:, 0] termination motion_*_tracking_error_above, bad_anchor_pos_z_only, bad_anchor_ori, BadMotionLinkPosZOnly, bad_base_ori, MotionBasePoseTrackingBreak pose errors event ReferenceStateInitialization, ObjectReferenceStateInitialization the reset state (next section)

Pick the term that reads what your dataset fills. A link-only human (HHI-Assist, OMOMO's SMPL-H joints) has no dofs_pos, so motion_dofs_pos_tracking_exp cannot run on it; a rigid object has no DOFs and usually no links, so it is tracked with the motion_base_* terms. The yaw-aligned MotionRelativeBody* rewards need both links_pos_w and links_quat_w and suit free-floating characters whose world heading does not matter; for objects, where world position and heading are the target, use the direct motion_link_* or motion_base_* terms.

The entity_base_pos_b / entity_base_ori_b observations are the simulated counterpart of motion_future_base_*_b: an object's live pose in the robot's anchor frame. Build such a free object with align=False so get_pos() is the authored body frame a reference records (see Entities).

docs.title: Resets and reference-state initialization
docs.text:
On reset, each motion term draws a new clip and start time for the resetting environments, and a RESET-mode event puts the entity onto the reference. BeyondMimic's event:

from eden.managers.terms.events.motion import ReferenceStateInitialization

reset_from_motion=ReferenceStateInitialization.configure(
    mode=en.EventMode.RESET,
    entity_name="robot",
    pose_range={"x": (-0.05, 0.05), "y": (-0.05, 0.05), "z": (-0.01, 0.01),
                "roll": (-0.1, 0.1), "pitch": (-0.1, 0.1), "yaw": (-0.2, 0.2)},
    velocity_range=_VELOCITY_RANGE,
    dofs_position_range=(-0.1, 0.1),
    priority=100,
),

ReferenceStateInitialization writes the reference's base pose, base velocity and joint state onto a robot (a floating or immobile base), with optional noise; overall_noise_scale scales every noise range at once so a curriculum can anneal it. ObjectReferenceStateInitialization does the same for a free rigid object. Both accept max_depenetration_velocity (m/s, default None) and depenetration_window_s (default 0.1) to cap how fast the contact solver may push a body out of an overlap it was seeded into, which keeps a light object from being flung when the reference pose intersects a hand or the floor.

The reset runs in a fixed order around the scene reset, and three things follow from it:

  1. motion_manager.reset() runs first and only resamples clip, start time and clock; it does not refill data.
  2. The window is refilled while the scene reset and RESET events run. A RESET event must read its initial state with motion_manager.get_reset_reference_state(envs_idx, [entity_name]), which is what the RSI events do. Reading motion_manager.data there can return the previous step's window.
  3. During the managers' own reset() calls the window already holds the new episode, so reading motion_manager.data there raises a RuntimeError. A term that grades the episode that just ended calls motion_manager.record_ended_episode_validity(entity_name) in build() and reads motion_manager.ended_episode_validity(entity_name) in reset(); a term that needs the new episode's reference reads it in post_reset().

docs.title: Start times and clip selection
docs.text:
These MotionTerm options control what a reset draws:

option default effect motion_start_from_middle_range (0.0, 0.0) start at a uniform fraction of the clip in [lo, hi]; (0.0, 1.0) starts anywhere motion_bin_length_s None split each clip into bins of this length and sample a start bin. When set, motion_start_from_middle_range is ignored (a warning says so). adaptive_sampling False weight start bins by a smoothed failure rate (BeyondMimic's scheme); needs motion_bin_length_s. Tuned by adaptive_kernel_size, adaptive_lambda, adaptive_uniform_ratio, adaptive_alpha, adaptive_failure_rate_max_over_mean. env_starting_stub_sampling_strategy "independent" "independent" draws a clip, then a start time in it; "concat_motion_bins" draws a bin over all clips laid end to end, so long clips are picked more often (needs motion_bin_length_s) start_at_timestep_zero_prob 0.0 with this probability, start at frame 0 instead freeze_at_timestep_zero_prob 0.0 each step, an environment still at time 0 stays there with this probability. Re-rolled every step, so 0.5 holds an environment about two steps on average: it adds start jitter, it does not freeze. motion_weights None initial per-clip sampling weights, a list or a path to a JSON/YAML file with a motion_weights key. Its length must equal the number of loaded clips.

docs.title: Hard-motion mining
docs.text:
adaptive_motion_weights=True turns on a per-clip curriculum: clips that end in early termination are drawn more often, clips that play to the end less often. It is stepped once per training iteration by Eden's rsl-rl on-policy and distillation runners (single-GPU and DDP); the FlashSAC runner refuses a config that enables it, because it would never step it. The update is set by motion_weight_update_mode:

  • "snapshot" (default) recomputes weights from the failure rates drained since the last update, clamps outliers at motion_weight_failure_rate_max_over_mean times the mean, and mixes with uniform by motion_weight_uniform_mix. Nothing compounds across updates.
  • "compound" multiplies each weight by motion_weight_success_discount per success and motion_weight_failure_amplify per failure, floored at motion_weight_floor. It integrates every past outcome and can collapse onto a single clip on a large library; keep it for ablations.

motion_weight_update_every_n_iters sets the cadence. With compute_per_motion_metrics=True (which requires adaptive_motion_weights=True) the manager also logs Mimic/mpjpe_*, Mimic/root_pos_err_* and Mimic/root_quat_err_*, plus Mimic/g_mpjpe_* when metric_anchor_link_name is set. log_per_motion_metrics adds per-clip histograms to Weights & Biases; log_motion_id_to_filename adds the file name of the most-sampled clip.

docs.title: Clip ends
docs.text: By default a clip that runs out holds its last frame with zero velocity, validity turns False, and a motion_ends termination (if configured) ends the episode. With MotionManagerOptions.resync_on_motion_end=True the environment instead draws a new start, and every RSI event teleports its entity onto it, without ending the episode. The RSI terms are resolved after the build, so enabling resync without one raises at construction.

docs.title: Several actors in one reference
docs.text:
A scene with several tracked entities (a humanoid and an object, two hands and an articulated object, two people) is a dataset with several sequence keys and an entities_map entry per key. The Weave HOI task (eden/tasks/weave_hoi/config.py):

default=MotionTerm.configure(
    dataset_options=WeaveG1InspireHOIDataset.configure(split=self.split, objects=objects, ...),
    entities_map={"robot": "robot", "left_hand": "left_hand", "right_hand": "right_hand", "object": "object"},
    target_dofs_name={
        "robot": _RIG.robot_dofs,
        "left_hand": _RIG.left_hand_dofs,
        "right_hand": _RIG.right_hand_dofs,
        "object": [],
    },
    target_links_name={**_ALL_LINKS, "object": []},
    motion_start_from_middle_range=(0.0, 1.0),
    env_motion_groups=(
        MotionGroupOptions(entity_name="object", metadata_key="objects", variant_labels=objects)
        if len(objects) > 1
        else None
    ),
),

Each sequence also carries two metadata flags, set by the dataset: is_free_floating (consulted by assert_motion_field_present, which refuses base_* fields of a fixed-base sequence) and entity_kind ("robot", "humanoid", "human", "hand", "rigid_object", "articulated_object" or "other"; advisory only, never branched on). For a fixed-base actuated tool, leave the base_* fields empty, set is_free_floating=False, and track it with the motion_link_* and motion_dofs_pos_tracking_exp terms.

docs.title: One object per environment from a bank
docs.text:
When the partner object differs per environment (a GroupedEntityOptions entity holding a bank of meshes, one variant per environment), a clip only makes sense in an environment holding the object it was recorded with. env_motion_groups=MotionGroupOptions(...) restricts every draw to matching clips:

  • entity_name: the grouped scene entity ("object");
  • metadata_key: the dataset's per-clip label list to match (default "objects"); the dataset must declare it in _PER_CLIP_METADATA_KEYS so it survives subsetting;
  • variant_labels: one label per variant, in the entity's grouped_entities order. Build it from the same constant that builds grouped_entities.

The build fails if a clip's label matches no variant, if a variant has no clip, or, under DDP, if a rank holds environments of a group it has no clip of. Entity.env_variant_idx gives the variant each environment holds. env_motion_groups cannot be combined with symmetric_augmentation.

docs.title: Several motion terms
docs.text: A manager may hold more than one motion term (two libraries, say). Environments are split into contiguous slices, one per term, proportionally to each term's number of clips, with at least one environment per term. An entity tracked by two terms must have the same number of DOFs and links in both.

docs.title: Mirroring
docs.text:
MotionManagerOptions.symmetric_augmentation=True mirrors the reference across the x-z plane for a random half of the environments, redrawn at every reset. It needs all three maps:

  • symmetric_augmentation_joint_mapping: the index of each joint's mirror joint;
  • symmetric_augmentation_joint_reverse_buf: a per-joint sign (-1.0 for joints whose angle flips);
  • symmetric_augmentation_links_mapping: the index of each tracked link's mirror link, in target_links_name order.

Warning

If any of the three maps is missing, no environment is mirrored and nothing reports it. Check all three are set.

For mirroring the clips themselves once, at load time, use the MirrorLR dataset modifier instead (see Motion datasets).

docs.title: The dataset cache and eden preprocess
docs.text:
Preparing a library (parsing files, resampling, forward kinematics for link poses, velocity estimation) can take minutes to hours. When the dataset's processed_data_path is set, the first load writes the prepared clips there and later loads read them back through torch.load(mmap=True), so several ranks on one machine share the page cache. Each task exposes processed_data_path as a task flag where it makes sense (--processed_data_path).

# Build the cache once, before a long training run
eden preprocess --task general_mimic --dataset_name amass --processed_data_path /data/caches/amass_g1.pt

eden preprocess --task <name> accepts the same task flags, --config and --override as eden train, plus --cpu. It builds every dataset its motion_options declares (forward kinematics run on the GPU unless --cpu). A task without motion_options is an error. When the task has no processed_data_path, nothing is saved, unless the dataset derives its own default path: BeyondMimic's BvhCsvG1Dataset keys one in Eden's cache directory by the settings that shape the clip.

To split a very large library across GPUs, start one process per GPU with --num_batches N --batch_idx K. Each process prepares a contiguous slice of the clip list and saves it next to the canonical cache path, with a .batch_K_of_N suffix. Pass --batch_idx explicitly: it defaults to 0. Training loads only the canonical path, so these batch files are not picked up by a training run as they are, and Eden has no command that merges them.

What the cache does and does not hold:

  • Filters are re-applied on load. include_pattern, exclude_pattern and the list files filter a cached full library, so one cache can serve several subsets.
  • Modifiers are not in the cache. The modifiers stack runs after every load, so changing it never needs a rebuild. Note that a modifier such as SmoothStartTransition therefore re-runs its per-clip IK on every load.
  • Settings that shape the data are checked. target_framerate, the sequence keys, and every option a dataset lists in _cache_identity_fields (frame drops, velocity recomputation, dataset-specific settings) are recorded in the cache; loading it with a different value raises. Delete the file or point processed_data_path elsewhere. A cache that predates a recorded setting (so its value is unknown) is also refused, unless the dataset is configured with strict_cache_identity=False, which accepts it with a warning.
  • The format is versioned. A cache written by an older layout fails to load with a message asking you to rebuild it.

Do not use eden preprocess on a task with modifiers

eden preprocess saves the dataset after its modifiers ran, so the cache it writes holds modified clips, and the next load applies the modifiers to them a second time. GroundFirstFrame (on by default in general_mimic) is unaffected because a second pass shifts by zero, but SmoothStartTransition, Translate, Rotate, MirrorLR or SpeedScale would be applied twice. Until this is fixed, build the cache of such a task by loading it once (for example a short eden train run) rather than with eden preprocess.

docs.title: Multi-GPU runs
docs.text:
Under DDP, rank 0 downloads and prepares the dataset while the other ranks wait at a barrier, then every rank loads the cache rank 0 wrote. This only works with processed_data_path set; without it every rank prepares its own copy. MotionManagerOptions.mp_split_method decides which clips each rank keeps on its GPU:

  • "None" (default): every rank holds the whole library.
  • "Even": clips are dealt round-robin; trailing clips that do not divide evenly by the world size are dropped, with a warning.
  • "Segment": each rank holds one contiguous slice.

Hard-motion mining works with every split: weights and outcome counts stay sized to the full library on every rank and are all-reduced each update. A rank left with no clip of an adaptive term raises. See Multi-GPU training for launching.

docs.title: Frozen policies use MotionCommand instead
docs.text: Eden has a second, lighter path for motion references: the MotionCommand command term (eden.managers.terms.commands.mimic), used on a plain RLEnvBase by the frozen-policy ports in the policy zoo. It loads BeyondMimic-format .npz clips as they are, with no dataset pipeline, cache, curriculum or window, and exposes the current frame (plus gather_motion_frames for arbitrary future frames) on the command term. Both paths use the same field names (links_*_w, base_*_w), so metric code reads either. Use the motion manager for training; see Commands for MotionCommand.

docs.title: Observations
docs.text: The observation manager computes what the policy (and the critic) see each step. This page covers observation groups, the per-frame pipeline every term's output goes through — modifiers, noise, clip, scale, the non-finite check and history — the built-in terms, sensors and cameras as observations, and how to write your own term or modifier. The general term contract is in Writing terms; read its compute() is a read section before you write a stateful observation.

docs.title: Observation groups
docs.text:
observation_options is an ObservationManagerOptions whose entries are groups (ObservationGroupOptions), and each group's entries are terms. The manager computes every group and returns a dict from group name to that group's tensor. The velocity-tracking tasks (eden/tasks/velocity_tracking/base_config.py) define a noisy, history-stacked policy group and a clean critic group that adds a privileged term:

from eden import observations
from eden.managers.modifiers.observations import UniformNoise
from eden.options import ObservationGroupOptions, ObservationManagerOptions
from eden.terms import ObsTerm

_POLICY_OBSERVATIONS = dict(
    base_ang_vel=ObsTerm.configure(
        func=observations.base_ang_vel,
        noise=UniformNoise.configure(n_min=-0.2, n_max=0.2),
        params={"entity_name": "robot", "frame": "body"},
    ),
    projected_gravity=observations.ProjectedGravity.configure(
        entity_name="robot",
        noise=UniformNoise.configure(n_min=-0.05, n_max=0.05),
    ),
    dofs_pos=observations.DofsPos.configure(
        noise=UniformNoise.configure(n_min=-0.01, n_max=0.01), entity_name="robot", offset_from_default=True
    ),
    dofs_vel=observations.DofsVel.configure(
        entity_name="robot",
        noise=UniformNoise.configure(n_min=-1.5, n_max=1.5),
        scale=0.05,
    ),
    actions=ObsTerm.configure(func=observations.last_action),
    commands=ObsTerm.configure(func=observations.generated_commands, params={"command_name": "velocity_command"}),
)

_CRITIC_OBSERVATIONS = dict(
    base_lin_vel=ObsTerm.configure(
        func=observations.base_lin_vel,
        noise=UniformNoise.configure(n_min=-0.5, n_max=0.5),
        params={"entity_name": "robot", "frame": "body"},
    ),
    **_POLICY_OBSERVATIONS,
)

observation_options = ObservationManagerOptions(
    policy=ObservationGroupOptions(**_POLICY_OBSERVATIONS, enable_corruption=True, history_length=5),
    critic=ObservationGroupOptions(**_CRITIC_OBSERVATIONS, enable_corruption=False),
)

Group names are yours to choose. With rsl_rl, the runner's obs_groups maps groups onto the actor and the critic; when it is left empty, rsl_rl falls back to the group named policy for the actor and to critic (or policy, when there is no critic) for the critic, and warns that obs_groups is unset. See Training runs.

A group's own fields:

Field Default Meaning concatenate_terms True concatenate the terms into one tensor; False returns a dict from term name to tensor concatenate_dim -1 the dimension to concatenate along terms_order None the order of the terms in the output; None is declaration order. If set, it must name every term of the group exactly once enable_corruption True False drops the noise of every term in the group (see Noise) history_length None a history window enforced on the whole group (see History) flatten_history_dim True flatten a group history into the feature axis backfill True fill a fresh group history with the first frame instead of zeros nan_policy "disabled" what to do with a NaN or ±Inf a term delivers (see Non-finite values)

Sharing a term dict between groups is safe. A group takes its own deep copy of every term handed to it — whether through the constructor, model_copy(update=...), updated(...) or attribute assignment — so the policy and critic groups above never share a term object, and editing one group's term never edits the other's. A term may be written as a plain dict, but it must then name its registered term ({"name": "base_lin_vel", ...}); a nameless dict is refused as the misspelled group field it usually is.

Adding or removing a term on an inherited config:

group = config.observation_options.policy
group.base_height = ObsTerm.configure(func=observations.base_height, params={"entity_name": "robot"})
group.disable_term("actions")  # also removes it from terms_order, if the group declares one

An assigned term is checked on that line — an unknown name, a bad parameter, or a name the group class already has (keys, clone, …) raises there, not at build. When a group declares terms_order, an added term must also be listed in it.

docs.title: The per-frame pipeline
docs.text:
Every frame of a term's output goes through the same stages, in this order:

raw compute() → modifiers (in list order) → noise → clip → scale → group nan_policy → history window

These are the fields every observation term accepts, beside its own parameters:

Field Default Stage modifiers [] transforms such as a moving average or a delay; Observation modifiers noise None a noise model, applied in training only; Noise clip None (min, max) clamp scale 1.0 a float, or a list matched against the term's feature dimension history_length 0 a per-term history window; History flatten_history_dim True flatten the window into the feature axis backfill True fill a fresh window with the first frame instead of zeros

They are options-only: configure() accepts them and the manager applies them from outside, but they are not mirrored as attributes on the term, so a term's compute() cannot read one. Don't declare a parameter named scale (or any of these) on an observation term of your own.

The order matters when you port a config. In the velocity-tracking dofs_vel term above, the noise (±1.5 rad/s) is added before scale=0.05, so it stays in rad/s rather than being rescaled.

docs.title: Noise
docs.text:
Three noise models are built in, in eden.managers.modifiers.observations:

Model Parameters UniformNoise n_min=-1.0, n_max=1.0 GaussianNoise mean=0.0, std=1.0 ConstantNoise bias=0.0

Each also takes operation: "add" (the default) adds the noise, "scale" multiplies by it. Values may be floats or tensors (per-component).

Noise is training-time corruption. It is skipped whenever env.training is False — eval, play (eval_mode) and deployment — and dropped for every term of a group with enable_corruption=False. The group keeps the noise in its config, and the manager logs one info line at build naming the group and the terms whose noise it is not applying. That is what lets one term dict serve a noisy policy group and a clean critic.

Noise is added after the modifiers

Modifiers belong to the signal the policy was trained on, so they run in every mode; noise does not. In training, a moving average therefore smooths the clean signal and the noise reaches the policy unsmoothed, while on hardware the same average smooths the real sensor's noise. To train against filtered noise, add the noise inside the term, or in a modifier of your own placed ahead of the average.

docs.title: Clip and scale
docs.text:
clip is a clamp, so it passes NaN through — it is no guard against NaN on its own (see nan_policy). It is read every step, so changing term._options.clip after build takes effect at once.

scale is a float, or a list giving a per-component scale matched against the term's feature dimension: the last dimension of its raw compute() output, before history stacking. The length is checked at build, and a term whose raw output is (num_envs,) — no feature dimension — refuses a list scale. An all-ones list or 1.0 costs nothing on the hot path.

scale and noise are resolved once, at build. Assigning term._options.scale afterwards changes what the options report but not what the manager multiplies by, and nothing raises. Read what is applied off term.effective_scale, and change it at runtime with:

env.observation_manager.set_term_scale("policy", "dofs_vel", 0.1)

which re-runs the build-time check and updates both. Call it at setup: because scale is applied before a frame enters the history window, retuning a term whose window already holds frames would mix two scales in one window, so set_term_scale refuses that with a RuntimeError. The window counts as empty before the first compute() and again after a full env.reset() — which is where the training wrappers leave you, since their from_config builds and resets.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
A term's history_length keeps a window of its last history_length frames, oldest first. With flatten_history_dim=True (the default) a (num_envs, dim) term becomes (num_envs, history_length * dim); with False it is (num_envs, history_length, dim). With backfill=True (the default) a fresh window — after a reset — is filled with the first frame; with False it starts at zeros. history_length=1 logs a warning; use 0 for no history.

A group's history_length instead keeps one window over the concatenated group, which requires concatenate_terms=True and replaces every term's own history settings (the manager logs which ones it overrides). The two layouts differ when flattened: per-term history gives [term_a frames…, term_b frames…], a group history gives [frame_oldest (a, b), …, frame_newest (a, b)]. Match the layout the policy you are porting expects.

The window advances once per control step and once per env.reset(), on the manager's update_history=True pass. Other reads — the final-observation snapshot, get_observations() — compute the current frame and show it in the newest slot without pushing it.

docs.title: Observation modifiers
docs.text:
modifiers is a list of transforms applied to the term's output in list order, before noise. Unlike noise, they run in every mode — training, eval and deployment — because a policy trained on a delayed or smoothed observation must be deployed with the same delay or smoothing. Two are built in, in eden.managers.modifiers.observations:

Modifier Parameters What it delivers ExponentialMovingAverage alpha (required, in (0, 1]), backfill=True y(t) = alpha * x(t) + (1 - alpha) * y(t-1); alpha weights the newest frame (as in pandas' ewm). With backfill, the first frame after a reset is delivered unchanged. Needs a floating-point frame ObservationDelay control_steps (required, >= 1), backfill=True the frame from control_steps control steps earlier; until enough frames exist, the first frame (or zeros without backfill) 
from eden import observations
from eden.managers.modifiers.observations import ExponentialMovingAverage, ObservationDelay, UniformNoise
from eden.options import ObservationGroupOptions

policy = ObservationGroupOptions(
    dofs_vel_smooth=observations.DofsVel.configure(
        entity_name="robot",
        modifiers=[ExponentialMovingAverage.configure(alpha=0.2)],
        noise=UniformNoise.configure(n_min=-0.01, n_max=0.01),
    ),
    dofs_pos_late=observations.DofsPos.configure(
        entity_name="robot",
        modifiers=[ObservationDelay.configure(control_steps=2)],
    ),
    nan_policy="sanitize",
)

Stateful modifiers advance on the same update_history=True pass as the history window, so a delay of k is k window pushes. Each term instance owns its modifier instances: the same modifier on a policy and a critic copy of a term keeps two independent states.

docs.title: Non-finite values: nan_policy
docs.text:
nan_policy is a group field. It checks each term's frame at the end of that term's pipeline — after clip and scale, before the history window — so every report names the term, and a clip that bounds an infinity (a depth or raycast term's +inf for "no hit") is never reported:

nan_policy A NaN, or an infinity no clip bounded Cost "disabled" (default) reaches the policy unchanged none "sanitize" replaced with 0.0 on the device, no sync "warn" replaced with 0.0; the first occurrence per term is logged with the env ids one GPU sync per group per compute, while any of the group's terms has not warned yet "error" raises FloatingPointError naming the term, the kind of value and the envs one GPU sync per group per compute

The check covers every computation, the final-observation snapshot included: a simulation that diverged to NaN just before an env terminated shows up there, and that frame is what a value bootstrap reads. What it cannot do is clean a stateful modifier upstream of it. A NaN that reaches an ExponentialMovingAverage stays in the average until the env resets, and for that time the policy receives 0.0 for the term (under "sanitize" or "warn").

A modifier runs before the clip, so keeping an infinity an infinity is the modifier's job: a NaN made there is one no clip can bound. The shipped ExponentialMovingAverage is written for that (an infinite input stays infinite); a filter of your own written with torch.lerp meets inf - inf and returns NaN.

docs.title: Built-in observation terms
docs.text:
Built-in terms are importable from eden.observations (from eden import observations). The full list, with every parameter, is in the Term Catalog and from eden terms --kind observation. By family:

Family Module (eden/managers/terms/observations/) Examples Proprioception proprio.py DofsPos, DofsVel, DofsForce, DofsControlForce, base_lin_vel, base_ang_vel, base_pos, base_quat, base_rpy, links_pos, links_quat Commands, actions, time common.py generated_commands, last_action, episode_phase, MetricObservation Locomotion locomotion.py ProjectedGravity, base_height, sin_phase, cos_phase, ScaledCommands, GridScanDots, VelocityTrackingErrorIntegral Contact contact.py ContactForceNorm, GroupedContactFlags, motion_contact_flags Manipulation manipulation.py EndEffectorPose, EndEffectorToObjectDistance, ObjectToOracleDistance, GripperState Privileged (domain-randomization state) privileged.py GainScale, MotorStrengthScale, AddedMass, ComOffset, FootFriction Motion tracking tracking.py motion_dofs_pos, motion_future_dofs_pos, motion_links_pos_b, robot_body_pos_b, motion_phase Cameras camera.py rgb_image, depth_image, segmentation_image, normal_image, pointcloud_image Sensors sensors.py SensorRead

DofsPos and the other DOF terms read every DOF of the entity by default, in the entity's dofs_name order; pass dofs_name=[...] to select joints in an output order of your choosing. DofsPos(offset_from_default=True) subtracts default_dofs_pos. The base-pose terms read the solver frame by default; relative=True gives the authored frame — see Entities for why the two differ.

The motion-tracking terms need a motion reference; they are covered in Motion tracking.

docs.title: Sensors and cameras as observations
docs.text:
SensorRead concatenates sensor readings into one observation: sensor_names (a list of names or patterns; None, the default, reads every sensor in the scene), read_ground_truth=False (read the noiseless value instead of the sensor's noisy reading) and post_process_func (applied to each reading). Readings with more than two dimensions are flattened.

The camera terms read a camera by camera_name. rgb_image returns the renderer's native (N, H, W, C) uint8 by default; for a CNN policy, normalize=True gives floats in [0, 1] and channels_first=True gives (N, C, H, W) (either flag also drops an alpha channel). pointcloud_image zeroes invalid pixels so an infinite depth never reaches the policy. Image terms are usually put in a group of their own with concatenate_terms=False, or in a group no flat-vector policy reads. Cameras, renderers and sensors themselves are covered in Sensors and rendering.

docs.title: Shared computation across groups
docs.text:
Many tasks reuse one term in several groups — an identical policy and critic copy that differ only in noise or history. The manager detects terms whose raw output is provably identical (same registered term, same parameters, ignoring the post-compute fields) and computes them once per observation pass, reusing the result for the other copies. This is only sound because compute() is a pure read; it is one more reason per-step state must live in post_physics_refresh(), which reaches every instance, including the duplicates the cache skips.

To share a value between an observation and a reward or termination, compute it once as a metric and read it with observations.MetricObservation — see Share a computation across terms.

docs.title: Writing an observation term
docs.text:
A function term is the right form for a pure read of env state:

import torch

from eden.managers.observation_manager import OBSERVATION_TERM_REGISTRY


@OBSERVATION_TERM_REGISTRY.register()
def episode_phase(env, *, centered: bool = False) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Normalized episode time as a (num_envs, 1) tensor."""
    phase = env.episode_length_buf.float() / env.max_episode_length
    if centered:
        phase = 2.0 * phase - 1.0
    return phase.unsqueeze(-1)

That is the built-in episode_phase (eden/managers/terms/observations/common.py). Return a (num_envs, dim) tensor — unsqueeze(-1) a scalar per env — so the term has a feature dimension to scale and concatenate.

A class term (ObservationTerm) is the form for anything resolved once or carried between steps. The rules specific to observations:

  • compute() runs several times a step and at build, before any reset; it must change nothing a second call would see. Per-step state advances in post_physics_refresh() (phase 7, once per control step, also on hardware). VelocityTrackingErrorIntegral is the worked example, in compute() is a read.
  • The output shape is learned from the build-time call, so compute() must already return the right shape then.
  • Resolve the entity with self.resolve_entity(name) in compute(): deployment swaps the sim entity for the real robot's state, and observations are exactly what must read the real robot.

docs.title: Writing a modifier
docs.text:
Subclass ObservationModifier and register it with @OBSERVATION_MODIFIER_REGISTRY.register() (both from eden.managers.modifiers). A modifier follows the same read/commit split as an observation term:

  • compute(frame) is a read. It returns this frame's output given the modifier's state, and it runs as often as the observation is computed (the snapshot, get_observations(), the build probe). It must not change the state.
  • advance(frame) is the commit. The manager calls it right after compute(frame) on the update_history=True pass — once per control step and once per env.reset(). Stateless modifiers leave it as the no-op it is.
  • compute returns a tensor it does not write afterwards: the manager uses the output after advance has run, so a view of state that advance updates in place would change under it. Return a fresh tensor, or .clone().
  • Neither method writes into frame, and advance copies what it keeps (self._last.copy_(frame), not self._last = frame): frame may be the cross-group cached output, the term's own buffer, or a view of simulator state.
  • build(frame) allocates state from a sample frame (size it with torch.zeros_like(frame); don't seed it from the values, which are read before any reset). reset(envs_idx) restarts the rows of envs whose episode restarts, with the same indices as the history window.
  • Return the shape, dtype and device you receive. The manager checks this at build, because scale, history and concatenation are sized from the raw output.
import torch

from eden.managers.modifiers import OBSERVATION_MODIFIER_REGISTRY, ObservationModifier


@OBSERVATION_MODIFIER_REGISTRY.register()
class RunningMax(ObservationModifier):
    """The largest value each component has reached since the episode began."""

    def build(self, frame):
        self._max = torch.full_like(frame, -torch.inf)  # allocated once, written in place

    def reset(self, envs_idx=None):
        self._max[slice(None) if envs_idx is None else envs_idx] = -torch.inf

    def compute(self, frame):  # a read, however often it runs
        return torch.maximum(self._max, frame)

    def advance(self, frame):  # once per control step
        torch.maximum(self._max, frame, out=self._max)

A modifier inherits one quirk from the history window: a read made after the step's push and before the next step (get_observations() between steps) applies the current frame a second time. With backfill right after a reset — where rsl_rl makes its one such call — that gives the same value; otherwise it runs one push ahead. Nothing in the training loop reads there. ExponentialMovingAverage and ObservationDelay in eden/managers/modifiers/observations/temporal.py are the shipped examples.
