docs.title: Writing a rig
docs.text:
Subclass one of the three bases with default fields and register it:

from pydantic import Field

from eden.options.entities import RobotOptions
from eden.options.materials import RigidMaterialOptions
from eden.options.robots import COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY, ManipulatorOptions, Robotiq2f85, UR5e


@COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY.register()
class MyUR5eRobotiq(ManipulatorOptions):
    arm: RobotOptions = Field(default_factory=lambda: UR5e(material=RigidMaterialOptions(gravity_compensation=1.0)))
    gripper: RobotOptions = Field(
        default_factory=lambda: Robotiq2f85(is_fixed_base=False, collision_link_patterns=[".*pad"])
    )
    ee_link: str = "ee_link"
    grasp_links: list[str] = ["left_pad", "right_pad"]

A new rig shape subclasses CompositeEntityOptions and implements entity_parts() (the ordered (name, options) pairs) and attachments() (child → (parent, link[, offset, quat])). Do not override entity_options(): it holds the duplicate-name check, and a subclass that overrides it raises at class definition. The modules under eden/options/robots/composite/ are the reference implementations, and tests/options/robots/composite/ pins their contracts.

docs.title: Actuators
docs.text:
An actuator spec is a class in eden.options.actuators that describes one motor:

Attribute Meaning EFFORT_LIMIT torque limit (N·m), written as the DOF's symmetric force range ROTOR_INERTIA, GEAR_RATIO single-stage (floats) or two-stage planetary (3-tuples); ARMATURE() is the reflected inertia STIFFNESS, DAMPING passive joint spring and damper (not kp / kd) FULL_TORQUE_SPEED, NO_LOAD_SPEED, DRIVING_TORQUE_LIMIT, BRAKING_TORQUE_LIMIT the torque-speed envelope STATIC_FRICTION, DYNAMIC_FRICTION, FRICTION_ACTIVATION_SPEED joint friction model parameters

A robot maps DOF patterns to specs in its dofs_spec class variable. At build, a DOF covered by the spec gets the spec's stiffness, damping, armature and effort limit unless the robot's options set that property explicitly. Robots that derive their gains from the spec do it in the class body with the Raibert heuristic in eden.utils.actuator, which targets a 10 Hz closed-loop bandwidth by default (NATURAL_FREQ = 2π·10):

  • kp = ARMATURE · ω²
  • kd = 2 · ζ · ARMATURE · ω, with damping ratio ζ = 2.0 by default
  • action scale = 0.25 · EFFORT_LIMIT / kp
# eden/options/robots/unitree_go2.py
_Go2_DOFS_SPEC = {"*_hip_joint": UnitreeGo2HV, "*_thigh_joint": UnitreeGo2HV, "*_calf_joint": UnitreeGo2HVCalf}

class Go2(RobotOptions):
    dofs_spec: ClassVar[dict[str, type[ActuatorSpecOptions]]] = _Go2_DOFS_SPEC
    default_dofs_kp: dict[str, float] = {p: s.RAIBERT_HEURISTIC_KP() for p, s in _Go2_DOFS_SPEC.items()}
    default_dofs_kd: dict[str, float] = {p: s.RAIBERT_HEURISTIC_KD() for p, s in _Go2_DOFS_SPEC.items()}
    default_dofs_armature: dict[str, float] = {p: s.ARMATURE() for p, s in _Go2_DOFS_SPEC.items()}
    default_dofs_force_limits: dict[str, float] = {p: s.EFFORT_LIMIT for p, s in _Go2_DOFS_SPEC.items()}

The shipped specs cover Unitree motors (Unitree7520_22, Unitree7520_14, Unitree5020_16, Unitree5020_16_DOUBLE, Unitree4010_25, Unitree8010_6, Unitree8010_6Calf, UnitreeGo2HV, UnitreeGo2HVCalf), DAMIAO motors (DamiaoDM4310, DamiaoDM4340) and the LimX Oli joint groups (LimxOliHipKnee, LimxOliAnkleWaist, LimxOliShoulderElbow, LimxOliWristHead).

docs.title: Adding a robot
docs.text:
1. Get the asset. Put the URDF / MJCF (and its meshes) where file can reach it: a local path while you develop, or the repo path in the asset dataset once it is uploaded. Give URDF links explicit <mass> and <inertia> (why).

  2. Write the preset in eden/options/robots/<vendor>_<model>.py, subclassing RobotOptions and registering it:

    from typing import ClassVar

from eden.options.catalog import ROBOT_REGISTRY
from eden.options.entities import RobotOptions


@ROBOT_REGISTRY.register()
class MyArm(RobotOptions):
    file: str = "arms/my_arm/my_arm.xml"
    is_fixed_base: bool = True
    dofs_name: list[str] = [f"joint{i}" for i in range(1, 7)]
    default_dofs_pos: dict[str, float] = {"joint2": -0.5, "joint3": 1.0}
    default_dofs_kp: dict[str, float] = {"*": 400.0}
    default_dofs_kd: dict[str, float] = {"*": 40.0}
    default_dofs_armature: dict[str, float] = {"*": 0.1}   # from the source asset, not Genesis' default
    default_dofs_force_limits: dict[str, float] = {"joint[1-3]": 87.0, "joint[4-6]": 12.0}
    ee_links_name: ClassVar[list[str]] = ["flange"]

    The registry key is the snake-cased class name (my_arm); a robot registry also accepts name= for an alias. Import the class in eden/options/robots/__init__.py so en.robots.MyArm and the registry find it. 3. Take the dynamics from the source. Copy kp / kd, armature, damping, frictionloss and effort limits from the stack the robot was tuned on (Isaac Lab actuator config, MJCF armature, vendor data sheet). Never inherit the 0.1 armature fill for a URDF (the 0.1 trap), and remember Isaac Lab's actuator stiffness is Eden's default_dofs_kp. A motor shared by several joints is better written once as an ActuatorSpecOptions subclass and mapped through dofs_spec. 4. Declare the asset facts your tasks will need: feet_links_name (and the same names in links_to_keep for a URDF, so they are not merged away), ee_links_name, gripper open_dofs_pos / close_dofs_pos / tcp_offset / stroke, hand metadata.target_hand_links, max_substep_dt for a closed-loop mechanism. 5. Look at it and audit it. eden view MyArm -c shows the collision geometry. After building an env, read back get_dofs_kp(), get_dofs_kd(), get_dofs_armature() and get_dofs_force_range(): those are the values the solver integrates. 6. Test it in tests/options/robots/test_<module>.py, following the existing files there (see Testing).

docs.title: Adding an asset family
docs.text:
An asset family is a base options class that a group of assets (robots or objects) shares, for example YCBOptions in eden/options/objects/ycb.py:

class YCBOptions(EntityOptions):
    up: tuple[int, int, int] = (0, 0, 1)
    front: tuple[int, int, int] = (0, 1, 0)
    registry: str = "..."            # the Hugging Face user or org that hosts the dataset
    dataset: str = "eden_ycb"
    assets_subdir: ClassVar[str] = "ycb"
  • Name a cache subdirectory with assets_subdir, a class constant. An unset local_dir then means that subdirectory of the asset root, resolved at load time, so EDEN_ASSETS_DIR moves every default and a saved config's local_dir stays unset. Never give local_dir a default.
  • Fetch through the options. Inside the family, call options.fetch_asset(file) for an entity's files and FamilyOptions.fetch_family_asset(file) for files no entity is built from. Never call get_asset_path(..., local_dir=options.local_dir). Two source scans in tests/options/test_entities.py refuse both mistakes.
  • Register the members in a family registry (Registry("...") from eden.utils.registry) if they should be addressable by key; eden view and eden snap index every class under eden.options.objects and eden.options.robots, and family-registry entries as <registry>/<key>.
  • A policy's files follow the same rule, with registry, dataset, local_dir and assets_subdir as class constants (not options) and fetch_asset / resolve_local_dir as class methods; see Extending policies.

docs.title: Scenes and terrains
docs.text: A scene is the set of named entities an environment builds: the robot, the ground, the props, and the welds between them. This page covers SceneOptions and the scene presets, the object libraries you can drop into a scene, placing objects on support surfaces, procedural terrains, and Gaussian-splat scenes of real rooms. How each entity behaves once built is on Entities; the robots themselves are on Robots.

docs.title: SceneOptions
docs.text:
SceneOptions (in eden.options.entities) takes each entity as a keyword argument; the keyword is the entity's name in env.entities and in every term that refers to it.

import eden as en
from eden.options.entities import BoxOptions, PlaneOptions, SceneOptions
from eden.options.objects.ycb import YCB003CrackerBox

scene_options = SceneOptions(
    plane=PlaneOptions(),
    robot=en.robots.Droid(base_pos=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)),   # a composite: expands into "robot" + "gripper"
    box=YCB003CrackerBox(default_root_pos=(0.5, 0.0, 0.1)),
    marker=BoxOptions(size=(0.02, 0.02, 0.02), default_root_pos=(0.5, 0.2, 0.3), fixed=True),
)

What SceneOptions checks when it is constructed:

  • Every value is an entity options object or a composite rig; anything else raises.
  • A composite is placed under its primary body's name (Droid's arm_name, "robot" by default), and no two entities, plain or composite-produced, share a name.
  • A scene with a Mochi entity holds only Mochi and kinematic entities (see Mochi entities).

attachments_dict welds entities together (see Attaching entities). named_entities() returns every entity the scene will build, composites expanded. A task variant drops an entity with scene_options.remove_entity(name), which also removes that entity's own weld; it refuses an entity others are welded onto, a field declared on a SceneOptions subclass, and a single body of a composite. Removing an entity does not touch the terms, cameras or sensors that name it, so update those too.

Gaussian-splat options are not part of SceneOptions: they live on the config root because they select the environment class (see Gaussian-splat scenes).

docs.title: Scene presets
docs.text:
The presets in eden.options.scenes (also en.scenes) are factory functions that return a plain SceneOptions, so a config built from one saves and reloads like any other.

Preset Short alias Entities it adds EmptySceneOptions(robot, *, is_support_enabled=False, surface=None, **entities) en.scenes.Empty robot, plane BimanualEmptySceneOptions(right_robot, left_robot, *, ...) en.scenes.BimanualEmpty right_robot, left_robot, plane TabletopSceneOptions(robot, *, plane=None, table=None, **entities) en.scenes.Tabletop robot, plane, table (a work table at x = 0.5 m) KitchenCountertopSceneOptions(robot, *, plane=None, countertop=None, **entities) en.scenes.KitchenCountertop robot, plane, countertop LBMEvalSceneOptions(left_robot=None, right_robot=None, plane=None, **entities) en.scenes.LBMEval the LBM Riverway dual-arm station with two Pandas (default) on its gantry plates 
scene_options = en.scenes.Empty(robot=en.robots.G1Dofs29(), cube=BoxOptions(size=(0.1, 0.1, 0.1)))

In Empty and BimanualEmpty, is_support_enabled and surface configure the default plane. Passing plane=... replaces the flat ground with your own entity (a TerrainOptions, a low-friction plane) under the same name, so everything that addresses the ground by name keeps working; combining it with is_support_enabled or surface raises, since there is no default plane left to configure.

Benchmark ports ship their own scene factories, each returning a SceneOptions:

Module Factories eden.options.scenes.libero LiberoTabletopSceneOptions, LiberoFloorSceneOptions, LiberoKitchenTabletopSceneOptions, LiberoLivingRoomTabletopSceneOptions, LiberoStudyTabletopSceneOptions, LiberoCoffeeTableSceneOptions (each LIBERO workspace with its Panda, mounted where LIBERO mounts it) eden.options.scenes.robocasa.base RobocasaOneWallSmall, RobocasaOneWallLarge, RobocasaLShapedSmall, RobocasaLShapedLarge, RobocasaGalley, RobocasaUShapedSmall, RobocasaUShapedLarge, RobocasaGShapedSmall, RobocasaGShapedLarge, RobocasaWraparound, each also as ...Empty (kitchen only, no accessories); first argument style ("industrial", "scandinavian", "modern_1", …) eden.options.scenes.robocasa365.base Robocasa365Layout001 … Robocasa365Layout010, each also as ...Empty; first argument style ("style001", …) eden.options.scenes.replica_cad.base ReplicaCADSceneOptions(config_path), assembled from an upstream ReplicaCAD scene JSON eden.options.scenes.calvin CalvinPlayTableSceneOptions(robot=None), the CALVIN play table with its three blocks

Of these, only the LIBERO scenes back shipped tasks (see LIBERO); the others are scene and asset ports you can build tasks on.

docs.title: CALVIN play table
docs.text:
Eden ships no CALVIN tasks, only the scene and its assets, as a starting point for your own:

import eden as en
from eden.options.scenes.calvin import CalvinPlayTableSceneOptions

scene_options = CalvinPlayTableSceneOptions(robot=en.robots.FrankaEmikaPanda())  # set the robot's pose yourself

CalvinPlayTableSceneOptions(robot=None, **entities) returns a SceneOptions with plane, table and the three blocks block_red, block_blue and block_pink resting on the table, plus robot when you pass one and any further entities. Place the robot yourself: the factory sets no robot pose.

The assets are in eden.options.objects.calvin, built from the original CALVIN URDFs (table D) and fetched from the family's own Hub dataset (CALVIN_HF_DATASET = "eden_calvin") into the calvin cache subdirectory:

Class Registry key (CALVIN_OBJECT_REGISTRY) What it is CalvinPlayTable table the play table, fixed and articulated: DOFs base__slide, base__drawer, base__button, base__switch (all 0 by default) CalvinRedBlock block_red the medium block CalvinBlueBlock block_blue the small block CalvinPinkBlock block_pink the large block

Every CALVIN asset is scaled by CALVIN_GLOBAL_SCALING = 0.8. On first use the table's URDF tree is copied to a per-user cache with the texture coordinates stripped from its OBJ meshes, so the mesh loaders accept them, and its concave base is decomposed tightly (decompose_robot_error_threshold=0.0) so blocks rest on the visual tabletop instead of inside a single convex hull.

docs.title: Objects
docs.text:
Object libraries live in eden.options.objects.<family>. Each family is an EntityOptions subclass that fixes the Hub dataset, the cache subdirectory and the asset's axes, and each object is a subclass that names its file:

from eden.options.objects.ycb import YCB003CrackerBox, YCB006MustardBottle
from eden.options.objects.objaverse import ObjaverseApple

box = YCB003CrackerBox(default_root_pos=(0.5, 0.0, 0.1))
apple = ObjaverseApple(variant=3, default_root_pos=(0.4, 0.1, 0.05))   # Objaverse classes hold several meshes

Override fields as for any entity: is_fixed_base, scale, material=RigidMaterialOptions(rho=..., friction=...), default_geoms_sol_params (to stiffen an object a gripper holds, see Closed-loop grippers).

Module Family What it holds Classes ycb YCBOptions the YCB object set (YCB002MasterChefCan, …) 79 objaverse ObjaverseObjectOptions Objaverse meshes, one class per category with numbered variants; OBJAVERSE_OBJECTS_REGISTRY 82 robolab RoboLabObjectOptions, RoboLabFixtureOptions the RoboLab library (YCB, HOPE, HOT3D, HANDAL, VOMP, Objaverse, fruits and vegetables, blocks, fixtures) converted to URDF; ROBOLAB_REGISTRY keys like "ycb/banana" 323 replica_cad ReplicaCADObjectOptions ReplicaCAD stages and furniture; REPLICA_CAD_STAGE_REGISTRY, REPLICA_CAD_OBJECT_REGISTRY 107 robocasa / robocasa365 RoboCasa / RoboCasa365 kitchen layouts and accessories; ROBOCASA*_KITCHEN_REGISTRY, ROBOCASA*_ACCESSORIES_REGISTRY 149 / 137 libero LiberoObjectOptions LIBERO objects and workspaces; LIBERO_OBJECT_REGISTRY 42 robosuite RobosuiteObjectOptions the robosuite benchmark objects and the Rethink mount 24 lbm_eval LBMEvalObjectOptions LBM-eval objects and the Riverway station 51 polaris PolarisObjectOptions PolaRiS objects 32 simpler SimplerObjectOptions SIMPLER objects 10 calvin CalvinObjectOptions the CALVIN play table and blocks; CALVIN_OBJECT_REGISTRY 5 dextoolbench DexToolBenchOptions the DexToolBench hand tools; DEXTOOLBENCH_REGISTRY 13 arctic ArcticObjectOptions ARCTIC articulated objects; ARCTIC_OBJECTS_REGISTRY 6 omomo OMOMOObjectOptions OMOMO interaction objects; OMOMO_OBJECTS_REGISTRY 16 piano, husky, mujoco_playground single assets: Piano (an 88-key keyboard), HuskySkateboard, DexCube 1 each

"Classes" counts every class in the module, family bases included. Each family caches into its own subdirectory of the asset root, and its files download on first use (see Assets).

Mesh objects and the solver frame

A free mesh object is re-origined onto its centre of mass, so get_pos() and default_root_pos are different points unless you pass relative=True (see Which frame?). The gap is largest for tools and long objects whose centre of mass sits far from the mesh origin (2.9 to 14.8 cm on the DexToolBench tools).

Primitives (BoxOptions, SphereOptions, CylinderOptions, PlaneOptions) need no asset. A primitive's mass comes from its volume and material.rho (RigidMaterialOptions defaults to rho=200.0).

docs.title: Finding an asset
docs.text:
• eden view <Name> opens any robot or object in the viewer (-c shows collision geometry); eden snap <Name> renders an image; eden arrange <Name> [<Name> ...] poses several with sliders and prints a SceneOptions snippet. Names are class names (RoboLabYcbBanana) or family-registry keys (robolab/ycb/banana, and the bare key when it is unambiguous).
  • In code, eden.options.catalog.find_entity_options(name) resolves the same names to the class. It reads an index of every class under eden.options.objects and eden.options.robots, cached on disk and rebuilt when a source file changes.

  • eden.options.catalog.MANIFEST is a smaller, curated index with semantic metadata (category, placement, whether an asset is a support surface or a container), currently populated from ReplicaCAD:

    from eden.options.catalog import MANIFEST

MANIFEST.ensure()
MANIFEST.names(category="furniture/seating")
opts = MANIFEST.make("sofa", default_root_pos=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0))

docs.title: Placing objects on support surfaces
docs.text:
An entity with is_support_enabled=True extracts its upward-facing surfaces after the build, and the placement event terms sample collision-free poses on them for another entity, per environment:

# examples/recipes/scenes/asset_placement.py
env = EnvBase(
    env_options=EnvOptions(num_envs=8),
    scene_options=SceneOptions(
        plane=PlaneOptions(),
        station=LBMRiverwayStation(),          # support-enabled, restricted to its table top
        cube=BoxOptions(size=(0.04, 0.04, 0.04), is_fixed_base=False),
    ),
    event_options=EventManagerOptions(
        place_cube=EventTerm.configure(
            mode=EventMode.RESET,
            func=place_uniform,
            params={"entity_name": "cube", "support_entity_name": "station", "samples_per_area": 100},
        ),
    ),
)

The placement terms in eden.managers.terms.events.placement are place_uniform, place_constant_xy, place_range_xy, PlaceGaussian and PlaceFromLayouts (see Events). The support fields on the entity tune the extraction:

Field Default Meaning is_support_enabled False extract support surfaces at build support_links_name [] only these links' geometry counts (empty: every link); use it on a multi-link asset whose other surfaces must not receive objects support_minimum_clearance 0.05 the free height a surface needs above it support_shrink 0.1 inset applied to each surface polygon support_sample_method "uniform" "uniform" or "grid" support_num_sample_points 300 sample points per square metre (uniform) support_grid_size 0.01 grid spacing (grid)

Support surfaces are extracted only for contact-producing rigid entities: the option is ignored on a kinematic entity (with a warning) and rejected on deformable and Mochi entities.

docs.title: Terrains
docs.text:
A TerrainOptions entity is a height field stitched from a rows × cols grid of terrain generators, one per subterrain cell. The built entity is a fixed Terrain, placed with default_root_pos at the grid's [0, 0] corner.

# eden/tasks/velocity_tracking/terrain/config.py
import eden as en
from eden.options.entities import SceneOptions, TerrainOptions
from eden.utils.terrains import (
    FlatTerrain,
    PyramidSlopedTerrain,
    PyramidStairsTerrain,
    RandomUniformTerrain,
    WaveTerrain,
)

def _make_terrain_grid() -> list[list]:
    grid = []
    for i in range(10):                      # rows: difficulty increases along x
        t = i / 9
        sh, sl, rh, wa = round(t * 0.1, 4), round(t * 1.0, 4), round(0.02 + t * 0.08, 4), round(t * 0.2, 4)
        grid.append([
            FlatTerrain.configure(),
            FlatTerrain.configure(),
            PyramidStairsTerrain.configure(step_width=0.3, step_height=sh),
            PyramidStairsTerrain.configure(step_width=0.3, step_height=sh),
            PyramidStairsTerrain.configure(step_width=0.3, step_height=-sh),
            PyramidStairsTerrain.configure(step_width=0.3, step_height=-sh),
            PyramidSlopedTerrain.configure(slope=sl),
            PyramidSlopedTerrain.configure(slope=-sl),
            RandomUniformTerrain.configure(min_height=-rh, max_height=rh, step=0.02, downsampled_scale=0.5),
            WaveTerrain.configure(num_waves=4.0, amplitude=wa),
        ])
    return grid

scene_options = SceneOptions(
    terrain=TerrainOptions(
        subterrain_size=(8.0, 8.0),
        horizontal_scale=0.1,
        vertical_scale=0.005,
        terrain_generators=_make_terrain_grid(),
        default_root_pos=(-10 * 8.0 / 2.0, -10 * 8.0 / 2.0, 0.0),   # centre the 80 x 80 m grid on the origin
    ),
    robot=en.robots.G1Dofs29(),
)

examples/recipes/terrain/terrain_gen.py previews every generator.

docs.title: TerrainOptions fields
docs.text:
Field Default Meaning terrain_generators [[FlatTerrain.configure()]] the grid; must be rectangular, rows along x and columns along y subterrain_size (32.0, 32.0) size of each cell in metres (holds every built-in parkour course) horizontal_scale 0.25 height-field cell size in metres vertical_scale 0.005 metres per height unit randomize False when False, every cell is generated from seed 0, so the terrain is the same on every run use_checker_surface False render a checkerboard (1 m squares by default); cannot be combined with surface uv_scale None texture repeats across the whole terrain, a scalar or (x, y); None picks one repeat per axis, or 1 m checker squares default_root_pos (0, 0, 0) world position of the grid's [0, 0] corner; default_root_quat must stay the identity

A terrain is always fixed, carries no DOFs, and cannot take a Mochi material. To put a robot on terrain in a preset scene, pass it as the ground: en.scenes.Empty(robot=..., plane=TerrainOptions(...)).

docs.title: Generators
docs.text:
All generators are in eden.utils.terrains and registered in TERRAIN_GENERATOR_REGISTRY. Configure one with <Generator>.configure(**params); heights are in metres unless the parameter says otherwise.

Generator Parameters (defaults) FlatTerrain none RandomUniformTerrain min_height=-0.1, max_height=0.1, step=0.1, downsampled_scale=0.5 SlopedTerrain slope=-0.5 PyramidSlopedTerrain slope=-0.1 DiscreteObstaclesTerrain max_height=0.05, min_size=1.0, max_size=5.0, num_rects=20 WaveTerrain num_waves=2.0, amplitude=0.1 (waves along both axes) StairsTerrain, PyramidStairsTerrain step_width=0.75, step_height=-0.1 SteppingStonesTerrain stone_size=1.0, stone_distance=0.25, max_height=0.2, platform_size=0.0 FractalTerrain levels=8, scale=1.0 PerlinNoiseTerrain octaves=6, persistence=0.5, lacunarity=2.0, scale=20.0, amplitude=1.0 (in vertical_scale units), seed=-1 (random) GapTerrain gap_width=0.3, gap_depth=1.0, platform_width=1.0, num_gaps=4 PitTerrain pit_depth=0.5, pit_size_range=(0.5, 1.5), num_pits=8, platform_size=1.0 RidgeTerrain ridge_height=0.15, ridge_width=0.1, ridge_spacing=0.5 CraterTerrain crater_depth=0.3, crater_radius_range=(0.5, 2.0), num_craters=6 NarrowBeamsTerrain num_beams=16, beam_width=0.3, beam_height=0.2, platform_width=1.5, floor_depth=1.0 RandomGridTerrain grid_width=0.5, grid_height_range=(0.0, 0.3), platform_width=1.0 RandomBoxesTerrain num_boxes=40, box_size_range=(0.3, 1.0), box_height_range=(0.05, 0.5), platform_width=1.0 TiltedGridTerrain grid_width=1.0, tilt_range=15.0, height_range=0.1, platform_width=1.0 NestedRingsTerrain num_rings=5, ring_width=0.4, gap_width=0.2, height_range=(0.1, 0.4), platform_width=1.0 HeightFieldFileTerrain file: an exported height-field .npz (see below)

The parkour course generators, ported from extreme-parkour, carve corridor courses and also emit waypoint goals for goal-following commands: ParkourTerrain, ParkourGapTerrain, ParkourHurdleTerrain, ParkourStepTerrain, ParkourDemoTerrain and GapParkourTerrain. HalfSlopedTerrain emits a slope direction, and HalfPlatformTerrain and CustomSteppingStonesTerrain are standalone obstacles. Their parameters and the guarantees on their goals are documented in eden/utils/terrains/parkour_terrains.py; the extreme_parkour task uses them on 16 × 4 m lanes. A generator that raises (a course that does not fit its cell) is reported with the cell's row and column.

docs.title: The Terrain entity
docs.text:
After the build, the terrain answers height and layout queries:

Member Returns bounds (x_min, x_max, y_min, y_max) in world metres get_height(grid) heights (world z) at (B, h, w, 2) world xy points, bilinear; pass normalize=False if the points are already in [-1, 1] subterrain_origins (rows, cols, 3) world centres of the cells goals, goals_count (rows, cols, max_goals, 3) world waypoints per cell and the real count per cell (raises unless every cell's generator produces goals) slope_vectors (rows, cols, 3) per-cell slope directions (only HalfSlopedTerrain sets them) height_field_units the stitched height field in vertical_scale units (numpy, dim 0 = x) export_height_field(path) write the height field in metres to a versioned .npz

The GridScanDots observation (eden.managers.terms.observations.locomotion) samples get_height around the robot for a height scan; the velocity-tracking terrain task uses it (see Observations).

docs.title: Height fields on disk
docs.text:
Terrain.export_height_field(path) and eden.utils.terrains.export_height_field write a small .npz format (version 1: height_field in metres with axis 0 along world +x, horizontal_scale, and the origin of corner [0, 0]), for offline tools such as the terrain-adaptive retargeter (see TCRS terrain adaptation). To rebuild that exact terrain in a scene:

from eden.utils.terrains import terrain_options_from_height_field_file

terrain = terrain_options_from_height_field_file("terrain.npz")   # a TerrainOptions at the file's origin

It wraps the file in a one-cell grid of HeightFieldFileTerrain with vertical_scale=1.0 and the matching subterrain_size; building that by hand, the sizes must match the file or the generator raises.

docs.title: Writing a generator
docs.text:
Subclass TerrainGenerator, declare parameters as annotated class attributes, register it, and fill subterrain.height_field_raw (indexed (x, y), in vertical_scale units) in compute:

import numpy as np

from eden.utils.terrains import TERRAIN_GENERATOR_REGISTRY, TerrainGenerator


@TERRAIN_GENERATOR_REGISTRY.register()
class RampTerrain(TerrainGenerator):
    """A ramp that rises along x."""

    rise: float = 0.5   # metres over the cell

    def compute(self, subterrain):
        rows, cols = subterrain.height_field_raw.shape
        ramp = np.linspace(0.0, self.rise / subterrain.vertical_scale, rows)
        subterrain.height_field_raw[:] = ramp[:, None]
        return subterrain

Then use it in a grid as RampTerrain.configure(rise=0.3). Generators that emit goals set subterrain.goals (an (N, 2) array in cell-local metres); see the parkour module for the conventions.

docs.title: Gaussian-splat scenes
docs.text:
A splat scene renders a photogrammetric capture of a real room (a Gaussian-splat .ply) behind the simulated robot and objects. This is how the PolaRiS tasks put a simulated DROID arm into scanned kitchens and evaluate policies in them (real-to-sim evaluation).

The splat is not an entity. It is configured with splat_options on the config root, and the config class selects the environment class:

Config Environment splat_options type Backend EdenSplatConfig SplatEnvBase SplatOptions gsplat, composited over the sim render EdenSplatRLConfig SplatRLEnvBase SplatOptions gsplat, with the full RL manager surface EdenNyxSplatConfig NyxSplatEnvBase NyxSplatOptions Nyx path tracer, splat as a light field

All three are in eden.utils.configs; the options are in eden.options.splat. Each splat file is a PCDOptions passed by name:

# eden/tasks/polaris/base_config.py (make_polaris_splat) and food_bussing/config.py
from eden.options.splat import PCDOptions, SplatOptions

splat_options = SplatOptions(
    background=PCDOptions(
        path="food_bussing/assets/g60_corner_charuco_static/splat.ply",
        dataset="eden_polaris",
        assets_subdir="polaris",
        pos=(0.52, 0.6, 0.42),
        quat=(0.5, -0.5, -0.5, -0.5),
    ),
)

PCDOptions fields: path (fetched from registry / dataset when it is not a local file, at construction), scale, pos, quat (wxyz), multiplier and tint (Nyx only), and attach_entity / attach_link, which make the splat follow an entity's pose per environment (requires SplatOptions(per_env_gaussians=True)).

SplatOptions fields:

  • per_env_gaussians (default False): one shared Gaussian set for every env (memory-light), or one per env so attached splats follow each env's poses (memory grows with num_envs).
  • minibatch (default None): render this many envs at a time to bound peak VRAM.
  • camera_mode (default "auto"): "single" renders one env-invariant view and broadcasts it, "batched" renders every env's camera, and "auto" picks batched for attached or following cameras and when per_env_gaussians is on. "single" with per_env_gaussians=True raises.

The splat stands behind empty space only where the camera's SplatComposite overlay lets it; a task whose splat replaces a simulated surface (a table plane) names that entity in the overlay, as the PolaRiS tasks do with SplatComposite.configure(entities=["plane"]). Camera overlays, the renderers and the Nyx options are covered on Sensors and rendering.

To inspect a capture on its own, eden view path/to/splat.ply opens it in the viewer (-m scales its radiance, --env-brightness sets the background). The PolaRiS tasks are described on PolaRiS.

docs.title: Scripted demonstrations (eden datagen)
docs.text: eden datagen rolls a task's scripted demonstrator out in parallel envs and records every episode to HDF5 — the same layout as a teleoperated recording, so eden lerobot convert reads either. The demonstrators are a port of OCBench's scripted policies (eden/extensions/scripted_demos/), built to produce data that moves like a person — smooth, randomly paced, with retries and deliberate mistakes — rather than a rule-based controller with noise on top. This page covers running the generator, what it records, and how to write a demonstrator for a new task.

docs.title: Run it
docs.text:
eden datagen --task robosuite_stack --num_episodes 1000 --num_envs 32 --output_dir data/demos
eden datagen --task robosuite_stack --robot ur5e_2f85 --export succeeded   # OCBench's own arm, keep successes
eden datagen --task robosuite_lift --p_mistake 0.0                          # no deliberate mistakes
eden datagen --task robosuite_pick_place --camera_only                      # sees through the task camera
eden datagen --task robosuite_door --latch no_latch                         # a task variant flag
eden datagen --task simpler_put_carrot_on_plate \
    --override 'env_options: {use_gjk_collision: false}'                    # SIMPLER: see below
Flag Default Meaning --task — A task with a registered demonstrator (below). Its variant flags (--robot, --latch, --object, …) are accepted too; eden datagen --task <name> --help lists them. --num_episodes 100 Episodes to end before stopping. --num_envs 16 Parallel envs. --output_dir / --filename data/demos / the task name The dataset is <output_dir>/<filename>.hdf5. An existing file of that name is replaced. --export all all keeps every episode, tagged with its success; succeeded keeps only successes; separate writes failures to <filename>_failed.hdf5. --seed 0 Seeds the env and the demonstrator. --p_mistake the demonstrator's own Probability that a subgoal is a deliberate mistake. --episode_length_s the demonstrator's own, else 90 The generator's episode time limit. --camera_only off Run without the simulator's object state (demonstrators that support it). --show_viewer, --cpu off Open the Genesis viewer; use the CPU backend. --config, --override — Layer a config file or inline YAML onto the task config, as for eden train.

The run ends by printing a report: episodes, successes, how many were cut short, steps, wall time, and subgoals started by kind (goal, clear, mistake) — or, for a tool routine, motions ended by <tool>:<status>. For a tool routine the trace of the first unsuccessful episode follows; it is the place to start when the success rate is low. Logs go under logs/datagen/<task>/.

docs.title: Tasks with a demonstrator
docs.text:
SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY (eden/extensions/scripted_demos/registry.py) maps a task name to its demonstrator factory. A task without one is refused with the list of tasks that have one.

Task Demonstrator Variant flags, camera-only robosuite_lift, robosuite_stack keyframe (LiftController, TowerController) --robot robosuite_pick_place tool routine (eden/tasks/robosuite/pick_place/routine.py) --object; camera-only robosuite_door tool routine (door/routine.py) --latch robosuite_wipe tool routine (wipe/routine.py) robosuite_tool_hang tool routine (tool_hang/routine.py) robosuite_two_arm_transport two-arm routines (two_arm_transport/routine.py) simpler_stack_green_cube_on_yellow_cube keyframe (TowerController) simpler_put_carrot_on_plate, simpler_put_spoon_on_table_cloth, simpler_put_eggplant_in_basket tool routine (eden/extensions/scripted_demos/put_on_routine.py) camera-only polaris_block_stack_kitchen_batched, polaris_food_bussing_batched, polaris_pan_clean_batched, polaris_move_latte_cup_batched, polaris_organize_tools_batched, polaris_tape_into_container_batched tool routine (put-on, bound in eden/tasks/polaris/scripted_demos.py) whiteboard_write_text, whiteboard_write_in_colour, whiteboard_draw_table the task's own ScriptedDrawer art_calligraphy_dai, art_calligraphy_san, art_calligraphy_ei, art_calligraphy_lettering_minimum the task's own ScriptedWriter art_painting_sunset, art_painting_fuji_study, art_painting_fuji the task's own ScriptedPainter

The whiteboard and art demonstrators move a held tool through the arm's IK alone, with no gripper action and no randomness; they accept only --p_mistake 0. See Whiteboard and Art.

docs.title: What an episode records
docs.text:
The generator replaces the task's recorder options with this set, written with HDF5FileHandler:

Key Recorder Content obs/<group> ObservationRecorder Every observation group at the start of each step — what the step's action was chosen from. action ActionRecorder The action sent to the task's own action terms, so it replays as-is. state/{qpos,dofs_vel,pos,quat} StateRecorder The arm's state; a two-arm task records both arms, concatenated in scene order. eden lerobot convert reads this as observation.state. reward, done, terminated, timeout, timestamp RLStepRecorder Per-step RL buffers. initial_state/entities/... InitialStateRecorder Every entity's state after reset, for replay. attribute success — The task's success metric when the episode ended.

An episode ends when the demonstrator has finished the task (its success is the task's success metric at that step), when the task ends it (a termination, e.g. an object off the table), or at the generator's time limit — the generator enforces that limit itself, because a task need not declare a time-out. Episodes still running when --num_episodes is reached are dropped, not written cut short. The env is built in eval mode. The layout and its conversion are described in Datasets and recording.

The generator refuses a task with no success metric (no metric term with contributes_to_success=True), since its episodes could not be labelled, and it refuses export_mode=EXPORT_NONE.

SIMPLER tasks record no observations

SIMPLER tasks are evaluated from the camera and declare no observation groups, so their episodes have no obs/* keys (and no images).

docs.title: What makes the data demo-like
docs.text: Property Where What it does Smooth, non-Markovian motion trajectory.py Each subgoal is a keyframe plan executed on a per-env clock: Hermite splines that come to rest at stop keyframes (before closing, at the place, at the end) and pass through the others; rotation and gripper ease with a quintic smoothstep. Human speed profile trajectory.py Segments are stretched so a minimum-jerk profile never exceeds a peak tool speed: T >= 1.875 d / v_peak. Speed varies per episode controller.py One segment_dt per episode, uniform in speed_range (default (0.7, 1.5) s). Tool routines draw a speed factor from their own speed_range (default (0.8, 1.25)). Varied grasps and paths primitives.py Grasp face (usually the nearest), wrist tilt up to max_tilt (25° by default), approach heights, contact offsets, an optional pause before lifting, when the fingers close, and a carry midpoint that bows sideways and sometimes overshoots. Recovers from failure controller.py A pick whose object does not follow the hand is re-planned from wherever the hand is (max_pick_retries=2), every random offset scaled by 0.75 per retry. Suboptimal high-level plans block_world.py With probability p_mistake (default 0.1) a subgoal is replaced by a wrong one — a block moved to a random free spot or onto another — and the demonstrator works its way back. Unsaturated actions rig.py + the task binding See Speed and saturation.

docs.title: The robot it drives
docs.text:
A demonstrator drives an arm with a two-finger gripper through the task's own action terms. It reads what it needs from the scene entry holding the robot (gripper_rig() in rig.py); two shapes qualify:

Scene entry Arm / fingers IK link Tool point a ManipulatorOptions composite (robosuite's rigs, DROID, UR5e + Robotiq) the arm entity / the welded gripper entity the composite's ee_link the gripper's tcp_offset, carried through the weld a RobotOptions whose asset has its own fingers (SIMPLER's WidowX250) every actuated DOF except those of open_dofs_pos / the DOFs of open_dofs_pos ee_links_name[0] the robot's tcp_offset, in that link's frame

A robot of the second shape must declare open_dofs_pos, ee_links_name and tcp_offset; a missing one is refused by name. tcp_offset is the pad midpoint with the fingers open — measure it off the built finger pads (the WidowX's is (0.0935, 0, 0) in its IK link). Its direction is the approach axis: +z for a Franka Hand or a Robotiq mount, +x for the WidowX.

The action terms are found by what they drive, not by name (find_rig_actions()): one DifferentialIKController on the arm's IK link and one BinaryJointController on the fingers. robosuite names them robot_arm / robot_gripper, SIMPLER and PolaRiS ee_controller / gripper_controller. Every action term of the task must be one of the two (for one arm, or for each arm of a two-arm task).

docs.title: How it drives the robot
docs.text:
The demonstrator plans the tool point and converts it to the task's action every step (RigDriver in rig.py): a 6-D world-frame delta of the IK link's pose, at most max_step_translation per axis (default 0.05 m) and max_step_rotation (default 0.3 rad) per step — OCBench's ee_action_delta clip — and 2g − 1 for the binary gripper. The IK term squashes its input with tanh, so the recorded arm action is atanh(delta / scale), with the ratio capped at 0.9 (MAX_COMMAND_RATIO).

Object poses come from the scene in their authored frames (get_pos(relative=True)), never from the noisy policy observations. The keyframe controller also handles what OCBench did not need on Eden's robots:

  • Headings respect the wrist. A Panda's last joint turns ±2.9 rad and the task's damped-least-squares IK has no posture term, so the arm drifts in its null space. Every heading is moved by a symmetry of what it grasps (a quarter turn for a cube, a half turn for the gripper) into the range the last joint can still reach (yaw_window()).
  • Plans start from the hand's actual orientation, not its heading alone (the robosuite Panda's home pose is tilted).
  • The plan waits at the grasp and the release. Contact gates hold the plan clock until the hand is within contact_gate_tolerance (1 cm) of the gate — or has come to rest against contact within 4 cm of it (slower than 1 cm/s for 0.6 s: SETTLE_SPEED, SETTLE_TIME, SETTLE_REACH), the way a person lowers a cube onto another until it stops.
  • A pick is judged by whether the object follows the hand: the check waits until the hand has risen three quarters of the way to its hover and fails the pick only if the object rose less than half as much (PICK_CHECK_RISE, PICK_FOLLOW_FRACTION).
  • The fingertips, not the tool point, stay above the table. The workspace floor is for the fingertips: the driver measures how far the fingers reach past the tool point on the built rig (tip_reach) and raises the tool's floor by it.
  • The gripper never closes during the descent: closing ramps over the contact segment or the pause before lifting only, which suits a binary gripper.

docs.title: Speed and saturation
docs.text:
The task's action realizes only part of each command per step (damped IK into a position-PD arm), so an arm asked to follow a fast plan lags it, and the command saturates — the bang-bang data the demonstrators exist to avoid. Each binding sizes its peak speed and step clip to what its action realizes:

  • robosuite and SIMPLER bindings use a peak speed of 0.12 m/s, PolaRiS 0.15 m/s; OCBench's own default (PickPlaceParams.peak_speed) is 0.3.
  • SIMPLER's WidowX has a generous IK scale (0.5 m per action unit) but trails its plan at 5 Hz, so its binding lifts max_step_translation to 0.1 m, caps the wrist tilt at 0.1 rad, and uses Bridge-scale hover heights (_DESCENT_HEIGHT = (0.04, 0.12)).

A new binding should measure how often its arm commands sit at the clip before choosing peak_speed and max_step_translation.

docs.title: Writing a demonstrator
docs.text: Register a factory under the task's name, next to the task (eden/tasks/<suite>/scripted_demos.py), and list that module in SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY's populated_by. A factory is (env, *, seed, p_mistake) -> demonstrator; one that also takes privileged has a camera-only mode, and one whose episodes need longer than 90 s declares it as an attribute (my_factory.episode_length_s = 200.0).

docs.title: Keyframe demonstrators
docs.text:
A keyframe demonstrator is a batched state machine: fast, but a new kind of task means a new subclass. Block worlds reuse TowerController or LiftController (block_world.py):

from eden.extensions.scripted_demos.block_world import TowerController
from eden.extensions.scripted_demos.primitives import PickPlaceParams
from eden.extensions.scripted_demos.registry import SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY


@SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY.register(name="my_three_block_tower")
def my_three_block_tower(env, *, seed=0, p_mistake=0.1):
    return TowerController(
        env, ["base", "middle", "top"], table_z=0.8,
        spot_bounds=((-0.12, -0.15), (0.12, 0.15)),
        workspace=((-0.35, -0.35, 0.805), (0.35, 0.35, 1.25)),
        effector_bounds=((-0.2, -0.15, 0.92), (0.05, 0.15, 1.1)),
        p_mistake=p_mistake, seed=seed, params=PickPlaceParams(peak_speed=0.12),
    )

Any other pick-and-place task subclasses ScriptedPickPlaceController and implements choose_subgoals(env_ids, objects) -> list[Subgoal | None], returning None for an env whose task is complete.

docs.title: Tool routines
docs.text:
A tool routine is a scripted policy written for one robot as a plain Python generator, against a handful of robot tools — the form a person or a coding agent writes a demonstrator in. RoutineDemonstrator (routines.py) runs one instance per env, batched:

import math

from eden.extensions.scripted_demos.registry import SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY
from eden.extensions.scripted_demos.routines import RoutineDemonstrator


def pick_and_lift(tools):
    for attempt in range(3):
        cube = tools.object_footprint("cube")                    # or tools.locate("cube") through a camera
        yaw = cube.yaw + math.pi / 2 - tools.finger_axis_yaw    # close across the short side
        yield tools.open_gripper()
        yield tools.move_to(cube.top_center + (0, 0, 0.10), yaw)
        yield tools.move_to((*cube.top_center[:2], cube.top_z - 0.02), yaw)
        yield tools.close_gripper()
        yield tools.move_by((0, 0, 0.15))
        if tools.holding():
            return
        tools.note(f"attempt {attempt} missed (closure {tools.gripper_closure():.2f})")


@SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY.register(name="my_lift")
def my_lift(env, *, seed=0, p_mistake=0.0):
    return RoutineDemonstrator(env, pick_and_lift, seed=seed, workspace=((-0.35, -0.35, 0.805), (0.35, 0.35, 1.25)))

A motion is yielded, and the routine gets an Outcome back when the motion has ended. Its status is one of reached, contact, done, timeout, blocked or no_contact, and outcome.ok is true for the first three, so checks and retries are ordinary Python. Routines resume only at those boundaries; every motion in flight is evaluated as batched torch and turned into the task's actions by the same RigDriver the keyframe controller uses.

Tool (tools.py) Kind What it does or reads move_to(pos, yaw), move_by(offset) motion Straight, minimum-jerk path at the episode's speed; yaw is turned by a half turn into the range the last joint reaches. Ends reached within tolerance (default 1 cm) or timeout (timeout_s, default 2 s past the path's own duration). move_to(pos, rot=tools.aim(approach, closing)) motion The same to a full effector rotation (a hand that leans or points sideways), judged on the whole rotation. move_until_contact(direction, max_distance) motion Constant speed until a finger presses on something that is not the robot (contact), the hand is held back without one (blocked), or the distance is used up (no_contact). close_gripper(), open_gripper(), wait(s) motion Hold the arm, set the fingers; done. tool_pos(), tool_yaw(), tool_rotation(), gripper_closure(), holding() robot The robot's own state. holding(): commanded closed and stopped short of closing (holding_closure, default 0.9). heading_window() robot The lowest and highest heading the last joint can turn the hand to from here. object_footprint(name), grasped(name) privileged Off the simulator: the footprint of the collision mesh; two finger links touching the object. link_pose(name, link=None) privileged A link's (or the root's) pose in the asset's authored frame — for an articulated fixture's parts, or a kinematic entity with no collision mesh. locate(name, camera=None) camera The footprint of the pixels showing name, back-projected through depth: what the camera sees, occlusion included. The segmentation stands in for a perfect text-prompted segmenter. shared, rng, note(text) episode A per-episode dict (shared between arms), the episode's random stream, and a line in the trace.

A Footprint is the same whichever way it was measured — center, yaw (of the long axis), half_length, half_width, top_z, bottom_z, and top_center (where a hand coming from above meets it, off the centre when the object leans) — so a routine written against it runs privileged or camera-only unchanged.

Camera-only. RoutineDemonstrator(..., privileged=False, cameras=("agentview",)) refuses object_footprint and grasped with PrivilegedToolError, naming the camera tool to use instead, so a demonstrator meant for deployment cannot read simulator state by accident. With several envs each camera must render every env: eden datagen --camera_only sets env_options.env_separate_rigid for you; built by hand, the demonstrator refuses a shared camera. Camera-only runs render every env's view at each routine boundary, so they are slower.

The trace. Every ended motion and every tools.note(...) is a line of demo.trace(env_id):

 36.75 s  # bread -> goal quadrant (0.149, 0.083)
 37.25 s  move_to(0.214, -0.311, 0.953, yaw=-1.06) -> reached in 1.50 s (off target 10 mm)
 38.75 s  move_to(0.214, -0.311, 0.844, yaw=-1.06) -> timeout in 3.50 s (off target 185 mm)
 47.05 s  # bread: pick 1 missed (closure 1.00)

A routine written for one task lives with that task, in eden/tasks/<suite>/<task>/routine.py, as a factory that returns the routine; the suite's scripted_demos.py binds it to the scene. A routine several suites share lives in eden/extensions/scripted_demos/ (put_on_routine.py, used by SIMPLER and PolaRiS). Each routine module's docstring records the design decisions its rollouts forced — read it before changing the routine.

docs.title: Two-arm routines
docs.text:
A two-arm task is two routines, one per arm, each written against its own Tools and run side by side by MultiArmDemonstrator (multi_arm.py). Each arm resumes its routine when its own motion ends; they coordinate through tools.shared, a dict both routines of an env share for the episode:

from eden.extensions.scripted_demos.multi_arm import MultiArmDemonstrator


def giver(tools):
    ...  # carry the object to the hand-off pose
    tools.shared["offered"] = True
    while not tools.shared.get("taken"):
        yield tools.wait(0.1)
    yield tools.open_gripper()


def taker(tools):
    while not tools.shared.get("offered"):
        yield tools.wait(0.1)
    ...  # close on the object
    tools.shared["taken"] = True


demo = MultiArmDemonstrator(
    env, {"robot0": giver, "robot1": taker},
    workspace={"robot0": ((-0.45, -0.75, 0.805), (0.45, 0.2, 1.3)), "robot1": ((-0.45, -0.2, 0.805), (0.45, 0.75, 1.3))},
)

Options that differ per arm are dicts keyed by every arm's scene entry; other options apply to both. A single-arm RoutineDemonstrator on a two-arm task is refused, naming the other arm's terms. An env's task is complete when both routines have returned; an arm that finishes first holds still. The trace interleaves both arms' lines, each prefixed with its arm, and the report counts motions per arm (robot0/move_to:reached).

docs.title: Running a demonstrator by hand
docs.text:
Every demonstrator exposes reset(envs_idx=None), update_subgoals() (returns a per-env "done" mask) and act() (returns the action dict). The generator's loop, reduced:

from eden.extensions.scripted_demos.registry import SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY

demo = SCRIPTED_DEMO_REGISTRY.get("robosuite_lift")(env, seed=0)
demo.reset()
while True:
    done = demo.update_subgoals()
    if done.any():
        env.reset(done)
        demo.reset(done)
    env.step(demo.act())
    if env.reset_buf.any():       # the env ended some episodes itself
        demo.reset(env.reset_buf)

Reset the demonstrator for every env the env resets: a routine that keeps running after the env has reset the scene under it acts on a scene it no longer knows. generate_demos() in eden/extensions/scripted_demos/generate.py is the full version, with the recorder, success labels and the time limit.

docs.title: Suite notes
docs.text: These are the constraints found while making each suite's demonstrators succeed; the routine module docstrings carry the full reasoning.

docs.title: robosuite
docs.text:
• PickPlace carries objects over the tallest thing in the way, not just the bin rims; places on the robot's side of the target cell (the far cell centres are at the edge of the Panda's reach); grasps up to 4.5 cm deep (GRASP_DEPTH) so the milk carton is not held by its gable top; and waits for the reset's drop to settle before looking.
  • Door leans the hand 30° away from the panel (LEAN: a hand pointing straight down has its palm in the panel), presses the handle down until the latch clears the frame, then pulls with the rigid back finger and turns the hand with the door. Door positions are read with link_pose, since the door is re-posed every reset.
  • Wipe feels for the table with move_until_contact at low speed and sweeps just above the touch height: the pad is position-controlled, so commanding it into the table pushes back with tens of newtons per millimetre, and robosuite's excess-force penalty starts at 60 N. It levels the hand first, and stops at every marker.
  • ToolHang pinches each object above its centre of mass and expects it to turn in the pinch (there is no torsional friction on the pads), re-measuring the grasp after each turn. The wrench's contacts are stiffened (GRASPED_SOL_PARAMS).
  • TwoArmTransport hands the hammer across in the air, because neither arm reaches both the start bin and the target bin. robot0 lets go only after robot1's fingers have closed (taken on tools.shared). The robosuite Panda rig uses robosuite's gripper actuation, and the carried objects carry stiffened default_geoms_sol_params so they do not creep out of the pinch. The DROID rig (--robot droid) is not covered by this routine.

docs.title: SIMPLER
docs.text:
• Run with MPR collision: --override 'env_options: {use_gjk_collision: false}'. Genesis's GJK narrowphase can report a non-finite contact between thin convex geoms (the WidowX's finger pads are thin boxes), which a long scripted rollout eventually hits. The generator stops with this fix in its message; catching the error and resetting does not help, because every env's solver state is invalid after it.
  • Every SIMPLER task enables torsional friction with a 2 cm contact patch on the fingers: without it, a spoon pinched at its thin handle spins about the line between the pads.
  • RoutineDemonstrator keeps commanding a move's target through the waits and gripper motions that follow it, because the WidowX's damped IK closes the last centimetre slowly and the pads would otherwise close high.
  • The put-on routine looks until the object has stopped before picking: eggplants roll across the basin after the reset.

docs.title: PolaRiS
docs.text:
• The demonstrators are registered on the *_batched tasks: eden datagen needs the RL surface and many envs, and the single-env PolaRiS tasks are teleop and inference scenes.
  • Success is PolaRiS's own rubric (eden/tasks/polaris/rubric.py, the rubric metric of every PolaRiS task): reach, lift and placement criteria mapped onto EeNearEntity, object_bottom_above_height and object_a_within_b_xy, with RubricMetricTerm keeping PolaRiS's bookkeeping.
  • Objects wider than the Robotiq 2F-85's stroke (the latte cup, the tape roll) are gripped by their wall (grasp="rim"). A thin wall barely stops the fingers, so the PolaRiS demonstrators use holding_closure=0.97.
  • Goal(container=True) drops the object anywhere inside a container, avoiding what already lies in it (avoid=) and staying within reach (max_reach=); clutter= names entities a pinch keeps its fingers off.
  • The batched tasks render with the batch renderer, which privileged datagen does not use. On a GPU it cannot launch on, swap in the rasterizer before building: config.renderer_options = genesis.options.renderers.RendererOptions(). The PolaRiS demonstrators are privileged only: their camera-only mode has not been run.
