docs.text:
• Datasets and recording — the HDF5 layout and eden lerobot convert.
  • Teleoperation — recording human demonstrations of the same tasks.
  • Grasp sampling — learned grasp poses.
  • robosuite, SIMPLER, PolaRiS — the suites these demonstrators script.

docs.title: Sensors and rendering
docs.text:
This page covers everything an Eden environment can observe besides its own state: cameras and the renderers behind them, Gaussian-splat backgrounds, camera overlays, video recording, and the Genesis sensors (IMU, contact, lidar, depth, tactile and the rest). Read it when you give a policy pixels, record a rollout, or attach a sensor to a robot.

Cameras are declared in a config's cameras_options, sensors in its sensors_options, and the renderer in its renderer_options. All three are built with the env, in env.build(); afterwards they are reachable as env.cameras[name], env.sensors[name] and env.scene.visualizer.

docs.title: Declaring a camera
docs.text:
A camera is a named CameraOptions entry of CamerasOptions. From the vision lift task (eden/tasks/manipulation/lift_box_rgb/config.py), a 128x72 wrist camera mounted on the robot's tool flange:

from eden.options.camera import CameraOptions, CamerasOptions

cameras_options = CamerasOptions(
    wrist=CameraOptions(
        cam_resolution=(128, 72),
        cam_fov=80,
        attach_entity_name="robot",
        attach_link_name="attachment",
        attach_offset=(0.070, -0.026, 0.013),
        attach_quat=(0.103966, 0.692961, 0.703320, 0.119734),  # wxyz
    ),
)
Field Default Meaning cam_pos, cam_lookat, cam_up (1.5, 0.0, 1), (0.0, 0.0, 0.5), (0.0, 0.0, 1.0) World pose of a free camera. cam_resolution (720, 480) Image size as (width, height). cam_fov 80.0 Vertical field of view, in degrees. cam_intrinsic None A 3x3 intrinsic matrix. When set, it overrides cam_fov and cam_resolution (with a warning). cam_extrinsic None A 4x4 world-to-camera matrix. When set, it overrides cam_pos, cam_lookat and cam_up. cam_near, cam_far None Clipping planes in meters; None keeps the renderer's default. model, cam_aperture "pinhole", 2.0 Camera model ("pinhole" or "thinlens") and aperture. follow_entity_name "" Follow an entity, keeping the camera's orientation. attach_entity_name, attach_link_name, attach_offset, attach_quat "", "", None, None Mount the camera on a link. All four go together; the quaternion is wxyz. debug False A debug camera rasterizes even in a scene that uses the batch renderer. overlays [] What is painted onto every RGB frame (see Camera overlays). sensor_options None Build the camera as a Genesis camera sensor instead (see Camera backends).

follow_entity_name and the attach_* fields exclude each other. An entity name that does not exist raises at build and lists the scene's entities.

docs.title: Reading images
docs.text:
On a built env, a camera renders on demand:

Method Returns render_rgb() The RGB frame, with the camera's overlays painted on. Recorded when the camera is recording. render_depth() Depth. render_segm() Segmentation ids. render_normal() Surface normals. render_pointcloud(world_frame=True) (points, valid_mask), one 3D point per pixel. render(rgb=True, depth=False, segmentation=False, colorize_seg=False, normal=False) The raw multi-output pass, (rgb, depth, segmentation, normal). No overlays. snapshot(image_path=None) Writes render_rgb() of the first image to a PNG (default {log_dir}/snapshot_<time>.png).

A camera that renders several environments at once (the batch renderer, the sensor backend, or a scene with EnvOptions.env_separate_rigid=True) returns one image per environment, with a leading batch dimension. A plain rasterizer camera returns the image of the one environment it is bound to.

The pose can be read and moved after the build: get_pos(), get_quat(), get_lookat(), get_up(), get_transform(), set_pose(transform=None, pos=None, lookat=None, up=None), set_pos(pos), set_quat(quat), each with an optional envs_idx=.

docs.title: Cameras as observations
docs.text:
Five observation terms read a camera by name: rgb_image, depth_image, segmentation_image, normal_image and pointcloud_image (which zeroes the pixels that hit nothing, so infinite depth never reaches the policy). rgb_image returns the renderer's native output, (N, H, W, C) uint8, unless you ask for a CNN-ready tensor: normalize=True converts to float in [0, 1], channels_first=True permutes to (N, C, H, W), and either one drops an alpha channel (the batch renderer returns RGBA). The vision lift task feeds the wrist camera to its CNN this way:

from eden import observations
from eden.options import ObservationGroupOptions
from eden.terms import ObsTerm

wrist_rgb = ObsTerm.configure(
    func=observations.rgb_image,
    params={"camera_name": "wrist", "normalize": True, "channels_first": True},
)
camera_group = ObservationGroupOptions(wrist_rgb=wrist_rgb, enable_corruption=False)

A group that holds a single image term keeps its (N, C, H, W) shape, which is how rsl_rl's CNN actor-critic recognizes an image group. See Observations for groups, noise and history.

Rendering one image per environment per step is the expensive part of a vision task: use the batch renderer when you train from pixels with many environments.

docs.title: Segmentation
docs.text: EnvOptions.segmentation_level ("entity" by default, or "link", "geom") sets what one segmentation id stands for. env.segmentation_idx_dict maps an id to the scene element (an entity_idx, or a tuple at link and geom level); env.entity_segmentation_ids maps the other way, entity_idx -> [ids]. Use the latter to mask an entity out of a segmentation image: at link or geom level an entity owns several ids.

docs.title: Camera backends
docs.text:
A camera is built one of two ways:

  • The default backend (sensor_options=None) calls Genesis' scene.add_camera(). It renders RGB, depth, segmentation, normals and point clouds, through the scene's renderer.
  • The sensor backend (sensor_options=<Genesis camera sensor options>) calls scene.add_sensor(). Use it for Nyx (NyxCameraOptions) or for a camera with its own lights (RasterizerCameraOptions(lights=...), as the LIBERO port does). It renders RGB only: render_depth(), render_segm(), render_normal(), render_pointcloud() and render() raise. Read it with render_rgb() or read() (Genesis' CameraData, whose .rgb is the image), and use pick_pixel(camera_index, x, y) to cast a ray through a pixel. The sensor's pos, lookat, up, fov and res are filled from the cam_* fields unless you set them on the sensor options. cam_near / cam_far are passed on too; setting a different plane on both raises rather than letting one win.

An overlay that reads segmentation or a point cloud cannot run on the sensor backend and is refused when the env is constructed.

docs.title: Renderers
docs.text:
renderer_options picks the renderer the scene's cameras use. The interactive viewer always uses the rasterizer.

Renderer Options Install Use it for Rasterizer gs.renderers.Rasterizer() (the default) included Everything by default: debugging, recordings, small vision tasks. Batch renderer (Madrona) BatchRendererOptions (eden.options) gs-madrona, Linux x86-64 only Training from pixels: one batched render of every environment. Ray tracer RayTracerOptions (eden.options) Genesis' ray tracer Offline, high-quality stills. Nyx path tracer per camera: CameraOptions(sensor_options=NyxCameraOptions(...)) pip install 'eden-world[nyx]' / uv sync --inexact --extra nyx; no macOS build; CUDA only Photoreal renders and Nyx splat scenes.

docs.title: Rasterizer
docs.text: The rasterizer draws shadows when EnvOptions.rasterizer_shadows is on (the default); Eden applies the switch to rasterizer camera sensors too. EnvOptions.background_color (default (0.04, 0.08, 0.12)) is the empty-space colour. Shadows need a GPU-backed OpenGL context: a software renderer (llvmpipe) draws none.

docs.title: Batch renderer
docs.text:
BatchRendererOptions subclasses Genesis' gs.renderers.BatchRenderer and adds a declarative lights list.

Madrona renders ambient-only until you add lights

Without lights the cameras come out near-black, and Madrona bakes the light count when the scene is built, so every light has to exist before env.build(). Declare them on BatchRendererOptions.lights (one scene.add_light(**kwargs) dict each) and Eden adds them right after it creates the scene. Genesis' plain gs.renderers.BatchRenderer has no such field.

From eden/tasks/manipulation/lift_box_rgb/config.py:

from eden.options import BatchRendererOptions

renderer_options = BatchRendererOptions(
    lights=[
        {"pos": (0.3, -0.6, 1.5), "dir": (0.0, 0.4, -1.0), "directional": True, "castshadow": False, "intensity": 3.0},
        {"pos": (0.3, 0.6, 1.5), "dir": (0.0, -0.4, -1.0), "directional": True, "castshadow": False, "intensity": 3.0},
    ]
)

use_rasterizer=True (Genesis' field) makes Madrona rasterize instead of ray trace; the extreme-parkour student uses it for its batched depth camera. The first run of a scene compiles Madrona's render kernels, which takes a while (the extreme-parkour README reports 10–15 minutes for its scene).

docs.title: Nyx
docs.text:
Nyx is a CUDA path tracer that plugs into Genesis as a camera sensor (gs_nyx_plugin). Import its options inside your script, after eden.init(); importing them registers the plugin with Genesis. A Nyx scene needs at least one light or environment map. From examples/recipes/rendering/nyx_multi_camera_multi_env.py, two Nyx cameras over four environments:

import eden as en
import genesis as gs

from eden.options.camera import CameraOptions, CamerasOptions

en.init(backend=gs.gpu)
from gs_nyx_plugin.nyx_camera_options import NyxCameraOptions  # registers the plugin with Genesis

lights = [
    {"type": "point", "pos": (2.5, -2.5, 4.0), "color": (1.0, 0.97, 0.92), "intensity": 80.0},
    {"type": "directional", "dir": (0.2, 0.3, -1.0), "color": (1.0, 1.0, 1.0), "intensity": 2.0},
]
cameras_options = CamerasOptions(
    wide=CameraOptions(
        cam_pos=(0.5, -2.5, 4.0),
        cam_lookat=(0.0, 0.0, 0.3),
        cam_fov=42.0,
        sensor_options=NyxCameraOptions(spp=32, denoise=True, lights=lights),
    ),
)
# after env.build() and a step:
rgb = env.cameras["wide"].read().rgb   # (num_envs, H, W, 3)

The lights of every Nyx camera are merged scene-wide. More recipes live in examples/recipes/rendering/ (minimal_nyx.py, nyx_light_types.py, nyx_materials.py, nyx_object_picking.py). The Nyx plugin knows only Genesis' own solvers: a Mochi scene rendered through Nyx needs the bridge in examples/recipes/mochi/_nyx.py, or it renders a still frame of the rest pose without any error.

docs.title: Ray tracer
docs.text: RayTracerOptions subclasses Genesis' gs.renderers.RayTracer with an indoor environment map (decoded on first use) and one overhead light. Several Eden features refuse it at build: the Mochi solver, PlanePaintOverlay, and a background composite with a non-zero shadow_strength.

docs.title: Surfaces
docs.text: What a body looks like is its surface, an eden.options.surfaces class: DefaultSurfaceOptions, PlasticSurfaceOptions, MetalSurfaceOptions, BSDFSurfaceOptions, GlassSurfaceOptions or EmissionSurfaceOptions. A Genesis gs.surfaces.* object is accepted too.

docs.title: Gaussian splats
docs.text:
A Gaussian splat gives a scene a photoreal background (a captured kitchen, a table top) while the physics runs on simple collision geometry. Eden has two backends, each with its own config leaf and env class:

Backend Config Env Options Install gsplat EdenSplatConfig / EdenSplatRLConfig SplatEnvBase / SplatRLEnvBase splat_options=SplatOptions(...) pip install 'eden-world[batch-splat]' / uv sync --inexact --extra batch-splat (also in vis); CUDA Nyx EdenNyxSplatConfig NyxSplatEnvBase splat_options=NyxSplatOptions(...) the nyx extra

env_class_for_config(cfg) picks the env from the config class. Each splat is a PCDOptions entry given as a named extra of the splat options. path is a PLY file, fetched from the Hugging Face dataset named by registry / dataset when it is not a local file; scale, pos and quat (wxyz) place it.

docs.title: gsplat
docs.text:
From the PolaRiS port (eden/tasks/polaris/base_config.py), simplified:

from eden.entities.camera_overlays import SplatComposite
from eden.options.camera import CameraOptions
from eden.options.splat import PCDOptions, SplatOptions

splat_options = SplatOptions(
    background=PCDOptions(path=path, dataset="eden_polaris", assets_subdir="polaris", scale=scale, pos=pos, quat=quat),
)
external_camera = CameraOptions(..., overlays=[SplatComposite.configure(entities=["plane"])])

The splat is composited over the sim pass by segmentation: wherever a camera's frame shows nothing, or one of the entities of its SplatComposite (here the ground plane standing in for the real table), the splat replaces it. Robot and object pixels stay from the sim pass.

A camera shows the splat only if it declares a SplatComposite

A splat env's camera without one shows the plain sim pass. EdenSplatConfig.recording_camera() (what eden inference --rec adds) declares one with no entities, so the splat shows behind empty space; a task whose splat stands in for a sim surface overrides it to name that entity.

SplatOptions fields:

  • per_env_gaussians (default False). False stores one Gaussian set and renders every environment's camera from it: memory-light, and the splat looks the same in every environment. True gives each environment its own Gaussians, so a splat bound to an entity (PCDOptions(attach_entity=..., attach_link=...)) follows that environment's simulated pose. Memory then grows with num_envs, which fits tens to hundreds of environments.
  • camera_mode (default "auto"). A SplatCamera renders one view and uses it for every environment's image (a fixed camera over a shared background); a BatchSplatCamera renders every environment's view. "auto" picks the batched camera for an attached or following camera or under per_env_gaussians=True, the single view otherwise. "single" and "batched" force one class for every camera; "single" with per_env_gaussians=True is refused.
  • minibatch (default None). Chunk size over the views, which bounds peak GPU memory: gsplat evaluates view-dependent colour per rendered view.

docs.title: Nyx splats
docs.text: NyxSplatOptions renders the splats inside the path tracer as Nyx light fields. Every camera of a NyxSplatEnvBase becomes a Nyx camera: one declared without sensor_options gets a NyxCameraOptions built from the splat options (spp=32, denoise=True, near, far, lights, env_map_paths), and the env's light fields and environment maps are merged into one that brings its own. tone_mapper (default "ACES_1_3"; also "Neutral", "Off", "Reinhard") and exposure_compensation (in EV, default 0) are written into each camera's profile. PCDOptions.multiplier and tint scale a splat's radiance on this backend only. max_pt_depth must stay None: the plugin has no path-depth control, so a value is refused rather than ignored.

docs.title: Camera overlays
docs.text:
Some task state is visible in the real world but has no geometry in the scene: ink on a whiteboard, strokes of a brush. A camera overlay paints that state onto every RGB frame the camera produces, after the renderer made it. A background composite is an overlay too. Overlays apply in render_rgb(), so they reach the returned frame, the recording, snapshot() and any observation that reads the camera; render() stays the raw pass.

An overlay is declared by registry key on CameraOptions.overlays, with the overlay class's configure(), so it survives a saved config.json. From the whiteboard task (eden/tasks/whiteboard/config.py):

from eden.entities.camera_overlays import PlanePaintOverlay

CameraOptions(
    cam_pos=(-0.30, -1.05, 1.68),
    cam_lookat=(0.45, 0.02, 1.18),
    cam_fov=42.0,
    cam_resolution=(960, 540),
    overlays=[PlanePaintOverlay.configure(metric_name="drawing", color=ink)],
)

Eden ships three overlays (eden.entities.camera_overlays):

Overlay Paints PlanePaintOverlay(metric_name, color=None, max_gap=0.002, supersample=4) The marks a metric term returns (a PaintedPlaneSource, such as the whiteboard's drawing metric) where the camera sees the plane they lie on. Shaded like the surface, so marks keep its shadows. BackgroundImageComposite(image_path, entities=[], shadow_strength=0.0) An image in place of the background: a real-image backdrop, or a green screen. SplatComposite(entities=[], shadow_strength=0.0) The env's Gaussian splat in place of the background. Only a gsplat env's camera can carry it.

Rules:

  • One background composite per camera, declared first. The overlays after it leave its pixels alone, since they no longer show the sim surface an overlay locates its marks on.
  • Parameters are checked in the config. An unknown parameter or a bad value raises when the CameraOverlayOptions is constructed, naming the overlay and its parameters.
  • A point-cloud overlay costs a second render. PlanePaintOverlay needs each pixel's world point, so the camera renders the view's depth once more per frame (once for all its overlays).
  • PlanePaintOverlay needs a plain-coloured surface on the rasterizer or the batch renderer; an image-textured surface and the ray tracer are refused at build.
  • Frames rendered before the managers exist are not painted, for instance the one the observation manager renders while it loads to size its terms.

docs.title: Shadows on a background
docs.text:
By default a composited background receives no shadows: the objects seem to float. Set shadow_strength (0 to 1) to darken the background wherever the sim pass shows a shadow on the composite's entities; it needs at least one entity, since the shadows are read from them.

  • Rasterizer: the camera renders the view a second time with shadows off and compares each pixel with itself, so any surface works. EnvOptions.rasterizer_shadows must stay on, and the OpenGL context must be GPU-backed.
  • Batch renderer: shadows cannot be switched off per render, so the unshadowed brightness of each background entity is estimated from its brightest pixels in view. This is exact for a flat, untextured surface under directional lights. An image-textured background entity is refused, and Genesis' plane is one by default (a checkerboard), so give it a plain colour, PlaneOptions(color=(0.5, 0.5, 0.5)). At least one light needs castshadow=True. A point light's falloff is read as shadow, and a view where almost all of the entity is in shadow loses the shadow.

Shading holds about 20 * N * H * W bytes of temporaries per frame (about 1 GB at 1024 envs of 224x224).

docs.title: Writing an overlay
docs.text: Subclass CameraOverlay, declare its parameters as class attributes, register it with @CAMERA_OVERLAY_REGISTRY.register(), and implement paint(rgb, buffers, envs_idx). rgb is (N, H, W, 3) on the env's device in the renderer's dtype; return the same shape and dtype, and never write into rgb (it may be the renderer's own buffer). Set _needs_segmentation = True or _needs_pointcloud = True to receive those in buffers. Resolve whatever the overlay reads in build(), which runs after the managers are built, and check parameter values in the classmethod check_parameters(params).

docs.title: Recording video
docs.text:
Recording belongs to Eden's Camera:

camera = env.cameras["rec"]
camera.start_recording("rollout.mp4", fps=1.0 / env.dt)   # real-time playback
for _ in range(steps):
    env.step(actions)
    camera.render_rgb()                                   # one frame per call
camera.stop_recording()

The contract:

  • One frame per render() or render_rgb() call, not per scene.step(). A kinematic replay that never steps the scene records exactly as a stepped rollout does.
  • start_recording(video_path=None, fps=60.0) fixes the path and the frame rate for the whole video. The default path is {log_dir}/video_<time>.mp4. Playback runs at fps render calls per second, whatever the simulation time step, so pass fps=1 / env.dt for real time when you render once per control step. (eden inference --rec uses the default 60 fps and renders once per control step, so a task with a 50 Hz policy plays back 1.2x fast.)
  • Frames are encoded on a background thread and streamed to the file, so a long recording does not fill memory.
  • A camera that renders several environments writes one video per environment, {stem}_{i}{ext}.
  • Starting a second recording raises, stopping one that was never started raises, and a recording that captured no frame writes no file and warns. A camera destroyed while recording finalizes its file.

Never use Genesis' own start_recording

Genesis' gs.Camera.start_recording captures inside scene.step(), so it records nothing for a replay script. Use Camera.start_recording / stop_recording. Contributors: do not inline Camera._render() into render() — the public methods record exactly once per call, and the inlined call would capture twice.

eden inference --rec records a run without any code: it calls config.add_recording_camera(), which adds config.recording_camera() as a camera named rec, and records it every step to the run's log directory. The default recording camera follows the robot entity from 1.5 m out; a task whose subject is elsewhere, or that paints state through an overlay, overrides recording_camera(). A rec camera the config already declares is kept; if it lacks the overlays of the task's own recording camera, Eden warns and names them. The recording camera is a method rather than a cameras_options entry so that training runs never pay for it.

docs.title: Sensors
docs.text:
A sensor is a named SensorOptions entry of SensorsOptions, wrapping any Genesis sensor options. From examples/recipes/sensors/sensors_imu_contact_go1.py:

import genesis as gs

from eden.options.sensors import SensorOptions, SensorsOptions

sensors_options = SensorsOptions(
    imu=SensorOptions(
        sensor=gs.sensors.IMU(delay=0.01, acc_noise=(0.01, 0.01, 0.01)),
        attach_entity_name="robot",
    ),
    contact_fl=SensorOptions(
        sensor=gs.sensors.Contact(),
        attach_entity_name="robot",
        attach_link_name="FL_foot",
    ),
)

After the build, env.sensors["imu"].read() returns the measured value (with noise, delay and jitter applied) and read_ground_truth() the exact one. get_pos() / get_quat() give the sensor's world pose (wxyz), and set_pos_offset() / set_quat_offset() move an attached sensor relative to its link.

SensorOptions field Meaning sensor The Genesis sensor options (gs.sensors.*, or an Eden engine sensor). attach_entity_name, attach_link_name The entity and link the sensor rides on. Empty for a static sensor. Eden resolves them into the sensor's entity_idx / link_idx_local at build. track_link_names For sensors with a track_link_idx field: links to track, each "entity" (all its links) or "entity/link". filter_link_names For contact sensors (Contact, ContactForce, and the taxels): counterpart links to ignore, same grammar. Refused on a sensor without filter_link_idx.

docs.title: Sensor types
docs.text:
Every Genesis sensor options class works. The ones Eden's tasks and recipes use, and the rest that Genesis ships:

Sensor (gs.sensors.*) Measures IMU Linear acceleration and angular velocity of a link. Contact Whether a link is in contact. ContactForce Contact force on a link. JointTorque Joint torques of an entity. Lidar (alias of Raycaster) with GridPattern / SphericalPattern Ray distances and, optionally, hit points. DepthCamera with DepthCameraPattern A ray-cast depth image. KinematicTaxel, ElastomerTaxel, ProximityTaxel, ContactProbe, ContactDepthProbe Tactile readings at probe points on a link. SurfaceDistanceProbe, TemperatureGrid Distance to surfaces; a temperature grid.

The ray-casting sensors return a (points, distances) named tuple. return_points=False measures distances only (points is then None), which is cheaper; see examples/recipes/sensors/sensors_lidar_go2.py. A non-colliding background mesh is invisible to ray casts unless its material sets use_visual_raycasting=True before the build.

Camera sensors (RasterizerCameraOptions, BatchRendererCameraOptions, NyxCameraOptions) go on CameraOptions.sensor_options, not in SensorsOptions, so they get the camera API. Eden's own audio sensors (motor noise, contact sounds, a piano, microphones) are described in Engine add-ons.

docs.title: Sensors as observations
docs.text:
SensorRead concatenates sensor readings into one observation: sensor_names (sensor names, regular expressions or glob patterns; None, the default, for every sensor), read_ground_truth (default False) and an optional post_process_func applied to each reading. A reading with more than two dimensions is flattened per environment, and a named tuple contributes each of its tensors.

from eden import observations

contacts = observations.SensorRead.configure(sensor_names=["contact_*"])

docs.title: When sensors update
docs.text:
By default (EnvOptions.update_sensors_every_substep=False) Genesis' sensor update runs only on the last scene step of a control step: the intermediate readings would be overwritten before the observation manager reads them at the end of env.step(), so updating them is wasted work. For ray-casting sensors it is a large saving; the code comment in EnvBase._scene_step_with_sensor_gating records about 2.3x on a depth-camera motion-tracking task at decimation=4.

The skip turns itself off when any sensor sets Genesis' delay or history_length, whose buffers need a fresh sample every simulation step. Set update_sensors_every_substep=True to update on every step unconditionally. Eden's audio sensors advance their per-step state outside this loop, so they keep time either way (see Engine add-ons).

scene.read_sensors() raises in a scene with an Eden sensor

Genesis' scene.read_sensors() / entity.read_sensors() label results through gs.sensors.types, which cannot name a sensor defined outside Genesis. Read sensors through env.sensors[name].read() or SensorRead instead.

docs.title: The viewer and browser recordings
docs.text:
show_viewer=True (on EnvBase or from_config) opens Genesis' interactive viewer, which always rasterizes. These EnvOptions fields change what it draws: show_link_frame, show_world_frame, show_camera_frustums, show_FPS (all False), enable_default_keybinds (True) and background_color.

eden.extensions.visualization.viser.ViserViewer shows a running scene in the browser through Viser (the vis extra: pip install 'eden-world[vis]' / uv sync --inexact --extra vis; recording needs Viser 1.1.0 or newer). It can also record a trajectory into a file anyone can replay in a browser:

from eden.extensions.visualization.viser import ViserViewer

viewer = ViserViewer(env, enable_gui=False)           # host="localhost", port=8080 by default
viewer.server.initial_camera.position = (2.5, -2.5, 1.5)
viewer.server.initial_camera.look_at = (0.0, 0.0, 0.3)
try:
    viewer.start_recording("trajectory.html")
    for _ in range(200):
        env.step()
        viewer.update()
    viewer.stop_recording()
finally:
    viewer.close()
  • start_recording(output_path, fps=None) captures the scene at time zero. The path must end in .html (a standalone page with the player, which you can open directly or embed in an <iframe>) or .viser (the binary recording, for a Viser player you host). Each update() advances playback by env.dt, or by 1 / fps when fps is given, independent of wall-clock speed. Call the recording methods and update() from the simulation thread.
  • stop_recording() saves the file atomically and returns its path; a failed save ends the recording, since Viser's serializer is single-use. close() saves an active recording and stops the server; is_recording reports whether one is open.
  • A recording keeps interactive camera control and trajectory playback, not GUI callbacks or a live simulation. It is held in memory until saved, and its size is dominated by the meshes, not by the number of frames.

examples/recipes/rendering/viser_recording.py -c -s 200 -o go1.html records a Go1 headless on the CPU; viser_visualization.py in the same folder shows the live viewer.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Physics: time stepping and solver settings, including the Mochi solver's renderer limits.
  • Observations: image and sensor observation groups, noise and history.
  • Scenes and terrains: splat scenes and real-to-sim assets.
  • Engine add-ons: Eden's audio sensors and how out-of-tree sensors are hosted.
  • API: camera and sensor options, splat options, Camera and overlays, engine sensors, visualization.

docs.title: Task Configuration
docs.text:
A task in Eden is one Pydantic config class. It declares the scene, the managers and their terms, the simulation settings and, for RL tasks, the training runner. This page covers the config classes, every option group they hold, the task registry that finds them by name, the layout of a task package, and how configs are validated, derived from one another, saved and loaded. Read it before you write or change a task.

Reference template

eden/tasks/benchmark/reacher/config.py is the canonical task config. Copy its shape when you start a new task.

docs.title: A task at a glance
docs.text:
An abridged excerpt of ReacherConfig from eden/tasks/benchmark/reacher/config.py. Each field is an option group, and the decorator registers the class as the task reacher:

import eden as en
from eden import actions, rewards, terminations
from eden.constants import ReferenceSource
from eden.managers.terms.commands.oracle import UniformT3Command
from eden.options import (
    ActionManagerOptions,
    CommandManagerOptions,
    EnvOptions,
    RewardManagerOptions,
    SceneOptions,
    TerminationManagerOptions,
)
from eden.tasks import TASK_REGISTRY
from eden.terms import DoneTerm, RewardTerm
from eden.utils.configs import EdenRLConfig


@TASK_REGISTRY.register(modifiers=(ReacherDifficultyMod,))  # key "reacher", one TaskMod
class ReacherConfig(EdenRLConfig):
    env_options: EnvOptions = EnvOptions(num_envs=4096, episode_length_s=9.0, sim_dt=0.01, sim_substeps=2, decimation=1)

    scene_options: SceneOptions = en.scenes.Empty(
        is_support_enabled=True,
        robot=en.robots.Yam(default_root_pos=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), default_root_quat=(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)),  # wxyz
    )

    action_options: ActionManagerOptions = ActionManagerOptions(
        joint_pos_controller=actions.ImplicitPDController.configure(
            entity_name="robot", dofs_name="joint*", scale=0.05, reference_source=ReferenceSource.DELTA
        ),
    )

    command_options: CommandManagerOptions = CommandManagerOptions(
        reaching_target=UniformT3Command.configure(
            x_range=(0.3, 0.5), y_range=(-0.1, 0.1), z_range=(0.25, 0.35), resampling_time_range=(2.0, 3.0)
        )
    )

    reward_options: RewardManagerOptions = RewardManagerOptions(
        action_rate=RewardTerm.configure(func=rewards.action_rate_l2, weight=-0.01),
        joint_pos_limits=RewardTerm.configure(func=rewards.dofs_pos_limits, weight=-10.0, params={"entity_name": "robot"}),
    )

    termination_options: TerminationManagerOptions = TerminationManagerOptions(
        timeout=DoneTerm.configure(func=terminations.time_out, time_out=True),
    )

The real file also declares the observation groups, a custom reward registered inline, a curriculum and the RSL-RL runner. ReacherDifficultyMod is a TaskMod: it adds the --difficulty flag.

Every value is a field default. Do not build fields in __init__ or model_post_init; Deriving a config from another explains why.

docs.title: The config hierarchy
docs.text:
Pick the config class whose environment your task needs, and subclass it. Each config class is paired with exactly one environment class, which env_class_for_config looks up:

Config (eden.utils.configs) Subclasses Adds Environment EdenConfig — the base option groups (below) EnvBase EdenRLConfig EdenConfig reward_options, termination_options, command_options, curriculum_options, runner_options RLEnvBase EdenMimicConfig EdenRLConfig motion_options MimicRLEnvBase EdenSplatConfig EdenConfig splat_options (SplatOptions) SplatEnvBase EdenSplatRLConfig EdenRLConfig splat_options (SplatOptions) SplatRLEnvBase EdenNyxSplatConfig EdenConfig splat_options (NyxSplatOptions) NyxSplatEnvBase

Most tasks subclass EdenRLConfig; motion-imitation tasks subclass EdenMimicConfig. A plain EdenConfig has no reward or termination, which suits teleoperation, data collection and viewers. The splat configs render a Gaussian-splat background. Their environment classes need the batch-splat extra (pip install 'eden-world[batch-splat]'), or the nyx extra for Nyx. splat_options is a root field rather than part of the scene because it selects the environment class.

API reference: Configs.

docs.title: Option groups
docs.text:
Every option group is a field whose name ends in _options, except language_instructions. cameras_options and sensors_options are plural because each holds several named items.

Field Type Read by Guide env_options EnvOptions the environment and the Genesis scene: env count, timing, solver Physics scene_options SceneOptions the entities, by name Entities, Scenes and terrains observation_options ObservationManagerOptions ObservationManager (groups of terms) Observations action_options ActionManagerOptions ActionManager (controllers) Actions event_options EventManagerOptions EventManager (resets, randomization) Events cameras_options CamerasOptions cameras, by name Sensors and rendering sensors_options SensorsOptions sensors, by name Sensors and rendering metric_options MetricManagerOptions MetricManager (shared computations, success) Metrics and recorders recorder_options RecorderManagerOptions RecorderManager (episode recording) Metrics and recorders renderer_options Genesis RendererOptions the Genesis scene's renderer Sensors and rendering language_instructions list[str] not the environment: carried on the config for language-conditioned policies Remote policies reward_options RewardManagerOptions RewardManager Rewards and terminations termination_options TerminationManagerOptions TerminationManager Rewards and terminations command_options CommandManagerOptions CommandManager (goals, targets) Commands curriculum_options CurriculumManagerOptions CurriculumManager Curricula runner_options a runner options class, or None the trainer, not the environment Training runs motion_options MotionManagerOptions MotionManager (motion reference) Motion tracking splat_options SplatOptions / NyxSplatOptions the splat renderer Scenes and terrains

Most groups accept None, and the environment substitutes an empty group of the right type. The splat environments are the exception: a splat config with splat_options=None raises ValueError when its environment is constructed.

The manager option groups (*ManagerOptions) hold named terms: each keyword is a term key, and its value is a term configured with .configure(...). How to write and configure terms is in Terms, and eden terms --grep <text> lists every registered term with its parameters.

docs.title: env_options
docs.text:
EnvOptions (eden.options.envs) holds the simulation settings. These are the fields every task sets:

Field Default Meaning num_envs 4096 Parallel environments. Under multi-GPU training this is per rank. sim_dt 0.005 Physics time step, in seconds. sim_substeps 1 Genesis substeps inside one physics step. decimation 4 Physics steps per control step (the action repeat). episode_length_s 20.0 Episode length, in seconds. Must be positive and finite.

The control step is env.dt = sim_dt * decimation seconds, so the control rate is 1 / (sim_dt * decimation) Hz, and an episode lasts ceil(episode_length_s / env.dt) control steps. The solver, integrator, contact and batching fields, and the options of the other solvers, are in Physics. API reference: EnvOptions.

An episode with no time limit

episode_length_s cannot be infinite: RLEnvBase raises on inf, NaN or a value that is not positive. For an episode with no time limit, keep a finite length and leave the time_out termination term out.

docs.title: scene_options
docs.text:
A scene is a SceneOptions whose extra keywords are entities, keyed by the name that terms use to find them. The presets in en.scenes are factory functions that return a plain SceneOptions:

import eden as en
from eden.options import BoxOptions

scene = en.scenes.Empty(
    is_support_enabled=True,
    robot=en.robots.Yam(default_root_pos=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0), default_root_quat=(1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0)),  # wxyz
    cube=BoxOptions(size=(0.05, 0.05, 0.05), default_root_pos=(0.4, 0.0, 0.05)),
)

en.scenes.Empty adds a ground plane named plane. Passing plane=TerrainOptions(...) replaces the flat ground under the same name. is_support_enabled and surface configure only the default plane, so passing either one together with plane= raises ValueError. Entity types, robots and terrains are covered in Entities, Robots and Scenes and terrains.

docs.title: runner_options
docs.text:
runner_options configures the learner; no environment reads it. The base classes are:

  • RslRlOnPolicyRunnerOptions (PPO) and RslRlDistillationRunnerOptions, from eden.options.learning.rsl_rl. eden train uses RSL-RL by default.
  • RlGamesPpoRunnerOptions, from eden.options.learning.rl_games. eden train dispatches to rl_games when runner_options is an instance of it.

Algorithm-specific runners subclass the RSL-RL ones: RslRlFlashSacRunnerOptions, RslRlRmaDepthDistillationRunnerOptions and RslRlContrackRunnerOptions (listed in Where an algorithm lives), and RslRlWeaveRunnerOptions in eden/tasks/weave_hoi/runner.py.

runner_options.seed seeds the run. The training wrappers apply it before they construct the environment (see Environments). Runner fields, custom algorithms and checkpoints are covered in Training runs.

docs.title: The task registry
docs.text: TASK_REGISTRY (eden.tasks) maps task names to config classes. A task registers itself where it is defined, so there is no central list to update.

docs.title: Registering a task
docs.text:
from eden.tasks import TASK_REGISTRY
from eden.utils.configs import EdenRLConfig


@TASK_REGISTRY.register()  # key "my_reach", derived from the class name
class MyReachConfig(EdenRLConfig):
    ...

The key is the class name in snake case with a trailing _config removed: ReacherConfig registers as reacher, and PolarisPanCleanConfig as polaris_pan_clean. register() takes three keyword arguments:

  • name= sets the key explicitly. Use it only when no class name produces the key you want (see Task Package Layout).
  • modifiers= attaches TaskMods, the task's variants and CLI flags.
  • override=True replaces an existing registration with the same name. It is for a script that registers a class at run time, for example TASK_REGISTRY.register(MyReacher, name="reacher", override=True). It does not resolve a clash between two scanned files (see Name clashes).

Registering a name that is already taken, without override=True, raises ValueError. Registering anything other than a class raises TypeError.

docs.title: Looking a task up
docs.text:
from eden.tasks import TASK_REGISTRY

TASK_REGISTRY.list_tasks()                         # every task name, sorted
config = TASK_REGISTRY.build("reacher")            # a config instance, with the task's TaskMods applied
config = TASK_REGISTRY.build("reacher", difficulty="hard")
ReacherConfig = TASK_REGISTRY.get("reacher")       # the bare class

get() returns the class, and instantiating it runs no TaskMod

TASK_REGISTRY.get(name)() builds the config without its TaskMods. For a task whose robot or dataset is bound by a mod, that config constructs and saves without complaint and then fails at env.build(), unless the config overrides check_bindings() (see TaskMods). Use build() for a config you will run. Use get() when you need the class itself: for an issubclass check, or to subclass it.

A miss raises KeyError with the closest name and every available task. eden list prints every task on the command line, with its source (eden for built-in tasks) and its modifiers.

docs.title: How discovery works
docs.text:
The first lookup scans eden/tasks/**/*.py with Python's ast module and records every class decorated with @TASK_REGISTRY.register, without importing any task module. Importing eden.tasks imports no task. Only the module that defines the task you ask for is imported, by get() or build(). That keeps eden list fast and offline, since a task module can pull in heavy dependencies or download assets.

The scan follows three rules:

  • It recognizes @<name>.register only where <name> is bound in the same file by from eden.tasks import TASK_REGISTRY or from eden.tasks.registry import TASK_REGISTRY (an as alias works). A file that uses the bare name TASK_REGISTRY without that import gets a warning, so the miss is not silent.
  • It skips __init__.py and every file whose name starts with _. Put decorated classes in a module such as config.py.
  • A file that cannot be read or parsed is skipped, with a warning that names it.

docs.title: Tasks in your own package
docs.text:
A task does not have to live in the Eden tree. Put it in your own installable package, and name the package that holds the task configs under the eden.tasks entry-point group in your pyproject.toml:

[project.entry-points."eden.tasks"]
my_project = "my_project.tasks"   # the key is free-form; the value is the package to scan

# my_project/tasks/reach.py: the same decorator and import as a built-in task
from eden.tasks import TASK_REGISTRY
from eden.utils.configs import EdenRLConfig


@TASK_REGISTRY.register()
class MyReachConfig(EdenRLConfig):  # key "my_reach"
    ...

After you install the package (uv pip install -e ., or any install), eden list shows my_reach with your distribution's name in its Source column, and both eden train --task my_reach and TASK_REGISTRY.build("my_reach") find it. The same scan rules apply: no tasks in __init__.py or in files whose name starts with _.

The scan reads your task files without importing them, but locating a dotted package imports the packages above it. For my_project.tasks that is my_project/__init__.py, which the first task lookup of every eden process imports, eden list included. Keep that file light: no task imports, no heavy dependencies, no downloads. An entry point that names a top-level package (my_project_tasks = "my_project_tasks") imports nothing at all.

A script that never goes through the eden CLI can add a package itself, before its first lookup. Only that process sees it, and a package that cannot be found is skipped without an error:

TASK_REGISTRY.add_search_path("my_project.tasks")

docs.title: Name clashes and broken entry points
docs.text:
Both of these problems raise only from a lookup they could change, so a broken or clashing plugin never blocks the tasks it has nothing to do with. Each also warns once when the scan runs.

  • Task names are global. A name registered in two scanned files, in Eden or in a plugin, raises ValueError naming both files, from every lookup of that name and from eden list. Neither class registers when its module is imported, so the answer never depends on import order. Adding override=True does not help, because the scan has no import order to apply it in. Give your task a name of its own; to start from a built-in task, subclass its config under a new name.
  • An entry point that does not resolve fails the lookups it could answer. If the value is not a scannable package (a typo, a module:attr reference, a plain module, or a parent package that fails to import), the scan cannot know which tasks it holds. A lookup that finds nothing, and eden list, raise RuntimeError naming the distribution, the value and the fix. A task found elsewhere still resolves. Entry points are re-read on every rescan.

docs.title: Task Package Layout
docs.text:
The rules to follow when you add a task to eden/tasks. tests/tasks/test_init.py checks the naming, file and __init__.py rules across every built-in task.

  • The task name is snake case and starts with its package's name. A task in eden/tasks/polaris/ is polaris_pan_clean, and one in eden/tasks/robosuite/ is robosuite_lift. A package with a single task is named for it (piano). benchmark/ is the one exception, because it holds Eden's own reference tasks (reacher, move_forward).
  • The config class is <Package><Task>Config, so the key derives from it. The registry snake-cases the class name and strips the suffix (PolarisPanCleanConfig → polaris_pan_clean), and every registered config class ends in Config. A saved config.json records the class's module and name, so renaming or moving a registered config breaks loading the runs saved from it.
  • Pass name= only where no class name produces the key. A name= equal to the derived key fails the test. The cases in the tree are:
    • a name the package runs together while the class keeps its capitals (name="beyondmimic" on BeyondMimicConfig; likewise assistmimic, flashdexretarget, omnireset);
    • an acronym the snake-casing would split differently (name="manipulation_lift_ycb_rgb");
    • a class name already used elsewhere (name="homie" on HomieLocomotionConfig).
  • The config lives in a config.py. That is eden/tasks/<package>/config.py, or eden/tasks/<suite>/<task>/config.py once each of a suite's tasks needs a module of its own (robosuite/lift/config.py, manipulation/lift_box/config.py). A suite's shared base config and helpers go in other modules at the suite's top level (polaris/base_config.py, robosuite/common.py, art/common.py). Tasks that differ from one base by a few fields share one config.py (whiteboard/config.py, art/calligraphy/config.py).
  • Terms go where their number suggests. A few task-specific terms are registered inline in config.py, as reaching_reward is in reacher. More go in a custom_terms.py, and many in a custom_terms/ package with one module per manager (observations.py, rewards.py, ...). A term that any task could use belongs in eden/managers/terms/ instead. See Inline registration.
  • A task package's __init__.py is its docstring and nothing else. Importing eden.tasks.<pkg>.custom_terms.rewards must not build the task's config, and the registry needs no import to find a task. A custom_terms/__init__.py may re-export its terms. eden/tasks/libero/__init__.py is the one exception, because it is a documented API surface.
  • Variants are TaskMods. See A TaskMod or a separate task?

docs.title: Strict fields
docs.text:
ConfigurableOptions, the base of every Eden options class, sets Pydantic's extra="forbid". A misspelled field raises ValidationError on the line that contains it, in a task config, EnvOptions, entity, camera, sensor and runner options alike. EnvOptions(decimatoin=4) fails at construction, not at build, and the message names the closest valid field and lists every field the class has.

Classes that hold dynamically named children subclass DynamicConfigurableOptions, which restores extra="allow":

Class Its extras are SceneOptions named entities (robot=..., cube=...) ManagerOptions: every *ManagerOptions, and RewardGroupOptions named terms; named groups in ObservationManagerOptions, and optionally in RewardManagerOptions ObservationGroupOptions named observation terms CamerasOptions / SensorsOptions named cameras / sensors SplatOptions / NyxSplatOptions named point clouds (PCDOptions) ManagerTermOptions, the base of every *TermOptions the parameters .configure() passes to the term CameraOverlayOptions, TerrainTermOptions, DatasetOptions, DatasetModifierOptions, FileHandlerOptions, MetadataOptions .configure() parameters extension options: PolicyOptions, ClientOptions, RetargeterOptions, DeploymentOptions, TeleopOptions, PlannerOptions, PoseEstimatorOptions, GraspSamplerOptions, SystemIdentificationOptions .configure() parameters

extra="allow" does not mean unchecked. Term options validate their extras against the registered term's parameter names when they are constructed, so RewardTermOptions(name="upright", wieght=2.0) raises, and the term checks them again when it is built. Extension options are checked on the .configure() path only.

A term key cannot shadow an attribute of the options object that holds it: a term named lock or clone raises TypeError and suggests another key.

docs.title: Subclass, and override fields as class defaults
docs.text:
A variant of a task is a subclass that redeclares the fields it changes. To change one part of an inherited option group, start from the parent's default and call updated():

from eden.options import RewardManagerOptions
from eden.tasks.velocity_tracking.base_config import VelocityTrackingBaseConfig

base = VelocityTrackingBaseConfig.model_fields["reward_options"].default


class MyConfig(VelocityTrackingBaseConfig):
    reward_options: RewardManagerOptions = base.updated(
        track_linear_velocity=base.track_linear_velocity.updated(weight=0.0),
    )

options.updated(field=value) returns a deep copy with those fields replaced. It raises ValueError on a name the class (or, for a term, the registered term) does not accept, and the copy is always unlocked, so you can edit it further. model_copy(update={...}) checks names the same way, which Pydantic's own model_copy does not, but it is a shallow copy unless you pass deep=True, and it keeps the source's lock state. Neither method validates the values you pass.

Pydantic deep-copies option defaults for each instance, so a class-level default is never shared between two config objects.

Never build a config's fields in __init__ or model_post_init

Loading a config validates it with model_validate, and Pydantic v2 calls a custom __init__ when it validates. A config that sets fields in __init__ re-applies them on every reconstruction: in load_from_file, in with_overrides_from_dict, and so in eden train --config and --override. Those overrides are then reverted without any message. Declare every value as a field default. For a scene, write a factory function that builds on the parent's; the en.scenes presets are factories for this reason.

docs.title: Copying, locking and removing children
docs.text:
• options.clone() returns a deep copy that keeps the source's lock state, and clone(unlock=True) returns an editable one. Prefer clone() or copy.deepcopy to model_copy(deep=True): only they tolerate values that cannot be deep-copied, which they share by reference instead.
  • options.lock() freezes an options object and everything below it, and writing to a locked object raises RuntimeError. unlock() reverses it. Both apply downward only, so a child can be unlocked inside a locked parent. Saving a config locks it by default (below).
  • scene_options.remove_entity(name) and disable_term(name) on a manager's options remove a named child. A TaskMod uses them to drop an entity or a term; see TaskMods.

docs.title: Saving
docs.text:
config.save_as_json("logs/my_run/config.json")   # or save_as_yaml(path), or save_as_file(path) by extension

save_as_json and save_as_yaml take an optional path (by default config.json / config.yaml in the run's log directory) and raise ValueError on the wrong extension. Every save locks the config unless you pass lock_config=False, so editing it afterwards raises RuntimeError; use config.clone(unlock=True) for an editable copy. A training run saves the config it trains with next to its checkpoints.

A saved file is an envelope. _meta records the config class and the Eden and Genesis that saved it; config holds the fields, and every nested options object is stamped with its own class so that the exact types come back on load:

{
    "_meta": {
        "eden": {"version": "...", "commit": "..."},
        "genesis": {"version": "...", "commit": null},
        "_option_module_": "eden.tasks.benchmark.reacher.config",
        "_option_class_": "ReacherConfig"
    },
    "config": {
        "env_options": {"num_envs": 4096, "...": "...", "_option_module_": "eden.options.envs", "_option_class_": "EnvOptions"},
        "...": "..."
    }
}

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
from eden.utils.configs import EdenConfig

config = EdenConfig.load_from_file("logs/reacher/<run>/config.json")   # returns a ReacherConfig

load_from_file rebuilds the class the file records, so a generic loader does not need to know the task. The class you call it on still constrains the result: the saved class must be that class or a subclass of it, or the load raises TypeError. A file without class metadata loads as the class you called it on. If the saved class cannot be imported (it was renamed, moved, or defined in a script run as __main__), the load raises ImportError naming it, rather than falling back to a base class. When the installed Eden or Genesis differs from the one that saved the file, the load logs a warning.

Loading validates every Eden options object, so an unknown or stale field, or a term parameter that no longer exists, raises at load and names the class and the field. Embedded Genesis options are not validated: an unknown key on one is dropped with a warning.

The subclass rule is not task identity

load_from_file's "this class or a subclass" is right for a library loader, but several tasks register a config that subclasses another task's (ManipulationLiftBoxRGBConfig is a ManipulationLiftBoxConfig). When a saved config has to be one particular task's, compare the exact class. eden train --config does; see TaskMods.

docs.title: Partial overrides
docs.text:
A partial override is a nested mapping of only the fields to change:

config = config.with_overrides_from_dict({"env_options": {"num_envs": 64}})
config = config.with_overrides_from_file("overrides.yaml")   # .json, .yaml or .yml

Both return a new config and leave the original untouched. The override is deep-merged into the config: nested mappings merge key by key, and a key the override does not mention keeps its value. A list replaces the old list whole, so an override of hidden_dims: [512, 256] sets exactly that list. An override that names a different options class (_option_class_) for a nested object replaces that object whole instead of merging into it. The result is validated like a load. On the command line the same mechanism is --config <partial file> and --override '<inline YAML>'; see TaskMods.
