docs.title: Velocity Tracking: Design Notes
docs.text: Why eden/tasks/velocity_tracking/base_config.py is set up the way it is. The config file holds what you need to change a value; this page holds the reasons, the provenance and the hardware findings behind those values. Read it before you add a robot, change what the policy observes, or retune a penalty. For how to train the tasks, see Locomotion tasks.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
Two tasks share one base config:

Task Config class Adds to the base velocity_tracking_flat VelocityTrackingFlatConfig (flat/config.py) A plain ground plane. velocity_tracking_terrain VelocityTrackingTerrainConfig (terrain/config.py) A procedural terrain grid, a height scan in both observation groups, an out_of_terrain_bounds termination, 128 collision pairs.

Both register two TaskMods, VelocityTrackingRobotMod (--robot) and VelocityTrackingObsMod (--obs_preset). Build a config through the registry so the mods run:

from eden.tasks import TASK_REGISTRY

config = TASK_REGISTRY.build("velocity_tracking_flat")                           # G1 29-DOF (default)
config = TASK_REGISTRY.build("velocity_tracking_flat", robot="oli")              # LimX Oli 31-DOF
config = TASK_REGISTRY.build("velocity_tracking_terrain", obs_preset="privileged")

Control runs at 50 Hz (sim_dt=0.005, decimation=4), episodes last 20 s, and the runner is rsl_rl PPO with a [512, 256, 128] ELU actor and critic, 24 steps per env per iteration, 30 000 iterations.

docs.title: Robot binding
docs.text:
The task is robot-parametric. Everything in VelocityTrackingBaseConfig is robot-agnostic except a handful of slots, which VelocityTrackingRobotMod fills at build time from VelocityTrackingRobotMod._PRESETS and from the robot options themselves:

Slot Filled from scene_options.robot The preset's robot class (G1Dofs29 or Oli). Every joint position controller on robot: dofs_name, scale The robot's dofs_name; the preset's whole-body action-scale dict (G1_ACTION_SCALE, OLI_ACTION_SCALE). Upright.link_name, BodyAngVelXYPenalty.link_name The preset's torso link. RandomizeComShift.links_name [torso link]. FeetClearance.feet_link_names, FeetSlip.feet_link_names, RandomizeFrictionRatio.links_name The robot's RobotOptions.feet_links_name. FeetClearance.target_height The preset's swing-foot apex target. runner_options.experiment_name Prefixed with the robot key: velocity_tracking_flat → g1_velocity_tracking_flat.

These slots ship as empty sentinels ("", [], 0.0, and a controller scale of None), so a link name from one robot can never leak into another. VelocityTrackingBaseConfig.check_bindings() raises ValueError, naming every field still at its sentinel and the mod that fills it; EnvBase.from_config calls it before constructing anything. That is what catches a config made without the mod: TASK_REGISTRY.get("velocity_tracking_flat")(), the class itself, a subclass registered with modifiers=(), or a term added after the mod ran.

docs.title: Found by type, filled only when unset
docs.text:
The mod finds the slots by term type on the robot entity, never by term key, and fills a slot only while it still holds its sentinel. So a variant may rename, drop or split terms in its own class body — two joint position controllers for the legs and the upper body, say, each keeping the robot's action scale — and may pin any slot itself. The term classes the mod binds are listed in _ROBOT_BOUND_FIELDS, and reward groups are searched too. A manager group that a config sets to None (action_options and reward_options are both optional) has nothing to bind and nothing to report.

For the joint position controllers:

  • dofs_name left empty gets every joint of the robot, in the robot's order. Only one DOF-owning action term may then exist on the robot (_robot_dof_owners): a whole-robot controller collides with any other term that commands a joint. A joint position controller counts as DOF-owning even with an empty dofs_name, because the mod is about to fill it; any other action term (NullJointAction, the velocity controllers, BinaryJointController, the task-space terms) counts once it names DOFs of its own. Terms that split the robot must each name their joints.
  • scale left at its None default, with no scale_ratio, gets the robot's whole-body action-scale dict with dict_keys_scope="entity", so a controller that owns only the legs takes the leg entries and skips the rest. An authored scale=1.0 is kept, and a controller that sets scale_ratio counts as scaled.
  • No joint position controller at all on robot raises ValueError, listing the action terms the config has.

The mod copies every mutable value it assigns. Assignment on an options model is not validated, so pydantic does not copy, and one shared list would let an edit to one term silently rewrite another (or hand a caller a handle on the module-level *_ACTION_SCALE dict). TaskRegistry.build runs each mod once on a fresh config, so the read-modify-write on experiment_name is safe.

push_robot (PushByVelocity) needs no binding: with its default base_joint_name=None it finds the free base joint by type, which covers both the MJCF <freejoint> a G1 declares and the root joint Genesis synthesizes for Oli's URDF. encoder_bias (RandomizeDofsPosOffset) leaves action_term_name=None, so it covers every joint position controller on the robot, and a split controller keeps the bias on all of its joints.

docs.title: Adding a robot
docs.text:
Everything else — observations, commands, terminations, curriculum, PPO settings and the posture tolerance maps — is robot-agnostic, so adding a humanoid is one entry in _PRESETS plus its key in the robot Literal of VelocityTrackingRobotMod.__init__. The current presets, from base_config.py:

_PRESETS: dict[str, dict] = {
    "g1": {
        "robot_cls": en.robots.G1Dofs29,
        "action_scale": en.robots.G1_ACTION_SCALE,
        "torso_link": "torso_link",
        # Swing-foot apex target [m]; mjlab's G1 value.
        "foot_clearance_height": 0.10,
    },
    "oli": {
        "robot_cls": en.robots.Oli,
        "action_scale": en.robots.OLI_ACTION_SCALE,
        # No ``torso_link`` in Oli's URDF: the last waist link is the trunk.
        "torso_link": "waist_pitch_link",
        # G1's 0.10 scaled by standing height (1.65 m / 1.32 m).
        "foot_clearance_height": 0.125,
    },
}

The robot must set feet_links_name, and its joint names must follow the <side>_<body part>_<axis>_joint convention the posture maps match (see Posture tolerances).

Oli's URDF has no torso_link. Its waist is a three-joint serial chain, and waist_pitch_link, the last body of that chain, is the trunk that carries the arms and head — the equivalent of G1's torso_link.

docs.title: Observations
docs.text:
The observation is split by what a deployed policy can measure. Every policy term comes off the robot's own joint encoders or IMU:

Term Policy Critic Noise (uniform) base_lin_vel (body frame) — yes ±0.5 base_ang_vel (body frame) yes yes ±0.2 projected_gravity yes yes ±0.05 dofs_pos (offset from default) yes yes ±0.01 dofs_vel, scale=0.05 yes yes ±1.5 actions (last action) yes yes — commands (velocity command) yes yes — height_scan (terrain task only), scale=0.2 yes yes ±0.1

base_lin_vel has no sensor on a humanoid. On hardware the policy would get either zeros or a contact-aided Kalman estimate, and neither is what training produced. It is privileged information, so it belongs to the critic, which only ever runs in simulation — the standard asymmetric actor-critic split, and one fewer thing that can be wrong on the robot. The critic has no history: it estimates a value from a state it sees fully. The policy group sets enable_corruption=True and the critic enable_corruption=False, so the critic reads the same terms without noise.

The policy stacks 5 frames (history_length=5). From a single frame the policy cannot tell a real velocity from a one-step sensor glitch; with history it can average one out.

Robot Policy, per frame Policy, 5 frames Terrain policy, 5 frames privileged policy G1 29-DOF 96 480 (96 + 187) × 5 = 1415 99 Oli 31-DOF 102 510 (102 + 187) × 5 = 1445 105

The terrain variant stacks its 187-dot height scan into the same 5-frame window. That is the cost of having one history mechanism rather than two.

docs.title: Why dofs_vel is scaled by 0.05
docs.text: Joint velocity is the noisiest channel a real robot reports, and a single bad joint can dominate an unscaled 31-vector. On one deployed Oli, waist_roll was measured reporting a velocity about 10× its own position derivative and uncorrelated with it, which at scale 1.0 reached the policy 2–4× outside the ±1.5 rad/s range it trained against. Scaling by 0.05 (the legged_gym convention) keeps the channel informative while bounding what one broken encoder can do. Observation modifiers apply in the order raw → noise → clip → scale, so the noise stays in physical rad/s and only the network input shrinks.

docs.title: --obs_preset
docs.text:
VelocityTrackingObsMod changes only the policy group; the critic keeps base_lin_vel and stays single-frame under both presets.

  • proprioceptive (default) — the table above: sensor-only, 5 frames. Deploys with no state estimator. It is identical to the unmodified config, so applying it is a no-op, and a config that round-trips through it is bit-identical to one that never did.
  • privileged — the recipe the task shipped before the split. The policy also reads base_lin_vel (first in the vector), in a single frame, with dofs_vel unscaled in both groups. The three changes revert together because they are one recipe: reverting only the group membership would build a config that loads an old checkpoint at the right width and then feeds it joint velocities 20× larger than it trained on. The mod states terms_order explicitly, because a newly assigned term would otherwise land last; the terrain variant's height_scan keeps its place at the end. A policy trained this way needs eden deploy --estimate_lin_vel on hardware.

docs.title: Commands and curriculum
docs.text:
UniformVelocityCommand resamples every 3–8 s. 10 % of envs are commanded to stand still and 30 % track a heading (heading_control_stiffness=0.5). The initial ranges are ±1 m/s forward and lateral and ±0.5 rad/s yaw. VelocityCommandCurriculum widens them in stages counted in env steps (5000 * 24 is iteration 5000 at 24 steps per iteration). A stage that does not name a range keeps the previous one:

From env step lin_vel_x (m/s) ang_vel_z (rad/s) 0 (−1.0, 1.0) (−0.5, 0.5) 5000 × 24 (−1.5, 2.0) (−0.7, 0.7) 10000 × 24 (−2.0, 3.0) (−0.7, 0.7), unchanged

docs.title: Posture tolerances
docs.text:
VariablePosture holds the robot near its default pose with a per-joint tolerance that depends on the commanded speed: STD_STANDING below walking_threshold=0.05, STD_WALKING up to running_threshold=1.5, STD_RUNNING above. The maps are regular expressions over joint names, so every humanoid that follows the <side>_<body part>_<axis>_joint convention (G1, Oli) shares them.

Every DOF must be matched: resolve_per_dof_std raises ValueError naming any joint the map does not cover. (It used to fall back to 0.1 silently, which made an uncovered joint train against a tolerance nobody chose.) The head entries cover Oli's head joints and stay in the maps for robots without a head (G1), so adding a robot with one is a preset entry and not also a std-map edit.

docs.title: Smoothness penalties
docs.text:
Three penalties on successive derivatives work together against jitter:

action_rate_l2        = ||a_t - a_{t-1}||^2                    (1st difference)
action_rate_l2_smooth = above + ||a_t - 2a_{t-1} + a_{t-2}||^2 (adds the 2nd difference)
dofs_acc_l2           = ||v_t - v_{t-1}||^2                    (joint acceleration)

The first difference alone does not distinguish a fast smooth motion from one that reverses every control step. In one hardware run, an Oli trained with only the first difference reversed its waist_roll command on 81 % of consecutive steps at 3 rad/s mean, and the resulting ≥ 25 Hz torque was audible; the second-difference term penalizes exactly that alternation.

DofsAccL2 sums (v - v_prev)^2, a velocity difference that is not divided by dt. legged_gym's weight of -2.5e-7 applies to a true acceleration, so it has to be scaled by 1/dt^2 to carry the same weight. The config writes it as -2.5e-7 / 0.02**2 rather than folding it into a literal, so the provenance stays visible (eden/tasks/husky/config.py does the same).

docs.title: The full reward set
docs.text:
Term Weight Notes track_linear_velocity 2.0 track_lin_vel_with_z_penalty, std √0.25 track_angular_velocity 2.0 track_ang_vel_with_xy_penalty, std √0.5 upright 1.0 Upright on the torso link, std √0.2 pose 1.0 VariablePosture, see above body_ang_vel −0.05 BodyAngVelXYPenalty on the torso link joint_pos_limits −1.0 dofs_pos_limits action_rate_l2 −0.1 action_rate_l2_smooth −0.05 ActionRateL2Smooth dofs_acc_l2 −2.5e-7 / 0.02² DofsAccL2 foot_clearance −2.0 FeetClearance, active above a 0.05 command foot_slip −0.1 FeetSlip, active above a 0.05 command self_collisions −1.0 self_collision_cost

Episodes end on time-out or when the robot tilts past 70° (fell_over). The terrain task also ends an episode, counted as a time-out, when the robot comes within 3 m of the terrain edge (out_of_terrain_bounds).

docs.title: Domain randomization
docs.text:
Event Mode Range reset_base reset xy ±0.5 m, z +0.01 to +0.05 m, yaw ±3.14 rad push_robot interval, every 1–3 s linear ±0.5 m/s in x and y, ±0.4 in z; angular ±0.52 rad/s roll and pitch, ±0.78 yaw randomize_friction startup ratio 0.3–1.2 on the feet links randomize_com startup torso CoM shift ±2.5 cm in x and y, ±3 cm in z encoder_bias startup ±0.015 rad joint-position offset

RandomizeComShift writes per-env link CoMs, which needs EnvOptions.batch_links_info=True. The terrain variant replaces the whole env_options block, so it restates that flag; without it the term raises at build.

docs.title: The terrain grid
docs.text: _make_terrain_grid() in terrain/config.py builds 10 rows of increasing difficulty by 10 columns, approximating mjlab's ROUGH_TERRAINS_CFG mix: 20 % flat, 20 % pyramid stairs, 20 % inverted pyramid stairs, 10 % pyramid slope, 10 % inverted pyramid slope, 10 % random uniform bumps, 10 % waves. Each sub-terrain is 8 × 8 m at a 0.1 m horizontal and 0.005 m vertical scale, and the grid is centred on the world origin. The height scan is GridScanDots, a 17 × 11 grid read from the terrain's get_height(), matching mjlab's 1.6 × 1.0 m ray-cast at 0.1 m resolution.

docs.title: Not yet ported from mjlab
docs.text: The config docstrings list what the mjlab velocity tasks have and these do not: critic-only foot observations (height, air time, contact, contact forces) and the contact-based rewards (feet_air_time, foot_swing_height, soft_landing), the angular_momentum reward, the rel_forward_envs command option and, for the terrain task, the terrain-level curriculum.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Locomotion tasks — how to train and replay these tasks.
  • TaskMods — the robot-binding pattern this task is the worked example of.
  • Observations — groups, history, noise and modifier order.
  • Deployment — eden deploy, including --estimate_lin_vel.

docs.title: Command reference
docs.text:
This page lists every eden command and subcommand with its flags, as --help prints them. Use it to look up a flag; the linked guides explain the workflows behind each command.

Every command prints its own help with --help. For the commands that take a task, add the task so that its variant flags are listed too:

eden --help
eden train --task reacher --help        # the shared flags plus reacher's --difficulty

Without an activated virtual environment, run uv run eden ... in a clone, or python -m eden ... anywhere Eden is installed.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Command What it does eden list List every registered task, its source and its task mods eden terms List registered terms and the parameters they accept eden train Train a registered task eden inference Roll out a trained checkpoint, or a published policy, in simulation eden export Export a checkpoint's policy as ONNX / TorchScript plus policy_spec.json eden deploy Run a policy on hardware, or against a MuJoCo model (--mujoco) eden smoke Build a task and step it a few times, as a sanity check eden preprocess Build a motion task's dataset cache ahead of training eden datagen Record scripted demonstrations of a task into HDF5 eden examples list / smoke Browse and smoke-run the runnable examples eden lerobot convert Convert an Eden HDF5 recording into a LeRobot v3 dataset eden pose gvhmr Estimate SMPL-X motion from monocular video eden retarget ... Retarget human motion to robots (OmniRetarget, OTRetarget, SOMA, DexRetargeter, FlashDexRetarget) eden gello ... Calibrate and stream a GELLO leader arm eden metaquest bridge Meta Quest WebXR teleoperation bridge eden pico bridge PICO (XRoboToolkit) teleoperation bridge eden teleop sonic ... SONIC whole-body teleoperation (robot process and operator station) eden wuji ... Find and monitor Wuji Gloves eden view / arrange / snap Look at an entity, arrange a scene, take a snapshot eden gif Convert an .mp4 to a .gif eden clean Remove empty log directories

docs.title: Global options
docs.text:
These go before the subcommand, because the task commands hand everything after their own flags to the task's parser:

Flag Meaning --log-theme {auto,human,agent} How the command renders console output. agent (the default): no ANSI colors, no greeting box. human: color. auto: color on a terminal, honoring NO_COLOR and FORCE_COLOR. It sets EDEN_LOG_THEME for this process and everything it launches. 
eden --log-theme human train --task reacher

Putting --log-theme after the subcommand is an error that says where it goes. To pick a theme for a whole shell, set EDEN_LOG_THEME instead (Environment variables).

docs.title: Flags shared by the task commands
docs.text:
train, inference, export, deploy, smoke, preprocess and datagen share one argument parser. Every one of them takes:

Flag Meaning --task TASK The registered task name (eden list). Adds the task's variant flags. --config CONFIG A .json, .yaml or .yml file. A config Eden saved (it carries its class metadata) replaces the task's config; any other file is merged into it as a partial override. --override YAML An inline YAML mapping merged into the config, e.g. --override 'env_options: {num_envs: 64}'. Repeatable; later ones win; applied after --config. --checkpoint CHECKPOINT Path to a checkpoint file. --cpu Use the CPU backend instead of the GPU. --run_name RUN_NAME A name folded into the run directory, <timestamp>-<run_name>-<id>, and so into the W&B run name. --<variant> One flag per argument of each of the task's mods, e.g. --difficulty {easy,medium,hard} for reacher.

When --checkpoint points into a run directory that holds a config.json, inference, export and deploy load that config instead of rebuilding the task from its current defaults. --config (as a partial) and --override still apply on top, but a variant flag set away from its default is refused, because the saved config already decides it.

docs.title: eden list
docs.text:
eden list

Prints every registered task with its source (eden for a built-in task, otherwise the distribution or module it comes from) and the task mods that give it variant flags. Takes no flags, and imports no task module, so it is fast and needs no network.

docs.title: eden terms
docs.text:
eden terms                         # every registered term
eden terms --kind reward           # one kind
eden terms --grep 'height|altitude'
eden terms --json                  # for tooling
Flag Meaning -k, --kind KIND Only this kind of term, e.g. reward, observation, event. -g, --grep PATTERN Only terms whose name, parameters or summary match PATTERN, a case-insensitive regular expression. Exits 1 with a message when nothing matches. --json Emit the catalog as JSON. --markdown Emit the catalog as the full docs page, with parameters (Term catalog is generated this way).

--json and --markdown are mutually exclusive.

docs.title: eden train
docs.text:
eden train --task <task> [variant flags] [flags]

Trains a registered task with the runner its runner_options select: rsl_rl by default, rl_games when the options are an rl_games runner's. Each run writes to logs/<task>/<timestamp>[-<run_name>]-<id>/ under the current directory: checkpoints, config.json, run.json, and the logger's files. A task whose runner_options is None is not trained through eden train. See Training runs.

Besides the shared flags:

Flag Meaning --num_envs N Override the task's number of parallel environments (per rank in a multi-GPU run). --logger {tensorboard,neptune,wandb} rsl_rl's logger. Default tensorboard. Ignored for rl_games. --resume REF Continue a previous run of this task, found under logs/<task>/: latest (the most recently modified), a run id, or a substring of a run name. Loads that run's latest checkpoint into a new run directory, which records its parent. Cannot be combined with --checkpoint. --wandb_group GROUP The W&B group for this run. Default: the task name. Ignored unless --logger wandb.

--checkpoint starts training from that checkpoint's weights.

docs.title: eden inference
docs.text:
eden inference --task <task> --checkpoint <path/to/model.pt> [flags]
eden inference --policy <name> [--task <task>] [flags]

Rolls a policy out in simulation, in evaluation mode, under logs/<task>/ (or logs/inference/ without a task). It needs either --checkpoint (with --task) or --policy, which runs a frozen published policy instead; the two cannot be combined. See Training runs and the policy zoo.

Flag Meaning --vis, --show_viewer Open the Genesis viewer. --rec Record an .mp4 through a rec camera, saved in the run's log directory. --num_envs N Parallel evaluation environments. Default 1. --steps N Stop after N steps. Default: one episode for a checkpoint, 1000 steps for --policy. --episodes N Run until each environment has finished ceil(N / num_envs) episodes. Not with --policy. --async, --sim2sim Run deployment-style: the policy runs in a background thread, the simulation is paced to wall-clock time, and the last action repeats when the policy is late. A simulation-side rehearsal of eden deploy. --policy NAME, --extension_policy NAME A published policy: a package name under eden/extensions/policies/ (e.g. holosoma, homie), its POLICY_REGISTRY key, or the key without _policy. Makes --task and --checkpoint optional. --robot ROBOT The robot options class from eden.robots for a --policy run without a task. Default G1Dofs29. Ignored with --task. --entity_name NAME The scene entity the policy controls. Default robot. --base_command VX VY WZ A constant velocity command for policies driven by one. Default: stand still. --motion_file FILE The reference motion .npz for motion-tracking policies (e.g. sonic); required by those. --clip_name CLIP The clip to track, for policies with per-clip checkpoints (e.g. beyondmimic_moves).

docs.title: eden export
docs.text:
eden export --task <task> --checkpoint <path/to/model.pt> [flags]

Exports a trained checkpoint's policy for a runtime outside Eden, with a policy_spec.json describing its observations, actions and control rate. The environment is built from the checkpoint's config.json, with one environment. See Exporting a policy.

Flag Meaning --format FORMAT Comma-separated formats from onnx and jit. Default: all of them. --out DIR The output directory. Default: exported/<checkpoint name>/ beside the checkpoint. --no_verify Skip checking each exported graph against the policy on the environment's observations. The ONNX check needs the onnx extra.

docs.title: eden deploy
docs.text:
eden deploy --task <task> --checkpoint model.pt --mujoco [--vis]     # sim-to-sim
eden deploy --task <task> --checkpoint model.pt                      # hardware
eden deploy --policy <name> [--mujoco]                               # a published policy, no task

Runs a policy through the deployment loop: on the real robot that the task's scene names, or, with --mujoco, against a MuJoCo model of it. Training-time randomization is stripped, and the deploy config is saved as deploy_config.json in the run directory. Read Deployment before using it on hardware: it explains every safety flag below.

Policies and slots. Several policies can be loaded at once and switched live (the G1 remote's Select button, or the keys n and 1 to 9; nine at most).

Flag Meaning --checkpoint PATH The trained policy. --policy NAME, --extension_policy NAME A published policy to load as an extra slot (repeatable). Makes --task and --checkpoint optional. --extra_checkpoint PATH Another checkpoint to preload as a slot (repeatable). --base_policy {auto,holosoma,none} A known-good policy loaded as slot 1 and active on boot. auto (default) loads the Holosoma walking policy on a G1 29-DOF and nothing elsewhere. --policy_checkpoint NAME=PATH Point a published policy at a local checkpoint (repeatable). --robot ROBOT The robot for a task-less --policy deploy. Default G1Dofs29. --entity_name NAME The scene entity to deploy. Default robot. For a composite rig (an arm with a hand), every part deploys through its own backend; name one part to deploy it alone. --motion_file FILE The reference motion for motion-tracking policies; the motion restarts from frame 0 at each switch. --on_motion_end {continue,stand,switch} What a motion-imitation deploy does when its clip ends. Default continue. --motion_end_slot N The slot --on_motion_end switch hands control to. Default 1. --stand_steps N Control cycles of the --on_motion_end stand ramp. Default 100.

Gains and commands.

Flag Meaning --deploy_kp_kd_scale S Scale on the default Kp/Kd. Ramp up from 0.2 to 1.0 when commissioning. --gain_ramp_steps N Control steps over which a slot switch ramps to the new slot's gains. Backend default 50; 0 jumps. --target_lpf A First-order low-pass on the commanded joint targets, a in (0, 1]; 1.0 is off. --init_steps N Control cycles of the ramp to the start pose before the policy takes over. Default 250; 0 disables it. --init_target {default,motion,motion_rsi} Where that ramp drives the joints: the default pose, or frame 0 of the tracked clip. motion_rsi also teleports the base and works only with --mujoco. --velocity_command {constant,keyboard,gamepad,task} What drives the task's velocity command. Default constant (holds --base_command). task keeps the training-time random command generator. --base_command VX VY WZ The constant velocity command. Default: stand still. --velocity_command_scale VX VY WZ A per-axis limit on the substituted velocity command. --gamepad_layout {ps4,xbox} Axis scaling for --velocity_command gamepad. Default ps4. --disable_joints NAME ... Joint names or patterns sent with kp = kd = 0, for bench debugging. Never on load-bearing joints of an unsupported robot. --ignore_action_terms TERM ... Action terms whose commands the wire format cannot carry and that you drive yourself; without it, deployment refuses to start. --part_option PART.OPTION=VALUE Composite rigs: set one option of one part's backend (repeatable), e.g. --part_option robot.robot_ip=172.16.0.2.

State estimation and diagnostics.

Flag Meaning --estimate_lin_vel Estimate the base linear velocity onboard with a contact-aided Kalman filter. --feet_links LINK ... The foot links that filter uses. Default: the robot's declared feet. --debug_record Record commanded targets and measured state, written as an .npz. --debug_record_path PATH Where. Default <log_dir>/deploy_record.npz. --debug_record_flush_steps N Steps per streamed chunk of the recording. Backend default 100.

Backend-specific.

Flag Meaning --publish_rate HZ LimX Oli, Unitree G1 and Go2: the rate at which the held command is re-sent between control ticks. Backend defaults: 1000 Hz (Oli), 500 Hz (G1, Go2). --power_protect_factor N Unitree Go1 only: the SDK's power-protection factor, 1 to 10 (10%–100% of rated power). Backend default 10.

MuJoCo sim-to-sim (with --mujoco).

Flag Meaning --mujoco Deploy against a MuJoCo model of the robot instead of hardware. Works for any task or robot. Add --vis for MuJoCo's viewer. --menagerie Use the robot's MuJoCo Menagerie model instead of its own training asset. Errors if the robot has none. --async Run the physics on its own thread in wall-clock time, as a robot's controller does, instead of in lockstep. --mujoco_props [ENTITY ...] Composite rigs: the scene entities to simulate besides the rig. Default: every colliding one but the ground. --imu_noise ACC GYRO White noise on the simulated IMU (per-axis standard deviation). --imu_bias AX AY AZ GX GY GZ A constant bias on the simulated IMU. --imu_noise_seed SEED Seed for --imu_noise. --gantry Hang the robot from a simulated overhead hoist. Simulation only. --gantry_body LINK ... The bodies the ropes are tied to. Default: the robot's declared mount links, else its base. --gantry_attach X Y Z The attachment point in each rope's body frame, in metres. --gantry_height Z The world height of the anchor. Default: 1 m above the attachment point. --gantry_step M Metres the + / - keys move the anchor. Default 0.05. --gantry_slack M Slack in the rope. Default 0 (taut). --gantry_support S Scale on the rope force, 0 to 1. Default 1. --gantry_no_draw Do not draw the ropes and their force arrows in the viewer. --gantry_force_scale S Metres of force arrow per newton. Default 1e-3.

--vis (--show_viewer) opens the Genesis viewer mirroring the hardware state, or MuJoCo's viewer with --mujoco.

docs.title: eden smoke
docs.text:
eden smoke --task <task> [flags]

Builds a task and steps it a few times with no action, under logs/smoke/<task>/. It runs every term's build(), so a wrong name in the config fails here in seconds rather than in a training run. Prints ✅ smoke OK: built '<task>' with N env(s) and ran M step(s). on success.

Flag Meaning --num_envs N Environments to build. Default 2. --steps N Steps to run. Default 2. --eval_mode Build in evaluation mode (training and randomization off). --show_viewer Open the Genesis viewer. --profile Time each term's compute() instead, and write term_cost.json. --profile_warmup N Warm-up steps before measuring, with --profile. Default 10. --profile_steps N Measured steps, with --profile. Default 50.

docs.title: eden preprocess
docs.text:
eden preprocess --task <task> [--num_batches N --batch_idx I]

Builds the dataset cache of a motion task ahead of training. With --num_batches N greater than 1 the clip list is split into N contiguous batches and this process handles one, so you can run one process per GPU.

Flag Meaning --num_batches N Split the clip list into this many batches. --batch_idx I The batch this process owns, in [0, N). Default 0: pass it to every process, or they all build batch 0.

docs.title: eden datagen
docs.text:
eden datagen --task <task> [flags]

Rolls a task's scripted demonstrator out in parallel environments and records the episodes to HDF5. Only tasks with a scripted demonstrator support it. See Scripted demonstrations.

Flag Meaning --num_episodes N Episodes to record. Default 100. --num_envs N Parallel environments. Default 16. --output_dir DIR The dataset's directory. Default data/demos. --filename NAME The file name without extension. Default: the task name. --export {all,succeeded,separate} Keep every episode (tagged with its success), only the successful ones, or the failed ones in a separate <filename>_failed file. Default all. --seed SEED Seed of the environment and the demonstrator. Default 0. --p_mistake P Probability that a subgoal is a deliberate mistake. Default: the demonstrator's own. --episode_length_s S The episode time limit. Default: the demonstrator's own, else 90. --camera_only Locate objects through the task's cameras instead of the simulator's state (demonstrators that support it, e.g. robosuite_pick_place). --show_viewer Open the Genesis viewer.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: These read the examples/ directory of a clone; a PyPI install has none. See Examples.

docs.title: eden examples list
docs.text: Flag Meaning --tier {project,policy,recipe} Only this tier. --capability TAG Only examples with this capability: a full namespace.leaf tag (sensor.lidar) or a namespace (sensor). --hardware {cpu,gpu,gpu-fp64,real-robot} Only examples with this hardware requirement. --search QUERY A substring search over key, purpose and capabilities. --json Print JSON records instead of a table.

docs.title: eden examples smoke
docs.text:
eden examples smoke recipes/physics/mpm_tutorial

Runs one example headless for a few steps, with EDEN_SMOKE=1. The key is positional, as eden examples list prints it. It refuses (exit 2, with the reason) examples that need real hardware, a teleoperation device, a missing optional dependency, or a GPU the machine lacks.

Flag Meaning --timeout SECONDS Per-example timeout. Default 900.

docs.title: eden lerobot convert
docs.text:
eden lerobot convert --hdf5 teleoperation.hdf5 --output-dir lerobot_output --repo-id local/teleop --force

Converts an Eden HDF5 recording into a LeRobot v3 dataset. It reads state/qpos, state/dofs_vel, state/pos, state/quat, action and timestamp from each demo_* group under /data, the layout the state and action recorders write. See Datasets and recording.

Flag Meaning --hdf5 PATH The input HDF5 file. --output-dir DIR Where the LeRobot dataset is created. --repo-id ID The LeRobot dataset repo_id. --robot-type TYPE The robot type recorded in the LeRobot metadata. --task TEXT The task string stored for every frame. --image-writer-threads N Threads LeRobot uses to encode videos. --force Overwrite --output-dir if it exists (it must be empty or a LeRobot dataset).

docs.title: eden pose gvhmr
docs.text:
eden pose gvhmr --src video.mp4 --out motion.npz

Recovers world-grounded SMPL-X motion from monocular video with GVHMR and writes AMASS-style .npz files. Needs the pose extra and GVHMR's checkpoints (gvhmr-download-checkpoints). See Pose estimation.

Flag Meaning --src SRC A video, or a directory searched recursively. Required. --out OUT The output directory (the source tree is mirrored), or an .npz file for a single video. Required. --pattern GLOB The file pattern for a directory --src. Default *.mp4. --checkpoint-root DIR GVHMR's checkpoint directory. Default: $GVHMR_CHECKPOINT_ROOT, else ./inputs/checkpoints. --ckpt FILE The GVHMR checkpoint. Default <root>/gvhmr/gvhmr_siga24_release.ckpt. --static-cam Assume a static camera (skips visual odometry; much faster). --use-dpvo Use DPVO instead of SimpleVO for camera motion. --f-mm MM Full-frame focal length in mm. Default: estimated. --output-root DIR Where GVHMR writes and reuses its per-video intermediates. --skip-existing Skip a video whose output already exists. --verbose Save GVHMR's intermediate overlays.

docs.title: eden retarget
docs.text: Each retargeter is a subcommand. See Retargeting and Hand retargeting.

docs.title: eden retarget omniretarget
docs.text:
Robot-only OMOMO to G1 retargeting with OmniRetarget, ignoring the object.

Flag Meaning --src DIR The OMOMO dataset directory (the .pt sequence files). Required. --out DIR The output directory; joint positions are written as <task-name>.npy. Required. --task-name NAME The sequence to retarget, with or without .pt. Default sub3_largebox_003. --num-frames N Truncate the sequence to N frames. --skip-existing Skip when the output exists.

docs.title: eden retarget otretarget
docs.text:
Joint robot and object retargeting from surface interactions with OTRetarget. Needs the ot-retargeter extra.

Flag Meaning --source {omomo,seed} The demonstration format. Required. --src PATH omomo: a sequence directory or a folder of them; seed: a .bvh file or a directory of them. Required. --out DIR The output directory; one <rig>_<clip>.npz per clip. Required. --body-model-path PATH omomo: the folder with SMPLX_{NEUTRAL,MALE,FEMALE}.npz; seed: SOMA_neutral.npz. Required. --objects-dir DIR omomo: the release's objects/ folder. --rig {g1_wuji,oli_wuji,g1,oli} The target embodiment. Default g1_wuji. --num-frames N Truncate each clip to N frames. --cpu Run Genesis on the CPU. --skip-existing Skip a clip whose output exists. --shard K/N Retarget only every N-th clip of the sorted list, starting at the K-th. Default 0/1. --clip-list FILE A text file of clip names, one per line: retarget only those. --supports omomo: add the untracked tables the object rests on as fixed plates. --keep-going On a clip that raises, write <rig>_<clip>.error.txt and continue; exit non-zero at the end.

docs.title: eden retarget soma
docs.text:
Batch retargeting of AMASS-style SMPL, SMPL-H or SMPL-X motion to a robot with SomaRetargeter. Needs the soma-retargeter extra (uv in a clone only).

Flag Meaning --src PATH An .npz clip, or a directory searched recursively. Required. --out PATH The output directory (source tree mirrored), or a file for a single clip. Required. --body-model {smpl,smplh,smplx} The source body model. Default smplx. --body-model-path PATH The body-model file (e.g. SMPLX_NEUTRAL.npz) or a per-gender directory. Required. --robot {unitree_g1,limx_oli} The target robot. Default unitree_g1. --gender {neutral,male,female} The default gender; a clip's own gender field overrides it. Default neutral. --target-fps FPS The frame rate every clip is resampled to. Default 30. --source-fps FPS Override the source frame rate when the clip's metadata is missing or wrong. --num-frames N Truncate each clip to N frames. --snap-to-ground Shift each clip vertically so its lowest collision point touches the ground. --skip-existing Skip a clip whose output exists. --cpu Use the CPU backend.

docs.title: eden retarget dex
docs.text:
Offline position retargeting of MANO keypoints to a dexterous hand with DexRetargeter. Needs the dex-retargeter extra.

Flag Meaning --src PATH An .npz with keypoints (T, 21, 3) and fps, or a directory of them. Required. --out PATH An output .pkl file (single input) or directory. Required. --preset {xhand1_right_position} The hand preset. Default xhand1_right_position. --skip-existing Skip a clip whose output exists.

docs.title: eden retarget flashdex import
docs.text:
Imports a released hand-object dataset (MANO hands and object poses) into a FlashDexRetarget dataset: <dataset>/human_demo/<clip>.npz and <dataset>/objects/<id>/visual.obj. Needs the flashdexretarget extra.

Flag Meaning --source {dexycb,hot3d,oakink2,taco} The release, read by its eden.datasets loader. --raw DIR The downloaded release's root directory. --dataset DIR The dataset directory to write. --mano-dir DIR The directory with MANO_RIGHT.pkl and MANO_LEFT.pkl. --sides {both,right,left} The hands to import. Default both. --textures Export the objects with their materials and textures, for rendering. --config FILE A .yaml or .json file of option values (eden.options.extensions.flashdexretarget). --override YAML An inline YAML mapping merged over the options last; repeatable.

docs.title: eden retarget flashdex kinematic
docs.text:
Kinematic retargeting of an imported dataset onto robot hands: support disks and reject rules (<robot>/report.csv), convex object parts, MuJoCo physics IK (<robot>/retargeted/), <robot>/motion.pt and object SDF grids.

Flag Meaning --dataset DIR The dataset directory from the import. --robot {xhand,sharpa} The target robot. Default xhand. --workers N Processes. Default: half the CPU cores. --config FILE A .yaml or .json file of option values. --override YAML An inline YAML mapping merged over the options last; repeatable. Steps can be skipped, e.g. --override "steps: {retarget: false, pack: false}".

docs.title: eden gello calibrate
docs.text:
Computes per-joint offsets and a gripper range for a GELLO leader arm held at a known pose, and prints a ready-to-paste GelloLeaderConfig(...). Needs the gello extra.

eden gello calibrate --port /dev/ttyUSB0 --start-dofs 0 0 0 0 0 0 --signs 1 1 -1 1 1 1 --gripper \
    --output configs/gello_ur5e.yaml
Flag Meaning --port PORT The Dynamixel serial port. --start-dofs RAD ... The arm's known joint positions (rad) at the calibration pose. --signs S ... The sign (-1 or 1) of each arm joint. --joint-ids ID ... Dynamixel IDs of the arm joints. Default 1..N. --gripper A gripper is attached. --gripper-id ID The gripper's Dynamixel ID. Default N+1. --baudrate, --warmup-reads, --max-pi-multiple, --gripper-open-delta-deg, --gripper-close-delta-deg Low-level calibration settings. -o, --output PATH Save the GelloLeaderConfig (.json, .yaml or .yml).

docs.title: eden gello leader
docs.text:
Reads calibrated joint positions from the leader arm and sends them to a GelloZMQServer over ZMQ.

Flag Meaning -c, --config PATH The GelloLeaderConfig file from eden gello calibrate. --port PORT The Dynamixel serial port. --zmq-host HOST The ZMQ host. --zmq-port PORT The ZMQ port.

docs.title: eden metaquest bridge
docs.text:
Runs the televuer WebXR server that a Meta Quest connects to over Wi-Fi, and bridges its poses and the stereo view to Eden over ZMQ. On start it prints the URL to open in the headset's browser. Needs the metaquest extra and its git group.

Flag Meaning --width PX The full stereo frame width (both eyes). Default 1280. --height PX The frame height. Default 480. --fps FPS The headset display rate. Default 30. --display-mode {immersive,ego,pass-through} Default immersive. --tracking {hand,controller} Track hand joints (default) or motion controllers.

Note

eden metaquest bridge --help currently prints Vuer's own parameters instead of these flags. The table above is read from eden/utils/devices/metaquest/xr_bridge.py.

docs.title: eden pico bridge
docs.text:
Publishes PICO headset and controller tracking over ZMQ and streams Eden's rendered view back to the headset. Needs the pico extra and the xrobotoolkit_sdk module built from source.

Flag Meaning --fps FPS The pose publish rate (frames are forwarded as they arrive). --control-address HOST:PORT Where to listen for the app's OPEN_CAMERA / CLOSE_CAMERA commands. --pose-port PORT The ZMQ PUB port for the tracking state. --frame-port PORT The ZMQ PULL port for Eden's rendered frames. --no-video Publish tracking only. --no-derived-body Publish only the lossless body_raw, without the derived per-joint body and trackers. --tracker-role SERIAL=ROLE Label a motion tracker by serial, e.g. --tracker-role PA1234=waist (repeatable).

docs.title: eden teleop sonic robot
docs.text:
The robot side of SONIC whole-body teleoperation: a G1 body, the SONIC policy and its planner, listening for the operator's commands. The body is the Genesis simulator by default. Needs the sonic extra and an onnx extra.

Flag Meaning --mujoco / --real Drive the body through the eden deploy MuJoCo backend, or the real Unitree G1 over DDS. -v, --vis Show the viewer (MuJoCo's own under --mujoco). -c, --cpu Use the CPU backend. -s, --steps N Stop after N control ticks. --operator-host HOST The host running the operator station. --cmd-port PORT, --debug-port PORT The command and debug ports. --encoder-path, --decoder-path, --planner-path Local overrides for the SONIC ONNX models. --max-close-ratio R The Dex3 close limit in [0.2, 1.0] (Genesis body only). --no-band Start with the elastic band (the gantry under --mujoco) released. --drop-band-after SECONDS Release the band this many seconds in. --auto-reset Reset to the launch state when the base falls with the band off. --deploy_kp_kd_scale, --target_lpf, --disable_joints, --debug_record, --debug_record_path As for eden deploy, with --mujoco or --real. --joint-vel-limit RAD_S --real: stop when any body joint exceeds this speed (0 disables).

docs.title: eden teleop sonic operator
docs.text:
The operator station: PICO body tracking, calibration, the mode state machine, and streaming to the robot process.

Flag Meaning --robot-host HOST The host running eden teleop sonic robot. --port PORT, --feedback-port PORT The command publish port and the robot's debug port. --target-fps FPS The pose stream rate. --num-frames N Frames per pose message. --record-dir DIR Record each sent pose message as .npz here. --no-service-start Do not spawn the XRoboToolkit PC service. --bridge-host HOST Connect to an eden pico bridge on this host instead of spawning one. --bridge-port PORT, --bridge-fps FPS The bridge's pose port and publish rate. --no-bridge-start Connect to a bridge already running locally. --sdk Read the XRoboToolkit SDK in-process instead of through the bridge. --vis-vr3pt Visualize the calibrated VR 3-point pose (needs the sonic-viz extra). --vis-smpl Also render the SMPL body (needs --vis-vr3pt). --waist-tracking, --no-g1 Visualization only: the waist follows the neck; hide the G1 mesh.

docs.title: eden wuji scan
docs.text: Lists every Wuji Glove on the bus. Needs the wuji extra (Linux only). Takes no flags.

docs.title: eden wuji monitor
docs.text:
Shows a Wuji Glove's live hand pose and tactile sheet in the terminal, the first check after plugging one in.

Flag Meaning --sn SN The glove's serial number. Default: the only one found. --side {left,right} Pick between two connected gloves. --streams STREAM ... The streams to subscribe to, from hand_skeleton, hand_joint_angles, tip_poses, emf_poses, tactile, tactile_zones, tactile_binary, tactile_residual, tactile_point_cloud. Default hand_skeleton hand_joint_angles tactile. --rate-hz HZ Lower the device's push rate. Default 120 Hz. --seconds S Run for this long; 0 runs until Ctrl-C. --exclusive Take the glove for this process alone.

docs.title: eden view
docs.text:
eden view Yam                     # an entity options class by name
eden view scan.ply                # a Gaussian-splat .ply

Opens an entity, by the name of its options class or a composite rig's name, or a Gaussian-splat .ply file, in a viewer.

Flag Meaning -c, --collision Show collision geometry (entity mode). -m, --multiplier M The splat's radiance multiplier (splat mode). --env-brightness B A constant-color environment map's brightness in [0, 1] (splat mode).

docs.title: eden arrange
docs.text:
eden arrange FrankaEmikaPanda YCB003CrackerBox -o scene_snippet.py

Spawns entities (by options class name) with ImGui sliders for each one's base pose and joints, and exports a SceneOptions snippet with the arrangement. Needs the vis extra.

Flag Meaning -c, --collision Show collision geometry. -o, --output PATH Also write the snippet to this file. --spacing M Initial x-spacing between entities. Default 1.0 m.

docs.title: eden snap
docs.text:
eden snap Yam -o yam.png

Renders one image of an entity.

Flag Meaning -o, --output PATH The output image. Default snapshot.png. -c, --collision Show collision geometry.

docs.title: eden gif
docs.text:
eden gif video.mp4                # writes video.gif beside it

Converts an .mp4 to a .gif at 10 fps and 640 px wide. Calls ffmpeg, which must be on your PATH.

docs.title: eden clean
docs.text:
Removes empty log directories, and run directories that hold only a config.json (runs that stopped before saving anything else). Takes no flags.

Warning

eden clean currently looks for a logs/ directory inside the installed eden package (eden/utils/logs), not the logs/ directory of your working directory, so it usually finds nothing.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: This page lists every environment variable Eden's code reads or sets, and the ones from the libraries underneath it that you are most likely to need. Variables that hold a path expect an absolute one unless the entry says otherwise.

docs.title: Eden's own
docs.text: Variable Effect Default EDEN_ASSETS_DIR The root that robot, object, scene and policy assets are downloaded into. Must be absolute: a relative path raises a ValueError. Read every time a path is resolved. See Assets. $XDG_CACHE_HOME/eden/assets, i.e. ~/.cache/eden/assets EDEN_LOG_THEME The console theme: agent (plain text, no colors, no greeting box), human (colors) or auto (colors on a terminal). An empty value counts as unset; any other value raises. eden --log-theme and eden.init(logger_theme=...) set it for the process and its children. agent EDEN_SMOKE Smoke mode, in which examples run a few steps headless (en.is_smoke()). Read as a boolean: 0, false and no turn it off, any other non-empty value on. eden examples smoke sets it to 1. unset (then PYTEST_VERSION decides) EDEN_RESYNC_DEBUG 1 turns on debug output from the motion manager's motion-end resync. unset EDEN_GO1_SDK_PATH A directory holding an uninstalled build of the Unitree Go1 SDK (robot_interface.*.so), added to sys.path for the Go1 deployment backend. unset EDEN_PXREA_SDK_DIR An extra directory searched for the XRoboToolkit PC Service's shared library, which the PICO SDK module links against. Searched before /opt/apps/roboticsservice/SDK/x64. unset

docs.title: Caches and downloads
docs.text: Variable Effect Default XDG_CACHE_HOME The root of Eden's per-user cache ($XDG_CACHE_HOME/eden/): the default asset root, sample clips, processed motion caches and generated meshes. ~/.cache HF_HOME Read by huggingface_hub. Moves the Hugging Face cache, where motion datasets are downloaded ($HF_HOME/hub). ~/.cache/huggingface HF_HUB_OFFLINE Read by huggingface_hub. 1 makes a missing file fail at once instead of after a network timeout; files already on disk are unaffected. unset HF_TOKEN Read by huggingface_hub. A Hub access token, the same as hf auth login. unset QD_OFFLINE_CACHE_FILE_PATH Read by Quadrants, Genesis' kernel compiler: where compiled kernels are cached. In a multi-GPU run, import eden appends rank_<LOCAL_RANK> to it so that ranks do not contend for one cache lock. ~/.cache/quadrants/qdcache/kernel_compilation_manager

docs.title: Multi-GPU runs
docs.text:
torchrun sets these; Eden reads them. See Multi-GPU training.

Variable Effect WORLD_SIZE The number of ranks. Above 1, import eden pins each rank to one GPU, and eden.init() sets up NCCL. Default 1. LOCAL_RANK The rank's index on its node. import eden uses it to pick the rank's GPU from CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES. Default 0. RANK The global rank. Default 0. CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES Read and rewritten by import eden in a multi-GPU run: each rank keeps only its own GPU. A list shorter than the number of ranks on the node raises.

In a multi-GPU run import eden also sets QD_VISIBLE_DEVICE and TI_VISIBLE_DEVICE to the rank's GPU. All of this happens when eden is imported, which is why eden must be imported before genesis and torch.

docs.title: Console output
docs.text: Variable Effect NO_COLOR Any non-empty value disables colors under the auto theme. FORCE_COLOR Any non-empty value enables colors under the auto theme, even when not writing to a terminal.

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text:
These are read by Genesis' renderer.

Variable Effect PYOPENGL_PLATFORM The OpenGL platform for offscreen rendering: egl (the default on Linux), osmesa (software rendering), cgl (macOS) or pyglet. Must be set before genesis is imported. When it is unset on a Linux machine with no display and no EGL library, Genesis selects osmesa if it is installed. EGL_DEVICE_ID The GPU that EGL renders on.

docs.title: Training and logging
docs.text:
Variable Effect WANDB_RUN_GROUP Read by Weights & Biases. eden train --logger wandb sets it to --wandb_group (default: the task name) unless it is already set.

Weights & Biases reads its other variables too (WANDB_API_KEY, WANDB_PROJECT, ...); the project defaults to eden through RslRlOnPolicyRunnerOptions.wandb_project.

docs.title: Policies and ONNX Runtime
docs.text:
Read when a policy runs through ONNX Runtime (eden/extensions/policies/onnx.py). Boolean variables treat 0, false, no and the empty string as off.

Variable Effect Default ONNX_CPU On: use only the CPU execution provider. off ONNX_INTRA_OP_THREADS Intra-op threads per ONNX session; a positive integer, anything else raises. 1 TENSORRT_EP, ONNX_TRT, ORT_TRT Any of them on: use the TensorRT execution provider when it is available, ahead of CUDA. off ORT_TRT_FP16 TensorRT FP16. on ORT_TRT_INT8 TensorRT INT8. off ORT_TRT_CACHE Cache TensorRT engines. on ORT_TRT_CACHE_PATH Where TensorRT engines are cached (relative to the working directory). .ort_trt_cache ORT_TRT_WORKSPACE TensorRT's maximum workspace size, in bytes. TensorRT's own RESIDUAL_GAIN The OmniXtreme policy only: the gain on its residual correction. 1.0

docs.title: Hardware and devices
docs.text: Variable Effect GS_UNITREE_NETWORK_INTERFACE, UNITREE_NETWORK_INTERFACE, CYCLONEDDS_NETWORK_INTERFACE The network interface for Unitree DDS traffic, checked in that order. Unset, Eden picks an interface that is up. ROBOT_IP The LimX Oli's IP address, when the backend's robot_ip option is not set. Default 10.192.1.2. WUJI_TELEMETRY_DISABLE Read by wuji-sdk. 1 turns off the background telemetry the SDK starts on import. Eden does not set it.

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text: Variable Effect GVHMR_CHECKPOINT_ROOT GVHMR's checkpoint directory for eden pose gvhmr, when --checkpoint-root is not given. Default ./inputs/checkpoints. GRASPGEN_CHECKPOINT_DIR The directory GraspGen downloaded its models to (grasp_gen download); a relative gripper_config is resolved against it.

docs.title: Task Suites
docs.text: Eden ships 66 registered tasks: its own locomotion, motion-tracking and manipulation tasks, plus ports of established benchmarks. This page lists every one of them by family, shows the commands every task shares, and links to the page that documents each family in depth. Read it to find a task to train, or to see what a task name on the command line refers to.

docs.title: Find a task
docs.text:
eden list prints every registered task with its variant modifiers:

eden list

Available Tasks in Eden: Task Name | Source | Modifiers
  ...
  velocity_tracking_flat | eden | VelocityTrackingRobotMod, VelocityTrackingObsMod
  ...

The first column is the name you pass to --task. The last column names the task's TaskMods: typed presets that turn into command-line flags (--robot, --difficulty, --song, ...). A task's --help lists its flags with their choices and defaults:

eden train --task velocity_tracking_flat --help

Every task registers itself with @TASK_REGISTRY.register(...) in a config.py under eden/tasks/<package>/; there is no central index. The task name defaults to the config class name in snake case with the trailing _config dropped (ManipulationLiftBoxConfig → manipulation_lift_box), and the convention is to name the class <Package><Task>Config so the task reads <package>_<task>. A registration may pass an explicit name= instead (beyondmimic, homie, omnireset, ...). See Task configs for the registry and the package layout.

docs.title: The commands every task shares
docs.text:
The same five commands work for any task. Substitute the task name and its flags.

# Build the task with 2 envs and step it twice: a quick check that it builds on this machine.
eden smoke --task reacher

# Train. num_envs is per GPU rank; each task sets its own default.
eden train --task reacher --difficulty hard --num_envs 2048 --logger wandb

# Resume the most recent run of this task (or a run id, or a run_name substring).
eden train --task reacher --resume latest

# Roll a checkpoint out. --rec records an mp4 into the run's log directory.
eden inference --task reacher --checkpoint logs/reacher/<run>/model_<iter>.pt --rec

# Export the policy for a runtime outside Eden (ONNX / TorchScript + policy_spec.json).
eden export --task reacher --checkpoint logs/reacher/<run>/model_<iter>.pt

A training run writes into logs/<task>/<timestamp>-<run id>/: the checkpoints model_<iter>.pt, the exact config.json the run trained with, and progress.json. See Training runs for the runners, resuming, loggers and the run directory layout, and Policy export for eden export.

eden inference replays the checkpoint's own config

When the checkpoint has a config.json beside it, eden inference (and eden deploy) loads that file, not the task's current defaults, so the rollout runs the environment the policy was trained in. Task-mod flags such as --robot cannot apply to a saved config, so passing one is an error. Change a field with --override instead, for example --override 'env_options: {episode_length_s: 30.0}'. A --task that disagrees with the saved config only warns, and the run is logged under the saved config's task.

eden inference needs a --checkpoint. To roll out a published controller instead of your own checkpoint, use eden inference --policy <name>; see the policy zoo.

To train on several GPUs, launch the same eden train command under torchrun; see Multi-GPU training.

docs.title: Locomotion
docs.text:
Locomotion tasks — velocity tracking, parkour, recovery and skateboarding.

Task Robot What the policy learns velocity_tracking_flat Unitree G1 29-DOF (--robot oli: LimX Oli) Follow a planar velocity command on flat ground velocity_tracking_terrain Unitree G1 29-DOF (--robot oli: LimX Oli) The same on stairs, slopes, bumps and waves, with a height scan extreme_parkour_teacher Unitree Go2 Cross a grid of parkour courses from privileged scan dots extreme_parkour_student Unitree Go2 Distil the teacher onto a forward depth camera mujoco_playground_getup Unitree Go1 Stand up after a fall mujoco_playground_handstand Unitree Go1 Balance on the front legs with the rear legs raised homie Unitree G1 29-DOF Track velocity and base height with the legs while the upper body moves husky Unitree G1 (23-DOF skater model) Ride a simulated skateboard: push, steer and balance move_forward Unitree Go2 (--robot go1) Walk forward; a small benchmark task

docs.title: Motion tracking
docs.text:
Motion-tracking tasks — whole-body imitation of reference clips, with and without objects.

Task Robot What the policy learns beyondmimic Unitree G1 29-DOF Track one motion clip (BeyondMimic recipe) general_mimic Unitree G1 29-DOF Track a library of clips (LAFAN1 or AMASS) with an adaptive per-clip curriculum weave_hoi G1 + two Inspire RH56DFQ hands Track OMOMO human-object clips with the object simulated contrack xArm7 + XHand Track a hand-object clip with contact annotations assistmimic Two SMPL humanoids A caregiver helps a weakened recipient up off the floor assistmimic_bed Two SMPL humanoids A caregiver helps a recipient out of bed

docs.title: Manipulation and dexterous hands
docs.text:
Manipulation tasks — arm-and-gripper lifting and reaching, in-hand reorientation, piano, assembly and hand-object tracking.
