docs.title: Motion-Tracking Tasks
docs.text:
Eden's motion-tracking tasks train a policy to reproduce reference motion clips in physics: a humanoid dancing, a humanoid carrying an object, a hand manipulating an object, two humanoids interacting. This page gives, for each task, the robot, the data it tracks and where that data comes from, its flags, and the commands to train and replay it. How a dataset becomes the motion reference a task reads is on Motion tracking; the commands every task shares are on the task index.

Whole-body tracking, human-object interaction, and two-agent assistance. Task Robot Tracks Flags Default num_envs beyondmimic Unitree G1 29-DOF One BVH-retargeted CSV clip --raw_data_path, --processed_data_path, --target_framerate 4096 general_mimic Unitree G1 29-DOF A library of G1-retargeted clips (LAFAN1 or AMASS) --dataset_name and 24 more 4096 weave_hoi G1 + two Inspire RH56DFQ hands OMOMO human-object clips, object simulated --objects, --split, --raw_data_path, --processed_data_path 4096 contrack xArm7 + XHand One hand-object clip with contact annotations --data, --target_framerate 4096 assistmimic Two SMPL humanoids Paired Inter-X help-up clips — (trained by an example script) 1024 assistmimic_bed Two SMPL humanoids Paired HHI-Assist get-out-of-bed clips — (trained by an example script) 1024

All but the AssistMimic tasks are EdenMimicConfig tasks: they declare a motion_options block that loads a dataset into the motion manager, and the task's data mod (BeyondMimicDataMod, GeneralMimicDataMod, WeaveHOIDataMod, ContrackDataMod) is what fills it from the flags. Build them with TASK_REGISTRY.build(...) or eden train; a bare config class has no motion reference.

docs.title: BeyondMimic
docs.text:
The BeyondMimic single-clip tracking recipe on the G1: the policy sees the reference joint state and the reference torso pose relative to its own, and is rewarded for matching the reference's 14 tracked links. Explicit PD control at 50 Hz, 10 s episodes, and at the end of a clip the episode resynchronizes onto the reference instead of freezing.

eden train --task beyondmimic                                   # the bundled sample clip
eden train --task beyondmimic --raw_data_path /data/my_g1_csvs  # a directory of clips, or one .csv
eden inference --task beyondmimic --checkpoint logs/beyondmimic/<run>/model_<iter>.pt --rec
Flag Default Meaning --raw_data_path the sample clip A directory of BVH-retargeted G1 CSV files, or one file. Each CSV row is base_pos(3), base_quat_xyzw(4), dofs_pos(29). Omitted, the sample clip G1_gangnam_style_V01_bvh_60hz.csv is fetched from Eden's example-data repo on the Hugging Face Hub on first use. --processed_data_path a keyed file in ~/.cache/eden The processed-motion cache. The default is keyed by every setting that shapes the prepared motion, so a cache built for one clip set, rate or frame range is never loaded for another. --target_framerate 50.0 Rate (Hz) the clip is retimed to.

An empty path (--raw_data_path "$UNSET_VAR") is an error rather than a silent fall-back to the sample clip.

Trim the first row of the sample clip

Row 1 of the sample CSV is a retargeting artifact: the root jumps 11.6 cm between rows 1 and 2. Velocities are differences of positions, so it gives a 5.8 m/s root velocity at frame 0, and reference-state initialization then launches the robot at reset with no error raised. The dataset's frame_range field slices the CSV rows before anything else (a Python slice, [start, end)), and the task leaves it unset. Trim the artifact with an override:

eden train --task beyondmimic \
    --override 'motion_options: {default: {dataset_options: {frame_range: [1, 1942]}}}'

examples/projects/mimic/beyondmimic/README.md describes the same issue for its CSV-to-npz conversion script.

The frozen published BeyondMimic controllers run without training through the policy zoo (eden inference --policy beyondmimic_moves).

docs.title: General mimic
docs.text:
Multi-clip G1 tracking at the scale of tens to hundreds of clips — what ProtoMotions calls a motion tracker, as opposed to the single-clip BeyondMimic policy. Same action, rewards and tracked links as BeyondMimic (taken from ProtoMotions' g1-bones-deploy numbers), plus a lookahead of the reference 1, 2, 4 and 8 motion frames ahead (+20, 40, 80 and 160 ms), 5 s episodes so the curriculum sees more episode ends, and an adaptive per-clip sampling curriculum that spends more episodes on the clips the policy fails.

eden train --task general_mimic                                       # LAFAN1 retargeted to G1
eden train --task general_mimic --dataset_name amass --raw_data_path /data/amass_g1
eden train --task general_mimic --include_pattern '^walk'             # only the LAFAN1 walks
eden train --task general_mimic --arch_preset sonic_flat              # SONIC's 6-layer MLP, for AMASS scale

The most used flags (run eden train --task general_mimic --help for all of them):

Flag Default Meaning --dataset_name lafan1 lafan1: LAFAN1 retargeted to the G1 (CSV). amass: AMASS retargeted to the G1, in IsaacLab-AMP NPZ format. Both are downloaded from the Hugging Face Hub when --raw_data_path is omitted. --raw_data_path, --processed_data_path, --target_framerate auto-download, auto, 50.0 As for BeyondMimic. --include_pattern, --exclude_pattern none A regular expression (re.search) on each clip's file name; keep or drop the matches. --include_list_file, --exclude_list_file none A YAML or JSON list of clips to keep or drop, matched on file name without extension (ProtoMotions amass_*_train.yaml files work). --adaptive_motion_weights / --no-adaptive_motion_weights on The per-clip curriculum. --motion_weight_* flags tune it; --motion_weight_update_mode snapshot (default) is SONIC's stateless formulation. --smooth_start_transition off Prepend each clip with a stand-up → IK → SLERP segment so the reset from the default pose to frame 0 is not a teleport. A modifier, so it runs on every load and leaves the cache alone; do not combine it with eden preprocess (see the warning). --ground_first_frame on Shift each clip up so frame 0 sits on the floor. Runs a transient Genesis env per cache load; set --ground_first_frame_chunk_size for libraries of 100k+ clips. --arch_preset default default (3-layer MLP) or sonic_flat (SONIC's 6-layer MLP, for AMASS-scale libraries). --compute_per_motion_metrics, --log_per_motion_metrics on, on Per-clip tracking errors and per-clip W&B scalars. Turn the per-clip scalars off for very large libraries.

For a large library, build the processed cache ahead of training, sharded across GPUs, with eden preprocess --task general_mimic ... --num_batches N --batch_idx K. To replay every clip of the library once with a translucent reference ghost, use examples/projects/mimic/general_mimic/main.py inference --model <checkpoint>.

docs.title: Weave G1-Inspire-HOI
docs.text:
A port of Weave's G1-Inspire-HOI-v0: a G1 with two Inspire RH56DFQ hands tracks OMOMO human-object clips, and the object is simulated and tracked too. The object is reset from the reference with the robot, rewarded and terminated on its world pose, and observed in the pelvis frame; per-link contact labels from the reference are observed five frames ahead and rewarded, and losing a grasp the reference expects ends the episode. Each hand's six follower finger joints are driven in software from its six drivers, so the action is 41-D (29 body joints + 2 × 6 finger drivers). Training uses a SimBaV2 actor-critic with PPO and the Muon optimizer, at Weave's hyperparameters.

eden train --task weave_hoi                                    # all 9 objects, test split
eden train --task weave_hoi --objects smallbox                 # a single-object specialist
eden train --task weave_hoi --objects smallbox,largebox --split train
eden smoke --task weave_hoi --objects smallbox --num_envs 4
Flag Default Meaning --objects all Comma-separated objects: clothesstand, floorlamp, largebox, largetable, smallbox, smalltable, tripod, whitechair, woodchair. Several objects share one policy, each env holding one object. --split test test (1,605 clips, Weave's train.yaml) or train (7,869). --raw_data_path download Root of an appolyn/Weave snapshot (holding reference/ and objects/). Omitted, the selected split and objects are downloaded into the Hugging Face cache. --processed_data_path none A processed-motion cache .pt. Omitted, the npz files are read on every build.

A run on all nine objects uses the experiment name weave_hoi; any other object set gets its own, weave_hoi_<obj>-<obj>..., so runs on different object sets are kept apart. The Weave paper reports 95.3 % success for the joint nine-object policy on the test split at 27k iterations, and about 91 % for single-object specialists at 3k (from eden/tasks/weave_hoi/README.md, which also lists every deviation from Weave: friction combination, per-object density, finger gain randomization, contact force, observation width 1011 instead of 999, and a depenetration cap).

docs.title: ConTrack
docs.text:
A port of ConTrack: a fixed-base xArm7 + XHand tracks one reference clip of robot joints, object pose and per-finger contact annotations. The rig is the XArm7XHand1_R / _L composite, which expands into a robot (7-DOF arm) and a hand (12-DOF) entity. The policy outputs residual joint targets around the reference, and rewards come in three named reward groups (task rg, style rs, penalty rp) that a constrained-MDP PPO balances with a dual controller. One clip per run, as in the source.

eden train --task contrack --data /data/clip.h5 --num_envs 8000
eden train --task contrack                     # the sample clip, fetched on first use
Flag Default Meaning --data the sample clip One ConTrack reference clip (.h5). Omitted, the sample clip is fetched from Eden's example-data repo on the Hugging Face Hub. The mod reads the clip while building the config (handedness picks the left or right rig), so on an air-gapped host pass --data explicitly. --target_framerate 50.0 Reference retiming rate (Hz). It must match the control rate; ConTrack's source runs at 60 Hz.

The training backend is installed separately

The CMDP-PPO algorithm lives in rsl_rl_contrack, a standalone fork of rsl_rl that is not an Eden extra. eden train --task contrack raises with the exact install command when it is missing. Building the env, eden smoke and clip playback work without it. See examples/projects/mimic/contrack/README.md.

docs.title: AssistMimic
docs.text:
A simplified port of AssistMimic on PHC's SMPL humanoid (69 DOFs, no fingers): a PHC-initialized caregiver helps a weakened recipient while both track a paired interaction clip. Both humanoids live in one env, each with its own observation group, reward group and action term.

Task Dataset Scene Recipient assistmimic Inter-X floor lower body at half gain, 80 N·m assistmimic_bed HHI-Assist floor and bed also hips (20 N·m) and trunk (40 N·m); the caregiver is paid for unloading them

Two agents per env is something no single-agent runner trains, so the configs declare no runner_options and eden train refuses them. The trainer (rl_games PPO through Eden's rl_games wrapper, one PHC-initialized actor per role and a shared critic) is the example examples/projects/mimic/assistmimic/main.py, run in stages:

cd examples/projects/mimic/assistmimic
uv run python main.py adapt --dataset inter-x -b 1024 -s 700       # 1. adapt PHC's phc_3 to Genesis
uv run python main.py train --dataset inter-x \
    --phc-caregiver <adapt run>/phc_genesis_caregiver.pth \
    --phc-recipient <adapt run>/phc_genesis_recipient.pth           # 2. train both roles together
uv run python main.py play --dataset inter-x --checkpoint <checkpoint>.pth --clip 0 -r

--dataset hhi-assist selects assistmimic_bed. The example needs the rl-games extra (pip install "eden-world[rl-games]", or uv sync --inexact --extra rl-games in a checkout). The PHC checkpoint (about 439 MB) and the sample clips download on first use. The example's README covers the stages, checkpoints, evaluation, data conversion and the port notes.

docs.title: PolaRiS
docs.text: Eden ports the six DROID scenes of PolaRiS, a real-to-sim evaluation suite in which a Franka with a Robotiq 2F-85 works in front of a Gaussian-splat capture of a real scene. Read this page to run the scenes, score a policy with PolaRiS's rubrics, or generate demonstrations. The code is in eden/tasks/polaris/.

docs.title: The tasks
docs.text:
Each scene is registered twice: a single-env task for teleoperation and policy inference, and a *_batched variant that renders many envs at once.

Task (--task) Batched variant Instruction Rubric (success) polaris_block_stack_kitchen polaris_block_stack_kitchen_batched "Place and stack the blocks on top of the green tray" both cubes put in the tray, then the green cube over the wood cube polaris_food_bussing polaris_food_bussing_batched "Put all the foods in the bowl" the ice cream and the grapes put in the bowl polaris_pan_clean polaris_pan_clean_batched "Use the yellow sponge to scrub the blue handle frying pan" the sponge put in the pan polaris_move_latte_cup polaris_move_latte_cup_batched "put the latte art cup on top of the cutting board" the cup put on the cutting board polaris_organize_tools polaris_organize_tools_batched "put the scissor into the large container" the scissor put in the large container polaris_tape_into_container polaris_tape_into_container_batched "put the tape into the container" the tape put in the container
  • Single-env tasks are EdenSplatConfigs (built as a SplatEnvBase): one env, no rewards or terminations beyond the episode length, for teleoperation and policy inference.
  • Batched tasks are EdenSplatRLConfigs (built as a SplatRLEnvBase): four envs by default, the gs-madrona batch renderer with a soft two-light rig, and every env's splat rendered and composited under it. They reuse the single-env task's objects, splat, instruction and rubric verbatim. Their reward and termination managers are empty for now: they are RL-typed scaffolding that renders batched but has nothing to train against yet. env_options.num_envs and splat_options.minibatch trade VRAM for throughput.

docs.title: Scoring: PolaRiS's rubrics
docs.text:
PolaRiS scores each task with a rubric: criteria built from three checkers, each counted once it has ever passed, some only after others have. Success is every criterion reached; progress is the fraction reached. Every Polaris task, batched or not, carries one success metric, rubric (a RubricMetricTerm), built in eden/tasks/polaris/rubric.py:

PolaRiS checker Eden criterion reach(obj, 0.2) EeNearEntity: the gripper's base link (PolaRiS's ee_frame, the Robotiq base_link) within 20 cm of the object lift(obj, h) object_bottom_above_height: the object's lowest point h above the table is_within_xy(a, b, fraction) the gripper open (left_driver_joint < 0.1 rad, PolaRiS's finger_joint test) and object_a_within_b_xy

Most tasks are one put_in(object, container) chain: reach, lift, then let go over the container (80 % of the object's footprint over the container's).

Lift is measured from the table, not from the spawn height

PolaRiS compares the object's origin with its spawn height. The scanned assets put their origins anywhere, and Eden drops its objects onto the table at reset, so the height is measured from the table top (z = 0 in every scene) to the object's lowest point instead.

docs.title: The robot and the scene
docs.text:
• Robot. PolarisDroid: a gravity-compensated Franka arm and a Robotiq 2F-85, welded at the arm's attachment link. It differs from Eden's Droid in its home pose (calibrated to the splat cameras) and in a 2 cm torsional friction patch on the pads, without which a pair of scissors pinched across its middle pivots and slips out once lifted. The gripper is the pad-only DROID gripper: a full-collision gripper penetrates mesh objects and ejects them on contact.
  • Physics. sim_dt=0.004 with 4 substeps, so the substep is 1 ms and the 2F-85's closed loop stays stiff, and torsional friction on. Graspable objects are stiffened per object (default_geoms_sol_params), never through a global constraint time constant, which ejects mesh objects on contact.
  • Control. decimation=5: 50 Hz, a DifferentialIKController on attachment (ee_controller) and a binary gripper on the two driver joints (gripper_controller). The episode is 30 s.
  • Cameras. external_camera and wrist_camera, with intrinsics written for a 1280 × 720 image, each compositing the splat behind the rendered scene (SplatComposite, the ground plane drawn by the splat).
  • Splats and objects. Each scene's splat (<scene>/assets/.../splat.ply) and its objects (eden.options.objects.polaris) download on first use from the eden_polaris dataset into polaris/ under the asset directory.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Splat rendering goes through gsplat, which JIT-compiles a CUDA extension on first import, so the CUDA toolkit (nvcc) must be installed.

uvpip 
uv sync --inexact --extra vis           # single-env tasks
uv sync --inexact --extra batch-splat   # batched tasks

pip install 'eden-world[vis]'           # single-env tasks
pip install 'eden-world[batch-splat]'   # batched tasks

The batched tasks also need gs-madrona, the CUDA-only batch renderer, installed separately. See Installation and Sensors and rendering.

docs.title: Evaluating a DROID policy
docs.text:
The DROID-family remote-policy clients (PiPolicy with policy_setup="droid" or "droid_jointpos", Gr00tPolicy with "oxe_droid_relative_eef_relative_joint", Cosmos3Policy, MolmoAct2Policy and GalaxeaVlaPolicy with "droid_franka") target this rig. Replace the config's observation and action options with the client's, as on the SIMPLER page.

Set the env to DROID's 15 Hz first

Every DROID checkpoint's action row is one 1/15 s step (DROID's RobotEnv.control_hz), and the DROID clients check the env's control rate when they are constructed. Eden's PolaRiS tasks step every 20 ms (50 Hz), which would replay each chunk 3.3× too fast. Set the timing PolaRiS itself uses (droid_cfg.py: sim.dt = 1/120, decimation = 8), with sim_substeps=9 to keep the Robotiq's substep under 1 ms:

cfg.env_options.sim_dt = 1 / 120
cfg.env_options.decimation = 8
cfg.env_options.sim_substeps = 9

See Remote policies for the DROID setups and their checks.

docs.title: Scripted demonstrations
docs.text:
Every *_batched task has an eden datagen demonstrator (eden/tasks/polaris/scripted_demos.py): the put-on tool routine on the DROID rig, one put-on per object the rubric scores, reading object footprints off the collision meshes (privileged). They are registered on the batched tasks because eden datagen needs episode ends and many envs, which the single-env tasks do not have.

eden datagen --task polaris_move_latte_cup_batched --num_envs 16 --num_episodes 64

What each demonstrator does and its success rates are in Scripted demonstrations.

docs.title: robosuite
docs.text: Eden ports the eleven manipulation tasks of robosuite (MIT) as registered RL tasks. Read this page to train or evaluate on them, to swap the robot, or to know exactly where a port differs from the original. The code is in eden/tasks/robosuite/.

docs.title: The tasks
docs.text:
Each task is one robosuite_<task> config in eden/tasks/robosuite/<task>/config.py. The arena, the robot placement, the object placement ranges, the dense-reward multipliers and the success predicates follow robosuite's numbers. The module docstring of each config lists those numbers and every deviation for that task.

Task (--task) robosuite source Extra flags Dense reward robosuite_lift Lift robosuite's robosuite_stack Stack robosuite's robosuite_pick_place PickPlace, PickPlaceMilk / Bread / Cereal / Can --object {all,milk,bread,cereal,can} robosuite's robosuite_nut_assembly NutAssembly, NutAssemblySquare / Round --nut {both,square,round} robosuite's robosuite_door Door (use_latch) --latch {latch,no_latch} robosuite's robosuite_wipe Wipe robosuite's robosuite_tool_hang ToolHang Eden's (robosuite's is sparse) robosuite_two_arm_lift TwoArmLift --arrangement {opposed,parallel} robosuite's robosuite_two_arm_peg_in_hole TwoArmPegInHole --arrangement {opposed,parallel} robosuite's robosuite_two_arm_handover TwoArmHandover --arrangement {opposed,parallel} robosuite's robosuite_two_arm_transport TwoArmTransport --arrangement {opposed,parallel} Eden's (robosuite has none)

Every task also takes --robot (see Swapping the robot). The flags are TaskMods, so eden train --task <task> --help lists them with their choices; see Task mods.

  • --object and --nut are robosuite's single_object_mode=2 variants: the other objects and every term that names them are removed (eden.tasks.robosuite.variants.drop_object), and success narrows to the kept object.
  • --latch latch is robosuite's use_latch=True: a sprung handle whose bolt holds the door shut until the handle turns past about 1.25 rad, so it is the harder variant. no_latch loads the bare-handle door.xml.
  • --arrangement is robosuite's two-arm env_configuration: opposed faces the arms across the workspace, parallel stands them side by side facing +x. A non-default arrangement suffixes the experiment name.
  • robosuite's PickPlaceSingle and NutAssemblySingle pick a random object at every reset. They have no counterpart: a config fixes its entities, and swapping an entity per reset is not expressible in one.

ToolHang and TwoArmTransport have no dense reward in robosuite (robosuite ignores reward_shaping=True for TwoArmTransport), so every shaping term in those two configs is Eden's. Their success terms (success and transported) are robosuite's predicates, check for check, so success rates are comparable; returns are not.

docs.title: Train, evaluate and build
docs.text:
eden train --task robosuite_lift
eden train --task robosuite_lift --robot droid          # another arm + gripper
eden train --task robosuite_door --latch no_latch
eden inference --task robosuite_lift --checkpoint <path/to/checkpoint.pt>

Every task trains 4096 envs by default (common.robosuite_env_options) with one shared PPO recipe (common.ppo_runner_options, 3000 iterations). See Training runs for where logs and checkpoints land and how to resume.

To build an env in Python, pass the TaskMod flags as keyword arguments to TASK_REGISTRY.build:

import eden
from eden.envs.base import RLEnvBase
from eden.tasks import TASK_REGISTRY

eden.init()
config = TASK_REGISTRY.build("robosuite_stack", robot="droid")
env = RLEnvBase.from_config(config)
env.build()
observations, _ = env.reset()

docs.title: The MDP
docs.text:
Timing. robosuite steps MuJoCo at 500 Hz and its policy at 20 Hz. Eden keeps the 20 Hz control rate over a 5 ms Genesis step with 2 substeps (decimation=10, from eden.tasks.robosuite.common.robosuite_env_options).

Actions. Per arm, 7-D: a 6-D delta end-effector pose and a binary gripper, as robosuite's OSC_POSE + GRIP. The pose delta is a DifferentialIKController with robosuite's per-step limits (5 cm and 0.5 rad); the gripper is a BinaryJointController. The terms are keyed <slot>_arm and <slot>_gripper (robot_arm / robot_gripper on the single-arm tasks). TwoArmPegInHole has no gripper action, as in robosuite.

Observations. robosuite's proprioceptive set per arm (joint sin/cos and velocities, eef_pos, eef_quat, gripper positions and velocities) plus, per object, <obj>_pos, <obj>_quat and gripper_to_<obj>. A policy group carries 0.5 cm uniform noise on the object poses; a critic group has the same terms uncorrupted (common.policy_and_critic).

Resets. Each arm's joints get robosuite's initialization noise (robosuite samples N(0, 0.02) per joint; Eden uses the uniform half-width ±0.02), and objects are placed in robosuite's ranges.

docs.title: Where the ports differ from robosuite
docs.text:
All of these are deliberate. Each config's module docstring lists the task-specific ones.

  • Episode length. robosuite runs 1000 steps (50 s). Eden defaults to 10 s (eden.tasks.robosuite.common.EPISODE_LENGTH_S). For parity, pass --override 'env_options: {episode_length_s: 50}'.
  • Reward composition. robosuite returns the success reward instead of the shaping terms (or the max of its staged rewards). Eden sums separate terms, weighted by robosuite's multipliers. The ordering of states is the same (a solved state always beats an unsolved one); the absolute scale is not robosuite's.
  • Fixed object sizes. robosuite resamples cube, peg and hammer dimensions on every hard reset. Genesis builds geometry once, so each task fixes them at the midpoint of robosuite's range.
  • Placement without rejection sampling. Where robosuite draws several objects from one region and rejects overlaps, each object gets its own sub-region (for example, each PickPlace object spawns in its own quadrant of bin1).
  • Early termination. An object that falls below the table ends the episode (common.fallen_termination). robosuite only terminates on the horizon, except in Wipe.
  • Stiffer contacts on what a hand carries. In ToolHang and TwoArmTransport the objects a hand picks up carry a 0.005 s contact time constant (common.GRASPED_SOL_PARAMS) instead of Genesis' 0.02 s default. At the default, the 20 N pinch sinks the pads millimetres into a 3 cm handle and the object turns or creeps out of the fingers. The objects are stiffened, not the pads, so every other task's contacts are unchanged.
  • robosuite's Panda gripper. The default rig's Franka Hand gets robosuite's PandaGripper actuation: kp 1000 clipped to ±20 N, no velocity gain, joint damping 100, armature 1, friction loss 1, pad friction 2 (eden.tasks.robosuite.rigs). Eden's stock FrankaHand closes with at most 4 N per finger, which cannot lift robosuite's 0.25 kg lid.
  • The delta-pose action acts at the flange, not between the fingers. robosuite's OSC_POSE controls the end-effector site between the fingers. The ports run differential IK on the rig's ee_link, the arm's mounting flange, which is the gripper's tcp_offset behind it (10.3 cm on the Franka Hand, 14.1 cm on a Robotiq 2F-85). Translations match; a pure-rotation action sweeps the fingertips through an arc of up to 0.5 rad × tcp_offset (about 5 cm) where robosuite turns them in place. The eef_pos observation is the pad midpoint, as robosuite's is. Moving the control point would change the action space of every task and checkpoint, so it is kept as a documented deviation.
  • One frame for every object reading. Genesis re-origins a free rigid body onto its centre of mass, and the root-pose getters default to that frame. Every object quantity in these ports (the <obj>_pos / <obj>_quat observations, gripper_to_<obj>, the reaching rewards, the lift and containment metrics, the fallen-object terminations and the placement events) reads the frame the asset was authored in (relative=True), which is the frame robosuite's object-state reports. The two differ by 6.8 cm on the hammer and 5.8 cm on the ToolHang frame, and the offset rotates with the object. Object pose observations go through common.object_pose_observations() so the choice is made in one place.
  • TwoArmPegInHole's objects are held, not flange-mounted. robosuite builds those robots without grippers and mounts the peg and the plate on the bare flange. Eden's rigs keep their grippers, so the mounting poses are re-based on each rig's tool point (ManipulatorOptions.tcp_offset) and the fingers start closed on the object (ManipulatorOptions.preset_hold). The peg and hole geometry the reward reads is unchanged.
  • Wipe. robosuite's rigid wiping pad is replaced by the rig's two-finger gripper (its action slot stays); robosuite's 100 markers 5 mm apart become 16 markers 3 cm apart, each a scene entity; a marker counts as wiped when the grasp point passes within 2 cm horizontally and 3 cm vertically. The contact-count bonus and the summed reward's normalisation are dropped.

docs.title: Swapping the robot
docs.text:
Every robot slot holds a ManipulatorOptions composite: an arm and a welded two-finger gripper, expanding into <slot> and <slot>_gripper entities at build. The default is panda_franka_hand (PandaFrankaHand: the hand-less Panda plus the FrankaHand), robosuite's own robot at robosuite's home pose. --robot takes any arm + two-finger-gripper composite in COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY; today that is panda_franka_hand, droid, ur5e_2f85 and ur10e_2f85.

eden train --task robosuite_two_arm_lift --robot ur5e_2f85 --arrangement parallel

Swapping is a scene edit. Every robot-shaped term names only its slot and reads the arm, the gripper, the mount link, the pad links and both DOF lists off the composite in build(). RobosuiteRobotMod replaces the composite in each slot, retargets the <slot>_arm and <slot>_gripper action terms, refits the substep and suffixes the experiment name. The new arm stands where the Panda stood.

A Robotiq rig raises sim_substeps

A gripper whose MJCF encodes a closed loop declares the coarsest substep it stays stiff at (RobotOptions.max_substep_dt; the Robotiq 2F-85's is 1 ms, because Genesis clamps a solref time constant to 2 × substep_dt). Swapping in such a rig raises sim_substeps from 2 to 5 (common.fit_substeps_to_rigs, logged at info level). That costs 2.5× the physics per step; the alternative is a gripper that silently cannot hold anything.

Checkpoints do not transfer across robots

The observation width follows the arm's DOF count, so a policy trained on one rig does not load on another.

A new rig needs only a ManipulatorOptions registration in COMPOSITE_ROBOT_REGISTRY whose gripper declares a tool point and a stroke (RobotOptions.tcp_offset / stroke); it then appears in --robot automatically.

docs.title: Scripted demonstrations
docs.text:
eden datagen has a demonstrator for seven of the tasks: robosuite_lift, robosuite_stack, robosuite_pick_place, robosuite_door, robosuite_wipe, robosuite_tool_hang and robosuite_two_arm_transport (eden/tasks/robosuite/scripted_demos.py). robosuite_pick_place can also run camera-only, locating the objects through the agentview camera:

eden datagen --task robosuite_tool_hang --num_envs 16 --num_episodes 32 --output_dir data/demos
eden datagen --task robosuite_pick_place --camera_only

What each demonstrator does and its measured success rates are in Scripted demonstrations.

docs.title: Assets
docs.text:
The objects are the option classes of eden.options.objects.robosuite (RobosuiteCan, RobosuiteSquareNut, RobosuiteDoor, RobosuitePotWithHandles, ...), registered in ROBOSUITE_OBJECT_REGISTRY under robosuite's names, plus the RethinkMount pedestal every arm stands on. Their files are robosuite's own object MJCFs, meshes and textures, and MJCFs re-authored from robosuite's procedural composites. They download on first use from the Kashu7100/eden_robosuite dataset into robosuite/ under the asset directory; a local copy there wins. See Assets.

The arena looks like robosuite's: every scene carries LIBERO's floor workspace (robosuite's arena MJCF, the 6 × 6 m tiled floor and six visual walls, from the eden_libero dataset) as a kinematic entity, over an invisible plane that provides the ground collision (common.arena_entities).

Genesis' MJCF loader differs from MuJoCo in ways that would leave every object grey or broken, so each option derives a Genesis-ready copy at load time (resolve_runtime_file; the transforms are in eden.options.objects.mjcf_transforms). The serialized file keeps naming the source, so saved configs stay portable. The transforms:

  • unwrap robosuite's wrapper body, and add or strip the root free joint to follow is_fixed_base;
  • give every collision geom a visual-only twin carrying its material (Genesis draws collision geoms with a grey proxy surface);
  • replace cube textures, which Genesis cannot map onto geoms without texture coordinates, with the material's mean colour;
  • declare radians: robosuite's object files have no <compiler> element, so loaded on their own their angles compile as degrees (the door's hinge range 0 0.4 became 0.4 degrees and the door could not open).

docs.title: SIMPLER
docs.text: Eden ports the four WidowX (BridgeData V2) tasks of SIMPLER, the real-to-sim evaluation suite for generalist manipulation policies. Read this page to evaluate a VLA such as Octo, OpenPI or GR00T on them, or to generate demonstrations. The code is in eden/tasks/simpler/.

docs.title: The tasks
docs.text:
Task (--task) SIMPLER task Instruction Success metric simpler_put_spoon_on_table_cloth PutSpoonOnTableClothInScene "put spoon on table cloth" placement: the spoon on the cloth (object_a_is_on_b) simpler_put_carrot_on_plate PutCarrotOnPlateInScene "put carrot on plate" placement: the carrot on the plate simpler_stack_green_cube_on_yellow_cube StackGreenCubeOnYellowCubeInScene "put green cube on yellow cube" placement: the green cube on the yellow one simpler_put_eggplant_in_basket PutEggplantInBasketScene "put eggplant in basket" placement: the eggplant inside the sink's basket box (object_in_region)

The tasks are built for evaluation and demonstration, not RL: they define a success metric but no rewards, and they default to one env and SIMPLER's 5 Hz control. Every scene's objects are source (what is moved) and target (where it goes), so a metric or a demonstrator reads the same names on every task.

docs.title: What matches SIMPLER
docs.text:
• The robot. A system-identified WidowX 250 (eden.tasks.simpler.base_config.DEFAULT_ROBOT): its kp/kd tables come from fitting the real BridgeData V2 arm, not the robot's stock gains, and it is gravity-compensated.
  • The frame. The world frame is the arm's base_link, as in SIMPLER, which mounts its cameras on that link.
  • The camera. SIMPLER's base-mounted 3rd_view_camera pose for each scene, with the Logitech C920 intrinsics the BridgeData V2 demonstrations were recorded with (C920_INTRINSIC).
  • The real-image backdrop. Each camera composites the scene over SIMPLER's real "inpainting" photo (real_inpainting/bridge_real_eval_1.png for the table tasks, real_inpainting/bridge_sink.png for the sink), through a BackgroundImageComposite camera overlay. The ground plane, and on the sink task the sink, are drawn by the photo rather than rendered.
  • The layouts. The three table tasks place their objects from SIMPLER's own episode grids (bridge_table.config.simpler_layouts, applied by the PlaceFromLayouts event): every ordered pair of corners of a square round the grid centre, once per source yaw, in SIMPLER's episode order.
  • Control. 5 Hz (sim_dt=0.005, decimation=40), a DifferentialIKController on gripper_link (ee_controller) and a binary gripper (gripper_controller).

Where Eden differs:

  • Torsional friction is on, with a 2 cm contact patch on the fingers (default_geoms_friction_torsional). Without it a spoon pinched at one point spins about the line between the fingertips and hangs below the grasp.
  • The sink is fitted by eye. Its pose and scale (SINK_POS, SINK_SCALE) were aligned to the backdrop photo through the task camera, and the eggplant spawns on the basin floor's +y half so a rolled one stays reachable.
  • The sim step is 5 ms (200 Hz), where SIMPLER used 2 ms.

docs.title: Evaluating a generalist policy
docs.text:
Three remote-policy clients have a setup for SIMPLER's WidowX:

Client Setup Notes OctoPolicy (eden.extensions.policies.octo.policy) (single setup) one action per request PiPolicy (eden.extensions.policies.pi.policy) policy_setup="widowx_bridge" Bridge EE-delta Gr00tPolicy (eden.extensions.policies.gr00t.policy) policy_setup="simpler_env_widowx" 256 × 256 images

Each client brings its own observation groups and action terms (its gripper is a GripperDecisionController reading the server's open/close convention, not the task's BinaryJointController), so replace both on the config before building. The clients need the policy-client extra (pip install 'eden-world[policy-client]', or uv sync --inexact --extra policy-client in a checkout).

import eden as en
import genesis as gs
from eden.envs.base import env_class_for_config
from eden.extensions.policies.gr00t.policy import Gr00tPolicy
from eden.options.managers.actions import ActionManagerOptions
from eden.options.managers.observations import ObservationManagerOptions
from eden.tasks import TASK_REGISTRY

en.init(backend=gs.gpu)
cfg = TASK_REGISTRY.build("simpler_put_carrot_on_plate")
cfg.observation_options = ObservationManagerOptions(**Gr00tPolicy.observation_options(policy_setup="simpler_env_widowx"))
cfg.action_options = ActionManagerOptions(**Gr00tPolicy.action_options(policy_setup="simpler_env_widowx"))
env = env_class_for_config(cfg).from_config(cfg, eval_mode=True)
env.build()

policy = Gr00tPolicy(env, Gr00tPolicy.configure(host="localhost", port=5555, policy_setup="simpler_env_widowx"))
policy.set_task(cfg.language_instructions[0])

for episode in range(5):
    obs, _ = env.reset()
    policy.reset_server()
    for _ in range(100):
        obs, *_ = env.step(policy.step(obs))

eden inference --task simpler_put_carrot_on_plate --policy gr00t runs the same loop from the command line with the client's defaults. The PiPolicy and Gr00tPolicy setups check the env when the client is constructed and refuse one that does not step at SIMPLER's 5 Hz, or whose observation and action terms do not match the setup. See Remote policies.

docs.title: Scripted demonstrations
docs.text:
Every SIMPLER task has an eden datagen demonstrator (eden/tasks/simpler/scripted_demos.py): a keyframe tower controller for the cube stack and a put-on tool routine for the other three. The put-on demonstrators can also run camera-only (--camera_only), locating the objects through the task camera.

eden datagen --task simpler_stack_green_cube_on_yellow_cube --num_envs 16 --num_episodes 64
eden datagen --task simpler_put_carrot_on_plate --camera_only

Success rates and what each demonstrator does are in Scripted demonstrations.

docs.title: Whiteboard drawing
docs.text:
Three RL tasks in which a Panda writes and draws on a whiteboard with a marker it holds by friction alone. They are Eden's port of the drawing tasks of RoboWorld's whiteboard environment (gym-anything/robotics, MIT): the same references at the same sizes and places on the same board, the same ink law and the same verifiers. Read this page to train on them, record them, or understand how the ink is graded. The code is in eden/tasks/whiteboard/.

Task (--task) Original task Reference Marker Success Episode whiteboard_write_text write-text HELLO, 0.60 m wide black lettering F1 ≥ 0.85 within 2 mm 90 s whiteboard_write_in_colour write-in-colour WELCOME, 0.70 m wide green lettering F1 ≥ 0.85 within 2 mm 120 s whiteboard_draw_table draw-table blank table, 0.60 m wide (thick frame, header line, two column lines) blue every line ≥ 90 % covered, no gap over 10 mm, ≤ 1 cm² of stray ink 240 s 
eden smoke --task whiteboard_draw_table
eden train --task whiteboard_write_text        # 512 envs

The scripted drawer at the end of its plan (Genesis CPU, one env), with the reference drawn faintly under the ink.

docs.title: The workcell
docs.text:
The board, the marker and the ink law are the original's; the robot is not. The original's G1 humanoid has to take a capped marker from the tray and uncap it; here a Panda with its Franka Hand already holds the uncapped marker.

  • The board is the original's MooreCo 8 × 4 ft board (2.4384 × 1.2192 m, bottom edge 0.9144 m up). Every drawing is centred where the original puts it: 1.28 m high, 5 cm right of the board's middle (common.DRAWING_CENTER).
  • The arm stands on a 0.63 m stand (common.STAND_HEIGHT) 0.50 m from the board, its base right in front of the drawing centre. The height and distance were searched, not copied: the original's height puts the drawing centre in the Panda's wrist singularity, and one continuous IK family has to reach the whole table with every joint at least 0.12 rad inside its limits.
  • The marker is the original's STAEDTLER 351 B: a 14 mm barrel, 16.2 g uncapped, and a 5 × 2 × 7.5 mm chisel nib. The original bonds an elastic nib (0.9 MPa) to the barrel. Here the nib is a body on a 2 mm slide along the barrel with the spring that solid nib has along it, E A / L = 1200 N/m, so the press force is read off the solver's nib–board contact. The hand holds the barrel pitched 20 degrees nib-down with the chisel turned 45 degrees, so horizontal and vertical lines come out equally wide.

Nothing holds the marker but friction

At every reset PlaceMarkerInGrasp puts the marker between the pads and commands the fingers shut at the Franka Hand's rated 70 N grasp. There is no weld, latch or gripper action. MarkerDropped ends the episode once the marker's grip point is more than 2 cm from the pads' midpoint. The pads have torsional friction (the nib's drag acts 10 cm ahead of them), and the pads and the barrel carry stiffened contact parameters: on Genesis' default 0.02 s time constant the pinch crept, the barrel sliding 2.5 mm under a 1 N press.

docs.title: Ink and grading
docs.text:
WhiteboardDrawing (eden.tasks.whiteboard.custom_terms) is each task's success metric, keyed drawing, and owns the ink. The laws and verifiers are ported in eden/tasks/whiteboard/grading.py.

  • Ink is laid only where the solver reports the nib geom pressing on the board, never on proximity, and only while the marker faces the board (its axis within 78 degrees of the board's normal, the original's gate). The transfer is the original's, (1 - p)(1 - exp(-350 dt min(F, 1 N) m)) under the chisel's elliptical footprint m = clip(4 (1 - r), 0, 1); the visible weight is the original's clip((p - 0.02) / 0.13, 0, 1).
  • The nib is sampled after every 5 ms sim step, not once per 50 ms control step: its pose, its press and whether it faces the board. Each sample lays one footprint, so a touch or a lift inside a control step inks exactly the sim steps it lasted. The original integrates at every 0.5 ms tick. A sample from an env the solver failed on (non-finite pose or press) draws nothing.
  • Ink off the pigment grid (beyond the drawing's area) is not graded; only its visible area is added up, and all of it counts as stray. Off the grid the pigment is kept, under the same law, in a patch that follows the nib 3 cm either way (grading.OFF_GRID_PATCH), so a stroke, a resting nib, a light press that darkens over time and a nib tapping one spot all count the area they would ink on the grid. The only overcount is ink the nib comes back to after moving more than 3 cm away.
  • Grading is incremental. Ink only grows, and only under the nib, so the running totals the F1 and the stray-ink rule need are updated in the cells each step inks, never over the whole grid.
  • Text is graded with the original's F1 (TextJudge): ink within 2 mm of the reference raster over all ink, and the reference reached by ink within 2 mm. Success at 0.85.
  • The table is graded with the original's table verifier (TableJudge), at the placement shown. Each line is read across its normal for the ink centred on it, junctions excluded; a line passes at ≥ 90 % coverage with no uncovered run over 10 mm, and the board passes with at most 1 cm² of visible stray ink. The table's grade is 1.0 exactly when it passes.

Not ported:

  • The table's registration search. The original accepts a copy up to 30 mm, 5 % or 2 degrees off where it is shown; here the placement must match, which is stricter.
  • The table's skip fill. The original credits skips under 6 mm between long inked stretches.
  • The "no other colour" check. The hand holds one marker.
  • The 1500 µL reservoir. A task uses at most about 25 µL of it.

The original's lettering threshold passes an unfinished word

F1 ≥ 0.85 can be reached before the whole word is inked, if the ink is precise. The scripted drawer's text episodes end on success before the word is finished. The threshold is the original's, kept as is.

docs.title: Recording the ink
docs.text:
The ink lives in the metric, not in the scene, so a plain camera shows a clean board. eden inference --rec records the task's recording_camera(): the arm and the whole board from behind the robot's right shoulder, with a PlanePaintOverlay that paints the drawing's visible ink in the marker's colour where the camera sees the board's face. It shades the ink as the renderer shaded the board, so the arm's shadow falls across the strokes, and it uses the frame's point cloud, so the arm hides the strokes behind it. The training config declares no camera, so training builds none.

To show the ink in another camera, give its CameraOptions the same overlay:

from eden.entities.camera_overlays import PlanePaintOverlay
from eden.options.camera import CameraOptions
from eden.tasks.whiteboard import common

ink = common.COLORS[config.scene_options.marker.ink]  # the marker's colour, the one place the task sets it
camera = CameraOptions(cam_pos=..., cam_lookat=..., overlays=[PlanePaintOverlay.configure(metric_name="drawing", color=ink)])

docs.title: The policy's view
docs.text:
• Actions. One term, arm: differential IK at the nib's tip, 20 Hz, up to 1 cm and 0.05 rad a step. A rotation turns the marker about where it writes.
  • Observations (policy and critic groups are identical; no noise is configured): the arm's joint positions and velocities, the nib tip's (u, v, gap) in the drawing frame and the marker's axis (NibPose), the nib's press averaged over the control step (NibForce), the next four reference points to ink, five guide points apart, each with a flag where a new stroke starts on the way to it (NextStrokePoints), the drawing's grade and the last action.

  • Rewards.

    • inked: reference points first inked, 100 for the whole drawing.
    • stray: visible ink off the drawing, -5 per cm².
    • reach / reach_fine: the nib toward the next point on the board's face.
    • success: a bonus of 50.
    • action_rate and arm_joint_vel: small penalties.

    Every per-step term but the penalties is positive, so dropping the marker, which ends the episode, forfeits the rest of the reward. - Terminations. timeout, drawn (success) and marker_dropped.

docs.title: The scripted drawer
docs.text:
ScriptedDrawer (eden/tasks/whiteboard/scripted_demos.py) shows each task can be completed through the task's own action, and it is each task's eden datagen demonstrator:

eden datagen --task whiteboard_write_text --num_episodes 100 --num_envs 16 --output_dir data/demos

It has no randomness and makes no deliberate mistakes, so --seed changes nothing and --p_mistake must be 0. Per stroke it travels to a hover point off the board, presses in, traces the stroke and lifts back, trimming the press depth each step toward a 0.8 N press on the nib (an integral force loop: the arm's 1–3 mm tracking error is larger than the nib's 2 mm of spring, so a fixed depth skips). It reads the arm's kinematics, the nib's pose and press, and the reference; it never touches the marker or the ink. tests/tasks/whiteboard/test_scripted_demos.py pins all three tasks (marked slow). See Scripted demonstrations.
